The tPBM P300 voltage (p = 0.125) and Flanker voltage (p = 0.215) were also non-significant, so the Discussion overstates the tPBM qEEG findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pooled or alternative analysis in the paper showing tPBM Flanker time and voltage changes with p < 0.05.

quotes.text: Each method significantly decreased the Flanker (visual ERP) response time
it was only statistically significant in the latter group

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion claims each method significantly decreased Flanker response time, but the Results report p = 0.1 for tPBM, and the paper itself says the Flanker T reduction was significant only in the wbPBM group. The statement is contradicted by the paper's own Results (the tPBM reduction was a nonsignificant trend).

issues.title: Day 12 timepoint chosen for showing significance; many uncorrected outcome tests across 2 arms
issues.explanation: The paper states that Day 1 versus Day 12 was reported because it showed 'maximal therapeutic changes that demonstrated statistical significance', after earlier timepoints showed no significant difference. Nine outcomes in each of two arms, plus age and gender subgroup tests, were analysed with unadjusted paired t-tests at 0.05. Several reported significant results (p = 0.028 to 0.046) would not survive any correction, so the positive findings are a selected subset.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome and timepoint, or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis showing the main results remain significant.

quotes.text: where we observed maximal therapeutic changes that demonstrated statistical significance
a two-tailed, paired T-test for pre- and post-treatment comparison

second_reader.what_stands: The Day 12 timepoint is described as chosen because it showed maximal, statistically significant changes, and roughly 18 arm-level paired t-tests plus subgroup tests are run with no stated primary outcome or multiplicity correction. The data-dependent timepoint selection and absent correction mean the nominal p-values, many between 0.03 and 0.05, should be treated as exploratory.

issues.title: Discussion says 14 participants received tPBM; Methods and Results give 7 per arm (14 in total)
issues.explanation: The Methods and Results state that 7 participants received tPBM and 7 received wbPBM, 14 in total. The Discussion says only one of the 14 participants treated with tPBM failed to improve, which implies 14 in the tPBM arm. This is a reporting error about the denominator for a responder statement, and it leaves unclear how many tPBM participants the responder claim covers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the tPBM arm had 14 participants, or that the sentence refers to all 14 participants.

quotes.text: There were two separate groups, n = 7 each (digital randomizer program).
Only one of the 14 participants treated with tPBM failed to improve on the Flanker or P300 voltages

issues.title: Open-label design; all participants reported symptom improvement without a measured symptom scale
issues.explanation: No masking was used, and the paper states that all subjects reported improved symptoms, with no instrument or scale reported for this. Cognitive test performance and effort can be influenced by expectation in an unblinded study. The qEEG measures are less subjective but still unblinded and uncontrolled, so the impact on the conclusion is partly covered by the no-control issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded assessor ratings or a validated symptom scale with sham comparison.

quotes.text: All subjects reported improvements in their symptoms
subject masking is planned

issues.title: MoCA gains called significant for both arms although both are printed as p = 0.052
issues.explanation: The text calls MoCA improvements significant after tPBM and wbPBM, but both p values are 0.052, above the conventional 0.05 threshold, and the paper states 'p < 0.05 or beyond' as the criterion. No other alpha or correction is declared. The two arms also share an identical p despite different means and SDs, which warrants checking against the source data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alpha of 0.10, or source data showing a p below 0.05 for MoCA in both arms.

quotes.text: we noted significant improvements in MoCA scores following tPBM (27 ± 1.53 to 29.42 ± 0.97, n = 7, p = 0.052)

issues.title: Age range 37 to 42 years is incompatible with median 56 and five participants over 65
issues.explanation: Results 3.1 gives ages ranging from 37 to 42 years with a median of 56, which is impossible. The age subgroup analyses also include 5 participants above 65, inconsistent with a maximum age of 42. The demographic description is therefore unreliable, though the efficacy results do not depend on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The source demographics (Figure 1C) showing the range is, for example, 37 to 82 years.

quotes.text: ages ranging from 37 to 42 years
with a median age of 56 years
subjects above 65 years (1.4 ± 1.1, n = 5)

issues.title: Over-65 P300T change printed as 20.03 ± 0.05 s versus 0.02 s in under-65 group
issues.explanation: The subgroup age comparison prints a P300T value of 20.03 s for the over-65 group, against 0.02 s for the under-65 group and about 0.3 s for all other P300T values. It is almost certainly a typographical error, but as printed it is not credible and the associated p = 0.71 cannot be verified. It affects only an exploratory subgroup result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data or the figure showing the value is 0.03 s or similar.

10.1002/jbio.202300003.headline_claim: Photobiomodulation therapy can restore anosmia and ageusia induced by COVID-19 and promotes full regain of smell and taste, acting as an immunomodulator.
10.1002/jbio.202300003.overall: The paper shows that self-reported smell and taste scores rose over 12 PBM sessions in 20 unblinded patients with no control group. It cannot show that PBM caused the recovery, let alone that it acted as an immunomodulator. The dosimetry is internally inconsistent in several places (wavelength, energy), and the '100% improved above 50%' claim contradicts the paper's own Table 4.

primary_outcome.name: Self-reported smell (S-VAS) and taste (T-VAS) visual analogue scores from T0 to T12

issues.title: Single-arm, unblinded pilot (n=20) with no control; causal restoration claim rests on pre-post change
issues.explanation: All 20 patients received PBM and are compared only with their own baseline, so PBM cannot be separated from natural recovery, placebo or expectation effects. The limitation is disclosed, but the Conclusions still say PBM 'can restore' smell and taste. There is no sample-size justification or registration.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent sham or untreated control group, or longitudinal pre-treatment data showing no recovery during a comparable lead-in.

quotes.text: C: not applicable.
Also, there was a lack of a control group.

second_reader.what_stands: This is a single-arm pilot of 20 patients with no comparator, and the restoration claims rest on within-patient pre-post change. The authors acknowledge the missing control group in the limitations, but the Conclusions still state causal efficacy without qualification. Blinding is not described at all, so 'unblinded' is an inference from the absence of any blinding procedure and from the self-reported outcomes.

issues.title: '100% improved above 50%' contradicted by Table 4 (e.g. ageusia 10→10 and 5→6; anosmia 8→10, 7→10)
issues.explanation: Sections 3.3 and 3.5 and the Figure 4 and 6 legends say every patient improved by more than 50% in smell and in taste. Table 4 shows patient MAPM15 with taste at 10 throughout, and JENW12 with taste moving only from 5 to 6. Several anosmia rows also rise by less than 50% of their baseline. The responder claim is therefore not supported by the paper's own data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A defined improvement metric (for example percentage of the achievable range) under which every patient exceeds 50%, together with Figures 4 and 6 data.

quotes.text: we observed 100% of the patients showed an improvement in gustatory functionality above 50%
we observed that 100% of the 20 patients showed an olfactory improvement above 50%

second_reader.what_stands: Table 4 contradicts the '100% improved above 50%' statements for both senses under every reasonable definition of improvement. The examples given (ageusia 10->10 and 5->6; anosmia 8->10 and 7->10) all fall at or below 50% of baseline. The paper never defines how the percentage was computed, so the exact count of non-qualifying patients depends on the definition used.

issues.title: Only self-rated modified VAS outcomes in an open-label study; coffee test performed but never reported
issues.explanation: All efficacy results come from unblinded self-reported 0-10 scores. No validated objective smell or taste test was used, and the coffee test results are not shown. Baseline taste is described as '3.8 ... indicating a complete loss of taste', although 0 is defined as complete absence. Self-report in an uncontrolled study is vulnerable to expectation effects, so the size of the improvement is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Validation data for this VAS, or objective psychophysical test results (such as the coffee test) showing the same improvement.

quotes.text: The limitations of our research pilot are related to a lack of the objective quantitative assessment tools to measure patient's perception of both smell and taste senses.
indicating a complete loss of taste

second_reader.what_stands: The only reported outcomes are patient self-rated modified VAS scores gathered without any described masking, which the authors partly acknowledge as a limitation. The coffee test is said to have been done at every session but its results are never reported, and it too depends on self-report.

issues.title: Conclusion asserts immunomodulation and maintained recovery with no immune endpoint and no follow-up
issues.explanation: The Conclusions say the study 'showed' that PBM acts as an immunomodulator, but no cytokine, oxidative-stress or other mechanistic outcome was measured. The statement that function has been 'well maintained' is based only on patients not returning to the clinic. These claims go beyond what an uncontrolled, self-reported pilot can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Measured inflammatory or immune markers, or objective follow-up data after treatment end.

quotes.text: Our clinical pilot study showed that PBM therapy can act as an immunomodulator in restoring anosmia and ageusia
Hence, we trust that patients ' olfactory and gustatory functionality have been well maintained.

second_reader.what_stands: No immunological outcome was measured, so the claim that PBM 'acts as an immunomodulator' in this study is not supported by its data and is borrowed from the literature. No post-treatment follow-up was collected either, so 'well maintained' rests on absence of return visits. The authors flag both gaps as needing future work, but the Conclusions still state the immunomodulation as a finding.

issues.title: Anosmia laser wavelength is 660 nm in methods and Figure 1 legend but 808 nm in PICO and Table 2
issues.explanation: The anosmia protocol text and the Figure 1 legend say 660 nm, while the PICO item and Table 2 say 808 nm. The Discussion opens with 'PBM-laser 660 nm', which points the same way as the methods text. The reader cannot tell which wavelength was delivered, which matters for a paper whose stated aim is to introduce standardised dosimetry.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An erratum or device datasheet showing the anosmia device emits only one of the two wavelengths and that the other mentions are typographical.

quotes.text: the photonic energy of 660 nm directly irradiated the olfactory supporting cells and olfactory bulb
808 nm-laser PBM for anosmia
(A) Description of laser device emitting 660 nm

issues.title: Table 2 total anosmia energy 60 J per session does not match 100 mW × 120 s × 2 points = 24 J
issues.explanation: Table 2 gives 100 mW for 2 minutes per spot over 2 points, which is 24 J per session, but lists 60 J. The ageusia section computes 12 J per spot for the same power and time, so the anosmia dose is internally inconsistent. This undermines the claim to provide a reproducible standardised dosimetry.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Additional irradiation points or durations in the anosmia protocol that give 60 J.

quotes.text: 60 J per session
2 points (one point for each nostril)

issues.title: Red wavelength for ageusia printed as 680 nm in methods and Discussion, but 660 nm in Tables and Figure 2
issues.explanation: The ageusia protocol and the Discussion give the red beams as 680 nm. The rationale paragraph, Table 3 and the Figure 2 legend give 660 nm. This is a small internal inconsistency that is probably a typo.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable beyond confirming the typo against the device specification.

quotes.text: three laser beams red (680 nm) and three laser beams NIR (808 nm)
We chose dual wavelengths emitting 660 nm and 808 nm

issues.title: Table 2 lists beam spot size 0.2 cm² but irradiated area 0.03 cm² for anosmia; irradiance uses 0.03
issues.explanation: Irradiance 3.33 W/cm² equals 100 mW divided by 0.03 cm². If the true spot at tissue were 0.2 cm², irradiance would be about 0.5 W/cm². Whether these are two different quantities cannot be settled from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement defining the two areas and which one governs delivered irradiance.

quotes.text: Average 0.2 cm 2
quotes.location: Table 2, beam spot size at target

quotes.text: 0.03 cm 2 per spot

issues.title: Independent-groups one-way ANOVA applied to repeated measures on the same 20 patients
issues.explanation: The same 20 people supply every timepoint, but the analysis uses a one-way ANOVA, which assumes independent groups. This is the wrong model for repeated data, although it makes significance harder to reach, not easier. It also cannot show a treatment effect, because it measures change from baseline only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A repeated-measures or mixed-model reanalysis giving materially different conclusions.

quotes.text: For data analysis between treatment sessions (T0 -T12), the Kolmogorov -Smirnov normality test and subsequent one-way ANOVA analysis were performed

10.1002/jcsm.13530.headline_claim: Telerehabilitation improved cardiorespiratory and muscular fitness and body composition in older people with post-COVID-19 syndrome to a greater extent than a control group.
10.1002/jcsm.13530.overall: The positive headline, that the programme improved fitness and body composition more than control, is only partly supported. The sample-size primary (VO2peak) was null, many outcomes were tested without correction across outcomes, and the 'ITT' analysis is in effect a completers analysis of 106 of 120. Exercise capacity and power output, and possibly leg extension power, are the more credible findings. The body composition and sarcopenia claims are tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Relative VO2peak (the paper's sample-size primary variable); the Methods also describe primary outcomes more broadly as cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular fitness and body composition

issues.title: Title and main finding claim greater improvement though the sample-size primary (VO2peak) showed no between-group effect
issues.explanation: Relative VO2peak was the only outcome used for the sample-size calculation, and both groups improved to a similar degree. The title and the first Discussion sentence nonetheless say the programme improved fitness and body composition more than control. The positive claims come from secondary or post hoc outcomes (CPET duration, power output, leg extension power, FFM, SLM and SMM), and the Conclusions themselves say the programme was not more effective for VO2peak. Disclosure in the Conclusions does not cure the headline framing.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registered or pre-specified primary hierarchy that names CPET duration, power output or lean mass, rather than VO2peak, as the primary outcome.

quotes.text: The main finding of this study was that the telerehabilitation programme improved cardiorespiratory and muscular fitness, and body composition in older patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome to a greater extent than a control group.
The relative V ˙ O2peak was used as the primary variable to calculate sample size.
the telerehabilitation programme was not more effective in increasing V ˙ O2peak and leg fl exion power output and peak torque

second_reader.what_stands: The sample-size primary outcome (VO2peak) showed no between-group difference, and the authors say so in the Discussion and Conclusions, but the title and the first Discussion sentence state superiority for cardiorespiratory fitness in general. The superiority claim holds only for secondary or other CPET variables (duration, power output), not for the powered primary. The statement that the paper says nothing about this is not true, since the limitation is reported.

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes tested with no across-outcome correction; several claimed effects have P of 0.018 to 0.039
issues.explanation: The study tested many CPET, BIA, isokinetic and spirometry variables, and the conclusions rest on those that reached significance. Body composition interactions (FFM P = 0.039, SLM P = 0.032, SMM P = 0.034) and right leg extension torque (P = 0.019) are modest. They would not remain significant after any reasonable correction for the number of tests. The Conclusions on body composition and muscular fitness are therefore tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified single primary outcome or hierarchical testing plan, or an across-outcome adjusted analysis in which these effects remain significant.

quotes.text: When appropriate, Bonferroni adjustment was applied to identify multiple comparisons between the experimental groups.
An intervention · time interaction effect was found in FFM, SLM and SMM ( P = 0.039, F = 4.4, η p 2 = 0.1, SP = 0.5;

second_reader.what_stands: No across-outcome multiplicity control is described; Bonferroni is limited to pairwise comparisons after each ANOVA. The body-composition and several strength effects rest on nominal P values of 0.018 to 0.039 among a large number of tested outcomes, and these would not survive a conventional family-wise correction. The exact outcome count is approximate because of table extraction damage.

issues.title: Analysis labelled intention-to-treat, but results use 106 of 120 randomised (52 TRP, 54 CG)
issues.explanation: The Methods and limitations state that an ITT analysis was done and that missing cases were kept. The Results and Table 2 footnote report only 106 participants who completed the programme and evaluations (52 TRP, 54 CG), leaving 14 (11.7%) randomised participants unaccounted for in the analysis. No imputation or missing-data handling is described. The efficacy results are therefore effectively completer analyses, and dropout was higher in the TRP arm (8 vs 6), which could favour the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Analysis tables or the CONSORT figure showing 120 participants in the model, with a described missing-data method.

quotes.text: One hundred six older patients with postCOVID-19 sequelae completed the rehabilitation programme and the evaluations of cardiorespiratory and muscular fi tness and body composition (TRP, n = 52; CG, n = 54).
The missing cases were kept in the fi nal analysis
n = 106, telerehabilitation n = 52; control group n = 54.

second_reader.what_stands: The analysis is labelled intention-to-treat, yet the reported analysed sample is the 106 completers out of 120 randomised (8 TRP and 6 CG missing), which is a completer analysis in practice. The statement that all participants underwent all assessments and that missing cases were retained is inconsistent with the reported n, and no imputation or modelling approach for the 14 is described.

issues.title: Large between-arm differences in hospitalisation severity (ICU 46% vs 24%, ventilation 23% vs 2%) not adjusted for
issues.explanation: Table 2 shows the TRP group had markedly more ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy and prone positioning. The ANOVA adjusts only for age and sex, so the differences in change scores may partly reflect baseline severity. The authors acknowledge this, then assert a benefit 'especially' among patients with prolonged hospitalisation, which no subgroup or interaction analysis supports. The direction of bias cannot be determined from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis adjusting for ICU, ventilation and hospital days that leaves the interaction estimates unchanged.

quotes.text: A general linear model of mixed repeated measures (ANOVA) adjusted for age and sex was applied.
especially among older patients with prolonged hospitalizations and more severe ventilatory conditions

issues.title: Discussion says sarcopenia is being prevented and recovery sped up, from 12-week BIA lean-mass changes
issues.explanation: The Discussion infers sarcopenia prevention from small BIA gains in FFM, SLM and SMM, without any sarcopenia diagnosis, functional endpoint or follow-up. The statement that exercise speeds recovery is not backed by a recovery measure. The authors add a caution, but the statements are worded as findings. The caveat reduces but does not remove the overreach.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sarcopenia or recovery endpoint assessed at follow-up showing group differences.

quotes.text: sarcopenia and myopenia are being prevented in older people with post-COVID-19 sequelae
Physical exercise plays a key role in speeding recovery compared with usual care.
no specifi c diagnosis of sarcopenia and myopenia was made in the study participants

issues.title: Table 2 footnote says all asterisked differences are P<0.001; the text gives P=0.005 to 0.027 for most
issues.explanation: The Table 2 footnote defines every asterisk as P < 0.001. The Results text gives P = 0.027 for hospitalisation, 0.008 for days hospitalised, 0.017 for ICU admission, 0.010 for tracheostomy and 0.005 for prone position. The footnote overstates the strength of the baseline imbalances, but the individual P values in the text are internally consistent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table legend stating that the asterisk simply means P < 0.05 for the row.

quotes.text: *Signi fi cantly higher than CG ( P < 0.001).
Those in the TRP group showed higher hospitalizations (chi-square = 4.9, P = 0.027)

issues.title: VO2peak interaction described as 'verified' at P = 0.05 against a stated threshold of P < 0.05
issues.explanation: The Results describe a significant intervention x time interaction for the primary VO2peak outcome at P = 0.05, while the stated threshold is P < 0.05. A P of 0.05 does not meet that threshold, so the wording is inconsistent. The effect is small because the authors go on to report no between-group VO2peak difference and an effect size of about 0.0.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An unrounded P below 0.05 for the VO2peak interaction.

quotes.text: In V ˙ O2peak, an intervention · time interaction effect was veri fi ed ( P = 0.05, F = 3.9, η p 2 = 0.0, SP = 0.5).
Statistical signi fi cance was set at P < 0.05.

10.1002/jcsm.13628.headline_claim: Intermittent hypoxic-hyperoxic training during inpatient rehabilitation improves functional capacity, symptoms and HRQoL in patients with long COVID, and is safe, feasible and promising, warranting validation in a controlled trial.
10.1002/jcsm.13628.overall: The primary 6MWT gain in the IHHT group (91.7 vs 32.6 m) is large and consistent across many outcomes, but it comes from a non-randomised, open-label pilot with large baseline and length-of-stay imbalances. The Conclusion's wording ('has been shown', 'demonstrated to be safe') goes beyond what this design supports, and several secondary claims lack between-group tests. The results are best read as a promising signal needing randomised, blinded confirmation.

primary_outcome.name: Change in 6-minute walking distance at end of inpatient rehabilitation (ANCOVA adjusted for baseline)

issues.title: Non-randomised, physician-assigned groups with large baseline imbalance (6MWT 352 vs 430 m, stay 29.5 vs 24.9 d)
issues.explanation: Patients were assigned to IHHT or control by the attending physician, and the groups differ at baseline in age, comorbidity, length of stay and function. The IHHT group started far lower on 6MWT and EQ-5D, so regression to the mean and more room to improve could inflate its gain. The IHHT group also stayed about 4.6 days longer, meaning more rehabilitation exposure. Baseline adjustment cannot remove these problems, so the effect sizes (for example 91.7 vs 32.6 m) cannot be attributed to IHHT alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specified allocation rules independent of patient status, or a propensity-adjusted or length-of-stay-adjusted analysis showing the same effect.

quotes.text: Patients  were  assigned  as  clinically  judged  by  the attending physician to the IHHT or control group.
Patients were assigned  to  the  study  groups  according  to  clinical  judgement (nonrandomized)

quotes.location: Table 1, Length of stay in rehab, IHHT group

second_reader.what_stands: Groups were formed by physician judgement (non-randomised), and the printed baselines show large differences: 6MWT 352 vs 430 m (about 1 SD) and stay 29.5 vs 24.9 days, plus age, CAD, COPD, HDL and GFR. The authors acknowledge the imbalance and adjust for baseline values, but adjustment cannot remove confounding by indication or by the longer stay in the IHHT arm (which would give more time to improve). The 6MWT baseline imbalance runs in the direction of more room for improvement in the IHHT group.

issues.title: Conclusion states benefit 'has been shown' and safety 'demonstrated' from a non-randomised, open pilot of 145 patients
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says IHHT 'has been shown' to improve capacity, quality of life and symptoms, and 'has been demonstrated to be safe'. The design is non-randomised and open-label, with large baseline imbalances and only about 5 weeks of in-hospital follow-up. Such a design supports a hypothesis-generating signal, not a demonstrated effect. The pilot label appears only in the limitations, not in the headline claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Conclusion wording limited to a preliminary or hypothesis-generating signal, or confirmation in a randomised blinded trial.

quotes.text: has been shown  to  improve  functional  capacity,  health-  related  quality of life and objective and subjective symptomatic status
Our  study  is  therefore  considered a pilot study with the intention to provide real life clinical treatment data to support the hypothesis

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion does say benefit 'has been shown' and safety 'has been demonstrated', which is stronger than a non-randomised, open, single-centre pilot of 145 patients with baseline imbalance can support for efficacy, and 0 events in 70 treated patients gives only limited safety precision. This is partly mitigated because the paper labels itself a pilot, discusses the design limitations and calls for a controlled validation study in the final sentence of the Conclusion.

issues.title: Open-label patients; patient-reported secondary outcomes (EQ-5D +31.3 vs +2.9) open to expectation effects
issues.explanation: Patients were not blinded and received a visible, active mask treatment, while control patients received no sham. Patient-reported outcomes (PGA, EQ-5D, FAS, Borg, MCRS) show large IHHT advantages and are the outcomes most open to expectation effects. Assessor blinding for functional tests is claimed, but it is stated only in one sentence and its feasibility is not described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sham-controlled or blinded design, or evidence that patient-reported outcomes track objective gains similarly in a blinded setting.

quotes.text: This pilot study was a prospective, controlled, open-  treatment, single-  centre, interventional study
who  were  unaware  of  the  group  assignment  of  the patients

issues.title: Handgrip, peg, spirometry and Table 3 benefits rest on within-group significance without between-group tests
issues.explanation: For handgrip, nine-hole peg, FEV1/PEF/VC and all clinical and biochemical variables, the paper contrasts 'significant in IHHT' with 'not significant in controls' and concludes benefit. A difference in significance is not a significant difference between groups, and no between-group test is shown for these rows. With over a dozen secondary outcomes and no multiplicity adjustment, some of these claims may be chance. The primary 6MWT result is not affected by this issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-group (ANCOVA or interaction) tests for these outcomes that remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

quotes.text: but no such improvement was observed in the control group after the rehabilitation
Such functional improvements included stair climbing power, maximum handgrip strength, nine-  hole peg test and respiratory functions (FEV1, PEF and VC)

issues.title: Control-group baseline values differ between Tables 1 and 3 (LDL 3.9 ± 2.6 vs 3.6 ± 1, plus others)
issues.explanation: Control-group baseline LDL is 3.9 ± 2.6 in Table 1 and 3.6 ± 1 in Table 3, with no explanation. Other control-group baselines also differ: weight 82.1 vs 82.4 kg, CRP 45.2 vs 46.3, HDL 1.6 vs 1.5, GFR 87.6 vs 87.9. These are small, but they suggest the two tables were built from different data sets or versions. None of these values is a primary or key secondary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that Table 3 used a restricted subset of patients with paired laboratory data.

quotes.location: Table 1, LDL, mmol/L row, control group

issues.title: No trial registration identifier reported for a prospective interventional study
issues.explanation: The study is described as prospective and interventional, yet no registry or protocol identifier is given. Without one, a reader cannot verify that the primary endpoint and analysis plan were fixed in advance. The primary endpoint is clearly named in the Methods, so the practical effect is limited.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with a registration date before enrolment, or a protocol document.

quotes.text: This pilot study was a prospective, controlled, open-  treatment, single-  centre, interventional study in hospitalized patients

issues.title: Table 1 diabetes: control '6 (88.0)' of n = 75 should be 8.0%
issues.explanation: The control-group diabetes cell prints 88.0% for 6 patients out of 75. That count corresponds to 8.0%, and 88% of 75 would be 66 patients. This is a typographical slip in a baseline table that affects no outcome analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A count of 66 diabetic controls, which would make 88.0% correct but contradict the 'ns' comparison and the other comorbidity rows.

quotes.location: Table 1, Diabetes mellitus row, control group

script.explanation: 6/75 = 8.00%, but the paper prints 88.0, outside the rounding interval [87.95, 88.10]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 6.8 rather than 75.

10.1002/jmv.28373.headline_claim: The WHO Borg CR-10 pacing protocol substantially reduces post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE) episodes in people with post-COVID syndrome while increasing activity levels.
10.1002/jmv.28373.overall: The data show a falling trend in self-reported PESE episodes in a small single-arm cohort, but they cannot show that the protocol caused it, and the Conclusions word it more strongly than the design allows. The estimate is best read as hypothesis-generating pending a controlled trial.

primary_outcome.name: Total number of PESE episodes per week (Poisson mixed model, week-on-week change)

issues.title: Single-arm 6-week cohort: 16% weekly PESE fall cannot be attributed to the protocol
issues.explanation: All 31 analysed participants followed the protocol and were compared only with their own earlier weeks. Natural fluctuation in a relapsing-remitting condition, regression to the mean after enrolment at a symptomatic time, and the effect of weekly clinician contact would all produce a falling trend without any protocol effect. The paper itself says no causal effect was demonstrated, yet the Conclusions say the protocol was 'shown' to reduce PESE.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group, or a randomized comparison, showing a smaller fall in PESE episodes without the protocol.

quotes.text: Notably, no concurrent control group was used to compare and demonstrate a causal effect of the WHO Borg protocol based on physical activity.
shown for the first time in the current literature to substantially reduce PESE episodes whilst increasing activity levels

second_reader.what_stands: With a single-arm design, completers-only analysis, and weekly clinician contact, the 16% weekly fall in PESE episodes cannot be attributed to the protocol; the paper's own limitations acknowledge the lack of a control group, so the problem is real but openly stated. The statistical estimate itself is internally consistent.

issues.title: Conclusions say protocol 'shown' to substantially reduce PESE despite uncontrolled design
issues.explanation: The Conclusions use causal, confident language ('shown ... to substantially reduce'), and the Discussion states that using the Borg scale 'has been shown as an effective measure to reduce PESE'. The authors also admit an RCT is required to confirm the intervention. The conclusion should have been framed as an association in an uncontrolled cohort. This is the interpretive counterpart of the missing control group, and the two together are the main weakness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled evidence of benefit, or Conclusions reworded as hypothesis-generating.

quotes.text: shown for the first time in the current literature to substantially reduce PESE episodes whilst increasing activity levels
has been shown as an effective measure to reduce PESE in PCS patients
quotes.location: Discussion, paragraph on ME/CFS heart rate monitoring

quotes.text: A randomized controlled trial, with a more significant number of participants representative of the broader population of PCS, would be required to confirm this rehabilitation intervention.

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions and a Discussion sentence use causal, definitive wording ('shown... to substantially reduce', 'shown as an effective measure') that goes beyond what an uncontrolled, single-arm, 31-participant cohort can support. The paper partly tempers this elsewhere (calling for an RCT and saying 'potential'), so the inconsistency is in the strength of the wording rather than concealment of the design.

issues.title: Unblinded, self-reported weekly PESE counts elicited by the clinician who sets the next target
issues.explanation: The primary outcome is recalled by the participant and elicited on a weekly call by the same clinician who then sets the next week's activity target. With no blinding and no comparator, expectation, social desirability and recall effects could contribute to the reported decline. The authors acknowledge the contact effect but still argue the reduction is less likely to be explained by biases. This is largely the same weakness as the missing control, so it adds only modestly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of independent or objective outcome measurement, or a control group receiving equivalent clinician contact without the protocol.

quotes.text: Participants received weekly telephone calls with a clinician, who administered a PESE questionnaire
It is also essential to recognize the regular contact during the 6 -week follow -up period

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; n=31 gives wide CIs for symptom and subgroup results
issues.explanation: No sample-size justification is given and only 31 of 34 consented participants were analysed. The authors concede that small numbers prevent subgroup and individual-symptom conclusions. The main effect CI (9%-24%) is wide, so the size of the effect is uncertain even though it excludes zero.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation or a larger replication with similar estimates.

quotes.text: The small sample size raises the uncertainty about the potential size of improvement.
small numbers with individual symptoms resulted in wide CIs

issues.title: Primary PESE count from a newly adapted questionnaire with no reported validation
issues.explanation: The primary outcome comes from a questionnaire adapted from the DSQ-PEM using C19-YRSm items, with no reported reliability or validity data in post-COVID syndrome. Counting episodes by recall each week may also vary with how the clinician elicits them. This weakens how far the absolute change in episode counts can be interpreted.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Published validation or reliability data for this adapted questionnaire in PCS.

quotes.text: This PESE questionnaire was adapted from the DSQ -PEM 15 using items from the modified C19 -YRS questionnaire 16
iterations to develop the PESE questionnaire

issues.title: Completer-only analysis (3 of 34 excluded) while 4 report being unable to follow the protocol
issues.explanation: Participants who did not finish the six weeks were removed from analysis, and the paper does not say why the 3 left. Section 3.3 states four participants could not comply because of infection or PEM exacerbation, and it is unclear how these relate to the 3 excluded. If non-completers had worse trajectories, the reported fall in episodes is overstated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A report of the reasons for the 3 exclusions and a sensitivity analysis including them.

quotes.text: 3 (9%) were excluded from data analysis because they did not complete the full 6 -weeks follow up period
Four participants could not comply with the protocol guidance

issues.title: Exploratory symptom and subgroup results at p<0.05 uncorrected; symptom ranking is tentative
issues.explanation: About eight symptom models, three trigger models, duration, number of symptoms and three subgroup interactions were tested at p<0.05 without adjustment. The primary result is unaffected, but statements about which symptoms improved most rest on borderline results. Fatigue and breathlessness have lower CI limits at 0% and p=0.05, and headache has p=0.02.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A declared adjustment or a pre-specified hierarchy showing these symptoms as confirmatory outcomes.

quotes.text: p < 0.05 was taken to indicate statistical significance.
The most substantial improvements were seen in fatigue, breathlessness and headache, and possibly palpitations

10.1002/jmv.29757.headline_claim: Intravenous umbilical cord-derived MSC infusion is safe and tolerable in long COVID patients and alleviates symptoms and interstitial lung lesions, and maintains SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies.
10.1002/jmv.29757.overall: The paper is an open-label, single-arm series of 10 patients whose efficacy and immune-regulation claims rest on uncontrolled within-patient comparisons with self-reported outcomes; it can support only a tentative, hypothesis-generating safety signal (with a notably high infusion-reaction rate). The authors acknowledge the missing control group, but the title and conclusions still state benefit more strongly than the design allows.

primary_outcome.name: Safety (adverse events related to cell administration)

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from a single-arm, open-label series of 10 with within-baseline comparisons and self-reported outcomes
issues.explanation: All efficacy findings (symptoms, EQ-VAS, CT scores, immune markers) are before-after changes in 10 patients (9 analysed) with no comparator, and testing is only baseline versus follow-up. Symptom outcomes are self-reported in an unblinded study, and natural recovery, regression to the mean and expectation effects cannot be separated from any treatment effect. The title ('improves the long COVID') and Discussion ('significantly alleviate symptoms') state effects that this design cannot attribute to the cells.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or randomized comparator arm, or blinded assessment, showing the same improvement relative to control.

quotes.text: To test differences between baseline and follow -up visits, ANOVA of repeated measurements was used
The improvement of symptoms was evaluated by a series of questionnaires, including a self -reported symptom questionnaire
The results showed that UC -MSCs were able to significantly alleviate symptoms at Month 1 and improve lung lesions at Month 6 in patients with long COVID.

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from a 10-patient (9 analysed) single-arm, open-label series using baseline-versus-follow-up comparisons and mostly self-reported outcomes, with no control for placebo effect, natural recovery or regression to the mean, and the Discussion wording is causal. This is partly mitigated because the authors call efficacy secondary, say 'show potential', and explicitly list the lack of a control group as a major limitation.

issues.title: Immune-regulation and antibody-maintenance conclusions exceed uncontrolled, unadjusted, mixed-significance data
issues.explanation: The Conclusions state MSC treatment 'can effectively regulate the immune balance' and maintain SARS-CoV-2 antibodies. The evidence is many uncorrected within-patient tests (n=10) with mixed significance, and antibody maintenance is inferred from a lack of significant decrease without a comparator or vaccination-adjusted analysis (three patients were vaccinated). Safety is called 'safe and tolerable' while the paper reports a 60% infusion-reaction rate, higher than the roughly 10% in the authors' earlier studies.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data with multiplicity-adjusted analysis showing the immune changes and antibody maintenance exceed those in untreated long COVID patients.

quotes.text: MSC treatment can effectively regulate the immune balance of patients and maintain a prolonged presence of SARS -CoV -2 -specific antibodies.
the incidence of infusion reactions was higher at 60% compared to approximately 10% reported in our previous studies and literature.

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions claim of effective immune regulation and antibody maintenance goes beyond uncontrolled, unadjusted data in 10 patients where several key changes were non-significant (Treg at Month 1, total IgG, IgM at Month 6, TNF-alpha, IL-10, IL-17A) and the antibody result is an absence of a significant decrease with no comparator. The immune findings are better described as exploratory changes in subset proportions; the 60% versus ~10% infusion-reaction figure is correctly reported, but its explanation is untested.

issues.title: Reported p-values of 0.000 and 'significant' claims rest on mixed timepoint results with a Treg p of 0.058
issues.explanation: Several p-values are printed as 0.00 or 0.000, which cannot be exact, and Treg increase at Month 1 (p = 0.058) is part of the 'significant increase' narrative. Significance appears at some timepoints and not others, with no correction across the many tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Exact p-values and a prespecified correction showing the Treg and B-cell trends remain significant.

quotes.text: Treg cells increased from 5.84 (1.91) at baseline to 7.00 (2.92) at Month 1 ( p = 0.058)
we observed a significant increase in the proportion of naive B cells and Treg cells

issues.title: No trial registry identifier reported for a study described as prospective
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective follow-up and gives only an ethics approval number, not a trial registration. Prespecification of primary and secondary outcomes, and of the many immune endpoints analysed, cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment listing the same outcomes.

quotes.text: we conducted a prospective long -term follow -up of UC -MSCs therapy in patients with long COVID

10.1002/pcn5.238.headline_claim: Regular online peer support with trained facilitators may be effective for treating depression among individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), per a single-arm pilot.
10.1002/pcn5.238.overall: The finding of a PHQ-9 reduction in 18 people is real as a descriptive result, but with no control group, P=0.04 and power about 0.56 it cannot show that peer support caused the change. The effectiveness wording in the conclusion goes beyond the design, even though the authors partly acknowledge this. Apart from one misprinted anxiety P value, the numbers are broadly consistent.

primary_outcome.name: Depression severity (PHQ-9)

issues.title: Effectiveness for depression inferred from an uncontrolled single-arm pre-post pilot (n=18, P=0.04)
issues.explanation: The only evidence is a within-person PHQ-9 change (13.33 to 11.12, P=0.04) with no control group. The authors concede the change may reflect elapsed time, yet the conclusion says peer support 'may be effective for treatment of depression'. Entry required PHQ-9 ≥ 5, which invites regression to the mean. The data support a hypothesis-generating signal, not an effect of the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or waitlist control group, or evidence that PHQ-9 scores were stable over a comparable untreated period in this population.

quotes.text: this single -arm pilot study suggests that online peer support with regular sessions and trained facilitators may be effective for treatment of depression among individuals with PASC.
we acknowledge that the change in depression observed in this study may have been caused by time elapsed rather than online peer support due to the single -arm design

second_reader.what_stands: The study is an uncontrolled single-arm pre-post pilot (n=18, P=0.04) and the Conclusion describes the intervention as possibly 'effective for treatment of depression', which goes beyond what the design supports. This is softened because the authors say 'may', acknowledge in the Limitations that time elapsed could explain the change, and call for a randomized controlled trial. The remaining problem is that the wording still implies effectiveness, and the only mitigation offered (adjusting for time since infection) does not control for other non-intervention explanations.

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; n=18 pilot, depression P=0.04 with post hoc power 0.56
issues.explanation: The sample size of 18 was set by pilot convention, not by a calculation for the primary outcome. Post hoc power for the depression result is only about 0.56, and the P value of 0.04 is borderline. A significant finding from so small a sample is likely to exaggerate the true change. This weakens the primary result, though pilots are expected to be small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size justification for PHQ-9 change, or a precision-based estimate showing the pilot was adequate for its stated aim.

quotes.text: The sample size was required to be 18 or more, based on the sample size criteria for pilot studies.

issues.title: ITT anxiety t = 1.03 printed with P = 0.16; the same t in per-protocol gives P = 0.32
issues.explanation: Table 3 gives the same paired t of 1.03 for anxiety in both analysis sets, but P = 0.16 in ITT and P = 0.32 in per-protocol. With about 17 df, a two-sided t of 1.03 gives P near 0.32, so the ITT value of 0.16 is wrong or is one-tailed without saying so. Anxiety is non-significant either way, so the conclusions do not change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the ITT anxiety test was one-tailed, or a different df or t for the ITT anxiety row.

10.1002/pmrj.12578.headline_claim: Virtual outpatient rehabilitation improved lower limb strength and cardiopulmonary endurance in COVID-19 survivors, and home physical therapy improved lower limb strength; virtual rehabilitation is described as an efficacious delivery method.
10.1002/pmrj.12578.overall: The headline claim that virtual rehabilitation is efficacious and better than no exercise is not supported by this design: it rests on within-group pre-post changes in a non-randomised, self-selected cohort with 50% differential loss, and the between-group tests were non-significant. The data are compatible with improvement over 2 weeks in those who returned, but not with a demonstrated treatment effect.

primary_outcome.name: Change in 30-second sit-to-stand score and 2-minute step test score (clinically meaningful difference achievement)

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from within-group changes; overall between-group responder tests not significant (P = .056, .12)
issues.explanation: Benefit is shown by pre-post Wilcoxon tests within each arm, which cannot separate treatment effect from natural recovery over 2 weeks. The between-group comparisons of responders were not significant overall (P = .056 for sit-to-stand, P = .12 for step test), and the step test VPT versus none comparison was also not significant (P = .25). Yet the conclusions state improvement 'compared with both no exercise and a nonsupervised home exercise program'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group analysis of change scores showing a significant VPT advantage over none and IE.

quotes.text: Changes in sit-to-stand scores and step test scores were tested using a Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test comparing initial to follow-up within-group
Across groups these differences were not
quotes.location: Results, page break before 'statistically significant ( P = .056)'

quotes.text: These differences were not statistically different across groups ( P = .12) or between VPT and the none group ( P = .25).

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy narrative leans on within-group pre/post changes, and both omnibus between-group responder tests (P = .056 for strength, P = .12 for endurance) were not significant. For endurance there is no significant between-group evidence at all (VPT vs none P = .25). For strength, the pairwise VPT vs none and HPT vs none tests were significant. These are uncorrected, based on very small groups, and not accompanied by a significant omnibus test.

issues.title: Efficacy conclusions despite non-significant between-group tests (P = .056, P = .12)
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion state that virtual rehabilitation improved strength and endurance and 'seems to be an efficacious method'. The group comparisons reported in the same abstract were non-significant for both primary outcomes. The paper also says VPT outcomes are better 'compared with both no exercise and a nonsupervised home exercise program', which the data do not test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Significant between-group tests in favour of VPT for both outcomes.

quotes.text: Virtual rehabilitation seems to be an efficacious method of treatment delivery for recovering COVID-19 patients.
resulted in clinically meaningful improvements in lower body strength and endurance compared with both no exercise and a nonsupervised home exercise program

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract and Conclusions claim efficacy, and improved endurance versus no exercise and versus unsupervised home exercise, but neither omnibus between-group test was significant (P = .056, .12). VPT vs none was not significant for the step test (P = .25), and VPT vs IE was never tested. Only the strength comparison of VPT vs none (P = .03) supports a between-group claim.

issues.title: Non-randomised, self-selected arms with baseline imbalances used for comparative efficacy conclusions
issues.explanation: Patients agreed to their assigned treatment plan, so arms differ by self-selection and clinical judgement. The groups differ at baseline in sex (24% to 57% female, P = .04), PHQ-4 (P = .02), impaired ADLs (P = .002) and days hospitalised (P < .001), and there is no adjustment. The 'none' group is also not a clean untreated control because it comprises people referred but who did not attend. Comparative statements versus no exercise are therefore confounded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Adjusted analyses or propensity-matched comparison showing the same effect.

quotes.text: therefore the population was not randomized
there were high levels of self-selection and bias introduced into the study

second_reader.what_stands: Arms were self-selected and not randomised, differed significantly at baseline on sex, PHQ-4, ADL impairment and length of stay, and were compared without adjustment. The authors disclose this and urge caution, but the Conclusions still draw comparative efficacy statements.

issues.title: 53 of 106 patients (50%) followed up, differentially by arm, with completers-only analysis
issues.explanation: Only half of patients returned, with follow-up ranging from 30% in the none group to 70% in VPT. Lost patients were excluded, and missing tests among completers were replaced by the series mean (10 for sit-to-stand, 15 for the step test), which shrinks variance. Patients who improved are more likely to return or less likely to; the direction of bias is unknown, but arm comparisons are unreliable, especially with only 6 in the none group.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis including all enrolled patients (e.g. baseline carried forward or multiple imputation) with the same conclusions.

quotes.text: Thus, 70% of the VPT group, 32% of the HPT group, 47% of the IE group, and 30% of the none group returned for follow-up visits.
Patients who were lost to follow-up were not included in the analysis.

second_reader.what_stands: Exactly half the cohort (53/106) was followed up, with return rates ranging from 30% (none) to 70% (VPT), and only completers were analysed. The authors acknowledge this as a source of bias but do not temper the conclusions or carry out any sensitivity analysis.

issues.title: Sit-to-stand meaningful difference defined as increase of 2 (Methods) versus >2 (Figure 1 caption)
issues.explanation: The Methods define the sit-to-stand threshold as an increase of 2 repetitions, while the Figure 1 caption says an increase of more than 2. Which was used for the 65%/88%/50%/17% responder figures is not stated. Patients improving by exactly 2 would be classified differently, so the responder proportions are slightly uncertain, but nothing else hinges on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement from the authors that the same threshold (e.g. >=2) was applied throughout and the caption is a typo.

quotes.text: an increase of 2 repetitions during the 30-second sit-to-stand test
The clinically meaningful difference in sit-to-stand is an increase of >2 for sit-to-stand

10.1002/pri.1972.headline_claim: A continuous moderate-intensity aerobic plus resistance training program is effective for patients post-COVID-19, improving lung function, respiratory muscle strength, exercise tolerance, fatigue and quality of life.
10.1002/pri.1972.overall: The paper shows that 26 completers improved on several measures over the study period, but the design (single arm, completers only, no control) cannot show that the programme caused the improvement, so the stated conclusion of effectiveness is not supported. The claim of broad improvement in lung function and respiratory muscle strength also overstates what the paper's own non-significant tests show. The percentage and denominator inconsistencies in Table 2 are minor.

primary_outcome.name: Maximal functional capacity (VO2peak) and submaximal functional capacity (6MWT), with fatigue and quality of life also reported

issues.title: Uncontrolled single-arm pre-post study concludes the programme 'is effective'
issues.explanation: All 26 completers received the programme and were compared only with their own baseline using paired t-tests, with no control group. Natural recovery from COVID-19 over the study period, regression to the mean, and practice effects on the tests cannot be separated from any training effect. The authors admit a control group could not be recruited and that natural evolution may contribute, yet the Conclusion states the programme is effective. The data support improvement over time in completers, not efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control arm, or a natural-history comparison, showing the changes exceed spontaneous recovery.

quotes.text: A cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program consisting of continuous moderate -intensity aerobic and resistance training is effective for patients post -COVID -19.
limited randomization and recruitment of a control group
Paired t -test was used to analyze intragroup variables before and after intervention.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, uncontrolled pre-post design analysed in completers only (26 of 41), and the conclusion and abstract nonetheless state the programme 'is effective' / 'proved to be effective', which is a causal claim the design cannot support. The authors do acknowledge the missing control group and natural evolution in section 4.1 and say the programme 'probably contributed', but that more cautious wording is not reflected in the conclusion.

issues.title: 15 of 41 patients (36.6%) who started did not complete; only completers analysed
issues.explanation: The paper says 41 patients started and 26 completed, and analyses only the 26. No intention-to-treat or sensitivity analysis is given, and the text does not say why patients dropped out. Patients who tolerate and finish exercise training tend to do better, so the pre-post gains probably look larger than they would in everyone who began the programme.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline data showing dropouts resembled completers, or an analysis that includes them.

quotes.text: A total of 41 patients started the intervention protocol, however 26 patients completed the cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program

issues.title: Conclusion claims improved lung function and muscle strength, but most such tests are non-significant; no multiplicity control
issues.explanation: About 30 comparisons were tested at an uncorrected 0.05. In Table 2, FVC (p = 0.249), FEV1/FVC (p = 0.090), MIP (p = 0.111), VO2AT (p = 0.850) and VE/VCO2 (p = 0.650) are not significant. Only FEV1 (p = 0.008) and MEP (p = 0.009) are. Yet the Discussion and Conclusion say the programme improved lung function and respiratory muscle strength overall. The ventilatory-disorder percentage changes (p = 0.102) and inspiratory weakness (p = 0.070) are also non-significant, so the claim rests on a favourable subset. The significant FEV1 and MEP results would not all survive a correction for this many tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchy of outcomes or multiplicity adjustment showing the claimed domains remain significant.

quotes.text: Rehabilitation improved lung function, respiratory muscle strength, maximal and submaximal exercise tolerance, fatigue, and quality of life of patients post -COVID -19.
p -value < 0.05 (two -tailed) was considered significant.
This program improved respiratory muscle strength, lung function, exercise tolerance, fatigue, and quality of life.

issues.title: Ventilatory-disorder percentages (21.70, 39.10, 4.50, 36.40) imply n = 22-23, not the n = 26 in the headers
issues.explanation: Table 2 labels both columns n = 26. Neither 21.70% nor 39.10% can be a count out of 26: 5/26 is 19.2% and 6/26 is 23.1%. Both fit a denominator of 23 (5/23, 9/23), and the post values 4.50% and 36.40% fit 22 (1/22, 8/22). The analysed n for these outcomes is therefore smaller and unstated, and the McNemar comparisons rest on those unreported denominators. This is a reporting error that does not change the main findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement or CONSORT figure showing that 23 and 22 patients had valid spirometry before and after rehabilitation.

quotes.text: Pre - rehabilitation ( n = 26)
39.10% of patients had restrictive and 21.70% obstructive

10.1002/pri.2086.headline_claim: A six-week cardiopulmonary rehabilitation protocol improved functional capacity (6MWT), reduced dyspnea, and increased upper-limb muscle mass in individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome, supporting its use in this population.
10.1002/pri.2086.overall: The direction of benefit on the 6MWT and dyspnea is plausible, but the primary-outcome between-group difference (100.46 m) and its p-value do not reconcile with the printed group changes or CI, and the dyspnea difference also mismatches. The 'safe' and 'reduced fatigue' claims go beyond the reported data. Treat the conclusions as tentative for a small, unblinded trial with an attention-control comparator.

primary_outcome.name: Six-minute walk test distance (6MWT, m)

issues.title: 6MWT between-group difference printed 100.46 m but the printed group changes give 137.67 m
issues.explanation: The paper reports a CPRG gain of 199.29 m and a CG gain of 61.62 m, and a between-group difference of 100.46 m. The difference of those changes is 137.67 m, and nothing in the paper explains the gap. This is the primary outcome, so the size of the headline effect is uncertain. The printed value is the smaller one, so the effect may be understated; the true mixed-model estimate cannot be established from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated covariate adjustment or imputation that makes the model-based difference 100.46 m, or a corrected value.

quotes.text: The inter -group difference was 100.46 m (7.40-193 m).
the CPRG increased the distance walked on the 6MWT by 199.29 m (99.45-299 m)

second_reader.what_stands: The printed between-group 6MWT difference (100.46 m) does not equal the difference of the printed group changes (about 137 m), and the paper gives no adjustment or other reason for the gap. Its CI width also does not match the within-group CIs. I could not tell from the paper which figures are correct. The between-group p value of 0.002 also looks inconsistent with a CI whose lower limit is 7.40 (that would normally imply p near 0.03).

issues.title: 'Safe' claimed with no adverse-event results; 'reduced fatigue' claimed despite null between-group fatigue
issues.explanation: The implications section calls the protocol safe and effective, but the Results report no adverse events. The discussion states that the protocol reduced fatigue, yet the between-group fatigue difference is null (2.31, p = 0.440). The trial also has multiple secondary outcomes without multiplicity control, and participants cannot be blinded to an exercise-vs-lecture comparison. These claims overreach the evidence, although the 6MWT and dyspnea results do favour the protocol.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adverse-event counts by group, and a between-group fatigue result favouring CPRG.

quotes.text: Cardiopulmonary rehabilitation proved to be a feasible, safe, and effective treatment for sequelae from COVID -19.
No inter -group difference was observed after the rehabilitation (2.31 [ -15.52-10.90]).
reduced dyspnea and fatigue, and increased muscle mass in the upper limbs in this randomized controlled trial

second_reader.what_stands: The paper says adverse events were recorded daily but reports no adverse-event results, so 'safe' is not supported by anything shown. The claim of reduced fatigue rests only on the within-group CPRG change, since the between-group fatigue comparison is null (p = 0.440, CI spanning zero) and the CG also fell by about 5 points. The abstract and conclusion do not make the fatigue claim, so the overstatement is confined to the Discussion and Section 4.1.

issues.title: mMRC between-group difference printed -1.45 but the printed group changes give -1.79
issues.explanation: The CPRG change (-2.11) minus the CG change (-0.32) is -1.79, but the paper prints -1.45 for the inter-group difference. No adjustment or missing-data handling is described that would explain a 0.34-point gap. The direction of effect is unchanged, so this is a one-result reporting inconsistency. Here the printed effect is smaller than the data imply.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A model specification (e.g., baseline adjustment) that explains why the model-based difference differs from the raw difference of changes.

quotes.text: the inter -group difference was -1.45 ( -1.98 to -0.92)

issues.title: Sample size (N=32) calculation lacks effect size; wide CIs in a 33-person trial
issues.explanation: The power calculation states alpha and 'beta of 0.80' but no effect size or variance, so it cannot be checked. The primary-outcome interval is very wide (7.40-193 m). The authors do acknowledge the limited sample and call for larger studies, which tempers the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The effect size and SD used in G*Power showing adequate power for the primary 6MWT comparison.

quotes.text: The sample size N = 32, (CPRG = 16; CG = 16) for linear mixed models was calculated using the software G* Power 3.1.0
Also, the sample size was limited due to recruitment during the pandemic period.

issues.title: CG mMRC change -0.32 printed with CI -0.18 to 0.83, which excludes the estimate (midpoint +0.325)
issues.explanation: The control-group dyspnea change is -0.32, but its printed 95% CI of -0.18 to 0.83 does not contain it. The interval is centred at +0.325, so it looks like a sign or ordering slip (likely -0.83 to 0.18). This is a reporting error in a secondary within-group result. It does not change the between-group conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement or supplementary table giving the CG interval as an interval that contains -0.32.

script.explanation: the estimate -0.32 lies outside its own CI [-0.18, 0.83]; the estimate -0.32 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [-0.18, 0.83] (expected about 0.3250) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

issues.title: Baseline differences in age, ICU stay, hospitalization and CT involvement in a 33-person trial
issues.explanation: The groups differ in age (50.8 vs 44 years), ICU admission (17.6% vs 50%), hospitalization (82% vs 50%) and lung involvement. These are plausible chance imbalances in a small trial, and they do not run consistently in one direction. The paper does not adjust for them, so their effect on the between-group result cannot be assessed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis adjusted for these covariates showing the same effects.

quotes.text: Although the hospitalization rate was 82.3% in CPRG and 50% in CG, the intensive care unit admission rate was higher in CG (50%) than in CPRG (17.6%).

issues.title: Non-completers excluded and no ITT analysis stated (33 of 34 analysed)
issues.explanation: The methods say people who failed to complete the protocol were excluded, and no intention-to-treat analysis is described. In practice only one CPRG participant (18 allocated, 17 analysed) was lost, so the impact is small. Outcome handling for the dropout is not described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated ITT or mixed-model analysis that included all 34 participants.

quotes.text: Those who failed to complete the protocol or refused to participate were excluded.

issues.title: Registration date and prespecified primary outcome not stated; Methods cite an ethics number as the registration
issues.explanation: Recruitment ran May 2021 to January 2022, but the paper never says when the trial was registered. The registry ID appears only in a late declaration, and the Methods cite the ethics number. Prospective registration and agreement with the registered primary outcome therefore cannot be verified from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry record showing registration before May 2021 with 6MWT as the primary outcome.

quotes.text: registered in the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (CAAE: 42496821.4.0000.5188).

10.1007/s00115-024-01732-3.headline_claim: An individualised, exertion-controlled training therapy followed by intensified cognitive behavioural therapy reduces post-COVID-19 leading symptoms (fatigue, sensorimotor instability, neuropsychiatric, cardiopulmonal/autonomic, secondary psychosomatic symptoms, pain) and improves motor and cognitive fatigability.
10.1007/s00115-024-01732-3.overall: The paper shows that fewer patients in a single uncontrolled cohort of 78 had the listed symptoms at a later visit, and that motor scores moved slightly. Cause-and-effect language about the therapy, the prevention of crash, and the male advantage is not supported by this design. The printed numbers mostly reconcile, apart from the 53% vs 56% sensorimotor figure and the Discussion's omission of the worsening of psychosomatic symptoms.

primary_outcome.name: not defined as a primary outcome; multiple leading symptoms and motor fatigability parameters reported

issues.title: Single-arm pre-post cohort of 78, with Wilcoxon within-group tests, used to claim demonstrated efficacy
issues.explanation: All results come from one self-selected cohort (78 of 407 screened) compared with its own baseline, with no comparison group and no blinding. The Wilcoxon tests only show a pre-post change within this group. They cannot separate the therapy from natural recovery over the roughly 230 days of the process, concurrent medical treatment, regression to the mean or patient expectations. The 'demonstrated efficacy' conclusion goes beyond what this design can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group, or a statement that the work is purely descriptive with the efficacy language removed.

quotes.text: konnte nachgewiesen werden, dass durch eine den medizinischen Hauptprozess am Post-COVID-19-Zentrum begleitende individualisierte beanspruchungsgesteuerte Trainings- und in Ansätzen auch kognitive Verhaltenstherapie
Für die Bewertung der Therapiewirksamkeit wurde der Wilcoxon-Test durchgeführt, da keine Normalverteilung in den Prä- und Postdatensätzen vorlag.

second_reader.what_stands: The motor results come from a single-group pre-post comparison of 78 patients with within-group Wilcoxon tests, and the text presents them as proven efficacy ('nachgewiesen'). Regression to the mean, spontaneous recovery after infection, learning or test-retest effects, and co-interventions (medication, CBT) cannot be separated from the training effect. No limitation about the lack of a control group is stated, and the borderline p-values come with no multiplicity adjustment.

issues.title: Six leading-symptom outcomes have no instrument; 'improvement' is a drop in symptomatic head-count
issues.explanation: The paper does not say how fatigue, sensorimotor instability, neuropsychiatric and other symptoms were recorded or when a symptom counted as present. The Table 4 'improvement' percentages are consistent with the number of symptomatic patients at the first visit minus the number at evaluation, divided by the first-visit number (e.g. 78 to 23 = 55, 71%). That is not a paired within-patient change and not a validated severity measure, and it cannot show that any patient got better rather than that the group count fell.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description naming validated symptom scales with defined thresholds and showing paired patient-level change.

quotes.text: Die Evaluation der individualisierten beanspruchungsgesteuerten Trainingstherapie erfolgte anhand der Post-COVID-19-Leitsymptome
In der Routinepraxis muss die Gültigkeit der eingesetzten Testverfahren, insb. bei einer Zusammenhangsbegutachtung, erfolgen.

second_reader.what_stands: No instrument, scale, threshold or definition of 'symptom present' is given for the six leading symptoms or for the Phase 2 psychosomatic outcome. 'Verbesserung' is the difference in the head-count of symptomatic patients, which ignores severity and shows no individual-level change. The sensorimotor row is also inconsistent: the printed 47% and 53% do not match 34/78 = 43.6% or 44/78 = 56%, and the text says 56%. The Fazit's remark that test validity must be ensured in routine practice is a general recommendation, not a limitation of the paper's own outcomes.

issues.title: Practice points claim crash prevention and fewer process disturbances; neither outcome was measured
issues.explanation: The practice points state that load control permits avoiding the crash phenomenon and that the programme avoids process disturbances. No result reports crash/PEM episodes, drop-outs or process disturbances. The causal 'leads to' wording rests on an uncontrolled cohort, and the Discussion says Fatigue and instability 'can be treated well' on the basis of small changes in motor scores (Cohen's d 0.2 to 0.6).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported crash/PEM incidence or process-disturbance data from the cohort.

quotes.text: erlaubt die Vermeidung eines Crash-Phänomens nach inadäquater Belastungssteuerung.
sowie der Vermeidung von Prozessstörungen in der Therapie.

second_reader.what_stands: The practice points assert that strain-controlled training avoids crash/PEM and that the management concept reduces process disturbances, but neither outcome was defined, measured or compared with a control. These claims rest on the introduction's rationale and on the Tab. 3 time intervals, which do not measure disturbances.

issues.title: Discussion says secondary psychosomatic symptoms were reduced; Phase 1 data show 11 to 19 patients (-72%)
issues.explanation: Table 4 and the Results text show secondary psychosomatic symptoms getting worse in Phase 1, with 8 more patients affected overall and 10 more among women. The Discussion lists them among the symptoms that 'could be reduced' without saying this applies only after the uncontrolled Phase 2 in 19 patients. A reader of the Discussion would not learn that one of six headline symptoms worsened.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Discussion sentence stating that the reduction refers only to Phase 2 and that Phase 1 showed worsening.

quotes.text: „sekundäre psychosomatische Symptome“ sowie „Schmerzen“ reduziert werden konnten
Verschlechterung der „sekundären psychosomatischen Symptomen“ um rd. 72 %.

issues.title: Sensorimotor instability improvement: Table 4 prints 53% for 44 of 78, but 44/78 = 56%
issues.explanation: The Results text says 56% and Table 4 says 53% for the same cohort and symptom. The printed counts (78 at baseline, 34 at evaluation, 44 improved) give 56.4%, so the table percentage is wrong. The accompanying '34 (47 %)' also does not equal 34/78 (43.6%). The error slightly understates the benefit and does not change the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator (about 83 patients) stated in the paper for this symptom.

quotes.text: „sensomotorische Instabilität“ um rd. 56 %

script.explanation: 44/78 = 56.41%, but the paper prints 53, outside the rounding interval [52.50, 54.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 83.0 rather than 78.

issues.title: Abstract claims men did better because of a faster start; no sex test, and median wait is 7 days in both
issues.explanation: The claim that men achieved more positive results through a faster start of training rests on side-by-side subgroup percentages in cohorts of 37 and 41, mostly with a handful of patients per cell. There is no interaction or between-sex test, no adjustment for age or severity, and the two sexes have the same median interval to therapy start. The Results themselves say there were no strong sex-specific differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal sex-by-outcome comparison that supports the effect, controlling for baseline severity and wait time.

quotes.text: Männer erzielten durch einen schnelleren Start der Trainingstherapie positivere Ergebnisse
Es gab keine starken geschlechtsspezifischen Schwankungen.

issues.title: No trial registry entry or protocol cited for a self-described interventional study
issues.explanation: Only ethics approvals are given. Without a registered plan, the choice of the six symptom outcomes and five motor parameters and the way 'improvement' is calculated cannot be checked against a prespecification. This is a transparency gap, not a demonstrated error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol with dates before data collection.

quotes.text: Das umgesetzte Studiendesign sowie das eingesetzte computergesteuerte Trainingssystem wurden von der Ethikkommission der TU Dresden genehmigt

10.1007/s00392-023-02300-6.headline_claim: Exercise is safe and improves maximal exercise capacity in post-COVID patients, while fatigue and quality of life improve over time irrespective of allocation.
10.1007/s00392-023-02300-6.overall: The physiological finding that supervised training raises VO2peak and oxygen pulse versus usual care is supported by the reported between-group tests, though in an open-label trial with only 44 of 57 randomized participants appearing in the analyses and no ITT. Claims of strength improvement versus control, of safety, and of MFI-20 benefit at follow-up go beyond what the reported tests show. The null fatigue result is of unknown power given the unreported sample size calculation.

primary_outcome.name: Subjective improvement in perceived fatigue (MFI-20) in at least 2 of 5 categories at follow-up

issues.title: 57 randomized but Table 1 and analyses cover 22+22=44; 13 (23%) unaccounted for in text
issues.explanation: The text states 57 patients were randomized, but Table 1 lists 22 per arm (44). No text or table explains the 13 missing participants, and the analyses appear confined to 44 without an ITT analysis. The CONSORT figure may explain it, but the text and Table 1 omit this, and baseline characteristics of all randomized participants are not shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Fig. 1 showing 13 post-randomization withdrawals/exclusions with reasons, and a statement that analyses are per-protocol or ITT with those numbers.

quotes.text: 57 patients with persisting symptoms post-COVID infection consented to participation and were randomized.
The mean age was 42.7 ± 13.4 years and 61% ( N = 27) were females.

script.explanation: The 57 randomized vs 22+22 in Table 1 does not reconcile: the arms of 'randomized' sum to 44, but the stage reports n=57 -- 13 participant(s) appear or vanish between the total and its own breakdown.

second_reader.what_stands: In the text and tables there is a real gap: 57 are reported as randomized, but Table 1, the percentages and the group sizes all refer to 22 + 22 = 44, and no passage in the extracted text explains the 13 (22.8%) difference or defines an ITT or completers analysis. Whether the paper as published leaves them unaccounted for cannot be settled here, because the CONSORT diagram (Fig. 1) is an image that could not be read and may give the numbers and reasons.

issues.title: Discussion says MFI-20 'improved more' in exercise group at follow-up; Results show no between-group difference
issues.explanation: The Discussion claims that MFI-20 improved more in the exercise group than controls in follow-up. The Results report no significant between-group differences in any questionnaire at 3 months, and the only MFI-20 finding is a within-group change in the exercise arm between 3 and 6 months. The statement is unsupported by a between-group test and conflicts with the abstract and the paper's final conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test of MFI-20 change at 3 or 6 months showing a significant difference favouring exercise.
