issues.title: Table 1: male total 23 vs 17 from arm counts (9+8); sham occupation 18 printed as 58.8% (30 gives 60.0%)
issues.explanation: The male counts in the two arms (9 and 8) add to 17, but the Total column prints 23, even though its percentage (28.3%) corresponds to 17 of 60. Separately, 18 active-employment participants in the sham arm is printed as 58.8%, which no integer denominator near 30 reproduces. These are baseline-table errors that affect no efficacy result, but they show the table was not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or dataset showing 17 males in total and 18 sham employed participants with a different denominator (for example missing occupation data).

quotes.location: Table 1, Occupation (Active employment) row, sham column

script.explanation: 18/30 = 60.00%, but the paper prints 58.8, outside the rounding interval [58.75, 58.90]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 30.6 rather than 30.

issues.title: Table 3 FDT Reading: p = 0.96 printed beside effect size 0.05 (0-0.21); text says all other ps > 0.19
issues.explanation: Other rows pair small effect sizes with large p-values (ES 0.03 with p = 0.219; ES 0 with p = 0.669). FDT Reading prints an effect size of 0.05 with a CI up to 0.21, which at about 52 error df corresponds to a p near 0.1, not 0.96. Either the p-value is mistyped, in which case the text's 'ps > 0.19' is also wrong, or the effect size is.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Author confirmation that p = 0.96 is correct and that the effect size is a rounding or model-specific artefact.

quotes.location: Table 3, Speed of processing (FDT) Reading row, sham tDCS + CT

quotes.text: No other group × time interactions were identified ( p s > 0.19)

issues.title: Analysis population not defined: 52 of 60 finished; endpoint data from 26 per arm, no ITT or sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Eight randomized participants lack endpoint data, and the paper does not state whether the model includes everyone randomized or how missingness was handled. A mixed model with baseline data from all 60 is a reasonable approach, but no sensitivity analysis or ITT statement is given. With 13% balanced attrition the effect on the findings is probably small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that all randomized participants with any data were analysed under the mixed model, with results unchanged under multiple imputation.

quotes.text: Sixty eligible participants were randomized into active tDCS + CT or sham tDCS + CT, and 52 finished the study (Fig. 1).

10.1016/j.cgh.2024.06.004.headline_claim: FMT is an effective and safe treatment for post-COVID insomnia and anxiety, improving insomnia remission, sleep quality and daytime sleepiness.
10.1016/j.cgh.2024.06.004.overall: The preference-allocated, open-label pilot gives a suggestive signal (remission 37.9% vs 10.0%, unadjusted OR 5.5), but the conclusion that FMT is effective and safe goes beyond what this design can show. A misprinted between-group ISI difference (-8.379, equal to its own CI limit) and an unlabelled SE in the text are reporting slips that do not change the binary primary result. Treat the findings as hypothesis-generating pending a blinded, sham-controlled trial.

primary_outcome.name: Insomnia remission (ISI from ≥8 to <8) at week 12

issues.title: Preference-based allocation with unadjusted OR 5.5; baseline months since diagnosis differ (8.6 vs 11.3, P=.025)
issues.explanation: Patients chose their own arm, so the control group cannot be assumed to be exchangeable with the FMT group. Table 1 shows a baseline difference in time since COVID-19 diagnosis (P = .025), although the text calls the groups 'comparable'. The authors report a stepwise logistic model but give no adjusted OR, and it was built on only 14 remitters. The 5.5 OR is therefore only suggestive of a treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported adjusted OR from a pre-specified model that stays large and significant, together with evidence that preference was unrelated to prognosis.

quotes.text: the group allocation was based on patient preference
Baseline characteristics of patients were comparable between the FMT and control groups
Months after initial COVID-19 diagnosis

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation was by patient preference, the 5.5 odds ratio is unadjusted (it equals the odds ratio from the raw 2×2 counts), and months since diagnosis differ (8.6 vs 11.3, P = .025), which I reproduced. The authors disclose this and report that duration was not significant in a stepwise model, but that model cannot remove selection bias from preference-based allocation or from unmeasured factors, and 'comparable' overstates the balance.

issues.title: Open-label, no-sham trial with a self-reported ISI threshold as the primary outcome
issues.explanation: Participants who undergo four endoscopic infusions know they are being treated, and the primary outcome is a self-completed questionnaire. Expectation and placebo effects could therefore produce part or all of the improvement. The no-treatment control cannot separate these from a true biological effect, so the efficacy claim is weaker than the 38% vs 10% remission difference suggests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded or sham-controlled comparison, or objective sleep measures (polysomnography or actigraphy) showing the same benefit.

quotes.text: Both the investigators and the subjects were not blinded
The primary outcome was insomnia remission defined as a change in ISI

second_reader.what_stands: The trial is open-label with no sham or placebo and a no-treatment control, and its primary outcome is a self-reported ISI threshold, so expectation effects could inflate the apparent benefit. The authors acknowledge this and recommend a blinded trial with objective measures.

issues.title: Final conclusion says the pilot 'demonstrates' FMT is effective and safe from 59 non-randomised, unblinded patients
issues.explanation: The data come from a preference-allocated, open-label pilot with 59 analysed patients, one of whom withdrew after allocation. Safety rests on 1 adverse event in 29 FMT patients over 12 weeks, which cannot exclude rarer harms. 'Demonstrate' overstates what the design supports; the evidence is hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The conclusion being worded as preliminary or hypothesis-generating, or a larger controlled safety dataset.

quotes.text: In conclusion, our study is the first to demonstrate that FMT could be an effective and safe treatment for post-COVID insomnia and anxiety.
One subject in the FMT group had upper respiratory infection during the study period

second_reader.what_stands: The concluding sentence 'is the first to demonstrate that FMT could be an effective and safe treatment' uses a stronger verb than a 59-patient, non-randomised, unblinded pilot supports, and the safety claim rests on one event in about 30 patients over 12 weeks. The statement is hedged ('could be') and elsewhere qualified by the limitations and calls for further trials, so it is overstated rather than flatly unqualified.

issues.title: Week-12 between-group ISI difference printed as -8.379, identical to its CI lower limit (-8.379 to -2.986)
issues.explanation: A point estimate cannot equal the lower bound of its own 95% CI. The CI midpoint implies a difference near -5.7, not -8.4. The printed -8.379 is probably a misprint, and it overstates the between-group ISI difference by about 2.7 points. The binary primary outcome and its OR are unaffected, but the continuous between-group effect is misreported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 2D or the raw data showing a between-group difference of -8.379 with a CI that was misprinted instead.

quotes.text: mean difference, –8.379; 95% CI, –8.379 to –2.986

script.explanation: the estimate -8.379 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [-8.379, -2.986] (expected about -5.6825) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

issues.title: Registered primary is 'change in insomnia severity'; paper's primary is ISI remission (<8)
issues.explanation: The registry primary outcome is a change in insomnia severity at 12 weeks, whereas the paper makes a dichotomised remission threshold the primary endpoint. The continuous ISI results are also reported, so nothing was hidden, but the paper does not say why the endpoint was dichotomised. This cannot be settled without the registry history, and the effect on the conclusion is modest.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing that remission was the primary outcome at registration, or a protocol stating this.

quotes.text: The primary outcome was insomnia remission defined as a change in ISI

issues.title: Anxiety and sleepiness conclusions rest on secondary outcomes with no stated between-group correction
issues.explanation: The conclusion says FMT 'could significantly alleviate insomnia and anxiety' and 'reduce daytime sleepiness'. Those are secondary outcomes tested between groups with no stated multiplicity control, and the open-label design applies to them as well. The PSQI and ESS P values are small enough that correction alone may not matter, but the GAD-7 between-group P is not reported in the text, so the anxiety claim is hard to appraise.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchical testing plan, or between-group GAD-7 and ESS P values that survive a Bonferroni or Holm correction.

quotes.text: Within-group changes in symptom scores across time were evaluated using repeated measures analysis of variance with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.
quotes.location: Methods, Sample Size Estimation and Statistical Analysis

quotes.text: FMT could significantly alleviate insomnia and anxiety, improve sleep quality and reduce daytime sleepiness.

issues.title: Results text gives baseline ISI as 17.1 ± 0.9, Table 1 gives ± 4.8; the 0.9 looks like an unlabelled SE
issues.explanation: The text prints the FMT group's baseline ISI as 17.1 ± 0.9, while Table 1 (mean ± SD) prints 17.1 ± 4.8. The text value matches the standard error (4.8/√29 ≈ 0.89), so the two are probably the same data on different scales. The text does not say so, and a reader would take 0.9 as an SD and think the baseline spread was far narrower than it was. The effect is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that the Results-text values are SEs, or evidence that the text SDs were derived from a different analysis set.

quotes.text: significantly improved from 17.1 ± 0.9 at baseline to 8.5 ± 1.0 at week 12

10.1016/j.clinme.2024.100251.headline_claim: Sulphur thermal water inhalations produced objective and subjective improvements, and reduced inflammatory markers, in long-COVID patients compared with placebo distilled-water inhalations, and the authors state this demonstrates clinical efficacy.
10.1016/j.clinme.2024.100251.overall: The headline conclusion that STW inhalation demonstrated clinical efficacy and safety is not supported by a 15-per-arm pilot that reports mainly within-arm changes, with retrospective registration, a partly unblinded delivery chain and uncorrected multiple testing. Several printed numbers (Table 5 percentages, SDW 6MWT changes, reinfection counts, IL-1beta significance) are internally inconsistent, though most affect single results rather than the whole. The findings are best read as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Spirometric/PFT changes and cardiopulmonary response to exertion (6MWT, SpO2, Borg) at Day 1, 14 and 90 (between-group comparison); the paper's stated aim is efficacy on pulmonary functionality

primary_outcomes.measure: To determine whether Sulfurous Thermal water (STW) inhalations may have effects on post covid-pulmonary sequelae assessing changes in pulmonar functionality through spirometric parameters.
To determine whether Sulfurous Thermal water (STW) inhalations may have effects on post covid-pulmonary sequelae assessing changes in pulmonar functionality through spirometric parameters.

To determine whether Sulfurous Thermal water (STW) inhalations can improve the cardiopulmonary response to physical exertion measured as SpO2, Heart rate, Borg score and traversed meters in patients affected by long COVID

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from within-arm changes; no between-group effect estimates for 6MWT, SGRQ, PFT or cytokines
issues.explanation: The key results are significance of change from baseline within the STW arm, set against a placebo arm described as 'not significant'. The Methods mention a between-group comparison, but no between-group difference or test is reported for the main outcomes, even though the registered primary outcomes are between-group. With only 15 per arm and baseline imbalance, a within-arm significant change does not show that STW beats distilled water. The conclusion of treatment efficacy is therefore not supported by the analysis shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table of between-group differences (or group-by-time interaction tests, or ANCOVA adjusted for baseline) showing significant STW-SDW differences.

quotes.text: The scores obtained in the administered tests (6MWT, Borg score and SGRQ) at T0 showed a significant variation in the STW group, at T1 and T2.
In the present study, the effectiveness of sulphur thermal water inhalation has been observed in the STW group compared to the SDW group.
Collectively, the STW group was composed of older subjects with higher scores of SBQ-LC.

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy claims rest on within-STW changes over time (the Abstract's 'significant variation in the STW group') and on side-by-side percentage changes. No between-group effect estimates or tests are reported for 6MWT, Borg, SGRQ, PFT or cytokines, despite a stated between-group primary analysis. Baseline imbalances and non-zero SDW changes mean the descriptive contrast is not a valid test of treatment effect.

issues.title: 15-per-arm pilot, sized for feasibility, concludes 'clinical efficacy' of STW
issues.explanation: The sample size comes from a prevalence-precision calculation and a pilot rule of thumb, not from an effect-size power calculation. With 15 per arm, many outcomes, baseline imbalance and no between-group tests, the data are hypothesis-generating. The Conclusion nevertheless states that STW 'demonstrated its clinical efficacy' and recommends its use in long-COVID treatment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A confirmatory trial, or a pre-specified effect-size power calculation with between-group results meeting it.

quotes.text: a target of 30 participants in total was chosen to be randomised in a 1:1 ratio, in a sample size of 15 per group.
In our study, probably due to the small sample size, no significant associated factors were detected

H2 S-rich STW showed positive effects on different inflammatory markers that, alongside the aforementioned effects, demonstrated its clinical efficacy and suggests its application in long-COVID treatment.

second_reader.what_stands: A 15-per-arm pilot sized by feasibility rules, not by power for the primary outcomes, concludes that STW 'demonstrated its clinical efficacy'. This is stronger than a pilot with no reported between-group tests and mixed PFT results can support. The paper's own pilot framing and small-sample remark are not carried into the conclusion.

issues.title: 'Safe, even during pregnancy' rests on one pregnant participant who developed an obstructive pattern at T2
issues.explanation: The Conclusion states that STW inhalation is safe even in pregnancy. Only one pregnant participant was enrolled, in the active arm, and she is the one person in whom a new obstructive spirometry pattern appeared at follow-up. The paper does not examine that finding. One person cannot support a safety claim for pregnant women.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the T2 obstructive pattern was unrelated to treatment (e.g. gestational effect) and a larger pregnancy safety dataset.

quotes.text: Sulphur thermal water inhalation in people affected by respiratory sequelae following SARS-CoV-2 infection is a safe procedure, even during pregnancy
One obstructive pattern was only observed at T2 in an STW participant
quotes.location: Results, Effects of inhalations on pulmonary functionality test (PFT)

second_reader.what_stands: The 'safe, even during pregnancy' statement rests on a single pregnant participant, and that participant is the one with a new obstructive pattern at T2, which the paper does not discuss. The paper does not say the finding was treatment-related, and it reports no adverse events. One participant cannot establish safety in pregnancy.

issues.title: Ethics approval reference CAR 181/2024 for a study conducted May-October 2023; approval date not stated
issues.explanation: The paper dates data collection to May-October 2023, but the only ethics reference carries a 2024 identifier. If approval came after enrolment, participants may have been studied before ethical review. The paper does not say when approval was granted, so this is unresolved rather than shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An approval letter dated before May 2023, or a statement that the 2024 number is a later re-registration of an earlier approval.

quotes.text: The study was performed from May to October 2023 at the Acque Albule, Terme di Roma spa facility
The study was approved by the University Committee for Research (CAR), University of Rome Foro Italico (CAR 181/2024).
quotes.location: Ethics approval and consent to participate

issues.title: SDW 6MWT mean changes printed as +12.14 m and +1.42 m; printed means give +7.86 m and +2.86 m
issues.explanation: The placebo-group walk-distance changes printed in Table 3 and repeated in the Discussion do not match the placebo group means in the same table. The percentage changes do match the means, so the metre changes are the faulty figures. Overstating placebo improvement slightly understates the apparent STW advantage on a registered primary outcome. The total-column figures show a similar mismatch.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Participant-level 6MWT data showing mean individual changes of 12.14 and 1.42 m, which would require missing data not reported.

issues.title: Many outcomes and timepoints tested at p < 0.05 with no multiplicity control for clinical and biomarker results
issues.explanation: The Methods state only that p < 0.05 was significant, with no correction for the large number of comparisons across outcomes and times. The conclusions highlight the subset that reached significance. This weakens the secondary and exploratory findings, while the strongest effects may survive correction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of pre-specified primary comparisons with a hierarchical or corrected testing plan, or adjusted p-values for the key outcomes.

quotes.text: A p -value < 0.05 was considered significant.
Statistical analysis of the differences between groups was calculated using the Kruskal-Wallis test with FDR correction for multiple comparisons.

issues.title: Inhalation assistant was unblinded and participant masking was only an unreported pre-study odour check
issues.explanation: The person delivering the intervention knew the allocation, and participant blinding depends on an odour check whose method and results are not given. No assessment of whether participants guessed their arm is reported. This matters most for subjective outcomes (Borg, SGRQ) and effort-dependent 6MWT results, where expectation could favour STW.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data from a blinding questionnaire showing participants could not identify their arm beyond chance, or evidence that the assistant had no contact with outcome assessment.

quotes.text: Therefore, the inhalation assistant was unblinded to the treatment assigned but blinded to the medical condition of the participants.
any possible difference in perceived odour (sulphur vs water) during inhalation was assessed before starting the study

issues.title: Trial registered 2024-02-09, after the 2023-05-30 start; paper omits this and asserts no outcome changes
issues.explanation: According to the ClinicalTrials.gov record, NCT06294756 was first submitted about 8 months after the study started and is marked retrospective. The paper gives the registration number without a date and states that no outcomes were changed since their formulation, which cannot be verified against a prospective record. The registry's primary outcomes are spirometry and 6MWT/Borg/SpO2, whereas the abstract's headline emphasis falls on inflammatory markers and the microbiome. Outcome selection therefore cannot be shown to be pre-specified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A dated protocol or earlier registry version from before May 2023 showing the same primary outcomes.

quotes.text: The study was registered on Clinicaltrial.com with ID NCT06294756.
no changes to selection criteria, outcomes nor treatment protocol were made since their formulation

issues.title: Discussion cites one (placebo) reinfection; Table 2 lists 11 (4 STW, 7 SDW), likely pre-enrolment history
issues.explanation: The Discussion says only one placebo participant had a reinfection during the 3-month study, implying protection by STW. Table 2 and the Results report 4 reinfections in STW and 7 in SDW, which look like infection history. The two statements cannot both describe the trial period, and the Discussion figure has no supporting data in the paper. The sentence reads as a benefit claim that the tables do not show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table of on-trial reinfections showing exactly one event, in the SDW arm.

quotes.text: just one patient, undergoing placebo inhalations, presented a reinfection
four had reinfection although all participants were vaccinated
n participants reinfection 11 4 7

issues.title: IL-1beta fall at T1 called 'statistically decreased' in Discussion but reported as p = 0.12 in Results
issues.explanation: Results state the T1 decrease in IL-1beta was not significant (p = 0.12), while only IL-6 reached p < 0.05. The Discussion groups both cytokines as statistically decreased at T1 and calls this an immediate effect. The Discussion therefore overstates the early IL-1beta result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the IL-1beta T1 comparison reached significance, or that the Discussion sentence refers only to IL-6.

quotes.text: This decrease was also observed in IL-1 𝛽 cytokine expression but was not statistically significant ( p = 0.12).
quotes.location: Results, Effects of STW inhalations on long-COVID serum markers

quotes.text: In the STW group, the serum IL-6 and IL-1 𝛽 cytokine level was statistically decreased already at T1

issues.title: Table 5 percent changes contradict their own means: STW IL-1beta -51.14% and -24.78%, SDW hs-CRP -6.51%
issues.explanation: For STW IL-1beta, the printed T0 mean of 73.66 and T2 mean of 37.94 give -48.49%, which the text uses, but the table prints -51.14%. The T1 cell prints -24.78% where the means give -20.70%. For SDW hs-CRP at T2, 1.41 to 1.71 is a rise of about 21%, but the cell reads -6.51%, apparently copied from the STW column. The errors inflate the apparent IL-1beta fall and hide a placebo-group rise.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw individual-level data showing the mean of individual percent changes equals the printed values (unlikely to differ this much from the ratio of means).

issues.title: Baseline Actinobacteria mean 20.2% is below genus means nested in it (Corynebacterium 45% + Propionibacterium 12.4%)
issues.explanation: The text gives Actinobacteria at 20.2% and says Firmicutes dominated, yet reports Corynebacterium at 45% and Propionibacterium at 12.4%, both Actinobacteria. Genus abundances inside a phylum cannot exceed the phylum total from the same data. The microbiome description therefore cannot be taken at face value, though this is a secondary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that phylum and genus values come from different classifiers or sample subsets, or corrected values.

quotes.text: Both nasopharyngeal microbial communities were dominated by the Firmicutes phylum (34.7% ± 8.4%), followed by Proteobacteria (26.1% ± 11.7%) and Actinobacteria (20.2% ± 10.5%).
quotes.location: Results, Effect of STW on nasal microbiome

quotes.text: At the genus level, Corynebacterium (45% ± 11.4%) and Staphylococcus (14% ± 8.2%) were the most abundant genera
quotes.location: Results, Effect of STW on nasal microbiome

issues.title: Table 2 shows enrolled participants outside stated criteria: a positive T0 swab and 60 days since negativisation (>4 months required)
issues.explanation: Inclusion required a negative SARS-CoV-2 swab at enrolment and long-COVID lasting more than 4 months since negativisation. Table 2 lists one SDW participant positive at T0 and a minimum of 60 days since negativisation in the STW arm and total sample. These are small departures, but they show eligibility was not applied as written. They also blur the definition of the studied population.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the criteria were counted from a different date (e.g. symptom onset), or a correction of the Table 2 cells.

quotes.text: a negative swab for SARS-CoV-2 infection at enrolment (Visit 1, T0)
Positive to SARS-CoV-2 1 0 1 (T0)
lasting more than 4 months since swab negativisation

issues.title: Baseline microbiome described as 'no different' between arms while ANOSIM reports p = 0.001
issues.explanation: The Results say the nasopharyngeal community structure did not differ between STW and SDW at T0, yet the quoted test gives p = 0.001. Either the statement or the p-value is wrong. If the arms did differ at baseline, the later between-arm microbiome contrasts (e.g. higher Shannon index in STW, p = 0.001) are harder to attribute to treatment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected p-value above 0.05 or a clarification that the test result was non-significant.

quotes.text: was no different between STW and SDW participants at T0
quotes.location: Results, Effect of STW on nasal microbiome

issues.title: Total mean age 52.70 does not equal the average of the equal-sized arm means (57.06, 47.92 -> 52.49)
issues.explanation: Both arms have 15 participants, so the pooled mean age should be 52.49, not the printed 52.70. The 0.21-year gap exceeds rounding. It has no effect on any outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Different group sizes in the age calculation, or corrected means.

quotes.text: with a mean age of 52.7 ± 13.35 years
The average of STW participants was 57.06 ± 11.82 years
average age 47.92 ± 13.31 years

issues.title: Text says all PFT parameters were lower in STW at baseline; IC is higher in STW (102.43 vs 101.35)
issues.explanation: The Results say every PFT parameter had lower baseline means in the STW group. Table 4 shows IC at T0 of 102.43 in STW against 101.35 in SDW. The overall point (STW lung function lower at baseline) mostly holds, so this is a minor wording error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected IC value in Table 4, or a rewording of the sentence.

quotes.text: All PFT parameters had lower mean values in STW sample at baseline
quotes.location: Results, Effects of inhalations on pulmonary functionality test (PFT)

10.1016/j.clinph.2022.10.017.headline_claim: Eight weeks of oral PEA-LUT restores GABAB-ergic intracortical inhibition (LICI) and LTP-like cortical plasticity in long COVID patients.
10.1016/j.clinph.2022.10.017.overall: The main finding, a larger LICI change in the PEA-LUT arm than in placebo, is reported with a modest interaction (p = 0.034) in a small trial of 34 completers, with an undescribed pseudorandomized allocation and retrospective registration. The headline wording ('normalizes', 'restores', 'demonstrates') goes beyond what a no-healthy-control, small, unadjusted design supports, and the null cognitive results are missing from the abstract. The remaining flags are minor text inconsistencies that do not change the results.

primary_outcome.name: LICI at ISI 100 ms (% of test MEP amplitude), PRE vs POST

primary_outcomes.measure: changes in % of test amplitude in LICI 100
primary_outcomes.time_frame: LICI 100 was assessed two times, at enrollment and after 8 weeks of treatment duration

issues.title: Allocation 'pseudorandomized' with balancing on covariates, undescribed; paper still calls it an RCT
issues.explanation: The paper says allocation was centralized and pseudorandomized with balancing on age, sex, education and illness duration, but gives no method and no allocation concealment. A non-random or predictable allocation can bias comparisons, and the arms still differ by about 5 years in mean age. The 'randomized, double-blind' framing and the causal conclusion are therefore less firm than presented.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of a concealed, unpredictable allocation sequence such as minimisation with a random element.

quotes.text: Group allocation was centralized and occurred in a pseudorandomized manner taking into account a balance of age, gender, education, and duration of illness (Table 1).
This randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigated the neurophysiological and cognitive impact of PEA-LUT administration

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes allocation only as 'pseudorandomized' with balancing on four covariates, gives no method, sequence generation or concealment details, and still labels the study a randomized controlled trial and 'double-blind'. The label and the method description are not reconciled in the text; whether allocation was truly random cannot be judged from the paper.

issues.title: No sample-size justification; 17 per arm; primary interaction p = 0.034; conclusion says 'demonstrates'
issues.explanation: No power calculation is reported and each arm has 17 completers. The primary LICI treatment-by-time interaction is modest (F = 4.92, p = 0.034), yet the closing statement says the RCT 'demonstrates' enhancement of GABAB neurotransmission and plasticity. This language is stronger than a small unplanned-size study supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation showing adequate power for the LICI effect.

quotes.text: Patients were assigned to one of two study groups (n = 17 each)
In conclusion, the present RCT demonstrates that PEA-LUT is able to enhance GABAB-ergic neurotransmission and LTP-like cortical plasticity in long Covid patients.

second_reader.what_stands: There is no sample-size justification; the study analysed 17 per arm, the primary interaction is p = 0.034, and the final sentence says the RCT 'demonstrates' the effect without caveat. The p values themselves are internally consistent, but the strength of the wording exceeds what a single small trial with a modest primary p value and no stated multiplicity handling supports.

issues.title: Title/abstract say 'normalizes'/'restore' without a healthy comparator; null cognitive results omitted
issues.explanation: Normalisation or restoration needs a reference group measured in the same study, which this trial lacks. The LICI increase is shown relative to placebo, not to normal values. The null results on MoCA and FAB are disclosed only in the Discussion, while the title, highlights and abstract present an unqualified benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A healthy-control group measured in the same study showing post-treatment values within the normal range.

quotes.text: Co-ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide/luteolin normalizes GABAB-ergic activity and cortical plasticity in long COVID-19 syndrome
Eight weeks of treatment with PEA-LUT restore GABAB activity and cortical plasticity in long Covid patients.
While we found that PEA-LUT had a beneficial impact on altered motor cortex physiology, we did not observe significant changes in the chosen cognitive measures.

second_reader.what_stands: The title and abstract use 'normalizes' and 'restore' although the study has no healthy comparator and reports no normative values, so normalisation is not demonstrated within this paper. The null cognitive results are not omitted from the paper as a whole (they appear in Results and Discussion with a ceiling-effect explanation) but are absent from the abstract, title and highlights.

issues.title: LTP-like plasticity claim relies on 2 of 4 uncorrected time-point interactions (p = 0.003, 0.025)
issues.explanation: Secondary outcomes (SAI, four LTP time points, MoCA, FAB) were tested at p < 0.05 without any stated correction across outcomes or time points. The plasticity claim rests on T1 and T10 reaching significance, with T10 near the threshold. This weakens the plasticity part of the conclusion but not the primary LICI result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified single plasticity endpoint or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis still significant.

quotes.text: Repeated measures ANOVA for MEP amplitude modulation in the LTP-like cortical plasticity test revealed a significant interaction (treatment -time) 1 and 10 minutes following iTBS.
Patients treated with PEA-LUT but not with PLACEBO showed a significant increase of LICI and LTP-like cortical plasticity.

issues.title: Retrospective registration: study start 16 Aug 2021, registered April 2022 (registry first submitted 30 Mar 2022)
issues.explanation: The trial was registered about seven to eight months after it started and after recruitment began, so prespecification of outcomes and analysis cannot be confirmed. The registered primary outcome matches the paper, which reduces but does not remove the concern. The paper's registration date also differs slightly from the registry's first-submission date.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version dated before August 2021 with the same outcomes.

quotes.text: The study was registered with clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05311852) on April 5, 2022 with ''Actual Study Start Date' August 16, 2021

issues.title: 5 of 39 enrolled withdrew after baseline; only 34 completers analysed, arm and reasons not given
issues.explanation: Analyses include completers only and no intention-to-treat analysis is given. The paper does not report which arm the five withdrawals came from or why, so differential dropout cannot be excluded. With 17 per arm, even a few missing patients matter.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing arm and reason for the 5 withdrawals, or an ITT sensitivity analysis.

quotes.text: Thirty-four patients were studied (five patients withdrew from the study after pre-intervention assessment).
A total of 34 post COVID-19 patients completed the evaluation sessions.

issues.title: Two LICI 'PRE' test MEP sentences give different values (0.93/0.86 vs 0.90/0.82); one is likely a mislabelled POST
issues.explanation: The Results state PRE test MEP amplitudes for LICI twice with different values for both groups. The pattern of the SAI paragraph suggests the second sentence was meant to be POST. As printed, a reader cannot tell which baseline value is correct, and no LICI POST test amplitude is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected text labelling the second sentence as POST.

quotes.text: In LICI protocol performed at PRE, mean test MEP amplitude for the PEA-LUT group and for the PLACEBO group were 0.93 ± 0.42 mV and 0.86 ± 0.43 mV, respectively.
In LICI protocol performed at PRE, mean test MEP amplitude for the PEA-LUT group and for the PLACEBO group were 0.90 ± 0.43 and 0.82 ± 0.43, respectively.

issues.title: iTBS frequencies swapped: Methods 50 Hz pulses/5 Hz bursts; Discussion 5 Hz bursts at 50 Hz theta
issues.explanation: The Methods describe 3 pulses at 50 Hz repeated at 5 Hz. The Discussion calls the stimulation 'high-frequency bursts (5 Hz) at theta frequencies (50 Hz)', which reverses the two frequencies. Theta is about 5 Hz, so the Discussion is the wrong one. This does not affect results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the two passages disagree in the paper itself.

quotes.text: This iTBS protocol consisted of 3 TMS pulses at 50 Hz, repeated every 200 ms (5 Hz) for 2 s.
i.e., a stimulation with high-frequency bursts (5 Hz) at theta frequencies (50 Hz)

issues.title: FSS described as 9 items scored 1-7 but score range given as 7-63 (should be 9-63)
issues.explanation: With nine items each scored 1 to 7, the minimum total is 9 and the maximum 63. The paper gives the minimum as 7. This is a descriptive slip; the inclusion cut-off of FSS > 36 is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of a scoring convention that gives a minimum of 7 for nine items.

quotes.text: FSS is a self-administered 9-item questionnaire
FSS sum score ranges from 7 to 63

10.1016/j.clinsp.2025.100614.headline_claim: Twelve weeks of supervised combined aerobic and strength training is an efficient model for improving fitness, fatigue and dyspnea in patients recovering from mild to moderate COVID-19.
10.1016/j.clinsp.2025.100614.overall: The headline claim that the supervised combined training programme is highly effective is not supported by the design: the three arms did not differ significantly on the main outcomes, and the conclusions rest on within-group change, completers only, with an unmatched control. The only clear between-group signal is on a subjective dyspnea scale. Numerical inconsistencies (8 vs 12 weeks, table sums, pooled weight change, isokinetic claims) are individually minor but add to the picture of an unreliable report.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; cardiorespiratory and submaximal fitness variables (VO2peak, speed at POC/VT1/VT2, test duration) are analysed together

issues.title: Efficacy concluded from within-group change; no significant between-group differences on main fitness outcomes
issues.explanation: Pre/post change in a group that is being trained cannot separate the programme from familiarisation with the tests, time, or other changes. A control arm exists but no between-group comparison was significant for the main outcomes, so the data do not show that training caused the improvement. Only the dyspnea scale shows a trained vs control difference, and that is a pooled comparison with a subjective measure in unblinded participants.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified between-group (group x time) interaction analysis showing significant effects of training on the main fitness outcomes versus control.

quotes.text: The three groups did not have significant statistical differences when compared to each other, but there was significant intragroup improvement in the analyzed variables.
The statistical significance of the dependent variables in G1 and G3 (trained) indicates that the difference between the groups is unlikely to have occurred at random.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does conclude efficacy ('efficient training model', 'justified the engagement') from within-group pre/post changes while stating that between-group differences on the main fitness, body-composition, spirometry and isokinetic outcomes were not significant. The Discussion also treats within-group significance as if it showed a difference between groups, which does not follow. The dyspnea comparison of trained groups vs G2 is a real exception, but it is not a main fitness outcome.

issues.title: Discussion claims 'highly effective' and reduced hospital admissions; neither is supported by the data
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the results demonstrate high effectiveness, while the paper's own main result is that between-group differences were not significant. It also states that training reduces hospital admissions and healthcare burden, which was not measured in a sample of non-hospitalised employees. Template-like text further suggests the closing sections were not tied to the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data on hospital admissions or resource use, or a significant between-group effect on the prespecified main outcomes.

quotes.text: The present results demonstrate that a concurrent exercise program combining aerobic and strength activities is highly effective in improving the physical fitness of patients recovering from COVID-19.
Physical training reduces the need for hospital admissions for patients and reduces the burden on the healthcare system and optimizes the medical resources used.

second_reader.what_stands: The hospital-admission claim has no supporting data in the paper, because no hospitalization or health-system outcome was measured and participants were non-hospitalized by design. 'Highly effective' is stronger than the results allow: it is supported only by within-group changes in some submaximal and exercise-tolerance measures and by the dyspnea contrast against G2, while most between-group comparisons were not significant.

issues.title: 24% loss of patients, completers-only analysis, and no flow diagram or per-arm attrition
issues.explanation: The paper states that 24% of patients were lost but gives no participant flow, no number randomised per arm and no reasons for loss. Exclusion criteria remove anyone who missed sessions or the re-evaluation, so the analysed 69 are probably completers. The 24% loss is not inconsistent with 69 analysed, but the within-group improvements apply only to patients who completed the programme and could be biased upward.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CONSORT flow diagram with arm-wise losses balanced across arms, or an intention-to-treat analysis giving similar results.

quotes.text: During the research process, the authors had a loss of 24 % of patients.
(ii) Missing four consecutive training sessions, and (iii) Failure to attend the reevaluation tests.

issues.title: Control arm differs from trained arms in nutrition guidance and supervision, and its exercise was unmeasured
issues.explanation: G2 received no nutritional guidance and no supervision and was told to train alone, whereas G1 and G3 received supervision and nutrition support. Any trained-vs-control difference therefore cannot be assigned to combined training alone. Because G2's own exercise was not recorded, the contrast is between supervised training and an unknown level of self-directed activity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data on G2 exercise volume and a design that gave all arms the same nutrition advice.

quotes.text: instructed to train outside the hospital and did not receive nutritional guidance

issues.title: Repeat CPX test timing stated as eight weeks in one place and 12 weeks elsewhere
issues.explanation: The CPX section says the identical protocol was repeated after eight weeks of supervised training. The training-design section, abstract and objective say the two CPX sessions were 12 weeks apart. The reader cannot tell what follow-up interval the main cardiorespiratory results reflect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol statement showing the repeat CPX was at eight weeks as a planned interim test with a separate 12-week test.

quotes.text: after  eight  weeks  of  supervised  physical training
separated by a period of 12-weeks

issues.title: Isokinetic strength: Results find no significant change; Discussion reports 8-12% gains as real
issues.explanation: The Results state no significant isokinetic differences within or between groups. The Discussion then treats 12% and 8% increases in peak torque/weight, and 12% and 10% in total work, as strength gains with a physiological explanation, contrasted with an unchanged control. The significant strength evidence is the training load progression, which is not the isokinetic measure. The abstract's claim of improved muscular fitness leans on the weaker evidence here.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An isokinetic table showing significant within-group change in G1/G3, or wording in the Discussion that clearly flags these percentages as non-significant trends.

quotes.text: In the isokinetic assessment, no statistical differences (p ≥ 0.05) were found between and within groups between the tests performed.
increased strength by 12 % and 8 %, respectively

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; 21 to 26 per arm, null between-group results uninformative
issues.explanation: The paper reports no power calculation, and arms of 21 to 26 can miss moderate differences. The null between-group results therefore cannot be read as no difference. The authors do acknowledge the small sample in their limitations section, but that disclosure sits beside confident efficacy statements elsewhere.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation in the registered protocol showing adequate power for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: A limitation of the present study was the use of a small sample, which could generate less precision in the estimates

issues.title: Table 1 G3 sex counts (7 men + 16 women = 23) exceed the stated G3 total of 22
issues.explanation: The two sex categories are mutually exclusive, yet the G3 column sums to 23 while the header gives n = 22. The men's percentage (27%) does not match 7/22 either, so the men's count is probably a typo for 6. This is a small reporting slip that does not affect any outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that one G3 participant was counted in both sex categories, or a corrected table with 6 men.

issues.title: Unfilled drafting placeholder left in the Discussion mechanism sentence
issues.explanation: The Discussion contains the text '(explain the physiological mechanisms, e.g., ...)' in place of an actual explanation. This shows that the mechanistic statements around it were not written or checked against the data, and the mechanisms suggested were not measured in the study.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable: the text is printed in the paper.

quotes.text: (explain the physiological mechanisms, e.g., increased mitochondrial

issues.title: Sample text counts differ from Table 1 sums: diabetes 7 vs 6, and headache, smell and taste off by one
issues.explanation: The Sample paragraph reports 7 participants with diabetes, but the Table 1 group counts add up to 6. Symptom counts in the text (headache 30, smell 32, taste 34) also differ by one from the table sums (31, 31, 33). These off-by-one discrepancies are minor and do not affect any outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that one participant had diabetes but was missed from the table, or a corrected table showing 7.

quotes.text: However, 10 % (n = 7) had diabetes

issues.title: Pooled weight change of 0.5 kg does not follow from 2 kg loss in G1/G3 and none in G2
issues.explanation: The Discussion says G1 and G3 lost about 2 kg and G2 none, then says the whole sample lost 0.5 kg. A group-size weighted average of those figures is about 1.4 kg, so the numbers do not fit. The lean mass figures show a smaller version of the same mismatch. The body composition results were non-significant, so the conclusion is little affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Group-level mean weight changes (with n) showing a pooled loss of about 0.5 kg, for example a much smaller G1 or G3 change than 2 kg.

quotes.text: When we analyze the complete sample, the loss drops to 0.5 kg.
a decrease in body weight of an average of 2 kg after intervention

issues.title: Many outcomes and timepoints tested at alpha 0.05 without cross-outcome correction
issues.explanation: Dozens of variables across CPX transition points, spirometry, isokinetic, load and dyspnea measures were tested without a stated primary outcome or correction across outcomes. Most of the highlighted significant results have very small p-values and would likely survive correction, so the effect on conclusions is small, but borderline results such as p = 0.01 are vulnerable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome, or Bonferroni/Holm adjusted p-values for the secondary outcomes that remain significant.

quotes.text: was considered at α < 0.05

10.1016/j.clnesp.2021.08.031.headline_claim: Apportal (a multi-nutrient supplement) reduces chronic fatigue and improves quality of life and health status in subjects with persistent fatigue after SARS-CoV-2 negativity.
10.1016/j.clnesp.2021.08.031.overall: The paper shows that fatigue and quality-of-life scores improved over 28 days in a single uncontrolled cohort, but cannot show that the supplement caused this. The causal and 'effective in almost all subjects' conclusions are not supported, and the improvement-direction wording in the headline FACIT percentages is contradictory. The study is best treated as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: FACIT-Fatigue total score change (proportion improving by at least 5 units is the stated sample-size target; RTE trend across T0, T1, T2 reported for FACIT-Fatigue)

issues.title: Causal efficacy claimed ('can reduce chronic fatigue', 'effective in almost all') from a single-arm uncontrolled study
issues.explanation: All 201 participants received Apportal and were compared only with their own baseline over 28 days, with no control group, blinding or between-group test. Spontaneous post-Covid recovery, regression to the mean, expectation effects and self-reported questionnaires cannot be separated from any supplement effect. Yet the abstract says the product 'can reduce chronic fatigue', the discussion attributes improvement to the supplement, and the conclusions claim it is effective in 'almost all subjects (90.05%)', 'regardless of gender, age, and severity of the previous disease' (no severity analysis is shown) and is 'the first evidence to offer a solution'. The within-person time trends (Wald p < 0.0001) show change over time, not a treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical matched control group showing slower recovery of fatigue scores over the same period.

quotes.text: the study lacks a control group that will clarify if the recovery occurs in the same way and at the same time even without supplementation
This study shows that Apportal ® can reduce chronic fatigue and improve quality of life and health status
appears to be effective in almost all subjects (90.05%), regardless of gender, age, and severity of the previous disease

second_reader.what_stands: The paper makes causal efficacy claims ('can reduce chronic fatigue', 'demonstration', 'effective in almost all subjects (90.05%)') from a single-arm, open-label study with self-reported outcomes and no control group. The authors acknowledge the missing control group in Limitations, but the abstract and conclusions do not carry that caveat, and the 90.05% figure is only the share with a rise of at least 1 FACIT point, which cannot be attributed to the supplement.

issues.title: FACIT-Fatigue responder counts defined as a score 'reduction', contradicting higher-is-better scale
issues.explanation: Methods say a higher FACIT-Fatigue score means less fatigue, and the sample-size section defines recovery as an increase of at least 5 units. Results 3.2 and 3.4 instead define improvement as a score reduction of at least 1, 5 or 10 units. If the counts truly follow the stated wording, they would measure worsening; more likely the wording is wrong, but the paper does not say, so the headline 76.62% and 90.05% cannot be interpreted with certainty. Section 3.2 also cites a 'T3' that does not exist.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary data or analysis code showing that responders were counted as score increases (or that the scale was inverted before counting), so that 'reduction' is only a wording slip.

quotes.text: in which the higher the score the lesser the fatigue
By considering the reduction of at least 1 unit in the questionnaire as an improvement
The increase in the score of the FACIT-fatigue questionnaire represents an improvement in the feeling of fatigue

issues.title: Pre-specified 5-unit recovery outcome not tested against assumed 60%; abstract headlines the 1-unit threshold
issues.explanation: The sample size was based on the proportion with at least a 5-unit FACIT gain, compared with a hypothesised 60% in untreated people. The Results give 74.63% at T2 but never test it against 60%, and the abstract instead leads with the 90.05% figure for a 1-unit change, a threshold well below clinical relevance. The 60% benchmark is itself unsupported and the 5-unit result is labelled 'T0 and T3'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported test of the 5-unit responder proportion against the 60% benchmark, with justification for that benchmark.

quotes.text: defined as the proportions of patients who showed an increase of at least 5 units in the FACIT scale
The data of FACIT-questionnaire showed an improvement of at least 1 unit in 76.62% of subjects after 14 days and in 90.05% of subjects after 28 days.

issues.title: Manufacturer-funded study by manufacturer employees; sponsor's role in design/analysis not described
issues.explanation: Two authors work for the company that markets Apportal (and a third for a group company), and the company funded the work. Conflicts are declared, but no statement describes whether the sponsor shaped the design, analysis or the favourable conclusions. Combined with the uncontrolled design, this reduces independent confidence in the positive claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in analysis and interpretation, or independent analysis of the raw data.

quotes.text: Maria Sole Rossato and Germano Tarantino are Pharmanutra S.p.a. employees.
This work was supported by Pharmanutra Spa, Pisa (Italy).

issues.title: No registry entry or protocol reported for a prospective 28-day supplement study with a power calculation
issues.explanation: The paper describes prospective enrolment, fixed time points and a pre-specified recovery definition, but gives no registration number or protocol. The stated primary outcome (at least 5 units on FACIT) is not the one emphasised in the abstract (at least 1 unit), so selective emphasis cannot be excluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol showing the primary outcome and analysis plan were fixed before enrolment.

quotes.text: At the beginning (T0), after 14 days (T1) and after 28 days (T2) of supplementation, general fatigue, mental fatigue and Quality of Life indexes were evaluated

10.1016/j.clnesp.2022.08.029.headline_claim: After 28 days of daily Apportal supplementation, COVID-19 survivors with fatigue showed significant improvements in muscle strength, physical performance and self-rated health, which may be associated with the supplement.
10.1016/j.clnesp.2022.08.029.overall: The finding that mean grip strength, exhaustion time, sit-to-stand repetitions and VAS scores were higher at 28 days than baseline is plausible as a description, but a single-arm, open-label design cannot attribute it to the supplement. Several printed numbers also conflict with the paper's own tables (VAS SDs, ferritin p, a direction reversal, heart disease percentage), which are fixable reporting errors that do not change the descriptive results. The causal reading in the conclusion should be treated as tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Hand grip strength (kg), with hand grip exhaustion time, 1-min sit-to-stand repetitions and self-rated health also reported as significant

issues.title: Single-arm, unblinded before-after study cannot attribute strength and function gains to the supplement
issues.explanation: All 30 participants took Apportal and were compared only with their own t0 values; there was no control group, randomisation or blinding, and participants were selected by physicians. Over 28 days, natural post-COVID recovery, regression to the mean, learning effects on the sit-to-stand and grip tests, effort and expectation, and lifestyle changes would all produce the same pattern. The authors acknowledge this, but the conclusions still describe the improvement as 'associated with' supplementation and recommend continued use, so the supplement effect is not established by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control or placebo arm showing the same changes were not seen without the supplement.

quotes.text: The major limitation is represented by the absence of a control group and the limited study sample, especially males.
we found a signi fi cant improvement in means of muscle strength and physical performance

second_reader.what_stands: This is a single-arm, uncontrolled, non-randomised before-after study with no stated blinding, so the observed gains in grip strength, sit-to-stand and exhaustion time cannot be attributed to the supplement. The authors do state this limitation openly and hedge in the Discussion, but the Abstract Conclusions and the final conclusion present the improvement in a way that links it to the supplementation more strongly than the design supports.

issues.title: Conclusion says 'all sample' improved self-rated health, but only mean changes are reported
issues.explanation: The concluding paragraph states that all participants reported enhanced self-rated health. The analysis only shows a mean difference (57.6 to 71.4), and no individual-level change data are given; the minimum VAS is 30.0 at both t0 and t1. The statement over-generalises a group mean and suggests a uniform benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Individual-level data showing every participant's VAS rose between t0 and t1.

quotes.text: all sample reported enhancement of self-rated health status over the study period

issues.title: Self-rated health SDs in Abstract/Results (5.86, 6.73) are the sit-to-stand SDs; Table 2 gives 16.9 and 16.4
issues.explanation: The Abstract and Results report SDs of 5.86 and 6.73 for self-rated health. Table 2 gives 16.9 and 16.4 for the same means (57.6, 71.4), and the 5.86 and 6.73 values belong to the one-minute sit-to-stand row. The text understates the variability of the VAS scores by roughly a factor of 2.5, making the improvement look much more homogeneous than the table shows.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the VAS SDs were truly 5.86 and 6.73 and that Table 2 is the incorrect one.

issues.title: Ferritin p printed as 0.01 in Abstract but 0.08 (0.08022) in Results and Table 2
issues.explanation: The Abstract states the ferritin reduction is a non-significant trend yet gives p = 0.01, which would be significant. Results and Table 2 give p = 0.08. The Abstract p is a misprint and could mislead readers who read only the Abstract. A minor related slip: phase angle p is 0.01559 in Table 2 but 0.01 in Results text (rounds to 0.02).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing; the Abstract is inconsistent with the paper's own table.

quotes.text: (94.4 vs. 84.3, respectively; p ¼ 0.01)

issues.title: About 17 paired tests run without correction; primary results reported only as 'p < 0.05'
issues.explanation: The paper runs paired t-tests for grip (overall and by sex), exhaustion, sit-to-stand, VAS, five body composition measures and eight blood measures with no multiplicity adjustment or specified primary outcome. The key muscle results are reported only as 'p < 0.05', so a reader cannot judge how robust they are. The effect on the main conclusion is modest, mainly weakening the isolated phase angle finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome list with exact p-values showing the key results are far below a corrected threshold.

quotes.text: Repeated Measure T-Test (Paired T-Test) was used to compared differences in means between muscle strength and physical performance measures
None of the parameters of the body composition signi fi cantly improved, except for phase angle

issues.title: Results text says more sit-to-stand repetitions occurred at t0, but Table 2 and Abstract show t1 higher (28.3 vs 22.0)
issues.explanation: The Results sentence reads as if the higher repetition count (28.3) was at t0. Table 2 and the Abstract give 22.0 at t0 and 28.3 at t1. The data and conclusion are consistent with improvement, so this is a wording error that could mislead a reader about the direction of the effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing; the sentence is self-contradictory against the table. It would only be benign if the authors confirm it is a typo.

quotes.text: higher number of repetitions than at t1 at t0 (28.3 vs. 22.0; p < 0.05)

issues.title: Product owner Pharmanutra among the funders; role statement limited to design and interpretation
issues.explanation: Pharmanutra holds the rights to Apportal and is listed among the funders. The paper says it had no role in study design and data interpretation, but is silent on data collection, analysis, and manuscript preparation, and no author competing-interest statement is given. This is disclosed, so it is a weighing issue rather than an error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the funder had no role in data collection, analysis or reporting, and individual author declarations.

quotes.text: Pharmanutra is the pharmaceutical company that has the rights of the nutritional supplement Apportal ® .
This study was supported by Pharmanutra, Fondazione Memmo, Fondazione Angelini, Danone, Nutricia.

issues.title: Heart disease described as 3% of the whole sample; Table 1 gives 3/30 = 10.0%
issues.explanation: The Results text gives 3% for participants with heart disease, whereas 3 of 30 is 10.0%, which is what Table 1 reports. The error is in a descriptive baseline statement and does not affect the main efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator defined in the paper that makes 3 persons equal 3%; none is given.

quotes.text: 3 of 13 vs. 0 of 17, 3% of the whole sample

10.1016/j.clnu.2024.11.023.headline_claim: Two weeks of beetroot juice supplementation did not significantly improve functional outcomes compared with placebo in adults with long COVID, while beneficial effects were observed in gut microbiota composition and inflammatory markers.
10.1016/j.clnu.2024.11.023.overall: The null finding on functional outcomes is weak evidence of no effect: it comes from a small, per-protocol sample against a nitrate-containing placebo, in a retrospectively registered trial. The 'beneficial' microbiota and inflammation conclusion is not supported by the exploratory classification models and non-significant diversity results. The paper is best read as a preliminary pilot that generates hypotheses.

primary_outcome.name: Fatigue resistance (seconds until handgrip force falls to 50 % of maximum), change from baseline to day 14

issues.title: Conclusion claims 'beneficial effects' on microbiota and inflammation from exploratory PLS-DA models in 25 people
issues.explanation: The microbiota and inflammatory conclusions rest on classification models (accuracy 71.6% for inflammatory markers, with only two significant variables) in 25 participants, without clinical outcomes or multiplicity control. Diversity and community-level tests were non-significant. Labelling the changes as 'beneficial' and as an increase in 'probiotic species' goes beyond differences in abundance between arms, and sits beside a null result on all functional outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specified microbiota or inflammatory primary outcomes with adjusted between-group tests showing clinically meaningful change.

quotes.text: However, beneficial effects were observed in both gut microbiota composition (i.e., increase in probiotic species) and inflammatory markers.
Only two variables resulted significant for the model
did not reveal a sample grouping by treatment

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions state 'beneficial effects' on gut microbiota and inflammatory markers without hedging, although these rest on exploratory PLS-DA models in 25 people (15 vs 10), with no treatment separation in beta diversity (PERMANOVA p > 0.05) or alpha diversity, only two inflammatory variables flagged (IFN-gamma and MIP-1beta, both higher on beetroot juice), and an inflammatory model accuracy of 71.6 % that is only modestly above the 60 % majority-class rate. What does not stand is any claim that the paper hides the limitation: the limitations paragraph calls findings 'preliminary' and the m

issues.title: Placebo contained ~60 mg nitrate (vs ~600 mg active), so the null comparison may be biased toward no difference
issues.explanation: The placebo was diluted beetroot juice with about one tenth of the active nitrate dose, which the authors acknowledge may have been biologically active. If the placebo had some effect, the between-group difference in fatigue resistance and other functional outcomes would be shrunk. The null functional conclusion therefore cannot be read as 'no effect of beetroot juice versus an inert control'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that 60 mg nitrate has no measurable effect on the outcomes measured, or a nitrate-depleted control arm.

quotes.text: a solution containing 7 g of sugar, 180 mL of water, and 20 mL of beetroot juice [∼60 mg nitrate/drink]
It cannot be excluded that the nitrate content in the placebo may have been biologically active

issues.title: Analysis excludes 6 of 31 randomised (5/15 placebo vs 1/16 active); no analysis of all randomised participants
issues.explanation: The paper states that effects were analysed per protocol after six post-randomisation withdrawals, five of them from the placebo arm. Withdrawal before any dosing makes bias from this less likely than for dropouts during treatment, but the imbalance is large and unexplained. With only 15 vs 10 analysed, the group comparability shown in Table 1 is also weaker than in the randomised sample.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation that the withdrawals occurred before unblinding or allocation was known to participants, with reasons unrelated to the allocated arm.

quotes.text: Intervention effects were evaluated according to per-protocol analysis.
Six participants (one in the active and five in the placebo group) withdrew their consent before receiving the allocated intervention

issues.title: Trial registered August 2024, three years after the 2021 study period; paper does not say it was retrospective
issues.explanation: The study took place from March to July 2021, but NCT06535165 was first submitted on 2024-08-01. The paper simply states the trial was registered and gives no date or mention that registration was retrospective. Pre-specification of the primary outcome and of the many secondary and exploratory analyses cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version, or a dated protocol, predating enrolment and listing the same primary outcome.

quotes.text: from March 2021 to July 2021
Trial was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier no. NCT06535165.

issues.title: Primary null (diff 1.3 s, 95% CI -13.5 to 19.6) from 15 vs 10 analysed, powered for an optimistic 24 s effect
issues.explanation: The sample size was based on a 24 s difference taken from the long COVID vs adult gap, so the study is only able to detect a very large effect. The CI is wide enough to include differences up to about 20 s, so the study cannot show that beetroot juice is ineffective. The authors' framing as a pilot limits this, but the functional conclusion should read as inconclusive rather than negative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified justification that 24 s is a realistic supplement effect, or equivalence-type reporting of the CI.

quotes.text: the effect size was estimated as the difference between the values expected in the reference adult population and those of individuals with long COVID.
a sample of 22 participants, 11 per intervention arm, was estimated to provide 80 % power to detect a between-intervention difference of at least 24 s
Due to the small number of participants and the pilot nature of the study, findings should be regarded as preliminary.

issues.title: Sex-specific effect asserted from non-significant male subgroup comparisons (p = 0.15 and p = 0.45)
issues.explanation: The Discussion says beetroot juice had sex-specific effects with men responding more, but the male-subgroup differences for fatigue resistance (p = 0.15, CI including zero) and FMD (p = 0.45) were not significant. No interaction test is reported and the number of men is small. The claim is hypothesis-generating at best and rests on 25 participants split by sex and arm.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sex-by-treatment interaction test showing a significant interaction.

quotes.text: Our results indicate that beetroot juice supplementation had sex-specific effects on functional parameters, with male participants exhibiting a greater response.
although the difference between groups did not reach the statistical significance (p = 0.15)

issues.title: FMD difference printed 1.1% but the displayed group values 13.0 and 12.1 differ by 0.9
issues.explanation: The paper prints 13.0 vs 12.1 (difference 0.9) alongside a stated mean difference of 1.1 and a CI of -3.5 to 4.5 whose midpoint is 0.5. The summary statistic type (mean or median) is not stated for these values, so the discrepancy may simply reflect different estimators. The null FMD result is unaffected either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the displayed values are medians (or adjusted means) and that the difference and CI were computed by a nonparametric or model-based method.

quotes.text: mean difference = 1.1 %; 95 % CI: −3.5 to 4.5

issues.title: Funding statement says 'no external funding' despite Ministry support and company-donated product with employee authors
issues.explanation: Two authors are employees of the company that donated both active product and placebo. The funding statement conflicts with the acknowledgement of Ministry of Health support, and no role statement says whether the company had input into design, analysis or writing. The conflicts are disclosed, so this is a clarity problem rather than a hidden one.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clear statement of the sponsor's role and that the Ministry funding was internal institutional core funding.

quotes.text: A.T. and W.A. are employees of Aureli Mario S.S. Agricola, which donated both beetroot juice and placebo for the study.
This research received no external funding.
The study was supported by the Italian Ministry of Health—Ricerca Corrente 2024.

10.1016/j.ctim.2022.102823.headline_claim: Twice-daily inhalation of the Longevity thyme-orange-clove-frankincense essential oil blend for 14 days significantly lowered MFSI fatigue scores versus a placebo oil in post-COVID-19 women, which the authors read as evidence that it improves energy levels.
10.1016/j.ctim.2022.102823.overall: The main finding, a lower total MFSI score with the blend (adjusted means 25.42 vs 37.13, p = .020), is internally consistent in Table 2 despite a df label error, but it comes from a small, industry-funded trial with 4 of 44 consented participants excluded and a post hoc covariate model. The subscale and 'quality of life' claims are weaker: they rest on uncorrected tests of ten subscales and a depression-symptom score. Treat the conclusion as tentative and the secondary claims as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Total MFSI fatigue score on day 14, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline and selected covariates

primary_outcomes.measure: Change from baseline on the Multidimensional Fatigue Symptom Inventory (MFSI) at day 14.

issues.title: Five of ten MFSI subscales claimed as benefits at uncorrected p .003-.044; only one survives Bonferroni (.005)
issues.explanation: Ten secondary subscales and an exploratory PSQ-9 were tested at alpha .05 with no adjustment. The abstract and Overall evidence state that vigor, global, behavioral and general fatigue benefited, although behavioral (.044) and general (.030) would not survive even moderate correction. The Discussion's caution does not reach the abstract claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified multiplicity strategy or hierarchical testing order in the protocol, with subscales treated as hypothesis-generating in the headline claims.

quotes.text: Subscale analysis identified subscales of vigor, as well as global, behavioral, general, and mental fatigue as benefiting from the intervention.
Secondary outcomes of specific subdomains may also be affected by multiplicity, increasing the risk of type 1 errors.
This intervention is particularly beneficial for global and mental fatigue, as well as vigor.

issues.title: Exploratory depression-symptom score (PSQ-9/PHQ-9) presented as a quality-of-life improvement
issues.explanation: The only supporting measure is an exploratory depressive-symptom questionnaire, whose name is also printed inconsistently. The Discussion and Overall evidence nevertheless state a substantial improvement in quality of life. A depression-symptom score is not a quality-of-life instrument, and the result is exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A validated quality-of-life scale or a protocol defining this instrument as the quality-of-life measure.

quotes.text: exploratory analysis identified a substantial improvement to quality of life after the use of the essential oil blend, as measured by the PHQ-9.
provides a novel, non-invasive approach to improving quality of life
higher scores indicating higher levels of depression

issues.title: Primary analysis of 40 omits 4 of 44 consented, including an active-arm side-effect withdrawal
issues.explanation: The primary analysis drops one participant who never started, two protocol violators and one intervention-arm withdrawal for headaches. Removing the only tolerance failure from the active arm can make the intervention look better, and the paper does not report the arms of the other exclusions or an analysis including them. The 'modified ITT' label is not consistent with excluding post-start dropouts, although the loss is small (9.1%).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A full CONSORT diagram showing exclusions occurred before randomization, or a sensitivity analysis including all randomized participants.

quotes.text: Of those participants, one failed to begin the study, two were removed for protocol violations, and one withdrew due to side effects.
Participants were analyzed using a modified intent-to-treat analysis.
One participant in the intervention group reported experiencing headaches and withdrew on day 13.

issues.title: Primary ANCOVA covariates chosen post hoc from a saturated model and varied across subscales (n=40)
issues.explanation: The paper builds a saturated model and then a 'parsimonious' one from variables judged significant or theoretically relevant, with different covariates for different outcomes. The methods state only baseline as the covariate for the primary comparison, and no baseline-only result is reported. With 40 participants and 6 covariate terms, p = .020 could be sensitive to the choice; this is a robustness concern rather than a demonstrated error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified covariate list or a baseline-only ANCOVA giving a similar treatment estimate and p-value.

quotes.text: then a parsimonious model was developed using the statistically and theoretically significant variables
From those results, a parsimonious model was developed using all of the variables deemed critical to the model.

issues.title: Parsimonious model adjusted R² is 0.64 in text but 0.623 in Table 2 footer
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the parsimonious MFSI model's adjusted R² as 0.64, while the Table 2 footer for the same model prints 0.623. These cannot both be right. It is a small reporting error that does not alter the treatment-effect result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the text and footer refer to different models or different fit statistics.

quotes.text: adjusted R 2 = 0.64
Adjusted R Squared ¼ 0.623

issues.title: Four non-significant subscales described as 'improved during the intervention' without data shown
issues.explanation: The Discussion says somatic, affective, emotional and cognitive fatigue improved, though the between-group tests were non-significant and their statistics are not reported in the paper. The authors partly hedge in the following sentence. Describing improvement during the intervention can be read as treatment benefit when only a between-group comparison can show that.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adjusted means and between-group tests for these four subscales showing the described direction.

quotes.text: improved during the intervention but did not achieve statistical significance

issues.title: Table 2 olfactory function p = .681 does not match F = 1.89 on 3 and 27 df; time-since-diagnosis MS 235.602 vs SS 325.602
issues.explanation: In the primary ANCOVA table the olfactory-function covariate has F = 1.89 with df 3 and 27, which corresponds to p near .16, but the table prints .681. The time-since-diagnosis row also has SS 325.602 and MS 235.602 despite 1 df. These are table typos affecting covariate rows only, not the treatment test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the covariate was tested with different df or a different test than the table states.

quotes.text: Olfactory Function

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.681, but recomputed from the printed f = 1.89 p is at most 0.1559, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show. This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Primary F reported as F(1,39) but Table 2 error df is 27 (total 39); same df slip repeated for secondary tests
issues.explanation: The abstract and Results give the primary test as F(1,39), but Table 2 shows 27 error df, with 39 being the total df. The reported p (.020) agrees with 27 denominator df, so the significance conclusion survives. The df labelling is nevertheless wrong, and the same F(1.39) form is used for every secondary test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A model description showing only 1 + 39 df were available for the group test (e.g. fewer covariate terms than Table 2).

quotes.text: F (1,39) = 6.15, p = .020, partial eta squared = 0.198

issues.title: Participant with pre-study recurring headaches enrolled despite listed exclusion for recurring headaches
issues.explanation: Recurring headaches are a stated exclusion criterion, yet the adverse-events section reports a participant with recurring headaches before the study who was enrolled and later withdrew. This indicates eligibility screening was not applied as written. The effect on results is probably small since the participant is outside the analysed 40, but it also bears on how the withdrawal was handled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Screening records showing the headaches were not 'recurring' by protocol definition at enrolment.

quotes.text: recurring headaches, chest pain, abnormal pulmonary function, or uncontrolled hypertension
This participant also reported experiencing recurring headaches prior to the start of the study

issues.title: Behavioral subscale SE printed as 0.075 (placebo) and 0.75 (intervention) from the same model
issues.explanation: Adjusted means from one ANCOVA share a common SE, as for every other subscale. The intervention-arm SE of 0.75 is ten times the placebo value of 0.075 and would make a 0.24 difference trivially non-significant. The printed 0.75 is a slip with no effect on the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original published PDF showing 0.075 for both groups (extraction artefact).

quotes.text: 2.06 (SE = 0.075) for the placebo group
1.82 (SE = 0.75) for the intervention group

issues.title: 67.6% 'lost both taste and smell' is not attainable with n=40 (27/40 = 67.5%); shares sum to 100.1%
