10.1093/braincomms/fcaf447.headline_claim: Both psychoeducational interventions (cognitive-focused and affective-focused) produced improvement in subjective cognitive complaints in Long COVID patients, with maintenance at 8 months, though the cognitive arm was not superior on the primary outcome.
10.1093/braincomms/fcaf447.overall: The main finding of no difference between arms on the primary outcome is reported consistently. The claims of improvement and of intervention-specific effects rest on uncontrolled time effects and on within-arm significance contrasts. The cognitive arm's 'superiority' on secondary outcomes is not supported by the interaction tests, and the headline conclusions should be read as tentative. The numerical slips (96% versus 92%, 9% versus about 21% cumulative dropout) are minor.

issues.title: 'ITT' analysis of 122 excludes 8 of 130 randomised patients after randomisation
issues.explanation: Seven patients were removed for outlier baseline scores judged not credible, and one was removed as incorrectly randomised. The analysis set of 122 is then described as analysed 'according to ITT principles'. The exclusions are few, but they were decided after randomisation, with the arm-level counts (65/65 to 63/59) showing they were unevenly split. Because the primary result is a null between-arm difference, the effect on the conclusion is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis including all 130 randomised patients with the same conclusion.

issues.title: '9% dropout at 8 months' is incremental; cumulative loss is 28/130 (about 21%), 96/122 analysed at T2
issues.explanation: The Abstract and Limitations describe a low dropout of 12% at 2 months and 9% at 8 months. The same paper reports 15 + 13 = 28 global dropouts out of 130 and only 96 patients in the 8-month analysis. The 9% only reconciles as the additional loss after 2 months, so the cumulative 8-month attrition is about 21%. The wording makes the long-term follow-up look more complete than it was. Neither the 2-month nor the 8-month attrition level changes the main findings.

issues.title: Cognitive arm called 'superior' on secondary outcomes although interaction tests were null (P > 0.18)
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the cognitive intervention 'proved superior' for sleep, distress symptoms, attention and long-term memory. The Results report no group-by-time interaction for cognitive performance (all P > 0.18) and none for sleep or distress. Only psychosocial fatigue had an interaction, at an uncorrected P = 0.04. 'Superior' therefore rests on one arm reaching P < 0.05 and the other not, and the working-memory attribution contradicts the Results. The authors do call the secondary outcomes exploratory, but the sentence is stated as a finding and then used to argue for effects 'beyond a placebo effect'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary interaction tests showing significant, multiplicity-adjusted between-arm differences for sleep, distress, attention and long-term memory.

issues.title: Time-effect improvements in an uncontrolled two-active-arm design are worded as positive intervention effects
issues.explanation: The primary outcome showed no difference between arms. Improvement over time in both arms cannot be separated from regression to the mean, expectancy, practice effects or natural recovery, as the Limitations admit. The Conclusions nonetheless say positive effects were maintained and that patients considered the interventions beneficial. The Discussion adds that the results may support effects beyond placebo. The caveats are present, but the headline wording is stronger than the design supports, and the 8-month result comes from a per-protocol set of 96 of 122.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A no-treatment or waitlist comparison, or an analysis showing the within-arm gains exceed what regression to the mean and practice would produce.

The 96% figures in the Results belong to participation (125/130) and session completion (120/125). The adherence percentages are quoted with inconsistent denominators across the Abstract, Results and Discussion. This is a small reporting error and does not change the feasibility conclusion.

10.1093/braincomms/fcag364.headline_claim: At-home Microtesla Magnetic Therapy is feasible, safe and well tolerated, with preliminary, exploratory signals of cognitive and emotional benefit in long COVID; larger trials are needed to confirm.
10.1093/braincomms/fcag364.overall: The feasibility and safety conclusions are reasonably supported for a 30-person pilot, with 90.9% completion among all randomized participants. The efficacy language in the Discussion ('clinically meaningful improvements', 'compares favourably') goes beyond the data, since no between-group difference survived FDR correction and several measures favour sham. Remaining issues (incomplete race table, completer-only analysis, loose text-to-table statements) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: Feasibility: proportion of participants completing at least 80% of scheduled treatments and all three study visits

issues.title: Discussion asserts 'clinically meaningful improvements' though no efficacy difference survived FDR correction
issues.explanation: Only three Week 8 cognitive differences and one SF-36 difference reached nominal P<0.05, all uncorrected, with none surviving FDR and none showing a significant interaction in the mixed models for the cognitive outcomes. Several of these nominal differences come partly from sham-arm decline rather than active-arm gain (DSS sham -2.1, HVLT-R sham -4.4, SF-36 sham -10). Several other measures favour sham or show nothing. Describing the result as clinically meaningful improvement, comparing it favourably with other trials, and citing 'consistent improvements across neurocognitive domains' goes beyond a 30-person exploratory pilot with a feasibility primary outcome. The study supports only feasibility and hypothesis generation for efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified efficacy analysis with multiplicity control showing at least one robust between-group difference.

quotes.text: MMT treatment was also associated with clinically meaningful improvements in cognition and mood at treatment completion and at 8-week follow-up.
The magnitude of cognitive improvement observed with MMT compares favourably to other interventions studied in LC populations.
none of these differences remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion does state, without qualification, that MMT was associated with 'clinically meaningful improvements in cognition and mood', although the paper reports that no between-group efficacy difference survived FDR correction; this wording is stronger than the evidence, and the 'compares favourably' sentence rests on the same uncorrected, wide-interval differences. It is narrower than a flat contradiction because 'clinically meaningful' is defined by the paper as an effect-size threshold (0.5 SD, 2 points) that the point estimates do meet, and the next sentence plus the Limitations and C

issues.title: Discussion cites 100% compliance; primary feasibility outcome among all 33 randomized was 90.9%
issues.explanation: The primary outcome was the proportion completing at least 80% of treatments and all visits. Among all randomized participants this was 90.9% (30/33). The Discussion reports '100% treatment compliance', which counts only those who completed the study. This flatters the feasibility result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The Discussion explicitly restating 100% as completer-only adherence alongside the 90.9% figure.

quotes.text: Participants showed 100% treatment compliance and high usability ratings
90.9% completed at least 80% of treatments and all study visits

issues.title: Text says active beat sham on all remaining measures; several Table 3 differences favour sham
issues.explanation: The Results state that active MMT showed greater improvements than sham on the remaining attention, speed, inhibition and executive measures. Table 3 shows negative active-minus-sham differences on several of these at Week 4 (Digit Span Backward, HVLT-R Delayed Recall, D-KEFS Category Switching, BVMT) and on SDMT at Week 8. The Trail A and B direction cannot be settled because the scoring convention is unstated. The sentence therefore overstates how uniformly the data favour the active arm.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sentence refers only to a subset of measures, or a Table 3 scoring note showing the negative differences are favourable.

quotes.text: While the active group showed greater improvements than sham on remaining measures of attention, processing speed, inhibition and executive function

issues.title: Efficacy is complete-case: 3 of 33 withdrawn and extra unexplained missing outcome data (sham N 8-9)
issues.explanation: Efficacy comparisons use only completers, with no ITT or imputation. At 9% withdrawal this is a small risk, but one withdrawal was for missed visits and the arm of each withdrawn participant is not clearly reported. Some outcomes have missing sham data (e.g. HVLT-R Delayed Recall N=8 at Week 8) without explanation. With 10 sham participants, a few missing values can shift the exploratory results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis including all randomized participants, or the CONSORT figure showing withdrawals were balanced and unrelated to outcome.

quotes.text: Analyses were conducted using complete-case data; imputation was not used for missing values.
Three study participants were withdrawn from the study after enrolment

issues.title: Table 2 race counts sum to 9/10 (sham), 19/20 (active) and 28/30 (all)
issues.explanation: The four mutually exclusive race categories in Table 2 add to one fewer than the arm size in both arms. Percentages likewise sum to 90% (sham) and 95% (active). The paper gives no missing-race category, and the Fisher test on race (P=0.011) cannot be traced to a complete table. This is a minor reporting error and does not touch the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table footnote or supplement showing one participant per arm with unreported or missing race data.

issues.title: SDMT 'did not improve' vs positive change in both arms at Week 8 (sham +7.10, active +5.35)
issues.explanation: The Results say SDMT showed no improvement to Week 8, while Table 3 shows both arms gaining on SDMT. The sham arm gained more, so a between-group reading is consistent with the text. The wording is ambiguous but affects only one secondary measure.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors confirming the sentence refers to between-group differences.

quotes.text: The D-KEFS Category Fluency, RCFT, SDMT and MINT did not show improvements from baseline to 8 weeks.

issues.title: Race imbalance between arms (Fisher P=0.011; 30% vs 80% White) with unadjusted efficacy analyses
issues.explanation: Table 2 shows a marked difference in race between 10 sham and 20 active participants, and the efficacy comparisons are unadjusted. In a small trial this is likely chance and is disclosed as a limitation. Its effect on the exploratory estimates cannot be judged from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis adjusting for race that gives similar estimates.

quotes.text: Differences in race were observed between groups; however, subgroup sizes were small, limiting interpretability.

10.1093/cid/ciac226.headline_claim: Long COVID patients who respond to leronlimab show increased blood cell surface CCR5, suggesting an unexpected mechanism of abnormal immune downmodulation that is normalized by leronlimab.
10.1093/cid/ciac226.overall: The primary symptom outcome was null, and the headline CCR5 mechanism rests on within-arm and post-hoc responder-subgroup changes without a between-group test. The paper is honest that it is a small exploratory study, but the abstract's mechanistic conclusion is not supported by the design. Treat the CCR5 findings as hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: Change from baseline in symptom severity score through day 56

primary_outcomes.measure: Changes From Baseline in Daily COVID-19-related Symptom Severity Score Through Day 56.
primary_outcomes.time_frame: Changes in COVID-19 related symptoms from baseline (start of treatment) and day 56 (end of treatment)

issues.title: Abstract omits null primary outcome (adjusted difference -1.0, n.s.) and draws a mechanistic conclusion
issues.explanation: The registered primary outcome, change in symptom severity, showed no significant between-group difference after adjustment. The abstract reports only the CCR5 change in responders and concludes that leronlimab normalizes an immune abnormality. Responders are defined by post-randomization symptom improvement, and about half of placebo participants also improved, so the subgroup cannot support a mechanism the primary result does not show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An abstract that states the null primary result and frames the CCR5 data as hypothesis-generating only.

quotes.text: the adjusted mean difference was -1.0 (not statistically significant; Supplementary Table 2)
These findings suggest an unexpected mechanism of abnormal  immune  downmodulation  in  some  persons  that  is normalized by leronlimab.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract does not mention that the primary endpoint (symptom severity change) showed an adjusted difference of -1.0 that was not statistically significant, and it states a mechanistic inference ('abnormal immune downmodulation... normalized by leronlimab') from exploratory CCR5 data. The abstract does label the trial exploratory, and the body of the paper does report the null primary result and a small-pilot caveat, so the omission is limited to the abstract.

issues.title: CCR5 claims rest on within-arm and responder/non-responder significance, with no between-group test
issues.explanation: Significant change from baseline in the treated arm but not placebo, or in responders but not nonresponders, does not show that the arms or subgroups differ. The responder split is defined after treatment and subgroup sizes are small (14/12 and 10/18). The abstract's contrast between responders and nonresponders is therefore not statistically established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-arm or treatment-by-response interaction test showing a significant difference in CCR5 change.

quotes.text: cell surface CCR5 levels showed significant ( P < .0001) increases from baseline to day 56 among leronlimab-treated responders but not treated nonresponders

second_reader.what_stands: The CCR5 claims in the text and abstract rest on within-arm and within-subgroup baseline-to-day-56 comparisons, with no between-group or interaction test reported in the paper; the contrast between responders and non-responders is made by comparing significance levels. Whether such a test exists in the supplement cannot be seen, and the statistical methods are not described in the main text.

issues.title: Many symptom and immune endpoints tested uncorrected; immune-effect statements lack caveat
issues.explanation: The paper tests 24 symptoms plus many cell populations and cytokines, with no correction, and reports only borderline results for symptoms. Statements that leronlimab was 'associated with increases in key adaptive immune cell populations' give no effect sizes or p-values in the main text. This weakens secondary findings, though the authors do call the study exploratory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary tables showing adjusted p-values or a prespecified hierarchy for the immune endpoints.

quotes.text: reaching borderline statistical significance without correction for multiple comparisons due to the exploratory nature of this pilot study
leronlimab treatment was associated with increases in key adaptive immune cell populations

issues.title: Randomized count (55 in text, 56 in registry) differs from 54 analysed (26+28), with no flow reported
issues.explanation: The Methods say 55 people were randomized, the registry lists 56 enrolled, and the CCR5 figure uses 26 + 28 = 54. The 54 may be those with CCR5 samples, but the paper gives no participant flow, exclusions or dropouts. Readers cannot tell who was lost or whether the analysed sets are the randomized sets.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CONSORT flow diagram showing 55 randomized with one lacking a CCR5 sample, or a corrected total.

quotes.text: we performed an exploratory trial in 55 individuals with long COVID
in the overall leronlimab (n = 26) and placebo (n = 28) groups

issues.title: Sponsor officers are authors and sponsor paid writers; sponsor role in analysis not stated
issues.explanation: CytoDyn funded the trial, three authors are its officers, and its funded medical writers helped prepare the paper. The paper does not say who ran the analyses or who decided on the framing. Conflicts are disclosed, so this is context for reading the positive framing rather than a defect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in analysis, interpretation or the decision to publish.

quotes.text: This work was supported by CytoDyn Inc.
S. A. K., N. Z. P ., and C. R. are officers of CytoDyn Inc and report stock options and consulting fees from CytoDyn

10.1093/cid/ciad257.headline_claim: CBT was effective in reducing fatigue among patients with severe post-COVID-19 fatigue, and the effect was sustained at 6-month follow-up.
10.1093/cid/ciad257.overall: The CBT-versus-usual-care difference in fatigue is large, statistically robust and consistent across time points and secondary outcomes, with very low attrition. However, with an open-label design, a self-reported primary outcome and no attention-matched control, the size of the specific CBT effect is uncertain and likely overstated. The conclusion is better read as CBT being superior to usual care than as proof of a specific therapeutic effect.

primary_outcome.name: CIS-fatigue score, averaged across T1 and T2 (overall between-group difference)

issues.title: Usual-care comparator and unblinded self-reported outcome: specific CBT effect cannot be separated from nonspecific effects
issues.explanation: Control participants received usual care with no attention or treatment-rationale matching, and participants, therapists and assessors knew allocation while the primary outcome was a self-reported questionnaire. The authors concede a placebo condition would have been preferable, yet the abstract concludes 'CBT was effective in reducing fatigue'. The size of the difference (-8.8, d=0.69) likely includes expectation and attention effects of unknown magnitude, so the conclusion supports 'CBT package superior to usual care' rather than a specific CBT effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence from an attention-matched or objectively measured outcome showing a similar effect size.

quotes.text: A placebo condition matched with respect to the attention given and offering of a treatment rationale would have been preferable to rule out that the effects of CBT were (partly) nonspecific.
Due to the nature of the intervention, research assistants, participants, and therapists were not blinded to randomization outcome.
As there is no reliable biomarker of severe fatigue, we used a patient-reported outcome to assess fatigue severity.

second_reader.what_stands: The design (usual-care comparator, no blinding of participants, therapists or assessors, and a self-reported primary outcome) means the trial cannot separate specific CBT effects from nonspecific effects such as attention, expectation and a treatment rationale; the paper itself acknowledges this. It is not hidden or overlooked: the authors name each limitation and argue that CAU involved substantial other care, but they give no data on attention or credibility, so the effect on the self-reported outcome may include nonspecific components of unknown size.

10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2398.headline_claim: An individualized exercise program is a safe and well-tolerated treatment option for patients with persisting post-COVID symptoms, and these patients significantly improve in physical performance after 4 weeks compared with patients without exercise.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2398.overall: The main finding that supervised training raises VO2peak relative to usual care in a small open-label trial is plausible and directly compared, but it rests on 44 patients with no stated sample-size basis, primary outcome or multiplicity handling. Symptom benefits (fatigue, quality of life) were not shown to differ from usual care, and the safety claim is thinly supported. The conclusion should be read as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: VO2peak (relative oxygen uptake)

issues.title: Efficacy claim from 44 randomised patients; no sample-size basis or analysed numbers per arm reported
issues.explanation: The abstract randomises 44 patients and states they significantly improve in physical performance versus no exercise, but gives no sample-size justification and no numbers analysed per arm. Fatigue and quality-of-life comparisons (the patient-relevant symptoms) were not different between groups, so the small trial supports only an exercise-physiology effect. This is a modest, tentative result rather than evidence of treatment efficacy for symptoms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or full paper giving a prespecified sample-size calculation for VO2peak that 44 patients satisfied.

quotes.text: 44 patients consented and were randomized to four weeks of supervised personalized strength endurance training for 4 weeks or usual care
These patients signiﬁcantly improve in physical performance after 4 weeks compared to patients without exercise intervention.

issues.title: 'Safe' conclusion rests on about 22 exercising patients over 4 weeks with no adverse-event detail
issues.explanation: The safety conclusion is drawn from a one-sentence report of no training-related adverse events in a 44-patient, 4-week study. With so few exercising participants, a zero count cannot exclude uncommon harms such as post-exertional symptom worsening, and no method of adverse-event ascertainment is given. The statement is plausible for the short supervised setting but is stated more firmly than the data allow.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full report showing systematic adverse-event monitoring including symptom worsening, with confidence bounds appropriate to the sample.

quotes.text: There were no adverse events related to the training.
An individualized exercise program is a safe and well-tolerated treatment option in patients with persisting symptoms post-Covid.

issues.title: No primary outcome or multiplicity handling stated; oxygen-pulse result p<0.05 is fragile
issues.explanation: Several outcomes (VO2peak, oxygen pulse, MFI-20, MQOL, PCFS) are tested with no stated primary outcome or correction. The VO2peak result (p<0.01) is reasonably robust, but the oxygen-pulse result at p<0.05 would not clearly survive adjustment. The physical-performance conclusion rests on these two related spirometric measures, so it is tentative rather than established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome of VO2peak with a hierarchical testing plan.

quotes.text: VO2peak (exercise: 10.0±12.7% vs. control: 0.1±8.9%, p<0.01) and oxygen-pulse (exercise: 9.8±10.8% vs. control: 0.0±13.9%, p<0.05)

issues.title: Open-label design with self-reported fatigue and quality-of-life outcomes
issues.explanation: Fatigue, quality of life and functional status are patient-reported, so participants who knew their allocation could bias them. The abstract does not draw a between-group benefit from these outcomes, so the impact on the stated conclusions is limited. The objective spirometric outcome is less exposed to this problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: N/A; the concern is inherent to the design but not exploited in the conclusions.

quotes.text: a prospective randomized controlled study with open-label and blinded endpoint evaluation was designed

10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2594.headline_claim: Intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia training (IHHT) added to standard rehabilitation improved functional capacity, quality of life and perceived health in patients with post-COVID-19 conditions.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2594.overall: The abstract reports large, significant between-group differences favouring IHHT, but the open-label add-on design with no sham control, no stated blinding, and no reported sample size, analysis population, dispersion or adverse events means the effect sizes are tentative. The performance-test results are more credible than the patient-rated outcomes, for which the stated benefit is likely inflated. Format limits explain the missing registration and ethics details.

primary_outcome.name: Six-minute walk test (6MWT) walking distance, between groups

issues.title: Patient-rated outcomes (FAS, EQ-5D, MCRS) claimed as IHHT benefits without sham/attention control or blinding
issues.explanation: Controls received standard rehabilitation only, while the IHHT arm received 45-minute sessions on alternate days on top of it. Patients knew which arm they were in and extra attention and expectation could inflate self-reported fatigue, QoL and perceived health. The conclusion nonetheless states improved QoL and perceived health, and even the performance tests were not shown to be assessed blind.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of blinded outcome assessment and a sham or attention-matched control condition.

quotes.text: Patients were 1:1 allocated to the standard rehabilitation program or IHHT on top of standard rehabilitation.
Respiratory treatment by IHHT in patients with post COVID conditions resulted in improved functional capacity in multiple of functional tests and in improved QoL and perceived health.

second_reader.what_stands: As described, the trial compared IHHT plus standard rehabilitation with standard rehabilitation alone, with no sham or attention control and no stated blinding, so the self-reported outcomes (FAS, EQ-5D, MCRS) could be influenced by expectation and extra attention, and the conclusion presents them as IHHT effects without that caveat. The point is only partly established because this is a short abstract that may omit blinding or control details, and the paper states these outcomes were not described as blinded rather than that they were unblinded; the objective tests (6MWT, SCT) are not affecte

issues.title: No trial registration or protocol reported for the randomized trial with a 6MWT primary endpoint
issues.explanation: The abstract describes a prospective randomized trial and names the 6MWT as primary endpoint, but gives no registry identifier or registration timing. Whether the endpoint was prespecified cannot be verified from the paper. This is likely a consequence of the abstract format and does not by itself undermine the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry (with date before enrolment) listing the 6MWT between-group change as primary outcome.

quotes.text: The primary endpoint of the trial was improvement in walking distance in a six-minute walk test (6MWT) between groups.

issues.title: Hemoglobin and CRP findings rest on within-arm change versus baseline, not a between-group comparison
issues.explanation: The abstract contrasts significance in the IHHT arm with non-significance in controls, which does not show the arms differ from each other. This is a known inferential error, but it applies only to secondary laboratory markers and does not feed the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group (interaction or ANCOVA) test for hemoglobin and CRP change showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: compared to baseline (P<0.001), whereas these changes were not observed in the control group.

10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2601.headline_claim: A 3-month cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program after COVID-19 accelerates recovery of arterial and ventricular function, especially in individuals with lower baseline IL-1β.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2601.overall: The conclusion that rehabilitation accelerates arterial and ventricular recovery rests on within-arm before/after tests with no reported between-group comparison, in a 60-patient trial with no stated sample-size basis, so it should be read as preliminary. The IL-1β subgroup statement is weaker still. The point estimates suggest a possibly real effect, but this abstract does not demonstrate it.

primary_outcome.name: cf-PWV, LV-GLS and VAC (no single primary outcome designated)

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from within-arm changes (p<0.001 vs p=0.74/0.15); no between-arm test of change reported
issues.explanation: The paper tests baseline against follow-up separately in each arm and contrasts a significant result in the rehabilitation arm with a non-significant one in controls. A difference between 'significant' and 'not significant' is not itself a test of the intervention effect. The claim that rehabilitation accelerates recovery therefore has no direct between-group statistical support in the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-arm comparison of change (ANCOVA or group-by-time interaction) with a significant p-value for cf-PWV, GLS and VAC.

quotes.text: it was improved only in the study group (8.2±1.3m/sec vs. 6.6±1.0m/sec, p<0.001) but not in the control group
while no changes were observed in the control group (-18.7±2.9% vs. -18.3±2.1%, p=0.15)

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract infers a rehabilitation effect from a significant within-arm change in the study group (p<0.001) against non-significant within-arm changes in the control group (p=0.74 for cf-PWV, p=0.15 for GLS), and reports no between-arm test of change. The point holds for cf-PWV and GLS as checked; for VAC the control-arm result is not printed, so the point there is only partly checkable. This is a limitation of how the evidence is presented, and the possibility that a between-arm test exists but was left out of the abstract cannot be excluded.

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 60 patients; conclusion stated without caution
issues.explanation: Sixty patients were randomized, and no power calculation is reported. In an abstract this omission is common, and the effects shown look large. The concern is mainly that the conclusion is worded confidently while the design basis is unstated, which is partly covered by the between-group testing issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample size calculation in the full publication or protocol showing 60 patients gave adequate power for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: We enrolled 60 convalescent patients from COVID-19 and one-month post-acute disease
accelerates the recovering of arterial and ventricular function, especially in individuals with a lower baseline inﬂammatory burden

issues.title: VAC defined as cf-PWV/LV-GLS ratio with no validation reported; sign and units unclear
issues.explanation: The coupling index is a ratio computed by the authors, and no validation or rationale is given. Because GLS is negative, the ratio is negative, and its interpretation (more negative is better or worse) is not explained. Reported ΔVAC values are positive while VAC values are negative, so the direction of the change is hard to follow.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A cited validation of cf-PWV/LV-GLS as a ventricular-arterial coupling index and a clear statement of its direction of benefit.

quotes.text: Finally, the ratio of cf-PWV/LV-GLS was calculated as an index of VAC.
Finally, VAC was signiﬁcantly ameliorated only in patients receiving cardiopulmonary rehabilitation

issues.title: Median-split IL-1β subgroup (p=0.04, ~15 per subgroup, treated arm only) promoted into the conclusion
issues.explanation: The subgroup comparison is restricted to the treated arm, so it cannot show that inflammation modifies the effect of rehabilitation relative to control. It is a single unadjusted p=0.04 with no stated pre-specification, and the conclusion still says benefit is 'especially' in low-inflammation patients. The finding is hypothesis-generating at best.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specification of the IL-1β stratification and a significant treatment-by-IL-1β interaction in the whole randomized cohort.

quotes.text: those presenting with lower concentrations experienced a signiﬁcant beneﬁt in ΔVAC (IL-1β<8.4pg/ml: 0.14±0.08m/s% vs. IL-1β≥8.4pg/ml: 0.09±0.05m/s%, p=0.04)
especially in individuals with a lower baseline inﬂammatory burden

10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2904.headline_claim: In patients with COVID-19-related POTS, an individually tailored training seems to contribute to increased time in upright position, reduction of POTS-specific symptoms and improved functions, and the intervention seems feasible in terms of recruitment, compliance and safety.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehad655.2904.overall: This is a small single-arm feasibility abstract, and its conclusions are hedged but still attribute improvements to the training without any comparator. The efficacy and symptom-reduction claims are tentative at best, and the safety statement rests on 23 patients with an unquantified post-exertion malaise signal. Feasibility findings (recruitment, completion of 23 of 24) are the best-supported part.

primary_outcome.name: Time spent in upright position

issues.title: Single-arm pre-post design (n=24) used to infer that training contributes to improvement
issues.explanation: Measurements were taken only at baseline and after 12 weeks, with no comparison group. Natural recovery from post-COVID syndrome, regression to the mean, and expectation effects cannot be separated from any training effect. The authors hedge ('seem to contribute') and acknowledge the need for a comparison, but the results and conclusion still attribute gains to the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group, or a wait-list period showing stable outcomes before the intervention.

quotes.text: Measurements were carried out at baseline
an individually tailored training seem to contribute to increased time in upright position
Further studies are needed to verify these results and compare disease progression with and without intervention.

second_reader.what_stands: The design as described is a single group assessed before and after a 12-week intervention (n=24 enrolled, 23 completed), with no control arm, so the observed improvements cannot be attributed causally to the training, and the Conclusion's 'seem to contribute' goes beyond what that design supports. This is softened by the study being framed as a feasibility study, the hedged wording, and the explicit statement that further studies comparing progression with and without intervention are needed; I could not check Table 1 or Figure 1 because they were not in the extracted text.

issues.title: About 8 secondary outcomes with uncorrected p-values (some near .045) support symptom-reduction claim
issues.explanation: The abstract reports roughly eight outcome tests with no multiplicity adjustment. Several are marginal (FSS p<0.045, VOSS p<0.02) and would not be significant under even a simple Bonferroni correction over eight tests (threshold about 0.006). The symptom-reduction part of the conclusion is therefore weaker than presented, although the strongest results (PHQ-9, EQ-5D, p<0.001) would likely survive.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified analysis plan designating these as exploratory, or adjusted p-values still below 0.05.

quotes.text: less symptoms related to POTS (MaPS p<0.01, VOSS p<0.02, FSS p<0.045)
reduction of POTS-speciﬁc symptoms and improved functions

issues.title: Safety called feasible from 23 patients; number with post-exertion malaise not given
issues.explanation: The abstract says no severe adverse events occurred but that some patients described post-exertion malaise, without saying how many. A claim of safety from 23 uncontrolled patients, with an unquantified adverse symptom that is a recognised concern in post-COVID conditions, is not well supported. The wording is hedged and the information is disclosed, so this is a matter of interpretation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full-paper data showing the number with PEM was very small and transient, with adverse events systematically recorded.

quotes.text: No severe adverse events occurred however some of the patients described symptoms as post exertion malaise (PEM).
The intervention seems to be feasible in terms of recruitment, compliance and

10.1093/eurheartj/ehae666.298.headline_claim: Cardiopulmonary rehabilitation can accelerate the improvement of RV-pulmonary artery coupling (RVAC) by mediating both RV afterload reduction (PASP) and improving RV function in convalescent COVID-19 patients.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehae666.298.overall: The headline claim that rehabilitation accelerates RVAC improvement through afterload and RV function is only tentatively supported: it comes from a non-randomized 30 vs 10 comparison with no allocation description, no adjustment and no mediation analysis. The RVAC baseline values are also printed with the group assignment swapped between sections. The within-group changes are small, so the conclusion should be read as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: RV-pulmonary artery coupling (RVAC, RVGLS/PASP ratio)

issues.title: Non-randomized 30 vs 10 comparison with no allocation description or confounder adjustment
issues.explanation: Patients simply did or did not take part in rehabilitation, with no description of how this was decided and no adjustment beyond a statement that risk-factor prevalence was similar. Differences in disease severity, motivation or access could drive the different RVAC trajectories. The conclusion that rehabilitation accelerates improvement is therefore only tentatively supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that allocation was by a rule unrelated to prognosis, or an adjusted analysis showing the same interaction.

quotes.text: 30 subjects participated in a 3-month cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program (study group) and 10 did not (control group).
There were no major differences in the prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors between the two groups.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes a 30 vs 10 comparison in which patients participated or did not participate in rehabilitation, with no description of how patients were allocated and no mention of randomization. It reports no adjustment for confounders, and risk-factor balance is asserted only qualitatively ('no major differences'), so with 10 controls a non-significant baseline test is weak evidence of comparability. The limited detail may reflect abstract length, so the full report might contain more.

issues.title: Baseline RVAC group values swapped: -0.96/-0.86 in baseline sentence vs -0.86/-0.96 in T0 values
issues.explanation: The baseline sentence gives rehabilitation RVAC -0.96 (0.28) and no-rehabilitation -0.86 (0.27). The follow-up sentences give the reverse for the same groups at T0. One of the two is wrong; the RVGLS/PASP ratios favour the T0 assignment, so the baseline sentence is probably the one in error. Under the T0 assignment the control group starts with better (more negative) RVAC, which is the opposite of what the baseline sentence implies.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the baseline sentence used a different group coding, or the underlying data showing which assignment is correct and that the other is a typo (which would still leave a printed error).

quotes.text: RVAC was also similar at baseline (Rehabilitation: -0.96 (0.28)

issues.title: Mediation claim not tested: RVAC is the RVGLS/PASP ratio and no mediation analysis is reported
issues.explanation: The conclusion says rehabilitation improves RVAC by mediating afterload reduction and RV function. Only separate within-group changes and interaction tests are shown, and RVAC is by construction the ratio of the two components, so its change must follow from them. Nothing in the results tests a causal pathway; the PASP change itself was small (28 to 27 mmHg) and PASP showed no reported interaction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal mediation analysis or interaction test for PASP supporting the pathway.

quotes.text: by mediating both the RV afterload reduction (PASP) and improving RV function.
right ventricular-arterial coupling (RVAC) was estimated via the RVGLS/PASP ratio.

issues.title: Only 10 controls and no sample size justification or confidence intervals behind a confident conclusion
issues.explanation: The control group has 10 patients, no sample size calculation is given, and results are reported as means with SD and p values only. The absolute RVAC differences are small (e.g. -0.86 to -0.93), so the estimates are imprecise. This justifies describing the result as hypothesis-generating rather than the confident wording used.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample size calculation or confidence intervals showing adequate precision.

quotes.text: 40 convalescent COVID-19 patients were evaluated one and three months after the acute phase of the disease.
Cardiopulmonary rehabilitation can accelerate the improvement of RVAC

10.1093/eurheartj/ehaf784.3929.headline_claim: Individualised supervised aerobic and resistance exercise training (within a multidisciplinary programme) improves cardiorespiratory fitness in people with Long COVID.
10.1093/eurheartj/ehaf784.3929.overall: The headline finding of improved VO2peak in the intervention arm rests on a single primary outcome with a clear between-group difference (1.74 mL/kg/min, 95% CI 0.71 to 2.76), and appears reasonably reliable as far as an abstract allows. The main caveats are that the effect is of a bundled multidisciplinary intervention rather than exercise alone, and that the abstract lacks detail on blinding, analysis population and attrition (57/66 and 60/67 completed).

primary_outcome.name: Change in peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak)

issues.title: Title and conclusion credit exercise alone; arm also bundled medical management (50% / 27% of participants)
issues.explanation: The intervention arm combined supervised exercise with management of LV dysfunction and CV risk factors, and some participants started cardioprotective drugs. The comparison with usual care cannot separate exercise from these co-interventions. The Purpose discloses the bundle, but the title and Conclusion attribute the benefit to exercise training alone, a modest overreach.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A factorial or per-component analysis showing the medical management had no effect on VO2peak, or a conclusion worded as the multidisciplinary intervention.

quotes.text: received CV risk factor optimization (50%) or initiation of cardioprotective therapy (27%)
These results suggest that a carefully supervised and individualised exercise program improves cardiorespiratory ﬁtness in individuals with long COVID.

10.1093/eurjcn/zvag155.004.headline_claim: Tailored physical exercise is a relevant treatment option for COVID-19-related POTS, with significant within-group improvements in self-rated health, walking distance and orthostatic symptoms regardless of allocation, and exercise appears safe at group level.
10.1093/eurjcn/zvag155.004.overall: The abstract itself discloses that exercise did not outperform standard care on any outcome, so the finding is essentially null for the exercise component, and improvements in both arms cannot be attributed to the intervention. The recommendation that exercise remains a relevant treatment option and the safety statement go beyond what a 60-person trial with no printed between-group estimates can support. As a conference abstract, it omits detail (power, registration, adverse events) that the full paper may supply.

primary_outcome.name: Self-rated health measured by EQ-VAS

issues.title: Improvements reported within both arms (p<0.05) despite no between-group difference in any outcome
issues.explanation: Both arms improved on self-rated health, walking distance and orthostatic symptoms, and no between-group difference was found. Improvement in the standard-care arm shows that time, regression to the mean or natural recovery can explain the change, so within-group significance says nothing about exercise. The abstract does state the null comparison, so the problem is the interpretive emphasis rather than concealment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group estimate with CI showing a clinically relevant difference favouring exercise, or the conclusion being worded as no benefit over standard care.

quotes.text: There were significant improvements in self-rated health, walking distance, and orthostatic symptoms regardless of group allocation.
both groups showed significant improvements in self-rated health (p<0.05), with no between-group differences

issues.title: Null primary outcome (EQ-VAS) followed by 'relevant treatment option' conclusion
issues.explanation: The primary outcome showed no difference between exercise and standard care, yet the conclusion keeps exercise as a 'relevant treatment option'. The hedged wording and the stated need for responder analyses soften this, but the data presented give no evidence of benefit from the exercise component. The conclusion is therefore more favourable than the primary result supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified justification (e.g. responder hypothesis) or between-group estimates showing benefit in a subgroup defined in advance.

quotes.text: Tailored exercise may still be considered a relevant treatment option for PCC-related POTS

issues.title: 'Appeared safe' claimed from group-level means in 60 participants without adverse-event data
issues.explanation: The safety statement rests on the absence of deterioration in group-average outcomes. Averages can hide individual worsening, and the abstract reports no adverse events or post-exertional symptom data. The wording is cautious, so the overreach is modest.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adverse-event counts by arm with no excess in the exercise group.

quotes.text: At the group level, exercise appeared safe, with no evidence of deterioration in the assessed outcomes.

issues.title: No sample-size calculation reported; 54 of 60 analysed, null between-group results uninterpretable
issues.explanation: No power calculation is given in the abstract, so it cannot be judged whether 30 per arm could detect a meaningful EQ-VAS difference. With this size, 'no between-group difference' is not evidence of equivalence. The abstract format likely explains the omission.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A full-paper sample-size calculation based on a clinically important EQ-VAS difference with 30 per arm.

quotes.text: Of the 60 included participants, 54 completed the study

10.1093/europace/euad122.673.headline_claim: Individually tailored exercise was associated with increased time in upright position, reduction of POTS-specific symptoms and improved function in patients with COVID-19-related POTS, and the intervention seems feasible in terms of recruitment, compliance and safety.
10.1093/europace/euad122.673.overall: The paper is a small single-arm feasibility study, and its improvements cannot be attributed to the exercise because there is no control group. The conclusion is hedged ('associated with', 'further studies are needed'), so it is tentative at best. The safety statement is also thin given the unquantified post-exertional malaise.

primary_outcome.name: Time spent in upright position (h/day)

issues.title: Single-arm pre-post study (n=14) reports effects of training on upright time, symptoms and function
issues.explanation: All outcomes are baseline versus post-intervention in one group with no control arm. Natural recovery from post-COVID syndrome, regression to the mean, and expectation or placebo effects cannot be separated from any training effect. The wording 'associated with' is hedged, but the results are presented as effects of the exercise.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or waitlist control group, or a natural-history comparison showing the same patients were stable before the intervention.

quotes.text: Measurements were carried out at baseline and after intervention
individually tailored exercise was associated with increased time in upright position, reduction of POTS-speci fi c symptoms and improved function

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes a single group measured at baseline and after a 12-week intervention, with no control arm, and the authors say a comparison with and without intervention is still needed. The n=14 is the completers (1 of 15 enrolled did not complete), and results are from completers only. Claims of improvement are therefore pre-post changes that cannot be separated from natural recovery, regression to the mean or placebo/expectation effects, although the authors use the hedged wording 'associated with' and label the study a feasibility study. I could not check Table 1 or Figure 1 values bec

issues.title: Safety called acceptable in 14 patients despite unquantified post-exertional malaise and no control
issues.explanation: The Conclusion states the intervention seems feasible in terms of safety, while the Results mention that some patients described post-exertional malaise without giving a number or severity. With 14 participants and no comparator, the safety claim is imprecise and cannot show the training did not cause or worsen PEM. The efficacy wording overlap is covered by c1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported count and severity of PEM episodes, showing they were few, mild and transient, with safety stated with appropriate uncertainty.

quotes.text: The intervention seems to be feasible in terms of recruitment, compliance and safety.
some of the patients ' described PEM

10.1093/geroni/igaf122.4338.headline_claim: MY-Skills Mobile, a fully remote yoga and self-management intervention, is feasible and usable, shows preliminary improvements in symptoms, and represents an innovative, scalable model for populations with high symptom burden.
10.1093/geroni/igaf122.4338.overall: This is a brief abstract of two single-arm feasibility pilots, and its core claims (feasibility met, preliminary improvements, efficacy deferred to larger trials) are appropriately hedged. The closing 'scalable' wording overreaches slightly and the safety statement is under-explained, but neither undermines the feasibility conclusion. No effect sizes or statistics are given, so the reported improvements cannot be assessed from this text.

primary_outcome.name: Feasibility (recruitment, retention, attendance) with preliminary symptom change

issues.title: 'Scalable' model claim rests on pilots of 24 older adults and 9 long COVID patients
issues.explanation: The abstract's final conclusion calls MY-Skills Mobile a scalable model for populations with complex, overlapping health concerns. The evidence is two small single-arm pilots (24 older adults with 9 care partners, and 9 patients with long COVID), which assessed feasibility rather than scalability or generalisability. The wording is promotional and goes beyond the data, though the abstract does state that efficacy awaits fully powered trials.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full text showing that scalability was operationalised and assessed (e.g. delivery cost, reach, or implementation across sites), or the term being explicitly framed as a hypothesis.

quotes.text: MY-Skills Mobile represents an innovative, scalable model for delivering support to populations with complex, overlapping health concerns.
Future research will evaluate efficacy through fully powered trials.

issues.title: 'No adverse events' reported alongside five participants flagged for suicide-risk follow-up
issues.explanation: The abstract says no adverse events occurred but also that screening identified five participants needing follow-up. Those can be consistent if the flags reflect baseline risk and were handled by protocol, but the abstract does not explain the follow-up or how adverse events were defined. The safety statement is therefore not fully interpretable from the abstract.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full text defining adverse events and showing the five flags were baseline-present, handled by a stated safety protocol, and not attributed to the intervention.

quotes.text: No adverse events occurred, though suicide risk screening identified five participants needing follow-up.

10.1093/ofid/ofaf634.headline_claim: Distinct patient-reported outcome trajectories reflect the clinical heterogeneity of Long COVID, and NMV/r showed no clear benefit across subgroups.
10.1093/ofid/ofaf634.overall: This is a transparent exploratory descriptive analysis, and its main message (heterogeneous trajectories, no clear NMV/r benefit) is hedged appropriately. The headline null across subgroups rests on small classes and unreported arm comparisons, and the Discussion's causal and 'biphasic' statements go beyond what the design supports. Printed numerical slips (the 153 versus 155 count, 50.8% in n = 18, a heading that says three groups instead of four) are small and do not change the findings.'

primary_outcome.name: PGIS and PGIC trajectory groups (exploratory analysis; the trial's pooled core-symptom severity was its primary outcome)

issues.title: Discussion says findings 'demonstrate' natural recovery and a biphasic disease from 17-18-person improving groups
issues.explanation: There is no untreated control and both arms received ritonavir, so improvement cannot be separated from drug, placebo or natural course. Improving groups are small (17 for PGIS, 18 for PROMIS-PF). 'Similar improvement rates between arms' is not borne out by the fatigue classes (NMV/r 53.1% in improving vs 90% in severe). 'Biphasic condition' is inferred from a time-since-infection difference (373 vs 555 days) in 17 people.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A third untreated arm, or analyses showing the improvement rate is equal across arms with confidence intervals and adjusted for regression to the mean.

quotes.text: Our findings demonstrate that a subset of Long COVID patients experience natural improvement over time, independent of therapeutic intervention.
Although all participants received ritonavir, similar improvement rates between treatment arms suggest that observed recovery

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion's 'demonstrate' wording and 'independent of therapeutic intervention' go beyond what an exploratory, uncontrolled-for-natural-history analysis of 17-18 person improving groups can show, as all participants received ritonavir, no untreated arm exists, and the paper's own limitations concede the trajectories may not reflect pure natural history. The 'biphasic' conclusion rests on a time-since-infection difference that is large only in the 17-person PGIS group and is weaker or inconsistent in the other models, so it is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated finding. The 'similar improvem

issues.title: 'No clear benefit across subgroups' stated without any within-subgroup treatment comparison; groups of 17-30
issues.explanation: The abstract concludes NMV/r showed no clear benefit across subgroups, but no effect estimates or tests comparing arms within trajectory classes are given. Several classes are tiny (PGIS improving n = 17, PROMIS-PF severe n = 11) and the placebo arm has only 53 people. Absence of benefit in such groups is not informative either way; the null subgroup statement is under-supported rather than demonstrated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Arm-specific outcome estimates with confidence intervals within each class, or a pre-specified interaction test showing adequate precision.

quotes.text: NMV/r showed no clear benefit across subgroups.
Furthermore, the small sample size, particularly in the placebo arm due to the 2:1 randomization scheme, reduced our power.

issues.title: Arm proportions per trajectory class interpreted descriptively (e.g., NMV/r 90% vs 53% in fatigue classes) without testing
issues.explanation: The paper reports NMV/r proportions across data-derived classes using standardised differences only, and the abstract highlights that worsening groups had more NMV/r participants. With classes of 22 or 30 people, differences such as 81.8% vs 63.8% could easily arise by chance, so neither harm nor 'alignment with the primary trial' is established. The analysis is exploratory and says so, which makes this a matter of interpretation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal test of arm by class association showing the differences within chance.

quotes.text: The proportion of participants receiving NMV/r was higher in the severe fatigue group (90%)

issues.title: Female share 50.8% impossible for improving PROMIS-PF group of n = 18 (9/18 = 50.0%, 10/18 = 55.6%)
issues.explanation: With 18 participants the achievable percentages are 50.0% and 55.6%, so 50.8% cannot be a share of this group. The other groups' percentages are internally consistent, so this one value is misprinted. The ASD of 0.494 and the sex-difference description rest on it, but the qualitative point survives.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary Table 9 showing a different n for the improving group, or a denominator other than 18 for the sex row.

quotes.text: or improving (50.8%) groups (ASD = 0.494, Supplementary Table 9)
one group with what appears to have improving PROMIS-PF scores ( n = 18)

issues.title: Follow-up count 153 (=102+53 printed) does not add up; fatigue groups total 155 despite 'unclassifiable' rule
issues.explanation: The Results say 153 participants had follow-up, 'comprising 102 NMV/r and 53 PBO/r', but 102 + 53 = 155. The fatigue groups also total 155, although the Methods say participants without follow-up could not be classified. PGIS classes sum to 153 and PGIC to 152. The follow-up count and the classification rule cannot all be right, though the effect on findings is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that all 155 had follow-up data for core symptoms, with 153 referring to a different outcome.

quotes.text: of which 153 had at least one follow-up observation, comprising 102 NMV/r participants and 53 PBO/r participants
one with what appears to be stable and severe fatigue ( n = 30, Supplementary Figure 9)

issues.title: PROMIS-PF results heading says three groups; abstract and text report four
issues.explanation: The Results heading refers to three PROMIS-Physical Function groups, but the abstract and body describe four (improving, normal/mild, moderate, severe) with sizes 18, 13, 111 and 11. The heading is simply wrong. No result depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the final model had three groups, which the abstract, text and group sizes contradict.

quotes.text: Trajectory Modeling Identifies Three Participant Groups of PROMIS-Physical Function
For PROMIS-PF, four trajectories were identified

10.1093/ptj/pzad118.headline_claim: Both telerehabilitation exercise modalities (functional and aerobic, each with breathing techniques) are effective at improving stress symptoms and quality of life in long COVID, with functional exercise more promising for fatigue and functional performance.
10.1093/ptj/pzad118.overall: Neither exercise modality was shown to differ from the other (all interaction tests null), and with no control arm the within-group improvements cannot establish effectiveness. The conclusions that both programmes are effective and that FE is more promising go beyond the data. Several printed statistics are also inconsistent: the FE stress CI, the F df, the PSS range, and the dyspnea MCID statement.

primary_outcome.name: Fatigue (Fatigue Assessment Scale)

primary_outcomes.time_frame: It will be evaluated in two moments: Pre intervention: before starting the exercise program Post intervention: after 8 weeks of physiotherapy intervention

issues.title: FE called 'more promising' for fatigue and function despite null between-group tests (P = .675, .387)
issues.explanation: The fatigue score (the sample-size outcome) and the 30-second sit-to-stand test show no significant group-by-time interaction. The only support for FE superiority is that its within-group change was significant while AE's was not. A significant change in one arm and a non-significant change in the other is not evidence that the arms differ. The Conclusions and Impact sections therefore overstate what the head-to-head comparison showed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group test (e.g., ANCOVA on post-treatment fatigue) showing a significant FE advantage.

quotes.text: No significant differences in the intergroup effect were identified for the studied variables.
For improving fatigue and functional performance, FE shows more promising results.

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions call FE 'more promising' for fatigue and function although the paper's own between-group tests were null (P=.675 and .387) and the AE group also reached the fatigue MCID; the claim rests on FE reaching within-group significance while AE did not, which is not evidence of a between-group difference. The Discussion does say no interaction was found, but the Conclusions do not carry that caveat.

issues.title: 'Both modalities effective' for stress and QoL rests on within-arm change with no control group
issues.explanation: The trial compares two active exercise programmes with no untreated or usual-care arm, and no between-group difference was found. The claim that both programmes are effective for stress and quality of life rests on pre-post changes within each arm, which cannot show an effect of treatment. The quality-of-life claim also rests on a mean change of 0.1 with CIs spanning zero in both arms. The limitation is disclosed, but the conclusion is stated without qualification.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A contemporaneous untreated or usual-care comparison group, or a conclusion worded as pre-post change only.

quotes.text: the absence of a control group, which was not considered in this study
Both telerehabilitation exercise modalities are effective at improving stress symptoms and quality of life in patients with long COVID-19.

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that both modalities are 'effective' for stress and QoL rests solely on within-arm pre-post change in a two-arm trial with no untreated or usual-care control, so change over time cannot be separated from natural recovery, regression to the mean or non-specific effects. For QoL the within-group tests were not significant (P=.306 and .145) and 'effective' relies on exceeding an MCID threshold; the authors acknowledge the lack of a control group but still state the effectiveness conclusion without qualification.

issues.title: FE perceived stress CI -9.1 to 0.8 is off-centre around -4.9 and contradicts p = .021
issues.explanation: The FE group's perceived-stress change is printed as -4.9 with a 95% CI of -9.1 to 0.8, which includes zero, yet the same row gives P = .021 and the text calls it an improvement. The interval is centred on -4.15, not -4.9, and a CI of -9.1 to -0.8 would be centred on -4.95 and match the p-value. The most likely cause is a missing minus sign, a printed error that does not change the substantive result. The FE LCADL row (-0.9, CI -4.9 to 6.7, centre +0.9) also looks sign-shifted.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors' output showing the CI really is -9.1 to 0.8 with a p of .021 from a different test.

quotes.text: perceived stress (-4.9 points; 95% CI = -9.1 to 0.8)

script.explanation: the p-value recovered from the CI is 0.0524 (reachable range [0.0477, 0.0573] across the printed precision of the estimate and its bounds), but p = 0.021 is reported -- this recovery inverts a WALD interval, so if the paper used a bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood or Fieller interval the two numbers are not comparable; confirm the method before treating this as a finding; the CI includes the null (0.0), but the reported p = 0.021 says the result is significant

issues.title: Paper's primary outcome (fatigue, FAS) differs from registered primary (EQ-5D-5L quality of life)
issues.explanation: The sample size and the 'Primary Outcome' section in the paper are based on the Fatigue Assessment Scale, but the ClinicalTrials.gov record lists quality of life (EQ-5D-5L) as the primary outcome. The change is not explained in the paper. Neither outcome shows a between-group difference, so the effect on the conclusions is limited, but quality of life is promoted as an effective result in the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version listing fatigue as primary, or a protocol amendment before data collection.

quotes.text: Considering that a 4-point difference in the Fatigue Assessment Scale is considered to be a minimal clinically important difference (MCID)
The study protocol was registered prospectively on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04996212).

issues.title: Interaction F(1,82) does not fit 43 analysed participants; mixed ANOVA error df should be 41
issues.explanation: Table 2 reports every group-by-time interaction as F(1,82), but the analysis set is 43 participants analysed with a two-way mixed ANOVA. The expected error df is N - 2 = 41. A df of 82 suggests repeated measurements may have been treated as independent, or the df is mislabelled. The p-values barely change here (F near 0.2 to 1.3), so the between-group conclusions are not materially affected, but the reported analysis cannot be reproduced as described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the model used a different structure (e.g., mixed model on stacked observations) that legitimately gives 82 error df.

quotes.text: Therefore, 43 participants were considered for the analysis of this study

issues.title: 'No clinical changes' in dyspnea although AE LCADL change (-5.6, % -7.5) exceeds stated MCIDs
issues.explanation: The Discussion says no significant or clinical dyspnea changes were found. The AE group's mean LCADL change was -5.6 points (MCID -3) and -7.5% (MCID -4), both beyond the MCID, and Table 2 does not flag them as meeting it. The CIs touch zero and the MCID comparison is on the mean only, so the problem is a mislabelled secondary result, which understates a possible AE benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated rule that MCID is judged on the CI bound or the median rather than the mean change.

quotes.text: Regarding dyspnea in ADL, no significant or clinical changes were found.
The MCIDs for this questionnaire were -3 points and - 4 points

issues.title: Per-protocol analysis only: 43 of 48 randomised (10.4% lost), no ITT analysis
issues.explanation: The analysis includes only participants who completed the programme, and the authors give no intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis. Losing 5 of 48 after randomisation can bias within-group improvements upwards if non-completers did worse. The loss is small, so this weakens the secondary and within-group claims rather than overturning them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ITT or multiple-imputation analysis giving similar results, or dropouts balanced across arms with no baseline differences.

quotes.text: A per-protocol analysis was performed inclusive of the participants who completed the treatment plan.
Finally, 43 completed the study (FE group, n = 21; AE group, n = 22).

issues.title: PSS described as 14 items scored 0-4 (max 56) but reported on a 0-40 scale
issues.explanation: The Methods describe a 14-item PSS scored 0-4 per item, a maximum of 56, but the tables label the scale 0-40 and the cut-offs end at 40. Either the instrument is the 10-item version or the range is wrong. Reported scores (e.g., baseline 31.0) are in the range of both, so the effect is a description error that makes the instrument unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confirmation that the 10-item PSS was used and the text description is a typo.

quotes.text: The Perceived Stress Scale consists of 14 items
PSS (0-40), mean (SD)

10.1093/qjmed/hcaf050.headline_claim: Intravenous laser irradiation of blood (ILIB) shows potential in improving cognitive function and sleep quality, and may be an effective option for cognitive impairment and sleep disturbance in long COVID, likely via mitochondrial, immune and oxidative-stress pathways.
10.1093/qjmed/hcaf050.overall: The paper is a six-patient, uncontrolled, open-label pilot, and its conclusion is hedged appropriately in its final sentence. The text-table mismatches in MoCA/AIS values and the contradictory direction of the oxidative phosphorylation pathways reduce confidence in the reporting itself. The clinical improvements and mechanistic claims are best treated as hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: change in cognitive function (MoCA and MMSE)

issues.title: Single-arm, six-patient pilot with no control or sample-size justification cannot attribute changes to ILIB
issues.explanation: All six patients received ILIB, and the results are within-person pre/post comparisons by paired t-tests. Without a comparator, the improvements may reflect expectation, natural recovery or test practice. With n=6, no sample-size calculation and several uncorrected comparisons, the p-values of 0.01-0.03 are fragile. The authors acknowledge this and call the study a pilot, so it is tentative support at most. The efficacy language in the Discussion goes further than the design allows.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group, or sham-controlled data showing comparable change.

quotes.text: However, given the small sample size and lack of a control group, these findings should be interpreted with caution.
This prospective, single-center pilot study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of ILIB in alleviating cognitive dysfunction

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, open-label, six-patient pilot with no control group and no stated sample-size justification, so the pre/post changes cannot be attributed to ILIB (natural recovery, practice effects, expectation and regression to the mean are not separable). The authors do acknowledge this in the Conclusion and Limitations, so the limitation is disclosed rather than ignored, but the Abstract-level and Discussion language ('ILIB may be an effective therapeutic option', 'mechanism of action') still reads more causally than the design supports.

issues.title: Transcriptomic mechanism claims: oxidative phosphorylation 'upregulated' in text but 'downregulated' in Fig 2; no controls
issues.explanation: The Results text says mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation pathways were upregulated, while the Figure 2 legend says the same pathways were downregulated after ILIB. This undermines the claim of enhanced mitochondrial function. The comparison has no untreated or sham arm (the Figure 2 legend even mentions 'untreated patients', though all were treated), and sample numbers for RNA-seq are not given. The text also refers to a 'reduction in inflammatory markers' and says it correlates with AIS, yet no inflammatory markers or correlations are reported. The mechanism claims are therefore speculative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary data showing the direction of oxidative phosphorylation genes is consistent and a defined comparator (time-matched controls or variance partitioning) for the DE analysis.

quotes.text: significantly upregulated pathways included the mitochondrial electron transport
quotes.location: Results, Gene expression and pathway analysis

quotes.text: (C) KEGG pathway enrichment analysis highlighting pathways significantly downregulated after ILIB treatment, including oxidative phosphorylation
reinforcing the robust impact of ILIB on gene expression
quotes.location: Results, Gene expression and pathway analysis

second_reader.what_stands: As printed, the same oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial electron transport and glutathione terms are called upregulated in the Results text and Figure 3 but downregulated in the Figure 2 legend, and the direction of the compared contrasts (R1-R0 vs R0-R2) is not clarified, so the claimed 'enhanced mitochondrial function' is not supported by a consistent direction. In addition, there is no control group (comparisons are pre vs post in six patients), so the statement that the data show a 'robust impact of ILIB on gene expression' and a mechanism of action is not warranted; I could not dete

issues.title: Results text gives MoCA/AIS post-ILIB-1 SDs (3.1; 2.3) that match Table 1's Post-ILIB-2 column, not Post-ILIB-1
issues.explanation: The text reports MoCA after the first set of sessions as 26.8 (SD 3.1) and AIS as 11.4 (SD 2.3). Table 1's Post-ILIB-1 column gives 26.8 (3.8) and 11 (4.2). The text SDs match the Post-ILIB-2 column (3.1 and 2.3), and the text AIS mean of 11.4 matches no column (8.8 at ILIB-2). So the text and table disagree on which time point each figure belongs to, and the AIS mean is not in the table at all. The P values quoted in the text (0.03, 0.02) are those for the Post-ILIB-1 comparison, so the reader cannot tell which dataset they refer to.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrigendum or the raw data showing the table columns or text values were mislabelled and which set is correct.

quotes.text: 26.8 (SD ¼ 3.1) after the first set of ILIB sessions
quotes.location: Results, Cognitive function and sleep quality

quotes.text: 11.4 (SD ¼ 2.3) after the first ILIB session
quotes.location: Results, Cognitive function and sleep quality

issues.title: Open-label assessment with self-reported AIS (17.8 to 8.4) is open to expectation bias
issues.explanation: All assessments were unblinded, and sleep outcomes are patient-reported. A treatment involving an intravenous catheter and 30 one-hour sessions is likely to raise expectations. The authors mention open-label bias only briefly in the limitations while drawing a conclusion about sleep.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded outcome assessment or sham control showing the same AIS change.

quotes.text: the open-label design may introduce bias

issues.title: Efficacy-leaning wording in a six-patient uncontrolled pilot, though the conclusion is hedged
issues.explanation: The final conclusion is cautious and carries the right caveats, which is largely adequate. The earlier text, however, leans toward efficacy. This is a matter of degree rather than a clear overstatement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: N/A; depends on reader judgement of the wording.

quotes.text: ILIB appears to be a promising intervention for alleviating

issues.title: MMSE (co-primary) null result downplayed; MoCA favoured post hoc
issues.explanation: The opening Results sentence says cognition improved as measured by MoCA and MMSE, but MMSE did not change (P 0.25-0.79). The authors explain this by a ceiling effect and then support MoCA as the more sensitive tool. This is disclosed, but the explanation is post hoc and the headline cognitive claim rests on one of two co-primary measures.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified plan naming MoCA as the primary cognitive outcome.

quotes.text: As measured by the MoCA and MMSE, cognitive function showed significant improvement following ILIB treatment in Table 1.
quotes.location: Results, Cognitive function and sleep quality

quotes.text: However, changes in MMSE scores were not statistically significant ( P > 0.05).
quotes.location: Results, Cognitive function and sleep quality

10.1093/sleep/zsaf090.1410.headline_claim: Screening and treating comorbid obstructive sleep apnea with CPAP in post-COVID patients can improve cognitive fog.
10.1093/sleep/zsaf090.1410.overall: This is a single-arm, 14-patient pre/post abstract, so it can show that scores moved after CPAP but not that CPAP caused the change. Practice effects, expectation and natural recovery are not excluded, outcomes are uncorrected for multiplicity, and dropouts are not described. The conclusion is only tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Cognitive fog, assessed by a neuropsychological battery and MoCA (no single primary outcome named)

issues.title: Causal CPAP benefit inferred from 14 patients' pre/post scores with no control group
issues.explanation: Cognitive tests and questionnaires were taken at baseline and about 4 weeks after starting CPAP, in one group with no untreated or sham comparison. Practice effects on repeated neuropsychological tests, expectation on self-reported scales, and spontaneous improvement in post-COVID symptoms would all produce the same gains. Only 14 completers were analysed, which makes the estimates imprecise as well. The data cannot support the conclusion that CPAP improves cognitive fog beyond being compatible with it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control or sham-CPAP arm, or an untreated waiting period showing stable scores, with the same improvement seen only under CPAP.

quotes.text: at baseline and 4±2 weeks after starting CPAP.
Our findings suggest screening and treating

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract reports a single-arm pre/post comparison of 14 completers with no control group, yet concludes that screening and treating OSA 'can improve cognitive fog', which is a causal claim the design cannot support because practice effects, expectancy, regression to the mean and non-completer attrition are not addressed. The cautious 'suggest' wording and the dose-response correlations soften but do not remove this; the abstract's brevity may explain why limitations are not discussed, but none are stated.

issues.title: About 13 outcomes and 2 correlations tested uncorrected; Benson p=0.047 and TMT-A r p=0.048 are marginal
issues.explanation: The abstract lists some 13 cognitive and symptom outcomes and two correlations with nominal p-values and no primary outcome or multiplicity correction. The strongest results (p<0.01) may well hold up. The Benson delayed recall (p=0.047) and the TMT-A correlation (p=0.048) would not survive any correction. The conclusion of general cognitive improvement relies on the whole set.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome, or a correction showing the main findings remain significant.

quotes.text: Benson complex figure-delayed (13.9±0.6 vs 12.3±0.5, p=0.047)
Trial Making test A (r=-0.58, p=0.048)

issues.title: Only 14 completers analysed; number enrolled and dropouts not reported
issues.explanation: Results are for patients who completed the study, and the number recruited or lost to follow-up is not given. If some patients stopped CPAP or withdrew, the analysis keeps only those who tolerated treatment, which favours a positive result. Mean CPAP use of 5.8±2.6 hours suggests variable adherence among completers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A report that all recruited patients completed follow-up, or an analysis including all those who started CPAP.

quotes.text: Among 14 patients who completed the study

10.1097/cm9.0000000000003459.headline_claim: In hospitalized convalescent COVID-19 patients, UC-MSC infusion with standard care was safe and showed a trend of improvement in lung lesion resolution and pulmonary function over one year.
10.1097/cm9.0000000000003459.overall: The safety finding is reasonably supported, but the efficacy findings come from an unadjusted comparison with a retrospectively selected, imbalanced external control, with differential follow-up and uncorrected multiple testing. The authors hedge the final conclusion as a trend, so they should be read as hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; lung lesion change and pulmonary function are the emphasised outcomes
