10.1186/s13102-024-00909-2.headline_claim: Inpatient post-COVID rehabilitation did not improve objectively measured physical activity or sleep quality; patients remain highly inactive with poor sleep quality, and aftercare strategies are needed.
10.1186/s13102-024-00909-2.overall: The descriptive finding that PA and sleep medians barely changed between T1 and T2, and that sleep was poor, is well supported by the printed numbers. Reading that as rehabilitation having no effect, and recommending program changes, rests on a single-arm design with non-significant tests, and the group-difference results are unadjusted for multiplicity. The numeric slips are minor and affect no main result.

primary_outcome.name: Accelerometer-measured physical activity (inactivity time) and sleep parameters before vs after rehabilitation

issues.title: Dozens of unadjusted subgroup tests at alpha 0.05; scattered p = 0.01 to 0.04 reported as differences
issues.explanation: The authors test sex, age, severity and four comorbidities on 4 PA and 6 sleep outcomes, at T1, T2 and over time. They use an unadjusted alpha of 0.05. Several findings that the Abstract highlights have p = 0.01 to 0.04 (for example p = 0.038 for sex and inactivity, p = 0.010 for age and vigorous PA, and the comorbidity findings at p = 0.020 to 0.033). With this many comparisons, a few such p-values would be expected by chance, and the paper does not label the comparisons as exploratory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified multiplicity strategy, or labelling of these analyses as hypothesis-generating.

quotes.text: The level of signicance was set at p < 0.05.
The results did just show a signicant difference in vigorous PA (T1) for cardiovascular disease

issues.title: Single-arm pre/post study with non-significant tests read as showing rehabilitation had no effect
issues.explanation: With no control group, the data cannot separate rehabilitation effects from natural course, home-environment effects or post-discharge timing. The paper acknowledges this in the limitations, but the Abstract and Conclusion state flatly that PA and sleep did not improve after rehabilitation. A non-significant test is not evidence of no effect, and the paper reports no equivalence or interval estimates for the changes. The observed stability is real. Attributing it to the rehabilitation program is only tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified equivalence margin or a control comparison showing that the change is indistinguishable from zero or from untreated patients.

quotes.text: Nevertheless, under consideration of an observational study design without control group, the results should be interpreted with caution.
Even if there was no signicant difference in (in)activity levels after the rehabilitation program (p > 0.05)

issues.title: Recommendation to refocus rehabilitation on PA and sleep goes beyond uncontrolled data
issues.explanation: The paper concludes that rehabilitation should focus more on sleep and PA behaviour. The study did not test any intervention, and the program was explicitly not designed to improve sleep. The poor absolute levels are a reasonable descriptive basis for concern. They do not show that the existing program under-delivers or that a changed program would help.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled evidence that a modified program improves PA or sleep, or wording that frames this as a hypothesis.

quotes.text: the post-COVID rehabilitation program should focus more on a better treatment of sleep disturbances
the change of PA behaviour and how to acquire a good sleep hygiene should be addressed during inpatient rehabilitation in a more targeted and wellfounded manner

issues.title: Group-comparison n in Methods (sums to 100) differ from those in Results (sum to 98 paired)
issues.explanation: Section 2.4 gives group sizes summing to 100 for the Mann-Whitney comparisons (46/54 by age, 71/29 by severity, 27/73 by sex). The Results use the paired sample of 98 (46/52, 69/29, 27/71). The paper does not say that the group sizes were reduced, and the Methods wrongly state the n used for the tests. This is a labelling inconsistency, and the conclusions do not change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the Methods or Table A1-A14 that the group tests were run on the 98 paired patients, with the group n printed.

quotes.text: younger than 55 (n = 46) vs. at least 55 years (n = 54)
older ( ≥ 55 years, n = 52)
The paired study sample consist of 27 male and 71 female patients.

issues.title: No primary outcome stated; registration date and registered outcomes not reported
issues.explanation: The study cites DRKS 00022928 but does not state a primary outcome, the registration date, or whether PA and sleep were the registered outcomes. Readers cannot judge whether the reported analyses were pre-specified. This is a reporting gap, not demonstrated outcome switching.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The registry entry showing PA and sleep as registered outcomes and a registration date before enrolment.

quotes.text: It is registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under DRKS 00022928.

issues.title: Age-group summaries internally impossible: identical medians 5.91 h, and IQR upper bound 0.013 below median 0.07
issues.explanation: The Results give younger and older patients the same sleep-duration median (5.91 h) while reporting a significant difference. The Discussion gives about 5 hours for older patients. For vigorous PA, the older group's IQR ends at 0.013, below its median of 0.07. These are reporting errors in the group results, and the underlying tests cannot be checked from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary Tables A3-A4 showing different medians and IQRs from those in the text.

quotes.text: than older patients (Mdn = 5.91 h, IQR: 3.98-6.45, p = 0.012)
than older patients (Mdn = 0.07 min, IQR: 0.04 - 0.013, p = 0.010)

issues.title: Rehabilitation duration mean 28.84 days in Methods vs 28.88 days in Table 1
issues.explanation: The text and Table 1 give different means for the same variable, with the same SD. The difference is trivial and affects no result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the two values come from different analysis sets.

quotes.text: with a mean duration of 28.84 ± 5.16 days

10.1186/s13223-022-00711-0.headline_claim: Intranasal 1% tetra sodium pyrophosphate improves olfactory function (anosmia to hyposmia) after persistent post-COVID-19 olfactory dysfunction and is associated with reduced nasal calcium.
10.1186/s13223-022-00711-0.overall: The direction of the finding (larger TDI gain and calcium fall with TSPP than saline) is plausible given the large reported effects, but the paper's own numbers are not fully reproducible: ΔTDI means do not match pre/post means in either arm, the text and Table 2 disagree on non-responders, and the reported p-values and df do not match the t statistics. There is no registration or sample-size justification, and the Results state a calcium-chelation mechanism and clinical relevance more strongly than the data support, so conclusions should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Change in Snifin' Sticks TDI olfactory score (ΔTDI) before vs after treatment

issues.title: No trial registry identifier; ethics approval number given under 'Trial registration'
issues.explanation: The abstract's trial-registration entry is an ethics approval number, and no registry entry appears in the paper. Without registration the primary outcome, the analysis plan and the sample size cannot be verified as prespecified. That matters here because several outcomes (TDI subscores, calcium, sex subgroups) are tested and none is declared primary.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective registry record (e.g. ClinicalTrials.gov or PACTR) with a matching primary outcome.

quotes.text: Ethical Committee of Damietta Faculty of Medicine approved this study on January 2021 (approval number, IRB 00012367-21-03-010).

issues.title: Mean ΔTDI does not equal post minus pre means: TSPP 5.41 vs 5.55; saline 0.23 vs 0.16
issues.explanation: The paper defines ΔTDI as post minus pre TDI. In both arms the printed pre and post means imply a different mean change from the one reported in Table 2. The gaps are well beyond rounding. The key between-group ΔTDI comparison therefore uses values that cannot be reproduced from the paper's own table, so the reported change scores or the pre/post means are in error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that ΔTDI was computed on a subset of patients, or corrected Table 2 values consistent with the pre and post means.

quotes.text: the mean±SD of the TDI value before and after receiving TSPP was 11.28±0.79 and 16.83±2.13
the mean±SD of the TDI value before and receiving sodium chloride was 11.10±0.99 and 11.26±0.72

issues.title: No sample-size calculation (n=32/arm) while Results claim a 'relevant clinical improvement'
issues.explanation: The sample-size section gives no target effect, alpha or power, and 64 patients were simply 'selected' from 400 screened. The authors acknowledge the small sample as the major limitation, yet the Results declare a clinically relevant improvement. The study is a small, single-centre, 1-month trial. The apparent effect is large, so this weakens precision and generalisability more than it undermines the direction of the finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or sample-size justification stating the target effect and power.

quotes.text: Te major limitation is the small sample size, which predisposed to an underpowered analysis.
A total of 400 patients were screened for eligibility. Tus, 64 patients were selected for the study and randomly allocated to 2 groups.

issues.title: Results assert calcium-chelation mechanism and 'relevant clinical improvement' without mediation or MCID analysis
issues.explanation: The Results state that TSPP chelated calcium and masked its adverse effect on olfaction, and that the improvement was clinically relevant. No analysis links individual calcium change to TDI change, and no minimal clinically important difference is defined. The Discussion and abstract correctly hedge this as an association, so the overstatement is confined to the Results wording. The mean post-treatment TDI of 16.83 sits only just above the 16.75 hyposmia cut-off.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported analysis linking within-patient calcium change to TDI change, and a predefined clinically important TDI difference.

quotes.text: TSPP had the ability to chelate calcium from the nasal secretions and mask the adverse efect of calcium on the olfactory function.
It could be concluded that there may be an association between the decrease of calcium concentration in the nasal secretions by the TSPP and the increase in the measured olfactory score

issues.title: TSPP non-improvers: text says 5 (19%), Table 2 shows 6 still anosmic; 26+5=31, not 32
issues.explanation: The Results text says 26 TSPP patients improved and 5 did not. That sums to 31 of 32 randomized patients, and 5 of 32 is not 19%. Table 2 lists 6 patients still anosmic and 26 hyposmic after treatment (32 in total), which matches the printed 19%. The text count is therefore a reporting slip. The headline percentages are not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that one TSPP patient was excluded or missing from the post-treatment olfactory classification.

quotes.text: 26 patients (81%) showed an improved olfactory function from anosmia to hyposmia stage and 5 patients (19%) did not show improvement
81% showed improved olfactory function and 19% did not exhibit olfaction improvement.

issues.title: Reported p=0.0008 and 0.0006 are inconsistent with t=11.25 and t=8.39; df printed as 32 for 64 patients
issues.explanation: The unpaired t-tests are reported as t(32)=11.25, p=0.0008 and t(32)=8.39, p=0.0006. Statistics of this size give p-values many orders of magnitude smaller, and an unpaired test of 32 vs 32 has 62 df, not 32. The conclusion of significance holds, but the printed p-values and df are not reliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that these tests were run with a different statistic or a corrected multiplicity adjustment explaining the larger p.

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.0008, but recomputed from the printed t = 11.25 p is at most 1.191e-12, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show. This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Text swaps the sex split of the two arms relative to Table 1 (TSPP 18F/14M in text, 20F/12M in tables)
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the TSPP ('study') group as 18 females and 14 males and the control as 20 females and 12 males. Table 1 and Table 2 give the opposite: saline 14 males/18 females, TSPP 12 males/20 females. The age means in the text do match the table by arm. This is a labelling slip with no bearing on the efficacy result, though the sex-stratified TSPP results in Table 2 use the table's version.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 'study group' in the text refers to the saline arm.

quotes.text: the control group included 32 patients (20 females and 12 males)

10.1186/s13287-023-03522-1.headline_claim: Multiple infusions of autologous adipose-derived MSCs (HB-adMSCs) improved signs and symptoms of post-COVID-19 syndrome and were well tolerated over 40 weeks.
10.1186/s13287-023-03522-1.overall: The data show that nine of ten patients reported lower symptom and fatigue scores at week 40 than at baseline, but the design (single arm, unblinded, self-rated outcomes, n=10) cannot show that the cells caused this. The numerical slips (FAS median, AE percentage, effect-size N) are small and do not change the picture. The conclusion's wording of 'reversing' and 'sustainability' goes further than the design allows, though the authors do call for a controlled trial.

primary_outcome.name: Total VAS score and total FAS score (pre-post change)

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from uncontrolled, unblinded pre-post change in 10 patients with self-rated outcomes
issues.explanation: All 10 patients received the product and efficacy rests on Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons of baseline versus week 40 on patient-reported VAS, FAS and SF-36. With no control arm and no blinding, natural recovery from post-COVID symptoms, regression to the mean and expectation effects cannot be separated from a treatment effect. No sample size calculation is given, and with n=10 the p-values (0.0039 is the minimum attainable with 9 pairs) say only that nearly all patients improved. Only a tentative signal is supported, not efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical matched control cohort, or blinded assessment, showing that improvement exceeds natural recovery over 40 weeks.

quotes.text: no placebo comparator to evaluate
The primary goal of the expanded access program was overall comparison before and after HB-adMSC therapy

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from an uncontrolled, single-arm before-after comparison in 10 patients (9 analysed at EOS), with outcomes that are all patient-reported questionnaires and no blinding described. The authors acknowledge the small sample and the lack of a comparator, but not the absence of blinding or the self-reported nature of the outcomes. They still use efficacy language ('significant improvements', 'clinically relevant'). One caveat: the paper itself presents this as an expanded access program and calls for a placebo-controlled trial.

issues.title: Conclusion asserts reversal and 40-week therapeutic sustainability from an uncontrolled 10-patient series
issues.explanation: The Conclusions say the infusions improved and reversed signs and symptoms and implicated therapeutic sustainability over 40 weeks. The data are within-patient before/after differences in 10 patients (9 at the end), without a control. Last measurements at week 40 cannot separate sustained drug effect from spontaneous resolution, and the call for a randomized trial is the appropriate level of claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data showing the post-treatment trajectory differs from untreated post-COVID patients over the same 40 weeks.

quotes.text: improving and reversing associated signs and symptoms
implicated therapeutic sustainability

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions assert 'improving and reversing' signs and symptoms and 'therapeutic sustainability' over 40 weeks based on an uncontrolled series of 10 patients (9 at EOS), with no comparator and no pre-COVID baseline. Observed improvement at week 40 cannot be separated from natural recovery, so causal reversal and sustained therapeutic effect are not established by the design. The wording is softened by 'implicated', 'strong suggestion' and the call for a placebo-controlled trial, so the overreach is in the strength of the first sentence, not the paper's overall framing.

issues.title: Primary 'total VAS' is an unvalidated composite of symptom ratings with no stated construction or threshold
issues.explanation: The primary endpoint total VAS sums separate symptom ratings, but the paper does not say how many items are summed, whether the total has been validated, or what change is clinically meaningful. The drop from 37.6 to 4.90 is therefore hard to interpret, though the size of the change makes it unlikely to be a measurement artefact alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or reference describing the total VAS as a pre-specified, validated composite with a defined minimal clinically important difference.

quotes.text: on the scale from zero to ten centimeters
total VAS scores at each visit

issues.title: Baseline FAS total median is 32.5 in Results text but 33.0 in Table 2
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the baseline FAS total median as 32.5, while Table 2 prints 33.0 for the same cell. The IQR (27.0-35.0) is identical in both places. This is a small reporting slip in a primary endpoint. The direction and size of the change (about -17 points) are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing the baseline median is the value printed in one place, plus an erratum noting the other as a typo (which would still leave the inconsistency).

quotes.location: Table 2, FAS total row, Baseline column

issues.title: First author employed by the funder declares 'no competing interests'
issues.explanation: The first author is an employee of the foundation that funded the study, yet declares no competing interests, while three co-authors who work for the product company do declare theirs. The facts are all disclosed, so readers can assess them, but the statement is internally inconsistent with common practice. Authors' roles in design, analysis and writing are mostly with funder employees.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Journal or institutional policy that employment by a non-profit research foundation funder is not classed as a competing interest.

quotes.text: declares no competing interests that could have appeared to influence the work
funded in whole by Hope Biosciences Research Foundation

issues.title: Effect sizes computed with N=10 although EOS comparisons rest on N=9 (Table 3)
issues.explanation: Table 3 gives the end-of-study N as 9, and the exact Wilcoxon p-values (0.0039, 0.0078) match nine pairs. The effect-size footnote says N=10 was used, so the reported effect sizes are slightly smaller than N=9 would give. The effect is minor: all are large either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that Rosenthal's N was deliberately set to the enrolled number, or SF-36 EOS data for all 10 participants.

quotes.text: EOS Median (IQR) N = 9
ES = Effect Size (Rosenthal's formula with N = 10 subjects)

10.1186/s13287-025-04148-1.headline_claim: MSC therapy offers long-term safety and potential therapeutic benefit in severe COVID-19, aiding recovery from lung damage and enhancing quality of life in patients with Long COVID.
10.1186/s13287-025-04148-1.overall: The safety conclusion rests on mostly null comparisons with some unreconciled complication counts (34 vs 49 entries), and the efficacy claims are weaker than stated. The lung recovery claim is not supported by the non-significant CT results, and the quality-of-life claim rests on one uncorrected, patient-reported GH score collected after unblinding. A competing-interest declaration that contradicts the stated employment of three authors adds further caution.

primary_outcome.name: No prespecified primary outcome; 36-month normal lung CT (Table 1) is the lead efficacy result, with SF-36 general health also headlined

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in lesion proportion (%) of full lung volume from baseline to day 28.

issues.title: GH score, the only significant efficacy result, is patient-reported and collected after unblinding in June 2020
issues.explanation: Blinding ended on June 23, 2020, but the 36-month SF-36 was collected in March to May 2023. The general health score (12.86 difference, p = 0.0278) is patient-reported and so open to expectation bias. The Conclusions nonetheless say MSC enhances quality of life for Long COVID patients. The limitations section mentions self-report but not the loss of blinding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that participants and assessors remained unaware of allocation at 36 months, or a blinded objective measure showing the same benefit.

quotes.text: Both patients and investigators remained blinded in this trial until June 23, 2020
The general health (GH) score in the MSC group
quotes.location: Results, Impact of MSC to Long COVID

second_reader.what_stands: The GH score is a self-reported SF-36 measure collected in 2023, nearly three years after the stated unblinding on June 23, 2020, so it was collected after unblinding and is open to information bias, as the authors themselves acknowledge. The phrase 'the only significant efficacy result' is too strong: GH is the only significant overall SF-36 domain, but the paper also prints other nominal p < 0.05 values (emotional instability p = 0.0292, a subgroup sleep result, GH in age >=65), all described as descriptive without multiplicity correction.

issues.title: Non-significant lung CT results (p = 0.2819, 0.2164) presented as MSC aiding lung recovery
issues.explanation: Normal CT was 46.94% vs 34.48% (OR 1.68, 95% CI 0.65 to 4.34, p = 0.2819), and the TSS difference was -1.92 (95% CI -4.98 to 1.15, p = 0.2164). Both intervals include no effect, and the 6-minute walk and pulmonary function comparisons were also null. The paper nevertheless says MSC aids recovery from lung damage. The data support, at most, a numerical difference compatible with chance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified analysis with a significant lung-recovery difference, or conclusion wording limited to a numerical, non-significant trend.

quotes.text: aiding in recovery from lung damage and enhancing the quality of life
with a difference of -1.92 (95% CI: -4.98-1.15

second_reader.what_stands: The 36-month CT results are non-significant, with confidence intervals including no effect (OR 0.65-4.34; TSS difference -4.98 to 1.15), yet the Results, Discussion and Conclusions describe them as MSC contributing to or aiding lung recovery. The hedged wording ('suggest', 'potential') and the statement that p values are descriptive soften this, but the causal verbs go beyond what these data support.

issues.title: About 23% not assessed at 36 months, with unequal retention (76.6% MSC vs 85.3% placebo)
issues.explanation: Of 101 randomized, 78 were assessed at 36 months after two deaths and 20 lost. The analysis uses available cases with no sensitivity analysis. Retention is lower in the MSC group. The limitation is acknowledged in the Discussion, but the Conclusions do not carry it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis showing similar results with missing data accounted for.

quotes.text: Of these, 20 cases were lost to follow-up

issues.title: GH p = 0.0278 is one of ten SF-36 domains and many symptom tests, none corrected
issues.explanation: Ten SF-36 domains and dozens of symptom and subgroup comparisons were tested without any correction. Only GH (p = 0.0278) is reported as significant among the SF-36 domains. A Bonferroni threshold across ten domains would be 0.005. The paper labels p-values as descriptive, yet the Discussion and Conclusions use GH as evidence of benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified single quality-of-life endpoint (GH) or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis retaining significance.

quotes.text: Multiple comparisons were not involved in this study.

issues.title: Text gives 34 new-onset complication occurrences; Table 3 entries total 49 (24 MSC, 25 placebo)
issues.explanation: The Results say both groups had a similar number of new-onset complications, 34 in total. Adding the Table 3 entries gives 24 in the MSC group and 25 in the placebo group, 49 in all. The text also gives 22 MSC and 21 placebo patients affected, 43 in all, which is a third figure. The headline safety statement therefore rests on a total that cannot be reconciled with the table. The patient proportions (44.90% vs 72.41%) also differ markedly, so 'similar' is a loose description.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of 'occurrence' that yields 34 from the table, or a corrected Table 3.

quotes.text: 34 occurrences in total
quotes.location: Results, New-onset complications and tumor markers, para 1

issues.title: 'No competing interests' declared while three authors are current employees of an affiliated company
issues.explanation: Three authors are stated to be current employees of Wuhan Optics Valley Zhongyuan Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Two of them list that company and VCANBIO Cell & Gene Engineering, which provided the UC-MSC product, as affiliations. The same paragraph says all authors declare no competing interests. A reader cannot tell what role these authors had, and the paper concludes that the product is safe and promising. The declaration should be reconciled with the employment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confirmation that the company has no financial or product interest in MSC therapy and the employees had no role in analysis or reporting.

All authors declare no competing interests.

issues.title: Denominators drop without explanation: BMI strata 46/25 vs 49/29; reinfection 28 vs 29; runny nose 25 vs 26
issues.explanation: BMI strata in Table 1 add to 46 (MSC) and 25 (placebo), against 49 and 29 available CT values. Reinfection and symptom tables use a placebo denominator of 28 although all 29 are said to be assessed. One MSC symptom row has 25 rather than 26, and the Table 5 footnote calls the reinfected counts (26, 19) the 'available values'. The paper says no other missing data were processed and gives no reason for these gaps. Individually small and plausibly missing data, but they are undocumented and make the subgroup comparisons harder to trust.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement or supplementary table showing which participants lacked BMI, reinfection-questionnaire or runny-nose data.

issues.title: Hyperthyroidism in MSC group printed as 2/29 in text but 2/49 (4.08%) in Table 3
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the MSC hyperthyroidism proportion as 2/29 while the MSC group has 49 participants and Table 3 gives 2/49. The printed 4.08% matches 2/49, so the text denominator is wrong. This is a small reporting slip that changes no conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing plausible; the table and percentage agree with each other.

10.1186/s13690-024-01354-w.headline_claim: A multimodal online telerehabilitation programme, added to usual care, shows promising effectiveness in enhancing mental health-related quality of life in Long COVID patients.
10.1186/s13690-024-01354-w.overall: The headline claim of promising effectiveness on mental health-related quality of life rests on a single borderline result (p=0.046) in a trial with an unclear randomisation method, an unblinded self-reported outcome, a completer analysis, and no multiplicity handling; the powered physical component was null. The result is best treated as hypothesis-generating, and the reporting errors (self-efficacy direction, Table 2 labelling) are minor by comparison.

primary_outcome.name: SF-36 quality of life (physical and mental components), 3-month follow-up

issues.title: Randomization described only as alphabetical ordering; unadjusted change comparison despite baseline imbalances
issues.explanation: The only sequence-generation step described is arranging participants alphabetically, which is not randomisation, and nothing says how groups were then assigned or concealed. Two baseline variables differ, and the intervention arm had lower baseline mental health (32.95 vs 34.14), which leaves room for regression to the mean in a change comparison. The between-group test of change is an unadjusted t test, so the one significant result is less secure than presented.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Protocol detail showing a computer-generated random sequence with concealed assignment, and an adjusted analysis giving the same mental health result.

quotes.text: who  arranged  the  list  of  participants  in  alphabetical order.
number of persistent symptoms and the Sit-to-Stand Test score.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes the randomization only as an independent statistician arranging the participant list alphabetically, with no stated method of generating or concealing a random sequence. Group differences were tested with unadjusted t tests on change scores despite imbalance in symptom count and Sit-to-Stand; the authors acknowledge this as residual confounding but did not adjust for it. Both imbalances may be chance, and the mental-health baseline was balanced.

issues.title: Conclusion rests on one uncorrected mental subscale (p=0.046); powered physical component was null and omitted
issues.explanation: The sample size calculation was driven by the physical scale, which showed no between-group difference. The mental health subscale is the only significant change among both SF-36 components and nine secondary measures, with no multiplicity correction. The Conclusions present this single borderline result as promising effectiveness without mentioning the null physical component or the number of comparisons.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchy naming the mental component as the sole primary outcome, or an adjusted analysis retaining significance.

quotes.location: Table 2, SF-36 Physical Health, T1-T0, intervention
Table 2, SF-36 Mental Health, T1-T0, control

quotes.text: was required to detect a mean difference of 20 points on the physical scale

second_reader.what_stands: The positive conclusion rests on a single between-group change comparison (SF-36 mental, p=0.046) among about 11 unadjusted change tests, and the mental result was not significant at T1 (p=0.138), where the difference partly reflects a decline in the control group. The physical component, for which the main sample size was calculated, was null (p=0.678) and is shown in Table 2, but it is not discussed in the text or conclusion, so 'omitted' is overstated; it is reported in the table only. The mental scale also had its own prespecified power calculation, so it is not purely a post hoc outcome.

issues.title: Text says self-efficacy improved more with intervention; Table 2 shows -0.85 vs -0.77 (p=0.953)
issues.explanation: The Results text lists self-efficacy among outcomes where improvements were greater in the intervention group. Table 2 shows self-efficacy fell in both arms, slightly more in the intervention arm, with no difference (p=0.953). The sentence therefore overstates the secondary-outcome pattern; the main result is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 2 showing a favourable self-efficacy change for the intervention arm, or a sentence limiting the claim to the other listed outcomes.

quotes.text: sleep  disorders,  self-efficacy,  and  patient activation

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-reported SF-36 primary outcome and TAU-only control; conclusion not qualified
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation and reported their own quality of life. An effect of 3.2 points on a subscale could reflect expectancy rather than the program. The limitation is disclosed in the Discussion, but the Conclusions still say the program 'shows promising effectiveness'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An attention-matched control or an objective primary outcome showing the same effect.

quotes.text: The main variable of this study was quality of life, evaluated through the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF36)

issues.title: Completer-only analysis of 124/134 randomised; no ITT for the borderline mental health result (p=0.046)
issues.explanation: Only participants who attended the 3-month assessment were analysed. Losses were small, but the key result is borderline, so it could change with plausible outcomes for the 10 missing participants. An ITT or imputed analysis is not reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ITT or multiple-imputation analysis giving a similar estimate and p below 0.05.

quotes.text: The evaluation at three months from baseline was completed by 124 participants

issues.title: Table 2 baseline rows reuse the N=67 values under an N=62 header; mental health change differs from T1-T0 means
issues.explanation: The baseline means, SDs and p-values in Table 2 are identical to Table 1, which covers all 67 per arm, although the table is headed N=62. The T1 means come from completers, so the printed changes do not equal the differences of the printed means. The header is mislabelled, and the baseline for completers is not shown. The between-group p=0.046 does recompute from the printed change SDs.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary data showing the completer-only baseline means equal the printed values.

quotes.text: Intervention group N = 62 Mean (SD)

quotes.location: Table 2, SF-36 Mental Health, Baseline, intervention
Table 2, SF-36 Mental Health, 3 months, intervention

issues.title: Discussion infers benefit for high baseline self-efficacy from a change-score regression with no interaction test
issues.explanation: The authors observed no group difference in self-efficacy change, yet suggest the intervention works better for those with initially high self-efficacy and propose selecting patients on that basis. No analysis of baseline self-efficacy or its interaction with allocation is presented; the regression uses change in self-efficacy, which is measured after the intervention and is not a baseline moderator.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified interaction analysis of baseline self-efficacy by allocation showing effect modification.

quotes.text: Although self-efficacy was a contributing variable, no significant difference in changes were observed between the groups or timepoints.

10.1186/s40359-026-05149-2.headline_claim: The manual-guided group psychotherapy did not show significant superiority over waitlist/TAU control on somatic symptom burden, depressive or anxiety symptoms, and the authors frame the results as exploratory and to be interpreted cautiously.
10.1186/s40359-026-05149-2.overall: The headline is a hedged null result from an exploratory pilot, and the paper explicitly flags the small sample, lack of power calculation and complete-case attrition, so its conclusion is largely supported as stated. The remaining problems are minor reporting inconsistencies (follow-up and analysed n between text, table and df) and unquantified differential dropout. No efficacy claim depends on them.

primary_outcome.name: Somatic symptom burden (SSS-8)

issues.title: Complete-case ANCOVA keeps ~60% of randomized; post-waiting retention in CG (14/27) is far below IG (16/21)
issues.explanation: The randomized comparison uses only patients with both baseline and post-randomization data, with no imputation or sensitivity analysis. Retention differs between arms: 76% in the IG versus 52% in the CG at the post-waiting assessment. Losses could bias the comparison in either direction, so the null result is tentative. The authors disclose attrition bias and the conclusion is cautious, which limits the damage, but the arm-specific dropout is never reported or analysed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis (e.g. multiple imputation or baseline comparison of completers versus dropouts) giving the same estimate.

quotes.text: All regression analyses were conducted using a complete-case approach (listwise deletion) without imputation
At post-randomization, data were available for the CG at the post-waiting assessment (before crossover) for 14 patients for SSS-8

issues.title: Text gives 16 CG follow-up patients for SSS-8 and PHQ-9; Table 2 gives 15 and 17
issues.explanation: The Results say 16 control-group patients had follow-up data after crossover for SSS-8, GAD-7 and PHQ-9. Table 2 shows n = 15 for SSS-8 and n = 17 for PHQ-9 (16 for GAD-7). The Table 2 totals add up with the table values, so the prose appears to be mistaken. The follow-up data are exploratory and do not enter the randomized-phase ANCOVA, so no main result changes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Fig. 2 showing 16 CG patients with SSS-8 and PHQ-9 follow-up, with Table 2 n values being the typo.

quotes.text: Follow-up assessments after crossover treatment in the CG included 16 patients for SSS-8 and GAD-7 and 16 patients for PHQ-9.

issues.title: Fatigue item follow-up M = 3.76, SD = 1.15 stated identically for IG and crossover CG
issues.explanation: The text gives the same mean and SD for rapid exhaustion in the IG follow-up and the CG post-crossover follow-up. A coincidence at the two-decimal level in two different groups is unlikely but not impossible. It may be a transcription slip. Nothing in the primary or secondary efficacy analyses depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Fig. 3 or raw data showing distinct IG and CG values for this item that happen to coincide.

quotes.text: and at CG follow-up assessment after crossover treatment (M = 3.76, SD = 1.15)

issues.title: Open-label waitlist design with self-reported primary outcome (SSS-8)
issues.explanation: Patients and therapists knew the allocation and all outcomes are self-reported, which leaves room for expectation and demand effects. This is inherent to the intervention. The trial reports no significant benefit, so the bias is unlikely to inflate a claim. It does limit how far any future positive finding from this design could be trusted.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An objective or assessor-rated co-primary outcome showing the same pattern.

quotes.text: patients and therapists were not blinded to treatment allocation
Outcomes were based on self-report and follow-up was limited to three months

issues.title: Stated ANCOVA n (29/28/28) is one lower than the reported residual df imply (30/29/29)
issues.explanation: The text says the SSS-8 model included 29 patients, but the reported t(27) in a baseline-plus-group model implies 30. The same holds for PHQ-9 and GAD-7 (df 26, which implies 29, versus a stated 28). The IG and CG post-randomization counts (16 + 14, 16 + 13) also add to 30, 29 and 29. This is a small reporting discrepancy with no bearing on the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A model specification with only two estimated parameters, or Fig. 2 confirming 29 analysed patients with a different df calculation.

quotes.text: complete-case ANCOVA models included fewer patients than initially randomized

10.1186/s42234-022-00094-y.headline_claim: Remote, self-administered taVNS was feasible, tolerable and safe with high compliance, and showed a mild improvement in self-reported Long COVID symptoms and mental fatigue.
10.1186/s42234-022-00094-y.overall: The feasibility and short-term tolerability conclusions are reasonably supported for a 12-person pilot, though the cardiac safety monitoring covered only the first six sessions. The symptom-improvement statements rest on within-arm descriptive changes with a 20-point baseline imbalance and no between-group test, so they cannot be read as evidence of efficacy. The registered primary outcome (PHQ-9) differs from the paper's stated primary outcomes, and that is not disclosed.

primary_outcome.name: Feasibility (staff-rated self-administration assistance) and safety (heart rate); the registry lists change in PHQ-9 at week 4 as primary

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in Score of Patient Health Questionnaire-9

issues.title: Symptom benefit claimed from within-arm change in 6 v 6, with 66% v 46% baseline and no between-group test
issues.explanation: The Fig. 5 caption says taVNS 'reduced' symptoms and the Discussion reports a mild improvement. These rest on descriptive within-arm percentages in 6 participants per arm, with no between-group test or confidence interval. The sham arm started at 66% and the active arm at 46%, so arm differences at later timepoints and changes are confounded with baseline imbalance and regression to the mean. The later open-label comparison has no concurrent control, so the changes there cannot be attributed to stimulation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified between-group analysis adjusted for baseline showing a difference with an interval excluding no effect.

quotes.text: In this small sample, taVNS reduced the mean percent of Long-COVID symptoms experienced by participants.
At baseline, the sham group reported a higher number of symptoms present (sham – 66%, active 46%).
quotes.location: Results, Long COVID symptom improvements and individual trends in mental fatigue

second_reader.what_stands: The numbers are as stated (6 v 6; baseline 66% v 46%; no between-group test), and the Fig. 5 caption uses causal wording ('taVNS reduced', 'sham provided no benefit') based on within-arm and descriptive differences in a measure built after the clinical scales showed no significant changes. The 20-point baseline imbalance and 6 per arm leave regression to the mean and chance as live explanations, and the pre-registered PHQ-9 outcome is not reported. This is only partly a flaw, because the Methods describe the analysis as descriptive, and the Discussion and Limitations hedge ('mild', 'not powere

issues.title: Paper's primary outcomes (feasibility, safety) differ from registered primary (PHQ-9 change at week 4)
issues.explanation: The registry lists PHQ-9 change at week 4 as the sole primary outcome. The paper instead declares feasibility and safety as primary and treats symptoms as secondary. The PHQ-9 is reported only as part of a battery with 'no significant changes', with no numbers, and the change in primary outcome is not acknowledged. The effect is limited because the registered outcome was null and the paper makes no efficacy claim based on it, but the registry-paper mismatch is undisclosed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version listing feasibility and safety as primary outcomes.

quotes.text: This study was designed for primary outcomes of feasibility and safety, with secondary outcomes exploring symptom improvement in nine pre-identified Long COVID symptoms.
Individual analysis of these battery subcomponents revealed no significant changes in these measurements.
quotes.location: Results, Long COVID symptom improvements and individual trends in mental fatigue

issues.title: Composite symptom percentage and mental fatigue emphasised after a null battery
issues.explanation: After the validated scales showed no significant change, the authors turned to a composite of nine symptoms and individual mental fatigue trends. The Discussion states a 'mild improvement' in both. The caveat of low power is included, but no analysis supports the claim and the null result from the validated measures is not weighed in the same sentence. The effect on the paper's main conclusion is limited because feasibility and safety are the stated focus.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or registry entry predefining the nine-symptom percentage as an outcome with an analysis plan.

quotes.text: Thus, we wholistically monitored the symptoms of nine specific Long COVID symptoms
quotes.location: Results, Long COVID symptom improvements and individual trends in mental fatigue

quotes.text: Lastly, there was a mild improvement in overall self-reported Long COVID symptoms, as well as mental fatigue, although this small study was not powered to detect clinical effects.

issues.title: Self-sufficiency timing: 'within two days' in Conclusions vs fifth session (third day) in Results
issues.explanation: The Results say all users self-administered without assistance by the 5th session, on the third day of the intervention. The Conclusions say participants were self-sufficient within two days. At two sessions per day, five sessions cannot be completed in two days, so the Conclusions slightly overstate how quickly participants became independent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A figure or table showing all users unassisted by session 4 (end of day 2).

quotes.text: were self-sufficient within two days.
(third day of the 28-day intervention)
quotes.location: Results, Participants and feasibility of taVNS self-administration, para 2

issues.title: No-bradycardia safety statement rests on heart rate monitored in first 6 of 48 sessions
issues.explanation: Heart rate and blood pressure were recorded only during the first six one-hour sessions, out of 48 planned. The Discussion and Conclusions state no bradycardia or adverse cardiac effects without saying that later sessions were not monitored. Adverse events more generally were collected throughout, so the overall safety statement is partly supported, but the cardiac statement is wider than the monitoring. The sample of 12 also limits any safety conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Cardiac monitoring data or logs covering the remaining sessions.

quotes.text: We monitored the safety of taVNS by measuring blood pressure and heart rate during the first six 1-h taVNS sessions for each participant.
quotes.location: Methods, Safety monitoring using a telemedicine approach

quotes.text: Furthermore, stimulation was safe, even at home, with no bradycardia or serious adverse events occurring during the stimulation sessions.

10.1186/s43166-023-00227-4.headline_claim: A comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation program improves quality of life, reduces fatigue, anxiety and depression, and regains function in patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome.
10.1186/s43166-023-00227-4.overall: The finding that scores improved from admission to discharge is supported descriptively, but the causal claim that the rehabilitation program produced the improvement is not supported by a single-arm design in mostly post-ICU inpatients. Several table errors (the BMI mean, a duplicated HADS-anxiety delta row, and a text-table contradiction on fatigue) further weaken the secondary vaccination comparison.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; outcomes include Barthel Index, HADS, FSS, PCFS, FAC, NHP and others (before-after comparison)

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from an uncontrolled single-arm pre-post cohort of 39 inpatients, tested only within group
issues.explanation: All p < 0.001 results are paired baseline-to-discharge comparisons in one group with no comparator, so improvement cannot be attributed to the program rather than natural recovery over a long, mostly post-ICU admission. The Discussion nonetheless states that the program improves quality of life and reduces fatigue, anxiety and depression, and the Conclusion extends this to guiding care in other pandemics. The data show that scores improved during the stay, not that rehabilitation caused it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group comparison, or a between-group analysis of the program versus usual care.

quotes.text: First, the study did not include a control group.

There was a statistically significant improvement in baseline outcomes including BI, HADS, PCFS, FSS, MMRC, FAC, Modified Borg Scale, O2 support, and NHP after the comprehensive rehabilitative program
This study may be a guide for rehabilitation clinicians in other pandemics or viral infection outbreaks

second_reader.what_stands: The paper's efficacy claims ('improves quality of life, reduces fatigue, anxiety, and depression, and regains function') rest on an uncontrolled single-arm pre-post cohort of 39 inpatients tested only within group (paired t-test/Wilcoxon). The authors do acknowledge the missing control group and small sample as limitations, but the Discussion and Conclusion still use causal wording and recommend the program as a guide for other outbreaks, which the design cannot support because spontaneous recovery, regression to the mean and co-interventions cannot be separated from the program effect.

issues.title: Overall BMI mean 24.4 is below both subgroup means (27.9, 25.2); weighted mean should be about 26.6
issues.explanation: Table 1 and the Results give the whole-cohort BMI as 24.4, but Table 3 gives 27.9 for 20 vaccinated and 25.2 for 19 unvaccinated patients. A pooled mean must lie between the group means, so one of these figures is wrong. The error is confined to descriptive BMI, but it also bears on the reported vaccinated-versus-unvaccinated BMI difference (p = 0.040).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction showing the Table 1 or Table 3 BMI values were mistyped, or that the groups were not a partition of the 39 patients.

issues.title: HADS-anxiety ∆ change row duplicates the FSS ∆ row and contradicts its own baseline and discharge medians
issues.explanation: Table 3 prints the same delta medians and IQRs (9 (5.3-14.5) and 17.5 (8.8-24)) for HADS-anxiety and FSS. For HADS-anxiety the baseline and discharge medians differ by about 4 points (11.5 to 7.5 and 11 to 7), so a median change of 9 or 17.5 is implausible; a median change of 17.5 is nearly the whole 0-21 scale range. The HADS-anxiety between-group delta comparison is therefore unreliable as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw per-patient HADS-anxiety change scores showing a median change of 9 and 17.5 in the two groups.

quotes.location: Table 3, HADS-anxiety and FSS ∆ change rows, Vaccinated
Table 3, HADS-anxiety and FSS ∆ change rows, Unvaccinated

issues.title: Text says unvaccinated had significantly higher discharge fatigue; Table 3 shows lower FSS (26.5 vs 36, p=0.133)
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion state that unvaccinated patients had higher FSS at discharge and 'significantly higher levels of fatigue'. In Table 3 their median discharge FSS is lower (26.5 vs 36) and the difference is not significant (p = 0.133). The claimed higher PCFS and FAC are also not significant at discharge (p = 0.361, 0.409), so only the Barthel Index difference (p = 0.023) is supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the Table 3 discharge FSS columns are swapped and the true p value is below 0.05.

quotes.text: At discharge, unvaccinated patients had higher BI, FSS, PCFS, and FAC.
they had significantly higher

issues.title: 30 sessions at 5 days/week (about 6 weeks) versus mean stay of 37.5 days; delivered dose not reported
issues.explanation: The protocol says it was applied to all patients for 30 sessions, but many patients (mean stay 37.5 days, vaccinated 31.7 days) would have been discharged before reaching 30 sessions. The actual number of sessions delivered is not reported, so the dose behind the outcomes is unclear. This is a reporting gap rather than a demonstrated error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement or table of sessions actually completed showing at least 30 per patient.

quotes.text: 5 days a week, totaling 30 sessions

issues.title: No trial registration or pre-specified primary outcome reported for a prospective interventional cohort
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective study of a rehabilitation program but reports no registry entry and designates no primary outcome among about 15 outcome measures. This prevents checking for selective reporting. The impact is limited because all outcomes are reported and nearly all improved.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol dated before enrolment naming the primary outcome.

quotes.text: The single-center prospective study was conducted in Ankara City Hospital, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Hospital from January 2022 to May 2022.

10.1192/j.eurpsy.2024.257.headline_claim: Adding oral L-arginine to standard SSRI antidepressant therapy in elderly patients with Long Covid-related fatigue and depression significantly decreases severity of both physical and affective symptoms.
10.1192/j.eurpsy.2024.257.overall: The abstract's claim of a significant benefit of L-arginine on fatigue and depression rests on two p-values from a 96-patient trial with no placebo, despite a double-blind label, and with no arm sizes or effect estimates. The conclusion should be read as tentative, since unblinded symptom scales could account for some or all of the difference.

primary_outcome.name: Fatigue (Fatigue Symptom Inventory) and depressive symptoms (HAM-D) after 8 weeks; the paper does not designate one primary outcome

issues.title: No placebo in control arm despite 'double-blind' label; subjective fatigue and depression outcomes
issues.explanation: The control group received antidepressant only, with no placebo, yet the trial is called double-blind. Patients cannot be blinded to a twice-daily supplement they are or are not taking, and no placebo or blinding procedure is described. Both outcomes are symptom scales, so expectation and rater knowledge could contribute to the apparent benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the control arm received an identical-appearing placebo and that outcome raters were blinded.

quotes.text: whereas the second group received antidepressant only
This is a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized controlled trial

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract describes the control arm as 'antidepressant only' with no placebo or other blinding mechanism, so the 'double-blind' claim is not supported by what is written, and the primary outcomes (FSI fatigue and HAM-D depression) are symptom measures prone to expectation effects if participants knew their allocation. However, because this is a brief abstract, it cannot be established that no placebo or blinded rating was used, only that none is reported. HAM-D is clinician-rated and could be blinded to allocation, though the abstract does not say so, and FSI is self-reported.

issues.title: 96 patients, no sample-size calculation or arm sizes; efficacy stated without effect sizes or CIs
issues.explanation: The abstract randomises 96 patients but gives no arm sizes, no power calculation, no effect estimates and no confidence intervals. Only p-values (0.008 and 0.002) are given, so the size and precision of the benefit cannot be judged. Abstract length limits explain some of this, but the conclusion is still worded as established efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A full report giving a pre-specified sample-size calculation, arm sizes, effect estimates with confidence intervals.

quotes.text: conducted on 96 over 65 non-hospitalized patients suffering from Long Covid-related fatigue and depression
patients treated with L-arginine supplementation exhibited a 30% greater improvement in fatiguerelated symptom severity (p=0.008)

issues.title: No trial registration reported in the abstract; co-primary outcomes not designated
issues.explanation: No registry or identifier is given, so prespecification of outcomes cannot be checked. Two outcomes (FSI and HAM-D) are both reported with no primary designated and no multiplicity handling. This is common in conference abstracts and cannot be settled from the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with prespecified outcomes matching those reported.

quotes.text: This is a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized controlled trial conducted on 96 over 65 non-hospitalized patients

10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.463.headline_claim: The remote medical-psychological rehabilitation program effectively reduces depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress symptoms in people with post-COVID disorders amid wartime conditions.
10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.463.overall: The abstract reports large day-63 differences between a programme group and a control group, but gives no allocation method, baseline scores, per-arm numbers or description of the control, so the causal conclusion that the programme 'effectively reduces' symptoms is not supported by what is printed. Much of the missing detail may be a consequence of abstract length, so the result is best read as tentative rather than wrong. The ethics candidate is not a meaningful problem for an abstract of this kind.

primary_outcome.name: PHQ-9 depression, GAD-7 anxiety and PCL-5 PTSD scores at day 63 (no single primary outcome stated)

issues.title: Day-63 between-group effect reported without baseline data or description of control arm or allocation
issues.explanation: The abstract reports only post-treatment scores for a 'study group' and a 'control group'. It does not say how participants were allocated, what the control received, or what baseline scores were, and 240 is given as a single sample size without an arm split. Without these, the large day-63 differences cannot be attributed to the programme rather than to baseline imbalance or non-comparable groups. The problem is partly an abstract-length limitation, so it is weaker than a confirmed design flaw.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The full paper showing randomised or baseline-matched allocation, a described control condition, comparable baseline PHQ-9, GAD-7 and PCL-5 scores, and per-arm analysed numbers.

quotes.text: while in the control group it remained at 15.567±6.540 (p < 0.001; t = 11.437)
The study sample consisted of 240 individuals with anxiety and depressive post-COVID disorders.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract reports day-63 between-group results with no baseline scores, no arm sizes, no description of the control condition and no statement of how participants were allocated. The reported t statistics are arithmetically consistent with about 120 per arm, but that split is not stated in the paper.

issues.title: Causal 'effectively reduces' conclusion rests on one day-63 comparison with undescribed control
issues.explanation: The conclusion states that the programme 'effectively reduces' depression, anxiety and PTSD symptoms. The only evidence shown is a post-treatment between-group comparison, with no stated allocation method, baseline data or control-arm description. The abstract therefore supports a difference at day 63, not a demonstrated causal effect, and no limitations are mentioned.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The full paper showing a randomised or well-matched controlled design with baseline-adjusted results supporting a causal interpretation.

quotes.text: effectively reduces symptoms of depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress in individuals with post-COVID disorders amid wartime conditions.

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion's causal wording 'effectively reduces' rests only on one day-63 endpoint comparison with an undescribed control arm and unstated allocation, so it is not supported by what the abstract shows. The paper does report a control group and consistent, significant differences across three scales, so it is not unsupported by any data; the limitation is that the design information needed to interpret them causally is missing, and the abstract format may account for some of that.

10.1212/nxi.0000000000200296.headline_claim: Four weeks of paraprobiotics may improve some neurologic symptoms (dysautonomia, fatigue, depression) in long-COVID, possibly by reducing immune cell activation and TLR2 expression on T cells.
10.1212/nxi.0000000000200296.overall: The paper presents itself as a preliminary pilot, and its hedged wording is fairly honest. Its design (six patients, no control, open-label self-reports, many uncorrected immune tests) cannot support a positive treatment effect or the proposed TLR2/activation mechanism. Treat the results as hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: Clinical and immunologic effects of paraprobiotics (no single primary outcome named)

issues.title: Single-arm, six-patient before-after study cannot separate treatment effect from time or expectation
issues.explanation: All six patients took the product and were compared with themselves. The 'improvement' rule only asks whether the 2-to-3 change exceeded the 1-to-2 change, with no statistical test on the clinical outcomes. Regression to the mean, natural fluctuation, and expectation are therefore not excluded. The conclusion that treatment has a positive effect is tentative at best.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated comparison group, or a formal analysis showing the treatment-period change exceeds the pre-treatment trend.

quotes.text: A measurement was considered to improve due to treatment when the degree of improvement between visits/periods 2 and 3 was higher than the degree of improvement between visits/periods 1 and 2.
The results of this small exploratory study suggest that the treatment of patients with long-COVID with paraprobiotics might improve some of the neurologic symptoms

second_reader.what_stands: The study has one arm of six patients and no concurrent control. The pre-treatment run-in comparison gives some protection against steady trends, but it cannot account for expectation, regression to the mean, or ordinary fluctuation, particularly in largely subjective outcomes. The authors do say the findings are exploratory and preliminary, but the 'due to treatment' wording in the improvement definition is stronger than the design supports.

issues.title: Many immune comparisons at uncorrected p<0.05 in 6 patients underpin the mechanistic conclusion
issues.explanation: The authors examined more than 50 cell populations plus activation markers, TLRs, 13 cytokines and neutrophil functions, each tested at p < 0.05 with no correction. A few nominally significant results (HLA-DR on B and NK T cells, CD40 on nonclassical monocytes, TLR2 on T cells) are expected by chance in a screen this large. They are nonetheless used to explain the clinical benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified, limited set of immune endpoints, or results surviving a false-discovery or Bonferroni correction.

quotes.text: For the comparison of samples before and after treatment, we used the paired Wilcoxon test for nonparametric variables.
The signi fi cance level was set at p < 0.05.
analyzed the frequency of more than 50

second_reader.what_stands: The immune findings come from many paired Wilcoxon tests at an uncorrected p < 0.05 with six patients, and the paper reports about 8 nominally significant results out of an undeclared but probably over 100 tests, which is near the number expected by chance. The paper's mechanistic conclusion (modulation of immune activation and T-cell TLR2) rests on these results, though the authors label it preliminary and also report many null results.

issues.title: Open-label study with mostly self-reported outcomes (fatigue VAS, PHQ-9, COMPASS-31, CFS)
issues.explanation: Patients knew they were taking paraprobiotics and rated their own symptoms. Subjective fatigue, depression and dysautonomia scores are therefore vulnerable to expectation bias. Wearable steps and tapping are more objective, but they are a minority of the measures and are not shown to change significantly. This weakens the symptom conclusion and overlaps with the lack of a control group.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded or objective outcome assessment, or evidence that the objective measures alone showed improvement.

quotes.text: Subjective fatigue was reported with a visual analog scale (1 -10) through our smartphone application.
quotes.location: Methods, Smartphone App and Wearable Sensors

quotes.text: Improvements in several of the neurologic symptoms such as dysautonomia, fatigue, and depression were documented using both patient-reported outcomes

issues.title: Mechanism ('most likely' immune activation/TLR2) and 'increase the probability' wording exceed a 6-patient uncontrolled design
issues.explanation: No analysis links immune changes to symptom change, and there is no control group. Describing the immune effects as the most likely mechanism, or saying treatment increases the probability of improvement, implies a causal effect the design cannot show. The caveats in the Discussion soften this but do not remove it from the abstract and evidence statement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal mediation or correlation analysis, or a controlled study linking the immune changes to clinical response.

quotes.text: This study provides Class IV evidence that paraprobiotics increase the probability of favorable changes of clinical and immunologic markers in patients with long-COVID.
most likely by modulating immune cell activation and expression of TLR2 on T cells

issues.title: Product-maker grant disclosed, but funder role not described and disclosure line reads 'no relevant disclosures'
issues.explanation: The paraprobiotics are made by a Spanish company (Laboratorios Weltmont) whose affiliate gave an unrestricted grant. Several authors are also affiliated with Cellerys AG. The paper does not say whether the funder had any role in design, analysis or writing. Readers cannot judge from the paper alone whether 'no relevant disclosures' fully covers these relationships.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The online full disclosures showing no authors have ties to Weltmont, plus a statement that the funder had no role.

quotes.text: by an unrestricted grant of Weltmont Laboratories, Madrid, Spain
The authors report no relevant disclosures.

issues.title: Visit 1 timing: 'around 10 months' in Methods vs 33 weeks in the Figure 2 caption
issues.explanation: The Study Design places visit 1 about 10 months before treatment, but the Figure 2 caption (patient 2) says 33 weeks, about 7.6 months. Different patients may have started monitoring at different times, but the paper does not say so. The baseline-trend period is central to how improvement is judged, so the wording should be reconciled. It does not change any reported result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that visit 1 timing varied by patient, with patient 2's interval being 33 weeks.

quotes.text: Around 10 months before treatment initiation (visit 1)
since visit 1 (33 weeks before treatment initiation)

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified outcomes reported for a defined four-week intervention
issues.explanation: Patients were given fixed products and doses for four weeks and many outcomes were measured. No registry entry or prespecified primary outcome is given, so reported findings cannot be checked against a plan. Given the exploratory framing, this is a minor concern that adds to the selective-reporting risk from many outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol dated before treatment listing the outcomes.

quotes.text: The Cantonal Ethics Committee of Zurich approved the study procedures

issues.title: No adverse-event or tolerability information reported for the intervention
issues.explanation: The paper recommends paraprobiotics as safer than probiotics but reports nothing on side effects, adherence or dropouts over the four weeks. A reader cannot judge tolerability from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A report of adverse events and adherence, even if none occurred.

quotes.text: Clinical symptoms were reported systematically at each visit based on a predetermined questionnaire consisting of 26 questions (eTable 3).

10.1249/01.mss.0000985296.04035.50.headline_claim: Individualized, supervised exercise training was more effective than guideline-based usual care for regaining cardiovascular and muscular fitness and improving symptom severity and health status in outpatients with post-COVID-19 condition.
10.1249/01.mss.0000985296.04035.50.overall: The fitness and strength conclusions are supported by large reported effects, but the abstract is too brief to confirm how the crossover headline (7.43 ml/kg/min) was derived. The claimed benefit on symptom severity and health status has no matching result in the text and should be treated as unsupported.

primary_outcome.name: Peak VO2 (ml/kg/min)

issues.title: Conclusion claims better symptom severity and health status; only a weakness-symptom proportion (RR 0.63) is shown
issues.explanation: The conclusion says supervised exercise improved symptom severity and health status. The Results report no symptom-severity score, no fatigue result and no health-status measure. The only symptom result is a lower proportion of people with weakness (RR 0.63, CI 0.42 to 0.95). The fitness and strength claims have supporting numbers, but the symptom and health-status claims do not.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The full paper reporting a symptom-severity score and a health-status measure (for example a fatigue scale or EQ-5D) with significant between-treatment differences.

quotes.text: to regain cardiovascular and muscular fitness, improve symptom severity and health status in outpatients with post-COVID-19 conditions

issues.title: Crossover peak VO2 effect (7.43) not reconcilable with AB change (+3.83, -1.24); carryover handling unstated
issues.explanation: The headline peak VO2 difference of 7.43 is labelled a between-group difference 'in sequence AB and BA'. The only AB figures given are +3.83 after exercise and -1.24 after usual care, which differ by 5.07. The BA sequence is not shown, so the reader cannot tell how 7.43 was derived. The confidence interval (5.96 to 9.12) is also not centred on 7.43 (midpoint 7.54), and the abstract states no washout, period effect or carryover test. The size of the primary effect is therefore unverifiable from the abstract.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The full paper showing a crossover model with period and sequence terms, a washout or carryover test, and BA-sequence data that reproduce 7.43.

quotes.text: The between-group differences were 7.43 ml/kg/min (95% CI, 5.96 to 9.12); P<0.0001
decrease by −1.24 ml/kg/min (SD 3.90), after 6-week of usual care

10.1249/01.mss.0000987560.02549.a2.headline_claim: A progressive, individualized exercise program improves function, quality of life, and fatigue in people with Long COVID.
10.1249/01.mss.0000987560.02549.a2.overall: This is a small, uncontrolled 12-person pre/post pilot, so the finding that exercise improves function and quality of life is tentative at best. The gait speed result is printed as a decrease while the conclusion claims improved walking speed, which is a clear internal inconsistency probably due to units or direction. Most other changes are large and plausible but cannot be attributed to the program.

primary_outcome.name: 6-minute walk distance (6MWD)

issues.title: Single-arm pre/post study with no control group; improvements attributed to the exercise program
issues.explanation: All 12 participants did the exercise program and were tested before and after with paired t-tests. Without a control group, changes cannot be separated from natural recovery of Long COVID, test familiarity or expectation. The title and conclusion state that exercise improves function and quality of life, which is stronger than this design allows.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or waitlist control group, or evidence that symptoms were stable over a comparable period before the intervention.

quotes.text: Paired t-tests were used to evaluate changes in outcome measures following the intervention.
Exercise Training Improves Function And Quality Of Life In Patients With Long Covid

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract describes a single-group pre/post design (12 participants, paired t-tests, no control or comparison arm), yet the Title and Conclusion attribute the improvements to the exercise programme. Without a control group, changes cannot be separated from natural recovery, practice or learning effects on the tests, regression to the mean, or expectation effects, so causal wording such as 'Improves' is stronger than the design supports. This assessment rests on the abstract alone, so a control group described only in a full paper cannot be excluded.

issues.title: Gait speed printed as falling 3.28 to 3.01 m/s (p=0.006) yet conclusion claims improved walking speed
issues.explanation: The abstract reports gait speed in m/s falling from 3.28 to 3.01 with p=0.006, yet the conclusion lists significant improvement in walking speed. A fall in speed means slower walking, contradicting the claim. Values near 3 m/s are also implausible for walking speed, suggesting the measure is really a time (seconds) or the units are wrong; either way the reported result and the stated conclusion do not agree as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full text showing gait speed was measured as time over a fixed distance (so lower is better) or that the units are a labelling error, with direction of improvement stated.

quotes.text: gait speed (Pre=3.28±0.11
significant improvements in walking speed and distance

issues.title: Only 12 completers, no sample-size justification, with a confident efficacy conclusion
issues.explanation: Twelve participants completed the study and no sample-size calculation or number enrolled is given in the abstract. Small samples give imprecise estimates, and nine of twelve being women limits generalisability. Most of the weight of this concern is already covered by the single-arm and generalisation problems, so it is a modest additional weakness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size justification and full participant flow showing no selective dropout.

quotes.text: Twelve participants (9 females, 3 males), 49 ± 4 years old, completed this investigation.

issues.title: Self-reported fatigue (VAFS 5.0 to 2.8) and SF-12 gains in an open-label, uncontrolled study
issues.explanation: Participants knew they were exercising and rated their own fatigue and quality of life. Those improvements may partly reflect expectation. The objective walking and strength tests improved too, though these are also unblinded and uncontrolled, so the issue narrows the weight of the subjective claims rather than refuting them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Comparison with a control group, or assessor-blinded objective outcomes showing the same pattern.

10.1249/mss.0000000000003207.headline_claim: Heterogeneous individual responses occurred after an 8-week home-based IMT programme in people with postacute COVID-19 syndrome, and larger improvements in inspiratory muscle strength were strongly related to a greater cumulative IMT dose.
10.1249/mss.0000000000003207.overall: Only the abstract is available, so the heterogeneity and dose-response conclusions can be judged only partly. The inference of individual response heterogeneity from an SD difference against a small, non-randomised wait-list group, reported with 75% credible intervals, is stated more firmly than that design supports. The conclusions should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Heterogeneity of treatment response in maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), expressed as the difference between group SDs of change

issues.title: Non-randomised usual-care wait-list control (n=36) underpins the between-group SD comparison
issues.explanation: Heterogeneity of treatment response is inferred from the difference in SD of change between IMT (n=111) and wait-list controls (n=36). The abstract does not describe randomisation or allocation concealment, so the groups may differ in ways that alter variability of change. The sex difference (83% vs 94% female) is modest and is not itself a strong concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that allocation was random or otherwise unrelated to baseline characteristics, and that results were robust to adjustment for sex and baseline.

quotes.text: or acted as "usual care"wait list controls (n = 36, 34 females, 49 ± 12 yr
either completed an 8-wk home-based IMT intervention (n = 111, 92 females, 48 ± 11 yr

issues.title: Conclusion states heterogeneous responses 'occurred' based on 75% credible intervals for SD differences
issues.explanation: The abstract reports SD differences with 75% CrIs (MIP 4.7-37.7; SMIP 55.7-116.7), a lenient interval level, then concludes that heterogeneous individual responses occurred. An SD difference is indirect evidence, and the wording is stronger than 'suggests'. Whether this is overreach depends on the full methods, which are not in the text provided.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full methods showing a pre-specified interpretation threshold for 75% CrIs, and sensitivity analyses at 95% CrI.

quotes.text: Heterogeneous individual responses occurred after an 8-wk home-based IMT program in people with postacute COVID-19 syndrome.
the estimated difference between standard deviations (SD) of the IMT and control groups was 22.8 cm H2O (75% credible interval (CrI), 4.7-37.7)

issues.title: Within-arm association of cumulative power with strength change is described as 'clearly' a dose response
issues.explanation: Cumulative power is not randomly assigned; adherent or fitter participants may both train harder and improve more. The abstract nonetheless says the association is 'clearly indicating' a dose response. The effect is modest in consequence because the headline rests on heterogeneity, not dose-response.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Adjustment for baseline strength, age and adherence determinants showing the association is unchanged.

quotes.text: clearly indicating an IMT dose response for changes in inspiratory muscle strength

10.12659/msm.950105.headline_claim: VAT has demonstrated potential efficacy in alleviating multiple long COVID symptoms, including fatigue, and could be a feasible and well-tolerated adjunct, though the authors state the uncontrolled design does not show VAT caused the change.
10.12659/msm.950105.overall: This is an uncontrolled, open-label, single-session pilot with an unvalidated self-rated outcome and uncorrected multiple testing, so it can show feasibility but not efficacy. The small pre-post changes (7.2% in the total score) could arise from expectation, novelty or chance, and the 'superior' and 'significant effects' language overreaches. The headline claim of 'potential efficacy' stands only as a tentative, hypothesis-generating signal.

primary_outcome.name: Mean total symptom severity score (12 symptoms, self-rated 10-point scale), before vs after a single 10-minute session

issues.title: Uncontrolled, open-label pre-post design with self-rated outcomes used to claim efficacy
issues.explanation: All 42 participants received VAT and rated their own symptoms before and after a single session, knowing they were receiving the intervention. Placebo response, expectation, novelty and the passage of a clinic wait cannot be separated from any VAT effect. The wording 'demonstrated potential efficacy' goes further than this design allows, although the paper does flag the problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent sham or non-interactive VR control arm, or a blinded outcome assessment, showing the same change.

quotes.text: VAT has demonstrated potential efficacy in alleviating multiple symptoms, including fatigue
This prospective interventional study was open-label
