Standard of care (Control) was defined as the participant living as usual

second_reader.what_stands: The study is open-label with no sham, and the period-specific MoCA differences (+2.282 and -2.700, both with 95% CIs excluding 0) reverse sign, which indicates a treatment-by-period or sequence interaction. The paper attributes the pattern to a 'learning effect' and never tests or discusses the interaction, so 'show' is my approximate inference rather than a result the authors report.

issues.title: Many outcomes and post-hoc subsets examined with no multiplicity control; few CIs exclude 0 and are then highlighted
issues.explanation: MoCA total and 7 subscores, HVLT, digit span, fluency, GAD-7, PHQ-9 and its items, PCFS and several oximetry measures were analysed, with Period 1 repeats added after the overall results. Only a handful of intervals exclude zero (Period 1 MoCA total, attention, PHQ-9 Q1 and Q7), and with this many looks some are expected by chance. The PHQ-9 Q1/Q7 analyses are labelled post hoc in the Results, although the Methods call them hypothesised.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified analysis plan limiting outcomes, or adjusted CIs that still exclude zero.

quotes.text: No formal statistical hypotheses were tested in this pilot exploratory study.
Post-hoc analyses performed on specific PHQ-9 items, namely Q1 (Little interest/pleasure) and Q7 (Trouble concentrating), also showed trends for better scores with POC
quotes.location: Results, Psychological health and functional status

issues.title: Period 1 MoCA difference printed as 1.705 in text/abstract but 2.282 in Table 2
issues.explanation: The abstract and Results quote a Period 1 MoCA difference of 1.705 (0.140, 3.271), whereas Table 2 gives 2.282 (0.264, 4.300) for the same contrast. The Methods say Period 1 used a baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, which probably explains the figure in the text, but the table row is not labelled as unadjusted. A reader cannot tell which estimate is the intended one.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table footnote stating that the Period 1 row is unadjusted while the text reports the ANCOVA estimate.

quotes.text: where the mean treatment difference in this period was 1.705 [0.140, 3.271]

issues.title: Only 9/21 (42.9%) met the compliance criterion and 3 never used POC; no per-protocol cognitive analysis
issues.explanation: Less than half of participants used the device as prescribed, and 3 (14.3%) never used it for 3 hours a day. The cognitive and mood analyses were ITT only, so exposure was diluted. The per-protocol analysis was reported only for pulse oximetry.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Per-protocol cognitive analyses showing results consistent with ITT.

quotes.text: Nine patients (42.9%) were found to be compliant with the study device according to this criterion.

10.1371/journal.pone.0330938.headline_claim: Mental and physical symptoms partially improved during specialized inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation for post-COVID condition.
10.1371/journal.pone.0330938.overall: The descriptive findings (high screening-positive rates and lower symptom scores at discharge) are reasonably reported, with a single small percentage misprint in Table 2. Because the study is an uncontrolled pre-post series, improvement cannot be attributed to rehabilitation, which the authors acknowledge. The recommendation for specialized psychotherapy is not supported by the data.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome designated; admission-to-discharge change in PHQ and SF-36 measures

issues.title: Need for psychotherapy inferred from non-significant changes (panic p=0.241, eating disorder p=0.010)
issues.explanation: The Discussion says panic, eating disorder and PTSD symptoms 'did not change' and concludes these patients require psychotherapy. Eating disorder screens fell from 10/139 to 2/133 (p = 0.010), missing only the strict 0.005 threshold. Panic and eating disorder counts are small, so power is low. An uncontrolled design cannot show what psychotherapy would add, so the recommendation is not supported by the analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that psychotherapy was compared or that the unchanged-symptom subgroups were adequately powered to detect change.

quotes.text: In contrast, symptoms of panic disorder, eating disorders, and PTSD did not change from admission to discharge
quotes.location: Discussion, Changes from admission to discharge

quotes.text: suggesting that patients with post-COVID condition presenting with these symptoms require specialized psychotherapy in addition to pulmonary rehabilitation treatment
quotes.location: Discussion, Changes from admission to discharge

issues.title: Somatoform syndrome at discharge: 56/134 printed as 41.2%, but 56/134 = 41.8%
issues.explanation: Table 2 prints 56 of 134 discharge patients as 41.2%, but 56 divided by 134 is 41.8%. The 41.2% figure would fit 56/136, so either the count, the denominator or the percentage is misprinted. The discrepancy is small and does not change the significance or direction of the reported decrease.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors' data showing 55 of 134 or 56 of 136 patients, or a note that the percentage uses a different base.

quotes.location: Table 2, Somatoform syndrome row, Discharge column

script.explanation: 56/134 = 41.79%, but the paper prints 41.2, outside the rounding interval [41.15, 41.30]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 135.9 rather than 134.

issues.title: Uncontrolled admission-to-discharge comparison (n=140); improvement cannot be tied to rehabilitation
issues.explanation: All patients received the same inpatient rehabilitation with no comparison group, so the pre-post changes may reflect natural recovery, regression to the mean, or response bias on self-report. The authors state this limitation clearly and word the conclusion as improvement 'during' treatment. The residual concern is the Introduction's framing of evaluating treatment effects and the 'specialized' treatment wording in the Conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the absence of a control is acknowledged. It would be mitigated if the conclusion were worded strictly as descriptive.

quotes.text: the current study did not include a control group of patients that were not treated or received an alternative treatment
both mental and physical symptoms showed partial improvement during a specialized inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation treatment

10.1371/journal.pone.0340965.headline_claim: Eccentric cycling training induced greater functional and cognitive improvements than standard rehabilitation in COVID-19 survivors with post-ICU syndrome.
10.1371/journal.pone.0340965.overall: The finding that both rehabilitation modalities improved function is credible, but the claim that eccentric cycling is superior, especially for cognition, is only weakly supported: three of about twelve unadjusted between-arm comparisons were significant, MoCA was null, sequence effects were present after a short washout, and registration was about three years after recruitment. Several labelling errors in Results and Table 2 also reduce confidence in the reporting.

primary_outcome.name: Not identified in the paper; the Methods list several functional outcomes without designating one primary; the registry lists five co-primary measures (MRC strength, handgrip, 6MWT, 1-min sit-to-stand, TUG)

issues.title: Sequence effects for MRC, PCFS, MoCA, Barthel after a 2-week washout, dismissed by appeal to randomisation
issues.explanation: Main sequence effects were found for four outcomes (and a sequence x intervention interaction for 6MWT, P = 0.005, and expiratory flow, P = 0.04), and the washout was only two weeks. The authors accept possible carryover but conclude comparability 'due to randomization', yet randomisation balances order across arms without removing carryover from within-subject contrasts. The 6MWT result, one of the three headline outcomes, shows an interaction, so the paired ECC-vs-STD comparison is not clean for it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A period- and sequence-adjusted crossover analysis showing no carryover and the same treatment difference.

quotes.text: However, even when some carryover effect was detected, we believe that the improvements induced by both interventions are comparable due to randomization.
The two-way ANOVA revealed a sequence  ×  intervention effect (P  =  0.005) and main effect for intervention (P  =  0.02)

second_reader.what_stands: Sequence effects were found for MRC, PCFS, MoCA and Barthel after only a 2-week washout, and the limitations paragraph sets them aside as comparable 'due to randomization', which does not address carryover in a crossover design. The authors also leave out the 6MWT sequence x intervention effect (P = 0.005), and 6MWT is one of the outcomes on which ECC is said to be superior. The authors do acknowledge the short washout and the sequence effects, so the issue is disclosed but not adequately resolved.

issues.title: Conclusion of greater physical and cognitive gains rests on 3 of 12 outcomes; MoCA between-arm P = 0.51
issues.explanation: The Conclusion states ECC gave greater physical and cognitive improvements, but the cognitive test (MoCA) showed no between-arm difference (P = 0.51) and the paired delta comparison was non-significant for strength, handgrip, sit-to-stand, PCFS, PHQ-9 and expiratory flow. Only 6MWT, TUG and Barthel Index differed, with no correction for roughly a dozen outcomes and a marginal 6MWT result. The Discussion's 'partially accepted' is more cautious than the Abstract and Conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified, multiplicity-adjusted analysis showing a cognitive benefit.

quotes.text: Eccentric cycling training demonstrated greater improvements in physical and cognitive performance compared to standard rehabilitation.
The delta of change was similar between interventions for the MoCA (P = 0.51; Fig 5A).

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion of greater physical and cognitive gains rests on 3 of 12 outcomes at nominal P < 0.05 in the paired delta comparisons, with no multiplicity adjustment, and the only dedicated cognitive test (MoCA) shows no between-arm difference (P = 0.51). The 'cognitive' claim depends on the Barthel index, which measures daily-living independence. Table 2 interaction P values give a somewhat larger nominal count (5 of 12), but that does not change the point for MoCA.

issues.title: Trial registered in March 2025, about 3 years after 2022 recruitment; paper does not disclose this
issues.explanation: The paper cites NCT06895850 and describes recruitment from March to September 2022. The registry shows first submission on 2025-03-20, so registration followed completion of the study and outcome selection could not be verified in advance. With no single designated primary outcome and a headline built on a subset of outcomes, this matters more.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registration record or protocol dated before March 2022.

quotes.text: Recruitment started on March 1 st , 2022, and finished on September 30, 2022.
This study was registered at clinicaltrial.gov (NCT06895850).

issues.title: Barthel Index between-arm result labelled 'MoCA' (P = 0.02, Fig 5B) next to MoCA P = 0.51
issues.explanation: The Results first say the MoCA delta was similar (P = 0.51, Fig 5A), then say the MoCA delta was greater after ECC (P = 0.02, Fig 5B). Fig 5B is the Barthel Index and the sentence sits in the Barthel paragraph, so it is a labelling error rather than a real contradiction on MoCA. The correct reading is that MoCA did not differ between arms, which means the Conclusion's claim of greater cognitive improvement is not supported by any between-arm MoCA test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Fig 5B being the MoCA panel.

quotes.text: The delta of change was greater after ECC compared to STD REHAB for the MoCA (P = 0.02; Fig. 5B).
The delta of change was similar between interventions for the MoCA (P = 0.51; Fig 5A).

issues.title: TUG between-intervention result mislabelled as 6MWT in Results (P = 0.002, Fig 3E); 6MWT P = 0.02
issues.explanation: The Results give two sentences both attributed to the 6MWT with different p-values (0.02 and 0.002). The second cites Fig 3E, which the caption and Discussion identify as TUG, so it is a TUG result carrying the wrong label. The TUG between-arm test is thus effectively unlabelled and the 6MWT result is not duplicated, so a reader cannot tell this without the caption.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A figure showing Fig 3E is the 6MWT.

quotes.text: The delta of change after ECC was greater compared to STD REHAB for the 6MWT (P = 0.002; Fig 3E).
timed up and go (TUG; E)

issues.title: Abstract says all variables improved; muscle mass was not significant (P = 0.08 and 0.78)
issues.explanation: The Abstract states that all variables improved after both interventions. Table 2 gives muscle mass P = 0.08 (ECC) and P = 0.78 (STD REHAB), and the Discussion and Conclusions say muscle mass was unchanged. The body corrects it, so this is an abstract wording slip with little bearing on the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the abstract sentence is plainly broader than Table 2.

quotes.text: All variables improved after both interventions, but ECC showed larger improvements in 6MWT, TUG, and Barthel Index compared to STD REHAB.

issues.title: Several Table 2 effect sizes lie outside their printed 95% CIs (Barthel 0.26 vs 0.37-0.88, fat mass, muscle mass)
issues.explanation: In several Table 2 cells the effect size is not inside its printed CI (Barthel STD REHAB 0.26 vs 0.37-0.88; fat mass 0.10 vs 0.53-0.71; muscle mass 0.11 vs 0.51-0.73; handgrip STD 0.36 vs 0.27-0.98 is inside, TUG STD 0.38 vs 0.25-1.00 inside). The fat and muscle rows and Barthel look like lost minus signs on the lower bound, which would restore centring. Whether this is a print or extraction fault cannot be settled, but the printed table is wrong as it stands.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original PDF showing a minus sign before the lower bounds.

script.explanation: the estimate 0.26 lies outside its own CI [0.37, 0.88]; the estimate 0.26 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [0.37, 0.88] (expected about 0.6250) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

10.1371/journal.pone.0348275.headline_claim: The 30-second sit-to-stand test is feasible, safe and reliable in post-COVID-19 condition, and distribution-based estimates suggest a provisional minimal important difference of about two repetitions.
10.1371/journal.pone.0348275.overall: The descriptive findings (feasibility, reduced performance, weak symptom correlations, ICC 0.82) are broadly reliable. The headline thresholds are not: the printed MDC95 of 4.25 and the SEM-based MID of 1.38 do not follow from the paper's own formulas, and 'safe' and 'no learning effect' are worded more strongly than the data support. The MID of 2 remains a tentative, distribution-based suggestion.

primary_outcome.name: 30s-STS repetitions: test-retest reliability and related measurement properties (analysis focus of this paper)

issues.title: MDC95 of 4.25 repetitions conflicts with stated formula and SEM 2.35 (formula gives about 6.5)
issues.explanation: The Methods define MDC95 as 1.96 times the square root of 2 times SEM. With SEM 2.35 this is about 6.5 repetitions, not 4.25. The printed value is repeated in the Abstract, Discussion and Conclusions as the threshold above which change exceeds measurement error. If the formula is right, the threshold is around 6 to 7 repetitions, so the test looks more sensitive to change than the data support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that a different MDC formula or confidence level was used to obtain 4.25.

quotes.text: The SEM was 2.35 repetitions, with a corresponding MDC95 of 4.25 repetitions
defined as 1.96 times the square root of 2 times SEM

second_reader.what_stands: With the paper's own formula and SEM of 2.35, MDC95 is about 6.5 repetitions, not 4.25, and the Bland-Altman limits of agreement point to a similar magnitude (about 7). The conclusion that changes above four repetitions exceed measurement error therefore appears to understate the detectable-change threshold, and the reported 4.25 cannot be reproduced from the printed numbers.

issues.title: SEM-based MID of 1.38 is half the value from the stated formula (SD 6.5, ICC 0.82 gives about 2.76)
issues.explanation: The Methods define the SEM-based MID as SD baseline times sqrt(1-ICC). With baseline SD 6.5 and ICC 0.82 this is about 2.76, not 1.38. The printed 1.38 is the lower end of the MID range quoted in the Abstract and Results, so the range, and the basis for choosing 2, is partly unsupported. The proposed MID of 2 sits within either range, so the practical conclusion changes little.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different baseline SD or ICC used for this calculation, or a stated halving step.

quotes.text: standard error of measurement based approach (SD baseline * square root[1-ICC])
SD baseline * sqrt[1-ICC]
quotes.location: Table 5, Standard error of measurement row

issues.title: 'Safe' conclusion rests on in-session events only; delayed post-exertional symptoms were not assessed
issues.explanation: No adverse events were recorded during exercise testing and oxygen saturation stayed stable, which supports acute safety. No follow-up assessment of post-exertional malaise after the test is described, even though 94% of participants reported it and the authors say it is unclear whether such a short test could trigger it. The unqualified 'safe' in the Abstract and Conclusions goes beyond in-session safety.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing delayed symptom monitoring after the tests (e.g. next-day PEM reports) with no worsening.

quotes.text: The 30s-STS test is feasible, safe, and demonstrates good test-retest reliability.
it is unclear whether such a brief, 30-second task is sufficient to trigger PEM
No adverse events were recorded during exercise testing.

issues.title: 'No learning effect' stated although mean bias 0.84 (95% CI 0.26-1.42) excludes zero
issues.explanation: Scores rose between screening and baseline by 0.84 repetitions, with a confidence interval that excludes zero, and by 1.17 when submaximal-effort participants were excluded. The paper nonetheless says there was no learning effect and no apparent bias. The effect is small, but the statement is stronger than the estimate and sits awkwardly with the recommendation to use a familiarisation test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified margin of equivalence showing the bias is trivially small.

quotes.text: Mean bias between was 0.84 repetitions (95% CI, 0.26 to 1.42).
We did not observe a learning effect when the test was repeated within approximately two weeks.

issues.title: Results text pairs z-scores -1.23/-2.11 with the wrong effort groups; Table 3 gives maximal -1.2, submaximal -2.1
issues.explanation: The Results say the submaximal group had lower z-scores, then print -1.23 for submaximal and -2.11 for maximal, which is the reverse. Table 3 and the Discussion give maximal -1.2 and submaximal -2.1. The pooled mean of -1.4 only works with the Table 3 assignment, so the text is the error. The conclusions are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the text deliberately lists maximal first, which the sentence structure and the Discussion contradict.

quotes.text: mean (SD) z-scores -1.23 (1.14) versus -2.11 (0.97)

quotes.location: Table 3, Repetitions z-score row, Submaximal column

issues.title: Results call the MID of 2 'triangulated' though all anchor-based analyses failed
issues.explanation: No anchor met the correlation or AUC thresholds, so the proposed MID comes only from distribution methods. The Results nevertheless label it a 'provisional triangulated MID', and Section 3.4 refers to a 'triangulation process'. The Conclusions state correctly that a triangulated MID remains to be established. The inconsistency is one of wording.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described process that combined anchor and distribution evidence in reaching 2.

quotes.text: We propose a provisional triangulated MID of 2 repetitions for the 30s-STS in people with PCC.
Future studies are warranted to establish a triangulated minimal important difference

issues.title: Limits of agreement defined as bias ±1.96 x standard error, but reported limits use the SD of differences
issues.explanation: The Methods define limits of agreement as the mean difference plus or minus 1.96 times its standard error. Using the standard error would give very narrow limits, whereas the reported limits (-6.21 to 7.89) match 1.96 times the SD of differences (3.6). The definition is wrong, though the reported values appear correct.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the SD, not the SE, was used.

quotes.text: defined as the mean difference ±1.96 times its standard error

issues.title: Physical activity correlations stated as 0.22-0.26 but S2 Fig reports 0.20 for moderate activity
issues.explanation: The Results give the range of physical activity correlations as 0.22 to 0.26. The S2 Fig caption lists r = 0.20 for time in moderate physical activity. The difference is small and all values are weak, so the interpretation is unchanged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the 0.20 panel is not part of the physical activity analysis.

quotes.text: with correlation coefficients between 0.22 and 0.26

10.1371/journal.pone.0351407.headline_claim: tDCS (F3 anode, F4 cathode, 20 sessions over four weeks) produced no detectable change in resting-state EEG microstates or F3–F4 functional connectivity relative to sham, and the authors conclude a true negative is most likely while acknowledging limited power.
10.1371/journal.pone.0351407.overall: The null finding for microstates and F3-F4 connectivity is reported transparently with no significant results, but with only 13 per arm and no power calculation it cannot distinguish no effect from a modest one, and the 'true negative' reading is stronger than the data allow. Reporting slips (benzodiazepine counts, GFP vs the Bonferroni family) are minor and do not change any conclusion.

primary_outcome.name: Change in Fatigue Impact Scale at end of treatment (clinical primary; EEG measures were secondary exploratory outcomes)

issues.title: Benzodiazepine users: text says 4 active/2 sham, Table 1 shows 8% (1 of 13) in both arms
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion state 6 benzodiazepine patients (4 active, 2 sham). Table 1 for the same 13-per-arm sample lists benzodiazepines/anticonvulsants at 8% in both arms, i.e. about one patient each, which is fewer than the benzodiazepine-only count. The authors rely on the claim that BZD use was balanced and minimal to dismiss a confounder, so the discrepancy matters modestly; the actual imbalance is 2:1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary Table S5 showing that the 6 BZD patients include participants outside the 26 analysed and the table row counts a different definition.

quotes.text: specifically benzodiazepines (BZD; 6 patients, n  =  4 in active group, n  =  2 in sham group)
Benzodiazepines/ Anticonvulsants8%8%

script.explanation: 4/13 = 30.77%, but the paper prints 8, outside the rounding interval [7.50, 9.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 50.0 rather than 13.

issues.title: 13-per-arm exploratory EEG null with no power calculation is read as 'true negative'
issues.explanation: There was no sample-size calculation and only 13 per arm contributed EEG data. The Discussion suggests small effect sizes imply a true negative, borrowing a Bayes factor from the clinical outcome, yet acknowledges limited precision. The null result is uninformative for small to moderate EEG effects; the paper's hedging limits the harm.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated minimal detectable EEG effect size or equivalence test showing the data exclude clinically relevant effects.

quotes.text: The sample size was determined by institutional capacity.
which in connection with the clinical results, would imply a true negative interpretation

issues.title: Bonferroni family of 12 temporal tests vs 16 columns in Table 3 (incl. GFP); no result affected
issues.explanation: Methods define the corrected family as 4 microstates x 3 parameters (12) with alpha 0.0042, but Table 3 reports four parameters per microstate including GFP. The family size is therefore unclear, though all uncorrected p-values exceed 0.16 so no decision depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors stating that the GFP column is a relabelled coverage/GEV column and only 12 parameters were tested.

quotes.text: (4 microstates  ×  3 parameters: duration, occurrence, coverage)
<th>Coverage</th><th>Duration</th><th>Occurrence</th><th>GFP</th>

issues.title: ISRCTN registration 6 May 2022 followed enrolment start (15 Mar 2022) by about seven weeks
issues.explanation: Registration followed enrolment start, so the registry entry cannot by itself prove prespecification. The authors disclose this and say the protocol was finalised earlier, and the study is a null result, so selective outcome reporting would not inflate any claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A dated protocol or ethics submission showing the EEG outcomes were specified before enrolment.

quotes.text: The study was registered after the beginning of the enrolment (start of enrolment - 15/3/2022; registration date - 6/5/2022)

10.1371/journal.pone.0351553.headline_claim: Incentive spirometer (IS) training is an effective, safe, low-cost respiratory training modality that improves dyspnea and functional status in individuals with Long COVID, with earlier intervention (within 3 months of recovery) giving the greatest benefit.
10.1371/journal.pone.0351553.overall: The paper supports only a modest, preliminary signal that IS training coincides with improved dyspnea and function: the within-group changes are large, but the control group is 10 open-label waitlist participants and the primary outcomes are subjective. Several text statements disagree with the tables (PCFS GEE coefficients overstated roughly 4-fold, an unsupported EG2 heart-rate claim, and a timing claim that D-12 magnitudes contradict), and 'safe' is not backed by adverse-event data. The headline conclusions of effectiveness, safety and best results with earliest intervention are therefore stronger than the evidence.

primary_outcome.name: PCFS scale (post-COVID-19 functional status) and D-12 dyspnea score; the paper lists D-12, PCFS and blood biomarkers (CaO2) as primary outcomes

issues.title: 'Earliest intervention gives greatest D-12 improvement' not supported: EG4 change -7.3 and GEE B -5.8 exceed EG1's -6.5 and -4.97
issues.explanation: The Discussion and Conclusion say early IS training yields the greatest improvement in dyspnea. On the D-12, the late-recovery group EG4 had the larger mean reduction and the larger GEE interaction coefficient. EG1's apparent advantage rests mainly on a smaller p value from a larger group, and no test compared the timing subgroups with each other. They also differ at baseline (D-12 and PCFS) and in recovery duration. The timing claim is therefore a descriptive impression, not a demonstrated effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal between-subgroup test (for example EG1 vs EG2-EG4 interaction, adjusted for baseline) showing a significantly larger effect with earlier intervention.

quotes.text: Although the earliest intervention group (EG1) exhibited the greatest improvement
This study confirms that early intervention with IS yields the greatest improvement in dyspnea.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper's own numbers do not show that the earliest group had the greatest D-12 improvement: EG4 has the larger raw change (-7.3 versus -6.5) and the larger GEE interaction coefficient (-5.800 versus -4.965), and the Discussion itself calls the pattern bimodal. The sentence 'confirms that early intervention yields the greatest improvement' overstates this. The point is narrower than a flat contradiction, however: EG1 has the lowest post-test D-12 score and the most precise, most significant within-group result, the EG4 versus EG1 difference in change is not tested and the CIs overlap broadly

issues.title: Efficacy framed via within-group pre-post significance; post-test PCFS group difference p = 0.099, no multiplicity control
issues.explanation: Much of the narrative ('significant improvements across all EGs') relies on paired pre-post tests, which cannot separate treatment from time. The paper itself notes spontaneous recovery as a concern. Between-group evidence exists in the GEE interactions, but it is based on a CG of 10, and many outcomes and contrasts were tested at p < 0.05 without correction. The post-test between-group PCFS difference was not significant. The Discussion's statement that EGs improved significantly more than CG on PCFS and D-12 is only partly backed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified, multiplicity-adjusted between-group primary comparison (for example pooled EG vs CG on PCFS) that was significant.

quotes.text: Post-intervention comparisons of the PCFS scale demonstrated significant improvements across all EGs.
However, after 6 weeks of intervention, these differences were no longer statistically significant

second_reader.what_stands: The post-test between-group PCFS difference is p = 0.099 (non-significant), and the paper frames efficacy substantially through within-group pre-post significance, with no multiplicity control across many outcomes; at a Bonferroni level of 0.01 across the five PCFS within-group tests, the EG4 result (p = 0.011) would not pass. This is partly mitigated by the GEE group-by-time analysis against the CG, whose Table 4 CIs exclude zero; the Results text, however, quotes PCFS B values that differ from Table 4, which I note but did not resolve.

issues.title: Comparator is 10 open-label waitlist participants not matched on recovery time; outcomes are subjective
issues.explanation: The only controlled comparison is between 10 waitlisted people and 75 treated people split into four subgroups that differ in recovery time and baseline PCFS. Both main outcomes are self-reported, with no blinding or sham, so expectation effects could account for much of the difference. The authors accept this in the limitations but still call IS effective. Effect estimates relative to the CG are imprecise and could easily be confounded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded outcome assessment or an objective primary outcome showing the same between-group effect.

quotes.text: the control group had a relatively small sample size and was not stratified according to recovery duration
because of the open-label design and absence of a sham intervention group
Ten participants were randomly assigned to the CG

second_reader.what_stands: The comparator is a small (n = 10) open-label waitlist group that was not stratified by recovery time (mean 6.2 months versus 1.2 to 11.1 in the EG strata, with baseline PCFS differing), and the main positive outcomes (D-12, PCFS) are subjective, while the more objective measures (CaO2, Hb, Hct, 6MWD in most groups) showed little change. The authors acknowledge the small CG, lack of stratification, open-label design, absence of sham and per-protocol analysis, so this is a disclosed limitation, but the Discussion's opening claims that IS is 'effective' go further than this design supports.

issues.title: PCFS GEE interaction B values in text (-2.4 to -3.5) are 3-4 times larger than Table 4 (-0.60 to -0.82)
issues.explanation: The Results text gives group-by-time B coefficients for PCFS of -3.487, -2.754, -2.892 and -2.387 for EG1 to EG4. Table 4 lists -0.823, -0.600, -0.633 and -0.600, and its CIs and the printed p values agree with the table, not the text. PCFS runs only 0 to 4, so a coefficient of -3.5 would be implausible given the observed changes of about -0.8 to -1.0. The text overstates the effect size by roughly a factor of 4, although the significance pattern is unchanged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text coefficients come from a different, unreported model (for example an unstandardised or alternative-coded fit) with the Table 4 values being a different specification.

quotes.location: Results, GEE Interaction on the PCFS Scale
Table 4, PCFS Scale block, EG1 row

issues.title: IS called 'safe' although no adverse-event data are reported; efficacy stated more firmly than data allow
issues.explanation: The first line of the Discussion says the findings show IS to be effective, safe and low-cost. No adverse events, safety monitoring or cost data are reported. With 75 treated participants over 6 weeks, a lack of reported harms is not evidence of safety. The firm 'effective' wording also sits above the limitations the authors list (open-label, 10 controls), though the later Discussion hedges with 'preliminary evidence'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported adverse-event record (for example in the protocol supplement) showing systematic monitoring and few events.

quotes.text: The findings indicate that IS is an effective, safe, and low-cost respiratory training modality
this study provides preliminary evidence supporting IS as a safe, simple, and accessible respiratory training strategy

issues.title: No trial registry identifier given for a trial that describes itself as a randomised controlled trial
issues.explanation: Only an ethics approval number is cited. Without a registration, the primary outcomes cannot be checked against a prior declaration. This matters because the paper lists several 'primary' outcomes (D-12, PCFS, CaO2) and many secondary tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective trial registration number and date in the submission metadata or protocol.

quotes.text: This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Tri-Service General Hospital (Approval No.: A202305044)

issues.title: Text says EG2 resting heart rate improved significantly; Table 3 gives p = 0.917 (change -0.6 bpm)
issues.explanation: The Results say EG2 showed significant improvements in resting heart rate and 6MWD at p < 0.05. In Table 3, EG2's resting heart rate shows a change of -0.6 with p = 0.917, so only 6MWD is significant. This overstates the physiological benefit in a secondary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Another EG2 resting heart-rate measure in the paper with p < 0.05.

quotes.text: EG2 also demonstrated significant improvements in resting heart rate and 6MWD

quotes.location: Table 3, p value row under Pre-HR/Post-HR (before 6MWT)

issues.title: Completer-only analysis: 5 of 90 withdrawals (5.6%) excluded, no ITT analysis, dropouts not shown by arm
issues.explanation: Only participants who completed follow-up were analysed, and the authors acknowledge possible attrition bias. With 5.6% attrition the effect is likely small, but the paper does not show which arms the dropouts came from. Three more participants lacked physiological data, so the per-outcome n is not stated in the tables.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing balanced dropout across arms, or a sensitivity ITT analysis with the same conclusions.

quotes.text: Participants who dropped out were excluded from the final analysis
per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis was applied, potentially introducing attrition bias

issues.title: EG1 baseline Hb is 11.6 g/dL in Table 2 but 11.5 g/dL in Table 3 (same SD 2.12)
issues.explanation: The same group and variable are reported with two different means in two tables. The difference of 0.1 g/dL has no bearing on any conclusion. It does show the tables were not fully reconciled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that Table 3 used a different analysable subset of EG1 (for example excluding the 3 participants without physiological data).

issues.title: 'Physiological items higher than psychological in all groups' contradicted by CG baseline (4.1 vs 4.1)
issues.explanation: The text says physiological D-12 scores were consistently higher than psychological scores before and after intervention in every group. The CG baseline values in Table 2 are identical. The deviation is tiny and does not affect any efficacy conclusion. The supplementary data cannot be checked here.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The supplementary item-level table showing physiological above psychological for the CG at baseline.

D-12 of psychological items 3.62(4.21) 4.1(3.99)

10.14218/fim.2024.00043.headline_claim: Daily ribavirin doses selected by electrodermal medicament testing correlate inversely with EAV readings at certain acupuncture points, which the authors present as a noninvasive way to select ribavirin doses in long COVID.
10.14218/fim.2024.00043.overall: The headline claim, that ribavirin doses chosen by electrodermal testing track disease-related EAV readings in long COVID, is not supported. The outcome is an unvalidated device reading, the dose is defined by that same reading, and 38% of randomised patients are lost with completer-only analysis. The paper has also been retracted, and it contains several small numerical and ethics-documentation inconsistencies.

primary_outcome.name: EAV electrodermal readings (AMV) after medicament testing, compared between ribavirin and placebo groups; tested ribavirin dose vs pretest reading correlation

issues.title: Dose-reading correlations (rho -0.77 to -0.92) follow from the dose-titration rule; Table 4 n (32, 41) unexplained
issues.explanation: The dose is defined as the number of tablets needed to restore a normal reading, so a lower starting reading will mechanically require a higher dose. The strong Spearman correlations and the near-identical post-test values of about 6 therefore follow from the procedure rather than from any disease effect. Table 4 also uses n = 32 and 41, not the 52 analysed experimental patients, and does not say why.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that dose selection was independent of the pre-test reading, and a stated rule for who enters each Table 4 row.

quotes.text: The final number of tablets placed in the honeycomb of the EAV device that restores normal electrodermal activity at the studied APs during the MT process is determined as the selected daily dose of the drug.
Ne_Ribavirin2021 & Ne_pre- test 2020-2021

second_reader.what_stands: The strong negative dose-reading correlations follow from the titration rule, so they are built into the procedure and do not test any hypothesis. The n of 32 (Ne) and 41 (Kr) in Table 4 are not explained anywhere. They match neither the group sizes nor the completer numbers, and they stay constant across years.

issues.title: All outcomes are arbitrary-unit Voll electrodermal readings with no validation or clinical endpoint
issues.explanation: Every result is an arbitrary measurement value from an electrodermal device, or a dose selected on that device, with no validation against disease, viral load or symptoms. The authors say the technique is complex and operator-dependent, and only two operators took part, with no reproducibility data. The study cannot show that the readings or the tested doses mean anything clinically.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Published validation of the dose-testing method against clinical or virological endpoints and inter-operator agreement data.

quotes.text: The arbitrary measurement value (AMV) was used to analyze the MT results.
The technical implementation of the technique is quite complex and requires skillful operation.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper has no clinical endpoint (no symptoms, function, viral measures or imaging) and no validation of the dose-titration method against any independent standard. Every reported measure comes from the Voll device, either as AMV readings or as doses derived from them. The authors openly acknowledge the lack of clinical evidence and of reproducibility testing, so the problem is real but disclosed.

issues.title: Results call an inverse dose-reading relationship 'convincing' and Discussion links it to organ damage
issues.explanation: The Results state that the tables convincingly demonstrate an inverse relationship, and the Discussion proposes that doses reflect organ damage from SARS-CoV-2. The study has no virological, clinical or diagnostic data, and the relationship is built into the dose-selection method (c10). Hedging in the Discussion does not cure the stronger Results wording.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Clinical or virological data linking tested doses to disease severity.

quotes.text: we suggest that the tested daily doses of the antiviral drug ribavirin may reflect varying degrees of damage to the organs and systems of the body
The data presented in these tables convincingly demonstrate an inverse relationship

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does use 'convincingly demonstrate' for the inverse dose-reading relationship, which conflicts with the tentative wording in the sentences right after it and with the circularity of that relationship. It also links doses to organ damage, but only with explicit caveats, and without any organ-damage data.

issues.title: 38% of randomised patients lost (46% vs 28% by arm); only the 101 completers are analysed, no ITT
issues.explanation: Of 164 randomised patients, 63 dropped out, more in the experimental arm. The EAV comparisons use only the 52 and 49 completers, with no intention-to-treat analysis or comparison of dropouts with completers. Differential loss could change who remains in each arm, and the direction of any bias cannot be judged from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ITT or multiple-imputation analysis giving the same group differences, or baseline data showing dropouts resembled completers.

quotes.text: 44 patients in the experimental group and 19 in the placebo group dropped out for various reasons
The final numbers of patients were 52 (51.5%) in the experimental group and 49 (48.5%) in the placebo group.

second_reader.what_stands: About 38% of the 164 allocated patients were lost, unequally by arm (about 46% vs 28%). The paper reports only the 101 completers and describes no intention-to-treat analysis or handling of missing data. That the analysis is completers-only is inferred from this silence and from Table 4's smaller n, not from an explicit statement.

issues.title: About 150 significance comparisons at p<0.05 across meridians, years and pre/post with no correction
issues.explanation: Tables 1-3 compare 12 measurement points over 3 periods, pre and post, and against placebo, all at an uncorrected 0.05 level. Many starred results are only p<0.05, so some could arise by chance. The methods also describe correlation significance as 'r < 0.05', which looks like a typo for p.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary test or an adjustment such as Holm or FDR that leaves the claimed results significant.

quotes.text: Intergroup differences were considered significant at p < 0.05.

issues.title: Examinations stated to start October 2020, before IRB approval of 27/11/2020; approval number 1549 vs 1550
issues.explanation: The Methods say examination and MT ran from October 2020, but the cited approval is dated 27 November 2020, and the approval number differs between Methods (1549) and the Ethical statement (1550). Either the dates are loosely stated or early patients were examined before approval. The paper does not resolve which.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: IRB letter showing approval before enrolment and the correct protocol number.

quotes.text: from October 2020 to December 2023
quotes.location: Materials and methods, Aim, design, and study settings
Materials and methods, Aim, design, and study settings

issues.title: A randomised placebo-controlled trial enrolling from 2020 reports no registry entry or protocol
issues.explanation: No trial identifier or protocol reference is given, so the planned outcomes, sample size and analysis cannot be checked. This matters here because the outcome is non-standard and many comparisons are reported. No sample size justification is given either.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective registry entry with matching outcomes.

quotes.text: This blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial aimed to investigate
quotes.location: Materials and methods, Aim, design, and study settings

issues.title: Randomisation and blinding are asserted but not described; arms 96 vs 68 and no concealment or blinding details
issues.explanation: The trial is called blind and randomised, but there is no sequence generation, concealment or description of who was blinded. The unequal arms contradict the stated ratio (see c1) and vaccination differed between arms at the end. The allocation process cannot be verified from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol describing concealed allocation and blinded assessors and a sequence-generation method.

quotes.text: patients were divided into two groups using a simple random sampling method
quotes.location: Materials and methods, Aim, design, and study settings

quotes.text: Among these patients, 42.5% were vaccinated against COVID-19: 51.9% in the experimental group and 37.2% in the placebo group.

issues.title: Stated 1.06:1 allocation ratio matches the 52:49 completers, not the 96:68 randomised groups (1.41:1)
issues.explanation: The Methods say patients were assigned at a 1.06:1 ratio. The Results show 96 and 68 patients were allocated, a ratio of about 1.41:1, and 1.06:1 only matches the 52 and 49 patients left at the end. The allocation description is therefore wrong or misleading, and the arms were noticeably unequal at baseline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol statement of unequal allocation giving 96:68, with 1.06 explicitly defined as the completer ratio.

quotes.text: we assigned patients to the experimental and placebo groups at a 1.06:1 ratio
quotes.location: Materials and methods, Description of the intervention

quotes.text: The final numbers of patients were 52 (51.5%) in the experimental group and 49 (48.5%) in the placebo group.

issues.title: Spearman analysis limited to 2 of 12 meridians (Ne, Kr), apparently those with the highest doses
issues.explanation: Correlations were calculated for Ne and Kr only, with no prespecified reason; Le, also among the highest, is omitted. Selecting by the largest doses can favour strong correlations. Table 4 does show the weak post-test results, which limits the concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified analysis plan naming Ne and Kr.

quotes.text: The Spearman coefficient was calculated for two meridians, Ne and Kr.

issues.title: Vaccination percentages inconsistent: 37.2% impossible at n = 49 and overall 42.5% does not match the arms
issues.explanation: Among the 101 completers, 51.9% of 52 is 27 patients, but 37.2% of 49 does not match a whole number (18/49 = 36.7%, 19/49 = 38.8%). The overall 42.5% also differs from the weighted mean of the arms, about 44.6%. The vaccination imbalance is used to describe the groups, so its numbers should reconcile.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Vaccination counts and denominators per arm that reproduce 51.9%, 37.2% and 42.5%.

quotes.text: Among these patients, 42.5% were vaccinated against COVID-19: 51.9% in the experimental group and 37.2% in the placebo group.

issues.title: Ne-3 2023 post-test printed as 7.8 ± 9.89 while every other post-test is about 5.7-6.1 with SD under 0.4
issues.explanation: All other post-test readings sit near 6 with small SDs, apparently at a device ceiling. The Ne-3 2023 post-test mean of 7.8 with SD 9.89 is far outside that pattern and likely a transcription error or an outlier driving the result. It is marked highly significant versus placebo in Table 3.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing this cell is correct.

issues.title: Text gives Kr 2023 Spearman rho as -0.866; Table 4 gives -0.826824
issues.explanation: The Results report rho = -0.866 for Kr in 2023. Table 4 gives -0.826824, and its t statistic (-9.1802) fits the table value. The other five coefficients in the text agree with the table to rounding, so this one is a transcription error, though it overstates the correlation slightly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected analysis showing -0.866 for this pair.

quotes.text: ρ = -0.821, ρ = -0.828, and ρ = -0.866 for the Kr meridian

issues.title: Results text gives 538.3 mg for Le-1a* in 2023 while Table 1 and an earlier sentence give 538.9 mg
issues.explanation: The Results give the 2023 Le-1a* dose as 538.9 mg in one sentence and 538.3 mg in another. Table 1 prints 538.9. This is a small typographical inconsistency that changes no conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; a typo, since the paper prints both values.

issues.title: Experience of the two MT experts is 33 and 22 years in Methods but 32 and 21 years in Limitations
issues.explanation: The same two specialists are described with experience differing by one year each between sections. The discrepancy is trivial and does not bear on the findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that experience was updated between enrolment and writing.

quotes.location: Materials and methods, Description of the intervention

10.14393/hygeia2071051.headline_claim: The Pilates method is an effective strategy for improving cardiorespiratory function and physical conditioning in individuals with post-COVID-19 sequelae.
10.14393/hygeia2071051.overall: The headline conclusion that Pilates is effective is not supported by the paper's own between-group results: the primary outcome (6-minute-walk distance) and respiratory outcomes show no difference between arms, and the Conclusion and abstract contradict the Results. The trial is also underpowered (39 of 96 required), has 25-28% attrition with unclear ITT handling, and relies on within-group changes. At best it is a small exploratory study suggestive of a possible reduction in perceived exertion.

primary_outcome.name: Six-minute walk test distance (TC6min, physical conditioning)

issues.title: Conclusion/abstract claim between-group differences in expansibility, respiratory strength and distance; Results show none
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says there were statistically significant between-group differences in thoracic expansibility and respiratory muscle strength, and a significant increase in walking distance. The Results state that no between-group difference existed for any cirtometry, manovacuometry or walking-distance measure. The abstract likewise reports GC with higher respiratory strength than GP at p<0.05, which Results and Table 3 do not show. These headline claims are therefore not supported by the paper's own between-group data. Only the 5-minute post-test Borg score differs between groups.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis (for example change scores or T16 comparisons) showing significant differences in expansibility, respiratory strength and distance, with the Results text being the error.

quotes.text: Não houve diferença entre os grupos em nenhuma das mensurações da cirtometria torácica, tanto no período T0 quanto no período T16 (p>0,05)
houve diferença estatisticamente significativa entre os grupos nas variáveis de aumento na expansibilidade torácica e na força muscular respiratória
Não houve diferença entre os grupos em nenhuma das mensurações relacionadas à distância percorrida, tanto no período T0 quanto no período T16 (p > 0,05)

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion asserts between-group differences in thoracic expansibility, respiratory muscle strength and walked distance, whereas the Results report none for those variables; the only between-group difference in Table 3 is perceived exertion 5 min after the walk test. The respiratory strength improvement was within the control group, not in favour of Pilates.

issues.title: Efficacy conclusion rests on within-group changes; primary 6MWT outcome shows no between-group difference
issues.explanation: The primary outcome, 6-minute-walk distance, improved significantly within the Pilates group but did not differ between groups at T16. Most claimed benefits (expansibility, walking distance, exertion) are within-group changes, which a control group would also show if it also improved or regressed to the mean. Within-group significance in one arm and not the other does not show a treatment difference. The conclusion that Pilates is effective is therefore not supported by the trial's comparative evidence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified between-group comparison of change in 6MWT distance (adjusted for baseline) that was significant.

quotes.text: O desfecho principal deste estudo, o condicionamento físico, foi avaliado por meio do Teste de Caminhada de Seis Minutos (TC6min)
Não houve diferença entre os grupos em nenhuma das mensurações relacionadas à distância percorrida

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy conclusion for the primary 6MWT outcome rests on a significant within-group change in the Pilates group, while the between-group comparison of distance is non-significant and no between-group change analysis is shown. Perceived exertion, a secondary measure within the 6MWT, is the only between-group difference.

issues.title: Analysed 39 participants against 96 required (48 per arm); effectiveness stated confidently
issues.explanation: The sample-size calculation needed 48 participants per group, but only 20 and 19 were randomised. The shortfall is acknowledged in the limitations, yet the abstract and conclusion state effectiveness without qualification. With the trial this underpowered, a null between-group result on the primary outcome cannot be read as evidence of benefit, and nominal findings are unstable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified calculation justifying a much smaller sample for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: seria necessária uma amostra de 48 indivíduos para cada grupo
Uma delas é o tamanho da amostra que foi menor do que o indicado pelo cálculo amostral

second_reader.what_stands: The study analysed 39 participants against a requirement of 96 (48 per arm), about 41% of the target, and the authors acknowledge this in the limitations. The conclusion nonetheless calls Pilates 'eficaz' without tempering for low power; the 'analysed 39' framing is correct only under ITT, and the 11 lost to follow-up (stated, though 4+6=10) means outcome data were presumably missing for some of them without an imputation method being described.

issues.title: Dozens of uncorrected comparisons; the sole significant between-group result (Borg p=0.010) is nominal
issues.explanation: The study tested well over fifty outcome-timepoint-comparison combinations at alpha 5% with no correction. The single significant between-group result (lower perceived exertion 5 minutes after the walk test) could easily arise by chance. This weakens a secondary result, not the null primary result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchy or correction showing this result survives adjustment.

quotes.text: menor percepção de esforço nos cinco minutos após o teste em relação ao GC (IC95% -2,193 - -0,322; p = 0,010)

issues.title: Baseline imbalance (education p=0.003, weight loss p=0.008, age 52 vs 43) with no adjusted analysis
issues.explanation: Groups differed at baseline in education, weight loss and anxiety symptoms, and GP was nine years older. The authors say the GC was in better physical condition. The between-group comparison was not adjusted for these differences, which could distort it in either direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A baseline-adjusted analysis showing the same between-group results.

quotes.text: a amostra do GC apresentava melhores condições físico funcionais comparados ao GP, o que pode ter interferido na comparação dos resultados

issues.title: ITT claimed for all 39 despite 10-11 lost to follow-up; handling of missing T16 data not described
issues.explanation: About a quarter of participants were lost to follow-up, yet all 39 are said to be analysed by intention to treat. The paper does not say how the missing T16 values were handled, and paired and independent t-tests need outcome data. The exclusion criterion for under 80% attendance also sits oddly with an ITT claim. The analysed numbers and the reliability of the T16 results are unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of imputation or a mixed model using all randomised participants, or a flow chart showing T16 data for all 39.

quotes.text: foram mantidos os 39 indivíduos como amostra analisados por meio da intenção de tratar
houve a perda de acompanhamento de 11 indivíduos

issues.title: 6MWT total change CI (-102.576 to 42.723) spans zero but p = 0.000; likely a dropped minus sign
issues.explanation: The printed CI for the GP total walk distance change includes zero, yet p is given as 0.000. The Table 3 means imply a change of about 72.65 m. A sign slip on the upper bound would reconcile everything, so this is probably a typo and not a substantive problem. It cannot be settled from the text alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original PDF showing '-42,723' (an extraction loss) would reject this.

issues.title: Losses stated as 11 but the arm split (4 GP + 6 GC) sums to 10
issues.explanation: The Methods state 11 participants were lost, then split this as four in the GP and six in the GC, which sums to 10. The loss figure affects the attrition rate (28.2% against 25.6%). It is a small reporting error, but the actual number of completers is unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 1 showing 11 lost, with one participant in a category not mentioned in the text.

quotes.text: houve a perda de acompanhamento de 11 indivíduos (quatro do GP e seis do GC)

10.14393/hygeia2071233.headline_claim: Supervised physical exercise was effective for relieving pain and improving functional capacity (30-second sit-to-stand) in individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome, and was superior to control for improving lumbar spine flexibility.
10.14393/hygeia2071233.overall: The conclusion that the exercise programme 'was effective' for pain and function rests mainly on within-group change in a completer-only analysis, with no post-intervention between-group difference and a large baseline imbalance in pain. The flexibility superiority claim comes from one borderline measure among many unadjusted tests and conflicts with the paper's own Results text. Several table and text slips (duplicated Table 1 rows, pain contradiction) reduce confidence further. The findings are at best tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; pain (VAS) and 30-second sit-to-stand are the outcomes the abstract emphasises

issues.title: Efficacy for pain and function rests on within-group change; no post-intervention between-group difference
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion say the programme was effective for pain and function. This rests on paired pre-post tests in G1 only. The between-group comparison after the intervention was non-significant for pain and sit-to-stand, and the groups differed at baseline in both, so the change in G1 cannot be separated from regression to the mean and non-specific effects of supervised contact. The language of 'concrete evidence' and policy relevance (including 'low cost', for which no cost data are given) goes well beyond a small, completer-only, unblinded-participant trial.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A baseline-adjusted between-group analysis (e.g. ANCOVA) showing a significant treatment effect on pain and sit-to-stand.

quotes.text: diferenças estas não observadas no pós-intervenção
fornecem evidências concretas sobre a eficácia desta abordagem na melhoria dos sintomas da síndrome pós-COVID-19

second_reader.what_stands: The pain and function conclusions rest on within-group pre/post tests, and the paper itself reports no between-group difference after the intervention for pain or sit-to-stand, with no baseline-adjusted or interaction analysis. The only between-group advantage claimed (lumbar flexibility) is stated separately in the abstract, and the pain and function claims are not worded as superiority over control.

issues.title: Completer-only analysis after 11 of 39 (28%) losses; analysed n not stated, no ITT
issues.explanation: Eleven of 39 randomised participants were lost, and the exclusion criteria drop anyone who attended under 80% of sessions. Only completers appear to be analysed, with no intention-to-treat or missing-data analysis. Table 3 headers still carry the randomised group sizes, so the reader cannot tell the true analysed n. Completer-only results can overstate the benefit of a programme requiring regular attendance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ITT or multiple-imputation analysis giving the same conclusions, plus a statement of the analysed n per group.

quotes.text: Ocorreu uma perda de 11 indivíduos durante o acompanhamento (cinco no G1 e seis no G2)
indivíduos que realizaram menos de 80% das sessões completas

second_reader.what_stands: The 11 of 39 losses (28%) are stated, the analysed n is not given in the text or in any table (Table 3 only shows the randomised n in the heading), and no ITT or imputation is described, with paired t-tests implying complete cases. 'Completer-only' is an inference rather than an explicit statement, and the flowchart image could not be read, so it may show the analysed numbers.

issues.title: Flexibility results contradict each other: 'no post-intervention difference' vs G1 superior on Schöber, pre and post
issues.explanation: Results paragraph 3 says the groups did not differ on spinal flexibility after the intervention. The abstract and conclusion say G1 was superior for lumbar flexibility, and Table 3 marks post-intervention Schöber for G1. Paragraph 4 also says G1 exceeded G2 on Schöber at both time points, but the T0 Schöber cells carry no between-group marker. A recomputation from the T0 means and SDs (about 15 vs 13 analysed) gives t about 1.7, p about 0.1, so a pre-intervention difference is not supported. The abstract's 'superior' claim therefore rests on one lumbar measure with a borderline difference (post-intervention t about 2.0), among about 20 unadjusted flexibility and strength comparisons.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Group n per time point and between-group p-values for each Schöber measure showing a pre-intervention difference, with the paragraph 3 sentence limited to non-Schöber tests.

quotes.text: Os grupos não apresentaram diferença nos valores dos testes flexibilidade da coluna vertebral e da força muscular, após as intervenções
o G1 apresentou maiores valores de flexibilidade da coluna lombar em comparação ao G2
tanto na fase pré-intervenção quanto na fase pós-intervenção

issues.title: Sample size taken from parent project; 28 of 39 analysed, power not shown
issues.explanation: No sample-size calculation, target or primary outcome is given for this study, which defers to the parent project. After 11 losses the analysed sample is 28, and the authors state that attendance compromised sample size. Non-significant between-group results cannot show equivalence, and the confident conclusions do not reflect this reduced power.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The parent trial's calculation showing adequate power for the analysed n on the primary outcome.

quotes.text: O tamanho da amostra para este estudo foi baseado no cálculo realizado no ensaio clínico do projeto principal.
a falta de assiduidade da amostra acabou comprometendo o tamanho da amostra

issues.title: Primary outcome and registration timing not stated; cannot check against ReBEC entry
issues.explanation: The paper cites a ReBEC number but names no primary outcome and does not give the registration date. Pain, function, flexibility and strength are all treated as outcomes, with the headline claim on pain and capacity. Without a prespecified primary outcome, the selection of positive findings cannot be checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment whose primary outcome is pain or the 30-second sit-to-stand test.

quotes.text: foi aprovado sob número do parecer 'RBR-9wrfxcn'

issues.title: G2 pain increase is significant in Results/Table 3 (0.57 to 2.15) but 'not significant' in Discussion
issues.explanation: Results and Table 3 report a statistically significant within-group pain increase in the control group, from 0.57 to 2.15. The Discussion says G2 showed no statistically significant increase. The control group also started with very low pain (0.57 vs 4.85 in G1), so the pattern looks like regression to the mean. This should be interpreted as such, not as a clean contrast between 'reduction' and 'no change'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction showing that the G2 pain change was not significant, with the marker in Table 3 an error.

quotes.text: enquanto o G2 apresentou aumento da dor
enquanto que o G2, não apresentou aumento estatisticamente significativo

issues.title: Discussion ranks chronic pain most common persistent symptom; Table 2 gives fatigue 20 vs chronic pain 9
issues.explanation: The Results list fatigue first among persistent symptoms. Table 2 counts fatigue in 20 participants and chronic pain in 9. The Discussion nonetheless says chronic pain was the most common. This does not affect the efficacy analysis, but it misstates the sample's profile.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition limiting the ranking to a musculoskeletal subset in which chronic pain exceeds fatigue.

quotes.text: a dor crônica foi o sintoma mais comum relatado, seguido por fadiga e fraqueza muscular
Os sintomas persistentes mais relatados foram a fadiga, fraqueza muscular, cefaleia

issues.title: Table 2 anosmia/ageusia p=0,047 not acknowledged in 'homogeneous except chronic pain'
issues.explanation: The Results say the COVID-19 clinical characteristics were homogeneous except chronic pain. Table 2 also shows p=0,047 for persistent anosmia/ageusia, which occurred only in G2. This is a minor omission among many baseline tests, with no bearing on the efficacy conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; this is a wording matter.

quotes.text: os grupos mostraram-se homogêneos, exceto pela variável dor crônica

issues.title: Table 1 rows for no comorbidity, cardiovascular disease and hypertension are identical (5 vs 6, p=0,731)
issues.explanation: Three comorbidity rows of Table 1 carry identical counts, percentages and p-values. The 'no comorbidities' row cannot logically equal two disease categories with the same members. At least two of the rows are wrong or copied, so the baseline comorbidity profile is unreliable. Another cell is also off: 7/9 is printed as 77,2% where 77,8% is correct.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing three genuinely identical splits, which is implausible for a no-comorbidity category.

quotes.text: Sem comorbidades
Hipertensão arterial sistêmica

10.14412/1996-7012-2022-3-67-74.headline_claim: Parenteral chondroitin sulfate added to oral celecoxib reduced knee pain and improved function in early knee osteoarthritis with long COVID, and was associated with changes in serum inflammatory markers and proteins.
10.14412/1996-7012-2022-3-67-74.overall: The clinical conclusion that adding parenteral CS reduces pain and improves function rests on an open-label trial with no sham injection and patient-reported endpoints, so it should be read as tentative. The biomarker and mechanistic claims are exploratory, uncorrected for multiplicity and overstated in the Discussion. A caption inconsistency in Figure 1 and incomplete sponsor disclosure add minor concerns.

primary_outcome.name: Knee pain intensity (VAS) and Lequesne functional index

issues.title: Open-label, no-sham design with patient-reported pain/function outcomes (25 injections vs none)
issues.explanation: The study is open-label and the efficacy endpoints are patient-reported VAS pain and Lequesne function. The treatment arm also received a course of 25 intramuscular injections while the control arm received celecoxib alone, with no placebo injection. Expectation, attention and injection effects therefore cannot be separated from any drug effect on subjective outcomes, so the pain and function conclusion is tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of blinded outcome assessment or a sham injection in the control arm.

quotes.text: проведено открытое проспективное контролируемое рандомизированное исследование
Пациентам 1-й группы дополнительно назначали парентеральную форму ХС
Интенсивность боли в КС определяли по ВАШ, тяжесть функциональных нарушений (ФН) суставов - по индексу Лекена.
quotes.location: Методы, Визиты и методы регистрации исходов

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is explicitly open-label, the control arm received no placebo or sham injection (celecoxib alone vs celecoxib plus a 25-injection CS course), and the primary endpoints (VAS pain, Lequesne function) are patient-reported or subjectively assessed, with no blinded outcome assessment described and no discussion of this as a limitation. The objective laboratory and ultrasound outcomes are less susceptible, but the clinical endpoints and the symptom-driven celecoxib dose-reduction decisions could be influenced by knowledge of allocation.

issues.title: Fig 1 legend gives p<0.0001 for group comparison 'at baseline' vs p=0.176 in Table 1
issues.explanation: Table 1 reports baseline VAS pain as 58.4 vs 58.2 mm with p=0.176, and the text says baseline groups did not differ. The Figure 1 legend says p<0.0001 when comparing groups at baseline and on day 50. The two statements cannot both hold, but the legend is most likely a careless caption, so the main efficacy result is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The figure itself showing the asterisk only on day-50 points, with the legend merely worded loosely.

quotes.text: * - p<0,0001 при сравнении 1-й и 2-й групп исходно и на 50-й день исследования

issues.title: About a dozen biomarker/protein comparisons with no multiplicity control; mechanistic claims rest on significant subset
issues.explanation: CRP, IL6, IL1β, D-dimer, fibrinogen, six serum proteins and ultrasound findings were tested with a single alpha of 0.05 and no correction. The mechanistic story in the Discussion is built from the comparisons that reached significance. This weakens the secondary and mechanistic results, not the clinical pain outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchy or correction for the biomarker analyses.

quotes.text: Различия считали статистически значимыми при р<0,05.
Во 2-й группе статистически значимых изменений изучаемых показателей не выявлено

issues.title: IL-15 suppression 'proves' a mechanism of action; serum detection-frequency data cannot show it
issues.explanation: The Discussion says IL-15 suppression proves a link in the mechanism of action of CS (reduced metalloproteinase secretion and pain sensitisation). The evidence is only the proportion of patients with a detectable serum protein band, in a qualitative proteomic analysis of an open-label trial. Such data cannot establish mechanism, and the paper offers no limitations paragraph.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A designed mechanistic analysis (e.g. mediation or synovial fluid data) supporting the causal claim.

quotes.text: Подавление экспрессии ИЛ15 доказывает наличие в механизме действия ХС звена
Следовательно, опосредованный фактором роста нервных волокон β эффективный нейроиммунный механизм действия ХС может объяснить снижение интенсивности боли и ФН

issues.title: No trial registration identifier reported for a randomized trial
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomized trial but gives no registry number or date, so pre-specification of outcomes and analysis cannot be checked. Only ethics approval is mentioned. This weakens confidence somewhat but does not itself show a result is wrong.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with a registration date before enrolment.

quotes.text: Исследование одобрено локальным этическим комитетом ООО «Медицинский центр «Новомедицина»» (протокол № 2 от 01.12.2020).

issues.title: Manufacturer supported publication; its role in design/analysis and author conflicts not stated
issues.explanation: The article was published with support from the company that markets the tested product. The statement does not say whether the company had a role in design, data handling or analysis, and no author-level conflicts are listed. This is a disclosure gap that is relevant to an open-label, industry-linked trial.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in design, analysis or interpretation and that authors have no conflicts.

quotes.text: Статья опубликована при поддержке компании ЗАО «ФармФирма «Сотекс».

10.14412/2074-2711-2021-2-65-72.headline_claim: Long-term oral Actovegin improves cognitive function, fatigue and emotional state in post-COVID patients with cognitive impairment compared with standard therapy alone.
10.14412/2074-2711-2021-2-65-72.overall: The headline claim that Actovegin improves cognition, fatigue and anxiety, and is safe, is not well supported. The comparison is an open-label, matched, non-randomized study against usual care only, with baseline imbalance, internal inconsistencies in the study dates and baseline p-values, and no adverse-event data. The direction of the reported effects may be genuine, but the size and the safety claim cannot be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: MoCA score (cognitive function) at day 60

issues.title: Groups described as randomized but allocated by matching; baseline MFI-20 differed (70.5 vs 64.6, p<0.01)
issues.explanation: The abstract says controls were randomized, but the Methods describe matched, non-randomized groups with no allocation procedure. The groups differed at baseline in fatigue (p<0.01 in Table 2), with the Actovegin group worse and with more room to improve. Between-group differences at follow-up may therefore partly reflect selection and baseline imbalance rather than the drug.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described random allocation procedure with concealment, or baseline-adjusted analysis showing the same effect.

quotes.text: were  randomized  to  the  control  group
matched-controlled
quotes.location: Пациенты и методы, group standardisation paragraph

quotes.text: в 1-й группе 70,50±1,12 балла, а во 2-й - 64,64±0,76 балла

second_reader.what_stands: The English abstract calls the control group 'randomized', but the methods describe matched-control allocation with no randomization procedure, and baseline MFI-20 differed by about 5.9 points (70.50 vs 64.64, p<0.01). The imbalance disadvantaged the Actovegin group in absolute level, but it still undermines a clean between-group comparison, and no baseline-adjusted analysis is reported.

issues.title: Study dates run to 31.01.2021 and courses last 60 days, but the manuscript was received 21.01.2021
issues.explanation: The Methods say the study ran until 31.01.2021, and every patient is said to have completed a full 60-day course. The manuscript was received on 21.01.2021, ten days before the stated end of the study. Patients included late in the window could not have finished 60 days of treatment before submission. Separately, the Methods give a mean duration of 57±3 days, which does not fit all patients completing 60 days. The data collection period and the completeness of follow-up are therefore not credible as described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected enrolment calendar showing that the last patient completed day 60 before 21.01.2021, or an erratum correcting the dates.

quotes.text: Исследование проводилось на протяжении 10 мес (с 01.04.2020 г. по 31.01.2021 г.)
Received/Reviewed/Accepted 21.01.2021/13.03.2021/16.03.2021
57±3 дня от начала включения в настоящее исследование

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states a study end date (31.01.2021) that is later than the printed received date (21.01.2021), and the text cites material dated February 2021, so the dates are internally inconsistent as printed. The paper does not explain this; it could be a revision date or a typographical error, which cannot be determined from the paper.

issues.title: Conclusion asserts high efficacy and safety and 'drug of choice' without adverse-event data
issues.explanation: The final paragraph claims high efficacy and safety of prolonged Actovegin therapy. The paper reports no adverse events, tolerability or safety monitoring, and follow-up ended at day 60. No comparison with other agents was made, so 'drug of choice' is unsupported. The abstract's more modest conclusion is closer to what the data allow.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adverse-event and discontinuation data by group showing no excess events.

quotes.text: высокой эффективности и безопасности
Препаратом выбора мы считаем Актовегин

second_reader.what_stands: The final conclusion states that the study shows high efficacy and safety and calls Actovegin the drug of choice, but the paper reports no adverse-event, tolerability or laboratory safety data, and the only comparator is usual care, so neither 'safety' nor 'drug of choice' is supported by data presented. Full completion of the course by all patients is the only indirect hint and does not establish safety.

issues.title: Open-label usual-care control, no placebo or blinding, for self-rated fatigue and anxiety outcomes
issues.explanation: The comparison group received baseline therapy only, with no placebo and no reported blinding. Self-reported fatigue and anxiety scores, and possibly assessor-rated cognitive scores, are vulnerable to expectation effects. The reported benefits in these outcomes could partly reflect knowing about treatment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of masked outcome assessment and a placebo or sham comparator.

quotes.text: Группу сравнения (2-я группа) составили 222 пациента
emotional disturbances - with Spielberger-Hanin test

second_reader.what_stands: The control group received usual care only, with no placebo and no description of blinding of patients or assessors, while the key outcomes (fatigue, anxiety, and in part cognition) are subjective or rater-dependent. The paper does not discuss this as a limitation. It is not stated that the study was unblinded, only that no blinding is described.

issues.title: Baseline p-values (age p=0.987; MoCA visit 1 p≥0.05) do not fit the printed means and spreads
issues.explanation: The groups are described as comparable at baseline. But the printed means and spreads imply a clear difference in age and in MoCA at visit 1. If the printed p-values are wrong or the spread values are mislabelled, the baseline comparability, and the credibility of the matching claim, is in doubt. The MoCA baseline difference favours the Actovegin group.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Per-patient baseline data showing the groups do not differ in age and MoCA at visit 1.

issues.title: No primary endpoint or multiplicity control across three scales, domains and visits
issues.explanation: The paper tests several outcomes (MoCA total and domains, MFI-20, anxiety) at several visits with Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Pearson and Fisher tests, without naming a primary endpoint or correcting for multiple comparisons. Isolated p<0.05 results, such as the anxiety findings, are weaker than they look. The effects on MFI-20 and MoCA at day 60 look large enough that the overall direction probably does not depend on this.
