issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary endpoint (for example MoCA at day 60) with the other outcomes labelled secondary.

quotes.text: Статистическую значимость различий в исследуемых группах вычисляли с использованием
Максимальный рост был выявлен среди следующих показателей

issues.title: Overall mean age 67.7±1.1 is inconsistent with group means 67.5 and 68.2 (n=222 each)
issues.explanation: With equal group sizes the overall mean must lie midway between the group means, about 67.85, which rounding cannot bring down to 67.7. The overall SD (1.1) is also lower than the SD in each group. This is a minor reporting error in the baseline table, and the group-level age data do not support a 40-75 range with SD about 1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level ages showing a total mean of 67.7 with these group means.

quotes.text: 67,7±1,1 года (от 40 до 75 лет)
Средний возраст, годы, M± σ

issues.title: Diarrhoea and skin rash rows in Table 1 are identical in every column (19; 12 vs 7; p=0.665)
issues.explanation: Two different symptoms share counts, percentages and p-values in all four columns. This may be a copy error in the table. The printed p also does not fit an exact test of 12/222 vs 7/222. The effect on the conclusion is small because these are baseline symptoms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data confirming that exactly 19 patients had each symptom with the same 12/7 split.

quotes.text: Диарея, n (%)
Кожная сыпь, n (%)

issues.title: Cough in total sample: 385/444 is 86.71%, but 85.71% is printed in Table 1 and text
issues.explanation: The count of 385 patients with cough out of 444 corresponds to 86.71%, not 85.71%. The group counts (189 and 196) sum to 385, so the count is consistent and the percentage is wrong. This is a one-digit error in a baseline symptom and does not affect the efficacy findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the total n with cough is 380, with the group counts then wrong.

quotes.text: Кашель, сухой или с небольшим количеством мокроты, n (%)

script.explanation: 385/444 = 86.71%, but the paper prints 85.71, outside the rounding interval [85.70, 85.72]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 449.2 rather than 444.

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified protocol reported for a prospective interventional comparison
issues.explanation: The paper describes ethics committee approval and written consent but gives no registry or registration number. Outcome selection and analysis decisions cannot be checked against a plan. This adds to the multiplicity concern but is not by itself an error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or published protocol dated before enrolment.

quotes.text: Протокол исследования одобрен этическими комитетами

10.14412/2074-2711-2021-4-88-93.headline_claim: MexiB 6 and Cholytilin (choline alfoscerate) may be the drugs of choice for asthenic, anxiety-depressive and cognitive disorders after COVID-19, based on symptom improvement over about 2 months.
10.14412/2074-2711-2021-4-88-93.overall: The reported improvements come from two non-randomised, uncontrolled pre-post groups, each selected on the baseline score of an outcome later re-measured, so they cannot be attributed to the drugs. The 'drugs of choice' conclusion is not supported by this design, even though the authors call for placebo-controlled trials. Safety results are missing and the sponsor's role is not described.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome designated; pre-post change in MoCA, FAB, MFI-20 and HADS scores in each arm

issues.title: Non-randomised, uncontrolled pre-post study with groups selected on baseline score; drug effect cannot be isolated
issues.explanation: Each group received one drug and was chosen by a baseline score on an outcome that was later re-measured. With no control group, the improvements cannot be attributed to the drugs rather than to natural recovery, regression to the mean from selecting extreme scores, or practice effects. There is no between-group analysis. The Cholytilin group was selected for low MoCA, so a rise from 23.50 to 26.36 is partly expected without treatment. The conclusion that the drugs 'may be the drugs of choice' goes beyond what this design can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated or placebo control group with the same selection criteria, showing the same pre-post change is not seen without the drug.

quotes.text: Пациентам с КН (общий балл по МоСА ≤25; n=50) назначался холина альфосцерат
Пациентам с преобладанием ТДР (оценка тревоги/депрессии по HADS ≥8 баллов; n=50) назначался МексиВ 6
препаратами выбора для терапии которых могут быть МексиВ 6 и Холитилин.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is non-randomised, uncontrolled and pre-post, and the groups were formed on baseline scores (HADS ≥8 or MoCA ≤25). Baseline differences between groups are large (e.g. MoCA 26.60 vs 23.50), so selection on extreme baseline values, regression to the mean, natural recovery over time, practice effects on repeat testing and unblinded assessment cannot be separated from any drug effect. The authors admit that randomised, placebo-controlled studies are needed, but the Russian Conclusion still calls the two drugs 'drugs of choice', which the design cannot support.

issues.title: Many outcomes tested without correction; MexiB 6 cognitive gains rest on p<0.05 with changes under 0.7 points
issues.explanation: Several scales and subscales were tested pre-post in each arm, with a plain p<0.05 threshold and no stated adjustment. The Cholytilin results at p<0.001 would probably survive correction. The MexiB 6 cognitive claims (MoCA, FAB) rest on p<0.05 and small changes (0.68 and 0.22 points), so they are fragile. The paper also does not name the statistical test used.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or an adjusted analysis in which the MexiB 6 MoCA and FAB changes remain significant.

quotes.text: Статистически значимо уменьшилась когнитивная дисфункция по тестам МоСА (с 26,60±1,31 до 27,28±1,39 балла; p<0,05)
Статистически значимые различия определялись при 0,95 уровне вероятности безошибочного суждения, или p<0,05.

issues.title: Safety is a stated aim and adverse events were assessed at two visits, but no adverse-event results are given
issues.explanation: The objective is to evaluate efficacy and safety, and the design says adverse events were assessed at the 2-week and 2-month visits. No adverse-event counts, discontinuations or tolerability statement appear in the results or conclusion. Readers get only the benefit side of the drugs.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table or statement of adverse events and dropouts for each arm.

quotes.text: Во время второго визита через 2 нед от начала терапии - оценивали наличие нежелательных явлений.
оценить эффективность и безопасность терапии астенических нарушений

issues.title: Manufacturer-sponsored article with no description of the sponsor's role in design, analysis or writing
issues.explanation: The article states that it was sponsored by a company and that the conflict of interest did not affect results. It does not say what the sponsor did, and it gives no author-level disclosures. The paper evaluates a combination product, and the sponsor's role in design and analysis cannot be checked. This reduces confidence in an uncontrolled efficacy claim but is not itself an error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in design, data collection, analysis or writing.

quotes.text: Статья спонсируется компанией ЗАО «Канонфарма продакшн».
Конфликт интересов не повлиял на результаты исследования.

issues.title: No trial registration or pre-specified primary outcome reported for a prospective treatment study
issues.explanation: The study is prospective with treatment assigned at baseline and re-assessment at 2 months, yet no registry entry is given. No primary outcome or sample-size reasoning is stated, so selective reporting of favourable scales cannot be excluded. This weakens a secondary point and does not by itself invalidate the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol dated before enrolment naming the same outcomes.

quotes.text: Дизайн исследования предусматривал три визита пациентов.

issues.title: Informed consent reported but no ethics committee approval statement
issues.explanation: The paper states that all patients signed informed consent but names no ethics committee or approval date. For a prospective interventional study this is a reporting omission. It does not bear on the efficacy numbers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ethics committee approval number and date for the study.

quotes.text: Все пациенты до включения в исследование подписали информированное согласие.

10.14739/2310-1210.2021.3.229981.headline_claim: Adding thiotriazoline tablets (200 mg twice daily for 30 days) to basic therapy in post-COVID syndrome significantly increases antiaggregant, anticoagulant and endothelioprotective effects and helps prevent thrombus formation.
10.14739/2310-1210.2021.3.229981.overall: The laboratory differences (eNOS, INR, platelet aggregation, D-dimer) may be real, but they come from a non-randomized, apparently open-label 15 vs 15 comparison with no baseline data by arm and no exact statistics. Several reported figures disagree with the tables (95.3% rate fall, 'disappeared' symptoms, minor text-table slips), and the infarction and stroke claim is not supported by any clinical outcome. The headline efficacy conclusion should be read as tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; the abstract reports coagulation/endothelial biomarkers (MNO, eNOS, D-dimer, platelet aggregation) and clinical symptoms/saturation

issues.title: Conclusion claims reduced infarction and stroke risk from D-dimer and INR changes in 30 patients over 30 days
issues.explanation: Conclusion 3 states thiotriazolin can reduce the risk of infarction and stroke. The study measured laboratory surrogates in 30 patients for 30 days and reports no clinical events. The claim also depends on a non-randomized comparison. This goes beyond what the data can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Event data showing fewer infarctions or strokes, or wording limited to biomarker changes.

quotes.text: а также о его способности снижать риски инфарктов и инсультов при постковидном синдроме

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion that thiotriazoline reduces infarction and stroke risk rests on surrogate markers (D-dimer, INR) in 30 patients over 30 days, with no clinical events measured. It extrapolates beyond the data, and the markers themselves are non-randomized between-arm differences. The D-dimer percentages themselves are arithmetically consistent with the printed table.

issues.title: Non-randomized 15 vs 15 comparison with no group-wise baseline data, yet causal efficacy conclusions
issues.explanation: Patients are described as simply receiving basic therapy or basic therapy plus thiotriazolin, with no randomization, concealment or allocation rule. Baseline values are given only for the pooled 30 patients, so balance between arms in severity, comorbidity or lab values cannot be checked, and no adjustment is made. The conclusions nonetheless attribute the differences to the drug.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random or concealed allocation, or a baseline table by arm showing balance.

quotes.text: а 15 пациентов на фоне базисной терапии дополнительно получали тиотриазолин

second_reader.what_stands: The two arms of 15 are not described as randomized, no allocation procedure is given, and baseline values are reported only for the pooled 30 patients, not by arm. Yet the conclusions state causal efficacy ('приводило к достоверному...') with no limitation noted, so the arms' baseline comparability cannot be judged.

issues.title: 30 patients (15 per arm), no sample-size rationale, confident efficacy conclusions
issues.explanation: With 15 per arm and no power calculation, group differences are imprecise, and the paper reports no test statistics or exact p values, only asterisks. The conclusions are worded as established efficacy rather than preliminary findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size justification or tentative wording of the conclusions.

quotes.text: В исследованиях приняли участие 30 больных в возрасте от 30 до 60 лет с постковидным синдромом
приводит к достоверному усилению базисной эндотелиопротективной, антиагрегантной и антикоагулянтной терапии

issues.title: About 8 laboratory endpoints and 10 symptoms tested at p < 0.05 with no correction
issues.explanation: The Methods state a single threshold of p < 0.05 for all analyses, with no correction or primary endpoint. Conclusions highlight the endpoints that reached significance. Exact p values are not reported, so the impact cannot be assessed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary endpoint or adjusted p values.

quotes.text: Для всех видов анализа статистически значимыми считали отличия р < 0,05 (95 %).

issues.title: Results text disagrees with tables: aggregation 99.4 vs 99.2, platelets 380.0 vs 377.0, saturation 97-98 vs 98-99%
issues.explanation: Several values quoted in the Results and Conclusions differ from the tables they cite. Basic-therapy platelet aggregation is 99.4% in text and 99.2% in Table 3, and platelet count is 380.0 ± 54.8 in text but 377.0 ± 52.4 in Table 3. The saturation level is 97-98% in the abstract and Results, but 98-99% in Table 1 and Conclusions, and symptom percentages in the text (32%, 35%, 42%, 12%) do not match Table 1 counts over n = 30 (30%, 33%, 43%, 10%). Also 14/15 = 93.3%, printed 93.4%. Each is small, but together they show the text was not checked against the tables. None changes a main claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data or an erratum showing the text values come from a different time point or analysis set that the paper labels.

quotes.text: Процент светопоглощения составлял в среднем 99,4 % против 60,0 %

quotes.location: Table 3, basic therapy row, platelet count

issues.title: 30-second aggregation rate 'fell 95.3%' but Table 3 means imply a 49.6% fall (157.3 to 79.3)
issues.explanation: The Results state thiotriazolin lowered the 30-second aggregation rate by 95.3%. Table 3 gives 157.3 in the basic group and 79.3 in the thiotriazolin group, a difference of about 50%. The 95.3% figure is not supported by the table and overstates the effect on this endpoint.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated base or calculation for 95.3% that reproduces from the paper's data.

quotes.text: скорости агрегации на 30 секунде - 95,3 %

issues.title: Palpitations, weakness and fatigue 'disappeared' with thiotriazolin, but Table 1 shows 2, 2 and 1 patients
issues.explanation: The text says complaints of palpitations, weakness and fatigue disappeared in the thiotriazolin group. Table 1 shows 2 of 15 still had weakness, 2 palpitations and 1 fatigue after treatment. The real result is a large reduction, not elimination, so the clinical benefit is overstated, though the direction of effect remains.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Table 1 correction setting these cells to zero, or text saying 'markedly reduced'.

quotes.text: исчезли жалобы на сердцебиение
исчезли слабость и повышенная утомляемость
Повышенная утомляемость

issues.title: Open-label design; symptom improvement (weakness, fatigue, palpitations) is subjective and unblinded
issues.explanation: No blinding is described, so patient-reported symptom improvement may be influenced by knowing the treatment. The laboratory endpoints are less affected. This weakens the clinical-improvement claim more than the biochemical claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that patients and assessors were blinded, or that symptoms were scored objectively.

quotes.text: исчезли слабость и повышенная утомляемость

issues.title: D-dimer fall of 29.5% described as a 'significant increase' in Results and Conclusion 3
issues.explanation: Conclusion 3 says thiotriazolin lowered D-dimer, then calls the same 29.5% change a 'significant increase'. Table 2 shows a fall, so the percentages are right but the direction word is wrong. A reader could take the sentence to mean D-dimer rose, so this is a reporting error that leaves the finding itself intact.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the table shows a decrease.

quotes.text: Тиотриазолин достоверно снижал в крови больных уровень D-димера
достоверное повышение относительно показателей при поступлении и до начала лечения на 29,5 %

10.14739/2310-1210.2021.6.233891.headline_claim: Combined intravenous ozone therapy (alternating ozonized saline and autohemotherapy) added to standard medication is effective and cost-effective for rehabilitation after SARS-CoV-2-associated polysegmental pneumonia (long COVID).
10.14739/2310-1210.2021.6.233891.overall: The headline claim that ozone therapy is effective and cost-effective is only weakly supported. Allocation was by patient choice, the comparison was unblinded with subjective outcomes, there was no economic analysis, and the central endpoint counts (18/21 vs 9/21) conflict with the paper's own 6-minute-walk means. The objective biomarker differences may point in a favourable direction, but they cannot be taken as reliable evidence of benefit.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly named; composite endpoints (absence of dyspnea, normalization of biochemical markers and SpO2, restored exercise tolerance on 6MWT) and 6-minute walk distance

issues.title: Groups formed by patient free choice; open-label, no sham, subjective outcomes
issues.explanation: Patients chose their own group, so allocation was not random and the groups may differ in prognosis or motivation. No baseline comparison is shown to support the claim of comparability. The control group received no sham or placebo infusion, and nothing indicates blinded assessment of the Borg and PCFS scores. Differences in these outcomes could therefore reflect selection, expectation or attention effects as well as ozone. The efficacy conclusion is stated without this caveat.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol showing concealed random allocation with blinded outcome assessors, or a full baseline table showing balance.

quotes.text: Методом вільного вибору пацієнтів поділили на 2 рівні групи (основну та контрольну)
Суб'єктивне оцінювання стану здоров'я здійснили за результатами анкети самозвіту пацієнта за PCFS

second_reader.what_stands: Patients chose their group rather than being randomised, the control group received no sham infusion, and no blinding is described. The key outcomes (PCFS, Borg dyspnoea and the 6MWT, which depends on effort) are partly subjective or effort-dependent, so they are open to selection and expectation bias. The paper does not say explicitly that the study was open-label; that is inferred.

issues.title: Endpoint counts (18/21 and 9/21) conflict with 6MWT means, 52 %/10 % recovery and other component rates
issues.explanation: The endpoint requires absence of dyspnoea, normalised biochemistry and SpO2, and a 6-minute walk over 550 m. The main group's mean 6MWT is 520 ± 30 m, so very few patients can have exceeded 550 m, and the authors say full recovery did not occur. The control mean is 405 ± 45 m, so 9 of 21 controls above 550 m is implausible. The Conclusions give 52 % and 10 % for full tolerance recovery, and the text gives 85 % for SpO2 normalisation and 16 of 21 for coagulation recovery. The headline 'twice as many reached the endpoints' is therefore not supported by the reported component data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level 6MWT distances and a definition of the endpoint count showing that 18 and 9 patients actually met every component, including >550 m.

quotes.text: Кінцевих точок дослідження досягли 18 осіб основної групи та 9 пацієнтів групи контролю
була довшою (520 ± 30 м)
Аналогічний результат зафіксували тільки в 10 % випадків групи контролю

second_reader.what_stands: The endpoint counts (18/21 and 9/21) cannot be reconciled with the printed 6MWT means (520 ± 30 m and 405 ± 45 m, both below the 550 m criterion), with the 52% and 10% walking results, or with the 25% SpO2 normalisation and 'isolated' CRP normalisation in controls. The paper does not explain how the composite was counted, and the stated endpoint definition cannot yield these counts. One caveat is that the 52%/10% figures may be a different, looser measure than >550 m, but the means and the control components still conflict with 9/21.

issues.title: 'Cost-effective' and 'effective' claimed with no cost data and a small, non-random, open comparison
issues.explanation: The abstract's conclusion calls the treatment effective and cost-effective. The paper reports no costs, no cost comparison and no economic analysis. The Discussion's economic justification rests on 'low cost' and 'faster improvement' only. Efficacy is stated confidently from 21 vs 21 patients in a non-randomised, unblinded comparison with no sample-size justification. The limitation of small sample is mentioned only in the Discussion and does not temper the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported cost analysis (costs per patient and per outcome in both arms) and a pre-specified sample-size justification.

quotes.text: є патогенетично обґрунтованим, ефективним, економічно вигідним доповненням
Ця програма відновлення організму після COVID-19 є економічно обґрунтованою внаслідок швидшого покращення толерантності до фізичного навантаження та низької собівартості.

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract's 'cost-effective' and 'economically advantageous' and the Discussion's 'economically justified' have no cost data behind them. 'Effective' rests on a small, non-randomised, unblinded comparison whose limitation section mentions only sample size, not the allocation method or the lack of blinding.

issues.title: Only unpaired t-tests described; within-group and proportion p-values have no stated method
issues.explanation: The Methods describe only Student's t-test for unpaired measurements. Between-group comparisons at one time point fit that test. Within-group before/after claims (p < 0,05) and comparisons of percentages (e.g. 95 % vs 24 %, p < 0,01) have no stated or appropriate method. Many outcomes and time points are tested with no multiplicity control, and no between-group test of change from baseline is shown for CRP.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statistics description naming paired tests and chi-square/Fisher tests for the relevant comparisons, with adjustment for multiple outcomes.

quotes.text: хоча ступінь виразності симптомів був меншим, ніж до лікування (p < 0,05)

issues.title: Control SpO2 after exertion at day 20: SD 1,4 in Results text vs 0,4 in Table 1
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the control group's SpO2 after exertion at day 20 as 93,0 ± 1,4 %. Table 1 prints 93,0 ± 0,4 for the same cell. One of the two is wrong. The gap (96,0 vs 93,0) is large relative to either SD, so the conclusion on this outcome is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An erratum or the raw data showing which SD (1,4 or 0,4) is correct would settle which place is wrong.

quotes.text: 96,0 ± 0,8 % в основній групі проти 93,0 ± 1,4 % у контрольній

quotes.location: Table 1, control group, SpO2 row, day 20

10.14739/mmt.2026.2.342420.headline_claim: Adding exogenous L-arginine and phenibut to basic therapy in patients with coronary artery disease and Long COVID contributes to reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms, improved cognitive function, and stabilised autonomic regulation, indicating a positive neuromodulatory effect.
10.14739/mmt.2026.2.342420.overall: The directional improvements in group II are plausible, but because allocation followed prescribed treatment and only within-group tests were run, the paper does not show that the added L-arginine and phenibut caused the improvements. The conclusions are overstated for a small, uncorrected, non-randomised comparison; the cognitive percentage inconsistency is minor and slightly understates the gains.

primary_outcome.name: Neurovegetative disorders: HADS anxiety/depression, MoCA cognition and Holter HRV indices (no single primary outcome named)

issues.title: Allocation by prescribed treatment, no randomisation procedure or baseline comparison; causal effect still concluded
issues.explanation: Patients were divided according to the treatment they were prescribed, so group membership may reflect clinician choice and patient characteristics. No baseline table, sequence generation or concealment is reported, and neither group's baseline comparability can be judged. The conclusion that the combination 'indicates a positive neuromodulatory effect' is therefore a causal claim the design cannot support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of a concealed random allocation sequence and a baseline table showing balanced groups.

quotes.text: A prospective study with parallel distribution and elements of randomization included 31 patients with CAD
Patients were divided into two groups depending on the prescribed treatment
which indicates a positive neuromodulatory effect of complex treatment

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation is described as depending on the prescribed treatment, with no randomisation method, concealment or baseline comparison table. Conclusion 1 and the abstract still attribute the changes to the treatment ('indicates a positive neuromodulatory effect'). Conclusion 2 is more cautious ('associated with'), and the paper has no limitations section.

issues.title: Superiority over basic therapy claimed without any between-group test; only within-group Wilcoxon tests
issues.explanation: Significance is established only by comparing each group with its own baseline, and the conclusions credit the added drugs for the differences. A significant change in one group and a non-significant one in the other does not show the groups differ. Group I also improved significantly on several HRV measures, so the contrast is not clear-cut.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group comparison of change scores (e.g. Mann-Whitney or ANCOVA) showing a significant treatment difference.

quotes.text: To assess the reliability of changes in dynamics
Three months after combined therapy using exogenous L-arginine and phenibut, a more pronounced decrease in anxiety and depressive symptoms was observed

second_reader.what_stands: The only inferential tests described are within-group Wilcoxon tests (plus chi-square for categorical data), yet the text claims a 'more pronounced' decrease in group II than in group I, and the abstract and conclusions credit the added drugs. The group difference is shown only as differing percentage changes, with no between-group test or test of change scores reported.

issues.title: No primary outcome or multiplicity control across HADS, MoCA domains and many day/night HRV indices
issues.explanation: Dozens of within-group tests are run (two HADS subscales, MoCA total and domains, and temporal and spectral HRV indices for two periods) at an uncorrected 0.05. Some results are mixed, e.g. HF fell in the active period while described as restoring balance. The positive summary relies on the nominally significant subset.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome with multiplicity adjustment, or adjusted p-values that stay significant.

quotes.text: A p-value of less than 0.05 was regarded as indicative of statistical significance.

issues.title: 31 patients (15 vs 16), no sample-size rationale, no limitations section, confident efficacy conclusions
issues.explanation: The study is small with no power calculation, and the conclusions use firm language ('significant', 'normalization'). The paper has no limitations discussion. This weakens the strength of the conclusions rather than invalidating the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation or explicit labelling of the work as exploratory.

quotes.text: included 31 patients with CAD

issues.title: MoCA % increases use follow-up as denominator (9.47, 27.44, 32.01%); HADS uses baseline; true rises 10.5, 37.8, 47.1%
issues.explanation: The paper reports MoCA total, Speech and Memory gains as percentages that only reconcile if divided by the final score, whereas the HADS reductions in the same paragraph are divided by the baseline. Relative to baseline, the increases are about 10.5%, 37.8% and 47.1%, so the cognitive gains are understated and are not comparable with the HADS percentages. The raw means are printed, so the direction of effect is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that cognitive percentage changes are deliberately expressed relative to the follow-up value.

quotes.text: by 9.47 % (from 24.09 to 26.61 points)
increased by 27.44 % (from 1.93 to 2.66; p < 0.05)
'Anxiety' subscale by 35.97 % (from 15.93 to 10.20)

issues.title: No clinical trial registry entry; only an institutional research-topic registration number
issues.explanation: The prospective intervention study cites no registry identifier, so prespecified outcomes cannot be checked against a prior record. The cited number is a state registration of the department's research topic.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry identifier with prespecified outcomes.

quotes.text: state registration No. 0118U007138 (2018-2023)

10.14744/ejp.2024.1204.headline_claim: taVNS increased cardiac vagal control (RMSSD) during post-exercise recovery in young adults with post-COVID syndrome, but did not significantly affect blood lactate or blood pressure.
10.14744/ejp.2024.1204.overall: The headline claim that taVNS enhanced cardiac vagal control rests on a within-group significant versus non-significant contrast rather than a between-group test, so it is not adequately supported. The small, retrospectively sized single-session study with a non-verifiable registration number supports at most tentative, hypothesis-generating conclusions. The other issues are minor.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; RMSSD, PNS, SNS, HR, lactate and blood pressure are reported as outcomes

issues.title: taVNS efficacy claimed from RMSSD significant in Group 1 but not Group 2, no between-group test
issues.explanation: The main efficacy claim rests on RMSSD rising significantly within the taVNS group while the rise in the placebo group was not significant. A difference in significance is not evidence of a difference between groups, and no between-group test of the 2nd-to-3rd measurement change is reported. The Abstract and Discussion conclusions that taVNS increased cardiac vagal control are therefore not supported by the analysis shown. The paper's own results also say both groups showed similar changes in several other measures.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported group-by-time interaction or between-group comparison of the RMSSD change from observation 2 to 3 that is significant.

quotes.text: while the RMSSD index showed a statistically significant increase in Group 1, the increase in Group 2 was not significant

The findings of the study demonstrate the efficacy of vagus nerve stimulation in boosting cardiac vagal activity, as evidenced  by  the  significant  rise  in  RMSSD  values  in Group 1 compared to the placebo group.

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy claim for taVNS on RMSSD rests on a significant within-group paired test in Group 1 versus a non-significant one in Group 2. The paper reports no between-group or group-by-time test of the RMSSD change, so 'significant rise in Group 1 compared to the placebo group' is not supported by a direct comparison. The limitations paragraph does not mention this gap. The caveat is that the garbled Table 2 means the exact p-value-to-group assignment is inferred, not certain.

issues.title: Sample size set retrospectively on optimistic repeated-measures assumptions (f=0.5, r=0.8); 22 per arm
issues.explanation: The sample size was determined retrospectively, assuming a large effect (f=0.5) and a within-subject correlation of 0.8 across three measures. These assumptions favour small numbers and do not address power for between-group differences in the secondary outcomes. Between-group null findings (lactate, blood pressure) and the group differences claimed are thus weakly informed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective power calculation targeting the between-group difference in RMSSD change.

quotes.text: The  sample  size  was  determined  retrospectively  using G*Power V.3.1.7 software
leaving 44 patients who completed the study, with 22 in each group.

issues.title: Six of 50 participants excluded without arm allocation, reasons or ITT analysis (12%)
issues.explanation: Fifty patients were included and 44 completed, with the six non-completers described only as unable to participate 'for various reasons'. The paper gives no arm allocation for them and no sensitivity or ITT analysis, and no CONSORT flow in the text. With 12% loss in a single-session study the bias is probably modest, but the analysis is of completers only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing the six were lost before randomization or balanced across arms, or an ITT sensitivity analysis.

quotes.text: A total of 50 patients were initially included in our study. However, six were unable to participate for various reasons, leaving 44 patients who completed the study

issues.title: Exercise session called 30 min, but 5+15+15 listed phases total 35 min
issues.explanation: The paper says each session lasted 30 minutes, yet the session description lists a 5-minute warm-up plus 15 minutes of fast walking and 15 of jogging. That is 35 minutes unless the warm-up is not counted. It is a minor description inconsistency that slightly affects reproducibility but not the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 30 minutes excludes the warm-up.

quotes.text: Each session lasted 30 minutes
The exercise session included a 5-minute warm-up phase on the treadmill, 15 minutes of fast walking, and 15 minutes of jogging.

issues.title: Trial registration ID 'NCT 0x764x70' is not a valid identifier; registration date not reported
issues.explanation: The registration number as printed contains letters and cannot be looked up, and no registration date is given. Prospective registration and pre-specification of outcomes therefore cannot be verified from the paper. It may be a typesetting error, so the weight is modest.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A valid registry record dated before enrolment with matching outcomes.

quotes.text: the study protocol was registered under the Clinical Trials Number NCT 0x764x70

10.14814/phy2.15636.headline_claim: Self-administered 4-week electrical stimulation is a safe and effective option for improving lower-extremity muscle perfusion and gastrocnemius endurance in people with musculoskeletal post-COVID-19 sequelae.
10.14814/phy2.15636.overall: The headline claim that E-Stim is safe and effective is not well supported. The study has 18 participants analysed as 36 independent legs, borderline interaction p-values, surrogate foot-based perfusion measures, baseline imbalance, no multiplicity control, and retrospective registration with a registered primary outcome unreported. The findings are hypothesis-generating at best.

primary_outcome.name: Muscle perfusion (OxyHb at t70) and gastrocnemius muscle endurance (GNMe), as the paper's main hypothesis

primary_outcomes.measure: Gastrocnemius Muscle Endurance (Muscle Sustained Contraction) in Response to Electrical Stimulation

issues.title: 36 legs from 18 people treated as independent samples in the analyses
issues.explanation: Each participant contributed both legs, and the two legs of one person are correlated. The authors state each leg was treated as an independent sample, with n = 20 and 16 legs. This inflates the effective sample size and understates p-values, which matters most for the borderline results (p = 0.022, 0.048, 0.031). The Pearson correlation in the IG also appears to use leg-level points.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A GEE specification that clusters on participant, with results unchanged.

quotes.text: Each LE was considered as an independent sample due to the variability in muscular and vascular status
including n = 20 LE in the IG and n = 16 LE in CG

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states that each of the 36 legs was treated as an independent sample although they come from 18 randomised participants who received the same allocation to both legs. GEE is named, but no clustering by participant or correlation structure is reported, so the effective sample size and the p-values may be overstated.

issues.title: 'Safe and effective' conclusion from 18 participants, surrogate outcomes, borderline between-group results
issues.explanation: The discussion concludes E-Stim is a safe and effective therapy. The evidence is 18 people, surrogate measures (plantar foot NIRS, sEMG), no functional outcomes, and between-group differences with p of 0.022 to 0.055 on leg-level analyses. The abstract-level claim of significant increases in both perfusion and endurance is stronger than the data allow, and no powered safety analysis exists.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A larger, adequately powered trial with clustered analysis and functional outcomes confirming the effect.

quotes.text: is a safe and effective therapeutic option for individuals with LE musculoskeletal PASC seeking to improve muscle recovery
is a practical and promising intervention for individuals with musculoskeletal PASC LE symptoms

second_reader.what_stands: 'Safe and effective' and 'practical and promising' are stated more strongly than 18 participants, surrogate NIRS/sEMG outcomes, no functional endpoint, leg-level analysis, and between-group p-values of 0.022 to 0.055 can support. The authors do list several limitations and use 'may' and 'potential' in places, so the overreach is in the headline wording rather than in an absence of caveats.

issues.title: Registered primary 'Ankle Strength' not reported; paper adds unregistered NIRS perfusion outcome
issues.explanation: The registry lists gastrocnemius endurance and ankle strength as primary outcomes. The paper reports no ankle strength data and states that functional outcomes were not assessed. The paper's headline perfusion outcome (plantar OxyHb by NIRS) does not appear among the registered primary outcomes, so the reported outcome set differs from the registered one without explanation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version, or a protocol, showing ankle strength was removed and perfusion added before data collection, with the change disclosed.

quotes.text: Our main hypothesis is that E-Stim therapy will improve both HR2S and LE muscle endurance in this population.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not report any ankle strength outcome and does not name a primary outcome, so the omission itself is visible. Whether ankle strength was the registered primary outcome and whether NIRS perfusion was unregistered depends on the ClinicalTrials.gov record, which is not in the paper and cannot be checked here.

issues.title: 'Only the IG regained endurance' rests on within-group significance; normalised interaction p = 0.055
issues.explanation: The discussion infers that only the intervention group regained endurance because the IG change was significant (p = 0.031) and the CG change was not (p = 0.522). That is a difference between significance and non-significance. The between-group interaction is borderline (p = 0.048 absolute, p = 0.055 normalised), and the between-group Intv2 difference was also only a trend (p = 0.055).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant-clustered between-group test with a robust significant interaction and a CI for the difference.

quotes.text: This suggests that only the intervention group regained muscle endurance as a response to E-Stim therapy.
There was a trend for a group × time × effect interaction

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that only the IG regained endurance rests mainly on one group reaching p < 0.05 within-group and the other not; the formal interaction is p = 0.048 for absolute values but p = 0.055 for normalised values, so it is borderline rather than clearly different between groups. It is not true that the claim rests on within-group significance alone, since the absolute interaction was just under 0.05, but the evidence for 'only' is weak.

issues.title: Registered 2022-01-18, after study start (registry 2021-08-18) and after recruitment began Nov 2021
issues.explanation: The registry record was first submitted on 2022-01-18. The registry start date is 2021-08-18 and the paper says recruitment began in November 2021. The paper does not disclose that registration was retrospective, so the outcomes could not be verified as prespecified. This also covers candidate c9.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the protocol and outcomes were fixed and time-stamped before enrolment.

quotes.text: Participants were recruited from the Baylor College of Medicine (BCM) Post-COVID-19 Care Clinic (Houston, TX, USA) between November 2021 and May 2022.

issues.title: Analysed 18 participants (36 legs) versus 32 'samples' planned; power basis unclear
issues.explanation: The calculation called for 32 samples (28 plus 10% dropout) at d = 0.5, but the analysed sample is 18 participants. Because the calculation counts samples while legs are analysed, it is unclear whether the target was met in legs (36) or missed in people (18). The limitations section says the sample may not confirm all observations, yet the conclusion states efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confirmation that the calculation was meant at leg level, with a clustered analysis adequately powered.

quotes.text: a total of 32 samples were required to detect significance
This led to a total of 18 participants

issues.title: Multiple timepoints and absolute/normalised outcomes tested at p ≤ 0.05 without correction
issues.explanation: Perfusion and endurance were each tested at several timepoints, in absolute and normalised form, at baseline and 4 weeks, with no multiplicity control. The key interaction p-values of 0.022 and 0.048 would not survive any simple correction. The two primary hypotheses were stated up front, which limits but does not remove the concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified analysis plan naming a single primary test and timepoint.

quotes.text: the statistical significance level was set at p ≤ 0.05

issues.title: Baseline imbalance in BMI (30.3 vs 37.0), pneumonia (4 vs 0), home oxygen (6 vs 1) in 10 vs 8 people
issues.explanation: The arms differ at baseline on BMI, cognition, pneumonia and home oxygen use. Table 1 also shows hospitalisation of 28 vs 8 days, and the authors state the IG was more ill. The imbalance runs in different directions, so its net effect on the results is unknown, and the adjusted results were not reported in the paper. With 18 people no adjustment can fully handle it, and allocation concealment is not described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The supplementary adjusted analyses showing the same estimates with unchanged intervals.

quotes.text: suggesting that the IG was more ill than the CG
Additionally, the IG had lower BMI ( p = 0.016) and poorer cognitive function ( p = 0.014)

10.14814/phy2.15931.headline_claim: A personalized 3-month pulmonary rehabilitation program improved exercise capacity, quality of life, functional status and airway volume in non-hospitalized patients with PASC, and the authors frame this as a positive effect of rehabilitation.
10.14814/phy2.15931.overall: The study shows that 17 patients who completed rehabilitation had improved questionnaire, exercise and some CT measures, but with no control group the improvement cannot be attributed to the programme, and about 30 uncorrected tests add to uncertainty. The take-home message additionally claims a decline in air trapping that the authors' own data contradict (p = 0.925). The numeric slips (FEV1 96 vs 93, duplicated 49% vs 37%) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly named in the paper; the stated primary aim is the impact of pulmonary rehabilitation on physical fitness and quality of life

issues.title: Uncontrolled pre-post design with no control group; efficacy claims rest on within-patient change
issues.explanation: All results are before-after changes in 17 patients with no comparison group, so improvement cannot be separated from natural recovery, regression to the mean, or repeat-testing effects. The authors acknowledge that baseline follows a period without therapy and includes natural recovering. Yet the take-home message says rehabilitation had a significant impact on quality of life and fitness, which the design cannot show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group analysed against the same endpoints.

quotes.text: Therefore, no control group was included in  this  study.
Rehabilitation  had  a  significant impact on quality of life and cardiorespiratory fitness of patients with PASC.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is an uncontrolled, retrospective single-arm pre-post study of completers (17 of 23), and its efficacy claims rest only on within-patient change. The authors acknowledge the lack of a control group and natural recovery as limitations, but the take-home message still states a significant impact of rehabilitation without this qualification.

issues.title: Take-home message claims decline in air trapping; Results report no significant change (p = 0.925)
issues.explanation: The headline message states that airway reopening resulted in a decline in air trapping. The Results state no significant difference in air trapping before and after rehabilitation, and Table 5 shows a small non-significant fall. The take-home message therefore claims an effect the study's own data do not support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant air trapping change in an analysis not shown, or a take-home message that is explicitly hypothetical.

quotes.text: resulting in decline in air trapping
There was no significant difference in air trapping before and after rehabilitation

second_reader.what_stands: The take-home message says rehabilitation resulted in a decline in air trapping, but the paper's own pre/post test shows no significant change (18.6 to 16.4, p = 0.925, N = 14). The Discussion's idea that air trapping 'could be resolved by reopening of the airways' is a hypothesis, not a result supported by this outcome.

issues.title: Completers-only analysis: 6 of 23 enrolled (26%) excluded for non-completion
issues.explanation: Patients who did not complete rehabilitation were excluded by design, so results describe those who finished, not all who started. Dropout reasons were mixed (injury, surgery, feeling better, unexplained), so the direction of bias is unclear. The paper discloses the numbers but does not provide an intention-to-treat analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An analysis including baseline data of all 23 patients showing similar results.

quotes.text: subjects who did not complete the pulmonary rehabilitation program until the end were excluded from the study.
Six of the subjects did not complete the program, 1 patient had a surgery on the foot

issues.title: About 30 outcomes tested at p < 0.05 without correction; CT findings rest on p = 0.013 to 0.020
issues.explanation: Across Tables 2-5 about 30 pre-post comparisons were run at an unadjusted 0.05 cutoff. A few would be expected to cross it by chance, and the CT results emphasised in the take-home message (airway volume p = 0.013, BV5 p = 0.020) are in that range. A Bonferroni threshold of about 0.0017 would leave mainly the strongest exercise and PCFS results significant.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or multiplicity adjustment in a protocol.

quotes.text: All  analyses  were  evaluated  using  a  significance  cutoff  of p < 0.05.
Total airway volume

issues.title: No sample size calculation; 17 analysed patients, with some outcomes at n = 12 to 14
issues.explanation: No power calculation is reported and sample size was determined by who was treated. Several outcomes have fewer patients than 17 (HADS anxiety n = 12, air trapping n = 14), widening uncertainty. Non-significant results such as TLC (p = 0.054) cannot be read as absence of effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample size justification.

quotes.text: A  discrete  sample  size  will  be  included  since  all  patients were extensively evaluated using classical outcome measures

issues.title: Discussion gives baseline FEV1 % predicted as 96%; Table 3 reports 93%
issues.explanation: The Discussion compares the study's baseline FEV1 % predicted (96%) with two earlier studies (82% and 86%). Table 3 gives the baseline FEV1 as 93%, and 96% is the FVC and TLC baseline value. The error is small and does not change the point that baseline lung function was near normal.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different FEV1 baseline value in the source data, or a statement that 96% refers to another measure.

quotes.text: The mean FEV1% predicted of the population at baseline was lower in these studies than in the population studied in this paper (82% and 86% vs 96%)
quotes.location: Discussion, paragraph on pulmonary function tests

issues.title: Same 49% vs 37% attributed to hospitalized vs nonhospitalized and to female vs male
issues.explanation: The Background gives 49% vs 37% as the PASC prevalence in hospitalized vs nonhospitalized patients. The Discussion gives the identical figures for females vs males, citing the same paper. One of the two attributions is wrong. This is a background citation issue and does not affect the study's own results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The cited meta-analysis reporting 49% vs 37% for both contrasts.

quotes.text: nonhospitalized  patients  (49%  vs  37%)
females have a higher prevalence of PASC than males (49% vs 37%)

10.15212/amm-2024-0089.headline_claim: Cs4 significantly reduced long COVID symptom severity compared with a waitlist control and is a safe option for persistent long COVID symptoms.
10.15212/amm-2024-0089.overall: The trial supports a self-reported improvement in the Cs4 arm relative to an open waitlist, but the size and attribution of the effect are uncertain given the lack of masking, retrospective registration and an unclear primary scale. Secondary-outcome claims and the safety and 'strong evidence' wording go beyond the data. Several small numeric slips (power, n = 60, sign errors) do not alter the main estimate.

primary_outcome.name: Change in C19-YRSm symptom severity from baseline to 12 weeks

primary_outcomes.measure: the change in symptom severity from 0 to 12 weeks measured by the modified COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRSm)
primary_outcomes.time_frame: will be assessed at baseline and 12 weeks.

issues.title: Open waitlist control with self-reported outcomes; effect of -8.7 cannot be separated from expectation
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation, and the control group received no inactive product. The primary outcome and all secondary outcomes are self-reported symptom scales, which are sensitive to expectation. The authors acknowledge performance and reporting bias, yet the highlights state that Cs4 'significantly reduced long COVID symptoms'. The trial can show an improvement relative to doing nothing, not a specific pharmacological effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An objective, blinded-assessed primary outcome showing a similar effect.

quotes.text: performance bias was possible because the participants were not blinded across groups
Cordyceps sinensis mycelium culture extract (Cs4) significantly reduced long COVID symptoms.

second_reader.what_stands: The control was open-label waitlist and the primary and secondary outcomes were all patient-reported, so the -8.7 difference at week 12 cannot be separated from expectation or reporting effects. The authors do name performance and reporting bias as limitations, but the Highlights, brief and conclusion still present the effect as a causal reduction in symptoms without carrying that caveat through.

issues.title: Post-hoc power of the primary outcome is 0.98 in Results but 83% in Discussion
issues.explanation: The Results state a statistical power of 0.98 for the C19-YRSm primary comparison. The Discussion gives the estimated power as 83% and credits it as a strength. Both cannot describe the same calculation, and the paper does not say how either was derived. Post-hoc power adds little confidence in any case.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated explanation that the two figures refer to different outcomes or methods, with the calculation shown.

quotes.text: with a statistical power of 0.98
the estimated power was 83% compared to 80% in the sample size calculation

issues.title: 'Safe' claim rests on 55 treated, mild-event data with numerically more enzyme abnormalities on Cs4
issues.explanation: No severe events were reported, which is accurate. However, AST, ALT, urea and creatine kinase abnormalities were more frequent in the Cs4 arm, though none reached significance. With 55 per arm and no safety power, absence of significance is not evidence of equal risk. The wording 'safe' is firmer than the data support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified safety analysis with adequate precision showing no excess abnormalities.

quotes.text: Cs4 is a safe option as no severe adverse events were reported.
The adverse events at 24 weeks, which were all mild
Results suggest that Cs4 may safely alleviate persistent long COVID symptoms.

issues.title: 'Strong evidence' of efficacy and population representativeness claimed from one open single-centre trial
issues.explanation: The Discussion says combining this trial with an earlier study in healthy elderly people gives strong evidence for efficacy in post-COVID symptoms. The earlier study measured exercise capacity in healthy people and does not bear on long COVID. The paper also suggests the 110 participants represent a broader population of Hong Kong residents because baseline characteristics were balanced, although balance concerns arm comparability, not generalisability. Both statements go beyond what this design supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: n/a; the claims are judged against the design.

quotes.text: provides strong evidence for Cs4 efficacy in alleviating post-COVID symptoms
it is more likely that the 110 participants represented a broader population of Hong Kong residents

issues.title: Sample size assumed SD 1.195 and effect 0.8; observed baseline SD 12.3 and effect 8.7
issues.explanation: The power calculation used a standard deviation of 1.195 and a 0.8-point difference on a scale where the trial observed a baseline SD of 12.3 and a between-group difference of -8.7. The calculation is therefore not on the scale actually used, and it also conflicts with the 0-30 item description. Post-hoc power figures of 0.98 and 83% add to this confusion. The trial is still adequately sized for the observed effect, but the prespecified calculation does not describe it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pilot data showing a primary-outcome SD near 1.2 on the scale used in the trial.

quotes.text: by 0.8 points based on the results of our pilot study

issues.title: Primary scale range stated 0-78 but described as ten items scored 0-3 (maximum 30)
issues.explanation: The primary outcome scale is given a range of 0-78. The Methods list ten symptom items each scored 0-3, which allows at most 30. A baseline mean of 23.2 with SD 12.3 would be nearly the largest SD possible on a 0-30 range, so the scoring used for the primary outcome is unclear. This makes the size of the reported -8.7 change hard to interpret against the scale.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The scale manual or supplement showing the symptom severity subscale actually spans 0-78 with items scored on a different range.

quotes.text: C19-YRSm (symptom severity) scores (range, 0-78), mean (SD)
Each item was scored on a scale from 0-3 to indicate severity.

issues.title: Trial registered 25 Sep 2023, after enrolment began (Apr-Jun 2023); not disclosed as retrospective
issues.explanation: The registry shows first submission about five months after the stated start, and the paper reports screening in April-June 2023. The paper says only that the protocol was registered and does not say this was done after recruitment. Retrospective registration weakens the assurance that the primary outcome and analysis were fixed in advance, although the registered primary outcome currently matches the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry audit trail showing an earlier submission before 17 April 2023.

quotes.text: The protocol was registered at ClinicalTrial.gov (No. NCT06054438).
A total of 151 potential participants were screened for eligibility

issues.title: About ten secondary tests at P<0.05 uncorrected; named benefits rest on P of 0.009-0.025
issues.explanation: The paper tests BFI, ISI, two HADS, four SGRQ and two SF-12 outcomes at an unadjusted two-sided 0.05. The conclusion highlights fatigue, insomnia and respiratory symptoms as particular benefits, but the BFI (P = 0.011), SGRQ symptoms (0.009), activity (0.025) and total (0.018) would not pass a Bonferroni threshold. These secondary findings should be presented as hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchical testing plan, or labelling of these outcomes as exploratory.

quotes.text: improvements in fatigue (mean difference, -8.1), insomnia (-2.9), respiratory symptoms (-6.3), and quality of life
may be a beneficial treatment for multiple long COVID symptoms, especially fatigue, insomnia, and respiratory symptoms

issues.title: Manufacturer of Cs4 funds an author, but its role in trial conduct and analysis is not stated
issues.explanation: The corresponding author declares funding from the company whose subsidiary-type name matches the product manufacturer. The paper does not describe whether that company had any role in design, analysis or reporting. The conflict is disclosed, but the missing role statement limits the reader's ability to judge.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A funder-role statement saying the company had no role in design, analysis or reporting.

quotes.text: YF received funding support from the Chinese Pharmaceuticals
Cs4 was manufactured by Chinese Pharm (Hong Kong, China)

issues.title: Waitlist group labelled n = 60 in Table 2 but n = 55 in Table 1 and Results
issues.explanation: Table 2 labels the waitlist control group n = 60 for the change-from-baseline rows. Table 1 and the follow-up percentages give 55 per arm, and the trial randomised 110 in total. The group cannot have 60 participants, so either the label is wrong or the table used a different population that is not described. The effect estimates are probably unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original typeset table showing n = 55 in that header.

quotes.text: control (n = 60)
quotes.location: Table 2, mean change from baseline rows

quotes.text: Waitlist control group (n = 55)

issues.title: Sign slips in two CIs: ISI (-4.6 to 1.2) and SGRQ symptoms (-10.6 to 1.6) straddle zero yet P < 0.01
issues.explanation: Two confidence intervals, for the ISI and the SGRQ symptoms subscale, are printed as spanning zero while the reported P values are 0.001 and 0.009. The estimates sit at the midpoint of the intervals only if the upper bounds are -1.2 and -1.6. This is a likely dropped minus sign and does not change any result. It is a reporting error that could mislead a reader.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The published PDF showing minus signs on both upper bounds.

quotes.text: subscale symptoms MD, -6.1; 95% CI, -10.6 to 1.6; P = 0.009
insomnia assessed by the ISI (MD, -2.9; 95% CI, -4.6 to 1.2; P = 0.001)

script.explanation: the estimate -6.1 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [-10.6, 1.6] (expected about -4.5000) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

issues.title: Waitlist 'Emotional change' printed as 36 (0.65) in a percent column; 36/55 = 65.5%
issues.explanation: One cell in an n (%) column is printed as a proportion, and a truncated one. The count agrees with the overall total of 76. Nothing depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: n/a; this is a format slip.

10.15275/rusomj.2025.0109.headline_claim: Adjunctive systemic ozone therapy with pharmacological treatment reduced oxidative stress markers and improved mental status in post-COVID-19 asthenic syndrome, and is presented as an effective and pathogenetically relevant strategy for outpatient management.
10.15275/rusomj.2025.0109.overall: Biomarker and symptom-scale improvements in the ozone arm may be real, but the study is open-label with no sham infusion, no registered primary outcome, and no multiplicity control, so the effect sizes are likely inflated. The headline '95% complete resolution' and the 'pathogenetically relevant' claim go beyond the data, and the Abstract describes resveratrol and neurotrophin results that do not exist elsewhere in the paper. Several printed counts, baselines and percentages are internally inconsistent, so the paper's numbers should be read with caution.'

primary_outcome.name: Change at day 30 in plasma MDA, SOD, GPx and mental status scales (no primary outcome designated)

issues.title: Open-label ozone infusions vs oral drug only; subjective scales drive the efficacy conclusion
issues.explanation: Main-group patients received 10 intravenous ozone infusions on top of oral treatment while the comparison group received only the oral drug, with no sham procedure and no description of blinding. Fatigue, sleep, anxiety, cognition and global severity were rated with scales that are open to expectancy and attention effects. The very large between-group differences (for example 94.2% vs 62.9% 'absence of illness') cannot be attributed to ozone itself from this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and laboratory staff were blinded and that patients received a sham infusion.

quotes.text: a comparison group (n=70) receiving only pharmacological treatment
patients in the main group also received systemic ozone therapy

second_reader.what_stands: The trial is open-label and compares an ozone infusion plus drug against drug alone, with no sham and no stated blinding, so non-specific effects of added infusions and expectation could inflate the symptom scale results. The conclusion also leans on lab biomarkers, so it is not driven by subjective scales alone, but these are also given without blinding detail.

issues.title: '95% complete resolution of symptoms' vs 94.2% (66/70) CGI-S 'absence of illness' in an open trial
issues.explanation: The headline figure of 95% is not what Table 4 prints (66 of 70, 94.2%) and is stated as complete resolution of PCAS symptoms in the Conclusion, although the underlying rating is a single clinician global-severity category. The Methods describe the CGI-I item, not CGI-S, and the same measure is not reported for the individual symptom scales (MFI-20 post-treatment median is still 20.5, ISI 5.0). The claim of symptom resolution therefore goes beyond the data reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified definition of complete resolution met by 95% of patients, with individual symptom scale data supporting it.

quotes.text: Notably, 95% of patients in the ozone therapy group experienced a complete or near-complete resolution
66 patients (94.2%) in the main group were rated as
specifically item CGI-I

second_reader.what_stands: The 95% figure is a loose rounding of 66/70 (94.3%) and is stated as 'complete resolution of PCAS symptoms', although the measure is a single clinician global severity rating, 'absence of illness', in an unblinded trial. The Methods name CGI-I as the instrument but the results are CGI-S, and the comparison group's CGI-S categories sum to 63 of 70.

issues.title: 'Pathogenetically relevant' claim rests on biomarker changes with no biomarker-symptom analysis
issues.explanation: The paper concludes ozone is pathogenetically relevant because oxidative markers improved alongside symptoms. Markers also improved in the comparison group, the design is open-label, and the Spearman correlations promised in the Methods are never reported, so no link between oxidative stress change and clinical change is shown. The recommendation for outpatient management also generalizes from adults aged 18-45 with BMI 18.5-24.9 and no comorbidities over 30 days.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported correlations or mediation analyses linking biomarker change to symptom score change.

quotes.text: our data suggest that adjunctive systemic ozone therapy is not only effective but also pathogenetically relevant
Correlations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient

second_reader.what_stands: The paper says Spearman correlations were assessed but reports none, so the claim that ozone therapy is 'pathogenetically relevant' rests on group-level co-occurrence of biomarker and symptom improvement plus an argument from earlier studies. No analysis links the biomarker change to symptom change within this trial.

issues.title: Abstract Results describe resveratrol and IGF-1/BDNF/NGF findings absent from the study
issues.explanation: The Abstract says patients treated with resveratrol showed larger changes in IGF-1, BDNF and NGF than the comparison group, approaching control levels. The Methods give ozone plus Brainmax as the intervention, and measure only MDA, SOD and GPx plus clinical scales. The Abstract therefore reports results for a drug and biomarkers the study never describes. A reader relying on the Abstract is misled about what was tested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Methods or Results section reporting resveratrol dosing and IGF-1, BDNF and NGF measurements in this cohort.

quotes.text: pronounced changes in plasma IGF-1, BDNF, and NGF levels
reduced levels of neurotrophic factors

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract Results describe resveratrol-treated patients and IGF-1, BDNF and NGF findings, including the control-group comparison, that appear nowhere in the Methods, Results tables, Discussion or Conclusion. The Abstract Results therefore do not match the study, which tested ozone and measured oxidative stress markers.

issues.title: Eight outcomes tested at p<0.05, no primary outcome; SOD p=0.036, GPx p=0.028, MoCA p=0.046
issues.explanation: Three biomarkers and five scales were each tested at an uncorrected 0.05 level and no primary outcome is named. MDA and the symptom scales are strongly significant, but the SOD, GPx and MoCA between-group results would not survive a simple Bonferroni adjustment over eight tests (threshold 0.00625). The conclusions about SOD, GPx and cognition should be read as tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome and a stated multiplicity plan.

quotes.text: Statistical significance was defined as p <0.05

issues.title: Randomized trial with no registry or registration number reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomized study but gives no trial registry entry and no designated primary outcome. Outcome selection and analysis choices cannot be checked against a prior plan.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry identifier dated before enrolment began in November 2021.

quotes.text: The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee

issues.title: Printed percent changes disagree with the printed medians: ISI -81.3% vs -72.5%; GPx +52.2% vs +59.1%
issues.explanation: In Tables 3 and 4 the percent change usually equals the change between the printed medians, but several main-group cells do not. ISI is printed as -81.3% (and repeated in the Discussion) while 18.2 to 5.0 gives -72.5%. GPx is printed as +52.2% while 2.2 to 3.5 gives +59.1%. MFI-20 (-74.7% in the table, 74.4% in the Discussion, 75.0% from the medians) and MoCA (+17.1% vs 17.8%) are also slightly off. The ISI error overstates the effect and the GPx error understates it, so the reporting of effect sizes is unreliable though the direction of each result is unchanged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that percent changes are medians of per-patient changes, with individual-level data showing 81.3% for ISI and 52.2% for GPx.

quotes.location: Table 4, ISI row, main group post-treatment

issues.title: Comparison-group baselines differ between Table 1 and Table 4 (MFI-20 81.3 vs 81.6; MoCA 24.1 vs 24.5)
issues.explanation: The same 70 comparison patients at baseline have different medians and quartiles in Tables 1 and 4: MFI-20 81.3 [78.1; 83.9] versus 81.6 [78.3; 84.6], and MoCA 24.1 versus 24.5. HAM-A (20.9 vs 20.7) and ISI upper quartile (18.8 vs 18.5) also differ. Main-group baselines match across tables. The differences are small, but baseline values should be identical.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that Table 4 uses a different baseline sample or assessment visit than Table 1.

quotes.location: Table 4, MFI-20 row, comparison group pre-treatment
Table 4, MoCA row, comparison group pre-treatment

issues.title: No sample-size calculation reported for 70 patients per arm
issues.explanation: The paper does not say how 70 per arm was chosen. This makes it hard to judge the precision of the borderline between-group results, though most outcomes are clearly significant.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or methods statement giving the power calculation.

quotes.text: enrolled 140 outpatients (77 women and 63 men)

issues.title: Table 1 baseline p-values (0.072, 0.070, 0.075) do not fit the printed counts, which imply p near 0.7
issues.explanation: For 41 vs 39 marked illness out of 70 per arm, a chi-square test gives p near 0.73, not 0.072. The same pattern holds for CGI-S moderately ill and severe COVID-19. The values look like misprints, but as printed they would suggest borderline baseline imbalance, contradicting the statement that groups were well matched.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 1 with p-values near 0.7, or an explanation of a different test used.

issues.title: Sex counts: 77 women/63 men stated for 140, but arms sum to 87/53; Table 1 header gives n=140 for 70
issues.explanation: The Methods say 140 patients (77 women, 63 men), but the two arms (43+44 women, 27+26 men) add to 87 women and 53 men. The Table 1 column header also labels the main group n=140 while its cells and the text use 70. The arm-level numbers are internally consistent, so the totals and header are misprinted. This does not affect efficacy results, but baseline reporting is unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the cohort included additional patients not randomized to either arm, or a corrected table showing 77/63 across arms.

quotes.text: enrolled 140 outpatients (77 women and 63 men)
Main Group (n=140)

issues.title: 'All' mental status changes called significant, but comparison-group MoCA change has p=0.072
issues.explanation: The Results say all mental status indicators showed statistically significant changes (p<0.05). Table 4 shows the comparison-group MoCA change (+4.9%) with p=0.072, which is above the stated threshold. The between-group MoCA result (p=0.046) is unaffected, but the statement is not accurate as written.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The sentence being restricted to main-group changes or to between-group comparisons.

quotes.text: All mental status indicators showed statistically significant changes

10.15395/mkb.v55n2.2753.headline_claim: Online WHO Stress Management can improve the average Insomnia Severity Index score in people with post-COVID syndrome, but the improvement is not clinically significant.
10.15395/mkb.v55n2.2753.overall: The headline claim that WHO Stress Management improves insomnia scores rests on a non-randomised, unblinded comparison with unadjusted baseline imbalance, unusable CIs, and p-values printed as 0.00 that contradict the text and the summary statistics. The raw mean fall is larger in the treatment arm, but the paper's own adjusted analysis finds no significant intervention effect, so effectiveness is at best tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score, pre- to post-intervention

issues.title: Baseline ISI difference given p=0.00 yet called both non-significant (Results) and significant (Discussion)
issues.explanation: The Results say there was no significant baseline insomnia difference at p=0.00, while the Discussion says the same p=0.00 showed a significant difference. A p of 0.00 cannot be both. The printed baseline means (18.56±4.58 vs 19.94±5.51, n=18 each) imply a difference of about 1.4 points, which would give p near 0.4, so the printed p=0.00 itself looks wrong, and the baseline balance, which matters for a non-randomised comparison, is unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the baseline p was <0.005 or >0.05 with a corrected value, or a different test than the summary statistics imply.

quotes.text: With p=0.00, there was no significant difference between insomnia scores in the control and
showed p = 0.00, which showed

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

second_reader.what_stands: The Results call the baseline difference non-significant while giving p=0.00. The Discussion calls the same p=0.00 significant and says the groups differed at baseline. A p of 0.00 is also implausible for means of 18.56 and 19.94 with SDs of about 5 and n=18 per group, so the reported p-value itself looks wrong.

issues.title: Table 2 delta scores (2.11, 10.33) lie outside the 95% CIs printed beside them
issues.explanation: In Table 2 the CI beside each delta does not contain it: 2.11 versus 17.54-20.96, and 10.33 versus 11.04-15.02. It is unclear what the intervals refer to; the first brackets a baseline mean, the second matches nothing printed. The main effect size therefore has no interpretable interval.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A column definition showing the CIs are for a different quantity, with a correct CI of the delta given.

quotes.text: WHO Stress Management (Mean±SD)
with a p-value of 0.00 (95% CI: 20.96-17.56)

script.explanation: the estimate 10.33 lies outside its own CI [11.04, 15.02]; the estimate 10.33 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [11.04, 15.02] (expected about 13.0300) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

second_reader.what_stands: The deltas are arithmetically consistent with the pre and post means. Neither delta lies inside the 95% CI printed beside it, and the table does not say what the CIs estimate. As presented, the CIs cannot be interpreted as intervals for the change scores.

issues.title: Non-randomised allocation with unreported assignment method and unadjusted baseline imbalance
issues.explanation: Participants were assigned to groups without randomisation, and the allocation procedure is not described. The groups differ at baseline in ISI (19.94 vs 18.56) and in several covariates (e.g., gadget use before bed 38.9% vs 5.6%). Post-intervention differences are not adjusted for baseline, so selection and confounding cannot be separated from any treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random or concealed allocation, or an ANCOVA adjusting for baseline showing the same effect.

quotes.text: quasiexperimental,  pre-test-post-test  control  group design
then  divided into an exposure group and a control group

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation was non-randomised and the method of assignment is not reported. Baseline imbalances (age, gadget use, baseline ISI) are present and the primary between-group comparisons are not adjusted for them. The Discussion's statement of no demographic difference contradicts the reported age p=0.03.

issues.title: Title and Discussion claim effectiveness while the adjusted intervention term is non-significant (OR 0.81, p=0.26)
issues.explanation: The title and Discussion say WHO Stress Management is effective, citing external meta-analyses, while the paper's own regression finds no significant intervention effect and says it has no causative effect. The conclusion then says the effect is not clinically significant, without reconciling this with an ISI fall of about 10 points. The reader cannot tell what is concluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An adjusted analysis showing a significant intervention effect, or a consistent conclusion.

quotes.text: the OR was 0.81 with p=0.26
provides effective results
but  it  is  not  clinically  significant

second_reader.what_stands: The title and the opening of the Discussion state effectiveness more strongly than the adjusted regression term (OR 0.81, p=0.26) supports. The paper does disclose this non-significance and qualifies its Conclusion as 'not clinically significant'. It attributes the shortfall to the online format without testing that explanation, and the paper's messages are mixed.

issues.title: Age difference reported as p=0.03 (control younger) but Table 1 counts are near-identical and Discussion says none
issues.explanation: The Results state the control group was significantly younger (p=0.03), the Discussion says no demographic test was significant, and Table 1's age counts (13/5 vs 14/4) are almost identical and cannot produce p=0.03. Table 1 also shows a lower share of younger adults in the control group, the opposite of the text. The age comparison is therefore unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Mean ages by group and an independent t-test giving p=0.03.

quotes.text: The control group had a younger mean age than the treatment group (p=0.03).
did not find any significant difference

issues.title: Table 3 CIs appear to be on the log-odds scale beside ORs; three predictors share OR 1.49
issues.explanation: The gender OR of 1.49 sits beside a CI of 0.01-0.46 that cannot contain it. The interval does contain the printed beta of 0.41, so it is probably a CI for the coefficient mislabelled as an OR CI. Gender, occupation and diet are all reported with OR 1.49, which is also odd. This affects only the secondary risk-factor table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 3 headers stating that the CI refers to the coefficient.

quotes.text: gender (OR 1.49)

issues.title: Effect inferred mainly from within-group Wilcoxon tests; between-group change comparison not reported
issues.explanation: The paper tests pre/post change within each arm (both p=0.00) and compares post scores between arms, but never compares change scores between arms. Both arms improved, so within-arm significance alone shows nothing about the intervention. The raw means (2.1-point fall vs 10.3-point fall) suggest a difference, but no valid test or interval of the difference in change is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test of change scores or baseline-adjusted post scores.

quotes.text: There was a decrease in the clinical mean in the treatment group

issues.title: Open-label design with self-reported ISI and unequal contact time between arms
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation and self-reported the ISI.
