The intervention group also received five Zoom sessions that the control did not, so attention and expectation are confounded with the module. The authors list non-blinding as a limitation, but the effectiveness statement does not reflect it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of an attention-matched control or blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: not being blinded at the time of sample selection and giving the intervention

issues.title: No trial registration reported for a prospective intervention study
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval but no registry number for a prospective study with an intervention. Outcome and analysis plans cannot be checked against a prior record. It is a quasi-experimental design, so the expectation is weaker.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier for the study.

quotes.text: This  research  has  received  permission  from  the  Health  Research  Ethics  Committee

10.15407/fz71.06.095.headline_claim: Pathogenetically based modified therapy for post-COVID menstrual cycle disorders provides significantly better outcomes than standard protocols.
10.15407/fz71.06.095.overall: The headline claim of superiority rests on an undescribed, non-randomised allocation, unadjusted percentages with no test results or subgroup sizes, and regimens that differ by subtype. The direction of effect is large and consistent, but the paper cannot attribute it to the treatment, and the guideline recommendation is not supported. A Conclusion statement about menometrorrhagia contradicts the paper's own control figures.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: Allocation to modified vs standard therapy not described; no randomisation or blinding, causal superiority claimed
issues.explanation: The paper never says how the 158 women were assigned to groups, and there is no randomisation, concealment, blinding or description of baseline comparability. Treatments also differ in content by disorder type (e.g. COCs only in the modified arm for several types), so differences could reflect selection, clinician choice or period. Despite this, the abstract and Conclusion state the modified therapy provides significantly better outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random allocation with concealment, or of a concurrent allocation rule independent of patient characteristics, with baseline balance shown.

quotes.text: Pathogenetically based personalized therapy for menstrual cycle disorders in women after COVID-19 provides significantly better outcomes than standard protocols.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not describe how women were allocated to the modified versus standard regimen and reports no randomisation or blinding, yet it states causal superiority ('provides significantly better outcomes', 'prove the key role'). Without allocation information the group difference cannot be attributed to the therapy, and clinicians assessing relapse and tolerability were probably aware of the treatment given (not stated either way).

issues.title: Guideline-update recommendation and mechanism claims exceed an unadjusted non-randomised comparison
issues.explanation: The Conclusion recommends the approach as a basis for updating clinical guidelines, and the Abstract states that eliminating vascular, immune and neuroendocrine consequences is the key factor in restoration. Neither mechanism nor component effects were measured; the multi-component regimens differ by subtype and cannot be disentangled. Only percentages are given, with 'P < 0.05' stated generically in figure notes and no test values, intervals or subgroup sizes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Randomised or adjusted evidence with per-subtype sample sizes, effect sizes and intervals, and measurements of the proposed mechanisms.

quotes.text: The developed approach may serve as a foundation for updating clinical guidelines on the management of menstrual disorders in women with post-COVID syndrome.
Elimination of vascular, immune, and neuroendocrine consequences of COVID-19 is a key factor in the effective restoration of menstrual function

second_reader.what_stands: The recommendation to update guidelines and the statement that eliminating vascular, immune and neuroendocrine consequences is a key factor rest on an unadjusted comparison with no stated allocation method, a multi-component bundle that cannot separate mechanisms, and no mechanistic measurements in the reported results. The guideline sentence is hedged with 'may', but the mechanism claims are worded as established ('key factor', 'confirm', 'prove').

issues.title: Conclusion says menometrorrhagia lowers normalization vs polymenorrhea, but control rates are 35.3% vs 33.3%
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says that the more complex disorder, particularly menometrorrhagia compared with polymenorrhea, has a lower chance of normalization after standard treatment. The Results give 35.3% for menometrorrhagia and 33.3% for polymenorrhea in the control group, which is the opposite direction (and a trivial difference). The conclusion is not supported by the data presented, though it is a secondary statement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure data showing control normalization lower for menometrorrhagia than polymenorrhea.

quotes.text: which is more than twice as high as in the control group (33.3%)
compared to 35.3% in the control group
particularly menometrorrhagia compared to polymenorrhea, the lower the likelihood of achieving full cycle normalization after a standard course of treatment

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified outcomes reported for an interventional comparison
issues.explanation: The paper reports an ethics approval but no registry entry or protocol, and no primary outcome is designated among relapse, normalization, therapy modification and adverse effects. Without prespecification, the reader cannot judge selective emphasis. This reduces confidence but is not itself an error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial or protocol registration entry preceding enrolment, listing the outcomes.

quotes.text: Ethical approval for this study was obtained from the Ethics Committee of the hosting institution (Protocol No. 1, dated 31.01.2022).

issues.title: Ukrainian abstract swaps group labels vs English abstract/Methods (group 1 n=78 standard vs group 1 n=80 modified)
issues.explanation: The English abstract and Methods define group 1 as the modified regimen (n=80) and group 2 as standard care (n=78). The Ukrainian abstract defines group 1 as standard care (n=78) and group 2 as the modified regimen (n=80), yet still says the 'group 1' relapse rate was lower. A reader of the Ukrainian version would reverse which arm did better. The body text is consistent, so this is a labelling error in one abstract only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the Ukrainian abstract labels match the Methods.

quotes.text: Patients of group 1 (n = 80) received a modified comprehensive pathogenetic regimen
Пацієнтки  1-ї  групи  (n  =  78)  отримували  лікування відповідно до уніфікованих клінічних протоколів МОЗ України

10.1556/2060.2025.00713.headline_claim: Twelve weeks of circuit training is a feasible and effective adjunct to pulmonary rehabilitation across COPD, post-COVID syndrome and asthma, with the largest spirometric gains in COPD, and is safe and scalable.
10.1556/2060.2025.00713.overall: The finding that patients improved on several measures after 12 weeks of supervised training is plausible, but with no control group and only within-group paired tests the paper cannot show that circuit training caused the improvement or that it is effective, safe or superior. The text also overstates significance in asthma (several p-values of 0.051–0.085 described as significant) and misstates which group gained most. The conclusions are best read as preliminary feasibility evidence from 30 patients.

primary_outcome.name: not specified; spirometry (FEV1), 6MWD and mMRC are reported as the main outcomes

issues.title: Effectiveness claimed from uncontrolled pre-post paired tests in 3 small groups (n = 15, 11, 4)
issues.explanation: All 30 participants received the intervention and were measured only at week 0 and week 12, so improvements cannot be attributed to circuit training rather than natural recovery (especially post-COVID), learning effects on the 6MWT, regression to the mean, or other concurrent care. The analysis uses within-group paired t-tests, and no between-group or control comparison is reported. The paper still concludes the programme is 'effective' and cites it as comparable or superior to other modalities. The supportable conclusion is feasibility with preliminary signals.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group, or a between-group analysis, showing a difference attributable to circuit training.

quotes.text: This study employed a prospective, quasi-experimental design with pre- and post-intervention assessments
This study demonstrated that a 12-week circuit training program is a feasible and effective adjunct to pulmonary rehabilitation
Paired t-tests: Pre-post comparisons (normality conﬁrmed via Shapiro-Wilk test).

second_reader.what_stands: The paper bases its claim of effectiveness on uncontrolled within-group pre-post paired tests in three small groups (15, 11, 4). It has no comparison group, so it cannot attribute the changes to the program. The conclusion's closing request for larger controlled studies only partly tempers the word 'effective' and the 'demonstrated' framing, and the missing control group is not listed among the limitations.

issues.title: Safety, scalability, superiority and unmeasured fatigue/cognitive/asthma-control benefits claimed from n = 30 uncontrolled
issues.explanation: The Conclusion calls circuit training 'safe' and 'scalable' for heterogeneous populations, and the Discussion says it is comparable or superior to conventional modalities, with no comparison arm. The Discussion also reports reductions in fatigue and improved asthma control and confidence, but no fatigue scale, quality-of-life instrument or asthma-control measure is reported. 'No adverse events' in 30 selected, supervised patients cannot establish safety across heterogeneous populations, and scalability was not tested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported fatigue, quality-of-life and asthma-control measurements, or a comparator arm supporting the superiority and safety statements.

quotes.text: safe, and scalable modality that can be integrated into rehabilitation protocols
substantial increases in 6MWD and reductions in fatigue and dyspnea
Psychosocial outcomes were inferred from adherence and informal feedback rather than standardized tools.

second_reader.what_stands: 'Safe' is supported only narrowly (no adverse events in 30 monitored participants), and 'scalable' has no supporting data. Reductions in fatigue, cognitive benefit and improved asthma control are discussed although no standardised outcome for them was measured or reported, as the Limitations partly admit for psychosocial outcomes. 'Comparable or superior' to other modalities is not testable in a single-arm study. The conclusion does hedge with 'larger controlled studies', but the Discussion's claims go beyond the data.

issues.title: 'Significant improvement in all groups' contradicted by asthma p = 0.051–0.085 for IVC, FEV1/FVC, TLC, FEV1/IVC
issues.explanation: The Results state that pulmonary function improved statistically significantly in all three diagnostic groups, and the abstract says IVC improved in all groups with P ≤0.051. Table 4 shows four asthma pulmonary-function outcomes above the stated 0.05 threshold (IVC 0.051, TLC 0.062, FEV1/FVC 0.078, FEV1/IVC 0.085), and Table 5 gives n.s. for the asthma chest-wall outcomes. Only asthma FEV1 (0.012) and FVC (0.045) pass, and these are from 4 patients with no multiplicity control.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different alpha stated for the asthma group, or a pooled all-group test in which these outcomes were significant.

quotes.text: IVC improved in all groups (P ≤0.051)
Rehabilitation resulted in clinically and statistically significant improvements in pulmonary function

issues.title: Conclusion's 'largest spirometric gains in COPD' contradicts Table 4, where post-COVID gains are larger
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says the largest spirometric gains were in COPD. In Table 4, post-COVID shows larger absolute gains than COPD for FEV1 (+9.1 vs +7.7), FVC (+6.6 vs +5.7), TLC (+7.5 vs +6.5) and IVC (+6.2 vs +5.8). The claim holds only in a clinical-relevance sense, which the conclusion does not state. It is a misstatement of the data, not a change to the overall finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 'largest' refers to clinical relevance relative to baseline impairment, rather than the size of the change.

quotes.text: with the largest spirometric gains in COPD
FEV1 increased by 9.1% (P < 0.001)

issues.title: No sample-size rationale; asthma subgroup of 4 and ~30 uncorrected tests underpin subgroup conclusions
issues.explanation: The study recruited 15, 11 and 4 patients with no power calculation. With only 4 asthma patients, p-values near 0.05 (0.012, 0.045) and subgroup claims about asthma benefit are fragile, and about 15 pulmonary-function tests plus walk, dyspnea and chest-wall outcomes were run without correction. The authors admit limited power, but the Discussion and Conclusion still state benefits for each diagnosis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation or a statement that the study was a pilot with no confirmatory claims.

quotes.text: The overall sample size was modest (15 COPD, 11 post-COVID, 4 asthma), which limits statistical power and generalizability.
SPSS v28 (α 5 0.05)

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified primary outcome reported for a prospective intervention study
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval but no registry identifier or protocol, and does not designate a primary outcome. With many outcomes tested, readers cannot check which analyses were planned. This weakens interpretation of the secondary and subgroup results, but it is common in small quasi-experimental studies.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol listing the prespecified primary outcome.

quotes.text: The study received ethical approval (3/2024, Semmelweis University)

issues.title: Maximum participant age 76 exceeds the stated inclusion limit of 70
issues.explanation: Table 1 lists age 35–70 as an inclusion criterion, yet the Results and Table 3 report a range of 35–76. At least one participant was apparently enrolled outside the stated criteria without explanation. This is a minor reporting inconsistency that does not change the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated protocol exception for older participants, or a corrected age.

quotes.text: Age between 35 and 70 years
ranging from 35 to 76 years

issues.title: Total former-smoker rate 50% does not match group rows, which imply 18/30 = 60%
issues.explanation: Table 3 gives 100% former smokers in COPD (15 patients), 27% in post-COVID (3 of 11) and 0% in asthma. These sum to 18 of 30 patients, or 60%. The Results text and the Total column state 50%. This is a small descriptive inconsistency with no bearing on the efficacy findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A footnote defining the smoking categories differently for the total column (for example a different denominator).

quotes.text: Half of the participants were former smokers.
27% former smokers

issues.title: Table 4 labels d = 0.63, 0.67 and 0.72 'large' although Methods define large as d ≥ 0.8
issues.explanation: The Methods set large at 0.8, medium at 0.5 and small at 0.2. Table 4 nonetheless labels COPD FEV1 (0.72), post-COVID FVC (0.67) and post-COVID IVC (0.63) as large. This inflates the apparent magnitude of effects, although the d values themselves are shown. It does not change any p-value.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that different effect-size thresholds were used for the table labels.

quotes.text: 0.72 (large)
0.67 (large)

10.15789/2220-7619-doc-2042.headline_claim: Intranasal IFN α-2b gel normalised salivary and nasal sIgA and prevented respiratory infections in people recovering from COVID-19 for up to 9 months.
10.15789/2220-7619-doc-2042.overall: The headline claim that IFN α-2b normalised sIgA and prevented respiratory infections for up to 9 months is not supported by this non-randomised, open study with only two sIgA time points per patient and no between-arm testing for saliva. Several text and abstract figures are misreported (fold changes, untreated 'time course'), and the nasal data contradict the premise of reduced sIgA. The saliva rise in treated group I (1.84 to 5.78) is the only clearly supported finding, and it is an uncontrolled association.

primary_outcome.name: sIgA concentration in saliva and nasal swab material, before and 30 days after the IFN α-2b course

issues.title: Non-randomised, open comparison with baseline imbalance underlies causal 'normalised sIgA and prevented infections' claims
issues.explanation: Patients were divided into treated and untreated halves with no randomisation, concealment or blinding described. Table 6 shows large baseline differences between the arms in several subgroups, and infection was ascertained from questionnaires. Yet the abstract concludes IFN α-2b normalised sIgA and prevented infections (0/65 vs 18/65). The design supports only an association.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described random or concealed allocation procedure, or baseline-adjusted analyses giving the same result.

quotes.text: были поровну разделены на получавших и не получавших интраназально
Intranasally applied IFN α -2b made possible to normalize sIgA level and prevent accumulation of respiratory infectious pathologies.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes an open comparison with no stated randomisation or allocation method, and baseline nasal and salivary sIgA differ clearly between arms in several time strata. The causal wording in the Abstract and Conclusion ('made possible to normalize sIgA level and prevent...') goes beyond what this design supports.

issues.title: Conclusion of sustained normal sIgA and infection prevention 'up to 9 months' exceeds one 30-day measurement
issues.explanation: The conclusion says IFN α-2b maintains normal sIgA and prevents infections for up to 9 months. The groups are patients at different times since illness, each measured only at baseline and about 30 days after starting. Saliva in treated groups II and III remains below the paper's own norm, and group III is not significantly changed. No follow-up beyond one month after treatment is reported for sIgA or infection.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Serial sIgA and infection data in treated patients over 9 months showing sustained normal levels.

quotes.text: в сроке до 9 месяцев (период наблюдения)
предупреждать развитие респираторных инфекционных патологий

quotes.location: Table 6, saliva row II, treated 30 days

second_reader.what_stands: Only one post-treatment measurement, 30 days after the course, exists per patient, so sustained normal sIgA and infection prevention for up to 9 months were not observed. In the 3-6-month stratum, salivary sIgA after therapy (3.33) remained well below the authors' norm and did not change significantly.

issues.title: Nasal sIgA at baseline is above the authors' norm (13.43), yet conclusions speak of reduced sIgA and 'normalisation'
issues.explanation: The conclusion states reduced sIgA was registered after COVID-19 and that IFN α-2b normalised it. For nasal sIgA, all treated baselines (28.61, 31.22, 37.06) and most untreated baselines (28.33, 27.11) already exceed the healthy norm of 13.43±3.24. IFN pushed group I to 39.83, further from the norm, so the nasal result is an increase above normal rather than normalisation. The norm is from only 15 younger controls (mean age 32 vs 48.5), which further weakens the comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An explanation that the nasal assay units or sampling differ between patients and controls so that the norm is not comparable, with a corrected norm.

quotes.text: nasal swabs - 13.43±3.24 mg/ml

quotes.location: Table 6, nasal row I, treated baseline

quotes.text: reduced sIgA level is registered

second_reader.what_stands: By the authors' own norm, nasal sIgA was elevated, not reduced, at baseline in every stratum and arm, and the 'normalisation' in nasal samples was in fact a rise further above the norm. The 'reduced sIgA' finding is supported for saliva, but not for nasal samples. The 'arbitrary normal range' also comes from only 15 controls with a mean age of 32 vs 48.5 in patients.

issues.title: Saliva sIgA effect inferred from within-arm change; no test named for sIgA comparisons
issues.explanation: The abstract's saliva result contrasts a significant change from baseline in treated patients with an 'insignificant' change in untreated ones; no direct between-arm test of saliva is given. Only nasal sIgA has between-group markers in Table 6. The Methods list only chi-square, so the test used for the sIgA p-values is not identified, and the untreated comparisons carry no p-values at all. Also only treated group I is significant; groups II and III are not.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated between-arm (or interaction) test for saliva sIgA showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: differed insignificantly compared to baseline level
Достоверность показателей определялась с использованием критерия хи-квадрат

second_reader.what_stands: The saliva claim rests on a single within-arm change in the 1-3-month stratum, with no between-arm saliva comparison. No test for continuous sIgA data is named; only chi-square is stated. The statement that untreated values did not differ from baseline is not supported by a described test, and the printed untreated nasal means show a large fall.

issues.title: No sample-size justification; time-window comparisons rest on 16-27 patients per arm
issues.explanation: The paper reports no power calculation, and the treated/untreated comparisons by time window use 16 to 27 patients per arm. With many subgroup comparisons and no multiplicity handling, the significant findings are fragile. The confident conclusions are not matched by this sample size.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported power calculation justifying these sizes.

quotes.text: Группу контроля (n = 15) составили условно здоровые лица

issues.title: sIgA second sampling: one month after course completion (Methods) vs one month into therapy (Results/Table 6)
issues.explanation: Methods say sIgA was measured one month after the 30-day course ended. Results, the abstract and Table 6 ('30 days later') imply sampling at the end of the 30 days, while still on therapy. These are different time points about 60 versus 30 days after start. A reader cannot tell whether the rise reflects on-treatment or post-treatment status.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement clarifying that the course ended at the 30-day sampling and the 'after completion' wording is a slip.

quotes.text: через месяц после завершения курса
спустя месяц на фоне терапии препаратом IFN α -2b

issues.title: Abstract 'untreated' nasal 15.66→10.23 and saliva 2.36→2.16 are 30-day values from different groups, not a time course
issues.explanation: The abstract presents the untreated group as having 'stably sustained decline up to 9 months', quoting 15.66 to 10.23 (nasal) and 2.36 to 2.16 (saliva) 'compared to baseline'. In Table 6 these are the 30-day values of untreated groups I and III respectively. The matching baselines are 28.33 and 27.11 (nasal) and 3.08 and 2.08 (saliva). The untreated arm is a cross-section at different times since illness with only two time points, not a 9-month follow-up. Untreated nasal values also halve within 30 days (28.33 to 15.66), which is not a 'stable' state.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing the same untreated patients were followed to 9 months with these values.

quotes.text: in nasal smears from 15.66±1.32 to 10.23±1.07 mg/ml

quotes.location: Table 6, nasal row I, untreated baseline

quotes.text: ranged from 2.36±0.56 down to 2.16±0.66 mg/ml

issues.title: Text says dyspnoea 2.3 times more frequent in group I; printed percentages give 1.5-fold (odds ratio 2.25)
issues.explanation: The text calls the dyspnoea difference 2.3-fold, but 57.7% versus 37.8% is a 1.5-fold ratio of frequencies. The 2.3 figure fits an odds ratio, which the paper never names. The wording is loose rather than the data being wrong, and nothing in the conclusions depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that the 2.3 is an odds ratio.

quotes.text: регистрировалась в 2,3 раза чаще

issues.title: Text says sputum 1.4-fold more frequent in group III vs I; Table 4 percentages give 2.2-fold
issues.explanation: The text reports sputum as 1.4 times more frequent in group III than group I, but the printed figures (33.3% vs 15.4%) give about 2.2-fold. No common alternative measure produces 1.4. This is a reporting error in one secondary symptom comparison; it does not touch the main findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition under which the ratio of these two groups is 1.4.

quotes.text: Выделение мокроты наблюдалось у больных III группы 1,4 раза чаще, чем в I группе

issues.title: Nasal sIgA fold rise printed as 1.5 but 39.83/28.61 = 1.39
issues.explanation: The abstract and discussion state that nasal sIgA rose 1.5-fold in treated group I. The printed values 28.61 and 39.83 give a rise of 1.39-fold. The saliva fold (5.78/1.84 = 3.14) is correct. A small overstatement of one secondary effect size.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Unrounded means whose ratio is at least 1.45.

quotes.text: by more than 3- and 1.5-fold, respectively

script.explanation: Nasal sIgA fold change group I, 30 days vs baseline: 39.83 / 28.61 gives 1.39217, not the printed 1.5. For the printed value to hold the denominator would have to be 26.5533, not 28.61.

10.15829/1728-8800-2021-2986.headline_claim: Inhaled active hydrogen (AFV, H(H2O)m) added to standard rehabilitation in COVID-19 survivors with chronic fatigue is safe and highly effective during recovery.
10.15829/1728-8800-2021-2986.overall: The headline claim that hydrogen inhalation is 'safe and highly effective' is not reliably supported. The study is small, open-label and unblinded, with many untested-for-multiplicity outcomes, unexplained baseline imbalances, and several text-versus-table contradictions on lactate, group sizes, lymphocytes and shunt reduction. The tabulated pre/post changes in lactate and oxygenation markers are suggestive but tentative.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome designated; the 6-minute walk distance is the most prominent between-group result

issues.title: 'Safe and highly effective' concluded from a 55-patient, 10-day open comparison with surrogate outcomes
issues.explanation: Blinding is not described and there is no placebo or sham inhalation. Outcomes are physiological and laboratory markers, several of them subjective or effort-dependent, such as the walk test. There is no sample-size justification and no discussion of limitations. Safety rests on the statement that no objective procedure-related adverse events were found in 28 treated patients over 10 days. The paper's own between-group evidence is mixed: SpO2 shows no group difference, and baseline imbalances and uncorrected testing are not addressed. 'Highly effective' is not supported at this level.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded, adequately powered trial with a prespecified primary outcome and adjusted analysis showing the same effects.

quotes.text: оказалась безопасным и высокоэффективным лечебным методом
объективных, связанных с процедурой, побочных эффектов у пациентов выявлено не было

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion's 'safe and highly effective' rests on 55 patients (and fewer for many outcomes), 10 days of follow-up, an unblinded no-sham comparison and surrogate laboratory or physiological outcomes, with no fatigue or clinical outcome reported and no limitations discussed. The narrower safety statement (no objective procedure-related adverse events) is reported, but zero events in 27 patients leaves an upper 95% bound of roughly 11%.

issues.title: Baseline imbalance in reflection index (59.5 vs 46.67) and 6MWD (430 vs 397) with no baseline adjustment
issues.explanation: At baseline the hydrogen arm had a much lower RI than control (p<0.01) and a higher 6-minute walk distance (p<0.001). The headline between-group claim, a 30% higher walking distance at day 10, is therefore partly baseline difference (about 8%). The RI rise from a lower starting level may also partly reflect regression to the mean. No ANCOVA or change-score comparison is given, so the post-treatment differences cannot be attributed to the treatment alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline-adjusted between-group analysis (ANCOVA or interaction) showing the same treatment differences.

quotes.text: 430±45  и  397±30  м  соответственно

second_reader.what_stands: The paper itself reports large baseline imbalances in RI (about 12.8 points, roughly 1 SD, p<0.01) and 6MWD (33 m, roughly 0.9 SD, p<0.001) despite randomisation, and the analyses described (paired within-group tests, group x time ANOVA, endpoint comparisons) include no explicit baseline adjustment such as ANCOVA. The imbalances are in opposite directions for the two outcomes and may be chance, but the paper does not discuss them or adjust for them; the group x time interaction in the ANOVA partly addresses differential change, so the absence of any adjustment is only partly total.

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes tested at p<0.05 with no primary outcome or multiplicity control
issues.explanation: The methods list blood gases from three compartments, blood counts, biochemistry, endothelial indices, capillaroscopy and the walk test. All are tested at an uncorrected 0.05 level with no designated primary outcome. The abstract and conclusion highlight those reaching significance. Borderline findings (SvO2 p<0.05, SpO2 p<0.05, leukocytes) are weak evidence under this approach, and the conclusion of high effectiveness rests on the selected subset.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol naming one primary outcome with a hierarchical testing plan, or adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: Различия считали статистически значимыми при р<0,05.
сопровождалась достоверным снижением лейкоцитов и повышением лимфоцитов

second_reader.what_stands: The paper tests a large battery of outcomes (at least about three dozen listed in the Methods) at an unadjusted p<0.05, names no primary outcome and describes no multiplicity control. The Discussion's claim of a significant rise in lymphocytes is also not supported by Table 2 (31.61 to 32.40, unmarked), and the Results themselves say only leukocytes changed.

issues.title: Results text says lactate rose in both arms; Table 3 shows it fell (hydrogen 2.06 to 1.10; control venous 2.05 to 1.1)
issues.explanation: The Results say lactate significantly increased (p<0.0001) on day 10 with hydrogen. They also say control venous and capillary lactate rose (p<0.05). Table 3, the abstract and the conclusion show lactate falling in the hydrogen group in all three blood compartments. Control venous lactate fell from 2.05 to 1.1 and capillary from 1.77 to 1.24, so the text has the direction backwards. Control arterial lactate did rise (1.74 to 2.04), which the text does not mention. The lactate normalisation claim must rest on the table, but the text as printed contradicts it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected or erratum version of the text stating that lactate decreased, or a Table 3 whose columns are shown to be mislabelled.

quotes.text: достоверное  увеличение  PaO2 (р<0,0001) и  уровня  лактата  в  крови

Table 3, Venous blood, Lactate row, control group 1st day

issues.title: Discussion claims a rise in lymphocytes, but Table 2 shows no change (31.61 to 32.40%)
issues.explanation: The Results state that of the inflammation markers only leukocytes changed. The Discussion says hydrogen produced a significant fall in leukocytes and a rise in lymphocytes, and presents this as an anti-inflammatory effect. Table 2 has no significance mark on the lymphocyte values (31.61 to 32.40%).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant lymphocyte increase in the data, or a corrected Discussion.

quotes.text: сопровождалась достоверным снижением лейкоцитов и повышением лимфоцитов
из которой видно, что изменения касались только уровня лейкоцитов

quotes.location: Table 2, Лимфоциты row, hydrogen group 1st day

issues.title: Shunt fraction fall stated as 'more than 60%'; Table 3 means give about 40% (8.98 to 5.34), and control fell 39.5%
issues.explanation: The text says the hydrogen group's intrapulmonary shunt fell by more than 60%. Table 3 values (8.98 to 5.34) imply a fall of about 40%. The control group's shunt fell by about the same proportion (7.14 to 4.32), and the paper makes no between-group test of this change. The conclusion's claim of a reduced shunt fraction attributable to hydrogen is thus overstated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Per-patient data showing a mean relative reduction above 60%, or a between-group test showing greater reduction with hydrogen.

quotes.location: Table 3, Qs/Qt row, hydrogen group 1st day
Table 3, Qs/Qt row, control group 1st day

issues.title: Minimum SpO2 gain claimed from a within-arm test while the between-group difference was null
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion cite the rise in minimum exercise SpO2 (92.25 to 94.25%, p<0.05) in the hydrogen arm as evidence of benefit. The Results say there was no significant between-group difference at day 1 or day 10. The control arm was only described as showing no change, with no interaction test. Many other results are likewise within-arm pre/post tests (lactate, PO2, SO2, ALT, bilirubin).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant group-by-time interaction or between-group test of the SpO2 change favouring hydrogen.

quotes.text: отмечался достоверный рост минимальной SpO2 с 92,25±2,9 до 94,25±1,56%
достоверной разницы между группами не было

issues.title: Text swaps final group sizes (27 hydrogen/28 control); dropouts and Table 3 give 28 hydrogen/27 control
issues.explanation: The Results say 3 control and 2 hydrogen participants dropped out of 30 per arm. That leaves 27 control and 28 hydrogen, as Table 3 headers show. The sentence immediately after gives 27 hydrogen and 28 control. Table 2 also reports n=22 to 25 per arm without explaining the extra losses, so the analysed numbers are not fully traceable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant flow diagram showing 27 hydrogen and 28 control completers.

quotes.text: В итоге в Основной группе было 27 пациентов
Из исследования на 3-и сут. в Контрольной группе выбыли 3 участника
Контрольная группа (n=27)

issues.title: Hydrogen-group baseline Qs/Qt SD is 5.7 in the abstract but 5.07 in Table 3
issues.explanation: The abstract gives the baseline shunt fraction as 8.98±5.7, while Table 3 gives 8.98±5.07. Only one can be right. The effect on the interpretation is negligible, because the mean difference is the same.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing which SD is correct (that would resolve it, not remove it).

quotes.location: Table 3, Qs/Qt row, hydrogen group 1st day

10.15829/1728-8800-2023-3517.headline_claim: Hydrogen (active hydrogen) inhalation therapy may shift physiological processes and may influence post-COVID syndrome recovery, with proteomic changes in exhaled breath condensate suggesting activated mitochondrial ATP synthesis and reduced pro-inflammatory activity.
10.15829/1728-8800-2023-3517.overall: The study is an exploratory pilot with unequal dropout, no described randomization method, no between-arm tests and no reported statistics for the key protein changes. Its claims of hydrogen-driven mitochondrial ATP activation and reduced inflammation go well beyond what protein detection in breath condensate shows. Only the descriptive proteome lists can be relied on; the causal and clinical interpretation cannot.

primary_outcome.name: Exhaled breath condensate (EBC) protein composition changes (proteomic profile) before and after AH therapy

issues.title: Hydrogen effect inferred from within-arm changes and visual comparison; no between-arm test or p-values
issues.explanation: Claims of a 'more substantial effect' of hydrogen rest on the proportion of patients with rising protein levels in each arm (Fig. 3) and on proteins that appear in only one group. No test of the between-arm difference is reported, and no statistics are given for the 36 proteins or the claim that they 'reliably' separate before and after. Clustering on proteins selected from the same data cannot show a treatment effect. With 20% unequal dropout and many proteins tested, the pattern differences could arise by chance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-arm (arm x time) analysis with multiplicity control, showing hydrogen-specific changes in the 36 proteins.

quotes.text: отражают более существенное влияние АФВ на количественные изменения ряда белков
в группе, получающей водородную терапию, таких пациентов было больше

second_reader.what_stands: The claim of a greater hydrogen effect rests on a visual comparison of Fig. 2 clustering and Fig. 3 bar charts, plus the statement that more patients in the hydrogen arm had increases. The text reports no between-arm test, p-value, confidence interval or multiplicity adjustment, and the 'достоверно' is not backed by any named test. I could not see the figure contents, so this judgement rests on the printed text and Methods only.

issues.title: Conclusions of mitochondrial ATP activation and reduced inflammation exceed the protein-detection data
issues.explanation: The abstract, key messages and Conclusion say the results indicate hydrogen-driven activation of aerobic mitochondrial ATP synthesis and a substantial reduction in pro-inflammatory processes. The data are protein detection lists and unquantified abundance patterns in 48 follow-up samples, with no inflammatory markers, clinical outcomes or functional assays. The corroborating blood lactate result is not presented, and its citation [20] is a mismatched keratin reference. A recovery benefit is therefore unsupported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Functional or clinical data in the paper (lactate, inflammatory markers, symptom scores) with a between-arm analysis supporting these statements.

quotes.text: полученные результаты указывают на активацию водородной терапией аэробного синтеза аденозинтрифосфата в митохондриях
а также существенное снижение доли провоспалительных процессов

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusions of activated mitochondrial aerobic ATP synthesis and a 'существенное' fall in pro-inflammatory processes go beyond what protein detection in exhaled breath condensate can show, and no pro-inflammatory fraction is quantified in the paper. The main text does hedge ('указывают', 'может'), but the Key messages sentence is stated more firmly. The lactate link rests on an external source I could not check.

issues.title: Open-label 'randomized' comparison with no randomization method and no sham inhalation
issues.explanation: The study is called randomized and controlled, but no sequence generation or concealment is described. The control group got standard therapy only, with no sham inhalation. Protein abundance is an objective readout, so bias is limited, but differences cannot be assigned specifically to hydrogen. This weakens causal interpretation rather than invalidating the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of the randomization and allocation concealment (in the cited earlier report [3]) and evidence that sample handling and analysis were blinded to arm.

quotes.text: 2 группа (контрольная) - 30 медицинских работников, которые получали только стандартную терапию

issues.title: Unequal attrition (3/30 hydrogen vs 9/30 control; 12/60 overall) with no handling analysis
issues.explanation: Table 1 shows 27 of 30 analysed after hydrogen therapy and 21 of 30 in controls at day 10. The Results attribute the 12 missing patients to personal reasons. The loss is three times higher in controls and is not examined. Comparisons of group-specific protein sets (e.g. 14 proteins only in controls) can be affected by the different sample sizes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with paired samples, showing the same protein changes.

quotes.text: Всего было исследовано 108 проб КВВ:
Число пациентов, n

issues.title: Protein count rise printed as 12% (abstract and Results); counts 398 vs 349 give 14.0% over baseline
issues.explanation: The Results say proteins after therapy are 12% more than before, citing 398 and 349. Relative to the 'before' value of 349 the rise is 14.0%. The 12% only results if the difference is divided by the post-therapy count. The error is small and slightly understates the stated increase. It also carries no statistical test, so it supports no main claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that the percentage is expressed relative to the post-therapy count, or that 398 and 349 are not the counts being compared.

quotes.text: Число белков в пробах после терапии АФВ, в среднем, на 12% больше, чем до нее (398 и 349, соответственно)

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified outcome stated for a study labelled randomized controlled
issues.explanation: The paper calls itself a randomized controlled prospective study but gives no registry identifier or primary outcome definition. The design is deferred to an earlier report [3]. Without this, the 36-protein and pathway findings cannot be judged against a plan. The effect on conclusions is small beyond the issues already raised.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier and prespecified outcome in the cited design paper [3] matching this analysis.

quotes.text: Дизайн исследования и подробная характеристика больных, включенных в программу, описаны ранее [3].

10.1590/fm.2023.36112.headline_claim: Multicomponent rehabilitation was not effective in treating post-COVID-19 because the observed increases in the studied variables were not statistically significant.
10.1590/fm.2023.36112.overall: The trial's descriptive data show the intervention group improving while the control group stayed flat, but the paper reports no valid between-group test of change and describes unexplained loss of 19 of 31 intervention participants alongside an ITT claim. The categorical 'not effective' conclusion is therefore not supported, and the results are best read as inconclusive. Table 1 and abstract numeric slips are real but do not affect the main findings.

primary_outcome.name: Not specified as primary; 6MWT, Berg balance scale and SF-36 are all reported as outcomes

issues.title: 'Not effective' conclusion rests on non-significance, with no valid between-group test of change reported
issues.explanation: The conclusion states the rehabilitation was not effective because the improvements were not significant. Table 2's p columns are labelled as normality and variance tests, and the reported ANOVA p-values are baseline checks, so no test of the intervention effect (change in IG versus CG) is shown. Non-significance would in any case not establish ineffectiveness. The IG improved by 54 m in 6MWT, 3.1 points in Berg and 6.3 points in SF-36 while the CG was flat or declined, and the same paragraph concedes a larger sample might show an effect. The conclusion is not supported by the analysis shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group (time x group) analysis of post-intervention or change scores, with confidence intervals, showing no difference.

quotes.text: Multicomponent rehabilitation was not effective in
Values obtained from the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of normality

second_reader.what_stands: The 'not effective' conclusion rests solely on non-significance, and the p-values in Table 2 come from normality (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) and variance-homogeneity (Levene) tests, so no valid between-group test of change is reported. Absence of significance in a small, high-attrition trial does not show absence of effect, and the point estimates favour the intervention (for example +61.4 m between-group difference in 6MWT change). The authors do partly soften this by calling for a larger sample, but the Conclusion's wording 'not effective' still overstates what the data show.

issues.title: IG completers fall from 31 to 12 at 24 sessions, yet Table 2 labels the IG n = 31 under 'intention-to-treat'
issues.explanation: Only 12 of the 31 intervention participants completed all 24 sessions and the final reassessment. Table 2 still labels the intervention group n = 31, and the Methods claim an intention-to-treat analysis. No missing-data method is described, so the T4 means may rest on 12 completers or on some unstated imputation. Control group follow-up is not described either. This weakens every pre-post figure in the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 2 or a supplement showing T4 outcomes were obtained for all 31 IG participants, or a described imputation method.

quotes.text: 23 completed 6 sessions and were reevaluated once; 17 completed 12 sessions and were reevaluated twice
12 completed 24 sessions and were reevaluated 4 times (Figure 2)

second_reader.what_stands: Completer numbers do fall from 31 to 12 at 24 sessions (about 61% loss), and Table 2 still shows n = 31 for the IG with T4 values, with no stated imputation or handling of the missing data. That is hard to reconcile with a true intention-to-treat analysis, which needs outcomes (observed or imputed) for everyone. The point is narrower than stated, though: the ITT claim sits in the Methods, and Table 2's header says only 'n = 31', not 'intention-to-treat'.

issues.title: Table 1: several percentages do not match their counts (9 (29.0), 8 (25.8) twice, 14 (54.9), 19 (31.7), 6 (10.6))
issues.explanation: Six percentages in Table 1 do not equal the printed count over the printed group size. The Marital status 'Other' total (9, 29.0%) should be 15.3%. The Family income 'Up to 1 MMW' and Ethnicity 'Other' totals (8, 25.8%) should both be 13.6%. The intervention group 'Other' comorbidities (14, 54.9%) should be 45.2%, and the total 'Other' (19, 31.7%) and diabetes (6, 10.6%) are slightly off (32.2% and 10.2%). These are reporting errors in a baseline table; they do not affect the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing the counts, not the percentages, are the typographical errors and the percentages are correct for a different base.

quotes.location: Table 1, Family income, Up to 1 MMW, total

script.explanation: 9/59 = 15.25%, but the paper prints 29.0, outside the rounding interval [29.00, 29.01]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 31.0 rather than 59.

issues.title: Table 1 p labels 'p ≤ 0.05' for rows with near-identical counts (e.g. diabetes 3/31 vs 3/28)
issues.explanation: Six Table 1 rows carry 'p ≤ 0.05', which would signal baseline imbalance between arms. For diabetes the arms have 3 of 31 versus 3 of 28 cases, so no significant difference is possible. The labels are never explained, and the table gives no test statistics. Readers cannot tell whether baseline balance was achieved, although the efficacy analysis is not directly affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported chi-squared statistics showing a real imbalance, or a statement that the labels are a typo for 'p ≥ 0.05'.

issues.title: Intervention-group baseline Berg: abstract 48.00 vs Table 2 48.8 (6MWT 464.40 vs 464.5)
issues.explanation: The abstract and Discussion give the intervention group's baseline Berg score as 48, but Table 2 gives 48.8. The table's own change of 3.10 matches 48.8, so the abstract figure appears to be the error. The abstract's baseline 6MWT (464.40) also differs slightly from the table's 464.5. None of this alters the non-significant findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected abstract or erratum showing that 48.00 is the true baseline mean and that Table 2's 48.8 and change of 3.10 are the typographical errors.

quotes.text: A pontuação na escala de Berg do GI foi de 48,00 + 4,00 (T0)

issues.title: Data analysis says ANOVA compared 'three groups' in a two-arm trial
issues.explanation: The Methods describe two arms, but the Data analysis section says a one-way ANOVA confirmed baseline homogeneity for three groups. No third group exists in the design or Table 2. It is probably a wording slip, but it leaves the baseline-comparison analysis unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Clarification that a third group (for example a screening or non-randomized group) was part of the baseline ANOVA.

quotes.text: one-way ANOVA was conducted to confirm initial homogeneity

10.17116/jnevro2022122081101.headline_claim: Anvifen (500 mg three times daily for 21 days) is effective for post-COVID 'brain fog', with anxiety and GABAergic mechanisms implicated, and is recommended as a pathogenetically justified treatment.
10.17116/jnevro2022122081101.overall: The headline conclusion that Anvifen is highly effective and can be recommended is not supported: it rests on an uncontrolled, open-label before-after comparison of subjective scales over 21 days, with no safety data. There are also several printing errors (impossible quartiles for FAS and SF-36 physical, baseline percentages that do not match counts). The reported improvements may well be real changes over time, but they cannot be attributed to the drug.

primary_outcome.name: unclear (no primary outcome designated; HADS anxiety, MoCA, TMT-B, FAS, sleep, SF-36 and HADS depression all analysed before/after)

issues.title: Clinical recommendation and 'high effectiveness' drawn from an uncontrolled 3-week study without safety data
issues.explanation: The authors write that Anvifen has high efficacy and recommend it as a pathogenetically justified treatment, and that the results confirm a GABA-deficiency view of the syndrome. An uncontrolled before-after comparison cannot establish efficacy or mechanism, and no adverse events are reported. The conclusion is stronger than the evidence permits.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data with safety reporting showing a benefit over placebo.

quotes.text: что позволяет рекомендовать   Анвифен как патогенетически обоснованный препарат для лечения пациентов с постковидным «туманом в голове».
Высокая эффективность агониста ГАМК-рецепторов   Анвифена в лечении пациентов с постковидным синдромом, проявляющимся «туманом в голове», подтверждает эту точку зрения

second_reader.what_stands: The paper draws a clinical recommendation and a claim of 'high effectiveness' from a 21-day uncontrolled before/after study, and reports no safety or tolerability data and no limitations. The recommendation and the 'pathogenetically justified' label go beyond what this design can support.

issues.title: Single-arm, open-label, uncontrolled 21-day study cannot attribute improvement to Anvifen
issues.explanation: All 92 patients received Anvifen and were compared only with their own baseline, with no control group, no placebo and no blinding. Symptoms of post-COVID syndrome tend to improve with time, and patient-rated scales are susceptible to expectation effects. The efficacy conclusion and treatment recommendation therefore do not follow from this design. Pre/post Wilcoxon tests on a single group (c7) and the subjective-outcome issue (c8) are the same limitation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent placebo or untreated control arm showing a between-group difference.

quotes.text: Всем пациентам назначали отечественный препарат   Анвифен
Высокая эффективность агониста ГАМК-рецепторов   Анвифена в лечении пациентов с постковидным синдромом

second_reader.what_stands: The study is single-arm and uncontrolled, with a before/after comparison of 92 patients all given Anvifen for 21 days, so improvement cannot be attributed to the drug rather than time, natural course or placebo/expectation effects. The paper does not explicitly say 'open-label', but no blinding or control is described.

issues.title: FAS post-treatment median 20 lies below its own Q1 of 23 (quartiles identical to baseline [23; 31])
issues.explanation: The post-treatment FAS row prints median 20 with interquartile range [23; 31], so the median is below the lower quartile, which is impossible for one distribution. The quartiles are identical to the baseline row, suggesting they were copied. The post-treatment FAS dispersion is therefore unreliable, and the FAS result (a key asthenia outcome) cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing the true post-treatment quartiles with a median of 20 inside them.

issues.title: Several baseline symptom percentages do not match counts of 92 (49 = 50%, 71 = 70%, 68 = 69%, 21 = 21%)
issues.explanation: Counts given in the history paragraph do not equal the printed percentages when divided by the stated 92 patients. For instance 49/92 is 53.3% not 50%, 71/92 is 77.2% not 70%, and 68/92 is 73.9% not 69%. The percentages seem to use a different, larger denominator (about 100), which the paper does not explain. This affects descriptive baseline data only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that percentages were computed on a different denominator (e.g. all eligible), or corrected counts.

quotes.text: нарушение сна (частые ночные пробуждения, раннее окончательное утреннее пробуждение) - у 49 (50%)
у 71 (70%), искажение вкуса - у 21 (21%)

script.explanation: 49/92 = 53.26%, but the paper prints 50.0, outside the rounding interval [49.50, 51.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 98.0 rather than 92.

issues.title: SF-36 physical post-treatment Q3 printed as 20, below median 53.8 and Q1 52.3
issues.explanation: The post-treatment SF-36 physical component is printed as 53.8 [52.3; 20], so the upper quartile is below the median and the lower quartile. This is almost certainly a typographical error in the upper bound. Same slip as the FAS row, which suggests the table was not carefully checked. The direction of the median change is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the printed ordering is impossible. A corrected Q3 would only fix it.

issues.title: SF-36 psychological p-value 0.00001 in abstract vs 0.0001 in Table 2
issues.explanation: The abstract and Table 2 give different p-values for the same comparison. Both are well below 0.05, so the inference is unchanged. It is a minor inconsistency. The identical p = 0.00001 across six outcomes also suggests a floor or placeholder value.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the two printings differ.

10.17116/jnevro2024124111140.headline_claim: The authors conclude that Cytoflavin reduces asthenia and normalises heart-rate-variability markers of dysautonomia in post-COVID patients, and may have a significant positive effect in complex treatment.
10.17116/jnevro2024124111140.overall: The headline claim that Cytoflavin corrects dysautonomia and is anti-asthenic is not supported: the controlled comparisons are null, the control group shows the same HRV trends, and the only positive result is a borderline within-group p=0.0498. Allocation was apparently non-random with unequal arms, and the key Table 1 contains cells copied from subgroup H and a reversed quartile pair. The descriptive HRV findings (high vagal activity in subgroups) are at best hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: MFI-20 asthenia score (within-group change, day 1 to day 35); aim was HRV and orthostatic indices

issues.title: HRV normalisation attributed to Cytoflavin though the control group showed the same trends, with no significant between-group differences
issues.explanation: The Results state that the same changes occurred in the control group and that no other significant differences were found between groups or before/after treatment. The Conclusion nonetheless reports a significant reduction in dysautonomia after Cytoflavin and normalisation of HRV indices. No significance test for the within-group HRV changes is shown, so these claims rest on comparing medians to norms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group or group-by-time test showing a significantly larger HRV change in the Cytoflavin group than in controls.

quotes.text: Описанные тенденции наблюдались и в ГС, однако показатели TP, VLF, HF были несколько выше, чем в ОГ
Других статистически значимых отличий выявлено не было как между группами, так и в результатах до и после лечения.
После курса лечения препаратом Цитофлавин у пациентов ОГ было отмечено значительное уменьшение проявлений дизавтономии.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper reports that the control group showed the same HRV trends and that there were no significant between-group or before/after differences, yet the conclusion attributes a marked reduction in dysautonomia to Cytoflavin. The larger numeric drops in OG are untested and confounded by higher baseline values, so the HRV normalisation cannot be credited to the drug from these data.

issues.title: Anti-asthenic effect claimed from a within-group p=0.0498 while the between-group comparison was null
issues.explanation: The only evidence for reduced asthenia is a before/after change in the treated group (p=0.0498, median 58.3 to 58.0). The treatment vs control comparison was not significant, and the paired test used is not described in the methods. The Conclusion nonetheless speaks of an anti-asthenic action and a significant positive effect of Cytoflavin, which the design and the data do not support. The small n (no sample-size calculation) also makes the borderline p fragile.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant between-group (or group-by-time) comparison favouring Cytoflavin on MFI-20.

quotes.text: Выявлены статистически значимые различия между показателями в 1-й и 35-й дни лечения ( p =0,0498).
При сравнении показателей ОГ и ГС статистически значимых различий выявлено не было.
Эти данные свидетельствуют о противоастеническом действии Цитофлавина у пациентов с ПКС.

second_reader.what_stands: The anti-asthenic claim rests on a within-group p of 0.0498 for a median change of 0.3 points, while the between-group comparison showed no difference and the control group's median fell by more (1.0 point). Within-group change alone cannot attribute the effect to Cytoflavin. The 0.0 lower quartiles also suggest scoring or missing-data problems that the paper does not explain.

issues.title: Table 1 (n=20) HF row, and most VLF/LF cells, repeat subgroup H (n=12) of Table 3; one TP quartile pair reversed
issues.explanation: The HF row for the whole treatment group in Table 1 is identical in all four cells to the HF row for the 12-patient high-vagal subgroup in Table 3, and many VLF, LF and TP cells are also identical or nearly so. The whole group includes 8 low-HF patients, so its median and quartiles cannot match those of subgroup H. In addition, the Table 1 rest-before TP cell reads [2594; 2107], so Q1 exceeds Q3. Table 1 is the basis for the claim that HRV indices normalised, so it needs re-checking against the source data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing that the pooled n=20 HF distribution has the same median and quartiles as subgroup H, which is arithmetically impossible given subgroup L.

quotes.location: Table 1, HF row, rest before treatment (identical cell in Table 3)
Table 1, TP row, rest before treatment
Table 3, TP row, rest before treatment

second_reader.what_stands: Most resting and standing VLF, LF and HF cells in Table 1 (n=20) are identical or near-identical to Table 3 (subgroup H, n=12), which is not arithmetically possible for the whole group when the other 8 patients have much lower values. The pre-treatment resting TP cell in Table 1 also has Q3 (2107) below Q1 (2594), so the quartile pair is reversed. I did not check which table holds the correct values.

issues.title: Cytoflavin (n=20) vs control (n=50) with no stated allocation method, concealment or blinding
issues.explanation: Patients were divided into two groups of very different size, and the paper does not say how. Without randomisation, concealment or blinding, differences between arms (or the absence of differences) may reflect baseline differences. Baseline MFI-20 is already different (58.3 vs 54.0), and no baseline comparability table is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or registration describing concealed random allocation and blinded assessment.

quotes.text: Испытуемые были разделены на две группы: основную (ОГ, n =20) и сравнения (ГС, n =50).
Пациенты ГС получали внутривенные инфузии 0,9% раствора хлорида натрия в течение 10 дней

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states that subjects were divided into two groups of 20 and 50 but gives no allocation method, concealment or blinding, and the unequal sizes with different comparator regimens suggest non-random assignment. Between-group differences are therefore open to selection and confounding.

issues.title: HF–MFI-20 correlation p=0.051 reported as statistically significant against a stated alpha of 0.05
issues.explanation: The Results give r=0.398, p=0.051 for HF, which does not meet the stated critical level of 0.05. The Discussion nonetheless lists PNS activity at rest among the significant positive correlations with asthenia. This is a small overstatement, but it feeds the interpretation that asthenia is linked to parasympathetic activity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alpha of 0.10 for correlations, or a corrected p-value below 0.05 for HF.

quotes.text: Критический уровень достоверности нулевой статистической гипотезы « p » в исследовании оставлял 0,05.

issues.title: Many HRV indices, positions and correlations tested at alpha 0.05 with no multiplicity control
issues.explanation: The paper tests numerous spectral indices, subgroup comparisons and correlations at an uncorrected 0.05 level. Borderline results such as p=0.0498 and p=0.031 would not survive any correction. This weakens secondary results more than it changes the headline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or a stated correction for multiple comparisons.

quotes.text: Критический уровень достоверности нулевой статистической гипотезы « p » в исследовании оставлял 0,05.

issues.title: No ethics approval or consent statement in the text for an interventional study of 70 patients
issues.explanation: The text supplied contains no statement of ethics committee approval or patient consent. This may reflect the journal layout, but as supplied it cannot be confirmed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ethics approval number and consent statement in the published article or its submission form.

quotes.text: Исследование проводилось в Центре изучения и лечения ПКС на базе Клиники высоких медицинских технологий им. Н.И. Пирогова СПбГУ в 2023-2024 гг.

10.17116/kurort20251020615.headline_claim: Adding transcranial electrical stimulation to pharmacotherapy (Cortexin) is an effective and pathogenetically justified component of treatment for post-COVID syndrome with neurological symptoms, chronic fatigue and cognitive decline.
10.17116/kurort20251020615.overall: The direction of the finding (TES plus Cortexin looks better than Cortexin alone on fatigue, CGI-S and cytokines) is consistent across tables. However, the open-label, no-sham comparator, the missing trial registration and randomisation details, and the unadjusted testing of six outcomes mean the confident conclusion of efficacy and pathogenetic justification is not supported by this design. The headline '95%' is also inconsistent with the paper's own 70/75 = 93.3%, and several p-values differ between abstract and body.

primary_outcome.name: Neurological status (MFI-20, MoCA, CGI-S) and plasma TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6 at 15 days; no single primary outcome designated

issues.title: Comparator is Cortexin alone with no sham stimulation or described blinding; add-on effect not isolated
issues.explanation: Only TES patients received a daily 20-30 minute device procedure, and the control arm received nothing comparable. Self-rated fatigue, clinician-rated CGI-S and cognitive testing are all open to expectation and attention effects. Blinding is not described, so the size of the effect (for example MFI-20 21.3 vs 33.2) cannot be attributed to the electrical stimulation itself.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of sham stimulation or blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: группа сравнения - только фармакотерапию
Пациенты основной группы с первого дня приема Кортексина дополнительно получали ТЭС

second_reader.what_stands: The comparator is Cortexin alone, with no sham stimulation and no blinding described (the Methods and abstract say so, and the paper does not mention masking of participants, assessors or analysts). The design therefore estimates the effect of adding an open-label TES course to Cortexin, not the specific effect of TES. Non-specific effects (attention, expectation, extra visits, subjective scales such as MFI-20, MoCA and CGI-S) are not separated, and the paper does not list this as a limitation while calling TES 'pathogenetically justified'. Note that the paper itself frames the question as an

issues.title: Abstract and Conclusion state 95% complete remission; Results and Table 2 give 70/75 = 93.3%
issues.explanation: The abstract and Conclusion say 95% of TES patients reached complete reduction of neurological manifestations. The only supporting data are the 70 of 75 CGI-S 'no symptoms' patients in Table 2, which is 93.3%. The headline figure therefore does not match the paper's own data, though the direction of the effect is unchanged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated definition of 'complete reduction' that yields 95% from a different count or denominator.

issues.title: Six outcomes, no primary or multiplicity control; MoCA, IL-1β and IL-6 results are borderline
issues.explanation: Six between-group outcomes were tested at an unadjusted 0.05 level, and no primary outcome is named. The strongest results (fatigue, CGI-S, TNF-α) would probably survive correction. The cognitive claim (MoCA p = 0.048) and the IL-1β and IL-6 findings would not, yet the Conclusion states them as established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome and hierarchical testing plan, or adjusted p-values still below 0.05.
