issues.title: Within-arm before/after comparisons use the Mann-Whitney U test, which ignores pairing
issues.explanation: The same patients were measured before and after treatment, so the within-group changes call for a paired test such as Wilcoxon signed-rank. The table notes say the independent-samples Mann-Whitney U test was used. Some printed within-group p-values (for example MoCA p = 0.036 in the TES group) do not fit the printed quartiles. These within-group p-values are secondary and the between-group claim is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that before and after samples were independent, or re-analysis with a paired test giving the same p-values.

quotes.text: p 2-1 - значимость различий в основной группе между исходными показателями и показателями после лечения ( U -критерий Манна-Уитни)

issues.title: Described as an RCT but no registration, randomisation method, concealment or sample-size rationale reported
issues.explanation: The paper reports no trial registration, so prespecification of the primary outcome and analysis cannot be checked. The randomisation method and allocation concealment are not described, and no sample-size calculation is given. For a study whose conclusion is confident efficacy, these gaps reduce confidence in the randomised design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with a prospective date and matching outcomes, and a description of randomisation and concealment.

quotes.text: рандомизировано в 2 группы (по 75 пациентов в каждой)
В соответствии с методом рандомизации пациенты были распределены на две группы по 75 человек

issues.title: Abstract p-values for CGI-S, MoCA, TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6 differ from Results and Tables 2-3
issues.explanation: For five of six outcomes the abstract prints a different between-group p-value from the Results text and tables. The differences are CGI-S 0.001 vs 0.002, MoCA 0.046 vs 0.048, TNF-α 0.003 vs 0.002, IL-1β 0.022 vs 0.020 and IL-6 0.012 vs 0.011. Each is small and none changes significance at 0.05, so this is a reporting inconsistency and not a change of conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the abstract p-values come from a different, specified comparison or analysis.

issues.title: IL-1β between-group reduction is 34.1% in Results text but 35.1% in Table 3 (same p = 0.020)
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the IL-1β difference as 34.1% and Table 3 gives 35.1%, both with p = 0.020. One of them is a transcription error. The difference is small and does not alter any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of the percentage under which both values are valid, for example different rounding of unrounded medians.

issues.title: Results text gives n=66 beside 70 (93.3%) CGI-S symptom-free TES patients; tables use n=75
issues.explanation: The Results sentence reports 70 patients (93.3%) and then gives 'n=66'. Table 2 and the rest of the paper use 75 per group, and 70/75 = 93.3%. A count of 66 is unexplained and conflicts with the stated full completion. The 93.3% only works with a denominator of 75.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An explanation of what the 66 refers to, for example a subset with a different assessment.

quotes.text: у 70 (93,3%) пациентов ( n =66)
Все включенные в исследование пациенты (основная группа и группа сравнения) завершили курс лечения.

10.17267/2238-2704rpf.2024.e5840.headline_claim: Comprehensive rehabilitation in low-resource settings effectively improves quality of life, reduces fatigue, and improves functional capacity among long-term COVID-19 survivors.
10.17267/2238-2704rpf.2024.e5840.overall: The finding that the six-week programme improved fatigue, walk distance and quality of life is plausible, but its size is unreliable: the effect sizes in the abstract (about 1.0 to 1.4) conflict with the d >8 stated in the Results and Discussion. The control arm, an active comparator, also improved, the assessor was unblinded and outcomes are largely self-reported. Claims of long-term habit formation and safety go beyond a 38-person, single-site, six-week study.

primary_outcome.name: Fatigue (FSS), EQ-5D-5L index and six-minute walk distance; no single primary outcome is designated

issues.title: Cohen's d reported as >8 in Results/Discussion but 1.37 or less in abstract for the same outcomes
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion describe a 'large effect (>8)' for fatigue, six-minute walk, EQ-5D VAS, dyspnoea and exertion. The abstract gives effect sizes of -1.23 to 1.37 for fatigue, walk and VAS. A Cohen's d above 8 means near-total separation of the groups and is implausible with change scores such as 66.27±15.17 m. The reported effect sizes cannot both be right, so the size of the between-group benefit is unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 2 and Table 3 showing that the abstract effect sizes are within-group, that the between-group values are labelled as such, and that the >8 figure comes from a documented calculation.

quotes.text: com grande efeito (>8) na fadiga
tamanho do efeito d de Cohens >8
distância percorrida no teste de caminhada de seis minutos (p < 0,0001, tamanho do efeito = 1,37)

second_reader.what_stands: The text does print 'd >8' in the Results and Discussion, which is not a valid effect-size threshold and does not match the abstract's 1.37 or lower. The most plausible explanation is a typographical omission of the decimal point (>0.8, Cohen's large-effect cut-off), so the abstract and body are not substantively contradictory. I could not check Quadro 2's actual d values because its contents were not in the supplied text.

issues.title: Abstract effect sizes appear within-group; control arm also improved, so net programme effect is unclear
issues.explanation: Between-group tests exist, but the abstract's headline p-values and effect sizes are not labelled as between-group, and the Discussion reports that the control arm also improved significantly in fatigue, walk, dyspnoea and exertion. The control was an active comparator (education plus breathing exercises), so attributing the changes to the full programme is only partly supported. The net effect of the extra components is unclear from the abstract.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 2 showing that the abstract p-values and effect sizes are between-group comparisons of change or endpoint values, adjusted for baseline.

quotes.text: O grupo controle também apresentou melhorias significativas na fadiga, TC6, dispneia em repouso e PSE em repouso
Melhorias significativas foram observadas na fadiga (p = 0,006, tamanho do efeito = -1,23)

issues.title: Outcome assessor unblinded and primary outcomes self-reported; participant blinding stated but not explained
issues.explanation: The authors say the outcome assessor was not blinded. The fatigue and quality-of-life outcomes depend on patient report, and the six-minute walk is effort-dependent with verbal encouragement. Participants in a supervised exercise arm are hard to blind. Expectation and assessment bias could inflate the between-group differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of how participants and assessors were blinded, or objective outcomes assessed by an independent blinded rater.

quotes.text: Os participantes foram cegados.
o avaliador do resultado não foi

issues.title: Claim of long-term sustained exercise habits rests on six-week outcomes with no follow-up
issues.explanation: Outcomes were measured only at baseline and six weeks, and the authors admit that long-term follow-up was not done. The Discussion nevertheless says the exercises promote sustained exercise habits over the long term. Habit persistence was not measured, so this is speculation presented as a finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up data showing continued exercise adherence and outcomes beyond the six-week intervention.

quotes.text: promovendo hábitos de exercício sustentados entre os participantes a longo prazo
quotes.location: 4. Discussão, penultimate paragraph before control-group paragraph

quotes.text: o acompanhamento de longo prazo dos participantes não foi feito

issues.title: Conclusions call the programme efficient and safe in low-resource settings from one site, n=38, six weeks
issues.explanation: Safety is supported only by a statement that no adverse events occurred, with no described monitoring method. Generalisation to low-resource settings generally comes from one outpatient department. The firm wording of the conclusions is stronger than a small single-centre trial supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified adverse-event monitoring protocol, or replication in multiple sites with larger samples.

quotes.text: pode ser aplicado de forma eficiente e segura em ambientes com poucos recursos.
Não houveram desistências ou quaisquer eventos adversos.

issues.title: CTRI number suggests July 2022 registration; study dated March 2022 to August 2023, enrolment start not given
issues.explanation: The registry ID implies registration in July 2022, but the paper dates the study from March 2022 and the trial's 'planned and conducted' span includes planning. Whether recruitment began before registration cannot be settled from the paper. If it did, registration was retrospective and outcome switching cannot be ruled out.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The registry record showing a registration date before the first participant was enrolled.

quotes.text: O estudo foi planejado e realizado de março de 2022 a agosto de 2023.

issues.title: Unedited placeholder inside the main between-group claim in the Discussion
issues.explanation: The sentence stating the main finding contains the placeholder '[Pontuações melhores ou piores? inserir aqui nesse espaço]' (better or worse scores? insert here). This shows the claim was not finalised and leaves unclear whether the scores improved or worsened. It also sits beside the unexplained d >8.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the text is in the paper as printed.

quotes.text: [Pontuações melhores ou piores? inserir aqui nesse espaço]

10.17267/2238-2704rpf.2025.e6078.headline_claim: Ten sessions of respiratory and motor physical therapy were associated with significant reduction in persistent symptoms and recovery of functional parameters in symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients, supporting structured rehabilitation programmes in similar services.
10.17267/2238-2704rpf.2025.e6078.overall: The within-patient improvements in a 26-patient completer sample are plausible as descriptive findings, but with no control group, selective inclusion of 26 of 63 referred patients, unblinded and partly subjective outcomes, and unadjusted multiple testing, the causal conclusion of 'efficacy' is not supported. The conclusion stands only as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Presence of persistent symptoms (identified at first assessment and still present at last)

issues.title: Single-arm pre-post study (n=26, no control) used to claim efficacy of rehabilitation
issues.explanation: All patients received physiotherapy and were compared with their own baseline about 47 days earlier, with no comparison group. Natural recovery from post-COVID symptoms over 7 weeks, regression to the mean, and the authors' own note that many patients already reported spontaneous improvement cannot be separated from treatment. Despite acknowledging this, the conclusion says the results 'reinforce the efficacy' of the service, which the design cannot support. Because only completers (those who stayed on for 10 sessions) were analysed and the outcomes are mostly subjective or effort-dependent, the same problem extends to the other design flags (completer-only analysis, within-group inference, unblinded outcomes); they are folded into this issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical untreated comparison group showing smaller change over the same interval.

quotes.text: Esses achados reforçam a eficácia de um serviço especializado  de  reabilitação  para  otimizar  ganhos funcionais
a ausência de grupo controle é uma limitação  importante  de  estudos  quase-experimentais

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm pre-post design (n=26, completers only, no control group), and the Conclusões say the findings 'reforçam a eficácia' of rehabilitation, which a design without a comparator cannot establish because spontaneous recovery, regression to the mean, learning effects on functional tests and completer selection are not separable from treatment. It is only partly a problem because the authors explicitly acknowledge the lack of a control group, selection bias and self-report bias in the Discussão and call for randomised trials; the issue is the mismatch between that caution and

issues.title: About a dozen outcomes tested at nominal p<0.05 with no multiplicity control; p=0.025 and 0.006-0.008 fragile
issues.explanation: The methods list many outcomes and use p<0.05 as the only threshold, with no correction or pre-specified primary outcome among the functional tests. With about 12 tests, a Bonferroni threshold would be about 0.004, which the fatigue scale (0.025), cough (0.008), fatigue complaint (0.006), 30-s sit-to-stand (0.006) and 2-min step test (0.006) would not meet. The weakest results are therefore secondary and tentative, while the smallest p-values would likely survive.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that tests were pre-specified as exploratory, or a corrected analysis showing the same results survive.

quotes.text: Valores de p < 0,05 foram considerados significantes.
escala de fadiga ( p =0,025) e teste de apneia ( p =0,001)

issues.title: Stated primary outcome (persistent symptoms) is not reported as such; headline results are secondary outcomes
issues.explanation: The Methods define the primary outcome as persistence of symptoms from first to last assessment and the secondary outcomes as changes in functional parameters. The abstract and Results headline mostly the functional tests (strength, TUG, sit-to-stand, step test, apnoea) and individual symptom p-values, with no persistence proportion given in the text. Readers cannot see the pre-specified primary result, and the conclusion rests on secondary outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 1A or a supplementary table reporting the proportion of patients with persistent symptoms with an accompanying test.

quotes.text: o desfe -cho primário foi a presença de sintomas persistentes (identificados na primeira avaliação e ainda presen -tes na última)
Os desfechos secundários foram as va -riações em parâmetros funcionais entre a avaliação inicial e a final.

issues.title: Text gives 19.2% ventilated 'among hospitalised'; Table 1 implies 5/10 = 50% (19.2% is 5/26)
issues.explanation: The Results text says that among hospitalised patients 19.2% used mechanical ventilation. Table 1 lists 10 hospitalised and 5 ventilated, so the share among hospitalised is 50%; 19.2% is 5 of all 26 patients. The same applies to the 11.5% for O2 catheter (3/26, not 3/10). This is a wording error in the text and the table itself is consistent; the main conclusions do not depend on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the percentages were intended as shares of the whole cohort (the text's 'among the hospitalised' being loose wording) would reduce this to a wording slip only.

script.explanation: 5/10 = 50.00%, but the paper prints 19.2, outside the rounding interval [19.15, 19.30]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 26.0 rather than 10.

10.17294/2330-0698.2128.headline_claim: The authors conclude that behavioral health treatment for long-COVID, here a mindfulness-based virtual group program, is feasible and has the potential to improve symptoms.
10.17294/2330-0698.2128.overall: The data show no change in depression and a non-significant fall in anxiety in eight self-selected patients with no comparator. They cannot support a claim of efficacy, and the benefit-oriented conclusion is stronger than the results allow. The study is best read as a small feasibility report, and the limitations are largely disclosed.

primary_outcome.name: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 (no single primary outcome designated)

issues.title: Single-group pre-post design (n=8) with uncontrolled psychotherapy and medication cannot attribute change to the program
issues.explanation: All eight participants received the program and were compared only with their own baseline. Six of eight were already on psychotropic medication, and individual psychotherapy could not be ascertained, so any change in GAD-7 could come from those treatments, time, or regression to the mean. The paper frames the work as examining efficacy, which this design cannot establish.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control or waitlist arm, or data showing that co-interventions were stable and unchanged across the study period.

quotes.text: Using this single group, pre-intervention, post-intervention repeated measures design
we do not know if individual psychotherapy is responsible for the decrease in anxiety scores

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is a single-group pre-post study of 8 people with no control arm, and it does not measure psychotherapy and only partly addresses medication, so any change cannot be attributed to the program. The authors do acknowledge this for individual psychotherapy and the anxiety change, but not for medication, and 'efficacy' wording in the Discussion goes further than the design allows.

issues.title: Benefit framing ('potential to improve symptoms') exceeds null PHQ-9 and non-significant GAD-7 results in 8 patients
issues.explanation: The PHQ-9 median was unchanged (11 to 11, p=0.906) and the GAD-7 decrease was not significant (p=0.227). With no control group and n=8, the data neither show nor exclude benefit. The conclusion and recap nonetheless say the program may improve neuropsychiatric symptoms, and the anxiety 'downward trend' is treated as supportive. The small sample is disclosed as a limitation, but the headline wording does not reflect it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A controlled analysis or larger sample showing a significant improvement, or conclusions limited to feasibility and hypothesis generation.

quotes.text: potential to improve symptoms
may improve neuropsychiatric symptoms in long-COVID
downward trend

second_reader.what_stands: The depression result is null and the anxiety result non-significant in 8 uncontrolled patients, so statements that the program 'may improve' or has 'potential to improve' symptoms are more favourable than the data support, especially in the Patient-Friendly Recap, which omits the null results. The Discussion does state that no significant improvement was found, blames the small sample, and asks for further research, so the framing is overstated rather than unqualified.

10.17650/1726-9784-2021-22-4-68-76.headline_claim: BESTFertil taken for 12 weeks produced a more pronounced recovery of semen parameters and resolution of post-COVID asthenic syndrome than no treatment in men after COVID-19.
10.17650/1726-9784-2021-22-4-68-76.overall: The headline claim of more pronounced semen recovery and asthenia resolution with BESTFertil is only weakly supported: most between-group semen comparisons are non-significant, and several effects are inferred from within-group tests in an open-label, unadjusted trial of 60 men. The asthenia result is nominally significant but subjective and unblinded. Conclusions should be read as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: not stated (semen parameters and asthenic syndrome scale both reported)

issues.title: TMSC benefit inferred from within-group p=0.032 vs 0.317; between-group TMSC comparison p=0.208
issues.explanation: The paper says only treated patients improved total motile sperm count, based on a significant within-group Wilcoxon test (p=0.032) versus a non-significant one in controls (p=0.317). The direct between-group comparison at visit 2 is not significant (p=0.208), and no baseline-adjusted or change-score comparison is given. The claimed treatment-specific TMSC improvement is therefore not shown by the data. Baselines also differ (median 48.5 vs 39.8 million), and the control group rose too.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified baseline-adjusted or change-score between-group test of TMSC showing a significant treatment effect.

quotes.text: Однако только у  пациентов, принимавших БЕСТФертил на протяжении 3 мес, наблюдалось улучшение по общему количеству подвижных сперматозоидов

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that improvement in TMSC occurred 'only' on BESTFertil rests on one within-group p-value being below 0.05 and the other above it. The one direct between-group comparison (Table 4) gives p = 0.208, and no test of change between groups is reported, so the data do not show a TMSC benefit specific to BESTFertil.

issues.title: 'More pronounced recovery of semen parameters' claimed; only volume differs between groups (p=0.042 of 7)
issues.explanation: The abstract conclusion says treated patients had more pronounced recovery of semen parameters. Of seven between-group comparisons at visit 2, only ejaculate volume is nominally significant (p=0.042), with no multiplicity adjustment, and the others are p=0.070 to 0.968. The main text itself says recovery occurred in both groups, so the stronger abstract wording is not supported. The TMSC-specific claim is covered under c1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Adjusted between-group analyses showing consistent significant advantages across semen parameters.

quotes.text: Постепенное восстановление показателей спермограммы отмечалось как у пациентов, принимавших, так и у пациентов, не принимавших БЕСТФертил.

second_reader.what_stands: Bullet 2 itself is appropriately worded (recovery in both groups), but the abstract and Discussion claim a more pronounced recovery with BESTFertil, and the between-group comparison supports this only for ejaculate volume (p = 0.042, unadjusted for 7 tests). The other six parameters, including progressive motility (p = 0.070) and TMSC (p = 0.208), show no significant difference between groups.

issues.title: Asthenia benefit rests on open-label, self-completed scale with no placebo (Fisher p=0.017)
issues.explanation: Patients knew whether they took the supplement and completed the asthenic condition scale themselves. The between-group difference in proportion with asthenia (p=0.017) could reflect expectation as well as a drug effect. The conclusion that asthenic syndrome was resolved is stated without this caveat, and the scale is not described as validated. The between-group test is on a dichotomised proportion, with a single non-adjusted p.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded or placebo-controlled replication, or objective validation of the scale for this setting.

quotes.text: Тип исследования: рандомизированное проспективное контролируемое клиническое испытание без ослепления.
С помощью точного теста Фишера было продемонстрировано  статистически  значимое  различие  между 1-й и 2-й группами по доле пациентов с признаками астенического состояния

second_reader.what_stands: The paper confirms that the trial was open-label, with no placebo or sham comparator, and that the asthenia outcome is a questionnaire completed by patients, so the Fisher p = 0.017 could reflect expectation or reporting effects and the paper does not weigh this as a limitation. I could not verify the Fisher result itself because the counts are in figures not available in the text, so the open-label vulnerability is established but not the absence of a true effect.

issues.title: Randomization method undescribed; baseline DNA fragmentation differs (21.2% vs 15.5%), no adjustment
issues.explanation: The paper calls the trial randomized but gives no sequence generation or concealment. Baseline DNA fragmentation was 21.2% in group 1 versus 15.5% in group 2, and the authors admit groups were not standardised. Regression to the mean could then explain the larger fall in group 1. The paper discloses this in the discussion but the abstract still presents the fall as a treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Description of a valid randomization procedure plus baseline-adjusted analysis showing the DFI effect persists.

quotes.text: стандартизация групп по  спермиологическим показателям не производилась.
Во 2-й группе на момент 1-го визита медиана этого показателя составила 15,5 % (МКР: 8,4)

issues.title: DNA fragmentation benefit claimed from within-group test; no between-group test reported (13.9 vs 14.9%)
issues.explanation: The abstract highlights the DFI decrease in group 1 (p=0.007) versus a non-significant change in group 2. No between-group comparison is given, and the end values are almost identical. The apparent effect is largely explained by the higher starting value in group 1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test of final DFI, or baseline-adjusted analysis, showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: а на момент 2-го визита снизилась до 13,9 % (МКР: 7,55), причем это различие было статистически значимым ( p = 0,007).

10.17816/568265.headline_claim: Ambulatory rehabilitation that includes hydrobalneotherapy (hydromassage, Biolong baths or sodium-chloride baths, combined with exercise therapy) produces positive dynamics and a reduction in allostatic load in post-COVID patients, supporting non-drug correction of post-COVID disorders.
10.17816/568265.overall: The headline claim that hydrobalneotherapy-based rehabilitation improved post-COVID complaints, function and allostatic load is only weakly supported. The control arm is a self-selected untreated group despite the 'randomized' label, and efficacy is inferred from uncorrected within-group pre-post changes with no between-group analysis. There are also reporting errors in the allostatic-load percentages, the Table 1 p-values and the ethics timeline, so the numerical results should be treated cautiously.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome prespecified; reported outcomes include complaint frequency, allostatic load index, spirometry, 6-minute walk, stress hormones and psychological scales

checklist.control: untreated comparison group, not randomized (patients who did not receive rehabilitation for various reasons)

issues.title: Control arm is patients who did not get rehabilitation 'for various reasons', despite a 'randomized' label
issues.explanation: The abstract says 160 patients were randomized to 4 groups of 40. The methods describe the control group as patients who, for various reasons, did not receive the rehabilitation course. That is a self-selected or non-equivalent comparator. Randomization method, concealment, blinding and baseline comparability of the control arm are not described. Attribution of changes in complaints, psychological scores and allostatic load to hydrobalneotherapy is therefore weak.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of true random allocation (including to the control arm) with concealment, and a baseline table showing the control arm is comparable.

quotes.text: по разным причинам не получившие курса реабилитационных мероприятий
Пациенты рандомизированы на 4 группы по 40 человек
Выполнено  проспективное  когортное  исследование в параллельных группах.

second_reader.what_stands: The control arm is described as patients who did not receive rehabilitation 'for various reasons', and the study is called a prospective cohort study, so the control arm does not appear to have been formed by randomization despite the 'randomized' wording in the Abstract and Methods. The paper does not say how controls were selected or why they did not get treatment, so the claim of randomization of all four groups is unsupported and the comparability of the control arm is unclear, but the paper's wording does not show how the control group was in fact formed beyond this.

issues.title: Efficacy rests on uncorrected within-arm pre-post tests across ~20 outcomes; no between-group test of change
issues.explanation: Benefit is inferred from Wilcoxon tests of pre versus post change within arms, and from changes being significant in treated arms but not in the control arm. No between-arm comparison of change, effect sizes or confidence intervals are given. Complaints, spirometry, 6-minute walk, hormones, enzymes, ejection fraction and several psychological and cognitive scales were all tested with no primary outcome or multiplicity correction. The conclusions then read the pre-post changes as an effect of the course. Pre-post change alone cannot separate treatment from natural recovery after COVID.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-arm comparison of changes (with correction for multiple outcomes) showing the treated arms differ from the control arm.

quotes.text: сравнение двух зависимых выборок
В контрольной группе значимой динамики жалоб не выявлено

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy claims rest on within-arm pre-post Wilcoxon or McNemar tests across roughly 20 or more outcomes, with no multiplicity correction or stated alpha, and no reported between-group test of change, even though the control arm's lack of significant change is used as the contrast. The Methods list Mann-Whitney, but no between-arm comparison of change scores is reported in the Results. Table 1 does not say which arm each row belongs to.

issues.title: Post-rehab allostatic-load shares impossible for n=40 (1,25%); Biolong sums to 103,75%, control to 98,75%
issues.explanation: Both groups have 40 patients, so each share must be a multiple of 2.5%, and 1,25% would be half a patient. The Biolong post-rehabilitation shares (1,25 + 32,5 + 50 + 20) add up to 103,75%. The control shares (22,5 + 30 + 45 + 1,25) add up to 98,75%, but the 1,25% there is the 'no load' category and looks like a typo for 2,5%. The post-rehabilitation allostatic-load distributions, which feed the conclusion that load fell, are therefore misprinted. The Biolong figures cannot be repaired from the text alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or figure 3 showing integer patient counts per category that sum to 40 in each group.

quotes.text: очень высокой нагрузкой - 1,25%
лица с отсутствием аллостатической нагрузки составили 1,25%

issues.title: Table 1: Z=-1,3 reported with p=0,05 (two-sided p≈0.19); Z=-2,3 with p=0,01 (≈0.02)
issues.explanation: In Table 1, Bass-Perry physical aggression has Z = -1,3 and p = 0,05. A two-sided p for this Z is about 0.19, so the change is not significant. The text nevertheless lists decreased physical aggression among the improvements. The Beck depression row has Z = -2,3 with p = 0,01, but the two-sided p is about 0.02. Several other rows also print p-values that do not match their Z, though rounding of Z may explain some of them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Output showing a Wilcoxon Z near -1.96 for this scale, or a statement that these p-values are one-sided or adjusted.

quotes.text: Физическая агрессия

script.explanation: The printed z = -1.3 supports p no smaller than 0.161513, but the paper reports p = 0.05 -- more significance than the statistic earns at its printed precision.

issues.title: Allostatic load reduction reported as significant with no test, using an in-house quartile-based index
issues.explanation: The allostatic load index is built from five domains using quartile deviations and locally defined bands. Only category percentages are shown for before and after, with no statistical test of the shift. The conclusion nevertheless describes a significant reduction. The index is not validated in this paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A paired and between-group test of the allostatic load index (or its categories), plus validation of the index in a comparable cohort.

issues.title: Ethics approval dated 24 May 2023, after the study period (Sept 2021 to March 2023) ended
issues.explanation: The study is stated to have been conducted from September 2021 to March 2023. The local ethics committee approved the protocol on 24 May 2023, after enrolment and data collection. The paper does not explain whether this was retrospective approval. This affects the reliability of the ethics statement, not the numerical results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of earlier ethics approval, or a corrected study period.

issues.title: Baseline repolarisation disorder printed as 5,6% overall but 8,1% 'before rehabilitation' in the treated groups
issues.explanation: The baseline for the whole cohort is 5,6%, but the 'before rehabilitation' comparator for the treated groups is 8,1%. A subset cannot have a higher count than the whole cohort. 8,1% also equals the bradycardia rate, which suggests the wrong figure was carried over. The claimed improvement from 8,1% to 2,5% is therefore not reliably stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing repolarisation disorders in about 13 of the treated patients at baseline, together with a corrected whole-cohort rate.

10.17816/acen.1358.headline_claim: Alpha-rhythm EEG biofeedback has advantages over non-feedback psychological practices in reducing general asthenia and improving verbal recall and working memory, and may be used at the outpatient stage of post-COVID rehabilitation.
10.17816/acen.1358.overall: The paper is a small, single-centre pilot (10 per arm) whose headline claim of biofeedback advantages rests on three nominal differences among about 35 uncorrected tests, one of which has an internally inconsistent p-value. Both arms improved similarly on most measures, authors from the device maker are not declared as conflicts, and the study start predates the ethics approval date. The conclusions about advantages and home use are tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: not designated; between-group comparison of change scores across all measures

issues.title: Three nominal between-group p-values (0.019-0.036) among ~35 uncorrected outcomes support 'advantages' of biofeedback
issues.explanation: The paper compared change scores on about 35 outcomes and subscales with alpha 0.05 and no correction. Only three between-group differences reached p between 0.019 and 0.036, and none would survive even a modest correction. The Conclusion nonetheless states that biofeedback has advantages for asthenia, recall and working memory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome and a multiplicity-adjusted analysis in which the asthenia, recall and N-back differences remain significant.

quotes.text: Динамика по всем остальным измеряемым параметрам была сопоставима в обеих группах.
Уровень статистической значимости  принят  равным  0,05.
БОСтерапия имеет преимущества в снижении общей астении

second_reader.what_stands: Three nominal p-values (0.019-0.036) among about 39 uncorrected between-group comparisons, with no primary outcome, are about what chance alone would give (about 2 expected). They do not firmly support the Conclusion's statement that biofeedback 'has advantages'. The paper's own Discussion notes that non-specific effects may explain part of the findings, but it never mentions multiplicity.

issues.title: Two authors are device-maker executives and the company supplied device and sham software, yet 'no conflicts' declared
issues.explanation: The CEO and a product manager of Neurobotics are co-authors on a trial of Neurobotics' own headset and programme, and the company produced the sham version used in the control arm. The Conflict of Interest section nevertheless declares no conflicts, and the funding statement says there was no external support. This is a material omission for a trial whose conclusions favour the product.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A conflict-of-interest statement or journal correction acknowledging the authors' Neurobotics employment and the company's in-kind support.

quotes.text: Авторы заявляют об отсутствии явных и потенциальных конфликтов интересов, связанных с публикацией настоящей статьи.
Гарнитура  и  программа  были предоставлены  в  безвозмездное  пользование.
Vladimir A. Konyshev -Chief Executive Officer, Neurobotics LLC,

second_reader.what_stands: Two authors are employed by the company that makes the device and wrote its software (one is the CEO, the other a product manager, so 'executives' slightly overstates the second). The company also supplied the active and sham software. The paper nevertheless declares no explicit or potential conflicts. The affiliations are visible, so nothing is hidden, but the declaration does not match the disclosed relationships.

issues.title: Same Mann-Whitney U = 25.5 (n = 10 vs 10) given p = 0.036 for recall deltas but p = 0.063 in Table 2
issues.explanation: For the 10-words immediate-recall comparison, the between-group delta test is reported as U = 25.5, p = 0.036. In Table 2 the same U = 25.5 with the same group sizes corresponds to p = 0.063, and U = 26 to p = 0.075. Similarly, U = 23.5 is given p = 0.034 although U = 22 gives p = 0.035 in Table 2, which should not be possible for a larger U. The recall 'advantage' may therefore not be significant at 0.05.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw delta data showing tie structure that yields p = 0.036 at U = 25.5 for this comparison, or a corrected U or p value.

quotes.text: Тест «10 слов», объём непосредственного воспроизведения
quotes.location: Table 2, row with U = 25,5 and p = 0,063

second_reader.what_stands: The same U = 25.5 with n = 10 vs 10 is reported with p = 0.063 (Table 2, baseline) and p = 0.036 (delta comparison). That is literally true. It can be reconciled only if the delta data have heavy ties, which the paper does not show, and the 0.036 result cannot be checked from the printed data. Whether it is an error cannot be determined, but the unexplained mismatch weakens confidence in the one nominal significant result for immediate recall.

issues.title: n = 10 per arm, no sample-size calculation; 'comparable efficacy' inferred from non-significance
issues.explanation: The authors acknowledge the small samples and lack of a power calculation. With 10 per arm, non-significant between-group results are uninformative about equivalence, yet the Conclusion describes 'comparable efficacy' of the two protocols. The limitation is disclosed, but the wording of the Conclusion still reads non-significance as similarity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified equivalence margin with confidence intervals showing the two arms to be equivalent.

quotes.text: отсутствие предварительного расчёта статистической мощности и размера требуемой выборки
При сопоставимой эффективности БОС-тренинга по α-ритму ЭЭГ и психологических практик без обратной связи

issues.title: Study period starts June 2022, four months before the ethics approval dated 19.10.2022
issues.explanation: The Methods say the study ran from June 2022 to June 2024, but the ethics committee protocol is dated 19 October 2022. The paper does not state when the first patient was enrolled, so it cannot be determined whether anyone was recruited or treated before approval. The discrepancy should be clarified by the authors.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the June 2022 date refers to preparatory work and that all enrolment began after 19 October 2022.

quotes.text: в период с июня 2022 г. по июнь 2024 г.

issues.title: Conclusion suggests home use; all sessions were outpatient clinic-based and sham arm improved on most scales
issues.explanation: The Conclusion extends applicability to home settings, though no home training was tested. The authors' own Discussion says the sham exercises had an independent effect and that the biofeedback results may partly reflect non-specific factors. The wording is hedged, so this is a modest overreach.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data from a home-based arm or a framing of home use explicitly as a hypothesis for future work.

quotes.text: в том числе в домашних условиях
данные, полученные при применении БОС-терапии, могут быть частично объяснены неспецифическим воздействием применяемых упражнений

issues.title: Reduced health anxiety presented as biofeedback-specific from within-arm significance; between-arm deltas comparable
issues.explanation: The abstract lists reduced health anxiety as a finding in the biofeedback group, and the Results contrast it with the control group where it was not significant. A difference between 'significant' and 'not significant' is not a test of a difference between arms. The paper's own between-group delta comparison found all other parameters comparable, so no biofeedback-specific health-anxiety effect is shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant group-by-time or delta comparison for SHAI total score favouring biofeedback.

quotes.text: В основной группе также отмечено снижение тревоги о здоровье и улучшение параметров запоминания информации.

quotes.location: Results, Within-group dynamics of emotional state

10.17816/rjpbr109501.headline_claim: Interval normobaric hypo-hyperoxic training added to standard rehabilitation improved cardiorespiratory and autonomic indices in post-COVID patients, with the effect reported as sustained for 3 to 6 months.
10.17816/rjpbr109501.overall: The reported before/after changes in the training arm may be real, but the design (small, open-label, unequal arms, no between-group test, no sample-size calculation, many uncorrected outcomes) cannot show that the training caused them. The claims of confirmed efficacy, 3-6-month durability and preventive use are not supported by the data shown, and a table-versus-text discrepancy on control-group SBP further weakens the comparison. The conclusion is tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Spirometry (FVC, FEV1, PEF and related flow indices) and circulatory indicators (Hb, HR, BP, SaO2, stroke and minute volume), before vs after the course

issues.title: Efficacy concluded from within-arm before/after tests; no between-group comparison of change reported
issues.explanation: All tables mark significance against each arm's own baseline (Wilcoxon). No between-group test of change is shown, although the paper states the effect of the training and calls efficacy 'confirmed'. The control arm also changed on several measures (SBP, HR, SaO2 up about 2 points, Hb up about 7 g/L), and baseline-to-follow-up improvement can arise from regression to the mean, concurrent care or natural recovery. With 30 versus 20 open-label patients, the specific effect of the training is not established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis of change scores or an ANCOVA showing significant differences in favour of the training arm.

quotes.text: Сравнение двух связанных выборок (до и после лечения) проведено по критерию Вилкоксона.
При этом перечисленные изменения были достоверны лишь у пациентов основной группы (табл. 1).

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from significant within-arm before/after tests (Wilcoxon) in the main group versus non-significance in the comparison group; no between-group comparison of change or of post-treatment values is reported, despite Mann-Whitney being named in the methods. Notably SBP improved significantly in both arms by similar amounts.

issues.title: Pilot of 50 open-label patients (no sample-size calculation) 'confirms' efficacy and suggests prevention
issues.explanation: The study is a small unblinded pilot with unequal arms (30 vs 20), no sample-size calculation, no stated registration and no between-group test. Even so, the Discussion and Conclusion say the results confirmed efficacy. The final sentence extends this to preventing viral infection, treating viral pneumonia and reducing infection severity, none of which was studied. The evidence supports at most a hypothesis-generating signal in a post-COVID rehabilitation population.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the study was designed and powered for efficacy and for preventive endpoints, or that infection outcomes were collected.

quotes.text: Результаты проведённого исследования подтвердили эффективность использования нормобарической интервальной гипо-гипероксической тренировки
Метод ИГГТ может быть эффективным в профилактике вирусной инфекции, реабилитации после вирусной пневмонии, а также в снижении тяжести вирусной инфекции в случае заражения.
Размер выборки предварительно не рассчитывался.

second_reader.what_stands: A 50-patient open-label pilot without sample-size calculation is described as having 'confirmed' efficacy, and the final paragraph suggests usefulness in prevention, reducing infection severity and pneumonia rehabilitation, none of which were studied. The authors do label it a pilot and call for a larger RCT, but the 'confirmed' and prevention statements are not supported by the data presented.

issues.title: 'Lasting' benefit for 3 to 6 months stated in abstract, but no follow-up data are reported
issues.explanation: Tables 1-4 give only baseline and end-of-course values. The abstract conclusion says the improvement persisted 3 to 6 months, and the Summary refers to unspecified 'distant studies'. Only a statement that no adverse events occurred is given for the 6-month period. The durability claim is not supported by the presented data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up measurements at 3 and 6 months for both arms with the number of patients examined.

quotes.text: сохраняющееся от 3 до 6 мес после завершения комплексной реабилитации
по данным отдалённых исследований, сохранялся от 3 до 6 мес

second_reader.what_stands: The claim of a benefit persisting 3 to 6 months is not backed by any reported follow-up outcome data; all presented results are from immediately before and after the course. A 6-month follow-up is mentioned in the methods, so follow-up may have happened, but its results are not shown, and the Conclusion itself asks for longer observation.

issues.title: Control-group systolic BP fall (137.34 to 126.33) is marked p<0.01 in Table 2 but called only a trend in the text
issues.explanation: The Results text says the comparison group showed only a tendency toward lower systolic pressure. Table 2 marks the same control-group change with ** (p<0.01). One of the two is wrong. If the table is right, the control group improved on systolic BP by about as much as the treated group, which undercuts the claim that this improvement is specific to the training.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An erratum or the raw data showing that the control-group SBP change was not significant, with ** a typesetting error.

quotes.text: тенденция улучшения показателя систолического давления

quotes.location: Table 2, systolic BP row, control group after course

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes tested at uncorrected p<0.05; exact p-values mostly not given
issues.explanation: Spirometry, haemodynamics, blood gases and about eight HRV indices are all judged at p<0.05 with no correction and no designated single primary outcome. Several results are marked only with a single asterisk. Some chance findings are therefore plausible. Whether any headline result would fail correction cannot be settled because exact p-values are not reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Exact p-values showing that the key outcomes remain significant after Holm or Bonferroni correction, or a stated single primary outcome.

quotes.text: Различия считались достоверными при p <0,05.
отмечена достоверная ( p <0,049) динамика показателей жизненной ёмкости лёгких

issues.title: Author from a company, with prior work promoting the hypoxicator type used; 'no competing interests' declared
issues.explanation: One author is affiliated with Cellgim-Rus Ltd. and wrote a review justifying the creation of a new hypoxicator generation (hypooxy-1). The trial used a 'GIPO-OKSI-1' hypoxia-hyperoxia device. The paper declares no competing interests and does not explain the company's role. Readers cannot tell whether the company has a stake in the device or the result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the company has no commercial link to the device or the study and the author has no financial interest in it.

quotes.text: ООО «Селлджим-Рус», Москва, Российская Федерация
justification for the creation of a new generation of hypoxicator hypooxy-1

10.17816/rjpbr628759.headline_claim: Medical rehabilitation combining sequential transcerebral microPolarization (MPGM) and diencephalic stimulation (DESGM), with drug support, is the most effective option for dyscirculatory encephalopathy associated with post-COVID syndrome.
10.17816/rjpbr628759.overall: The conclusion that sequential electrotherapy is the most effective arm is not supported, because only within-group pre/post tests are reported and no between-group outcome comparison is made. The open-label design, subjective outcomes, absent registration and uncorrected multiple tests further reduce confidence; the data support only that all three arms improved from baseline.

primary_outcome.name: Clinical symptom scores (VAS) and neuropsychological test scores

issues.title: Superiority claim rests on within-group Wilcoxon tests; no between-group outcome test reported
issues.explanation: Each arm's change from baseline was tested with a paired Wilcoxon test, and Mann-Whitney was used only to confirm baseline similarity. Differences between arms are inferred from which arms reached p<0.05 and from fold-changes. A significant change in one arm and a non-significant change in another does not show the arms differ. The comparative claim, and the interpretation of the symptom-specific effects of each modality, is therefore not supported by any reported test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis of post-treatment or change scores (ANCOVA or Kruskal-Wallis with post hoc tests) showing group 3 superior.

quotes.text: Подтверждение отсутствия различий между рандомизированными  группами  пациентов  получено  непараметрическим критерием Манна-Уитни.
в группе сравнения 1 - в 1,1-1,5 раза, в группе сравнения 2 - в 1,2-1,8 раза

second_reader.what_stands: The Mann-Whitney test is described only as a baseline-equivalence check, and no between-group test of outcomes (e.g. post-treatment values, change scores, or an ANCOVA adjusted for baseline) is described or reported. The conclusion that the sequential therapy is 'most effective compared with MPGM and DESGM alone' therefore rests on within-group Wilcoxon tests and on comparing the pattern of significant asterisks and fold changes across groups. The undefined '#' symbol on two rows is the only hint of a between-group comparison and is not explained in the footnote. This is a limitation of the in

issues.title: Open-label design with patient-rated VAS outcomes and no sham or blinded assessment
issues.explanation: The paper states the trial was open-label and the main symptom outcomes are patient-rated visual analogue scores. No blinded outcome assessor and no limitation discussion are given. Expectation effects could inflate improvements, particularly for a novel combined technique, which could favour the more elaborate arm.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation that outcome assessors were blinded or that neuropsychological testing was done by blinded raters.

issues.title: About 17 outcomes × 3 arms tested at uncorrected p<0.05, no primary outcome
issues.explanation: Nine symptom VAS scores and eight neuropsychological scales, each tested in three arms, were evaluated at an unadjusted 0.05 level without a designated primary outcome. Some isolated significant results could arise by chance. The practical weight is modest because most arms show many consistent improvements.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis.

issues.title: Participants who withdrew for adverse effects were dropped from analysis; group sizes still stated as 46 and 48
issues.explanation: Two patients in group 2 and one in group 3 left because of discomfort and were excluded from the statistical sample, yet the tables label n=46 and n=48, the original assignment numbers. Excluding dropouts due to adverse events from the analysis favours the interventions and is inconsistent with the stated group sizes. No intention-to-treat analysis is described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing that 46 and 48 are the analysed numbers after exclusions.

quotes.text: В дальнейшем они отказались  от  участия  в  исследовании  и  были  исключены из статистической выборки.

issues.title: Table 2 STAI reactive anxiety, group 2 baseline: median 52 lies outside its bracket [55; 60]
issues.explanation: The group 2 baseline reactive anxiety cell prints a median of 52 with a bracket of 55 to 60, so the median is below the lower bound. Medians must lie inside their own interval or quartile range, so one of the three numbers is misprinted. It affects a single baseline cell and does not change the main claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or source data showing the median and bracket are consistent (e.g. [45; 60] or median 57).

issues.explanation: The study is described as prospective and randomized, with ethics approval, but no trial registry entry is given and no primary outcome is designated. Without one, selective emphasis among about 20 outcomes cannot be excluded. This weakens confidence in the reported pattern but does not by itself show a problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry with a prespecified primary outcome.

10.17816/rjpbr692686.headline_claim: Adding the fifth-generation multisymbiotic VedaBiotic to a 9-day rehabilitation programme produces significant anti-inflammatory, anticoagulant and antioxidant effects and accelerates clinical symptom regression in post-COVID-19 syndrome, and the rehabilitation technology is safe and effective.
10.17816/rjpbr692686.overall: The paper shows within-arm improvements after a 9-day inpatient course, but the claim that the probiotic gives added anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and anticoagulant benefit rests mostly on one arm being significant and the other not, in an open-label study with unreported randomisation and a 96 versus 128 participant discrepancy. Several table values are internally inconsistent. The conclusions on safety, efficacy and use in other infections go well beyond what is shown, so the headline claim is only tentatively supported.

primary_outcome.name: unclear (no primary outcome is named; symptom frequency, blood markers, leukocyte indices and oxidative markers are all reported as outcomes)

issues.title: 128 patients reported, but the two analysed arms total 96 (64 + 32); 32 patients unaccounted for
issues.explanation: The Methods and Results say 128 patients took part. The arm sizes printed in the table headers are 64 (group I) and 32 (group II), which sum to 96. No flow diagram or text accounts for the missing 32. Either the arm sizes or the total is wrong, or a third of the sample is silently missing from the arm comparisons.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant flow showing 32 patients (e.g. a third group, or exclusions) were not part of the two compared arms, with baseline data for the 96 analysed.

quotes.text: В клиническом исследовании участвовали 128 пациентов с постковидным синдромом
Группа I (сравнения), n =64
Группа II (основная), n =32

script.explanation: The Total participants vs printed arm sizes does not reconcile: the arms of 'randomized' sum to 96, but the stage reports n=128 -- 32 participant(s) appear or vanish between the total and its own breakdown.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states 128 participants but the two analysed arms total 96 (64 + 32), and it gives no flow of participants, exclusions or dropouts to account for the 32 difference. The percentages in the tables are compatible with either n=32 or n=64 for Group II, so the discrepancy cannot be resolved from the paper, but it is real as printed.

issues.title: Conclusion claims 'high safety and efficacy' and extension to other infections beyond what the data show
issues.explanation: The only safety information is that no adverse events were recorded, with no method, counts or per-arm results. Efficacy rests on within-arm significance and unadjusted multiple tests in an open-label study. The conclusion further generalises to other acute infectious diseases, although only post-COVID-19 patients from one clinic were studied.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A defined safety monitoring plan with per-arm AE data in a larger sample, and data from other infectious conditions.

quotes.text: показала высокую безопасность и эффективность
Нежелательные явления при проведении настоящего клинического исследования не зарегистрированы.

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion's 'high safety' rests on a single sentence reporting no adverse events in a short, open-label study of at most 128 patients (32 on the probiotic), and 'high efficacy' rests largely on within-arm comparisons and uncorrected multiple tests; no limitations are discussed. The suggested use for other acute infections is not tested, since all participants had post-COVID-19 syndrome.

issues.title: Randomisation method, allocation ratio and baseline comparability by arm not reported (64 vs 32)
issues.explanation: The study is labelled randomised, but the Methods give no sequence generation, concealment or reason for the 2:1 split. No baseline table by arm (age, sex, CT extent, comorbidity) is given, so balance cannot be judged. The superiority of the add-on arm rests on a comparison whose allocation cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or CONSORT description of the allocation sequence and concealment plus a baseline table by arm showing balance.

quotes.text: Группа I (сравнения), n =64
Группа II (основная), n =32

second_reader.what_stands: The paper labels the study randomised but does not describe the randomisation method, allocation ratio or concealment, and presents no arm-by-arm baseline comparison; the 64 vs 32 split is unexplained. The baseline medians shown in the tables differ visibly for some variables (e.g., CRP), and no test of baseline balance is given.

issues.title: Superiority of VedaBiotic on leukocyte indices, TAS, IL-4 and D-dimer inferred from within-arm p-values only
issues.explanation: The conclusions that the add-on gives a stronger anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and anticoagulant effect rest on a change being significant in group II and not in group I. Only the ESR row (p I-II = 0.045) and Table 1 carry a between-group test. With n = 32 versus 64, significance in one arm and not the other can arise from sample size or noise alone. Group I even shows significant changes in several markers, so the markers are not specific to the add-on.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-arm tests (e.g. ANCOVA on change scores or an interaction test) significant for these markers.

quotes.text: в отсутствие таковой у лиц группы сравнения (I)

second_reader.what_stands: For the leukocyte indices, TAS, IL-4 and D-dimer the paper concludes a benefit of VedaBiotic from significant within-arm changes in Group II versus non-significant ones in Group I, without printing a between-arm test; this is a difference-in-significance inference. The ESR row is the exception, with a printed between-group p of 0,045, and Table 1 also gives between-group p-values for symptoms.

issues.title: 'Preventive' effect on hypercoagulation/DIC inferred from end-of-course D-dimer in ~30 patients
issues.explanation: The paper concludes that rehabilitation with the probiotic has a preventive effect on hypercoagulation and possibly DIC. The evidence is a before/after D-dimer change in the subgroup with raised values, measured only at the end of a 9-day stay. No clinical thrombotic events or follow-up are reported, so prevention is not demonstrated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up data showing fewer thrombotic events, or a pre-specified D-dimer analysis with between-arm comparison.

quotes.text: диссеминированного внутрисосудистого свёртывания крови

issues.title: D-dimer: 'only group II normalised' though group I median 248 ng/ml is below the stated norm of 250
issues.explanation: The text says only group II reached normal D-dimer, but group I's post-treatment median (248.00) is under the stated norm (<250). The claim holds only if normalisation means a significant change or all patients below 250, and that is not defined. The analysis is also restricted to the roughly 23% of patients with raised D-dimer, which invites regression to the mean. Group II's lower quartile of 0.00 ng/ml is also implausible for a measured D-dimer.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified definition of normalisation (e.g. significant change plus upper quartile below 250) and between-group test showing group II differs from group I.

quotes.text: физиологическая норма - менее 250 нг/ мл

issues.title: Open-label add-on with no placebo; symptom-frequency outcomes are subjective
issues.explanation: Patients in group II knew they received an extra preparation, and the complaint frequencies in Table 1 are subjective. The paper states there is 'no doubt' of a larger symptom-reducing effect without discussing this bias. Laboratory outcomes are less affected, but they are analysed with the weaknesses described elsewhere.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded outcome assessment or a placebo control showing the same symptom differences.

quotes.text: При этом не вызывает сомнений более значимое симптом-редуцирующее влияние

issues.title: About 25+ outcomes tested at alpha 0.05 without correction; no primary outcome defined
issues.explanation: The paper tests nine symptoms, several blood indices, four leukocyte indices, cytokines, oxidative markers and D-dimer, each at 0.05. Of seven nominal between-group symptom p-values only 0.001 and 0.000 would survive a Bonferroni threshold of about 0.0056 for nine tests. The headline conclusion rests on a few borderline results such as TAS (0.042) and ESR (0.045).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or multiplicity adjustment under which the key findings remain significant.

quotes.text: Критический уровень значимости при проверке статистических гипотез

issues.title: No trial registry identifier given for a prospective randomised study (2022-2024)
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomised controlled trial but names no registry or protocol number; only an ethics committee protocol is cited. This prevents checking whether the many outcomes reported were pre-specified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry entry dated before enrolment with matching outcomes.

quotes.text: (протокол № 2 от 16.04.2022)

issues.title: ISNL change in group II called significant with printed p = 0.05 against an alpha of 0.05
issues.explanation: The text lists ISNL among indices with statistically significant change in group II. Table 3 prints p = 0.05 for that comparison, which sits exactly on the stated threshold. If p is not below 0.05 the change is not significant by the paper's own rule. It may be a rounded value below it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The unrounded p-value for ISNL in group II being below 0.05.

quotes.text: Критический уровень значимости при проверке статистических гипотез

issues.title: Nuclear index median 0.20 exceeds its printed upper quartile 0.19 (group II after treatment)
issues.explanation: Table 3 gives the median as 0.20 with interquartile bounds [0.17; 0.19]. A median cannot be above the upper quartile, so at least one of the three numbers is misprinted. The 'before' cell in the same row also shows an odd three-decimal value (0.287), suggesting careless typesetting. One cell is affected and the main claims do not depend on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The source data showing a corrected value such as UQ = 0.29.

10.17816/rmmar109250.headline_claim: Medical rehabilitation programs (physical and rehabilitation medicine methods) are effective for patients with various manifestations of post-COVID syndrome.
10.17816/rmmar109250.overall: The headline claims, that the individualised programme is superior and that rehabilitation is effective, are not supported. The study is non-randomised with no allocation rule or baseline table, uses only within-arm before-after tests with no between-group comparison, and tests different programmes without blinding. The reported improvements may be real but cannot be attributed to treatment, and the descriptive statistics are ambiguous (SD vs SE).`

primary_outcome.name: not specified; SpO2, Stange/Gench breath-hold tests, Borg 6-minute-walk scale, MRC dyspnea scale and EQ-5D all reported

issues.title: Claim that observation group did 'significantly better' has no between-group test; arms received different programmes
issues.explanation: The abstract says the observation group showed significantly better recovery (p<0.05), but every p-value in the Results is a before-versus-after comparison inside one arm. No comparison of change between arms, no effect size and no confidence interval is given. The two arms also received different, non-equivalent programmes: the comparison arm got a generic basic set, the observation arm got individualised multi-modality programmes. Even a valid between-group test would not isolate any single component.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis (e.g. ANCOVA on follow-up adjusted for baseline, or a test of change scores) showing a significant advantage for the observation group.

quotes.text: Группа  наблюдения  показала  достоверно  лучшие  результаты  восстановления  ( p < 0,05).
В группе сравнения применялись методы физической и реабилитационной медицины основной группы из таблицы

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract's claim of significantly better recovery in the observation group is not backed by any reported between-group test; the printed p-values are all within-group before/after. The arms did receive different programmes (basic methods vs individualised extended programmes), so any difference cannot be attributed to a specific component, and on Shtange the comparison arm showed the larger raw gain.

issues.title: Effectiveness concluded from within-arm before-after changes over 14 days; no safety data, no valid comparison
issues.explanation: Efficacy is inferred only from each arm's change from day 1 to day 14, with p<0.05 inside each arm. Post-COVID symptoms often improve spontaneously, so improvement within an arm does not show a treatment effect. The conclusion states effectiveness for 'various manifestations' of post-COVID syndrome, which goes beyond non-randomised data on mostly short-term function tests. No adverse events are reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A controlled, adjusted between-group comparison with a no-treatment or usual-care reference, plus adverse event reporting.

quotes.text: возможность и эффективность применения методов физической и реабилитационной

second_reader.what_stands: Effectiveness is inferred from within-arm before/after changes over about 14 days, with no between-group test, no untreated control and no reported safety or adverse-event data. The conclusion's wording ('possibility and effectiveness', plus a call for further work) is somewhat tempered but still goes beyond what these data can support.

issues.title: Non-randomised allocation of 330 patients (170 vs 160), no allocation rule and no baseline comparison
issues.explanation: The paper calls the two groups 'representative' but never says how patients were assigned or whether assignment depended on severity or comorbidity. The observation arm received programmes tailored to comorbidity and symptom severity, so allocation by need is plausible and confounds the comparison. The baseline values scattered through the Results differ between arms, for example EQ-5D 1.48 vs 1.76 and MRC 3.84 vs 3.33, so baseline imbalance is likely.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A documented allocation procedure and a baseline characteristics table showing balanced groups.

quotes.text: Они были разделены на 2 репрезентативные группы
У пациентов группы наблюдения: до лечения 1,48 ± 0,18
до лечения 1,76 ± 0,23

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation of 330 patients into 170 and 160 is not described as randomised, no allocation rule is given, and no baseline comparison between arms is reported, so 'representative' is unsupported. The few printed baselines differ numerically, but whether the differences are meaningful cannot be established because the meaning of ± is not stated.

issues.title: No blinding or blinded assessment stated; Borg, MRC and EQ-5D outcomes are patient-reported
issues.explanation: Nothing is said about blinding of patients or assessors. Three of the main outcomes (Borg exertion, MRC dyspnoea, EQ-5D) are self-reported and can be inflated by expectation, particularly in the arm that received more elaborate individualised care. The objective outcomes (SpO2, breath-hold tests) lessen but do not remove the concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors were blinded, or that outcomes were measured by an independent assessor.

quotes.text: Отмечено уменьшение выраженности одышки по шкале одышки MRC
заполнялся опросник качества жизни EQ-5D

issues.title: Unlabelled '±' values incompatible with printed score ranges if they are SEs (e.g. Borg 0.86 ± 0.15, range 0-2, n=170)
issues.explanation: The tables and text never state whether the dispersion is SD or SE. Under the SE reading, the dispersion values imply SDs larger than the printed score ranges allow. Under the SD reading, several values look implausibly narrow. Either way the descriptive statistics cannot be interpreted as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that '±' denotes SD and that the printed ranges are correct, and a check that the narrow SDs are plausible.

issues.title: Ethics approval (24.06.2022) postdates the Sept 2020-Dec 2021 treatment period; retrospective status not stated
issues.explanation: Patients were treated between September 2020 and December 2021, but the ethics protocol is dated 24 June 2022. This is consistent with a retrospective analysis of clinic records. The paper never says so, and it also describes the work as a prospective-style two-point assessment, so the status of consent and approval is unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the study was a retrospective analysis of routine records, with a consent waiver, or earlier approval from the same committee.

quotes.text: было пролечено 330 пациентов, перенесших НКИ разной степени тяжести
протокол № 210 от 24.06.2022 г.

issues.title: Only day 1 and day 14 assessments; no follow-up after the course
issues.explanation: Outcomes were assessed at the start and end of a roughly 14-day course. Durability of benefit and later recovery cannot be assessed, and the general claim of effectiveness in post-COVID syndrome is not matched to this horizon. This is a limitation of scope rather than an error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up data at weeks or months after completion.

quotes.text: Обследование проводилось по 2 контрольным точкам: 1 день (первая), 14 день (вторая).

issues.title: Stange test dispersion values identical across arms (1.44 and 1.63 in both groups)
issues.explanation: The Stange test pre-treatment dispersion is 1.44 in both arms and the post-treatment dispersion is 1.63 in both arms, despite different means and group sizes. The Genche pre-values 1.43 and 1.42 are also nearly the same. This suggests a possible transcription error, which would affect any significance test based on these values.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data or a supplementary table giving the arm-specific SDs/SEs.

10.18093/0869-0189-2023-33-1-52-63.headline_claim: Bovhyaluronidase azoximer (Longidase) improved FVC, pulse oximetry, 6-minute walk distance and mMRC dyspnoea in post-COVID syndrome, and the authors conclude it is an effective treatment for post-COVID syndrome.
10.18093/0869-0189-2023-33-1-52-63.overall: The efficacy conclusion is only weakly supported: the registered primary CT outcome favoured the untreated control at day 75, and the benefits claimed for FVC, SpO2, walk distance and mMRC come from an open-label, non-randomised comparison with baseline imbalance, borderline p-values and no multiplicity control. The conclusion also overstates durability to day 180 for SpO2 and mMRC. The funding statement is hard to reconcile with the manufacturer's role.

primary_outcome.name: Change in residual lung lesion volume on HRCT at day 75 (registered primary; the stated aim in Methods)

primary_outcomes.measure: The severity of lung tissue lesions with fibrosis and interstitial changes on day 75

issues.title: Primary CT outcome favoured control at day 75 (-11.91% vs -8.39%, p = 0.021) but is absent from the conclusion
issues.explanation: The study's stated aim and registered primary outcome was the change in lung lesion volume on HRCT at day 75. The control arm improved significantly more (-11.91% vs -8.39%, p = 0.021), and there was no difference at day 180. The abstract reports the CT outcome only as a within-group reduction, and the conclusion lists only the secondary outcomes that favoured treatment. The primary outcome did not show a benefit of treatment, and the headline does not say so.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchy naming FVC or symptoms as primary, with the CT outcome declared secondary.

quotes.text: хотя на 75-й день снижение было статистически значимо более выраженным в контрольной группе
При терапии бовгиалуронидазой азоксимером у пациентов с ПКС отмечено улучшение показателей ФЖЕЛ, пульсоксиметрии, переносимости функциональных физических нагрузок и оценки одышки по mMRC.

second_reader.what_stands: The primary CT outcome at day 75 favoured the control group (-11.91% vs -8.39%, p = 0.021) and this is reported in the Results but not in the Abstract Conclusion or the closing Заключение, which list only the secondary outcomes that favoured treatment. It is not concealed, since the Results and Discussion state it (the Discussion says only that there was no significant difference in CT improvement, which understates the day-75 result), and the day-180 CT difference is null (p = 0.327).

issues.title: Open, non-randomised, untreated comparison used to conclude the drug is an 'effective treatment'
issues.explanation: Patients in the control arm received only observation, with no placebo, no blinding and no described allocation method. The symptom (mMRC) and walk-test results are open to expectation and effort effects, and the groups differ at baseline on walk distance and FVC. The Discussion nonetheless concludes the drug 'is an effective treatment option', and the paper lists no design limitation other than the absence of hyaluronan measurement. At best the data suggest an association with better secondary outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random allocation with concealment, or an explicit statement of these limitations tied to the efficacy conclusion.

quotes.text: У пациентов, составивших контрольную группу ( n = 79), выполнялось только динамическое наблюдение.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes an open-label, non-randomised-appearing (no randomisation described), untreated-observation comparison with unblinded subjective endpoints (mMRC, 6MWT effort), and nevertheless concludes in the Discussion that the drug 'является эффективным вариантом лечения'. Baseline 6MWT differed by about 41 m (roughly 2.4 SDs-based z if the printed values are SDs) and the paper still calls groups similar. The conclusion is stronger than this design supports, particularly as the primary CT outcome favoured control at day 75 and several secondary differences were null at day 180; the auth

issues.title: Primary HRCT lesion-percentage outcome: no scoring method, reader or blinding described
issues.explanation: The paper defines the CT outcome only as a percentage of lung volume with lesions. It does not say how lesions were segmented or scored, who assessed the images, or whether assessors knew the allocation. In an open-label trial this leaves the primary outcome open to unmeasured reader bias, which would not obviously explain the direction found (favouring control).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol description of a validated or software-based quantification method and blinded central reading.

quotes.text: Остаточные изменения в легких регистрировались в процентах от объема легких с поражениями, обнаруженными по данным КТВР.

issues.title: Borderline secondary results (p = 0.046, 0.049) claimed as benefit with no multiplicity control or sample size
issues.explanation: The statistical methods set a two-sided 5% level for all tests, with no hierarchy or correction across about ten between-group comparisons. Two of the headline secondary results are barely under 0.05, and the primary outcome did not favour treatment. Any adjustment for multiple tests would likely remove these borderline findings, and no sample-size justification is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchical testing plan or correction showing these results survive.

quotes.text: Все статистические критерии были двусторонними, уровень значимости - 5 %.

issues.title: Conclusion claims significant SpO2 and mMRC gains to day 180; day-180 between-group p = 0.081 and 0.142
issues.explanation: The conclusion says significant improvement was shown on day 75 and throughout the whole 180-day period, including dyspnoea (mMRC) and pulse oximetry. The Results report day-180 between-group p-values of 0.081 for SpO2 and 0.142 for mMRC, and describe the mMRC change as similar in both groups. Only FVC and walk distance were significant at day 180. The conclusion overstates the durability of benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the conclusion refers only to within-group change from baseline, stated as such.

issues.title: 'No sponsor support' and 'no conflicts' stated, yet the article is placed with support from the drug's manufacturer
issues.explanation: The paper says there was no sponsorship and no declared conflicts, but acknowledges that the article was published with support from NPO Petrovax Pharm. The registry names NPO Petrovax as lead sponsor of the trial. The role of the manufacturer in design, conduct, analysis or writing is not described, so readers cannot judge the independence of an unblinded efficacy conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the manufacturer had no role in design, data, analysis or reporting, and that no author has financial ties to it.

issues.title: Registered 2020-11-20, after the 2020-07-01 study start; the paper does not state registration timing
issues.explanation: The registry record shows the study start preceded first submission by about five months. The paper gives the registration number but does not say when registration took place. The registered primary outcome appears to match the paper's stated aim, which limits concern, but the primary result went against treatment and the conclusion focuses on other outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Earlier registry versions showing the primary and secondary outcomes were fixed before enrolment, or a statement of registration timing in the paper.

issues.title: Baseline FVC, treatment arm: text 88.8 ± 20.50 % vs Table 1 87.90 ± 21.03
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 1 give different baseline FVC mean and SD for the treatment group. The control values agree. Since FVC is the lead secondary outcome, the baseline value matters.
