10.18370/2309-4117.2023.68.44-47.headline_claim: The proposed approach (oral or vaginal micronized progesterone plus vitamin D, valerian and magnesium) corrects menstrual cycle disturbances in women with long COVID, with vaginal progesterone showing more promising outcomes than oral in patients with GI symptoms.
10.18370/2309-4117.2023.68.44-47.overall: The headline claim that the regimen corrects menstrual disturbances and that vaginal progesterone is better is not supported: the study is uncontrolled, the outcome is undefined and self-reported, and the route comparison has no analysis, unclear allocation and subgroup counts that do not add up. The relief percentages are descriptive only and cannot be attributed to treatment.

primary_outcome.name: Relief of menstrual cycle disorders / premenstrual symptom improvement at 3 and 6 months

issues.title: Single-arm, multi-component regimen with no control; 71-89% relief cannot be attributed to treatment
issues.explanation: Everyone received progesterone plus vitamin D, valerian and magnesium. Relief at 3 and 6 months is compared with nothing, so natural recovery from post-COVID cycle disturbance, regression to the mean and placebo response are indistinguishable from a treatment effect. Components cannot be separated either. The conclusion that the approach 'has shown' correction is therefore not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group showing less improvement.

quotes.text: All groups, regardless of symptoms, received vitamin D (2000 IU orally single daily dose with a meal), valerian root extract
The proposed approach has shown particular correction of the menstrual cycle disturbances in women with long COVID.

second_reader.what_stands: All women received the same multi-component regimen (vitamin D, valerian, magnesium, progesterone) with no untreated or placebo comparison, so the 71-89% relief cannot be attributed to the regimen or to any single component. The authors' Conclusion that the approach 'has shown particular correction' goes beyond what an uncontrolled design supports, although they do add a call for further research. The paper also gives no definition of 'relief', and the symptoms were self-reported.

issues.title: Route subgroups 90 + 90 = 180 conflict with 320 enrolled and two groups of 160
issues.explanation: The Methods say 320 women were enrolled and divided equally. The two progesterone-route subgroups are given as 90 and 90, summing to 180. If they are within each GI group, 180 exceeds the 160 in each group; if they are overall, 140 women have no stated route. The route comparison, which drives the secondary headline, cannot be interpreted without the true subgroup sizes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that subgroups are drawn from a stated subset, or a corrected count (e.g. 160 each) with a flow description.

quotes.text: A total of 320 women were enrolled in the study and divided equally into:
two subgroups: oral progesterone subgroup (n = 90) and vaginal progesterone subgroup (n = 90).

second_reader.what_stands: The route subgroups (90 + 90 = 180) do not add up to the 320 enrolled or to the two groups of 160, although the text says the division was equal. The paper does not explain the gap, so the denominators for the oral versus vaginal comparison are unclear.

issues.title: Vaginal-vs-oral superiority claimed from unreported 2.5-14% differences, no test, no allocation method
issues.explanation: The Results say vaginal progesterone performed '2.5-14% better' but give no per-route counts, denominators, test statistics or confidence intervals, and the route subgroup sizes are internally inconsistent. How women came to receive each route is not stated, so differences could reflect patient choice or GI status rather than the drug route. The conclusion nonetheless states vaginal progesterone 'offers more promising outcomes'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table of outcomes by route with counts and a between-group test, plus a described allocation method.

quotes.text: The vaginal progesterone [17] resulted in better results compared to oral, while on average performing 2.5-14% better.
Vaginal micronized progesterone offers more promising outcomes in patients with GI symptoms and disrupted absorption, compared to the oral variant.

second_reader.what_stands: The text gives a vague 2.5-14% range of advantage for vaginal progesterone with no test result, no confidence interval and no description of how women were allocated to route, and the subgroup sizes do not reconcile (see i1), so the superiority claim in the Conclusions is not supported by what is reported. I could not check Figures 2 and 3, which may hold the underlying values, and the authors do add that more research is needed.

issues.title: Ethics approval (29.11.2021) post-dates the January-June 2021 study period
issues.explanation: The study is described as interventional with follow-up at 3 and 6 months, run January to June 2021. Ethics approval is dated 29 November 2021, after recruitment ended. This is either a retrospective approval of existing records (which conflicts with the 'interventional' and 'planned visits' description) or a dating error. The paper does not reconcile it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of earlier approval, or an explicit statement that the analysis was retrospective with waiver.

quotes.text: The study was held in the Kyiv City Center of Reproductive and Perinatal Medicine (Ukraine) from January to June 2021.

issues.title: Relief outcome is undefined, self-selected symptoms, no scale or threshold or baseline
issues.explanation: Patients chose the symptoms they cared most about, and 'relief' is reported as an average percentage without a validated instrument, a definition of relief, or baseline values. The percentages cannot be compared across women or with other studies. The limitation is acknowledged in the Discussion but the Conclusions still claim correction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A defined, validated outcome measure with baseline and follow-up scores.

quotes.text: The patients selected the symptoms that they considered to be of the greatest importance.

issues.title: No trial registration or protocol reported for an 'interventional' study
issues.explanation: No registry number is reported, so the outcomes cannot be checked against a prior plan. Because the study is non-randomized and possibly retrospective, registration norms are less clear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment.

quotes.text: A single-center,  longitudinal,  interventional study was held in Kyiv, Ukraine between January

10.18370/2309-4117.2023.69.104-112.headline_claim: Ayurvedic phytocompositions Femicycle and Femimens are effective and safe for restoring menstrual health in women of early reproductive age after moderate or severe COVID-19.
10.18370/2309-4117.2023.69.104-112.overall: The headline claim that the herbal products are effective, safe and give full hormonal recovery is only tentatively supported. The comparison is open-label against background care without placebo, outcomes are largely subjective, safety evidence is one sentence, and the hormone table markers are contradictory. The 6-month symptom differences (e.g. dysmenorrhea 11% vs 35%) are suggestive, but the printed-number slips in Tables 1 and 2 and the text further lower confidence in the reporting.

primary_outcome.name: Menstrual health (frequency of menstrual disorders, e.g. infrequent menstruation, dysmenorrhea, PMS) 6 months after treatment start

issues.title: 'Safe' conclusion rests on one sentence about no side effects, with no adverse-event method or comparison data
issues.explanation: The conclusion calls the products effective and safe. The only safety evidence is a single sentence that main-group women had no side effects and high compliance. No method of collecting adverse events, no comparison-group safety data, and no follow-up beyond treatment are described. With 53 treated women, the study cannot establish safety.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospectively defined adverse-event collection protocol with reported results for both groups.

quotes.text: Ayurvedic phytocompositions Femicycle and Femimens are effective and safe naturopathic drugs for restoring menstrual health
had no side effects from taking herbal preparations and showed high compliance.

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion that the preparations are 'safe' rests on one unquantified sentence about the main group, with no stated method of adverse-event ascertainment, no safety laboratory data and no comparison-group data. With 53 patients, zero reported events still allows a true event rate up to about 6%. The paper therefore supports at most 'no side effects were reported', not a demonstrated safety profile.

issues.title: 'Full hormonal recovery' claim not supported by Table 4: markers contradictory, no direct group test at 9 months
issues.explanation: The abstract says the phytocompositions led to a full hormonal recovery. Table 4 marks nearly all 9-month main-group values 'cm', which the legend defines as significantly different from the control group. For 17(OH)-progesterone, 0.57 vs the control's 0.62 is unlikely to be significant, so the markers appear unreliable. The paper also reports no formal main-versus-comparison test at 9 months, and the comparison group's values also moved toward control. The claim of treatment-driven full recovery is therefore not established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clear table with control values and a defined legend showing main-group 9-month values do not differ from controls and differ from the comparison group by a stated test.

quotes.text: led to a faster recovery of menstrual health and a full hormonal recovery

second_reader.what_stands: The Table 4 significance markers on the main group at 9 months (mostly 'cm') say it still differs from controls on most markers, while several printed means are statistically indistinguishable from controls (17(OH)-progesterone, cortisol, ACTH, TSH). A few residual gaps do appear real (androstenedione about 11% below control, 17(OH)-progesterone about 8% below). No direct test of main versus control at 9 months is reported, so 'full hormonal recovery' is not demonstrated by the paper's own table. The comparison group also moved toward control values. What I checked was the table-based reading

issues.title: Open-label add-on versus background care only, no placebo or blinding, with patient-reported outcomes
issues.explanation: Both groups received diet, vitamins and psychotherapy, and only the main group received the herbal products. No placebo, blinding or sham is described. Dysmenorrhea, PMS and cycle pattern are subjective, self-reported outcomes. The between-group difference at 6 months therefore cannot be cleanly attributed to the herbal ingredients as opposed to extra attention and expectation. The conclusion that the products are 'effective' is only tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and patients were blinded, or that a placebo was used.

quotes.text: All patients with COVID-19 received a comprehensive rehabilitation program, which included diet therapy, vitamin-mineral complexes, and psychotherapy.
In addition to the comprehensive rehabilitation program, main group patients received 6 months of ayurvedic phytocompositions Femicycle or Femimens.

second_reader.what_stands: The design is an add-on to background care versus background care alone, with no placebo and no stated blinding of patients or assessors. The main clinical outcomes (dysmenorrhea, PMS, cycle complaints) are patient-reported, so expectation and reporting bias cannot be excluded. The hormone assays are objective, but the paper does not say whether laboratory staff were blinded.

issues.title: Randomisation method and allocation concealment not described
issues.explanation: The paper states random allocation but not how the sequence was generated or concealed. Baseline balance cannot be fully verified because Table 1 contains a mis-copied percentage. The reported baseline symptom rates, once corrected, are similar between the arms, so imbalance itself is not shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of computer-generated sequence and concealed allocation.

quotes.text: randomly divided into two groups: the main group (n=53) and the comparison group (n=51).

issues.title: No clinical-trial registration or pre-specified primary outcome or sample size reported
issues.explanation: The only registration cited is a departmental research-topic number. There is no trial registry entry, no pre-specified primary outcome and no sample-size calculation. Readers cannot check whether the reported outcomes were chosen in advance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clinical-trial registry identifier with registration date before enrolment and matching outcomes.

quotes.text: carried out within the framework of the planned research topic

issues.title: Promotional leaflet for Femicycle/Femimens attached; products described as dietary supplements; no funding statement
issues.explanation: The document includes a product advertisement citing this paper and repeating its conclusion, and states that the products are not medicines but dietary supplements. The paper declares no conflict of interest and gives no funding statement. The relationship between the authors and the manufacturer is therefore unclear, which matters for an open-label efficacy claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A funding and relationship-to-sponsor statement showing the manufacturer had no role.

quotes.text: Феміменс i Феміцикл не є лікарськими засобами. Дієтичні добавки.
There is no conflict of interest.

issues.title: Main group pools two different products assigned by symptoms and PRL level; no analysis by product
issues.explanation: Women with normal prolactin received Femicycle, while those with dysmenorrhea, PMS or raised prolactin received Femimens. Results are pooled and not shown by product. The efficacy conclusion for each named product is not supported by separate data, and assignment by clinical features is not randomised.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Separate outcome tables by product, with per-product numbers.

quotes.text: were prescribed the phytocomposition Femimens 1-2 capsules per day during meals

issues.title: Table 1 percentages wrong: comparison-group PMS 19/51 printed 20.59 (is 37.25); main amenorrhea 9/53 printed 16.08 (is 16.98)
issues.explanation: In Table 1 the comparison group PMS cell reads 19 (20.59), but 19 of 51 is 37.25%; 20.59 is the control group's dysmenorrhea figure copied from the cell above. Main-group amenorrhea 9 (16.08) should be 16.98%. These are slips in descriptive baseline percentages. They do not change the 6-month results, but the PMS slip hides that the comparison group's baseline PMS rate was slightly lower than the main group's.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing different counts for these cells.

script.explanation: 19/51 = 37.25%, but the paper prints 20.59, outside the rounding interval [20.59, 20.60]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 92.3 rather than 51.

issues.title: Cortisol 11.01 vs 13.91 labelled mg/dL in text and nmol/l in Table 2; reference range fits ug/dL
issues.explanation: The text gives cortisol as 11.01 and 13.91 mg/dL, while Table 2 gives the same numbers in nmol/l. Neither label matches the printed reference interval of 6.2-19.4, which is the usual ug/dL range. The between-group comparison is unaffected, but the unit is printed wrongly in at least one place.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the values were converted or that the assay was reported in a specific unit that matches both places.

quotes.text: Cortisol, nmol/l

issues.title: Text and Table 2 disagree: 17(OH)-progesterone 0.46 vs 0.44, and control SEs (0.02 vs 0.03; TSH 0.14 vs 0.10)
issues.explanation: The text gives the COVID-19 group's 17(OH)-progesterone as 0.46 +/- 0.01 ng/ml, while Table 2 gives 0.44 +/- 0.02. The control SE is also printed differently (0.02 in the text, 0.03 in the table), and the control TSH SE differs (0.14 vs 0.10). The stated 1.33-fold decrease fits neither mean. These are small copying inconsistencies and do not change the direction of any finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An erratum or source data showing which values are correct and that the discrepancy is a transcription issue only.

issues.title: National COVID-19 counts to June 2023 cited to a source dated 13 February 2022
issues.explanation: The Introduction gives Ukrainian case and death totals for March 2020 to June 2023, citing a statistics page whose reference says it is current as of 13 February 2022. The cited source cannot contain data up to June 2023. This is a background-citation error and does not affect the trial results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the source page was a continuously updated dashboard that the authors accessed in 2023.

quotes.text: In the period from March 2020 to June 2023, 5,526,748 cases
Coronavirus in Ukraine (current statistics as of February 13, 2022)

10.19163/1994-9480-2022-19-2-43-52.headline_claim: Transcutaneous supraorbital nerve stimulation with the Cefaly device added to standard rehabilitation more effectively reduces asthenia and anxiety symptoms in people recovering from COVID-19.
10.19163/1994-9480-2022-19-2-43-52.overall: The larger fall in MFI-20 and HAM-A totals in the Cefaly arm is plausible as reported, but the open-label, no-sham design with subjective outcomes means it cannot be attributed to the device. Subscale claims, the quality-of-life conclusion and several significance markers are inconsistent or unsupported, so the headline should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Asthenia (MFI-20 total score) and anxiety (HAM-A total score), change from baseline to day 24

issues.title: Open-label, no-sham comparison on subjective MFI-20/HAM-A scores cannot isolate a device effect
issues.explanation: Patients and staff knew allocation, the control group received rehabilitation only with no sham stimulation, and the outcomes are questionnaire or rating-scale scores. A group receiving 10 sessions of an active device plus attention would be expected to report greater subjective improvement for non-specific reasons. The conclusion that Cefaly 'more effectively' reduces asthenia and anxiety is therefore not supported as a device effect. Randomization is by envelopes, with no described concealment or baseline-adjusted analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of blinded outcome assessment or a sham-controlled arm with similar effects.

quotes.text: an open prospective study in parallel groups was conducted
patients received only rehabilitation treatment

second_reader.what_stands: The study was open-label with a no-treatment-add-on control and no sham, and the primary outcomes are subjective or rater-based scores (MFI-20, HAM-A). Expectation, attention and placebo effects from a device session therefore cannot be separated from any specific effect of stimulation, so the design cannot isolate a device effect. The paper does not report assessor blinding or discuss this as a limitation. This is a limit on causal attribution, not evidence that the device had no effect.

issues.title: Control-group significance for physical asthenia and reduced activity differs between Results text, Table 2 and abstract
issues.explanation: The Results text says the control group had no statistically significant change in physical asthenia, but Table 2 marks it *# (p<0.05 vs baseline and between groups). The abstract and discussion say rehabilitation affected physical asthenia and reduced activity, yet Table 2 gives reduced activity no marker in the control group. The text, the table and the abstract therefore do not agree on which control-group subscales changed. This affects the secondary subscale statements, not the total-score result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 2 or text showing which control subscales were significant, with the reduced-activity and physical-asthenia statements aligned.

quotes.location: Table 2, control group, after treatment, Физическая астения

quotes.text: в группе Cefaly® в сравнении с отсутствием статистически значимых изменений в контрольной группе
had an effect only on physical asthenia and reduced activity

issues.title: Component-level claims rest on 'significant in one arm, not in the other' within-group contrasts
issues.explanation: Statements that Cefaly works on all asthenia components and rehabilitation only on some are based mostly on within-group p<0.05 versus baseline in each arm. A difference in significance between arms is not itself a test of a difference between arms. Between-group results are reported explicitly only for the total scores and a few subscales.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-group tests of change from baseline for each subscale with the same conclusions.

quotes.text: had an effect only on physical asthenia and reduced activity
в группе Cefaly® в сравнении с отсутствием статистически значимых изменений в контрольной группе

issues.title: About 13 uncorrected subscale tests with no stated primary outcome; subscale emphasis is exploratory
issues.explanation: The paper tests two totals and about 11 subscales at p<0.05 each without a multiplicity correction, and no primary outcome is designated. The claim that Cefaly acts most on insomnia and tension is a selection among uncorrected tests. The total-score findings are less affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome and hierarchy, or adjusted p-values supporting the subscale statements.

quotes.text: Cefaly® therapy had the greatest effect on insomnia and tension.
По результатам показателя p менее 0,05 различие в группе считали статистически значимым.

issues.title: No trial registration or prespecified primary outcome or sample size reported
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval but no registry identifier, no designated primary outcome and no sample-size calculation. The reported outcomes therefore cannot be checked against a prespecified plan.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol predating enrolment that names the primary outcome.

quotes.text: Протокол исследования был одобрен локальным этическим комитетом.
an open prospective study in parallel groups was conducted

issues.title: Conclusion claims 'significant improvement in quality of life' though no quality-of-life measure was analysed
issues.explanation: The conclusions state that patients on Cefaly reported significant quality-of-life improvement. The measured outcomes were MFI-20 and HAM-A; the only other source is an unanalysed activity and sleep diary described qualitatively. The claim is not supported by reported data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported analysis of a quality-of-life instrument or quantified diary data.

quotes.text: Пациенты  на  фоне  терапии  с  использованием Cefaly®  отмечали  значительное  улучшение  качества жизни
увеличения объема домашних активностей и существенного снижения уровня физической астении.

issues.title: Control insomnia: text gives p<0.05 vs baseline (-38.27%), Table 3 shows only # (between-group)
issues.explanation: The text says insomnia fell 38.27% in controls with p<0.05 against baseline and between groups. Table 3 marks the control post-treatment insomnia cell with # only, with no * for change from baseline. The median change shown (3 to 2) is also not obviously a 38.27% reduction, and the same 38.27% figure appears for physical asthenia in the Cefaly group. It is a localized reporting inconsistency.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data or a corrected table showing a significant within-group change for control insomnia, and the source of the 38.27% figure.

quotes.text: на 38,27 % в контрольной группе

quotes.location: Table 3, control group, after treatment, Инсомния

issues.title: Table 1 percentages (e.g. 23.31%, 30.07%, 26.64%, 90.1/9.99) are not attainable with n = 30 per group
issues.explanation: With 30 patients per group, each patient is 3.33 percentage points, so shares such as 23.31, 30.07 or 26.64 cannot arise (nearest are 23.33, 30.00, 26.67). Some pairs also do not sum to 100 (90.1 + 9.99 = 100.09). This points to a computation or transcription problem in the baseline table, not a change in conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the percentages were derived from non-integer or weighted counts.

10.19163/2307-9266-2025-13-4-270-284.headline_claim: Adding L-carnitine to standard therapy is reported to be effective for correcting the frequency and severity of autonomic and cardiac disorders in children, adolescents and young adults with post-COVID syndrome.
10.19163/2307-9266-2025-13-4-270-284.overall: The headline claim that L-carnitine corrects autonomic, cardiac and symptom manifestations of post-COVID syndrome rests on an open-label comparison against standard therapy with a mainly complaint-based outcome, so it is at best tentative. Several printed numbers are inconsistent (abstract vs Results for echo and repolarization findings, and percentages that do not match n=45), and some Holter/echo conclusions depend on within-arm significance. The direction of these problems is mostly towards overstating benefit, though the large complaint-free difference (93.3% vs 66.7%) is probably real in direction if biased in size.

primary_outcome.name: Presence of long COVID signs (complaints and objective status) at 6, 12 and 24 weeks

issues.title: Open-label add-on vs standard care; headline outcome is complaint-free status (93.3% vs 66.7%)
issues.explanation: Patients and clinicians knew who received L-carnitine, and the control arm received no placebo. The headline outcome is the absence of complaints plus 'normalization of objective status', which is open to expectation and assessment bias. The paper does not state that Holter, echo or HRV readers were blinded. The conclusion that efficacy was demonstrated is therefore tentative at best.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and the readers of Holter and echo studies were blinded to allocation, or a placebo-controlled analysis of the primary outcome.

quotes.text: Within the framework of an open, simple, randomized, parallel-group comparative clinical study
the absence of complaints and normalization of objective status were noted in 93.3% of patients in the main group and 66.7% in the comparison group

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is open-label (unblinded) with L-carnitine added to standard therapy versus standard therapy alone, and the headline result is a complaint-free/normalized-status composite (93.3% vs 66.7%, p<0.05), so the characterization is accurate. The comparison is therefore subject to bias from knowing the allocation, particularly for subjective complaint-based outcomes, and the comparison-group count and the test behind p<0.05 are not stated (minor internal inconsistencies such as 12 patients printed as 40.0% in Table 1 also exist). This checks the description of design and headline outcome onl

issues.title: Comparison-group LV dilatation at 6 weeks: 9 of 12 in abstract vs 6 of 8 in Results
issues.explanation: The abstract says slight left ventricular dilatation persisted in 9 of 12 comparison-group patients at 6 weeks. The Results give 6 of 8 for the same finding. The two versions cannot both be right, and Table 2 does not show which. The abstract's wording makes the comparison group look worse.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement or table showing that two different echo subsets (12 and 8 patients) were used for the abstract and the Results.

quotes.text: persisted in 9 out of 12 patients
сохранялась незначительная дилатация ЛЖ у 6 из 8 пациентов

issues.title: No trial registration reported for a randomized interventional study (Feb 2022 - May 2024)
issues.explanation: The paper reports no registry identifier. The primary outcome (presence of PCS signs at 6, 12 and 24 weeks) therefore cannot be compared with a prespecified plan. Results for 12 and 24 weeks are described only in passing, which fits with selective emphasis on 6-week data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry entry dated before enrolment with the same primary outcome.

quotes.text: Исследование проводили с февраля 2022 по май 2024 года
quotes.location: Materials and methods, Duration and conditions

issues.title: Abstract: repolarization/rhythm abnormalities persist in >50% of comparison group; Results say resolved
issues.explanation: The abstract says repolarization abnormalities and rhythm disturbances, present at baseline in 43.3% of patients, persisted in more than 50% of the comparison group at 6 weeks. The Results say non-specific repolarization disturbances resolved in both groups. The Table 3 rhythm findings in the comparison group at 6 weeks are all below 50%, and the 43.3% baseline figure is not reported anywhere. The abstract therefore overstates the contrast between arms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table or analysis showing a combined repolarization/rhythm abnormality rate above 50% in the comparison group at 6 weeks, with a 43.3% baseline.

quotes.text: while they persisted in more than 50% in the comparison group
Неспецифические нарушения реполяризации нивелировались к 6 нед в обеих исследуемых группах.

issues.title: Percentages do not match n=45: Table 1 fatigue 12 = 40.0% (26.7%); text 10 = 23.3% (22.2%)
issues.explanation: Table 1 gives 12 comparison-group patients with fatigue at 6 weeks as 40.0%, but 12 of 45 is 26.7%. The Results text gives 10 patients with moderate-severe acute illness as 23.3%, but 10 of 45 is 22.2%. Several other Table 1 cells have the same type of slip (5 = 13.3%, 6 = 6.7%). The fatigue figure is for the key symptom, and it makes the comparison group look worse than the count supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the percentage was taken over a different, stated denominator (for example 30), or a corrected table.

quotes.location: Table 1, fatigue row, comparison group 6 weeks

quotes.text: зарегистрировано у 10 (23,3%) пациентов

quotes.location: Table 1, palpitations row, comparison group 6 weeks

script.explanation: 12/45 = 26.67%, but the paper prints 40.0, outside the rounding interval [39.95, 40.10]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 30.0 rather than 45.

issues.title: Several Holter/ECG/echo benefits inferred from within-arm significance; between-arm p-values often not significant
issues.explanation: For HRV means, the paper says the comparison group showed 'similar dynamics' that did not reach significance, while the main group's changes did. This contrasts significance in one arm with non-significance in the other, which is not a test of the difference. Where between-group p-values are printed they are sometimes non-significant, for example QTc p=0.70 and migration/SA block p=0.06. Rhythm and autonomic efficacy is therefore less secure than the abstract states.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-arm tests (for example ANCOVA or an arm-by-time interaction) for the Holter, HRV and echo outcomes showing a significant difference favouring L-carnitine.

quotes.text: В группе сравнения отмечалась сходная динамика

quotes.location: Table 3, comparison group after 6 weeks, QTc

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; 45 per arm, with a firm efficacy conclusion
issues.explanation: The authors state that no sample-size calculation was done because of limited eligible children. With 45 per arm and a large number of outcomes, the precision of secondary comparisons is limited. This weakens secondary results rather than the headline complaint-free difference.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation showing that 45 per arm gives adequate power for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: отсутствие предварительного расчёта размера
in comparison with the standard therapy ( n = 45)

issues.title: Mean age 14.5±2.6 vs 15.6±1.9 years described as 'not different'; recalculated t-test gives p≈0.02
issues.explanation: The Results say the two arms did not differ in age, but the printed means and SDs imply a significant difference at n=45 per arm. This is unexpected under age-stratified randomization with equal stratum sizes. Age could be related to symptom persistence, and no adjusted analysis is presented. The size of the effect on the conclusion is unknown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the printed ages are for subsets, or a corrected value showing balance.

quotes.text: не отличались по возрасту

issues.title: Baseline QTc 429.1 ms (text) is outside both group means in Table 3 (422.8 and 418.3 ms)
issues.explanation: The text gives a mean QTc of 429.1±11.6 ms for patients with post-COVID syndrome, compared with 399.3 ms in healthy peers. Table 3 gives baseline means of 422.8 and 418.3 ms in the two groups of 45. A pooled mean of the two groups must fall between those values, and the pooled SD (11.6) is smaller than both group SDs. The discrepancy affects only the comparison with healthy peers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 429.1 ms figure comes from a different group of patients or a different measurement than Table 3.

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes and timepoints tested at p<0.05 with no multiplicity control
issues.explanation: Symptoms, ECG, orthostatic test, echo, Holter, HRV and quality of life are all tested at an uncorrected 0.05 level. Many p-values are very small and would likely survive correction, but borderline ones (p=0.01-0.05) would not be reliable. The primary outcome is described loosely (signs of PCS at 6, 12 and 24 weeks), so it is unclear which test is confirmatory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome with a hierarchical or corrected testing plan for secondary outcomes.

quotes.text: Достоверность различий полученных данных устанавливали на уровне p <0,05.

10.20344/amp.19382.headline_claim: Persistent symptoms were frequent in patients referred to a PRM clinic after SARS-CoV-2 infection, SARS-CoV-2 infection and symptom persistence negatively affected physical condition, ADL and quality of life, and a home exercise programme was followed by statistically significant improvement.
10.20344/amp.19382.overall: The descriptive finding that persistent symptoms were common and were associated with worse test results in this referred sample is reasonably supported, apart from small count and percentage slips in the abstract and tables. The conclusions that infection and symptoms 'had a negative impact', and that the home exercise programme produced clinically relevant improvement, go beyond an uncontrolled, selected 27-patient before-after series and a cross-sectional comparison. The null risk-factor claims rest on very small groups and should be read as inconclusive.

primary_outcome.name: 1-Minute Sit-to-Stand test (1-MSTS), first vs second appointment

issues.title: Improvement credited to home exercise from an uncontrolled before-after change in 27 of 74 patients
issues.explanation: Only the 27 patients who neither entered another rehabilitation programme nor were discharged were re-assessed. They are a selected subgroup, 36% of the cohort. With no control group, spontaneous recovery over a month, regression to the mean and other rehabilitation contact cannot be separated from the exercise programme. Exercise adherence was not monitored. The abstract and discussion nonetheless say the programme was followed by significant, clinically relevant improvement and recommend PRM follow-up.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control group, or evidence that the 27 were representative and that spontaneous recovery over a month was negligible.

quotes.text: Com um plano de exercícios domiciliários implementado, observou-se uma melhoria estatisticamente significativa.
Twenty-seven patients were re-evaluated in a second appointment, approximately one month later.
the non-supervision or lack of adhesion surveillance of the home exercise program limits the conclusions

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract conclusion credits a statistically significant improvement to the home exercise plan, but the data are an uncontrolled before-after comparison in 27 of 74 patients (36.5%), selected by clinical pathway, with no adherence data and about one month of natural recovery. The authors do flag non-supervision and sample size as limitations, which softens the point, but the causal wording in the Abstract and the absence of a control group as a limitation remain.

issues.title: Conclusion says infection and symptoms 'had a negative impact', from a cross-sectional comparison within infected patients
issues.explanation: The only comparison is between 51 symptomatic and 22 asymptomatic patients at one time point. It shows an association between persistent symptoms and worse scores, and symptoms and poor function are partly the same phenomenon. Nothing in the study measures the impact of infection itself, because there is no uninfected group or pre-infection baseline, and no adjustment is made for age, comorbidity or severity. The causal wording in the conclusion goes beyond the design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-infection or uninfected-comparator data, or adjusted analyses supporting an effect of infection on these outcomes.

quotes.text: had a negative impact in the physical condition and functionality in ADL and quality-of-life
it was possible to confirm that the persistence of symptoms was associated with a worse physical condition

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion's wording that infection and symptom persistence 'had a negative impact' is causal, but the evidence is a single-time-point comparison within infected, referred patients (plus a non-matched external norm for infection), with no uninfected controls, no pre-infection baseline and no adjustment. The Discussion's 'associated with' is the supportable wording. The size of the group differences is real as reported, so the problem lies in the causal framing rather than the numbers.

issues.title: EQ-5D change of 0.5 on a 0-15 sum score is judged against a 0.03 utility-index minimal difference
issues.explanation: The Methods define the EQ-5D score as five domains each rated 0 to 3, and Table 4 reports a total of 7.1 falling to 6.6. The Discussion calls a decrease of around 0.03 in the EQ-D5 score the minimum clinically meaningful difference and concludes the QoL improvement is clinically relevant. That threshold belongs to a different scale (the utility index), so the comparison does not establish clinical relevance for the QoL change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A published minimal important difference for the 0-15 sum score used here, showing that 0.5 points exceeds it.

quotes.text: a decrease of around 0.03 in the EQ-D5 score
The average result of the EQ5D survey also had a drop of 0.5 points from 7.1 to 6.6

issues.title: ICU use stated as 51% in abstract and text, but Table 1 gives 51 patients (72% of 71)
issues.explanation: The abstract and the Results text say 51% of patients needed intensive care. Table 1 gives 51 (72%) among the 71 hospitalised patients, and Table 3 gives 37 + 14 = 51 ICU patients, so 51 is a count rather than a percentage. The headline hospital-severity figure is understated in the abstract and text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of the 51% denominator, for example a different population, that yields 51% from the paper's counts.

quotes.text: 51% necessitaram de cuidados intensivos

script.explanation: 51/71 = 71.83%, but the paper prints 51, outside the rounding interval [50.50, 52.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 100.0 rather than 71.

issues.title: Non-significant risk-factor comparisons (n = 51 vs 22) read as showing factors 'were not risk factors'
issues.explanation: The risk-factor analysis compares 51 and 22 patients with no sample-size justification and no confidence intervals. Differences such as complications (43% vs 19%, p = 0.053) and diabetes (29% vs 14%) are imprecise and cannot rule out effects of clinically meaningful size. The discussion concludes that sex, age, obesity and lung disease were not risk factors, which treats absence of significance as evidence of absence. The statement should have been that the study could not detect a difference.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A power calculation or confidence intervals showing that clinically important differences were excluded.

quotes.text: factors such as sex, old age, obesity or previous pulmonary disease were not risk factors for persistent disease in our population
The main limitations of this study are the reduced size of the study sample

issues.title: Symptomatic group is 51 in abstract and Tables 2-3 but 52 in the first-evaluation results text
issues.explanation: The abstract and Tables 2 and 3 give 51 symptomatic patients, while the Results text gives 52 for the same group. The tables footnote says one of the 74 patients was excluded for lack of symptom information, which fits 51 + 22 = 73 but not 52 + 22 = 74. The slip is small and the 70% figure is almost unchanged, but the text is internally inconsistent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 52 includes the patient later excluded for missing symptom data, with that patient actually classed as symptomatic.

quotes.text: Cinquenta e um (70%) tinham pelo menos um sintoma persistente
52 (70%) had at least one persistent symptom (Symptomatic Group)
Symptomatic (n = 51)

issues.title: Smokers/ex-smokers: 12 (18%) of 74 in Table 1 but 10 + 3 = 13 in Table 3 subgroups
issues.explanation: Table 1 gives 12 smokers or ex-smokers in the cohort of 74 and prints 18%. Table 3 gives 10 symptomatic and 3 asymptomatic smokers, which sum to 13 within a subset of that cohort. 12 out of 74 is 16%, not 18%, so Table 1 is inconsistent with both Table 3 and its own percentage. This is a minor slip that does not bear on any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing that one patient in Table 3 was not part of the 74-patient total.

script.explanation: 12/74 = 16.22%, but the paper prints 18, outside the rounding interval [17.50, 19.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 66.7 rather than 74.

10.20944/preprints202211.0400.v1.headline_claim: Adaptive force holding capacity (AFisomax) was substantially impaired in long COVID patients and normalised with health improvement, suggesting it is a sensitive functional parameter for assessing long COVID and supporting therapy.
10.20944/preprints202211.0400.v1.overall: The finding that AFisomax is lower before treatment and higher after treatment and at recovery in these 17 patients is supported descriptively. The paper cannot show that AF tracks recovery in general, or that it can support diagnosis or therapy choice, because there is no control or healthy comparison, testers were unblinded and the sample was selected on recovery. The numeric inconsistencies (trial counts, one impossible percentage, one df typo, elbow AFosc pairwise significance) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: AFisomax (maximal isometric adaptive force) across pre, post and end time points

issues.title: Uncontrolled pre-post design cannot show AF tracks recovery or can guide therapy choice
issues.explanation: All patients were measured before treatment, about 1 h after treatment, and at self-reported recovery, with no control group or healthy comparison and unblinded testers. The immediate rise in AFisomax cannot be separated from expectation, familiarisation or testing context, and the later normalisation cannot be separated from spontaneous recovery. The authors admit treatment causality is unknown, but still state that AF assessment might support diagnosis and the choice of an individual therapy approach. The data show only an association in 17 selected patients.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparison group (untreated long COVID, sham treatment, or repeated pre-pre measurements) showing the post change does not occur without treatment.

quotes.text: Therefore, a control group was not included.
Based on the present study, it cannot be judged whether the treatments were the reason for the recovery.
Nonetheless, its assessment might support the diagnostics of long COVID and especially the choice of the individual helpful therapy approach

second_reader.what_stands: The authors correctly state that the design cannot show whether treatments caused recovery and that spontaneous recovery is possible; this limitation is properly acknowledged. However, the design (no control group, 17 patients selected because they had improved, unblinded testers, no within-patient correlation of AF with symptoms) cannot establish that AF tracks recovery or can guide therapy choice. The paper's own data weaken the tracking claim: AF changed within about an hour of the first treatment without a health improvement, and was reported to fall back later. The therapy-guidance claim

issues.title: Unblinded testers applied the force and rated stability, knowing patient state
issues.explanation: The testers knew each patient's health state and subjectively rated stability. The authors reason that similar slope and AFmax across time points show no bias. This is plausible because AFisomax is derived from instrument signals, but it does not rule out subtle differences in force application at pre vs post/end. The effect cannot be quantified from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Repeat measurements by a tester blinded to time point, with the same AFisomax results.

quotes.text: Furthermore, the study was not blinded. The testers were aware of the patients' health state.
The MMTs were rated subjectively by the tester

issues.title: Analysed set restricted to 17 of 37 patients who had reported recovery (20 excluded)
issues.explanation: Only the 17 patients who felt substantially better by July 2022 entered the analysis, and the 20 who were still in therapy or had dropped out were left out. The 'normalisation with recovery' finding is therefore conditional on recovery, with no data on whether AF stays low in those who did not improve. The abstract and conclusions generalise to long COVID patients without stating the selection. This weakens the claim that AF tracks the recovery process.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: AF data from the 20 non-recovered patients showing persistently low AFisomax, or an analysis separating recovered from non-recovered patients.

quotes.text: Seventeen patients were included in this study since they reported a substantially improved or regained health state by July 2022.

issues.title: Elbow AFosc pairwise tests not significant, yet Discussion says AFosc was significantly higher pre vs post and end
issues.explanation: The Results say the elbow AFosc pairwise comparisons missed significance after Bonferroni correction. The Discussion then says AFosc was significantly higher for pre vs post and pre vs end, as hypothesized, without limiting this to hip flexors. Hypothesis 3 is therefore supported for hip flexors and only by the omnibus test (p = 0.012) for elbow. This is a secondary result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Discussion text that explicitly limits the claim to hip flexors, or elbow pairwise adjusted p-values below 0.05.

quotes.text: The pairwise comparisons missed significance after the Bonferroni correction (Figure 5a,d).
AFosc was significantly higher for pre vs. post and pre vs. end, as was hypothesized.

issues.title: Discussion rating counts (84 pre; 4 of 173 unstable post/end) do not match Table 1 (87 pre; 5 of 175)
issues.explanation: Table 1 gives 87 unstable pre-treatment trials and 5 unstable plus 164 stable plus 6 unclear (175) at post/end. The Discussion gives 84 at pre and 4 unstable of 173 at post/end. Exclusion of invalid trials may explain some of the gap, but the paper does not say so, and the totals still do not reconcile (257 vs 256 valid trials). This is a small reporting inconsistency and does not change the finding that nearly all pre trials were rated unstable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 84 and 173 counts exclude specific invalid trials, with counts that sum to the 256 valid trials.

quotes.text: All 84 MMTs at pre were assessed as 'unstable' by the testers.
as 'unstable' in four of 173 cases and as 'unclear' in six of 173 cases.
In total, 141 valid trials were gathered for the evaluation of hip flexors and 115 for elbow flexors

issues.title: End-point job-stress share of 30.33% is not attainable with n = 12
issues.explanation: With 12 patients the possible shares are 25.00% (3/12) or 33.33% (4/12), not 30.33%. The figure is probably a typo for 33.33%. It is a descriptive secondary statistic and nothing in the main findings depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the denominator for the job-related item differs from 12 so that 30.33% is attainable (it is not for any n of 12 to about 20).

quotes.text: at timepoint end, they amounted to 30.33% and 50.00% (n = 12), respectively.

issues.title: Text gives n = 11 for personal stress before COVID; Table 3 gives n = 12
issues.explanation: The Results attach one n of 11 to both the job-related and personal stress percentages before COVID. Table 3 gives n = 11 for job-related stress and n = 12 for personal stress. A reader cannot tell whether the 100% is 11/11 or 12/12. This is a small labelling inconsistency.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data in Table S2 showing that 11 patients answered the personal-stress item.

quotes.text: which were rated with an intensity of ≥ 2 in 90.91% and 100%, respectively (n = 11)

issues.title: Hip AFosc/AFisomax pre-vs-end test printed as t(17); with 17 patients the df should be 16
issues.explanation: All other hip paired tests use df 16, and the printed d implies n = 17 pairs. The t(17) is a typographical slip. The significance conclusion is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that an additional hip observation was included in this comparison only.

10.20944/preprints202309.0782.v1.headline_claim: A 4-week pulmonary telerehabilitation program (breathing plus aerobic exercises) is feasible and effective for young adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome.
10.20944/preprints202309.0782.v1.overall: The headline claim that the program is feasible and effective rests on a retrospective, non-randomized, unblinded 8 vs 8 comparison with a no-activity control, which the abstract mislabels as randomized. Several reported statistics are internally inconsistent: text versus table p-values, duplicated F values, implausible HR and RR magnitudes, and misattributed gains in the Discussion. The data can support a hypothesis of benefit, but not the effectiveness claim or the SpO2 claim.

primary_outcome.name: not prespecified in paper; physical capacity (1-min sit-to-stand) and cardiorespiratory capacity (6MWT) are the main reported outcomes

issues.title: Abstract says randomized; Methods describe retrospective convenience allocation to a no-activity control
issues.explanation: The abstract says 16 students were randomized, but the Methods describe a retrospective study with assignment by convenience after participants committed to the program, and a control group that did nothing. Allocation therefore depended on non-random factors such as commitment, and baseline differences exist (e.g. SBP 107.8 vs 122.5, 6MWT 461.6 vs 403.3). Between-group differences cannot be attributed to the program, and the abstract's label misleads readers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A documented random sequence generation and concealed allocation procedure.

quotes.text: Sixteen university students were randomized
The subjects were assigned by convenience

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract says participants were randomized, but the Methods describe a retrospective file review with convenience assignment to a no-activity control, and give no randomization procedure. The abstract wording is inconsistent with the stated design. Convenience allocation after commitment to continue also leaves room for selection bias.

issues.title: Pilot of 16 (8 per arm) with no sample-size rationale concludes the program is 'effective'
issues.explanation: The study is a small, non-randomized, unblinded pilot with no power calculation and a no-treatment control. It nevertheless concludes in the abstract and Conclusion that the program is effective in treating post-COVID-19 syndrome. At best it supports feasibility and a hypothesis of benefit; effectiveness is not shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified power calculation and a randomized, controlled analysis supporting efficacy.

quotes.text: The aim of this pilot study
effective in treating postCOVID-19 syndrome in young patients

second_reader.what_stands: A pilot of 16 participants (8 per arm) with no sample-size rationale and a non-randomized, convenience-allocated control concludes the program is 'effective in treating' post-COVID-19 syndrome. The small sample is acknowledged as a limitation. The causal 'effective' claim is stronger than the design supports, and feasibility outcomes such as adherence are not actually reported.

issues.title: SpO2 improvement claimed from a within-EG test although the group x time interaction was non-significant
issues.explanation: For SpO2 the ANOVA interaction was not significant (p > 0.143), while the CG also rose (91.4 to 92.1). The significant EG pre/post p of 0.042 is a within-group result and no multiplicity correction is mentioned. The abstract and Conclusion nonetheless present SpO2 as improved by the program.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant between-group SpO2 contrast or interaction.

quotes.text: can lead to improvements in SpO2, physical and cardiorespiratory capacities

second_reader.what_stands: The SpO2 group x time interaction was non-significant (p about 0.143), so the data do not show that the program improved SpO2 relative to control. The claim rests on a within-EG p = 0.042 that was not corrected for multiple outcomes and is not supported by the interaction. The Discussion also says none of the SpO2 changes was significant, which conflicts with the Abstract and Conclusion.

issues.title: Post-hoc p-values in Results text differ from Table 3/abstract for HR, RR, sit-to-stand and 6MWT
issues.explanation: The Results text gives EG post-hoc p-values of <0.001 (HR), <0.031 (RR), <0.002 (sit-to-stand) and <0.001 (6MWT). Table 3 and the abstract give 0.012, 0.012, 0.012 and 0.028 for the same comparisons. Three EG cells carry an identical 0.012, and no p-value in either place can be confirmed. All four effects are still nominally significant at 0.05 either way, so the direction of the findings holds, but the reported precision cannot be trusted.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text values are Tukey interaction contrasts and the table values are separate within-group tests, with the unadjusted outputs supplied.

quotes.text: significant decrease in heart ( p < 0.001)
in the EG after treatment ( p < 0.002)
significant decrease of RR and HR ( p < 0.012)

issues.title: Table 3 HR (~20) and RR (~73) values are physiologically implausible and appear swapped
issues.explanation: Table 3 lists HR as about 20 to 22 and RR as about 65 to 74, whereas resting adults have roughly the reverse. The table's rows appear to have their labels swapped, and the Discussion carries the swap into its text (HR down 4, RR down 8.7). The measurement scale cannot be taken at face value.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing HR near 20 and RR near 73 in this sample, which is not physiologically plausible.

quotes.text: RR= Respiratory rate; HR= Heart rate

issues.title: Physical and cardiorespiratory interaction tests share F(1,14)=15.121 but have p < 0.006 and p < 0.002
issues.explanation: The same F statistic with the same degrees of freedom cannot give two different p-values. One of the F values or p-values for the sit-to-stand and 6MWT interactions is misreported, so it is unclear which interaction result is correct.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Output showing different F values for the two interactions.

issues.title: 2 of 18 eligible students did not complete the program; completer-only analysis
issues.explanation: Two of 18 eligible students did not finish the program, and the analysis uses the 16 who did. The arm and reasons for non-completion are not reported. The loss is small, but a completer-only analysis could favor the program if non-completers did worse.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the two were excluded before allocation, or a sensitivity analysis including them.

quotes.text: but two of them did not complete the program

issues.title: Discussion gives EG gains as 1.7 repetitions and 7.5 m, but Table 3 gives 4.9 and 217.5 m
issues.explanation: One Discussion sentence says the EG improved by 1.7 sit-to-stand repetitions and 7.5 m on the 6MWT. Table 3 and a later sentence give 4.9 repetitions and 217.5 m for the EG. The 1.7 and 7.5 values are the control group's changes. This is an internal contradiction in the text, but it affects no table or test result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the 1.7 and 7.5 figures refer to a different EG measure, such as a between-group difference.

quotes.text: The EG increased the number of times it could stand up and sit down from a chair by 1.7
the distance covered after 6 minutes by 7.5 meters

issues.title: EG SpO2 gain printed as 2.3% in Discussion; Table 3 means give 3.0 points
issues.explanation: The Discussion states an EG SpO2 increase of 2.3, whereas the Table 3 pre and post means (91.3 and 94.3) differ by 3.0. The CG figure matches the table, so the EG figure is an isolated inconsistency. It slightly understates the table's change, and the SpO2 interaction is non-significant anyway.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that the 2.3 is a mean of individual changes using different data than Table 3.

10.20944/preprints202407.2492.v1.headline_claim: A marine oil supplement enriched in specialized pro-resolving mediators raises serum monohydroxylated SPMs at 500 mg/day and improves fatigue and dyspnea in post-COVID syndrome, supporting its use for PCS management.
10.20944/preprints202407.2492.v1.overall: The finding that serum monohydroxylated SPMs rise after supplementation is plausible from the before/after data, but it is not shown to differ by dose or against placebo. The 'clear' fatigue and dyspnea improvement at 500 mg comes from an open-label, uncontrolled arm of 16, and all between-group symptom tests are null. The claim should be read as exploratory and hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: Serum concentrations of monohydroxylated SPMs (14-HDHA, 17-HDHA, 18-HEPE) and pro-inflammatory/pro-resolving ratio

issues.title: 'Clear' 500 mg benefit claimed from within-group change although all between-group tests are null
issues.explanation: The 500 mg dose is declared best because the doses did not differ significantly, which is not evidence for that dose. Fatigue and dyspnea changes are within-group trends, with between-group p = 0.509 and 0.600 for mMRC and no significant FSS differences. The pro-inflammatory sum did not change significantly (p = 0.232). The paper also says both that multiple-testing corrections were used and that there was no adjustment. The study cannot show a dose-specific or placebo-adjusted benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Placebo-adjusted between-group analyses showing significantly larger improvement at 500 mg than placebo, with multiplicity handled.

quotes.text: There were no differences found between the three treatment groups.
Given that there were no statistically significant differences between the dosages of 500 mg, 1500 mg, and 3000 mg, a clear trend of favoring a 500 mg dosage per day can be postulated.
a clear improvement in fatigue and dyspnea was observed with this dosage.

second_reader.what_stands: All between-group comparisons are null (e.g. p=0.509 for mMRC), so the claim that 500 mg is favored or 'clearly' improves fatigue and dyspnea rests on descriptive within-group changes and a numerically higher share of improvers, not on any test. The authors do hedge in places with 'trend' and 'exploratory', but the Abstract Conclusions and Section 5 state 'clear improvement' without that qualifier.

issues.title: 500 mg group is unblinded and uncontrolled, yet carries the efficacy claim on patient-reported symptoms
issues.explanation: Group X received no placebo and no masking, yet the conclusions say fatigue and dyspnea clearly improved at 500 mg. Fatigue (FSS) and dyspnea (mMRC) are subjective, so expectation effects and natural recovery cannot be separated from any treatment effect. The paper itself notes a natural trend of improvement. Only five patients received placebo, and the symptom analyses show no significant group differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded, placebo-controlled comparison showing a significantly larger symptom improvement at 500 mg than in the placebo group.

quotes.text: the fourth to the independent, non-controlled, low-dose group (X)
except for group X, who were not blinded, for whom the products were thus not masked
Another limitation may be the fact that there is a natural trend of improvement in symptoms in patients with Post-COVID syndrome.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper itself states that the 500 mg group (X) was non-controlled and unmasked, and its fatigue and dyspnea outcomes are patient-reported scales. The conclusion nonetheless credits 500 mg with 'a clear improvement' in both, and the only limitation named is the natural trend of improvement, which is acknowledged but not weighed against that claim. The unblinded, uncontrolled design cannot separate a supplement effect from expectation or natural recovery.

issues.title: Dyspnea table analyses 51 of 53 randomised patients (A 15 vs 16, placebo 4 vs 5), unexplained
issues.explanation: The methods allocate 16/16/5/16 patients, but the week-12 dyspnea table totals 15 in group A and 4 in the placebo group. Two patients are therefore missing from this analysis, with no participant flow or reasons given. The placebo arm drops from 5 to 4, which matters when it is the only blinded control. The effect on the conclusions is small but the analysis population is undefined.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant flow diagram or text stating that two patients (one in A, one in placebo) withdrew or had missing week-12 mMRC data.

quotes.text: Group C: Placebo N = 5 patients;
Group A: N = 16 patients;
Data are displayed as N(%). Chi-square: X-squared = 8.2496, df = 9, p -value = 0.509

issues.title: Pilot with 5 placebo and 16 per active arm and no sample-size calculation; tests cannot detect group differences
issues.explanation: No sample-size calculation is reported, and a 5-patient placebo arm gives almost no power to detect differences in symptoms or lipid mediators. The non-significant between-group results therefore say little either way. This is acceptable for a declared pilot, but it weakens any dose-specific conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified power calculation showing adequate power for the between-group comparisons.

quotes.text: The limitations of this pivotal trial include the small number of recruited patients

issues.title: Methods both claim and deny multiple-testing correction across many mediator tests
issues.explanation: One sentence says ANOVA used multiple testing corrections, and the next says p-values below 0.05 were significant because there was no adjustment. Many analytes and time points are tested, so it is unclear which p-values are adjusted. The headline p-values such as 0.025 for the ratio are therefore hard to interpret.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that all reported p-values are unadjusted, or the adjusted values with the correction method.

quotes.text: Changes from the baseline were calculated using the ANOVA test, using multiple testing corrections
p -values below 0.05 were rated statistically significant as there was no adjustment for multiple testing.

10.20944/preprints202408.0871.v1.headline_claim: Feasibility of monitoring Long COVID symptoms with the digitalised C19-YRS (ELAROS) is shown, and pain and anxiety are most likely to improve after LC rehabilitation clinic attendance while swallowing difficulty is least likely to improve.
10.20944/preprints202408.0871.v1.overall: The descriptive result, that most patients report some symptom improvement and that digital C19-YRS monitoring is feasible, is reasonably supported. The claim that rehabilitation makes pain and anxiety most likely to improve is not supported by an uncontrolled, selected completer cohort of 50 with no inferential statistics. The Table 2 swallowing-row count error and the outcome-list mismatch are minor reporting slips.

primary_outcome.name: Symptom severity change on C19-YRS items between initial and final assessment (no single prespecified primary outcome reported)

issues.title: Uncontrolled before-after cohort (n = 50) used to name symptoms 'most likely to improve with intervention'
issues.explanation: Patients were compared with their own first assessment only, with no control group, no formal change analysis and no confidence intervals. Natural recovery, regression to the mean and the variable follow-up interval (about 6 to 26+ weeks) cannot be separated from any rehabilitation effect. Descriptions of improvement are supported, but the claims that symptoms are 'most likely to improve after intervention' and that clinic intervention effects have been 'identified' are stronger than this design can show. The wording throughout (conclusions and discussion) also implies a causal benefit of the clinic.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A matched untreated comparison group, or conclusions limited to describing within-patient change without attributing it to the clinic.

quotes.text: As this study was observational, it did not have a control arm to assess the natural progression of long COVID symptoms in the absence of our rehabilitation intervention.
Pain and anxiety symptoms are most likely to improve after intervention at long COVID clinic whereas swallowing difficulty is least likely to improve.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is an uncontrolled, single-arm before-after cohort of 50 patients, and the Abstract and Conclusions name symptoms 'most likely to improve after intervention' without a comparator, without confidence intervals or tests, and with differences between top symptoms of only a few patients (pain/anxiety 64% vs depression 58%). The Discussion does acknowledge the absence of a control arm and the Conclusions call for further research, so the limitation is disclosed rather than ignored, but the causal wording ('after intervention', 'with ... intervention') and the ranking of symptoms outrun wh

issues.title: Only completers of 2+ assessments analysed; number of eligible attenders and exclusions not reported
issues.explanation: Inclusion required a follow-up assessment at least 6 weeks later and under 25% missing data, but the paper does not say how many patients attended the clinic or how many were excluded. Completers may differ from dropouts, and the authors note that this selection may have favoured patients who had more health issues upfront. The size and direction of the selection effect cannot be assessed, which limits how far the improvement percentages can be generalised to clinic patients.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow count showing that nearly all clinic attenders met the inclusion criteria, or a comparison of baseline characteristics between included and excluded patients.

quotes.text: We have selected patients who completed their C19-YRS (>75% completion) as per our inclusion/ exclusion criteria
A total of 50 patients have submitted 186 assessments during their attendance

issues.title: Swallowing row: '54% (n = 7)' conflicts with n = 50; row counts sum to 30, not 50
issues.explanation: In Table 2 the 'No symptoms all time' cell for swallowing reads 54% (n = 7), but 7 of 50 is 14%, not 54%. The row's counts add to 30, while every other row adds to 50. Replacing 7 with 27 would fix both the percentage and the total, so this looks like a typo in one count. The qualitative finding on swallowing is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A source table showing 7 patients with no symptoms in the swallowing row and a different denominator for that row.

quotes.location: Table 2, Difficulty in swallowing row, No symptoms all time column

quotes.text: A total of 50 patients have submitted 186 assessments during their attendance

script.explanation: 7/50 = 14.00%, but the paper prints 54, outside the rounding interval [53.50, 55.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 13.0 rather than 50.

issues.title: Methods says 16 outcomes assessed but lists 17; Table 2 has 17 rows with mobility instead of overall health
issues.explanation: The Methods say 16 outcomes were assessed, but the list that follows names 17 items, ending with overall health. Table 2 also has 17 rows, but it includes 'Mobility Problems', which the list omits, and it has no overall health row. The number and identity of the analysed outcomes are therefore described inconsistently. This does not change the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that overall health was analysed separately and that mobility was counted within another item, giving 16.

quotes.text: 16  patient-reported  outcomes  of  a  total  of  22  items  were  assessed
issues with personal care, issues with ADLS, issues with caring for family/ social life and overall health
quotes.location: Methods and Study Population, list of outcomes

10.20953/1729-9225-2021-4-15-22.headline_claim: Azoximer bromide demonstrated clinical efficacy and safety in the treatment of post-COVID syndrome.
10.20953/1729-9225-2021-4-15-22.overall: The efficacy and safety conclusion for azoximer bromide cannot be relied on: it rests on an open, non-randomized comparison with an untreated group, self-rated diary outcomes and uncorrected multiple testing. Table 3 contains values that are arithmetically impossible on the stated scale and conflict with Table 2, and the validated fatigue measure shows no benefit. At most, the data suggest hypotheses about reduced headache and joint pain frequency.

primary_outcome.name: Resolution of post-COVID syndrome symptoms (duration and severity of main symptoms over 10 days)

issues.title: Open-label, non-randomized comparison with an untreated group and self-rated outcomes, unequal at baseline
issues.explanation: Participants chose or were placed in the drug or no-treatment group by an undescribed method, with no placebo and no blinding. Outcomes are patient-rated symptom diaries, so expectation effects, regression to the mean (the treated arm started higher on fatigue and sleep) and natural recovery all remain as explanations for the day-10 differences. Group differences at day 10 therefore cannot be attributed to the drug.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random or concealed allocation, a blinded or objective outcome assessment, or baseline-adjusted analyses giving the same result.

quotes.text: Группу сравнения составили 35 человек, которые не получали медицинских препаратов.
является проспективным открытым сравнительным неинтервенционным клиническим исследованием в параллельных группах
(1,70 ± 0,68 балла в исследуемой группе против 1,00 ± 0,23 балла в группе сравнения)

second_reader.what_stands: The study is open-label and non-randomized, with an untreated comparison group, subjective self-reported outcomes and acknowledged baseline differences on some symptoms. The paper does not say how participants were assigned to groups, and it uses no baseline adjustment or multiplicity control. Causal attribution of between-group differences to the drug is therefore weak.

issues.title: Table 2 counts and Table 3 means cannot both hold: headache mean 1,00 ± 0,39 with 10/55; dizziness 55/55 with 1,16
issues.explanation: The severity scale runs from 1 (not expressed) to 4, so a mean of 1,00 cannot come with a non-zero SD. Table 3 prints this for headache, joint pain, attention impairment and other rows, and the headlined day-10 differences in headache and dizziness rest on these values. Dizziness is recorded as present in all 55 treated patients (and all 35 controls) at every visit, yet the treated mean is 1,16, essentially 'not expressed'. The significant severity reductions cannot be trusted until the underlying data are clarified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of how absent symptoms were scored and which patients enter each mean, under which the Table 2 and Table 3 values reconcile.

quotes.location: Table 3, Headache row, day 10 experimental column
Table 2, Headache row, day 10 experimental column

quotes.text: головокружения (1,16 ± 0,42 балла против 2,03 ± 0,17 балла в группе сравнения)

second_reader.what_stands: The headache entry is internally impossible as printed: a mean of 1,00 with SD 0,39 cannot arise from scores of at least 1 on the 1-4 scale, whichever denominator is used. The dizziness half is not a contradiction, because 100% 'present' with a mean of 1,16 is plausible if a score of 1 counts as present. It does show that Table 2 presence is poorly defined, since 1 is 'not expressed'.

issues.title: Conclusion claims efficacy and safety, but fatigue (FAS) null, loss-of-smell p=0,054, and 10 days with no follow-up
issues.explanation: The conclusion says azoximer bromide reduced fatigue and loss of smell significantly and was effective and safe. The validated fatigue questionnaire shows no group difference, day-10 fatigue incidence was higher in treated patients (100% vs 88,57%), and the loss-of-smell frequency comparison gave p = 0,054. The study ran 10 days with no follow-up period, a non-randomized untreated control and no safety design, so 'efficacy and safety' overreaches.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded or randomized analysis with a prespecified primary endpoint, and a significant FAS result.

quotes.text: Применение азоксимера бромида статистически значимо снижало выраженность общей слабости

quotes.location: Results, para on loss of smell

quotes.text: Период наблюдения в данном исследовании отсутствовал.

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion states unqualified 'clinical efficacy and safety' and a significant fatigue reduction. The paper's own data show no significant FAS effect, no day-10 significance marker for fatigue severity, and more fatigue complaints in the treated group at day 10. The loss-of-smell frequency difference has p=0,054, above the paper's own threshold. Safety was observed for only 10 days in 55 people with no follow-up, which is too little to support a safety conclusion.

issues.title: About 15 symptoms at three visits tested at alpha 0.05 with no correction or primary outcome
issues.explanation: The paper tests many symptoms at days 1, 5 and 10 with a per-test threshold of 0.05 and names no primary endpoint. A few nominally significant results are then listed as efficacy findings. The smallest p-values would probably hold up, but the loss-of-smell result (p=0,03) and the day-5 fatigue result (p=0,02) are weak under any correction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or a multiplicity adjustment under which the headlined results remain significant.

quotes.text: значимости тестов выбрана вероятность ошибки первого рода, меньшая или равная 0,05

issues.title: Overall mean age 35,31 ± 8,15 in text vs 35,04 ± 6,69 in Table 1 total column
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 1 give different overall mean ages and SDs for the same 90 participants. The table value agrees with its own arm means; the text value does not. The error is in a descriptive statistic and does not affect efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text figure refers to a different population (e.g. all screened participants), or a corrected Table 1.

quotes.text: составил 35,31 ± 8,15 года

issues.title: Student t-tests applied to 4-point ordinal symptom scores with many tied values
issues.explanation: Scores take only four values and many cells are at the floor of the scale, so normality is doubtful. A rank-based test would be safer. It is unlikely on its own to change the picture.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A nonparametric reanalysis giving the same significance.
