10.21203/rs.3.rs-4112790/v1.headline_claim: Daily ribavirin doses identified by EAV medicament testing may serve as a prognostic marker of the course of long COVID, and the method is feasible.
10.21203/rs.3.rs-4112790/v1.overall: The headline claim that tested ribavirin dose may be a prognostic marker of long COVID course is not supported: no clinical outcome was measured, the dose and the reading come from the same device procedure, and 38% of patients were lost with completer-only analysis. At most the paper shows a procedural feasibility description and internal correlations between device readings.

primary_outcome.name: Association between EAV pretest readings and medicament-tested daily ribavirin dose (Spearman correlation)

issues.title: Outcome (EAV impedance and device-tested ribavirin dose) is unvalidated and circular, with no clinical endpoint
issues.explanation: The 'tested dose' is derived from the same EAV device reading it is later correlated with, so the relation is largely built in. No clinical outcome (symptoms, viral persistence, disease course) is measured, and the placebo arm gets glucose tablets tested with the same device. Nothing shows that the dose reflects disease status.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Independent validation showing tested dose predicts a clinical outcome in long COVID.

quotes.text: The AMV is calculated by subtracting the resulting EAV reading (E) and the lower level of the energy balance indicator (50) and is equal to E minus 50.
The number of tablets at which a positive response was observed was calculated by normalizing the absolute value of the EAV device readings

second_reader.what_stands: Both the outcome (EAV impedance reading) and the 'dose' (tablets needed to normalize that reading) come from the same device measurement. The dose-to-reading association is therefore largely built into the procedure, and the paper offers no independent validation or clinical endpoint. Feasibility is the stated aim, but the data cannot show that the dose reflects anything about the patient's disease.

issues.title: Prognostic-marker claim in title and conclusions unsupported: no disease-course outcome was measured
issues.explanation: The study reports only correlations between two readings from the same device and changes in readings across years. Disease course, symptoms or any clinical outcome are never measured, so the claim that tested dose predicts the chronic course has no data behind it. The limited hedging does not offset the title and conclusion wording.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data linking tested dose to clinical course outcomes.

quotes.text: The measured daily dose of ribavirin in patients with long COVID syndrome may indirectly serve as a prognostic marker of the course of the disease.
However, this statement requires further study.

second_reader.what_stands: The title, abstract, Discussion and Conclusions describe the tested dose as a possible prognostic marker or predictor of disease course, but no disease-course data were collected or analyzed. The caveats ('may', 'further studies') soften the claim without removing it, and the Discussion's statement that the data allowed prediction of disease course is stronger than anything the results show.

issues.title: 38% attrition (44/96 vs 19/68), differential, with completer-only analysis and no sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Of 164 allocated, only 101 were analysed. Loss was much higher in the experimental arm, so the groups analysed need not be comparable, and the between-group comparisons in Table 4 rest on completers. No handling of missing data is described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An intention-to-treat or sensitivity analysis showing the same results with all 164.

quotes.text: In the experimental group, 44 patients and 19 in the placebo group dropped out of the study
The final numbers of patients were 52 (51.5%) and 49 (48.5%).

second_reader.what_stands: Overall attrition was 38.4% (63/164), and it was higher in the experimental arm (45.8%) than in the placebo arm (27.9%). Analyses use only the 52 and 49 completers, and no ITT analysis, imputation or sensitivity analysis is described in Section 2.4. Dropout reasons are listed but not compared between arms, and baseline characteristics of completers versus dropouts are not given.

issues.title: Correlation analysis ignores repeated measures, uses unexplained n (32/41), and has a Kr 2023 ρ mismatch
issues.explanation: Correlations are computed separately for each year on the same patients with no handling of non-independence or multiplicity across many tests. Table 5 uses n = 32 and 41, not the 52 experimental completers, without explanation. The text prints ρ = -0.866 for Kr 2023 whereas Table 5 gives -0.826824.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that the correlations used subsets with complete data and a mixed model accounting for repeated measures.

quotes.text: Spearman's correlation coefficients were as follows: ρ = -0.821, ρ = -0.828 and ρ = -0.866 for the Kr meridian in the 2020–2021, 2022 and 2023 periods, respectively (p < 0,001).
Kr_Ribavirin2023 & Kr_pre-test2023

second_reader.what_stands: The 2023 Kr coefficient in the text (-0.866) conflicts with Table 5 (-0.8268), which is internally consistent. The samples of 32 and 41 are not explained against the 52 experimental completers. The same patients appear across the three periods, and the paper does not address this dependence in its p-values or period comparisons. Each coefficient is, however, computed within a single period, so the repeated-measures problem is narrower than 'correlation analysis ignores repeated measures' implies.

issues.title: Abstract labels 101 completers as randomized/recruited; Section 2.2 randomized 164 (96 + 68)
issues.explanation: The abstract says 101 patients were recruited and 52 and 49 were randomized to the two groups. Section 2.2 shows 164 were allocated (96 and 68), and 52 and 49 are the completers after 44 and 19 dropouts. The arithmetic reconciles, but the abstract presents the analysed completers as the randomized sample and hides 38% attrition.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing 101 randomized with no post-randomization losses.

quotes.text: Fifty-two participants were randomized to the experimental group and fourty nine to the placebo group and were considered for data analyses.
In this group of patients, the experimental group comprised 96 (58.5%), and the placebo group comprised 68 (41.5%).

issues.title: Described as blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with no registration or blinding details
issues.explanation: The paper calls itself a blind randomized placebo-controlled trial but reports no registry number, sample size calculation, allocation concealment or who was blinded. Prespecification cannot be verified. The weight is limited because no confirmatory efficacy claim is made.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry and a description of who was blinded.

quotes.text: This blind randomized placebo-controlled trial aimed to investigate the potential of EAV diagnosis

10.21203/rs.3.rs-4213319/v1.headline_claim: Cognitive behavioral therapy added to physiotherapy is a beneficial program for reducing depression and improving functional outcomes in post-COVID-19 patients.
10.21203/rs.3.rs-4213319/v1.overall: The paper's headline claim that CBT added to physiotherapy reduces depression and improves function rests on a small, unblinded trial with a self-reported primary outcome, retrospective registration and an unreported registered primary outcome (MMSE). Internal contradictions (the inverted alpha, the Discussion denying a functional difference) show careless reporting, and the key tables were not recoverable. The direction of the effect is plausible, but its size is uncertain.

primary_outcome.name: Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Katz ADL index (paper reports both as primary-level outcomes; registry lists MMSE, BDI, Katz as primary)

primary_outcomes.time_frame: The MMSE is easily administered and requires only 5-10 minutes to complete depending on the impairment of the individual
easily administered and requires only 5-10 minutes to complete depending on the impairment of the individual

primary_outcomes.measure: .Katz Index of Independence in Activities of Daily Living
primary_outcomes.time_frame: easily administered and requires only 5-10 minutes to complete depending on the impairment of the individual

issues.title: Self-reported BDI primary outcome with no blinding described; registry claims quadruple masking
issues.explanation: The BDI is a self-report questionnaire and the paper describes no blinding of participants or assessors. The study group received an extra, visibly different component, so expectancy effects can inflate the self-reported benefit. The registry says masking was quadruple, but the paper does not say how this could have been achieved. The depression result is therefore weaker than it appears.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of how participants and outcome assessors were masked.

quotes.text: The BDI is a 21-item self-report questionnaire used to assess the severity of depression in both normal and psychiatric populations

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes no blinding of any kind and its primary depression outcome is a self-reported BDI in an open add-on design, with no limitation noted about this. The registry's current record states quadruple masking, which is inconsistent with the paper's silence and with the design; earlier registry versions were not checked, so what was originally registered is unknown.

issues.title: Discussion says no posttreatment functional differences; Results report Katz difference p = 0.001
issues.explanation: The Results and Abstract report that posttreatment Katz scores differed significantly between groups (p = 0.001). The Discussion states the present study found no such differences in functional impairment posttreatment. This is an internal contradiction about one of the two primary outcomes. The Results and Conclusion agree with each other, so it is most likely a drafting error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Discussion stating that differences were found would resolve it.

quotes.text: The present study demonstrated that there were no such differences in functional impairment among the groups posttreatment.
posttreatment Katz index mean values were signicantly different between groups (p = 0.001)

issues.title: Registered primary outcome MMSE is not reported; only BDI and Katz are analysed
issues.explanation: The registry lists three primary outcomes, including MMSE, but the paper reports only BDI and Katz. MMSE appears only as an inclusion criterion, so a registered primary outcome is silently dropped. The two reported outcomes were registered, so nothing was swapped in. The paper's conclusion about depression and function is not contradicted but the omission is not explained.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that MMSE was reported elsewhere or removed before data collection.

quotes.text: The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score was used to measure depression severity, while functional outcomes were evaluated by the Katz Index of Independence in Activities of Daily Living.

issues.title: Trial registered 10/07/2023 (registry: 2023-08-05), after data collection began in January 2023
issues.explanation: The paper reports data collection from January to August 2023 and registration on 10/07/2023, so the protocol was registered after enrolment had started. The registry record gives a start of 2023-05-04 and first submission 2023-08-05, which is also after the start. The paper's date differs from the registry's, which adds uncertainty. The registered outcomes cannot be assumed to be the pre-specified ones.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry history showing a registration before the first participant was enrolled.

quotes.text: the date of rst registration is 10/07/2023
The data were collected from January 2023 to August 2023

issues.title: MANOVA named for a two-group pre/post design; model for baseline and change is not specified
issues.explanation: The paper names MANOVA 'to compare all variables of both groups' without saying how baseline, repeated measures or multiple outcomes were handled. With n = 36 and two outcomes, it is unclear whether the between-group tests are on change scores, post scores, or both. Table 2 and 3 contents are not extractable here, so the appropriateness cannot be checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A model specification showing ANCOVA or mixed-model analysis adjusting for baseline.

quotes.text: Multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) was utilized to compare all variables of both groups.

issues.title: Physiotherapy dose differs between arms (1-2 sets x 8-10 vs 2-5 sets x 15-20) despite 'same' program
issues.explanation: The control group received a full hour of physiotherapy at higher sets and repetitions, while the study group got 30 minutes at lower volume plus 30 minutes of CBT. The paper calls the physiotherapy 'the same' program, but the dose differs. This works against the CBT arm for physical outcomes (so the effect on function may be understated), but it means the arms differ in more than the CBT component. It does not undermine the trial's session-time matching.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol stating that both groups had identical physiotherapy volume.

quotes.text: Patients were given the same selected physiotherapy program only (2-5 sets with 15-20 repetitions) for one hour per session
for 1-2 sets with 8-10 repetitions each

issues.title: Methods define significance as 'p > 0.05' (inverted), while results use p ≤ 0.05
issues.explanation: The statistical analysis section says an alpha of p > 0.05 indicates significance, which is the reverse of the convention. The Results and Table 1 footnote treat p ≤ 0.05 as significant, so this is a printed slip rather than a changed analysis. No result depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: n/a; the slip is plain on the page, though it is harmless.

quotes.text: An alpha point of p > 0.05 was considered to indicate statistical signicance.

10.21203/rs.3.rs-4391458/v1.headline_claim: Daily high-dose wearable TENS was feasible, acceptable, and improved pain-related functional interference relative to low-dose TENS, gait parameters, and (in an FM subgroup) fatigue interference in people with PASC.
10.21203/rs.3.rs-4391458/v1.overall: The headline claim of a greater BPI-I decrease with high-dose TENS is weakly supported: the 4-week difference is about the size of an unadjusted baseline gap, within-group changes were not significant, and the analysis covers only 23 to 25 of 30 randomized. The fatigue and gait claims rest on within-group changes in very small groups and should be read as hypothesis-generating. The CI sign slip in Table 3 is minor and the p-value itself is arithmetically consistent.

primary_outcome.name: BPI-I (functional interference from pain, Brief Pain Inventory interference composite)

checklist.blinding: participants and care providers blinded; investigators collecting and analysing data not blinded

primary_outcomes.measure: Mean Change in Functional Interference From Pain From Baseline to 4 Weeks (Blinded Phase)

issues.title: BPI-I 'greater decrease' (-2.61) is about the size of the 2.37-point baseline gap; no adjustment made
issues.explanation: The IG began with a much lower BPI-I than the PG (3.17 vs 5.54, p = 0.021), and the authors explicitly made no covariate adjustment. The reported 4-week difference of 2.6 points is close to that baseline gap, while the within-group changes are small and neither is significant. So the claim of a 'greater decrease' with high-dose TENS is not supported by this analysis, and the stated Cohen's d of 1.12 is likely inflated by the imbalance. With 12 vs 13 participants, a 26-person requirement and the target of 30 missed, the result is at best hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A baseline-adjusted (ANCOVA or GEE with baseline covariate) analysis showing a similar between-group difference in change scores.

quotes.text: Baseline BPI-I was signicantly higher in the PG than the IG (Table 2).
No covariates adjustments were made due to low sample size.
However, within-group comparison did not show signicant improvement (Table 3).

second_reader.what_stands: The 2.61-point 4-week difference is about the size of the 2.37-point baseline gap (IG lower), and the differential change is only about 0.26 points with no significant within-group change in either arm. No baseline or covariate adjustment was done, so the 'greater decrease' wording is not supported by the printed numbers; the difference is mostly the baseline gap persisting.

issues.title: FM sub-group GFI gain (n = 5) headlined from within-group change; between-group p = 0.161
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion highlight a significant within-group GFI improvement of 6.08 in five treated FM participants. The between-group comparison in that sub-group is not significant (difference -3.806, CI -9.132 to 1.52, p = 0.161), and the PG-FM also improved by 1.75; the full-cohort GFI comparison was also null (p = 0.867). A within-group change in five people without a significant contrast against placebo cannot show a treatment effect on fatigue. The text's SE of 10.61 also conflicts with the table's 2.188.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant between-group GFI contrast in the FM sub-group, or a pre-specified FM sub-group analysis with correction.

quotes.text: Moreover, the IG-FM showed a signicant improvement in GFI scores at 4-weeks from baseline (mean change = 6.08 [SE = 10.61], p = 0.005).
those individuals with PASC meeting the 2010 ACR FM diagnostic criteria showed improvement in functional interference due to fatigue at 4weeks from baseline.

second_reader.what_stands: The FM sub-group GFI improvement in the Abstract and Conclusion rests on a within-group change in 5 participants, while the between-group comparison (p = 0.161, CI spanning zero) is not significant and is not mentioned there. The text SE (10.61) also disagrees with the table SE (2.188).

issues.title: 'Demonstrates the benefit' over low-dose and gait 'improvement' rest on within-group or imbalanced results
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the study demonstrates benefit of high-dose over low-dose TENS and that TENS is a promising alternative for gait, and the Conclusion states gait improvement. The gait claims are within-group changes from baseline, which cannot separate treatment from time or placebo effects, and the between-group BPI-S and GFI results were null. Together with 25 analysed participants and a baseline-imbalanced primary contrast, this wording overstates what a pilot can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-group gait comparisons (time x group) showing a robust advantage over low-dose TENS in an adequately powered sample.

quotes.text: Our study uniquely demonstrates the benet of high-dose TENS over low-dose in individuals with PASC and FM-like symptoms within a short timeframe.
In this context, high-dose TENS offers a promising alternative for improving gait parameters in PASC patients with FM-like symptoms.

second_reader.what_stands: The claim to 'uniquely demonstrate' benefit over low-dose rests on a whole-cohort BPI-I difference that is largely the baseline gap, while the FM sub-group between-group tests are all non-significant. The gait 'improvement' is described mainly as within-group change in the IG, with the PG results unseen. A time x group effect for cadence and stride time is reported but not verifiable here, and none is reported for double-support.

issues.title: Primary analysis uses 23 of 30 randomized (25 per text); losses not handled by ITT, extra missing data unexplained
issues.explanation: Five participants discontinued during the blinded phase and were excluded, so the comparison is a completer analysis. Table 3 then lists only 12 PG and 11 IG for BPI-I, and 11 and 10 for the other outcomes, without saying why they differ from the 25 stated in the text. The results therefore apply to completers with questionnaire data and may be biased if dropout related to dose.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Fig. 2 or supplementary material showing why Table 3 Ns are below 25 and a sensitivity or ITT analysis giving the same result.

quotes.text: Thus, 25 patients were included for analysis (IG, n = 12; PG, n = 13).
A sample size of n = 12 per group is expected to yield 95% power for detecting a time-effect difference.

issues.title: Table 3 BPI-I CI '-4.543, 0.689' spans zero yet p = 0.008; upper bound likely should be -0.689
issues.explanation: The printed 95% CI for the 4-week BPI-I difference includes zero, which contradicts the printed p = 0.008. The CI is symmetric about -2.616 only if the upper bound is -0.689, so this looks like a lost minus sign rather than a wrong result. A reader of the table as printed would see a non-significant interval beside a significant p.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original table or published version printing the upper bound as -0.689 (the sign loss then being an extraction artefact).

quotes.location: Table 3, All cohort BPI-I row, 95% CI

quotes.text: the IG exhibited a greater decrease in BPI-I compared to the PG (mean difference = 2.61, p = 0.008)

script.explanation: the estimate -2.616 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [-4.543, 0.689] (expected about -1.9270) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

issues.title: Investigators collecting and analysing data unblinded; primary outcome is self-reported pain interference
issues.explanation: The paper states that investigators collecting and analysing data were not blinded, although participants were. Because the primary outcome is a self-completed questionnaire, the main risk is unblinded data handling and any unmasking of the low-dose device by sensation, not interviewer bias. No blinding-integrity assessment is reported, so some bias cannot be excluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinding-success assessment showing participants could not distinguish dose, plus evidence that data analysis was blinded to arm.

quotes.text: Investigators collecting and analyzing data were not blinded.
quotes.location: Methods, Randomization, group allocation, and intervention

10.21203/rs.3.rs-4459921/v1.headline_claim: Pacing for Long COVID may offer potential benefits and is feasible, but further research is required to demonstrate its benefits.
10.21203/rs.3.rs-4459921/v1.overall: As a descriptive, non-comparative mixed-methods sub-study, its findings on acceptability and perceived usefulness are tentative and carry mostly small reporting errors. The text overstates agreement on understanding pacing (18 vs 16 from Table 6, and 'all' video participants vs 7 of 10). The conclusion that pacing is an important symptom-management component goes beyond the perception data, and the 44% questionnaire response limits generalisation.

primary_outcome.name: not_reported

issues.title: Text gives 18 (64.2%) agree/strongly agree on understanding pacing; Table 6 cells sum to 16 (57.1%)
issues.explanation: The Results say 18 of 28 respondents agreed or strongly agreed that the intervention helped them understand how to pace. Adding the Agree and Strongly Agree cells of Table 6 across the three arms gives 16. The text therefore overstates agreement by two participants (about 7 percentage points). This is a small reporting error in a descriptive item, but it feeds the claim of benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 6, or the raw questionnaire data, showing 18 respondents in the agree/strongly agree categories.

quotes.text: 18 participants (64.2%) believed that the intervention helped them understand how to pace their usual activities (strongly agree/agree)
quotes.location: Results, 2(c) Impact of pacing interventions on daily activities

quotes.text: Did the intervention help you understand how to pace your usual activities?

issues.title: Discussion says all 10 video participants found it helped understanding; Table 6 shows 7 agree, 3 neutral
issues.explanation: The Discussion states that every participant randomised to the video used it and found that it helped them understand pacing. Table 6 shows 0 strongly agree, 7 agree and 3 neutral among the 10 video respondents. Use was universal, but the perceived helpfulness was 70%, not 100%. The Discussion sentence overstates the positive result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing that the 3 neutral video respondents also reported that the video helped them understand pacing.

quotes.text: all the participants randomised to the pacing video used it during the trial and found that it helped them understand how to pace
quotes.location: Discussion, Findings in relation to existing literature

quotes.text: Participants who used the pacing video reported slightly more impact on their understanding of how to pace.

issues.title: Conclusion asserts pacing is 'an important component' of symptom management without outcome data
issues.explanation: This sub-study reports only perceptions and usage from 28 questionnaire respondents and 19 interviewees. It has no comparator and no clinical outcomes. Despite this, the Conclusion states that pacing 'is an important component of symptom management' and that research will improve clinical outcomes. The Discussion itself cites evidence of ineffectiveness in other conditions. The abstract is appropriately cautious, so the problem is mainly in the conclusion's wording.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled outcome data in the paper showing symptom benefit, or conclusion wording limited to acceptability and perceptions.

quotes.text: Pacing is an important component of symptom management for Long COVID.
which will ultimately be improving clinical outcomes and quality of life.

issues.title: Questionnaire response only 28/64 (43.7%) of intervention participants; positive summary may reflect responders
issues.explanation: Only 28 of the 64 participants allocated to an intervention completed the feasibility questionnaire, and the interviewees were a self-selected subset of 35 of 85 randomised. Non-responders are not characterised. Views of those who stayed engaged are likely to be more favourable. The Discussion generalises that 'most participants reported a positive experience', and the limitations section mentions only the small sample, not non-response bias.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparison of responders and non-responders showing similar characteristics and engagement, or wording that restricts the claims to respondents.

quotes.text: 28 participants who had been randomised to one of the pacing interventions (43.7%)
Overall, most participants reported a positive experience with the interventions

10.21203/rs.3.rs-6269439/v1.headline_claim: A 3-month personalized resistance exercise programme after COVID-19 improved walking distance (Incremental Shuttle Walk Test), health-related quality of life, anxiety, depression and grip strength, and is a generalizable therapy for persisting symptoms.
10.21203/rs.3.rs-6269439/v1.overall: The primary result (36.5 m, 95% CI 6.6 to 66.3, P = .02) is internally consistent, but it comes from an open-label trial with unblinded effort-dependent assessment and complete-case data missing for 17.6% of participants. The secondary improvements are uncorrected for multiplicity and self-reported, and the generalizability claim rests on underpowered interaction tests. There are also several table errors (Table 3 group B row, the Table 1 CRP and serology cells, a 2- vs 3-month label), none of which changes the main conclusions but which raise doubts about table checking.

primary_outcome.name: Incremental Shuttle Walk Test distance at 3 months

issues.title: Open-label trial: unblinded walk-test assessors, self-reported secondaries and extra staff contact only in the exercise arm
issues.explanation: The ISWT, which depends on participant effort, was run by staff who knew allocation. EQ-5D-5L and PHQ-4 are self-reported, and the intervention arm had fortnightly contact while controls had none beyond usual care. Expectation and attention effects could therefore add to or produce the observed differences. The Abstract and Key Points still say quality of life, anxiety and depression improved, with no sign of this caveat. The primary effect has a lower CI bound of only 6.6 m.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of assessor blinding for the ISWT, or an attention-matched control arm, or objective outcomes agreeing with the self-reported ones.

quotes.text: The Incremental Shuttle Walk Test and interviews were conducted by study personnel who were aware of the treatment allocation.
Participants in the intervention group received more contact with site staff compared with participants in the control group.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper confirms that the primary walk test and interviews were done by assessors who knew the allocation (the registry also lists no masking) and that the exercise arm had more staff contact (about 2-weekly contacts versus none by research staff in the control arm). Only the analysis was blinded, and the authors state both limitations but do not say how much they could bias the open-label primary result. The 'self-reported secondaries' element is the reviewer's inference: the PROMs (EQ-5D-5L, PHQ-4) are self-reported and unmasked, but grip strength is an objective measure, and the paper's o

issues.title: Table 3 group B row (119, 27 missing) duplicates the Female row; groups A+B+C sum to 256 against 192 analysed
issues.explanation: Table 3 gives group B as 119 analysed with 27 missing, which is 146 people. Table 1 has only 66 in group B, and the three groups would sum to 256 analysed against the 192 in the primary analysis. The values are identical to the Female row, so the group B count and possibly its summary and effect estimate are suspect. The group B interaction result (P = .61) cannot be trusted as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplement data showing group B really had 119 analysed participants, which would contradict Table 1 and the 192 total.

quotes.location: Table 3, Clinical presentation group, Group B row
Table 1, Clinical presentation group, Group B row

issues.title: Primary change score missing for 41 of 233 (17.6%); Discussion cites only 11.2% withdrawal and reasons were unavailable
issues.explanation: Only 192 participants contribute to the primary analysis (94 intervention, 98 control). That is 41 of 233 missing, more than the 11.2% withdrawal the Discussion calls 'relatively low'. The missing proportion is higher in the intervention arm (23 of 117, 19.7%) than control (18 of 116, 15.5%). Reasons for loss were not available and the primary analysis appears to be complete-case, so the 36.5 m estimate, whose CI lower bound is 6.6 m, depends on an unverified missing-data assumption. The 'No. (No. missing)' entries in Tables 2 and 4 are counted against the people assessed, so they also understate overall loss.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The eTable 7 imputed analysis giving a similar estimate and interval, with reasons for missingness reported.

quotes.text: Overall, the withdrawal rate was relatively low (11.2% overall)
The reasons for being lost to follow-up were not available.

issues.title: 'Generalizable therapy' rests on non-significant interaction tests that the authors say were not powered
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says the intervention may be a generalizable therapy, justified by the absence of significant subgroup interactions. Those tests were not powered, so absence of evidence is not evidence of homogeneity. Subgroup estimates differ widely (female 53.6 m, male 8.2 m; interaction P = .15) and the sample is mostly White and female. The Limitations paragraph notes the lack of power but the Conclusion and Abstract do not carry the caveat.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Adequately powered or pooled external data showing consistent effects across sex, ethnicity and deprivation groups.

quotes.text: Because there was no evidence of intervention effect heterogeneity across prespecified groups, the results may be considered generalizable.
this analysis was not powered for tests of interactions.

issues.title: About 19 secondary comparisons at P < .05 with no correction; 3 nominal hits headlined in the Abstract and Conclusion
issues.explanation: Table 4 tests many secondary outcomes at an unadjusted two-sided 0.05 level, and 3 reach nominal significance, about what chance alone would give. The Abstract and Conclusion state that quality of life, anxiety, depression and grip strength 'appeared to improve' without mentioning multiplicity. The Conclusion then lists them alongside walking distance with equal weight, so secondary findings read as established. The secondary results are best seen as hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchical or multiplicity-adjusted testing plan for secondary outcomes in the statistical analysis plan.

quotes.text: All P values were from 2-sided tests and results were deemed statistically significant at P < .05.
appeared to improve walking distance, healthrelated quality of life, anxiety, depression, and grip strength.

issues.title: Results text dates secondary-outcome effects at 2 months; Abstract and Table 4 say 3 months
issues.explanation: The Secondary Outcomes paragraph reports the EQ-5D-5L, PHQ-4 and handgrip effects 'by 2 months'. The Abstract and the Table 4 heading give the same estimates at 3 months, and the trial had a 3-month follow-up. The text label is almost certainly wrong, but a reader cannot tell which time point applies from the Results alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol statement of a separate 2-month assessment at which these estimates were measured.

quotes.text: By 2 months after randomization, compared with the control group, greater improvements in the intervention group were observed
Secondary Outcomes: Change at 3 Months From Baseline and Effect of the Intervention

issues.title: Table 1 serology: both arms print median 10494 (5694-21 127), but the pooled median is 9896
issues.explanation: The standard care and intervention columns have identical median and IQR for COVID-19 serology. The All column median (9896) is lower than both arm medians, which cannot happen because a pooled median lies between the group medians. One arm cell has probably been copied into the other. The row is also a 3-month measure in a baseline table, which may reflect timing of the sample. This is a baseline descriptor and affects only the serology subgroup tertiles.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw serology data showing a pooled median below both arm medians, which is mathematically impossible, or a corrected table.

Table 1, COVID-19 serology at 3 mo row

issues.title: CRP >0.5 mg/dL: arms print 34 + 34 = 68 but the All column prints 58

10.2139/ssrn.4178044.headline_claim: CoQ10 at 500 mg/day for six weeks does not appear to significantly reduce the number or severity of PCC-related symptoms compared with placebo, and the authors conclude CoQ10 should not be recommended as treatment for PCC.
10.2139/ssrn.4178044.overall: The main finding of no significant CoQ10 effect on either primary outcome is reasonably supported for this dose and duration. The CI excludes the 10-point difference the trial was powered for, and the EQ-5D index, which is validated, also shows no effect. The flaws are minor: two misprinted percentages and one mismatched p-value, a symptom score that has not been validated, a short registration delay, and a recommendation worded without caveats.

issues.title: Primary symptom score is an author-developed 32-item scale (0–128) with no validation reported
issues.explanation: One of the two primary outcomes is a new scoring system built by the authors from the literature and a Danish cohort. No validity, reliability or minimal important difference is reported for it. The null conclusion on symptoms therefore depends partly on an instrument of unknown sensitivity. The validated EQ-5D index, also null, partly mitigates this.

10.2139/ssrn.4216601.headline_claim: Anodal tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex may improve physical fatigue in post-COVID syndrome.
10.2139/ssrn.4216601.overall: The headline claim of a potential benefit for physical fatigue rests on a secondary subscale result, while the registered primary endpoint (MFIS total) was null and this null is missing from the abstract. The physical-subscale p-value is misprinted by a factor of ten, and the safety claim goes beyond a 47-patient pilot. Treat the efficacy signal as hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: MFIS-total score (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale)

issues.title: Null primary MFIS-total interaction (P=0.184) omitted from abstract; subscale (physical) presented as the finding
issues.explanation: The stated primary endpoint, MFIS total, showed no time-by-group interaction (P = 0.184). The abstract does not report this and instead headlines the significant physical-fatigue subscale. The Discussion then concludes that tDCS 'has a positive effect', which the primary analysis does not support. The subscale result is a secondary, uncorrected finding in a 47-person pilot and should be framed as hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or registry entry pre-specifying MFIS-physical as the primary or key confirmatory outcome.

quotes.text: The time-by-group interaction effect was not significant
Active tDCS was associated with a statistically significant improvement in physical
The Modified Fatigue Impact Scale score was used as the primary endpoint.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract reports the significant MFIS-physical result and does not report the non-significant MFIS-total interaction (P=0.184), although the abstract itself names the MFIS score as the primary endpoint, and the registry lists a single primary outcome 'Change in Fatigue'. The null total-score result is disclosed in the main text (Results 3.2 and Discussion) and the paper describes itself as a preliminary pilot, so the omission is limited to the abstract, and the abstract's hedged wording ('may improve') partly softens it.

issues.title: 'Confirms the safety' of tDCS claimed from 47 patients, 8 sessions, 4 vs 5 mild adverse events
issues.explanation: A small pilot with brief exposure can show tolerability, not confirm safety, because rare or delayed harms would not appear. The Discussion also says tDCS is among the first therapies to show positive results, despite a null primary endpoint. The efficacy claim is hedged elsewhere, so this affects the strength of the stated conclusions rather than the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Wording limited to 'was well tolerated in this small pilot', with no claim of confirmed safety or of positive results.

tDCS is one of the first therapeutic options to show positive results in this

issues.title: MFIS-physical interaction F(2,82)=3.517 printed with P=0.0034; statistic implies about 0.034
issues.explanation: The MFIS-physical time-by-group interaction is the paper's headline positive result. An F of 3.517 on 2 and 82 degrees of freedom gives p of roughly 0.034, ten times larger than the printed 0.0034. The result remains nominally significant, but it is much weaker than printed, and it was tested without correction across several subscales and secondary outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Output showing a different F value or df that yields P = 0.0034.

script.explanation: The printed f = 3.517 supports p no smaller than 0.0342119, but the paper reports p = 0.0034 -- more significance than the statistic earns at its printed precision.

issues.title: One randomised active-arm patient (48 vs 47; 24 vs 23) is dropped from analysis though flow says 0 excluded
issues.explanation: The Results and Figure 2 give 48 randomised (24 active, 24 sham), while the abstract and Table 1 describe 47 patients (23 active, 24 sham). Figure 2 shows one active participant discontinued after the first session and 23 analysed, yet states 0 excluded from analysis. So the analysis was per-protocol or completer, not the intention-to-treat set the 48 randomised implies, and the abstract does not say so. The effect on results is probably small, but the participant counts and the analysis population are not reported consistently.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the discontinued participant was randomised but not analysed, with the analysis population labelled per-protocol and the 47 described as analysed rather than enrolled.

issues.title: Active-arm baseline MFIS-total (68.26) differs from sum of subscale means (68.51)

For the active group they sum to 68.51, not the printed 68.26. The sham group reconciles, so this looks like a transcription or data slip. It is small and does not alter any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that some participants lacked a subscale score at baseline, so the means rest on different denominators.

quotes.text: MFIS (total score) 68.26 ± 10.15
MFIS-physical 29.65 ± 5.07
MFIS-psychosocial 6.47 ± 1.50

issues.title: EuroQol-5D 'group-by-time' effect (P=0.016) labelled significant, then interaction reported non-significant (P=0.120)
issues.explanation: A 'group-by-time' effect and a 'time-by-group interaction' are the same term, yet the paper reports it as significant (P = 0.016) and as not significant (P = 0.120). The likely intent is a main effect of time, which says nothing about the treatment. The abstract's null quality-of-life statement stands on the interaction, but the reader cannot tell which result belongs to which effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 2 or the supplement labelling the P = 0.016 term as the main effect of time.

quotes.text: showed a statistically significant main group-by-time effect (F(2,84) = 4.324, P = 0.016)
The treatment had no effects on quality of life.

10.2139/ssrn.4356755.headline_claim: AXA1125 significantly reduced fatigue (CFQ-11) versus placebo in fatigue-predominant Long COVID, despite no significant effect on the primary mitochondrial endpoint (τPCr), supporting further multicentre study.
10.2139/ssrn.4356755.overall: The null primary endpoint is reported honestly, but the efficacy message rests on uncorrected secondary self-reported fatigue scores in a 41-patient, 4-week pilot, and should be read as hypothesis-generating. Several Table 2 numbers (SDs, a placebo change) and the recruitment dates are misprinted, which lowers confidence in data handling but does not clearly reverse the main fatigue difference.

primary_outcome.name: Mean change from baseline to Day 28 in phosphocreatine (PCr) recovery rate time constant (τPCr) after moderate exercise, by 31P-MRS

primary_outcomes.measure: Change from baseline at Week 4 in the phosphocreatine (PCr) recovery rate following moderate exercise, as assessed by 31P-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS)

issues.title: Efficacy conclusion rests on uncorrected secondary self-reported fatigue scores after a null primary endpoint
issues.explanation: The primary endpoint (τPCr) was null, and the efficacy conclusion is drawn from CFQ-11 fatigue, a secondary patient-reported outcome. The paper states no allowance was made for multiplicity across the secondary outcomes. Wording such as 'did lead to improvements' and 'marked symptomatic improvement' is stronger than a small pilot with a null primary can support. The fatigue P values (0.0039-0.0097) are small enough that a signal is plausible, but the claim should be hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchical testing plan placing CFQ-11 first, or a confirmatory replication.

quotes.text: administrating AXA1125 twice daily did lead to improvements in both physical and mental fatigue symptoms
As this was a phase 2a study, there was no allowance for multiplicity for the secondary outcomes.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does draw an efficacy conclusion ('did lead to improvements') from secondary, self-reported CFQ-11 scores after a null primary endpoint, and states that no multiplicity allowance was made; the limitations do not address this or unblinding risk in subjective outcomes. It is narrower than a strong version of the claim: the null primary is stated first in the conclusion, the study is framed as a phase 2a pilot or feasibility trial calling for a larger trial, and the CFQ-11 total P=0.0039 would survive a Bonferroni correction over the four listed secondaries (alpha 0.0125), though the ph

issues.title: Placebo 6-MWT change SD 12.1 is impossible given baseline SD 106.5 and Day 28 SD 20.6
issues.explanation: The SD of a within-person change cannot be smaller than the gap between the baseline and follow-up SDs. Here that gap is about 85.9 m, but the change SD is printed as 12.1 m. The Day 28 SD of 20.6 also looks too small for an IQR of 506-636 m. At least one placebo 6-MWT SD in Table 2 is misprinted. The 6-MWT is a null secondary result, so the conclusions barely change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data or a correction showing the SDs and their correlation are consistent.

issues.title: 'No safety concerns' and 'minimal TEAEs' stated despite TEAEs in 52.4% (AXA1125) vs 20.0% (placebo)
issues.explanation: TEAEs occurred in 11/21 AXA1125 patients and 4/20 placebo patients, a roughly 2.6-fold difference. The text nonetheless describes AEs as infrequent and 'minimal' and reports 'no safety concerns', with no comparative testing of safety. A 41-patient, 4-week study cannot exclude uncommon harms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified safety comparison showing no difference, or an argument that the imbalance was due to the non-treatment-related event types.

quotes.text: Treatment with AXA1125 was well tolerated and raised no safety concerns
11 (52.4%, AXA1125) and 4 (20.0%, placebo) patients reported treatment emergent adverse events

issues.title: Rising τPCr (slower recovery) in AXA1125 arm described as a positive trend supporting metabolic improvement
issues.explanation: A higher τPCr means slower phosphocreatine recovery, so the AXA1125 arm moved in the unfavourable direction relative to placebo (+21.2 s vs +4.0 s). The Discussion nonetheless says a 'positive trend in τPCr' accompanying fatigue reduction suggests treatment response may be due to improved metabolism. The primary mechanistic endpoint gives no support for this claim, which the data neither show nor exclude.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the correlation with fatigue change reflects improving recovery times in responders and that the arm-level shift reflects outliers.

quotes.text: suggests that treatment response may be due to improvements in metabolism and oxidative stress

issues.title: AXA1125 physical fatigue change SD 0.75 is smaller than the minimum 1.39 implied by baseline and Day 28 SDs
issues.explanation: The change SD must be at least the difference between the baseline SD (2.54) and Day 28 SD (3.93), which is 1.39, but 0.75 is printed. The cell is therefore misprinted. The physical fatigue score is one of the paper's headline secondary outcomes, but the LS mean difference and P value come from the ANCOVA, not from this cell, so the finding itself is not obviously affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or supplementary data showing an SD of at least 1.39.

quotes.location: Table 2, CFQ-11 Physical fatigue (Likert) row, AXA1125 baseline
Table 2, CFQ-11 Physical fatigue (Likert) row, AXA1125 Day 28
Table 2, CFQ-11 Physical fatigue (Likert) row, AXA1125 change

issues.title: Placebo CFQ-11 total change printed -2.25 but Day 28 minus baseline gives -1.6
issues.explanation: With complete data, the placebo mean change should equal Day 28 mean minus baseline mean, which is -1.6, not -2.25. One of the three placebo numbers is wrong, and which one cannot be told from the paper. If the change were really -1.6, the unadjusted between-group difference would be larger than the -3.0 implied by the printed values. The primary fatigue result uses ANCOVA, so the effect is uncertain and likely modest.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the change was computed on a different set of patients or time basis, or corrected values.

quotes.location: Table 2, CFQ-11 Total fatigue (Likert) score row, Placebo

issues.title: Placebo baseline observed:predicted 6-MWT SD is 17.3 in Table 1 but 3.9 in Table 2
issues.explanation: The same placebo baseline mean (86.8%) is printed with SD 17.3 in Table 1 and SD 3.9 in Table 2. An IQR of 73.4-97.7 implies an SD near 18, so 3.9 is the likelier error. This is a minor reporting slip in a null secondary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the two tables use different populations or variable definitions.

issues.title: AXA1125 baseline bimodal total fatigue range starts at 6, below the stated inclusion threshold of 8
issues.explanation: Inclusion required a bimodal total fatigue score of 8 or more, yet the AXA1125 baseline range is 6-11. This is explained if baseline was measured after screening and fatigue fluctuated, but the paper does not say so. If any enrolled patient truly scored below 8 at screening, that is an unreported eligibility deviation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that Table 1 reports Day 1 scores distinct from the screening scores used for eligibility.

quotes.text: a total fatigue (bimodal) score of ≥8 on the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire

issues.title: Results give recruitment end as 23 May 2023, after the 14 April 2023 publication and contradicting May 2022 elsewhere
issues.explanation: The Results state recruitment ran until 23 May 2023, but the Summary and Methods say it ended in May 2022. The article was published online on 14 April 2023, so a May 2023 end date is impossible. This is a typographical error with no bearing on the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the dates cannot all be right.

quotes.text: Patients were recruited from 15th December 2021 until 23rd May 2023.
Between December 15th 2021, and May 23th 2022
Published Online 14 April 2023

issues.title: Text gives observed:predicted 6-MWT range 0.712-0.982, but Table 1 individual ranges span 48.0%-118.7%
issues.explanation: The Results describe a range of 0.712-0.982 around a mean ratio of 0.846. Table 1 gives individual ranges of 48.0-115.5% and 57.9-118.7%. The text range may be some other interval, but it is not labelled. This affects only the baseline description.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition showing 0.712-0.982 is a different quantity, such as a CI or group-level range.

10.2147/idr.s381715.headline_claim: Local ivermectin mucoadhesive nanosuspension nasal spray is effective for post-COVID-19 anosmia, with early recovery benefit at one week and no side effects, though the authors conclude it should be used for one week at most.
10.2147/idr.s381715.overall: The only robust finding is an early (1-week) difference in an open-label trial with a subjective self-rated outcome and retrospective registration; overall recovery and the 1-3 month results were null. The median-duration headline is internally inconsistent with the recovery proportions, so the efficacy claim is tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Recovery of anosmia (VAS) at one week

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-rated VAS smell outcome; 1-week difference (59.2% vs 27.7%) open to expectation bias
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation and rated their own smell on a 0-10 scale, with no masking of patients or assessors. Expectation effects could produce an early difference without a drug effect. The later null results are consistent with this, so the 1-week benefit is only tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded or objective olfactory testing showing the same early difference.

quotes.text: the study was open label without masking
use of subjective assessment of anosmia

second_reader.what_stands: The trial was unmasked and the main outcome was a self-rated VAS with no stated recovery threshold, so the 1-week difference (59.2% vs 27.7%) is open to expectation and reporting bias. The authors acknowledge the subjective outcome but not the absence of blinding. The paper cannot show how much bias occurred, only that the design allows it.

issues.title: Reported median recovery times (13 vs 50 days) conflict with recovery rates (59.2% by week 1; 61.7% by month 1)
issues.explanation: If 29 of 49 ivermectin patients had recovered by 1 week, the median time to recovery must be about 7 days or less, not 13. In the placebo group 13+16 = 29 of 47 (61.7%) had recovered by the 1-month assessment, so the median should be at most about 30 days, not 50. Table 3 labels 3-105 and 6-115 as interquartile ranges while the Results text calls them ranges. The headline median-duration result (p<0.001) therefore cannot be relied on as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of the time axis (e.g. days from a different origin) or a censored survival analysis that reconciles the medians with the recovery proportions.

quotes.text: Duration of anosmia till recovery [days, Median (Interquartile range)]
showed recovery in 29 patients (59.2%)

second_reader.what_stands: The median recovery times (13 vs 50 days) cannot be reconciled with the paper's own recovery proportions: 59.2% recovered by week 1 implies a median of about 7 days or less, and 61.7% recovered by month 1 implies a placebo median of about 30 days or less. The paper does not define the time origin or how recovery time was measured, and Table 3 labels the printed ranges as interquartile ranges.

issues.title: Trial registered retrospectively (2021-06-30), after enrolment began (2021-04-20)
issues.explanation: The registry shows first submission about ten weeks after the recorded study start and two months after the paper's stated recruitment end. Prespecification of outcomes therefore cannot be verified. The registered primary outcome (regaining of smell within 14 days) also differs from the paper's reported 1-week, 1-, 2- and 3-month recovery comparisons and median time to recovery.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version dated before enrolment began, with the same primary outcome.

quotes.text: Trial Registration No: NCT04951362.

issues.title: Discussion claims significant faster recovery and conclusion supports 1-week use despite null overall recovery (p=0.2)
issues.explanation: Cumulative recovery was not significantly different (95.9% vs 89.4%, p=0.2) and the 1-, 2- and 3-month comparisons were null. The Discussion nonetheless states a significant reduction in recovery duration and offers a virucidal mechanism. The abstract advice to use it for a week rests on a single early timepoint from an open-label subjective outcome, with no multiplicity control or safety data beyond a small sample.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified 1-week primary outcome with blinded assessment showing the same difference.

quotes.text: showed a significant reduction in the duration of recovery
it could be used for one week at the most

10.2147/jmdh.s530582.headline_claim: An individualized six-week Adapted Physical Activity protocol significantly improves health-related quality of life and anxiety/depression in long COVID patients, with benefits maintained at 5-7 months follow-up.
10.2147/jmdh.s530582.overall: The within-patient improvements in SF-12 and HADS are large, but the single-arm design cannot attribute them to the programme, so the claim of effectiveness is not supported beyond a promising signal. Recommendations for routine care outrun the evidence. Numeric slips (education counts, one 'strong' correlation) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: SF-12 physical and mental component scores (HRQOL) across three time points

issues.title: Single-arm before-after cohort used to claim the APA programme 'significantly enhances' outcomes
issues.explanation: All 50 patients received the same programme and are compared only with their own baseline. Natural recovery from long COVID over 5-7 months, regression to the mean, and expectation effects on self-reported scales cannot be separated from any programme effect. The conclusion that the programme 'demonstrates' enhancement and gives 'robust evidence' of effectiveness is stronger than this design supports. The limitation is mentioned, but the headline wording ignores it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated comparison group showing a smaller change.

quotes.text: This study demonstrates that an APA program can significantly enhance HRQOL and psychosocial outcomes
the absence of a control group limits  the  ability  to  draw  definitive  causal  inferences

second_reader.what_stands: The paper's evidence is an uncontrolled before-after change in a single 50-patient cohort, yet the Conclusions use causal language ('demonstrates... can significantly enhance'). The authors do acknowledge the missing control group and call for RCTs, so the problem is partly hedged, but the headline claim is stronger than a single-arm design supports and natural recovery and regression to the mean are not discussed.

issues.title: 'Robust evidence' and routine-care integration advised from an uncontrolled 50-patient cohort
issues.explanation: The Contributions section says the study provides 'robust evidence' of effectiveness and advocates integrating exercise into routine care, and the Implications section tells providers to implement such programmes. The Conclusion partly hedges by calling for randomized trials. An uncontrolled single-site study of 50 patients supports a hypothesis, not a practice recommendation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled evidence, or conclusions limited to hypothesis generation.

quotes.text: It  provides  robust  evidence  of  significant  short-  and  medium-term  improvements  in  health-related  quality  of  life (HRQOL), anxiety, and depression.
Integrating personalized APA into standard care for long COVID may enhance both physical and psychological outcomes

second_reader.what_stands: 'Robust evidence' and the advice to integrate APA into routine care rest on a 50-patient uncontrolled cohort with self-reported outcomes, so the wording overstates what the design can show. The final Conclusions sentence is hedged ('may', 'larger randomized controlled trials are needed'), but the Contributions and Implications sections are more assertive and the hedge does not match them.

issues.title: No registration or prespecified primary outcome for a prospective intervention programme
issues.explanation: The paper reports no registry entry and designates no primary outcome, though it delivers a protocolised 6-week intervention. Several outcomes were measured (SF-12, HADS, mMRC, 6MWT, spirometry) but 6MWT and spirometry are not reported in the results. Whether registration was required depends on whether this is viewed as a trial or an observational study.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol listing the outcomes before enrolment.

quotes.text: This single-center, prospective, longitudinal observational study included 50 patients

issues.title: Table 1 education counts sum to 45 (90%) of 50 patients; 5 unaccounted
issues.explanation: The three education categories in Table 1 add up to 45 patients and 90%, not the 50 patients in the study. No missing or 'no schooling' category is shown. This is a minor reporting gap that affects no outcome result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A footnote or fourth category (e.g. no schooling, n=5) that completes the total.

issues.title: 'Strong' correlations claimed for all, but one (rs = -0.45) is 'moderate' by the paper's own cut-offs
issues.explanation: The paper defines strong as 0.500 or above and moderate as 0.300-0.499, yet describes every SF-12/HADS correlation as strong with a range starting at -0.45. Only the SF12 Physical/HAD-A value at E3 falls below 0.5. The remaining 17 of 18 coefficients are strong, so the general statement mostly holds. The -0.45 also breaks the pattern of its row and may be a typo.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confirmation that -0.45 is a correct value and the text means 'mostly strong'.

quotes.text: rs ranging  from  -0.45  to  -0.72

10.21516/2072-0076-2025-18-4-107-112.headline_claim: A differentiated treatment approach for chronic conjunctivitis in post-COVID syndrome, guided by whether laser Doppler flowmetry shows a hyperemic or stagnant microcirculation type, is effective and should determine treatment choice.
10.21516/2072-0076-2025-18-4-107-112.overall: The claim that treatment should be chosen by LDF type, and that efficacy is due to this approach, is not supported: the study is non-randomised, uses eye-level within-group tests, has no between-subgroup comparison, no clinical outcomes and no multiplicity control. The comparator subgroups are inconsistently described (2b treated or untreated), and the 'normalisation' claims in subgroup 2a do not match the control values. At most the paper gives hypothesis-generating descriptive data.

primary_outcome.name: Laser Doppler flowmetry microcirculation parameters: mean perfusion M, fluctuation σ, coefficient of variation Kv

issues.title: Conclusion attributes efficacy to the LDF-guided approach from a non-randomised, flowmetry-only study
issues.explanation: The Conclusion states that treatment efficacy is due to the differentiated approach and that treatment must be based on microcirculation type. The study has no comparison between a type-matched and a non-type-matched regimen, and no randomisation or adjustment. It also reports no clinical outcome, only LDF parameters. The data could show that perfusion values changed after a multi-drug regimen, not that choosing the regimen by LDF type caused benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomised or adjusted comparison of LDF-guided versus non-guided treatment with clinical outcomes.

quotes.text: Эффективность лечения хронического конъюнктивита при постковидном синдроме обусловлена дифференцированным подходом
Лечение хронического конъюнктивита необходимо и должно основываться на определении типа микроциркуляторных нарушений.

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion attributes efficacy to the differentiated, LDF-guided approach and says treatment must be based on microcirculation type, but the study is non-randomised, uses only a surrogate flowmetry outcome, and has no arm testing whether LDF-based selection matters versus giving the same multi-drug regimen to all. The causal and 'must' wording is not supported by this design.

issues.title: Benefit inferred from within-subgroup changes; no between-subgroup test; 'significant vs not' contrast
issues.explanation: Efficacy is argued from changes from baseline within each subgroup. The 'a' subgroups are described as improving and the 'b' subgroups as not significantly changing. A difference in significance is not evidence of a difference between treatments. No test compares 1a with 1b or 2a with 2b, and follow-up means, SDs and p-values are not tabulated, only percentage changes and a few values.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A direct between-subgroup comparison (for example a group-by-time analysis) showing the a-regimens outperform the b-regimens.

quotes.text: У пациентов подгрупп 1б и 2б статистически достоверных изменений микроциркуляторных показателей не зафиксировано.
Через 3 мес отмечено достоверное увеличение средней перфузии на 35 %

second_reader.what_stands: The paper infers benefit of the 'a' regimens from significant within-subgroup change versus non-significant change in the 'b' subgroups, and reports no between-subgroup or interaction test. Inclusion of both eyes of each patient as units is also not addressed. The within-subgroup changes in 2a are described, but this is not evidence that 2a differs from 2b.

issues.title: Allocation to 'a' versus 'b' subgroups not described; b subgroups differ in baseline and regimen
issues.explanation: Within each microcirculation type, patients were split into an 'a' subgroup with a multi-drug regimen and a 'b' subgroup with hyaluronate only. The paper does not say how patients were assigned, so differences in outcome could reflect selection. Baseline perfusion and variability also differ between the pairs (for example Kv 31.8 vs 26.5 in the stagnant type). The regimens differ in many drugs at once, so no single element can be credited.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random or rule-based allocation to a/b, and baseline-adjusted between-subgroup analyses.

quotes.text: Пациенты подгруппы 1б патогенетически ориентированного лечения не получали
Пациентам подгруппы 2б назначали инстилляции гиалуроната натрия

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not say how patients were assigned to 'a' or 'b', and the 'b' subgroups differ both in regimen (hyaluronate only vs a multi-drug regimen) and somewhat in baseline sigma and Kv, with no adjustment. The Discussion's statement that 2b received no local or systemic treatment is also inconsistent with the Methods, which give them hyaluronate.

issues.title: 'Normalisation' in subgroup 2a not supported: end values (M 26.3, Kv 15.2) resemble hyperemic baselines, not controls
issues.explanation: The Abstract and Discussion call the 6-month values in subgroup 2a normalised and describe a normocirculatory type. The reported M of 26.3 and Kv of 15.2 are far from the healthy control values (21.8 and 22.6) and close to the hyperemic subgroups' baseline values. This looks more like a shift from stagnant toward hyperemic than a return to normal. No comparison with controls is shown at follow-up.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up comparisons showing 2a values statistically indistinguishable from the healthy control group.

quotes.text: через 6 мес у пациентов подгруппы 2а (М = 26,3 ± 6,1 п. е.)
формирование нормоциркуляторного гемодинамического типа микроциркуляции без признаков нарушения периферического кровообращения

second_reader.what_stands: By the paper's own numbers, the 6-month 2a values (M 26.3, Kv 15.2) lie about 3.8 and 2.8 control SDs from the control means (21.8; 22.6) and resemble the hyperaemic baselines (M 26.6-27.6; Kv 14.4-16.8), so the 'normoциркуляторный тип без признаков нарушения' and 'нормализация' claims are not supported; they show overshoot past control rather than return to it. No test against the control group is reported, and the 3-month 2a value (about 23.1) was closer to control than the 6-month value.

issues.title: Subgroup 2b given hyaluronate in Abstract and Methods but 'no local or systemic treatment' in Discussion
issues.explanation: The Abstract and Methods say subgroup 2b used sodium hyaluronate three times daily. The Discussion says the same subgroup received no local or systemic treatment and uses this to argue that therapy is necessary. The two accounts cannot both be true. It is unclear whether subgroup 2b was a treated comparator or an untreated one, and the Discussion's inference depends on which.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement from the authors that 'no treatment' in the Discussion means no pathogenetic treatment beyond hyaluronate, or a corrected Discussion.

quotes.text: Пациенты подгрупп 1б и 2б получали лечение препаратом, содержащим гиалуронат натрия, 3 раза в день
Пациентам подгруппы 2б назначали инстилляции гиалуроната натрия
Пациенты этой подгруппы не получали местного и системного лечения

issues.title: M, σ and Kv tested at 3 time points in 4 subgroups at alpha 0.05 with no multiplicity control
issues.explanation: Three parameters at three follow-up times in four subgroups gives up to 36 within-group comparisons, all at a per-test 5% level and with no correction. The headline normalisations rest on single parameters at single times. No p-values are printed, so readers cannot see how close to the threshold the results are.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified single primary parameter and time point, or p-values that survive a Bonferroni/Holm correction.

quotes.text: Достоверными различия между значениями считали при вероятности ошибки, равной или менее 5 %
Коррекция микроциркуляторных нарушений способствовала нормализации перфузии через 3 мес у пациентов подгруппы 1а

issues.title: Both eyes analysed as independent units (132 eyes from 66 patients) in t-tests
issues.explanation: All tables and tests count eyes, so each patient contributes two correlated observations. Student and paired t tests assume independent units, so the effective sample size is overstated and p-values are likely too small. The within-subgroup significance on which the efficacy claims rest is therefore less secure than shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Analysis with patient-level means or a mixed model accounting for two eyes per patient giving the same conclusions.

quotes.text: n - number of eyes.
различия оценивали с использованием t-критерия Стьюдента, парного t-критерия Стьюдента.

issues.title: No property interest declared, but ref. 22 is a patent for a post-COVID microcirculation method by 3 of the authors
issues.explanation: Three of the paper's authors are named on a Russian patent for correcting microcirculatory disorders in post-COVID syndrome. The paper declares that authors have no financial or property interest in any method mentioned. A patent is arguably a property interest in the topic method, and the study supports that approach. The paper does not explain the relation between the patent and the studied regimen.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confirmation that the patent is unrelated to the regimens studied or that the authors hold no rights or income from it.

quotes.text: Сафонова Т.Н., Зайцева Г.В., Кинтюхина Н.П., Медведева Е.С. Способ коррекции микроциркуляторных нарушений при постковидном синдроме. Патент РФ № 2791660 от 13.03.2023.
the authors have no financial or property interest in any material or method mentioned.

issues.title: English abstract conclusion refers to 'postconcussive syndrome' instead of post-COVID syndrome
issues.explanation: The English abstract's conclusion names a different condition from the one studied. The Russian text refers to post-COVID syndrome. It is a translation error that no reader would take as the real study population.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: n/a

quotes.text: in postconcussive syndrome

10.21518/1995-1477-2021-18-2-151-153.headline_claim: Post-COVID-19 chronic venous insufficiency in patients with pre-existing venous disease is marked by edema and pain, and the Russian diosmin-based product Venolek is a promising, low-cost means to relieve the edema-pain syndrome.
10.21518/1995-1477-2021-18-2-151-153.overall: The descriptive observation that some patients with chronic venous disease present with worse edema and pain after COVID-19 is plausible, but it comes from a self-selected series. The efficacy and cost-saving conclusions for Venolek are not supported: there is no control group, the pain score is open-label, the 12 untreated patients are not compared, no cost or safety data are given, and the headline 85% response rate does not fit the stated denominator of 35.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: Efficacy of diosmin inferred from 35 open-label treated patients with no comparator, test or spread
issues.explanation: Only 35 of the 47 patients received Venolek. The paper reports edema resolution and a VAS pain fall from 5-6 to 2-3 in these patients, with no control group. The 12 untreated patients are not described or compared. Pain is patient-rated and unblinded, and no statistical test, interval or measure of spread is given. Improvement after 1-2 months could reflect natural resolution of a post-infection flare, regression from a symptomatic peak, or expectation, so the drug effect is not identified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical comparison group, or blinded assessment, showing the changes exceed those in comparable untreated post-COVID patients.

quotes.text: 35 из 47 человек получили венотонизирующий препарат Венолек®
значительно снизилась выраженность болевого синдрома (до 2-3 баллов по ВАШ)

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy of the diosmin product is inferred from a single uncontrolled group of 35 treated patients, with no comparator, no statistical test, no measure of spread (only ranges of VAS scores) and no stated denominator for the 85% edema figure. Outcome assessment methods, timing and dropouts are not described, and the 12 untreated patients are not reported on. The claim of improvement is a descriptive observation and cannot support attribution of the change to the drug.

issues.title: Conclusion recommends Venolek as a low-cost option with no cost, safety or comparator data
issues.explanation: The Conclusions call Venolek very promising for edema-pain syndrome, explicitly in the framework of low-cost treatment. The data are an uncontrolled, unquantified description of 35 patients. No costs are analysed, no other diosmin product is compared, and no adverse events are reported. The cost and superiority framing therefore rests on assertion, not on the study's results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Cost data and a controlled comparison with other diosmin products, plus safety reporting, supporting the recommendation.

quotes.text: отечно-болевого синдрома при ХЗВ нижних конечностей

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion recommends Venolek as a promising low-cost option, but the paper gives no cost figures, no safety or adverse-event data and no comparison with another diosmin product or with no treatment. The cost advantage is asserted in the Discussion without numbers, so the conclusion goes beyond what the reported data show.

issues.title: Post-COVID worsening of venous insufficiency (94%) claimed from 47 self-presenting patients, no comparison
issues.explanation: Only patients who attended with complaints of deterioration after COVID-19 were included. Such a series cannot show how often chronic venous insufficiency worsens after COVID-19, nor that COVID-19 caused it. Prior measurements are not documented, and the 94% has no stated numerator or denominator. The conclusion that COVID-19 exacerbates these conditions is therefore not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A consecutive, unselected cohort with documented pre-COVID status, or a matched non-COVID comparison group.

quotes.text: то наблюдается значительное ее усиление, практически в 94% наблюдениях

second_reader.what_stands: The 94% worsening is derived from the 47 patients who presented to the clinics because they felt worse after COVID-19, with no comparison group, no unselected denominator of patients with venous disease and no pre-COVID baseline beyond a recalled calf circumference. The figure therefore cannot be read as the frequency of worsening of venous insufficiency after COVID-19, and the paper does not define how 94% was obtained or its denominator.

10.21518/2079-701x-2022-16-18-95-99.headline_claim: The DAST complex (a biologically active supplement) has a corrective effect on asthenoneurotic symptoms after ARVI or post-COVID syndrome and should be included in post-infection rehabilitation.
10.21518/2079-701x-2022-16-18-95-99.overall: The headline claim of a corrective effect on asthenoneurotic symptoms rests on two unquantified figures from an open, untreated-control study of 50 patients, with no between-group test, effect size or primary outcome. Several conclusions (antiviral, neuroprotective, cognitive, proven safety) are not measured at all. The conclusion can be treated at most as a hypothesis.

primary_outcome.name: not designated; abstract reports MRC dyspnoea, Beck depression, FAS fatigue and CRP

issues.title: CRP and FAS effects asserted from figures alone: no between-group test, estimate or CI, near-normal baseline CRP
issues.explanation: The CRP and FAS benefits are described only qualitatively from two figures. No between-group difference in change, p-value, CI or numeric end-of-study values are given. Mean baseline CRP was 4.4 and 3.8 mg/l, so little room for a fall existed, and a few high values (to 22 and 14 mg/l) could drive group means. The 'substantial anti-inflammatory effect' and fatigue improvement are therefore unsupported as stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test or CI on change in CRP and FAS showing a clear, clinically meaningful difference, with post-treatment values.

quotes.text: в первой группе отмечалось гораздо более выраженное снижение уровня СРБ после 14 дней приема DAST ® , чем во второй
в связи с чем можно судить о существенном противовоспалительном эффекте комплекса DAST ®

second_reader.what_stands: In the text, the CRP and FAS effects are asserted ('гораздо более выраженное снижение', 'существенный противовоспалительный эффект') with no printed between-group test, estimate or CI, and baseline mean CRP (4.4 and 3.8 mg/L) is near the normal range. I could not inspect the figure images, so I cannot say whether they show error bars or p-values.

issues.title: Open, no-placebo control for subjective FAS fatigue outcome; randomisation method not described
issues.explanation: Controls received nothing, so any difference in self-rated FAS may reflect expectation or attention rather than the supplement. No blinding or placebo is mentioned, and the randomisation method and concealment are not described. The authors nonetheless attribute the fatigue difference to the supplement and even propose improved wellbeing as the mechanism.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of blinded assessment or a placebo control, or an objective fatigue outcome showing the same difference.

quotes.text: вторая группа из 25 чел. - не получавшие данный комплекс
Данный эффект может быть связан с улучшением самочувствия вследствие вегетостабилизирующего и антистрессового действия DAST ®
quotes.location: Results and discussion, after FAS paragraph

second_reader.what_stands: The control group is described only as not receiving the supplement, with no placebo or blinding, and FAS fatigue is a subjective self-report outcome. The randomisation method is stated but not described.

issues.title: Conclusions claim antiviral, neuroprotective, cognitive effects and proven safety not measured or shown
issues.explanation: The conclusion says the supplement has antibacterial and antiviral effects, acts as a neuroprotector and antioxidant, improves cognition and speeds recovery. None of these were measured. Safety is called 'confirmed' from zero reported adverse events in 25 treated patients over 14 days, and the blood chemistry listed in methods is never reported. Compliance is also asserted without any described measurement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported data on antiviral, cognitive and oxidative outcomes and tabulated safety laboratory results supporting these statements.

quotes.text: обладает антибактериальным и противовирусным эффектом
Бикомплекс действует как природный нейропротектор и мощный антиоксидант, улучшает когнитивные функции
Безопасность использования средства растительного происхождения DAST ® подтверждена отсутствием нежелательных явлений

second_reader.what_stands: The antiviral, antibacterial, neuroprotective, antioxidant and cognitive claims in the Conclusion were not measured in this study, and the safety claim ('подтверждена') rests on zero reported adverse events in 25 treated patients over 14 days, without reported lab values. The safety data are consistent with no signal but cannot confirm safety.
