issues.title: No ethics approval, consent or trial registration statement in a randomised interventional study
issues.explanation: The paper describes randomising 50 patients to an intervention or none but gives no ethics committee approval, informed consent or registration. This may be a journal-format omission rather than an absence of approval. It cannot be resolved from the paper alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ethics committee approval number and consent statement, or a trial registry entry.

quotes.text: Все пациенты были рандомизированы в две группы наблюдения

10.21518/2079-701x-2022-16-2-76-84.headline_claim: Tofizopam (Grandaxin) 150 mg/day for 6 weeks reduced anxiety, vegetative and insomnia symptoms in patients with post-COVID anxiety disorder, and the authors conclude that its use is pathogenetically justified for post-COVID asthenovegetative and anxiety disorders.
10.21518/2079-701x-2022-16-2-76-84.overall: The reported fall in HAM-A and subscale scores is descriptive only, from 50 patients with no control group and unmasked clinician raters. The conclusions that the drug is highly effective, almost irreplaceable and pathogenetically justified go well beyond that design. Only the within-patient improvement can be taken as observed; the causal and mechanistic claims cannot be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: HAM-A total score change from baseline to 6 weeks

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from a single-arm open study: HAM-A 31.4 to 12.08 with no control group
issues.explanation: All 50 patients received tofizopam and were compared only with their own baseline. The fall in HAM-A cannot be separated from natural recovery after COVID-19, regression to the mean (entry required a high HAM-A score), or non-specific and expectation effects. The only tests are Wilcoxon comparisons of each time point against baseline (the screen's c3), which cannot show a drug effect without a comparator. The strong efficacy wording is therefore not supported by the design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control arm showing smaller improvement, or an explicit restriction of conclusions to descriptive change.

quotes.text: Работа  носила  характер  открытого  проспективного наблюдательного  исследования.
Данный факт показывает высокую эффективность препарата и делает его практически незаменимым в купировании тревожных расстройств

issues.title: Mechanistic and 'pathogenetically justified' conclusions drawn from an uncontrolled HAM-A series
issues.explanation: The authors attribute the symptom reduction to effects on GABAergic and nitroxidergic systems. They conclude the drug is pathogenetically justified for post-COVID asthenovegetative and anxiety disorders. The study measured only clinical scores in a single open arm, with no biomarkers, neurophysiology or comparator. The mechanism and the causal role of the drug are asserted, not tested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Mechanistic data from this cohort or a controlled design linking the effect to these pathways.

quotes.text: применение тофизопама является патогенетически обоснованным для терапии постковидных астеновегетативных и тревожных нарушений.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is an uncontrolled, single-arm, open-label HAM-A series with no mechanistic measurements, yet the Discussion attributes the improvement to GABAergic and nitroxidergic effects and both Discussion and Conclusion call the treatment 'pathogenetically justified'. The Conclusion's wording is partly grounded in cited literature on post-COVID pathogenesis, but the mechanistic attribution and the claim of justification are not supported by the paper's own data, and no limitation about the absence of a control is acknowledged.

issues.title: Open-label HAM-A scored by treating clinicians via interview and observation; no rater masking
issues.explanation: The HAM-A was completed during an interview with the patient, with the clinician also observing behaviour. Neither the paper nor the rating procedure mentions masking or independent raters. Expectation and rater bias could inflate the improvement in a subjective outcome. This weakens the size of the reported effect but is a narrower problem than the missing control.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that HAM-A raters were independent of treatment and masked to timepoint, or an objective corroborating outcome.

quotes.text: Работа  носила  характер  открытого  проспективного наблюдательного  исследования.
Самим пациентам  шкала  не  предъявлялась,  прямые  вопросы не  задавались.

issues.title: Sleep disturbance: 70% pronounced (Results) vs 'two-thirds' with any sleep disorder (Discussion)
issues.explanation: The Results say 70% of patients had pronounced sleep disturbance at baseline. The Discussion says 2/3 had sleep disorders, which would be a broader category and so cannot be smaller. The gap is small and probably loose wording, but the figure is reported inconsistently and no sleep-disorder denominator is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that '2/3' is only an approximate figure, or a different definition or denominator for the two sleep statements.

quotes.text: у большинства больных (70%) наблюдались выраженные нарушения сна
у 2/3 пациентов, обратившихся в клинику по поводу тревоги, отмечались расстройства сна

issues.title: No participant flow or dropout reporting for 50 patients over 6 weeks
issues.explanation: The paper does not say whether all 50 patients completed all visits or how missing data were handled. The counts that are given (for example 10 patients = 20%) fit a denominator of 50. The omission is a reporting gap rather than evidence of lost data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow statement confirming 50 of 50 completed all visits.

quotes.text: В исследовании принимали участие 50  пациентов,  перенесших  COVID-19

issues.title: No registration reported for a prospective drug-treatment study
issues.explanation: The study prospectively gave a drug to patients, but no registry entry or protocol is cited. This limits checking that the reported outcomes were prespecified. Because the paper labels itself observational, the omission is a minor transparency gap.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry number or ethics-approved protocol listing the same outcomes.

quotes.text: Работа  носила  характер  открытого  проспективного наблюдательного  исследования.

10.21518/ms2023-014.headline_claim: Alflutop (bioactive small sea fish concentrate) is effective and safe for early treatment of post-COVID lower back pain algic syndromes, and early prescription is recommended.
10.21518/ms2023-014.overall: The headline recommendation of early Alflutop use rests on an uncontrolled, open-label series of 50 patients with a subjective pain outcome and within-group change only, so it cannot be relied on as evidence of efficacy or safety. The baseline VAS is also reported inconsistently (6.6 vs 5.6, with an SD incompatible with the stated range), which makes the size of the reported improvement uncertain.

primary_outcome.name: Visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score

issues.title: Single-arm series of 50 with no control group used to attribute pain relief to Alflutop
issues.explanation: All 50 patients received the drug and there is no comparator, so improvement over 2 months cannot be attributed to Alflutop rather than spontaneous recovery of post-COVID pain, regression to the mean, or concomitant NSAIDs. The authors nonetheless describe the drug as having a large effect, and conclude that it should be prescribed early. This is the central weakness of the paper, shared with the open-label and within-group candidates.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group showing a smaller improvement.

quotes.text: Всем пациентам проводилась монотерапия препаратом Алфлутоп по 2 мл через день, 10 инъекций внутримышечно.
Результаты, полученные в программе, свидетельствуют о наличии у препарата большого воздействия и на дисфункциональную боль

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is a single-arm series of 50 with no control group, and it still attributes pain relief to Alflutop and claims a distinct effect on dysfunctional pain versus other chondroitin sulfates; the design cannot separate drug effect from natural recovery, regression to the mean or expectation. Concomitant NSAIDs in 10% and a mismatch in baseline VAS (6.6 vs 5.6) further limit interpretation.

issues.title: Recommendation for early use and 'no pronounced side effects' drawn from 50 uncontrolled patients
issues.explanation: The conclusion recommends early Alflutop prescription and says it has no pronounced side effects, but the data are an uncontrolled series of 50 patients followed 2 months. Efficacy cannot be separated from natural course, timing of treatment was never compared, and zero adverse events in 50 patients cannot rule out events occurring in up to about 6%. Also, claims of reduced systemic inflammation and no effect on coagulation are made without any reported laboratory values.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data on efficacy and timing, and a larger safety database.

quotes.text: позволяют рекомендовать раннее назначение препарата Алфлутоп в комплексной терапии постковидных алгических синдромов
не имеет выраженных побочных явлений

second_reader.what_stands: The recommendation for early use and the statement of no pronounced side effects rest on 50 patients in a single uncontrolled arm followed for 2 months; no early-versus-late comparison was made, and zero events in 50 is compatible with a true event rate of up to about 6%. The recommendation is stronger than this design supports.

issues.title: Baseline VAS is 6.6 ± 1.5 in abstract/Methods but 5.6 ± 1.5 in Results and Table
issues.explanation: The abstract and Methods give the baseline VAS mean as 6.6, while the Results text and the table give 5.6 for the same first visit. The table value of 5.6 also lies below the stated minimum of 6 for enrolled patients. The size of the pain reduction therefore depends on which baseline is correct (5.6 to 1.0 versus 6.6 to 1.0).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 6.6 and 5.6 refer to different time points or populations.

quotes.text: по ВАШ (6,6 ± 1,5 балла)
объективно по ВАШ 5,6 ± 1,5 балла

issues.title: Baseline VAS mean 6.6 ± 1.5 is incompatible with the stated 6-8 range (max SD about 1.0)
issues.explanation: The Methods say enrolled patients had VAS 6 to 8, which caps the SD near 1.0, yet the SD is 1.5. The mean of 6.6 within 6-8 is fine, but the SD is not. Combined with the 5.6 baseline in the table and the 4-8 inclusion criterion, the baseline description is internally inconsistent; this is part of the same baseline-description problem as the other VAS candidates.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that enrolled VAS values actually ranged 4-8, or that the 6-8 phrase is a loose description.

quotes.text: по визуальной аналоговой шкале (ВАШ) от 6 до 8 баллов
(среднее  значение  6,6  ±  1,5  балла)

issues.title: Inclusion VAS 4-8 in criteria versus 6-8 described for enrolled cohort
issues.explanation: The numbered inclusion criterion permits VAS 4-8, whereas the narrative says the enrolled patients scored 6-8. The difference could simply be criterion versus observed range, but the paper does not say so, and it compounds the baseline inconsistencies. Low impact on the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 4-8 is the eligibility range and 6-8 the observed range of enrolled patients.

quotes.text: выраженность болевого синдрома по ВАШ 4-8 баллов
по визуальной аналоговой шкале (ВАШ) от 6 до 8 баллов

issues.title: HADS depression at visit 2 (3 ± 1.0) marked p<0.05 vs baseline despite identical mean and SD
issues.explanation: The table footnote-style asterisk denotes a significant difference from baseline, yet the visit 2 depression value equals baseline exactly. Either the asterisk is misplaced or the values are rounded so heavily that they cannot be checked. Impact is minor, as depression was not a target of therapy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Unrounded depression scores showing a real change at visit 2.

quotes.location: Table, HADS Депрессия row, second visit

issues.title: Prior treatment of the 10 'primary' patients described inconsistently (NSAIDs+CS vs NSAIDs only)
issues.explanation: The abstract implies the 10 primary patients got NSAIDs and chondroitin sulfate, whereas Methods say 40 got NSAIDs plus CS and 10 got only NSAIDs. The groups of 10 may not be the same, but the text does not say so.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clarification that the 10 NSAID-only patients and the 10 primary patients are different groups.

quotes.text: 10 пациентов  получали  только  НПВС
получали терапию нестероидными противовоспалительными средствами и ХС

10.21518/ms2023-111.headline_claim: Ethylmethylhydroxypyridine malate 400 mg/day added to rehabilitation shows clinical efficacy in long COVID, including reduced oxidative stress, and is clinically safe because no adverse reactions developed.
10.21518/ms2023-111.overall: The headline claims of oxidative-stress reduction, mitochondrial normalisation, clinical efficacy and safety are not supported: this is a 24-patient, open-label, non-randomised comparison with no placebo, no sample-size calculation, selectively interpreted metabolites, and mostly within-group testing. The data are best read as hypothesis-generating. Minor MoCA text/table discrepancies add to concern about reporting care.

primary_outcome.name: Oxidative stress / metabolomic markers (taurine, asparagine, CoQ10, alpha-ketoglutarate, 8-OHdG) and clinical scales (mMRC, 6MWT, MFI-20, MoCA, Barthel); no single primary outcome is named

issues.title: Open-label, non-randomised, no-placebo comparison used to claim drug efficacy and 'more pronounced' improvement
issues.explanation: Controls received exercise only, with no placebo, and no blinding is described. Outcomes such as MFI-20, mMRC and MoCA are subjective or performance-based and sensitive to expectation. Group allocation was not random and baseline differences (e.g. age 62 vs 56, sex split 7/5 vs 6/6) exist, yet the abstract states the drug led to reduced oxidative stress and greater clinical improvement and the conclusion states efficacy. The design supports at most a hypothesis-generating signal.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded, placebo-controlled or randomised design, or adjusted analyses showing the same difference.

quotes.text: В нерандомизированное контролируемое проспективное исследование были включены 24 пациента
Применение препарата этилметилгидроксипиридина малат у пациентов с long COVID привело к снижению уровня оксидативного стресса и нормализации функции митохондрий

second_reader.what_stands: The study is non-randomised with an untreated, unblinded, non-placebo comparator, yet it states that the drug caused reduced oxidative stress, normalised mitochondrial function and gave a 'more pronounced' improvement. The paper has no limitations section and does not acknowledge that design, allocation or expectation effects could explain the differences. I did not find the term 'open-label' in the paper, but the absence of any blinding or placebo is evident.

issues.title: ~60 metabolomic markers plus 6 scales, five selected markers interpreted without correction or between-group tests
issues.explanation: The methods list 60 urinary organic-acid markers plus blood CoQ10, but results present only five, interpreted selectively as evidence of reduced oxidative stress. Only a few uncorrected within-group p-values are given (p = 0.042 in controls, p = 0.005 for CoQ10 in the drug group) and no between-group test is reported for the metabolites. Changes in the control group are read as worsening (e.g. aspargine up, taurine down) while similar or opposite shifts in the drug group are read as benefit, which makes the 'oxidative stress reduced' conclusion rest on selective, unadjusted interpretation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary metabolomic endpoint or full results table of all markers with corrected between-group tests.

quotes.text: органические кислоты в моче выявление функциональных метаболических изменений (60 показателей)
В группе препарата отмечается рост показателя от уровня Ме 622 до уровня Ме 747 (p = 0,005)

second_reader.what_stands: About 61 laboratory markers were measured, five were highlighted without a stated selection rule, and the paper reports no multiplicity correction and no between-group tests for any of them. The treated-group CoQ10 p = 0.005 and the control asparagine p = 0.042 are within-group tests, so claims of drug-versus-control differences in oxidative stress and mitochondrial function are not supported by an inferential comparison. The count of six scales is slightly off (five scales are reported).

issues.title: MFI-20 'greater improvement' claim has no between-group test; MoCA test compares final levels only
issues.explanation: For MFI-20 the table reports only within-group paired t-tests against baseline, and no between-group test, yet the abstract and discussion say improvement was greater with the drug (21% vs 13%). Both groups improved significantly (p < 0.001), so a difference in significance is not evidence of a difference between arms. For MoCA a between-group test at the 2nd point is given (#), but it compares end levels with a Kruskal-Wallis test and does not test change from baseline; the percentage gains are computed from medians (5/24 = 20.8%, printed as 20.1%).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test of change from baseline (e.g. ANCOVA) on MFI-20 and MoCA showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: Отличия статистически значимы по сравнению с исходным уровнем.
В группе контроля происходит снижение показателей астении, но менее значимое, чем в группе препарата

second_reader.what_stands: No between-group test is reported for the change in MFI-20, so the claim of greater improvement in the drug group rests on within-group significance and a difference in percentages that I could not reproduce for the control arm. The MoCA between-group test compares final scores only, not change from baseline, although baseline medians were equal; the MoCA text and table also disagree on the interquartile ranges.

issues.title: Clinical safety asserted from zero reported adverse reactions in 12 treated patients over ~16 days; no AE data shown
issues.explanation: The conclusion declares clinical safety because no adverse reactions developed, but the Results contain no adverse-event section or table, only the statement in the conclusion. With 12 drug-treated patients followed about 2 weeks, an event rate up to roughly 25% would be compatible with zero observed events. The safety claim is therefore not supported by the evidence presented.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported AE log with systematic collection showing no events and a larger or longer safety dataset.

quotes.text: а также клиническую безопасность ввиду отсутствия развития нежелательных реакций у пациентов с long COVID

second_reader.what_stands: The claim of clinical safety rests on zero reported adverse reactions in 12 patients over about two weeks, with no adverse-event data shown in the Results. With zero events in 12 patients, the true event rate could be as high as about 22% at the 95% level, and the short follow-up cannot address later or rarer effects. The paper does not present the safety data it says it collected.

issues.title: MoCA control 2nd point: Results text gives IQR 24-24, table gives 27-27, for median 27
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the control-group MoCA median at the second point as 27 with quartiles 24-24, which is impossible since a median cannot lie outside its own quartile range. The table gives 27 (27-27). The text is probably the error, but the paper does not say which is correct. It is a minor reporting slip; the control MoCA improvement is cited in the abstract as 12.5%.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw MoCA scores showing which quartiles are right (would only settle which is the slip, not remove the inconsistency).

quotes.text: Во второй  точке  Me  в  группе  контроля  составила  27  (Q 1 -Q 3 -24-24)

issues.title: MoCA drug group baseline: text IQR 24-24, table 23-24
issues.explanation: The text gives baseline quartiles 24-24 for the drug group, while the table gives 23-24. The discrepancy is one point and does not alter the median. It is a trivial slip, but shows the text and table were not reconciled (see the larger MoCA discrepancy in the control group).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing Q1 = 23 or 24 (would identify the slip but not remove it).

quotes.text: Ме в группе препарата 24 (Q 1 -Q 3 - 24-24)

quotes.location: Table, MoCA row, drug group, 1st point

10.21608/ijma.2023.194428.1627.headline_claim: Adding laser acupuncture to pedometer-based walking improves quality of life in post-COVID-19 patients more than pedometer-based walking alone, and the authors recommend the combined programme for post-COVID-19 management.
10.21608/ijma.2023.194428.1627.overall: The direction of the finding (laser plus walking scoring better than walking alone on SF-36 and fatigue) is plausible and statistically strong on the printed numbers. The design cannot attribute the difference to laser itself, because there is no sham control, no stated blinding and self-reported outcomes. The programme-level recommendation and the walking-improves-QoL claim go beyond what this small, short, unregistered trial supports.

primary_outcome.name: Quality of life (SF-36)

issues.title: No sham laser and no blinding stated for self-reported QoL/fatigue; added laser effect unseparated from expectation
issues.explanation: Group A got thrice-weekly laser sessions plus walking, while group B got walking only with telephone follow-up. No sham laser is used and the paper never says participants or assessors were blinded. SF-36 and the fatigue scale are self-reported, so the 4.6-point SF-36 gap could partly reflect expectation and extra attention. The claim that laser 'significantly increased' the effect of walking is not isolated from these non-specific effects. Blinding is covered here because it is the same problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that participants and outcome assessors were blinded, or a sham-laser or attention-matched control arm.

quotes.text: Group B: [n=30] patients received pedometer-based walking only.
Addition of laser acupuncture significantly increased effect of walking in this population.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes no sham laser and no blinding of patients or outcome assessors, and the self-reported SF-36 and fatigue scores are open to expectation and extra-contact effects. The added-laser effect is therefore not separated from these, yet the Highlights and Conclusion credit it to laser acupuncture without any caveat.

issues.title: Programme recommendation drawn from one 60-patient, 4-week, unblinded trial without safety data
issues.explanation: The conclusion says management of post-COVID syndrome 'should include' walking and laser acupuncture. The evidence is a small single-centre study with 4-week follow-up. It has no durability data, no adverse-event reporting and no sham control. The favourable direction of the between-group result is plausible, but the recommendation goes well beyond it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A larger multicentre blinded replication with safety and longer follow-up.

quotes.text: syndrome should include pedometer-based walking and laser acupuncture.

second_reader.what_stands: The programme recommendation rests on one 60-patient, 4-week trial with no blinding or sham described and no safety or adverse-event data reported, in a narrowly selected population. The Conclusion states the recommendation as 'should include' without any stated limitation.

issues.title: Randomised trial reports ethics approval but no trial registry or registration number
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval and consent but no registry entry. The primary outcome and analysis plan therefore cannot be checked against a prior record. This matters because seven outcomes are reported and none is designated primary.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with a registration date before enrolment.

quotes.text: Informed consent was provided by patients.

issues.title: Claim that walking improved QoL rests on pre-post change in an arm with no untreated comparison
issues.explanation: The highlights and discussion say pedometer walking improved QoL. The only support is the within-group pre-post change in group B (p = 0.0001). There is no no-treatment arm, and patients were recovering after COVID-19 anyway. The between-group comparison supports only the relative laser effect, not an absolute walking effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A usual-care or no-intervention control arm showing less QoL change.

quotes.text: Pedometer-based walking improved quality of life in these patients.

issues.title: Seven outcomes tested without a designated primary outcome or correction; QoL result likely robust
issues.explanation: All seven outcomes were tested at alpha 0.05 with no correction and no declared primary. The QoL result has p = 0.0001 and would survive correction, so the effect on the QoL conclusion is small. The weakness is mainly that the primary outcome is unstated and the many positive results are presented together.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome (QoL) in a protocol or registry.

quotes.text: Alpha was p < 0.05.

10.2174/1570159x20666220420113513.headline_claim: Oral PEA-LUT plus olfactory training produced greater recovery of smell than olfactory training plus placebo in post-COVID-19 olfactory dysfunction.
10.2174/1570159x20666220420113513.overall: The large 90-day difference in TDI and recovery rates is probably directionally real, but it rests on a quota-based odd/even allocation without described concealment, a retrospective-to-contemporaneous registration, and a control group tested only twice. The 60-day dosing claim and the Cohen's d argument are not supported, and several tables and abstract figures contain printing errors. Treat the efficacy conclusion as tentative..

primary_outcome.name: Change in TDI score (Sniffin' Sticks) from baseline to 90 days, between groups

primary_outcomes.time_frame: T1 (30 days), T2 (60 days), T3 (90 days)

issues.title: Allocation by random odd/even numbers until 55 controls; 2:1 block claim, 130:55 split, no concealment described
issues.explanation: The Methods describe block randomization at 2:1 but then say participants were sorted by randomly generated odd or even numbers until at least 55 controls were reached. This is a quota-driven rule, and the 130:55 split (2.36:1) departs from 2:1. No allocation concealment is described, and the reference number was assigned at recruitment. Such a procedure can allow predictable or non-random assignment, so the between-group comparison may not rest on true randomization.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concealed, centrally generated allocation sequence with documented block sizes per site and a CONSORT flow showing how allocation continued after controls reached 55.

quotes.text: Randomization was performed using an online random number generator, with participants sorted based on a random generation of odd or even numbers until there was a minimum of 55 participants in the control group.
Using a block randomization within each site, eligible participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes two incompatible allocation methods: block randomization within site at 2:1, and odd/even random numbers continuing until at least 55 controls were reached. The odd/even rule would not by itself produce 2:1, and the resulting 130:55 (2.36:1) is not a fixed-block outcome. No block size, sequence generation detail, or allocation concealment is given. This is a reporting weakness in the randomization description. I did not check whether actual allocation was concealed, only whether the paper describes it.

issues.title: Abstract compares subgroup means (12.8 vs 3.2) rather than whole-arm mean change (about 9.2 vs 1.3)
issues.explanation: The abstract's 'magnitude of recovery' of 12.8 is the mean among the 80 intervention patients who gained more than 5 points, and 3.2 is the mean among the 23 controls who improved at all. These are conditioned on improvement and are not the arm-level change. From the printed means the whole-arm change is about 9.2 points in the intervention arm and 1.3 in controls. The abstract therefore misdescribes the primary outcome, although the between-arm gap remains large.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the abstract that these figures are restricted to improvers, or an arm-level mean change with SD and CI.

quotes.text: Magnitude of recovery was significantly greater in the intervention group versus control (12.8 + 8.2 versus mean 3.2 + 3)
80 patients (66.7%) recovered by more than 5 points (mean 12.8 +8.2) of the TDI scores

issues.title: Intervention arm retested at 30/60/90 days, controls only at 90; 60-day claim has no control comparator
issues.explanation: Only the intervention arm had three extra Sniffin' Stick tests, so practice effects and extra contact could differ by arm, which the authors acknowledge. The T3 comparison is still same-time in both arms. However, the statement that PEA-LUT should be used for at least 60 days relies on intervention-only timepoints. There is no control data at 30 or 60 days, so that claim is not supported by a comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Control-arm assessments at 30 and 60 days, or a sensitivity analysis showing no retest/practice effect in the intervention arm.

quotes.text: The subjects in the control group were instead re-evaluated after 90 days only
PEA-LUT should be used for 60 days at least to prove statistically significant efficacy.

issues.title: Cohen's d of 0.8 reported with CIs that exclude it (1.046-1.763; -2.163 to -1.41) and misused as a sample-size check
issues.explanation: The same d (0.8) is printed for baseline and post-treatment, yet the intervals shown do not contain 0.8, and the post-treatment interval is negative. Baseline groups were said not to differ, so a d of 0.8 at T0 is also implausible. The authors then use d to claim that different group sizes did not affect the results, which an effect size cannot show. This section is unreliable but secondary.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Cohen's d table with intervals containing their estimates and a statement of what the d values compare.

quotes.text: Cohen's d was 0.8 (CI95%: 1.046-1.763) pre-treatment and 0.8 (CI 95%: -2.163 to -1.41) post-treatment.
Cohen's d test was performed to evaluate the effect of different sample size on the outcome.

issues.title: Registered 2021-04-16 versus registry start 2020-11-15; paper reports enrolment from April 2021
issues.explanation: The registry shows first submission on 2021-04-16 with a start date of 2020-11-15, so registration came after the stated start. The paper's own dates (registered April 2021; enrolment April to October 2021) imply registration at or after the start of enrolment. This limits confirmation that the analysis was pre-specified, particularly since the registry lists T1-T3 time frames for the primary outcome but controls had only T3.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the registry record was first submitted before the first participant was enrolled, or that the registry start date is a placeholder.

quotes.text: registered at Clinicaltrials.gov in April 2021 with number: 20112020PGFN
from April 2021 to October 2021

issues.title: Table 2 cortisone nasal spray: total 83 printed as 53.5% (83/185 = 44.9%); control 25 printed as 9% (25/55 = 45.5%)
issues.explanation: The total column gives 83 (53.5%) although the Results text gives 44.8% for the same 83 patients and 83/185 is 44.9%. The control cell 25 (9) is also wrong, since 25/55 is 45.5%. These are prior-treatment descriptors and do not affect the efficacy result, but they show the table was not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction showing different counts or denominators that produce the printed percentages.

quotes.text: 44.8% (83) patients were treated with nasal steroids only (3 puff /day for 30 days)

script.explanation: 83/185 = 44.86%, but the paper prints 53.5, outside the rounding interval [53.45, 53.60]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 155.1 rather than 185.

issues.title: Baseline TDI group difference printed p=0.7; printed means/SDs give p about 0.07, and no baseline adjustment
issues.explanation: The control and intervention baselines differ by 2.3 TDI points (20.6 vs 18.3), and the printed summary statistics give p of roughly 0.07, not 0.7. Baseline TDI was the only predictor of recovery in the intervention-group regression, yet the main comparison is not adjusted for it. Intervention patients started higher, so the direction of bias is unclear, but the claim of no baseline difference is stronger than the data show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw baseline data showing a different spread, or a stated test (e.g. Tukey on a mixed model) whose p of 0.7 is expected to exceed the simple t-test p.

quotes.text: No significant differences in TDI scores existed between the groups at baseline, T0 (Tph: p=0.7)

issues.title: Share improved in intervention arm printed 92.2% in Discussion but 120/130 = 92.3%
issues.explanation: The Results give 120 of 130 intervention patients improved (92%). The Discussion restates this as 92.2%, while 120/130 is 92.3%. This is a cosmetic rounding or typing slip with no effect on any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing needed; it is a minor rounding or typing slip.

quotes.text: 120 patients (92%) had improved (higher) TDI score
an increase in TDI score was observed in 92.2 percent of those receiving PEA-LUT

script.explanation: 120/130 = 92.31%, but the paper prints 92.2, outside the rounding interval [92.15, 92.30]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 130.2 rather than 130.

10.21760/jaims.10.11.10.headline_claim: Vardhamana Pippali Rasayana with Mrudwika Sharkara plus WHO rehabilitation is effective in post-COVID-19 syndrome and has a definite role in its treatment, compared with WHO rehabilitation alone.
10.21760/jaims.10.11.10.overall: The short-term between-group differences in symptom grades and function scores are large and consistently reported, but they come from a trial whose comparator differs in purgation, vehicle and dose form, with no described blinding and subjective outcomes. The percent-relief figures cannot be reproduced from the printed means, and several text and table values disagree. The 'definite role' conclusion is stronger than the evidence supports and should be read as a tentative signal.

primary_outcome.name: Post-COVID symptoms and functional status (no single primary outcome is named; the paper says the drug 'will be effective' and reports many measures)

issues.title: Group A got purgation, a sugar vehicle and a far larger dose form; group B a suji capsule only, blinding not described
issues.explanation: Group A received castor-oil purgation and the Rasayana mixed with Mrudwika Sharkara, while group B received a small placebo capsule only. Any difference could therefore come from the purgation, the sweet vehicle or the expectation effect of an obviously different regimen, not the Pippali itself. No blinding or concealment is described, and the main outcomes are subjective symptom grades. The conclusion that the Rasayana itself works is not supported by this comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of blinding and matching of the placebo, plus a control arm that received purgation and the same vehicle.

quotes.text: All the patients were initially given Koshtha Shuddhi (mild purgation) with Eranda Taila
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Intervention, Group A

quotes.text: 250  mg  of  capsule  filled  with  roasted  Suji  powder

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does show that group A received purgation with castor oil plus a sugar vehicle (Mrudwika Sharkara) and a gram-scale dose, whereas group B received only a 250 mg suji capsule twice daily with no stated purgation or sugar vehicle, so the arms differ in more than the active drug. Blinding, allocation concealment and any placebo purgation are not described, though the paper does label group B 'Placebo' in the abstract and Table 9; whether masking was actually used cannot be determined, so 'blinding not described' is accurate but not proof that none existed.

issues.title: 'Definite role' conclusion drawn from an open-looking one-month trial with no defined primary outcome
issues.explanation: The conclusion states that the Rasayana has a definite role in treating post-COVID syndrome and improves quality of life. The paper defines no measurable primary outcome, follows patients for one month, does not describe blinding, reports no adverse events, and compares a multi-component regimen with a minimal placebo. The discussion's only limitations are geography and comorbidity. The data support at most a tentative signal of short-term symptom improvement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary endpoint with a registered analysis, blinded assessment, and safety reporting.

quotes.text: has  a  definite  role  in  the  treatment  of Post COVID-19 syndrome
As  the  study  was  conducted  in  the  one  particular geographic  region

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does draw a 'definite role' conclusion from a roughly two-month trial whose stated primary outcome is only a general expectation of effectiveness, with no defined measure, and the 13 clinical outcomes are tested without multiplicity correction; the limitations paragraph does not address the unmatched comparator, unreported blinding, or short follow-up. It is not true that no limitations were acknowledged (geography, severity and comorbidities are mentioned), and the trial registry entry was not available to check whether a primary outcome was prespecified there; whether the trial was

issues.title: Percent-relief values cannot be reproduced from the printed means (cough 83.7% vs 81.25%; anxiety 62.9% vs 77.08%)
issues.explanation: The tables give before and after means beside a percent relief, but the two do not agree. For cough the means imply about 84% against 81.25% printed, and for anxiety about 63% against 77.08% printed. Myalgia and insomnia show 100% BT-AF relief although the printed follow-up means are 0.03 and 0.02, not zero. The method behind the percentages is not stated, so the headline relief figures cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated formula (for example per-patient mean of percent change among symptomatic patients) with patient-level data that reproduces the printed percentages and the 100% values.

quotes.text: symptoms of coughing on examine 81.25%, 83.33% and 96.88% respectively
While in myalgia 89.42%, 100.00% and 100.00% relief was found

issues.title: 'All parameters' superiority overstated: lab ANCOVA shows no difference; follow-up between-group result not shown
issues.explanation: The abstract claims a significant difference in all assessment parameters, but the paper's own ANCOVA for haematological and biochemical parameters reports no between-group difference. The statement about the follow-up stage cites Tables 9 and 10, which contain only after-treatment values. The sustained-effect claim therefore rests on within-group changes, which are not a comparison of the arms. Between-group results for symptoms and function at after-treatment do exist and are strongly significant, so the core short-term difference is not undermined.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group ANCOVA table at the follow-up time point, and a rewording of the abstract to the symptom and function outcomes only.

quotes.text: proving  the  pre-eminence  of  Group  A
On applying ANCOVA test showed that group A and B had no difference significant in after treatment stage (P<0.01).
follow-up  stage  (table  9  &  10)

issues.title: Text, tables and significance labels disagree in several cells (e.g. headache 3.87% vs 83.87%; p=0.05 labelled S)
issues.explanation: Several percentages in the running text differ from the tables by a single digit or a dropped decimal point, for example headache BT-AT, fatigue BT-AF, social relationship and PCFS BT-AF. Table 4 prints 3976 for 39.76, and some Table 4 significance labels contradict their own p values. Tables 7 and 8 call p = 0.05 significant although the methods define significance as p below 0.05. None of this changes the main comparison, but it lowers confidence in how carefully the tables were checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not refutable for the digit slips, which are visible on the page; the p = 0.05 labels would be defensible only if the authors had stated a different alpha rule.

quotes.text: In Headache 3.87%, 93.33% and 98.92%
97.14% and 93.39% during the stages
Calculated P value less than 0.05 will be considered significant in all statistical tests.

issues.title: Completer-only analysis (54 and 50 of 55 per arm); no ITT or dropout handling stated
issues.explanation: Efficacy tables use 54 and 50 analysed patients out of 55 randomized per arm, with no intention-to-treat analysis or handling of missing data described. Attrition is about 5.5% overall but uneven between arms (1 versus 5). With so few dropouts this probably does little to the conclusion, but it is not addressed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CONSORT diagram showing the reasons for the six exclusions were unrelated to treatment, or a sensitivity analysis with imputed values.

quotes.text: Table 4: Effect of therapy in subjective parameters in Group B (N=50)
randomized  55  patient

issues.title: Many outcomes and timepoints tested at 0.05 without correction; headline p-values are far below threshold
issues.explanation: No multiplicity adjustment is described for the dozens of tests. The main symptom and function comparisons report p<0.01, so this probably does not change the main result. It weakens only the borderline laboratory findings, which are labelled significant at p=0.05.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Showing that the primary comparison was pre-specified or that significance survives Bonferroni or Holm adjustment.

quotes.text: Calculated P value less than 0.05 will be considered significant in all statistical tests.

10.21760/jaims.9.11.8.headline_claim: Bharangi Guda, a Rasayana/Ayurvedic formulation, was helpful in post-COVID conditions associated with dyspnoea, cough, fatigue and anorexia, with high clinical and statistical significance on subjective parameters.
10.21760/jaims.9.11.8.overall: The headline conclusion cannot be relied on: this is an uncontrolled 30-patient before-after series, mislabelled as randomized, with no sample size justification or multiplicity handling, and its prevention claim goes beyond anything measured. The printed numbers are largely consistent apart from a typo in the CRP t-value (13.881 versus 3.88) and a few shifted table cells. Within-patient symptom improvement is plausible, but attribution to Bharangi Guda is unsupported.

primary_outcome.name: not specified; subjective and objective parameters assessed (no single primary outcome named)

issues.title: Single-arm before-after study, labelled 'randomized', with no control group; 30 subjects, 50 days
issues.explanation: All 30 subjects received the same multi-step regimen and were compared with their own baseline. Without a control group, improvement cannot be separated from natural post-COVID recovery, regression to the mean, or the other regimen components (Chitrakadi Vati, Haritakyadhi purgation). The 'randomized' label has no allocation method or comparison arm behind it. Blinding and adverse events are not described. The 'highly significant' result shows change from baseline, not effect of the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent randomized control arm with between-group analysis, or an explicit statement that this is an uncontrolled case series with no efficacy claim.

quotes.text: Assessment  of  results  were  done  on  objective  and subjective parameters of baseline data to pre medication data comparing with gradation.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Overall Assessment Criteria

quotes.text: Study design is Simple Randomized Clinical Study.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm before-after design with 30 subjects over 50 days and no control group, yet it is labelled 'Simple Randomized Clinical Study' in the abstract and methods. No randomization procedure or comparison arm is described, so the label is unsupported by the design.

issues.title: Conclusion claims the intervention prevents post-COVID effects; design only measured within-patient change
issues.explanation: The authors conclude that this kind of intervention is needed to prevent post-effects in individuals. The study enrolled people who already had post-COVID symptoms, so no prevention outcome could have been measured. With no control group the data also cannot show that the herbal formulation was 'helpful', and no adverse events are reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A controlled design with a prevention endpoint in at-risk, asymptomatic people.

quotes.text: During COVID19, this kind of interventions is needed to prevent posteffect in the individual.

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion says the intervention is needed 'to prevent posteffect', but the design only measured within-patient symptom change in people who already had post-COVID symptoms, with no control group and no measure of incidence. The data cannot support a prevention claim. The authors' remark about acute conditions is a partial caveat, but it does not temper this final sentence.

issues.title: No sample size justification; n=30 with about 21 unadjusted tests behind confident conclusions
issues.explanation: The paper gives no basis for choosing 30 subjects and no power calculation. It reports six subjective and fifteen objective tests, with no correction for multiplicity and no stated significance threshold. The conclusion still speaks of high significance. Several objective p-values (RDW 0.042, platelet and others) would not survive any correction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample size calculation and a multiplicity plan or primary outcome.

quotes.text: Sample Size: Total  30  Post-Covid  subjects  have  been selected
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Method of Collection of Data

issues.title: Significant falls in Hb (-0.52) and RBC (-0.43) labelled 'S' without noting the direction
issues.explanation: The objective table marks Hb and RBC as significant, but both fell from baseline, which is unfavourable. The conclusion mentions 'significance and non-significance' of objective parameters without stating direction. The results cannot be read as supporting benefit, and may signal harm or a lab artefact, with no discussion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reference ranges showing the changes remain normal and a statement that lower values are expected with recovery.

quotes.text: In  Objective  parameters  we  have seen significance and non-significance statistically

issues.title: 'Highly significant' subjective claim omits Weight (p=0.00294, labelled S) tabulated with subjective items
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion say subjective parameters were highly significant. The subjective table has a Weight row with p=0.00294, labelled only S, and the paper's own scheme gives HS to p<0.00001. The Methods list Weight as objective, so the table placement is inconsistent. The blanket wording is slightly too strong, but five of six rows are HS.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that Weight is classified as objective and that 'subjective parameters' means only the five symptom scores.

quotes.text: highly  significant  in  subjective  parameters
In Subjective parameters we have seen  clinically  and  statistically  high  significance

issues.title: No trial registration or ethics approval reported
issues.explanation: Neither a registry identifier nor an ethics committee approval is reported for a prospective interventional study. Without a registered protocol, outcomes cannot be checked against what was planned; the paper names no primary outcome and tests about 21 measures.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CTRI or other registry number and ethics committee approval for this study.

quotes.text: Study Design: Simple random clinical study
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Method of Collection of Data

issues.title: Inclusion limited to up to 1 year post-COVID, but conclusion refers to symptoms 1-2 years after exposure
issues.explanation: The eligibility criterion caps the interval at 1 year. The conclusion describes subjects symptomatic 1-2 years after exposure. Either the sample included people beyond the stated window or the sentence describes patients generally. No time-since-infection data are given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline data showing all subjects were within 12 months of diagnosis, with the conclusion sentence describing the wider clinic population.

quotes.text: Upto  1  year  subjects  have  been  considered  for study and diagnosed as COVID-19 positive.
even after 1-2 years after the exposure to COVID-19

issues.title: CRP t-value printed 13.881 but mean deviation 1.18 / SE 0.304 = 3.88
issues.explanation: The CRP row prints t=13.881. Dividing the printed mean deviation by the printed SE gives 3.88, and the printed p=0.00059 also fits a t near 3.9, not 13.9. The error is confined to this one cell. The CRP result remains significant either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw CRP differences showing t=13.9 and SE much smaller than 0.304.

script.explanation: CRP t = mean deviation / SE: 1.18 / 0.304 gives 3.88158, not the printed 13.881. For the printed value to hold the denominator would have to be 0.0850083, not 0.304.

issues.title: Anorexia grading cites a student thesis; adapted symptom grades not validated in post-COVID subjects
issues.explanation: Most subjective outcomes use named published scales, but the anorexia grading is sourced to a thesis and the paper reports no validation in this population. The grades appear to be simplified versions (for example the MRC table includes grade 5 'Death'). Because the unblinded, uncontrolled assessment relies on these scores, measurement subjectivity adds to the main design weakness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the grading tables are validated, unmodified versions, or that outcomes were rated by blinded assessors.

quotes.text: Anorexia [8]
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Grading of Subjective Parameters

10.21802/artm.2023.2.26.14.headline_claim: A two-month physical therapy program (therapeutic exercise with yoga elements, massage, aromatherapy, autogenic training) is effective for restoring quality of life in women with post-COVID-19 syndrome after cesarean section, with better results than the general rehabilitation program.
10.21802/artm.2023.2.26.14.overall: The headline claim that the physical therapy programme is effective and superior to usual care is only weakly supported: it rests on a small, non-randomised comparison of generic quality-of-life scores, with no numeric results or adjustment, and with natural postpartum improvement visible in all groups. The direction of the ОГ vs ГП difference may be real but its size and cause cannot be established from the paper.

primary_outcome.name: Quality of life: EQ-5D-5L dimensions and EQ-VAS

issues.title: Non-randomised, undescribed allocation to program vs usual care; efficacy stated causally without adjustment
issues.explanation: The program group and comparison group are defined by the intervention received, with no description of how women were allocated, no blinding, and no adjustment for confounders. The program also involved supervised in-person sessions and attention that the comparison group lacked, so differences in EQ-5D scores cannot be attributed to the programme content. The paper nonetheless concludes the programme is effective and superior.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random or concealed allocation, or an adjusted analysis showing the between-group difference persists after controlling for baseline and delivery-related covariates.

quotes.text: Результати обстеження жінок ГП та ОГ при першому обстеженні були статистично однорідними, що дало можливість робити висновки щодо ефективності програми фізичної терапії.
Це свідчить про переваги реабілітаційної програми для корекції ознак постковідного синдрому в жінок, які перенесли кесарів розтин

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes no randomisation or allocation method for ГП vs ОГ, claims baseline homogeneity without printed data or test, and states programme superiority causally using unadjusted t-tests on small groups with no multiplicity correction. Whether allocation was in fact non-random cannot be confirmed beyond the absence of any description, but the causal claim is not supported by the design as reported.

issues.title: Conclusion rests on 'positive dynamics' that natural postpartum recovery also produces (KG 90.2% vs ОГ 68.8%)
issues.explanation: The Conclusions state that positive dynamics evidence the programme's effectiveness. All three groups improved, including the control group with no COVID and no programme, who improved more on most subscales, so improvement alone cannot indicate efficacy. Only the ОГ versus ГП comparison speaks to the programme, and that rests on a non-randomised design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Conclusions restricted to the between-group ОГ vs ГП difference with appropriate adjustment.

quotes.text: а позитивна динаміка є свідченням ефективності апробованої програми фізичної терапії жінок з постковідним синдромом
у жінок КГ за підшкалою мобільності покращення становило 90,2%, ГП 31,6%, ОГ 68,8%

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions do cite 'positive dynamics' as evidence of efficacy even though the control group with no intervention improved more (90.2% vs 68.8% on mobility), and the Results themselves say all groups' improvement was associated with normal postpartum recovery. It is narrower than the point suggests, though, because the Results' efficacy claim rests mainly on the ОГ vs ГП comparison (68.8% vs 31.6%), which does separate the programme from natural recovery to a degree, subject to the design problems in i1.

issues.title: Very small groups (14 and 15) with no sample-size justification and no numeric results printed
issues.explanation: With 14 and 15 women per arm and no sample-size calculation, estimates are imprecise and prone to chance imbalance. The paper prints only percentage improvements and p<0.05 statements; means, SDs, effect sizes and exact p-values appear only in figures, so the strength of the claimed superiority cannot be judged. The confident conclusion is not matched by the precision of the evidence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation or reported effect sizes with confidence intervals showing adequate precision.

quotes.text: Основну групу склали 14 жінок після кесаревого розтину, які перенесли COVID-19 упродовж вагітності

10.21802/artm.2023.4.28.108.overall: The finding that both rehabilitation arms improved, with OG2 improving more, is plausible and the direction is consistent across scales. The superiority claim is weakened by the undescribed randomization and blinding and the absence of a prespecified primary outcome. It is further weakened by implausibly small dispersion values that conflict with the stated baseline equivalence. The 'accelerates recovery' claim is not supported by the measured outcomes.

issues.title: Conclusion 2 rests on within-group change; between-group superiority uses post values and t-tests only
issues.explanation: Conclusion 2 credits the programme with significant improvement versus baseline on all parameters, yet the standard-protocol arm also improved significantly (DGI +9%, FGA +16.4%). The superiority claim is therefore weaker than stated, though a between-group comparison exists.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis of change scores or an ANCOVA adjusted for baseline showing OG2 > OG1.

issues.explanation: The methods name only Student's t-test and a 0.05 threshold. There is no multiplicity control and no primary outcome. With many pairwise comparisons some false positives are possible. The consistent direction and large effects make the main finding fairly robust to this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or multiplicity-adjusted p-values that stay below 0.05.

issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or supplement describing the randomization sequence, concealment and blinding.

10.21802/artm.2024.1.29.142.headline_claim: A 3-month physical therapy program for older post-COVID patients with sarcopenia produced a statistically significantly better effect on nutritional, asthenic and respiratory parameters than the standard COVID-19 rehabilitation protocol.
10.21802/artm.2024.1.29.142.overall: The headline claim that the tailored programme beats the standard protocol is directionally plausible given the large differences printed, but it rests on tests with no multiplicity control, undescribed randomisation and blinding, and a multicomponent package compared with standard care without matching dose. Some table markers do not match the text or the 'all indicators' wording, and the printed spreads look more like standard errors than SDs. The results should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Not named as primary; stated aim is effect on nutritional, asthenic and respiratory parameters (BMI, limb circumferences, MNA, SNAQ, 6-minute walk test, spirometry, oximetry)

issues.title: Superiority over standard protocol rests on unspecified randomisation and unblinded, dose-unmatched comparison
issues.explanation: Randomisation is mentioned in one sentence with no method, concealment or description of what was blinded. The tailored programme differs from the standard-protocol arm in content and probably in amount of contact. Outcomes are partly self-reported (MNA, SNAQ, Borg, dyspnoea), which are open to bias when assessors or patients know the arm. The statement that the programme is 'significantly better' than standard care is therefore tentative, and the comparison with the healthy control group says nothing about treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described randomisation and concealment procedure, blinded outcome assessment, and equal supervised contact time in both arms.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does state a blind randomised split, so 'unspecified randomisation' is only partly right: the method of sequence generation, concealment and what or who was blinded are not described, and no flow or dropout information is given. issues.title: Uncorrected pairwise Student's t-tests across ~12 outcomes, 3 groups and 2 timepoints; no primary outcome
issues.explanation: The only test named is Student's t-test, with a fixed alpha of 0.05. Tables 1-3 apply it to many outcomes and to three kinds of contrast: control vs arm, before vs after, and OG1 vs OG2. No omnibus test, repeated-measures model or multiplicity correction is described. This makes the nominal p<0.05 flags less reliable, especially for the smaller between-arm differences that underpin the claim of superiority.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated prespecified primary outcome, or multiplicity-adjusted or mixed-model results showing the OG1-vs-OG2 differences survive.

issues.title: Dispersion labelled SD looks too small to be SD (BMI ±0.07-0.15, age ±1.2 in 60-75 y sample)
issues.explanation: Table headings and Methods describe the spread as standard deviation. They look more like standard errors, though even as SEs the age value would imply an SD of about 12 years, which cannot occur in a 60-75 range. issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that ± is SE, or individual-level data showing the actual SDs.

10.21802/artm.2025.1.33.13.headline_claim: Tivorel plus quercetin is an effective combination for improving endothelial function and haemostasis indicators in patients with type 2 diabetes and post-COVID syndrome, and also lowers lipids, glucose, HbA1c and inflammatory/oxidative markers.
10.21802/artm.2025.1.33.13.overall: The claim that tivorel plus quercetin is effective rests on a small, non-randomised, unblinded 20 vs 20 comparison with no described tests, correction or limitations. Several benefit claims rely on within-group changes that controls shared, and a few printed values (IL-1 vs IL-10 label, HbA1c, the control-arm significance statement) are inconsistent. The data are best read as hypothesis-generating, not as showing efficacy.

primary_outcome.name: Not designated; lipid profile, glucose/HbA1c, inflammation/oxidative stress, endothelial markers and haemostasis markers were all measured

issues.title: Non-randomised, unblinded 20 vs 20 comparison with unspecified controls supports an 'effective' conclusion
issues.explanation: Allocation method, blinding, control therapy and sample size are not described. The treated arm received IV and oral tivorel plus a month of quercetin, while controls got unspecified standard care. Baselines differ (HbA1c 6.20 vs 5.71, glucose 9.21 vs 8.12), and there is no adjustment, no safety reporting and no limitations section. Conclusions use causal wording ('призводило', 'є ефективною комбінацією'), which this design cannot support beyond tentative signals.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or methods text showing random allocation, blinded assessment and baseline-adjusted analysis.

quotes.text: Контрольну групу склали 20 пацієнтів, які отримували стандартну терапію без тіворелю та кверцетину.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper reports a 20 vs 20 comparison with no stated randomisation, blinding, allocation method or description of the control regimen, and with baseline differences (HbA1c 6.20 vs 5.71). It nonetheless concludes the combination 'is an effective combination' (Conclusion 3) without any design caveat. The claim that it was non-randomised and unblinded is an inference from the absence of any such statement, not something the paper declares.

issues.title: PTI, fibrinogen and CRP benefit claimed without a marked between-group difference; controls also improved
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusions credit the combination with lower CRP, PTI and fibrinogen. In Tables 3 and 5 the treated arm's values for these rows carry only the within-group mark (*), with no # for difference from controls. Control CRP and PTI also changed significantly. The 'effective' conclusion for these markers therefore rests on pre/post change, not on a demonstrated advantage over standard care.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group or baseline-adjusted analysis showing significant differences for CRP, PTI and fibrinogen.

quotes.text: Це свідчить про ефективність тіворелю та кверцитину у покращенні якості лікування ПС у хворих на ЦД 2-го типу.

second_reader.what_stands: For CRP and PTI, both groups improved significantly and no between-group significance is marked, so the statement that controls stayed 'significantly higher' than the main group is not supported by Table 3 or Table 5. For fibrinogen, controls did not change significantly but no between-group test is shown either. The efficacy wording in the abstract and Conclusion 3 is therefore supported by the starred within-group changes, not by any shown between-group difference, for these three variables. It is not true of all the biomarkers, since several others carry '#' marks.

issues.title: HbA1c falls 6.20% to 4.45% (-28.2%) in about a month, ending below the normal range
issues.explanation: HbA1c reflects roughly 2-3 months of glycaemia, so a 1.75-point fall within the ~4-week course, ending at 4.45%, is hard to explain. Baseline HbA1c of 6.20% is also low relative to the mean fasting glucose of 9.21 mmol/L in these diabetic inpatients. The implausible values undermine the glycaemic results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Methods confirming a distinct assay or measurement unit, and a longer follow-up consistent with HbA1c kinetics.

quotes.location: Table 2, HbA1c row, main group after treatment

issues.title: Text says only NFA changed significantly in controls; Table 5 also marks control PTI and AT III
issues.explanation: The Results say the only significant change in the control group was NFA. Table 5 puts the significance mark on three control rows: PTI (93.72 to 88.35), AT III (90.44 to 97.81) and NFA. The text understates how much the control group improved, which makes the contrast with the treated group look larger than the table supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the asterisks on control PTI and AT III were misplaced and that those changes were not significant.

quotes.text: У контрольній групі відбувалось достовірне зниження лише НФА на 12,8 %.

Table 5, AT III row, control after treatment

issues.title: ~25 markers across 5 domains, with no tests, alpha or multiplicity approach stated and no p-values
issues.explanation: The paper names only the software used. Which tests produced * and #, the alpha, and any correction for the roughly 25 markers across five domains are all unstated, and no exact p-values appear. With so many unadjusted comparisons some positive marks are expected by chance, which weakens the secondary results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description with named tests, alpha and a correction or a prespecified primary outcome.

quotes.text: Математичну та статистичну обробку отриманих результатів дослідження проводили з використанням програми STATISTICA 10.0.

issues.title: Fall in IL-10 (anti-inflammatory cytokine) presented as reduced systemic inflammation
issues.explanation: Conclusion 2 reads the 20.6% decrease in IL-10 as lower inflammatory activity. IL-10 is generally regarded as anti-inflammatory, so a decline is ambiguous at best, and could be read as reduced counter-regulation. Only CRP clearly supports the inflammation claim, and its between-group difference is unmarked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Context showing IL-10 was used here as a pro-inflammatory proxy, or additional inflammatory markers such as IL-6 or TNF-alpha.

issues.explanation: Both abstracts attribute a 20.6% reduction to interleukin-1. The Methods measure only IL-10, and the Results and Table 3 give 20.6% for IL-10 (9.52 to 7.56). The abstract therefore names a cytokine that was never measured. The effect on the paper's conclusions is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that IL-1 was also measured and also fell by exactly 20.6%.

issues.title: No ethics approval or consent statement for an interventional allocation of 40 inpatients
issues.explanation: Patients were allocated to an active drug regimen, yet the text contains no statement of ethics committee approval, consent or registration. This may be an omission in the write-up rather than in conduct, and it cannot be resolved from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An approval number and consent statement from the journal's full text or the authors.

quotes.text: Контрольну групу склали 20 пацієнтів, які отримували стандартну терапію без тіворелю та кверцетину.

10.21886/2308-6424-2022-10-4-32-42.headline_claim: Adding recombinant interferon α-2b with vitamins E and C to standard therapy for chronic recurrent prostatitis in post-COVID-19 patients normalises most patients' clinical and laboratory parameters.
10.21886/2308-6424-2022-10-4-32-42.overall: The paper's efficacy conclusion is weakly supported: allocation appears to have followed treatment choice rather than randomisation, the arms differ at baseline, there is no blinding, and the claimed benefit rests on within-arm changes in subjective scores with no between-arm estimates. The large symptom score falls in the interferon arms are suggestive, but 'proven effective', 'comparable to antibiotics' and 'normalised in most patients' are not shown by the data presented.

primary_outcome.name: NIH-CPSI symptom score (no primary outcome designated)

issues.title: 'Comparable to antibiotics' and 'proven' efficacy claimed with no between-arm effect sizes or CIs
issues.explanation: The Discussion says interferon results are comparable to antibiotic results, but no between-arm effect estimate, confidence interval or equivalence margin is given. Comparability cannot be shown by non-significance in a three-arm study of 16-18 per arm, and it also sits oddly with the abstract's claim that interferon arms did better at 3 and 6 months. Efficacy claims also lean on within-arm change (c3) and on non-randomised allocation (c2); this issue covers the combined overreach of the comparative and causal wording, including the 'proved effective' statement (c11).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-arm estimates with CIs against a prespecified equivalence or superiority margin, from a properly randomised comparison.

quotes.text: Нам удалось показать, что результаты лечения пациентов с ХРБП рекомбинантным интерфероном α-2b сопоставимы с результатами лечения антибактериальными препаратами.
Результаты исследования доказали, что терапия рекомбинантным интерфероном α-2b является эффективной

second_reader.what_stands: The paper asserts that interferon results are comparable to antibiotics and that efficacy was 'proven', but reports no between-arm effect estimates, confidence intervals or equivalence or non-inferiority framework. With non-random allocation, small arms and a co-administered vitamin complex, 'proved' is stronger than the evidence allows. Note too that the Results actually describe divergence between arms at 3-6 months, which sits awkwardly with the word 'comparable'.

issues.title: Called 'randomised', but allocation by 'choice of therapy'; unequal arms and baseline IPSS 5.3 vs 8.5 vs 7.0
issues.explanation: The paper labels the study prospective and randomised, but never describes sequence generation or concealment, and the design section says patients were divided into groups depending on the choice of therapy, which reads as non-random allocation. Baseline IPSS differed (5.3, 8.5, 7.0) while the paper only asserts groups were comparable on 'a number of indicators' without showing a baseline table. Between-arm differences could therefore reflect selection and baseline imbalance, not treatment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described random sequence and concealment procedure, plus a baseline table with between-group tests showing balance.

quotes.text: В период лечения в зависимости от выбора терапии пациенты были разделены на три группы.
в группе 2 - 8,5 ± 1,0, а в группе 3 - 7,0 ± 1,0 баллов
До лечения группы были сопоставимы по ряду показателей.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the study 'randomized' yet describes allocation as depending on the choice of therapy, with no randomisation procedure given. Baseline IPSS differs notably between arms (5.3 vs 8.5 vs 7.0), and the comparability claim has no supporting table or test. The arm sizes (18/18/16) are only slightly unequal, so that part is weak. Baseline NIH-CPSI (the primary-type symptom score) is well balanced, so baseline imbalance applies to IPSS rather than to all outcomes.

issues.title: Interferon benefit at 3-6 months inferred from within-arm changes; no between-group tests reported
issues.explanation: The abstract states that after 3 and 6 months the improvement was seen only in the interferon groups, which is a comparison between arms. The Results support it only by within-arm p-values versus baseline (e.g. group 1 vs group 2 trends), with no between-group test at 3 or 6 months. A significant change in one arm and not in another is not evidence that the arms differ.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported between-arm tests (or a repeated-measures model) at 3 and 6 months showing interferon arms differ from the antibiotic-only arm.

quotes.text: значимость различий между значениями показателей на различных этапах исследования по сравнению с исходными значени-ями определяли с применением критерия Wilcoxon.
через 1 месяц - 7,3 ± 0,5, через 3 месяца - 7,2 ± 0,8 и к 6 месяцам снизился до 2,2 ± 0,2 баллов (р < 0,05).

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that interferon arms benefit at 3-6 months rests on within-arm comparisons with baseline and on narrative contrast with group 1; no between-arm tests, effect sizes or CIs at 3 or 6 months are printed in the text, even though Mann-Whitney is named in the Methods. A single unspecified between-group significance statement appears at 1 month. Figures that might contain more were not available in the extracted text, so the absence is of reported results in the text. Group 1 also remained significantly improved from baseline at 6 months by the printed means, so 'no benefit' in the antibiot

issues.title: 'Normalisation in most patients' claimed without proportions; Qmax and prostate volume changes non-significant
issues.explanation: The conclusion says clinical and laboratory parameters were normalised in most patients, but results are given as group means, never as the proportion of patients reaching a normal value. Prostate volume only trended down (p>0.05), Qmax was within the normal range at all points including baseline, and group 3 Qmax at 6 months was not different from baseline. The claim is stronger than the data shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing most patients with values inside the reference range for each parameter at 6 months.

quotes.text: позволяет нормализовать у большинства пациентов как клинические, так и лабораторные показатели

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion that normalisation occurred in most patients is not supported by any reported proportion or responder analysis; only group means are given. Prostate volume change was non-significant and Qmax was already within normal limits, so the claim of 'laboratory' normalisation rests mainly on leukocyte and macrophage counts shown in figures. The clinical score means in the interferon arms do fall to low values, so the claim is plausible for symptoms but unquantified at patient level.

issues.title: No blinding stated; main outcomes are patient-completed NIH-CPSI and IPSS questionnaires
issues.explanation: The paper does not mention any blinding, and the primary outcomes are patient-reported symptom scores. Expectation effects could favour the interferon arms, which received an extra, novel-seeming treatment. This is partly mitigated by objective measures (microscopy, uroflowmetry), but those showed weaker results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and patients were masked, or objective primary outcomes that agree with the symptom scores.

quotes.text: Для оценки клинико-лабораторных показателей на всех этапах исследования анализировали результаты анкетирования с использованием шкалы симптомов хронического простатита

issues.title: Arms of 16-18 with no sample-size justification, yet efficacy described as 'proven' (впервые доказана)
issues.explanation: With 18, 18 and 16 patients and no power calculation, the study can only give tentative estimates of between-arm differences. The authors nonetheless state that efficacy was 'proven' for the first time, which this sample and analysis cannot support. The issue is chiefly the strength of the wording; it overlaps with the unsupported-conclusion problem under c10.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation showing adequate power for the primary comparison.

quotes.text: в нашем исследовании впервые доказана эффективность рекомбинантного интерферона α-2b как при монотерапии, так и в комбинации с АБт.

issues.title: No participant flow, dropout or per-timepoint n reported for 6-month follow-up
issues.explanation: The paper gives 52 patients and group sizes but does not report how many were assessed at 1, 3 and 6 months, nor whether any withdrew. Since the six-month results carry the main claim, missing denominators leave open whether the analysed sets match the allocated groups.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CONSORT-style flow showing all 52 patients assessed at every time point.

quotes.text: Период наблюдения составил 6 месяцев с мониторингом клинико-лабораторных показателей, оценённых до лечения, через 1, 3 и 6 месяцев от начала терапии.

issues.title: Six outcomes at four timepoints tested at p<0.05 with no primary outcome or multiplicity control
issues.explanation: The paper tests symptom scores, leukocytes, macrophages, Qmax and prostate volume at several timepoints against baseline at an unadjusted 0.05 level and designates no primary outcome. The conclusion then summarises favourable findings across outcomes. The effect is to inflate the chance of some significant result, though the large symptom score changes are unlikely to be wholly chance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome and a multiplicity strategy or hierarchical testing plan.

quotes.text: Пороговый уровень значимости установлен на уровне p < 0,05 при α = 0,05.

issues.title: Table 1 S. lentus frequency 40,0% not attainable from 52 patients (20/52=38.5, 21/52=40.4)
issues.explanation: The Methods say detection frequencies were computed on 52 patients, so each percentage should be a multiple of 1.92%. The printed 40.0% for S. lentus is not reachable: 20 patients gives 38.5% and 21 gives 40.4%. This is a small reporting error in a descriptive microbiology table and does not affect the efficacy conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator for S. lentus explicitly stated in the paper, or a corrected count/percentage pair.
