issues.title: Prospective randomised study with no registry identifier reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomised comparison but gives no trial registration number, so prespecified outcomes cannot be checked. This matters more because no primary outcome is named and many outcomes are reported. Ethics approval is dated October 2017, so registration was feasible.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry with a prespecified primary outcome matching the reported analyses.

quotes.text: Проведено проспективное рандомизированное сравнительное исследование с включением 52 пациентов

issues.title: Antibiotic-only active control, no placebo; group 2 differs from group 1 by an add-on and group 3 omits antibiotic
issues.explanation: The control arm receives levofloxacin only, so non-specific effects of an additional rectal treatment cannot be separated from the interferon effect. This is a defensible choice of comparator, but it limits what the symptom-score results can show. It is largely covered by the blinding and between-group issues above.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A placebo or sham suppository arm, or masked assessors.

quotes.text: Пациентам группы 1 (n = 18) проводили антибактериальную терапию (АБт) - левофлоксацин 500 мг перорально 1 р/сут 28 дней

10.21926/obm.icm.2401010.headline_claim: Medicament testing with an RNA polymerase nosode, ribavirin and dexamethasone restores decreased electrodermal impedance at acupuncture points in some patients with long COVID, suggesting feasibility of EAV-based diagnosis.
10.21926/obm.icm.2401010.overall: The headline claim concerns changes in a device reading when drugs are placed in the device, and it is not supported as a patient-level effect. The key comparisons are built on outcome-defined subsets, with an unvalidated outcome, no multiplicity control, no registration, and several internal numerical inconsistencies in Table 1 and the Results text. The paper's own stated conclusion of 'feasibility' is the most that can be defended.

primary_outcome.name: Post-medicament-test EAV readings at acupuncture points (arbitrary measurement value)

issues.title: Tables 3 and 4 split patients by response to the test, so a main-group 'restoration' is built in by selection
issues.explanation: Patients and points were classified as positive responders (readings returning to normal) or negative responders (readings dropping further) according to the device reading after the drug, and then pre/post readings were compared within those subsets. Post-test means of about +5.8 in the main-group positive table are therefore close to guaranteed by the classification. The paper never gives, per arm, how many of the ~50 patients responded positively, negatively or not at all, so the net effect of the drugs versus glucose cannot be assessed. This undermines the claim of a between-group difference.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A report of all randomised patients in both arms, with response proportions and unselected pre/post comparisons per meridian.

quotes.text: Results of positive response to medicament testing in the compared groups of patients.
In some of the patients studied, we observed a negative response to the tested drugs in the main group

second_reader.what_stands: Because patients are sorted into Table 3 or Table 4 by whether their post-test reading rose or fell, the large pre-to-post gain in Table 3 for the main group is partly built in by selection, and the pre/post p-values within Table 3 are not independent tests of an effect. The paper does show a comparison group with the same split (control post-test means stay near pre-test), and that between-group contrast is not purely a selection artefact, though the paper does not report the proportion of patients falling in each response category, so the real rate of 'restoration' cannot be judged.

issues.title: Sole outcome is an unvalidated EAV device reading (AMV = reading - 50), not linked to clinical status
issues.explanation: All results are device readings shifted by 50 units. The paper offers no evidence that these readings track long COVID, symptoms or any drug effect in people, and the cited references show only associations with other conditions. The readings are also operator-dependent and were taken by two investigators. Hence a change in AMV cannot be interpreted as clinical benefit or even as a reproducible physiological effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Validation data showing that EAV/AMV changes correlate with long COVID status or symptom improvement, or reproducibility data between operators.

quotes.text: The arbitrary measurement value (AMV) was used to analyze the MT results.
It is recommended only for statistical analysis and data comparison [10].

second_reader.what_stands: The only quantitative outcome analysed is the AMV, a simple transformation of an EAV device reading, and the paper reports no validation of the device and no link between AMV and clinical status. The authors themselves say fatigue/nervous-system associations 'require further research' and call for further clinical studies. 'Unvalidated' is a judgement from the absence of validation evidence in the paper; the paper cites outside literature (Voll, refs 18-26) for impedance-condition associations, but none shows AMV tracking long COVID status.

issues.title: Conclusion says drugs 'contribute to restoration' of impedance in patients, but drugs were only placed in a device
issues.explanation: The drugs were placed in the honeycomb of the EAV device and the patient's skin reading was observed; no patient received any treatment. The conclusion nonetheless attributes a restorative effect to the drugs in patients, and the Discussion proposes a physical mechanism of molecular vibration fields without evidence. What the data can show is that a device reading changed when a substance was in the circuit, which is a very different claim. The caveat about further clinical study partly limits the overstatement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that a mechanism or clinical benefit exists in treated patients, or reframing of the claim as a device-reading change only.

quotes.text: ribavirin, and dexamethasone as drugs that contribute to the restoration of electrodermal impedance at the APs of the identified meridians in some patients with long COVID syndrome.
To test ribavirin and dexamethasone, the drugs were placed separately into the honeycomb of the EAV device.

second_reader.what_stands: The measured 'restoration' is a change in a device reading while a drug sits in the honeycomb, not a response in patients who took the drug, so the Conclusion's wording that the drugs 'contribute to the restoration of electrodermal impedance' in patients goes beyond what the design tests. The authors do say further clinical studies are needed, which softens but does not remove the mismatch.

issues.title: ~22 meridians tested in two tables at p<0.05 with no multiplicity control; weaker cells unreliable
issues.explanation: Separate pre/post and between-group tests were run for many meridians, in both the positive-response and negative-response tables, with no stated correction or primary meridian. Many results are marked P < 0.001 or < 0.01 and would probably survive adjustment. The isolated single-asterisk or single-caret differences, and any statement about individual meridians such as Ge or Hau, are fragile. The overall claim of restoration is weakened mainly at the secondary, meridian-by-meridian level.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary meridian or a stated correction method with adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: Intergroup differences were considered significant at p < 0.05.

issues.title: Randomised placebo-controlled trial with no registration, no named primary outcome, and no stated sample size
issues.explanation: The paper describes itself as a blind randomised placebo-controlled trial over almost three years but gives no registry identifier, no prespecified primary outcome and no sample size justification. With dozens of meridian-level tests, reporting only the significant ones cannot be checked against a plan. The blinding described covers patients only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registration entry dated before enrolment naming the same outcomes.

quotes.text: In this blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we assigned a 1:1 ratio

issues.title: Main-group age SD 19.28 is impossible for ages 16-50 (maximum sample SD about 17.17 at n=50)
issues.explanation: Inclusion was restricted to ages 16 to 50, a range of 34 years. No sample of 50 people confined to that range can have an SD above about 17.2, yet Table 1 prints 19.28 for the main group. Either the ages, the SD or the inclusion range is misreported. The control SD of 17.17 sits exactly at the theoretical ceiling, which is also odd. This is baseline data only, so the efficacy result is not directly affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that some participants were outside 16-50 (for example a different inclusion range), or that 19.28 is a typographical error for another value.

quotes.text: subjects of either gender, aged 16 to 50

quotes.location: Table 1, Age row, main group column

issues.title: Text gives 54 females of 99, but Table 1 percentages imply 26 + 24 = 50 females
issues.explanation: Section 2.2 states 54 females and 45 males. Table 1 gives 52% female of 50 and 49% female of 49, which correspond to 26 and 24 women, or 50 in total. The two sources disagree by four participants. The error is small and does not bear on the efficacy findings, but it shows the baseline reporting is inconsistent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 54 females include participants not in the 99 randomised, or corrected Table 1 percentages.

quotes.text: Ninety-nine patients (45 males and 54 females, aged 16-50)

issues.title: Results name Ma among the 12 significant meridians; Table 3 has Le and no Ma row
issues.explanation: The Results sentence lists twelve meridians with restored readings, including Ma (stomach) and omitting Le (liver). Table 3 has twelve rows, includes Le, and has no Ma row. One of the two is wrong, so the reader cannot tell which meridians the claimed restoration applies to. The effect on the conclusions is minor.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An erratum or the underlying data showing which meridian is correct.

quotes.text: Ne, Kr, 3E, He, Pa/Mi(S), Pa/Mi(D), Ge, Ma, Hau, Ni, Bl, Pa/Mi-11

10.2196/49342.headline_claim: Combined digital interventions and personal pilot support reduced post-COVID symptoms compared with a comparison group, and the authors conclude that this combined approach is effective in treating PACS.
10.2196/49342.overall: The finding that IG and ACG participants report fewer symptoms over time is probably real as a self-reported change, but its attribution to the program is weak: the comparison with the CompG is non-randomised and untreated, outcomes are unblinded and self-reported on an unvalidated scale, and about half the randomised sample appears absent from the analyses. The conclusions about effectiveness and sustainability go beyond what the design supports, and the numeric slips in Tables 1 and 2 are small but leave the symptom scale poorly defined.

primary_outcome.name: Symptom severity (sum of 14 PACS symptom items)

primary_outcomes.measure: Change from baseline in the Post-/ Long-COVID symptoms at 3 months
Subjective prognosis of return to work

issues.title: Effect vs CompG rests on a non-randomised, untreated, differently recruited comparison group
issues.explanation: Hypothesis 1, the main treatment-versus-no-treatment claim, compares randomised IG and ACG participants with a CompG that was recruited by a different pathway across Germany, received nothing, and was only matched by propensity score. Differences in motivation, help-seeking and unmeasured prognosis cannot be removed by matching on age and a few covariates. The authors flag this, but the Conclusion still states that the study 'clearly demonstrated' effectiveness, so the effect estimate is only tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Randomised allocation to a passive control, or a sensitivity analysis showing the CompG contrast is robust to unmeasured confounding.

quotes.text: it should be kept in mind that the CompG was only matched but not randomized.
quotes.location: Limitations and Recommendations for Future Research and Practice

quotes.text: this group was recruited via a different recruitment pathway

second_reader.what_stands: The paper itself states that the CompG was matched but not randomised, was untreated (questionnaires only), and was recruited through a different pathway and geography (all of Germany versus Bavaria only). The effect versus CompG therefore rests on a non-randomised, differently recruited comparison, which the authors acknowledge in the Limitations and Conclusion. They also call the study a randomised controlled trial in the title, and the matching was on age, sex, precondition and BMI as listed in Table 3 rather than on baseline symptoms, so residual confounding and selection differences canno

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-reported outcomes and no attention control; Conclusion still says support 'seems effective'
issues.explanation: Participants knew their group and all outcomes were self-reported on a project-specific scale. Part of the IG/ACG improvement versus the CompG could therefore reflect expectation, contact with a pilot, or social desirability. The authors concede this, and that the specific effects of personal support and digital training cannot be separated, but the Conclusion still says professional support seems effective and that the study clearly demonstrated effectiveness. The conclusion is stronger than the design allows.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded or objective outcome, or an attention-matched control showing the same benefit.

quotes.text: Patients were not blinded regarding the study groups
these effects in self-reported symptom severity could also be attributed (partly) to the placebo effect
as it seems to be an effective way to support patients with PACS

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is open-label with only self-reported outcomes and no attention or placebo control, and it says so (Study Process, Discussion, Limitations). The conclusion nevertheless states that the study 'clearly demonstrated the potential and effectiveness' and that support 'seems to be an effective way', which is somewhat stronger than the design allows, although the authors do hedge and call for objective measures and rigorous randomisation.

issues.title: Methods say symptom score is a sum of 14 items (min 6 at entry), but Table 2 T1 means are 2.67-2.73
issues.explanation: The Methods describe the primary outcome as a sum of 14 items scored 0-3, and the entry rule requires at least 3 symptoms scored 2 or more, so any sum must be at least 6. Table 2 reports T1 means of 2.67-2.73 with SDs near 0.5-0.7, which is only possible on a per-item or per-endorsed-symptom scale. The outcome scale is therefore mis-described or mis-reported, and readers cannot tell what a change of 0.14 or 0.3 points means clinically.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper or protocol that the score is a mean per item (or per endorsed symptom), with the sum wording being a slip.

quotes.text: The sum of scores was calculated.
with severity ≥ 2 on a scale from 0 (no problem) to 3 (extreme problem)

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; IG vs ACG null (n=73 vs 152) read as the assessment 'failing'
issues.explanation: The IG size reflects clinic capacity and no power calculation is given for Hypothesis 2. The IG-ACG interaction estimates are small but imprecise (for example 0.09, SE 0.05 for T1/T2), and the Discussion says the assessment 'seems to have failed to create long-term advantages'. Absence of a significant difference in an unpowered comparison does not show absence of benefit. The authors partly acknowledge this by listing reasons an effect may emerge later.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified power calculation or equivalence margins with CIs excluding a meaningful IG benefit.

quotes.text: the target sample size of the ACG was set to twice the size of the IG
but no difference between the IG and the ACG was found.
seems to have failed to create long-term advantages in the IG

issues.title: IG/ACG analyses use about 116 people of 225 randomised, with no stated attrition handling
issues.explanation: The Hypothesis 2 group effects carry df of 114-116, implying roughly 116-118 participants contributed data against 225 randomised (73 + 152). That would be about half lost, and it is not discussed. The paper describes complete-case mixed models and no sensitivity or ITT analysis, so results may reflect those who stayed in the study.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 1 or text showing most randomised participants contributed data at every time point, or an ITT sensitivity analysis.

quotes.text: Random slopes could not be included in the HLMs, as there were not enough observations for the HLMs to converge.

issues.title: Primary symptom score is a project-built 14-item scale with only Cronbach alpha .80 at T1
issues.explanation: The symptom outcome that underlies Hypotheses 1 and 2 was built for the project and checked only for internal consistency at T1. No validity, sensitivity to change or clinically important difference is given, so the 0.1-0.4 point changes cannot be interpreted clinically. The authors themselves say the outcomes need objective validation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Published validation of the 14-item scale, or concordant results on an established PACS measure.

quotes.text: Symptom severity was measured at all time points with a scale developed for the project
Cronbach α was .80 at T1 across groups.
need to be validated with objective measurements
quotes.location: Limitations and Recommendations for Future Research and Practice

issues.title: Discussion says results show 'sustainability' though follow-up was 6 weeks and CompG had no T5
issues.explanation: Follow-up after the 6-week digital program was only 6 weeks, and only the IG and ACG were measured at T5. The Discussion nevertheless says the results show sustainability and that patients learned coping skills. The authors' own limitations section says the period is too short to conclude sustained improvement, so the Discussion wording is not supported by their data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A longer controlled follow-up including the CompG.

quotes.text: showing the sustainability of the health care facilitation program concerning symptoms
this period is too short to conclude that
quotes.location: Limitations and Recommendations for Future Research and Practice

issues.title: Registered 2022-02-10, after the recorded 2021-12-15 start; no primary outcome named in paper
issues.explanation: The registry record NCT05238415 was first submitted about 8 weeks after the study start date. The paper states only that the study was registered, without noting the timing, and designates no primary outcome, so readers cannot check outcome selection against the registered plan. The registry lists enrollment of 192 against 225 randomised and 1020 recruited in the paper, which also needs reconciling.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that registration or enrolment of the first participant occurred earlier, or that outcomes were fixed before data collection.

quotes.text: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials

issues.title: CompG sex counts sum to 762 of 795 (33 unaccounted); IG and ACG columns reconcile
issues.explanation: In Table 1 the IG and ACG sex counts add to 73 and 152, but the CompG female and male counts add to 762 against n=795. The 33 missing records are not explained, and the text total of 763 females out of 1020 does not state a missing-data denominator. Separately, the Methods say no participant indicated being diverse, yet the ACG shows 1 'Other'. This is a small reporting inconsistency and does not change any main result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that 33 CompG participants had missing sex, or a corrected Table 1.

quotes.text: CompG c (n=795)

issues.title: IG obesity cell 8 (8.0%) of n=73 is 11.0%
issues.explanation: Table 1 prints 8 (8.0) for obesity in the IG with n=73. Eight of 73 is 11.0%, so either the count or the percentage is wrong. It is a one-cell error that does not affect any outcome analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table showing 8 (11.0).

quotes.text: IG a (n=73)

script.explanation: 8/73 = 10.96%, but the paper prints 8.0, outside the rounding interval [7.95, 8.10]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 100.0 rather than 73.

issues.title: Text condition counts exceed Table 1 group sums: cardiovascular 192 vs 146, obesity 157 vs 111, mental illness 122 vs 95
issues.explanation: The Results give overall counts of previous conditions across all 1020 patients, but the group cells in Table 1 add to far fewer. The shortfall is 46 for cardiovascular disease and 46 for obesity, and 27 for mental illness. The paper offers no explanation, so it is unclear which source is correct, though no outcome analysis uses these counts directly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of a different denominator for the text counts, or a corrected Table 1.

10.2196/89631.headline_claim: A web-based yogic breathing and meditation program is feasible and shows potential benefit for people with long COVID, with secondary outcome improvements in mood, dyspnea and somatic symptoms.
10.2196/89631.overall: The feasibility claim rests on adherence data available for under half of eligible participants, with markedly more missing data in the waitlist arm, and the benefit claims come from an open-label self-report comparison against a waitlist with no multiplicity correction. The efficacy signals (mood, dyspnea, somatic symptoms) are best treated as hypothesis-generating. The numeric inconsistencies (race counts, adherence-outcome wording, registration timing) are minor..

primary_outcome.name: Adherence (completing at least 1 practice on >=4 days/week in all 3 active-intervention weeks)

primary_outcomes.time_frame: For Phase 1 analysis: Baseline to 3 weeks. For Phase 2 analysis: Baseline to 6 weeks.

issues.title: Open-label waitlist design with self-reported outcomes and ~15 uncorrected secondary tests supports only a tentative signal
issues.explanation: All efficacy outcomes are self-reported by unblinded participants compared with a no-activity waitlist, so expectancy and group-attention effects are confounded with the intervention. About a dozen of the many secondary outcomes reached P between .01 and .04 with no multiplicity adjustment, and the key secondary outcome (PSS) was null. The Conclusions state the study 'demonstrates' potential benefit; the evidence supports hypothesis-generating signals only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded or active-control comparison, or multiplicity-adjusted results where the mood and somatic outcomes still hold.

quotes.text: Outcomes were self-reported, and participants could not be blinded to group assignment
Significant group × time interactions indicated greater improvement in the intervention group across multiple POMS domains
This study demonstrates the feasibility and potential benefit of a brief, fully web-based yogic breathing and meditation intervention

second_reader.what_stands: The trial was open-label with self-reported outcomes and about 17 secondary tests (slightly more than 15) with no stated multiplicity correction. The prespecified key secondary outcome, PSS, was null, and most significant p values lie between .01 and .04. The data therefore support only a tentative signal. The authors do acknowledge the blinding and self-report limits and call the signal preliminary, but the Conclusions' 'demonstrates ... potential benefit' is stronger than this, and multiplicity is never discussed.

issues.title: Primary outcome adherence evaluable in 58/124 (47%); differential missingness; week-3 completion unreported
issues.explanation: Adherence, the primary outcome, was classifiable in 58 of the 124 participants who reached the active period, and 50.6% of the waitlist arm gave no response against none in the intervention arm. The missing-data test was significantly related to arm, and the efficacy models rely on a missing-at-random assumption. The Discussion nonetheless calls the program feasible in terms of adherence, while the best/worst case range for waitlist adherence runs from 18% to 75%. The week-3 completion count behind the n=185 efficacy models is also not given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Prespecified feasibility thresholds met in the evaluable and bounded analyses, and a report of the numbers with week-3 outcome data per arm showing balanced completion.

quotes.text: 57 (46%) remained enrolled but had incomplete or entirely missing adherence data
Missing adherence data among enrolled participants was concentrated disproportionately in the waitlist arm
in terms of demand, adherence, and acceptability

second_reader.what_stands: Only 58/124 (47%) of the primary-outcome population had evaluable adherence. Missingness was strongly unequal (36% complete in waitlist vs 64% in intervention; 51% of waitlist had no response vs 0%). The adherence-feasibility claim in the Discussion rests on this, and the bounds range from 18% to 75% in the waitlist arm. The absence of a reported week-3 completion rate is confirmed only for the text, not for Figure 1.

issues.title: Randomized count given as 189 and 188; 557 assessed minus 369 excluded equals 188
issues.explanation: The Deviations section explains that 189 includes one participant excluded after randomization, so 188 is the working denominator. However, the Methods call the 188 'randomized participants', and the flow text subtracts 369 from 557 (giving 188) while stating 189 were randomized. The labels are used loosely but no analysis is affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The CONSORT figure showing 189 randomized, 1 post-randomization exclusion, 188 analysed.

quotes.text: This participant is included in the total randomized count (189)
Recruitment and retention numbers were based on all 188 randomized participants.

issues.title: Text reports 160 (85%) non-Hispanic White participants; Table 1 reports 155 (82.4%)
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 1 give different counts for the same demographic category. The table's race and ethnicity rows add to 188 using 155, so the text value is the one that does not fit. It is a descriptive slip with no effect on the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated definition under which 160 combines non-Hispanic White with another Table 1 category.

quotes.text: 160 (85%) were non-Hispanic and White
non-Hispanic White 155 (82.4)

issues.title: Discussion says no adherence-outcome association; Results report one (SSS-8 dose-response, P=.015)
issues.explanation: The Results report one significant dose-response association between practice frequency and somatic symptom burden, while the Discussion states that adherence was not significantly associated with change in any secondary outcome. The statement is overbroad. The analysis is exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity, so the practical effect is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Discussion wording restricted to binary adherence, or the appendix showing the SSS-8 gradient result is not significant.

quotes.text: Adherence status was not significantly associated with change in any secondary outcome
except for a significant dose-response association with somatic symptom burden

issues.title: Trial registered 6 days after first participant was enrolled
issues.explanation: Registration came after enrolment began, so the registered design cannot be confirmed as fixed before data collection. The gap is only 6 days and was disclosed, and the registered primary outcome matches the paper's adherence outcome in substance. The concern is limited to the formal inability to verify prospective specification.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Protocol or IRB documents dated before 15 September 2021 specifying the same outcomes.

quotes.text: on September 23, 2021, 6 days after enrollment of the first participant.

issues.title: Practice durations 3 + 4 + 15 = 22 minutes versus 'approximately 30 minutes' combined
issues.explanation: The component times total 22 minutes while the combined time is given as about 30. This may reflect transitions or rounding, and it cannot be settled from the text. It does not bear on any result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that transitions and instructions account for the extra time.

quotes.text: When completed together, practice time was approximately 30 minutes.

10.2196/preprints.89631.headline_claim: The 3-week web-based Breathing and Wellness program is feasible and improves mood, dyspnea and somatic symptoms compared with waitlist control, offering a low-risk, low-burden option for long COVID.
10.2196/preprints.89631.overall: The headline claim of feasibility and meaningful improvement in mood, dyspnea and somatic symptoms is only weakly supported. It rests on an unblinded waitlist comparison of self-reported outcomes, about 17 uncorrected secondary tests, and 64% attrition that was higher in the intervention arm and handled by a MAR assumption. The 'low-risk' claim has no adverse-event data, and the feasibility claim rests on completers only. The numeric slips (71% vs 67%, reversed baseline comparison, effect sizes) are minor, but the flow counts (81 implied vs 68 completers) are not fully reconcilable.

primary_outcome.name: Compliance (practice frequency against the paper's definition)

primary_outcomes.time_frame: For Phase 1 analysis: Baseline to 3 weeks. For Phase 2 analysis: Baseline to 6 weeks.

issues.title: Feasibility rests on 74% compliance among 68 completers; 50 of 188 randomized (27%) were compliant
issues.explanation: The primary outcome, compliance, is reported only for the 68 participants who completed the study. Because 120 of 188 randomized participants did not complete, the compliance rate among all randomized is much lower and unknown. The conclusion that the program is feasible and low-burden is stated without that qualification, and the paper itself attributes the high attrition to burden, brain fog and fatigue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Compliance data for all randomized participants (or all intervention-period participants) showing a high rate, or a feasibility threshold that is defined on completers.

quotes.text: Of the 68 participants that completed the study
This web-based, low-burden yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible

second_reader.what_stands: The 74% is a completers-only figure (50 of 68), and relative to everyone randomized the same 50 compliant participants are 27% (50 of 188). The Abstract and Discussion present the 74% as supporting feasibility without giving the full-randomized figure, and compliance was the registered primary outcome. The Limitations acknowledge high attrition but not that it bears on the feasibility claim, and the paper states no pre-specified feasibility threshold.

issues.title: Open-label, no-treatment waitlist control with self-reported outcomes underlies the headline efficacy claims
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation, the control received nothing during the comparison window, and every efficacy outcome is self-reported. Between-group differences in mood, dyspnea and somatic symptoms could therefore partly reflect expectancy, attention or reporting effects. The limitation appears only late in the Discussion, while the Abstract conclusion reads the differences as meaningful clinical improvements.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An active or attention-matched control, or objective outcome measures, showing the same differences.

quotes.text: Participants were not blinded to their study group
In three weeks, participants demonstrated meaningful improvements across validated clinical scales for

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy findings in the Abstract rest on an open-label comparison with a no-contact waitlist and on self-reported scales only, with no objective measure (the authors note no lung-function tests). The authors disclose this as a limitation, but the Abstract Conclusions state 'meaningful improvements' without that caveat.

issues.title: About 17 secondary outcome tests in Table 5 with no multiplicity control; headline p-values .003 to .04
issues.explanation: Table 5 tests the Week 3 group-by-time interaction on roughly 17 outcomes and subscales, and the Methods state no correction or hierarchy. Of the headline results, total mood (p = .02) and somatic burden (p = .02) would not survive a Bonferroni threshold of about .003. With so many tests, a few nominal p-values below .05 are expected by chance. The conclusion states the improvements as established without calling them exploratory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchical or corrected testing plan, or adjusted p-values that still fall below .05 for the headline outcomes.

quotes.text: multiple POMS domains, including total mood disturbance (MD = −10, p = .02, η² = .05)
In three weeks, participants demonstrated meaningful improvements across validated clinical scales for

second_reader.what_stands: Table 5 reports 17 secondary-outcome tests with no stated correction or alpha, and most significant results (p .01 to .04) would not survive a Bonferroni adjustment. Only fatigue (p = .001) clearly passes, and sensory dimension (p = .003) sits at the threshold. The Abstract headline p-values run .003 to .02, with .04 appearing in the Results text.

issues.title: About 64% attrition, higher in the intervention arm (55% vs 35%), handled only by a MAR assumption
issues.explanation: Only 68 of 188 randomized participants are reported as completers, and Week 3 losses were 53 of 96 in the intervention arm versus 32 of 92 in the control arm. The mixed-model estimates rest on the assumption that missingness is unrelated to unobserved outcomes, which is doubtful when more people leave the active arm. No sensitivity analysis for missing-not-at-random data is reported, so the size of the between-group differences is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pattern-mixture, tipping-point or multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses giving the same between-group effects, or evidence the dropouts were similar across arms on baseline and early outcomes.

quotes.text: 53 participants were lost to follow-up

second_reader.what_stands: The 55% vs 35% loss at week 3, which is the primary comparison point, is exactly what the paper's flow counts give, and about 64% matches 1 - 68/188. The flow counts alone give about 57%, which the paper does not reconcile. Handling of missing data rests on the MAR assumption in the mixed model plus post-hoc checks that cannot test for MNAR. The statement is slightly overstated in that the arm gap is mostly gone cumulatively by week 6 (58% vs 55%) and 'only MAR' leaves out those two checks.

issues.title: Pooled secondary model attributes uncontrolled change from baseline to the intervention
issues.explanation: The time coefficient in the second model is called change 'attributable to the intervention', but there is no comparator during the pooled period, so it also captures regression, time and expectancy. The Discussion uses this model as reinforcement of the randomized result, though it adds no independent causal information. The paper itself raises the time-effect concern but answers it only by citing literature.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of a concurrent control for the pooled period, or analyses showing stable untreated trajectories outside the intervention window.

quotes.text: The time coefficient reflects the adjusted mean change from baseline attributable to the intervention.
practices may offer meaningful symptom relief.

issues.title: Stated losses imply 81 at Week 6 versus 68 completers; Table 4 gives no per-timepoint n
issues.explanation: The paper reports 96 and 92 randomized, with 53 and 32 lost by Week 3 and 3 and 19 lost between Weeks 3 and 6. That leaves 43 and 60 at Week 3 and 81 at Week 6, not the 68 reported completers. The Table 4 columns are labelled with n=94 and n=91 for both Baseline and Week 3, though the Week 3 data can come from far fewer people. A reader cannot tell how many contributed each mean, or how completers were defined.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram or definition showing 68 completers is a stricter subset (for example, complete compliance logs) and a stated Week 3 n for Table 4.

quotes.text: 53 participants were lost to follow-up
Of the 68 participants that completed the study
Intervention (n=94)

script.explanation: The Participation cascade from Results does not reconcile: 'week 3 remaining' (n=103) minus its 2 stated exclusion(s) (85) leaves 18, but 'week 6 remaining' reports 81 -- 63 participant(s) unaccounted for by the paper's own arithmetic. 'week 6 remaining' (n=81) minus its 2 stated exclusion(s) (22) leaves 59, but 'completed the study' reports 68 -- 9 participant(s) unaccounted for by the paper's own arithmetic.

issues.title: 'Low-risk' and 'meaningful symptom relief' stated without adverse-event data or clinical-importance thresholds
issues.explanation: The paper reports no adverse-event monitoring or results, so 'low-risk' has no data behind it. 'Meaningful' improvement is asserted from statistical significance and eta-squared alone, without comparison to established minimal important differences. The study was sized for PSS, which showed no difference, so the significant secondary outcomes were not powered tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported safety monitoring with no or few adverse events, and effect sizes compared against validated minimal clinically important differences.

quotes.text: offer a low-risk, low-burden option for individuals with long COVID
the sample size was determined based on our key secondary outcome, the

issues.title: Results text says non-compliant had worse baseline mood/symptoms; Table 3 shows the compliant group worse
issues.explanation: The Results say non-compliant participants had worse baseline total mood disturbance, negative mood, dyspnea and somatic burden. Table 3 shows higher (worse) values in the compliant group on each of these, and the Discussion also says compliant participants had greater baseline symptom burden. The Results sentence is therefore reversed for mood, dyspnea and somatic symptoms. This is a wording error in a secondary descriptive comparison and does not touch the randomized efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that POMS or SSS-8 were reverse-scored in Table 3, or a corrected table showing higher baseline scores in the non-compliant group.

quotes.text: Non-compliant participants also had worse total mood disturbance,
quotes.location: Results, Quantitative Results, paragraph after Table 2
Table 3, POMS Total row, Compliant column
Table 3, POMS Total row, Noncompliant column

issues.title: Effect sizes in text differ from Table 5 (MCS12 0.001 vs 0.009; vigor .03 vs .04; immediate perception .06 vs .07)
issues.explanation: Several partial eta-squared values printed in the Results text do not match Table 5. The differences are small and none changes a significance conclusion, but they show the text and table were not reconciled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or text, or an explanation that the text values come from a different model specification.

issues.title: Text gives 71% of non-compliant participants from the waitlist group; Table 2 gives 12/18 = 67%
issues.explanation: The Results say 71% of non-compliant participants came from the waitlist group. Table 2 and the Figure 2 legend give 12 of 18, which is 67%. The mismatch is small and nothing else depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator defined in the text, for example 17 non-compliant participants with randomization data.

quotes.text: Non-compliant participants were primarily from the waitlist group (71%)

quotes.location: Table 2, Randomization, Waitlist row, Noncompliant column

script.explanation: 12/18 = 66.67%, but the paper prints 71, outside the rounding interval [70.50, 72.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 16.9 rather than 18.

10.22034/jchr.2022.690506.headline_claim: Acetaminophen combined with NSAIDs is the best and safe choice for COVID-19 headache, and phenytoin added to treatment achieves freedom from pain for a long-term period in refractory cases.
10.22034/jchr.2022.690506.overall: The headline conclusion that phenytoin improves and sustains headache control is not supported: allocation was non-randomised and open-label, no between-group analysis is reported, group sizes and percentages are internally inconsistent, and the tables partly contradict the text (no pain-free group B patients). The paper's data are too unreliable to conclude anything about phenytoin's efficacy or safety.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: No between-group statistical test; claimed phenytoin superiority and the 80% figure rest on descriptive percentages
issues.explanation: The paper reports no test, effect size or confidence interval comparing groups. The '80% good control' figure is not traceable to any table, and Table 3 shows all patients in both groups still at pain scores 6-10 post-treatment, with group B higher at 9-10 (28.86% and 15.54% vs 19.53% and 10.85%). The statement that group B had a better response is therefore unsupported by the data shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table or analysis showing the 80% figure and a significant between-group difference.

quotes.text: Both groups showed good response to treatment used on long term follow up although Group B record better response
good control of Headache was achieved (80%) when adding Phenytoin to treatment protocol

second_reader.what_stands: No between-group test is reported, and the stated 80% control in Group B and 'better response' than Group A rest on descriptive percentages, with the 80% not derivable from any table. By my rough check the 24-week difference is small and compatible with chance (p about 0.29), and the 8-week counts are identical.

issues.title: Conclusions assert 'best and safe' analgesics and phenytoin 'freedom of pain' long term without supporting data
issues.explanation: The conclusion calls acetaminophen with NSAIDs 'the best and safe choice' although no alternatives or safety data were compared. It also says phenytoin achieves 'freedom of pain' long term, yet Table 4 shows no pain-free group B patient and no between-group test exists. Safety is a single sentence, 'no significant side effects', with no adverse event counts.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Adverse event data and a controlled analysis showing sustained pain freedom with phenytoin.

quotes.text: In refractory cases, antiepileptic drugs like phenytoin are added to achieve freedom of pain and for a long-term period.
No significant side effects have been recorded from the use of Phenytoin in this short period of treatment

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions call acetaminophen with an NSAID the 'best and safe' choice and say phenytoin achieves long-term freedom of pain in refractory cases. The paper has no comparator that could show 'best', no reported adverse-event data (the cited Table 4 is a pain table), no long-term pain-free outcome in the phenytoin group, and no defined refractory subgroup.

issues.title: Non-randomised, unblinded half-split allocation; phenytoin benefit cannot be separated from group differences
issues.explanation: Patients were split into 'half' for groups A and B, with no randomisation, concealment, baseline comparison or blinding described. Group B also received 'one of these drugs or both' plus phenytoin, so the regimens differ beyond phenytoin. The headline claim of a phenytoin benefit rests on a confounded, open-label comparison with a subjective patient-reported outcome. Candidates c7 and c9 are folded into this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of random allocation with concealment, blinded outcome assessment, and balanced baseline characteristics.

quotes.text: to half of the patients as a part of their treatment regimen for relieving fever and other symptoms (group A)
another half (Group B) we use one of these drugs or both with Phenytoin orally

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes a prospective split of patients into two halves with no stated randomisation, concealment or blinding. Phenytoin dose was titrated to severity and response, and the background analgesics differ between arms. Baseline symptom burden differs somewhat (e.g. myalgia 38% vs 57%), so any between-group difference cannot be attributed to phenytoin alone. The paper does not explicitly say that allocation was non-random or open-label.

issues.title: Discussion claims more pain-free patients with phenytoin; Table 4 shows 0 in group B vs 5 in group A
issues.explanation: The Discussion says adding phenytoin left more patients free of pain. In the only table with pain-free patients (Table 4), group A has 5 at pain score 0 and group B has none. Table 3 shows no patient in either group at scores 0-5. The data do not support the stated advantage and run in the opposite direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Acute-phase pain-score data showing more pain-free group B patients.

quotes.text: in which more patients are free of pain during the acute stage
Group A n= 46 5 10.5%
quotes.location: Table 4, 0 pain scale, Group A row

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion says more patients are pain-free with phenytoin in the acute stage and afterwards. Table 3 shows nobody pain-free in either group, and Table 4 shows 5 pain-free in Group A versus 0 in Group B, which is the opposite direction. Group B does have more patients with low non-zero scores (73% vs 54% at 4 or below), but that is not the 'free of pain' claim and no test supports it.

issues.title: Group sizes inconsistent: A=91, B=92 in Table 2; A=46, B=45, C=92 in Tables 3-5; 'Group C' undefined
issues.explanation: Table 2 gives groups of 91 and 92 (total 183). Tables 3-5 give groups A=46, B=45 and a new group C=92, and the text never defines group C or explains the halving. Response percentages therefore cannot be tied to the treated groups, and it is unclear which arm is the comparator. This undermines every group comparison in the paper. Candidate c10 duplicates this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement defining groups A, B and C and explaining how 91 became 46+45.

quotes.text: Group An=91
Group A n= 46
Group C n= 92

second_reader.what_stands: Group sizes differ between Table 2 (91/92) and Tables 3-5 (46/45/92), and 'Group C' appears in the tables without being defined in the Methods or text. The numbers are partly reconcilable (46+45 = 91), but the paper does not say how, so it is unclear which patients received phenytoin in Tables 3-5.

issues.title: Table 3-5 percentages are systematically mis-scaled (e.g. 26/92 printed 28.08%, 5/46 printed 10.5%)
issues.explanation: Percentages across Tables 3-5 do not match counts over the stated n. 26/92 = 28.26% (printed 28.08%), and 5/46 = 10.87% (printed 10.5%). Group C values equal count x 1.08 and group B values equal count x 2.22, i.e. each group uses a fixed wrong denominator (about 92.6 and 45.05). Group A uses 47.6 (5 -> 10.5, i.e. x 2.1). Individual errors are small, but they show the percentages were not computed from the stated n. Candidate c6 duplicates this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alternative denominator (e.g. per-protocol set) for each group that reproduces the printed percentages.

quotes.text: Group A n= 46 5 10.5%

script.explanation: 26/92 = 28.26%, but the paper prints 28.08, outside the rounding interval [28.07, 28.09]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 92.6 rather than 92.

issues.title: Abstract and Methods say 63% women; Table 1 and Results give 233/500 = 46.6%
issues.explanation: The abstract and methods describe the cohort as 63% women, while Table 1 and the Results give 233 women out of 500 (46.6%). The two statements cannot both be right. The error is descriptive and does not change the treatment comparison, but it shows poor reporting care.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 63% refers to a different subgroup (for example, a subset of the 183 severe-headache patients).

quotes.text: This is a prospective study of 500 patients (63% women)
females comprise about 46.6% of total patients

issues.title: Results text says group B 'need more treatments' while Table 5 shows fewer (6 vs 10 at 24 weeks)
issues.explanation: The Results text says fewer group B patients complain of headache yet 'need more treatments'. Table 5 shows group B needing treatment less often than group A at 4, 12 and 24 weeks, and about equally at 8 weeks. The sentence contradicts the table or is a wording slip. The table still favours group B, so the effect is a text error that understates the claimed benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data on number of treatment courses per patient showing group B received more.

quotes.text: fewer patients complain from headache and need more treatments

10.22141/2224-0721.20.8.2024.1462.headline_claim: In post-COVID type 2 diabetes patients, adding SGLT2 inhibitors to metformin over 9 months lowered homocysteine and ST2 cardiovascular markers, unlike metformin/sulfonylurea therapy, supporting a positive cardiovascular-risk effect of SGLT2i.
10.22141/2224-0721.20.8.2024.1462.overall: The headline claim that SGLT2i improves cardiovascular risk markers relative to standard therapy is not well supported: allocation was retrospective and driven by cost and tolerability, no between-group test was done, and homocysteine fell equally in both arms. There are also text-table contradictions (ST2 direction, homocysteine normalisation) and a mis-ordered quartile cell.

primary_outcome.name: not stated (homocysteine and ST2 presented as co-primary markers)

issues.title: Non-randomized retrospective grouping by treatment uptake; comparator selected by cost and tolerability
issues.explanation: Patients were grouped by whether they started gliflozins, not by randomization. Group 2 comprised those who did not start for cost, fear of kidney damage or genitourinary effects, and baseline severity differed. Differences in marker change cannot be attributed to the drug.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomized or adjusted analysis showing comparable groups and a between-group effect.

quotes.text: розподіл на групи пацієнтів відбувся ретроспективно, оскільки всім пацієнтам, у яких була діагностована СН, призначалися препарати іНЗКТГ-2
не зробили цього з матеріальних причин (10 пацієнтів)

second_reader.what_stands: Group allocation was non-randomized and made retrospectively according to whether patients actually started an SGLT2 inhibitor. Cost (10 patients), fear of kidney damage (2) and tolerability after starting (2) explain 14 of the 18 comparators. The other 4 have no stated reason, and the comparator was not 'chosen' by the investigators as the point implies. Groups also differ at baseline in HF stage and hypertension grade, and no adjustment is described.

issues.title: Conclusion 'confirms' positive SGLT2i effect and cardioprotection from non-randomized surrogate marker changes
issues.explanation: The conclusions state that results confirm a positive SGLT2i effect and refer to cardioprotective effect, based on two lab markers in a retrospective comparison without clinical outcomes. Homocysteine fell equally in both arms, and the authors themselves attribute it to SGLT2i only by exclusion of folate.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Randomized or adjusted evidence with clinical outcomes.

quotes.text: Отримані результати підтверджують позитивний ефект прийому препаратів групи іНЗКТГ-2 на рівні маркерів серцево-судинного ризику
оцінки тривалості кардіопротекторного ефекту терапії іНЗКТГ-2

second_reader.what_stands: 'Confirm' and 'cardioprotective effect' overstate what non-randomized, unadjusted surrogate-marker changes in small groups can show. Homocysteine improved in both arms, and the ST2 differences are small and within the normal range. The wording about 'markers' and the Discussion's own call for further data soften this, but the abstract conclusion and the closing sentence still treat the SGLT2-inhibitor benefit as established.

issues.title: Group contrast claimed from separate within-group Wilcoxon tests; no between-group test of change
issues.explanation: The only inferential test is the within-group Wilcoxon before/after. The conclusion that SGLT2i is superior to metformin/sulfonylurea is drawn from one group significant and the other differently so, without testing the difference in change. Both groups also showed the same homocysteine fall, so no contrast exists there.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test of change (or ANCOVA) favouring SGLT2i.

quotes.text: Для оцінки різниці показників до і після лікування використали t-критерій Вілкоксона
у групі 1 - від 16,8 до 9,9; у групі 2 - від 14,4 до 10,1 мкмоль/л; р < 0,05

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that ST2 fell with SGLT2 inhibitors 'in contrast to' standard therapy rests on two separate within-group Wilcoxon tests. No between-group comparison of change, adjustment for baseline, or interaction test is reported. The homocysteine result is a within-group finding in both arms, so it does not itself claim a group contrast.

issues.title: Results text says ST2 fell in both T2DM groups; Table 2 shows group 2 ST2 rose 4.9 to 5.7
issues.explanation: The Results paragraph states a significant ST2 decrease in both diabetic groups. Table 2 and the Abstract show group 2 ST2 median increasing from 4.9 to 5.7 ng/ml (p < 0.05). The text is wrong or the table is, and the group 2 worsening is the key contrast with SGLT2i.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected text or erratum showing group 2 ST2 in fact fell.

quotes.text: вірогідне зниження рівня цього серцево-судинного біомаркера в обох групах пацієнтів з ЦД2
на відміну від групи 2, де рівень ST2 підвищився (від 4,9 до 5,7 нг/мл; р < 0,05)

issues.title: Text says homocysteine normalised in all patients; Table 1 group 2 post-treatment maximum is 18.5 (limit 12.0)
issues.explanation: The Results say that after 9 months homocysteine normalised in all examined patients. Table 1 gives a group 2 post-treatment maximum of 18.5 µmol/l, above the stated upper reference of 12.0. At least one patient was therefore not normalised.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing all group 2 values were at or below 12.0 and the 18.5 is a typo.

quotes.text: через 9 місяців після одужання у всіх обстежених пацієнтів концентрація ГЦ нормалізувалась
Maксимальне значення 28,2 11,9 29,2 18,5

issues.title: Table 1 group 2 post-treatment homocysteine Q1 (20.4) exceeds median (10.1) and Q3 (10.8)
issues.explanation: A first quartile cannot exceed the median or third quartile. The printed 20.4 duplicates the pre-treatment Q3 for the same group, suggesting a transcription error. The affected cell does not change the main conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing a Q1 value consistent with the ordering.

10.22141/2308-2097.58.2.2024.605.headline_claim: A Bacillus-based multi-strain probiotic added to standard care produced clinically significant improvement in post-COVID post-infectious IBS, with faster relief of abdominal pain and flatulence and reduced need for symptomatic medication.
10.22141/2308-2097.58.2.2024.605.overall: The direction of benefit (less bloating, pain and rescue-medication use with the probiotic) is plausible, but the paper does not support its confident efficacy and safety conclusions. The trial is small, open-label, without placebo, registration or named statistical tests, and relies on patient-rated scales. Several printing and wording errors (impossible percentages, an inverted English abstract, contradictory significance statements) reduce confidence further, though none reverses the direction of the findings.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; symptom severity on 10-point VAS (abdominal pain, motility disturbance, flatulence) and responder rates

issues.title: No blinding or placebo; efficacy rests on patient-rated 10-point VAS symptoms
issues.explanation: The control arm received basic therapy only, and blinding is never mentioned. The symptom outcomes (pain, motility, bloating) are self-rated on a VAS and are prone to expectation effects when patients know they receive an extra product. The large 4-week differences, for example pain 1.4 vs 5.1, may be partly due to this. The conclusions do not mention the limitation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that patients and outcome assessors were blinded, or a placebo in the control arm.

quotes.text: 21 пацієнт першої групи (група порівняння) отримував базову терапію
оцінювали за візуальною аналоговою 10-бальною шкалою

second_reader.what_stands: Stands: the trial is open-label with an add-on versus no-add-on comparator, no placebo and no stated blinding, and the main symptom outcomes are 10-point VAS scores plus the IBS-SSS questionnaire, which are subjective. Not fully accurate: the paper does not explicitly say the VAS is patient-rated, and it also reports fecal calprotectin and ultrasound flatulence, so efficacy does not rest solely on the VAS.

issues.title: Confident efficacy and tolerability claims from 42 open-label patients, no power calculation
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the study confirmed high clinical efficacy and that the absence of side effects confirms good tolerability. The trial has 21 patients per arm, no sample-size justification, no blinding and no stated primary outcome. Zero adverse events in 21 patients cannot rule out adverse effects that occur in even 10% of patients. The conclusions are too strong for the design; the direction of effect may well be real but its size is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation and a blinded design, or a more cautious conclusion that acknowledges these limits.

quotes.text: Проведене нами дослідження теж підтвердило високу клінічну ефективність пробіотичного засобу в лікуванні таких пацієнтів.
Цей факт підтверджує також його добра переносимість при застосуванні і відсутність побічних ефектів у проведеному нами дослідженні.

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion makes unqualified claims of high efficacy and good tolerability from 42 patients (21 per arm) in a trial with no described blinding or placebo and no sample size or power calculation, and it includes no limitations discussion. With 0 adverse events in 21 treated patients, the data are compatible with an adverse-event rate up to about 14%, so the safety claim is weakly supported.

issues.title: Table 3: 8.6% of n = 21 is not attainable; Table 2 also prints 9.6% for 2/21
issues.explanation: With 21 patients per group, a share can only be 4.8% (1 patient) or 9.5% (2 patients), so 8.6% is impossible. The same value is printed at both 4 weeks and 1 month. Table 2 shows the same pattern, with 9.6% printed for what should be 2/21 = 9.5%. These are reporting errors on single cells. The direction of the ultrasound result is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the ultrasound denominator was not 21 in group 2 (for example missing scans), or a corrected table.

quotes.text: Виражений метеоризм на УЗД, %

issues.title: No named tests; responder p-values not shown; dispersions fall from SD ~2 to 0.1-0.5
issues.explanation: The statistics are described only as 'variational statistics' in Excel, with no test names. The Conclusions claim significantly more partial and complete responders (p < 0.05), but Table 2 shows no p-values for the responder rows and the Results say the 2-week complete-responder rate did not differ. Table 1 dispersions fall from about 2 at baseline to 0.1-0.5 after treatment (for example pain 1.3 ± 0.1), which looks like an SE rather than an SD. The reported significance cannot be verified from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of the tests used and that the dispersions are SDs, plus the between-group responder test results.

quotes.text: Статистична обробка результатів досліджень здійснювалася методами варіаційної статистики за допомогою прикладних програм Excel Microsoft Office for Windows.

issues.title: No trial registration or protocol reported for a randomised interventional study
issues.explanation: The paper describes a randomised trial but gives no registry number or protocol reference. Readers cannot check the planned primary outcome against what is reported. The paper reports many outcomes, and this makes selective emphasis harder to exclude.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry identifier or a published protocol.

quotes.text: Проведено просте рандомізоване клінічне дослідження з вивчення ефективності й безпеки застосування пробіотичного засобу

issues.title: Results text says 4-week change significant 'in both groups', then says control changes never were
issues.explanation: One Results sentence claims a significant difference for all symptoms in both groups at 4 weeks. The following sentences and Table 1 show only the probiotic group changed significantly. The two statements cannot both be right, but the abstract and tables show which was intended. This is a wording inconsistency, not a changed result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that 'both groups' referred to the between-group comparison across the two arms.

quotes.text: Через 4 тижні лікування виявлено клінічно значущу різницю щодо вираженості всіх досліджуваних симптомів в обох групах пацієнтів (р < 0,05)
зміни не були вірогідними щодо жодного досліджуваного симптому (р > 0,05)

issues.title: Conclusion lists abdominal pain as significantly faster without noting it was not significant at 2 weeks
issues.explanation: The Results state that at 2 weeks only bloating differed significantly between groups. The Conclusions list abdominal pain and normalised motility as significantly faster, without giving a timepoint. At 4 weeks the pain difference is significant, so the claim holds there, but the 'faster' wording overstates the early picture.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An explicit statement in the Conclusions that 'faster' refers to the 4-week comparison.

quotes.text: хоча ці зміни були вірогідними тільки щодо метеоризму (р < 0,05), але не щодо болю в животі й кишкової моторики (р > 0,05)
Використання пробіотичного засобу на основі бактерій роду Bacillus сприяло вірогідно швидшому зникненню таких симптомів постінфекційного СПК, як абдомінальний біль, метеоризм

issues.title: English abstract says days 'not needing' antispasmodics fell (3.1 vs 6.7); source measures days needing them
issues.explanation: The Ukrainian text and Table 2 count days per week on which patients needed rescue medication. This was lower in the probiotic group (3.1 vs 6.7). The English abstract says days without need decreased, which would imply the opposite. Readers of the English version get the wrong meaning for this outcome, but the data themselves are consistent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing in the paper; the discrepancy is textual.

quotes.text: the number of days per week during which patients did not need to take antispasmodics
шилася кількість днів на тиждень, протягом яких хворі мали потребу в прийомі спазмолітиків

issues.title: Multiple symptoms, timepoints and biomarkers tested at p < 0.05 without correction
issues.explanation: Three symptoms at three timepoints, responder rates, medication days, calprotectin and ultrasound are each tested with no correction or primary endpoint. The results are largely consistent in direction, so a correction would probably change little. This is mainly a caveat for the secondary and early-timepoint findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary endpoint or multiplicity plan.

quotes.text: Статистична обробка результатів досліджень здійснювалася методами варіаційної статистики за допомогою прикладних програм Excel Microsoft Office for Windows.

issues.title: Randomisation described only as 'computer method'; no sequence generation or concealment details
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were randomised by a computer method into two groups of 21. It gives no sequence-generation detail, allocation concealment or baseline comparison table. The equal arm sizes and similar baselines are compatible with proper randomisation. The gap matters mainly because the trial is also unblinded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description of concealed allocation.

quotes.text: Усі хворі були рандомізовані за допомогою комп'ютерного методу на 2 групи.

10.22416/1382-4376-2022-32-6-47-52.headline_claim: Adding Kolofort (antibodies to S-100, TNF-alpha and histamine) to omeprazole improves symptoms and quality of life in post-COVID-19 patients with functional dyspepsia.
10.22416/1382-4376-2022-32-6-47-52.overall: The pain advantage of adding Kolofort at day 28 is plausible but rests on a small open-label comparison with self-reported outcomes, no multiplicity control, and baseline p-values that contradict both the text and the printed means. The claims of durability and quality-of-life improvement go beyond a 4-week, unblinded study, and the headline conclusion should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Change in dyspepsia symptoms (epigastric pain VAS at day 28; primary endpoint stated as change in symptom severity)

issues.title: Patient-reported VAS and SF-36 outcomes in an apparently open add-on design with no placebo or blinding
issues.explanation: The control arm gets omeprazole alone and the intervention arm gets omeprazole plus Kolofort, with no placebo or blinding described. The primary outcome and the quality-of-life outcomes are patient-rated, so expectation effects can inflate the day-28 difference. The conclusion of efficacy therefore rests on a design that cannot separate drug effect from expectation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or methods statement showing placebo-matched or assessor-blinded delivery.

quotes.text: Первичная конечная точка исследования - изменение выраженности симптомов диспепсии.
для оценки клинических проявлений использовали 10-балльную шкалу ВАШ

second_reader.what_stands: The design is an add-on comparison (PPI vs PPI + Kolofort) with no placebo and no stated blinding, and every outcome is patient-reported (VAS, SF-36). The paper does not state whether it was open-label, so that part is an inference, and the paper does not list the lack of blinding as a limitation.

issues.title: Conclusion claims 'durable' relief and QoL gain; resolution equal at ~90% and follow-up ended at day 28
issues.explanation: The Results say that by day 28 up to 90% of patients in both arms had full resolution and the between-arm difference disappeared. The Conclusion nevertheless claims faster and more durable relief of pain. Follow-up stopped at the end of 4 weeks of treatment, so durability was not assessed; the pain difference rests on one open-label comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Post-treatment follow-up data showing a sustained between-group difference.

quotes.text: Полное купирование диспепсического синдрома в обеих группах составляло до 90 % пациентов без значимых отличий ( р < 0,06).
способствуя более быстрому и стойкому купированию болевого синдрома

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion's claim of 'стойкому' (durable) relief is not supported, because follow-up ended at day 28, the last day of treatment, and no post-treatment data are shown. Resolution was also about equal in both groups (~90%, not significantly different), so the advantage is in speed of improvement and in day-28 scores, not in final resolution. The quality-of-life gain is supported only at one end-of-treatment time point.

issues.title: Table 1 baseline p-values (0.012, 0.010, 0.001, 0.001) contradict the text and the printed means
issues.explanation: The Results say there was no significant difference in age, sex or baseline symptoms, but Table 1 prints p = 0.012 for age, 0.010 for sex and 0.001 for both VAS rows. The printed means and SDs imply much larger p-values (age about 0.14, pain VAS about 0.33). Either the p-values are wrong, or the arms were imbalanced at baseline, which would confound the between-arm comparison in a 21-per-arm trial. The same defect covers the screen's baseline-imbalance candidate (c3).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the p column is something other than a between-arm test, or corrected p-values consistent with the printed means and SDs.

quotes.text: Не было зарегистрировано значимой разницы в возрастно-половом составе и первоначальной выраженности симптомов диспепсии у всех участников
Выраженность боли в эпигастрии по ВАШ

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

issues.title: 42 patients, no sample-size calculation, no effect sizes or CIs, yet a confident efficacy conclusion
issues.explanation: Only means, SDs and bound p-values are reported for a trial of 21 patients per arm. No sample-size justification is given, and the Conclusion states that the study demonstrated efficacy. Combined with the lack of blinding and the unclear baseline balance, the estimate of benefit is imprecise and should be read as tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation or protocol supporting n = 42.

quotes.text: В параллельные группы были включены 42 амбулаторных пациента
Проведенное исследование продемонстрировало эффективность включения препарата Колофорт®

issues.title: Many uncorrected t-tests (4 VAS time points, 8 SF-36 scales) with unspecified pairing; 'p < 0.06' used as a threshold
issues.explanation: Student's t-tests are the only analysis described, and they were applied to several time points and eight SF-36 scales without multiplicity control or a covariate adjustment. Because baseline is reported as imbalanced, an unadjusted comparison at day 28 is vulnerable. Significance on secondary scales should be read cautiously.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of paired/unpaired tests with a pre-specified single primary time point, or a correction for multiple outcomes.

quotes.text: Статистическая значимость  оценивалась  с  помощью  критериев Стьюдента.
Критерием  значимости  было  принято значение р < 0,05.

issues.title: Company support declared, but no statement of the funder's role in design, analysis or reporting
issues.explanation: The only disclosure is a one-line note that the publication was supported by a company. No statement says who designed the trial, analysed the data or wrote the report. Together with the unblinded design this lowers confidence in the favourable conclusion, but the disclosure itself is present.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A funding statement describing an independent design, analysis and reporting process.

quotes.text: Конфликт интересов: публикация выполнена при поддержке «Материа Медика».

issues.title: Table 2: VT and SE between-group differences (8 and 4 points) lack ** while smaller-looking ones carry it
issues.explanation: Vitality at day 28 is 59,0 ± 5,5 versus 51,0 ± 5,5, which a t-test on n = 21 per arm puts near t = 4.7, yet the ** between-group mark is missing. Social functioning (61,0 vs 57,0) gives about t = 2.4, also unmarked. The table therefore understates the extent of between-group differences, and the star pattern does not match the printed means.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that between-group tests were run only on selected scales, or corrected table marks.

quotes.text: Различия достоверны, р < 0,05: * - до и после лечения; ** - между двумя группами сравнения.

issues.title: Table 2: group 1 baseline GH and VT both printed as 37,0 ± 5,4
issues.explanation: Baseline General Health and Vitality in group 1 have identical mean and SD. Given the coarse rounding of the table this may be coincidence, or a duplicated cell. No conclusion rests on these two baseline cells.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing both scales truly have mean 37.0 and SD 5.4.

quotes.location: Table 2, GH and VT rows, group 1 before treatment

10.22540/jmni-26-242.headline_claim: Adding sensory re-education to traditional physiotherapy significantly improves quality of life and proprioception in post-COVID-19 polyneuropathy but does not significantly affect tactile sensation.
10.22540/jmni-26-242.overall: The primary QoL result (post-treatment 75.77 vs 63.61, p = 0.001) is arithmetically consistent, but the trial is small, open-label, single-centre and short, with a self-reported primary outcome. The proprioception claims are exploratory, uncorrected, and partly argued from within-group changes seen in both arms. The registration dates also appear to conflict with the stated study period. The conclusion should be read as preliminary.

primary_outcome.name: Quality of life (Arabic WHOQOL-BREF)

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-reported primary outcome and unblinded assessors; registry lists masking as DOUBLE
issues.explanation: Participants and assessors knew the allocation, and the primary outcome (WHOQOL-BREF) is self-reported, so expectation effects could inflate the 12.16-point between-group difference. The paper itself says assessor unblinding could have biased the sensory and proprioception results. The registry record lists masking as DOUBLE, which is inconsistent with the paper. The headline conclusion does not carry this caveat.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of blinded assessment or an attention-matched sham control for the self-reported outcome, and a corrected registry masking description.

quotes.text: outcome assessors were not blinded to group allocation, which could have introduced detection bias

issues.title: Abstract advises adopting the paradigm in protocols based on 40 patients, 6 weeks, one centre, unblinded
issues.explanation: The Abstract states the findings support incorporating sensory re-education into rehabilitation protocols. The evidence is one single-centre trial of 40 patients with six weeks of treatment, no follow-up and unblinded assessment. The main-text Conclusion does add a call for larger confirmatory studies, but the Abstract does not.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; this depends on the reader's threshold for a practice recommendation.

quotes.text: These findings support incorporating sensory re-education into rehabilitation protocols to enhance functional outcomes in this population.
Larger studies with increased sample sizes are encouraged to confirm these findings.

issues.title: Proprioception 'efficacy verified' from uncorrected exploratory tests; within-group changes cited, one p = 0.047
issues.explanation: The Methods state that no multiplicity adjustment was applied and that the sensory secondary outcomes are exploratory. The Discussion nonetheless says the findings 'verified the efficacy' of sensory re-education for proprioception, citing significant pre-post changes in both groups, which do not show an added benefit. The Conclusion states the paradigm is beneficial for proprioceptive sense. The between-group evidence is four uncorrected tests, one of them barely significant at p = 0.047, plus eight SWM tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchical testing plan or multiplicity-adjusted p-values for which the proprioception between-group differences remain significant.

quotes.text: No formal adjustment for multiple comparisons was applied; therefore, analyses of secondary sensory outcomes should be interpreted as exploratory.
These findings verified the efficacy of sensory re-education in enhancing the proprioceptive sense of the wrist joint

issues.title: Paper dates the study from Nov 2022, but registry shows first submission June 2023 and start June 2023
issues.explanation: The paper states the study began in November 2022 and describes the trial as registered under NCT05911113. The registry record gives a first submission of 17 June 2023 and a start of 26 June 2023. If recruitment began in November 2022, registration was not prospective for the earliest participants, and the paper does not explain the date difference.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing registration before the first enrolment, or an explanation that the stated dates include non-trial activity.

quotes.text: The study was carried out from November 2022 to August 2023

issues.title: Pre-treatment LP-ART effect sizes described as 0.01-0.05, but Table 4 prints 0.08 (Medium) for left extension
issues.explanation: The Results say all pre-treatment LP-ART effect sizes were very small to small (about 0.01-0.05), which the authors take as good baseline comparability. Table 4 prints 0.08 and labels it Medium for the left wrist extension pre-treatment comparison. Group A had a lower (better) baseline error there (median 9.6 vs 12.8), so baseline comparability is slightly overstated for that measure.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 4 or erratum showing the left extension pre-treatment eta-squared is within 0.01-0.05.

quotes.text: ≈ 0.01–0.05), indicating good baseline comparability between groups
quotes.location: Results, LP-ART flexion paragraph on pre-treatment effect sizes

issues.title: Post-hoc power of 96% from observed d = 1.21 is read as only a 4% chance of a false negative
issues.explanation: Power computed from the observed effect size of the same data restates the p-value and does not show how likely a false negative is. The claim that this leaves only a 4% chance of a Type II error is a misinterpretation. The a priori calculation used an assumed d of 0.910 with 20 per arm.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; this is a statistical interpretation point.

quotes.text: This very high achieved power means that there is only a 4% chance of a false negative (Type II error).

10.22605/rrh8757.headline_claim: Both videoconferencing-guided synchronous and mobile-app-guided asynchronous telerehabilitation give long-term gains in clinical and hemodynamic parameters in discharged COVID-19 patients, with videoconferencing slightly better.
10.22605/rrh8757.overall: The finding that oxygen saturation improved more with videoconferencing is weak: it is confined to one outcome, uncorrected for multiplicity, and confounded by a significant baseline imbalance with no adjusted analysis. The claim that both programmes 'proved' beneficial rests on within-arm change without an untreated control, and the safety and cost claims go beyond the data. The study is best read as a small exploratory comparison.

primary_outcome.name: Oxygen saturation at rest and after exertion (between-group comparison); no single primary outcome designated

issues.title: 'Proved' positive effects of both programmes rests on within-arm change with no untreated control
issues.explanation: Both arms received an active programme and there is no no-treatment or usual-care group. Improvements from baseline to 8 months in post-COVID patients can reflect spontaneous recovery, so the pre-post changes cannot show that either programme caused them. The Conclusion nonetheless says the study 'proved' positive effects.
