The ISI error overstates the improvement by about 9 percentage points, but the direction of the effect and its significance are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing that the median of individual percentage changes is 81.3% for ISI and 17.1% for MoCa, with a stated method of calculating Δ that differs from change in medians.

quotes.location: Table 3, ISI AFS row, index before treatment

issues.title: Discussion gives IL6 between-group difference as 36.5%; abstract and Table 2 give 36.1%
issues.explanation: The IL6 difference between groups at day 30 is 36.1% in the abstract, Results and Table 2, and the printed medians confirm this (3.9 vs 6.1). The Discussion says IL6 was lower 'by 36.5%' than in the comparison group, which is actually the comparison group's own within-group change (Δ 5-4). The mistake is confined to one sentence and does not change the result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: No refutation expected; a corrected Discussion sentence would resolve it.

quotes.location: Discussion, paragraph on cytokine levels, IL6 sentence

issues.title: Index-group BMI 25th percentile is 18.3, below the inclusion floor of 18.5 kg/m²
issues.explanation: Eligibility required a BMI of 18.5–24.9 and excluded BMI below 18.5. If the index group's first quartile is 18.3, at least a quarter of that group (about 17 patients) had a BMI below the floor. Either the value is misprinted or eligibility was not applied as written. This is a minor inconsistency with no obvious bearing on the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that BMI was re-measured after enrolment, or a corrected Table 1 value of at least 18.5.

quotes.text: index 18.5-24.9 kg/m 2

quotes.location: Table 1, Body mass index row, index group

issues.title: Text says all mental-status changes were significant (p<0.05); comparison-group MoCa change has p = 0.072
issues.explanation: The Results state that after therapy the changes in mental-status parameters were significant at p < 0.05. Table 3 reports a non-significant comparison-group MoCa change (p = 0.072). The blanket statement is therefore not accurate for cognition in the comparison arm. It matters little, but it suggests the text was not checked against the table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the sentence refers only to between-group differences, with a table showing all of them below 0.05.

quotes.text: the changes were significant ( р < 0.05) and more pronounced in the index group
quotes.location: Results, paragraph on mental status parameters
Table 3, MoCa AFS row, comparison group

10.2478/sjph-2024-0017.headline_claim: Pulmonary rehabilitation has clinically significant effects on functional capacity and respiratory muscle strength in patients with post-COVID syndrome.
10.2478/sjph-2024-0017.overall: The paper shows that lung function, walking distance and respiratory muscle pressures were higher after three weeks of rehabilitation among 80 patients who completed the programme. It cannot show that the programme caused the gains: there is no control group, drop-outs are excluded, and the Discussion claims a comparison with non-participants that was not done. There are also several reporting slips (the 6.3% vs 16.3% figure, unsigned differences in Table 3, and unverifiable Table 2 P values), but the main flaw is the design.

primary_outcome.name: Respiratory muscle strength (PImax)

issues.title: Uncontrolled before-after study (n=80) used to claim clinically significant programme effects
issues.explanation: All 80 patients received rehabilitation and were measured at baseline and after three weeks, with no comparison group and no blinded assessment. Improvements in spirometry, walking distance and respiratory muscle pressure may reflect spontaneous recovery from COVID-19, test familiarity or regression to the mean. The authors concede that improvement could be 'attributable to the natural course of the disease', yet still conclude that the programme has clinically significant effects. The data show change, not an effect of the programme.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Inclusion of a contemporaneous non-rehabilitation control group, or natural-history data on the same measures over the same interval.

quotes.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted using hospital data on patients who participated in a pulmonary rehabilitation programme
the use of the PR programme has been shown to have numerous positive effects, with sufficient supporting evidence.
whether clinical improvement in post-COVID syndrome is attributable to the natural course of the disease, or if PR is crucial

second_reader.what_stands: The study is an uncontrolled before-after analysis of 80 completers, so it cannot separate the effect of PR from natural recovery, and the Abstract, Conclusion and Discussion ('clinically significant', 'sufficient supporting evidence') are stronger than that design supports. It is not fully accurate to say the limitation is ignored, since Section 4.1 acknowledges that natural course versus PR is unresolved, and the 'cross-sectional' label misdescribes the design.

issues.title: Discussion claims participants recovered better and faster than non-participants; no such group was studied
issues.explanation: The Discussion says that in this study patients who took part in PR recovered better and faster than those who did not. Every patient in the study took part and completed PR, so no comparison with non-participants exists. Statements about faster recovery and about improvement relative to ICU-only patients are likewise not tested. This reads as a comparative efficacy finding that the data cannot give.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An analysis in the paper comparing participants with a non-participating group.

quotes.text: In this study the COVID-19 patients who took part in the PR programme recovered better and faster than those who did not participate in it.
had participated in and fully completed the PR programme at the Clinic for Lung Diseases

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion statement that participants recovered better and faster than non-participants has no basis in the study's data, because no non-participant group was studied and balance and psychosocial outcomes were not measured. The comparison appears to come from the literature rather than from this study, but it is written as a finding of this study.

issues.title: Discussion gives 6.3% with PEmax <80% after PR; Table 2 and Results give 16.3% (13/80)
issues.explanation: The Discussion says 6.3% of patients still had PEmax below 80% of predicted at the last measurement. Table 2 and the Results give 13 of 80, which is 16.3%. The Discussion figure is about 10 percentage points too low, so the apparent normalisation of PEmax (35% to 6.3%) is exaggerated. The tables and Results are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the Discussion figure refers to a different threshold or subgroup of patients.

quotes.text: For PEmax, pathological values were found in 35% of patients at the first measurement and in 6.3% of them at the last measurement.

quotes.location: Table 2, PE max <80% row, After PR

script.explanation: 13/80 = 16.25%, but the paper prints 6.3, outside the rounding interval [6.25, 6.40]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 206.3 rather than 80.

issues.title: Only programme completers analysed; drop-outs and number screened not reported
issues.explanation: Eligibility required full completion of the programme, so any patient who stopped early is absent from the data. Completers are likely to be those who tolerated and benefited from rehabilitation, which can inflate average gains. The paper gives no count of patients who started but did not finish, so the size of this selection cannot be judged. This weakens the generalisability of the headline effect, but the effect is probably modest relative to the lack of a control.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Records showing that almost all starters completed the programme.

quotes.text: had participated in and fully completed the PR programme at the Clinic for Lung Diseases

issues.title: About 17 outcomes tested at P<0.05 with no correction; DLCO and SpO2 gains are marginal
issues.explanation: Table 3 reports 17 paired comparisons, each judged at P<0.05, with no primary outcome stated and no multiplicity adjustment. The main respiratory-muscle and 6MWT findings are strong enough to survive correction. The DLCO (P=0.007, 0.011) and post-walk SpO2 (P=0.036) improvements are not, though the conclusion lists DLCO as improved. The effect on the headline is limited.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or hierarchical testing plan covering DLCO and SpO2.

quotes.text: P<0.05 was considered significant.
the parameters of lung function, FVC, FEV1, and DLCO also improved significantly after PR (P<0.05)

issues.title: Table 2 chi-square P values do not match the counts and ignore that before/after data are paired
issues.explanation: The Methods say proportions were compared with a chi-square test, which assumes independent groups, but the same 80 patients are counted before and after PR. Treating the counts as independent gives P of about 0.009 for PImax <80% (57 vs 41 of 80) and about 0.007 for PEmax <80% (28 vs 13), whereas the table prints <0.001. For 6MWT (44 vs 17) the same calculation gives P<0.001 while the table prints 0.007. The P values may be swapped or may come from a paired test, so a reader cannot verify them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that McNemar's test was used, with the discordant-pair counts supporting the printed P values.

quotes.text: The comparison of proportions was assessed with a chi-square test.

issues.title: Table 3 mean-difference signs inconsistent with CIs; heart-rate CI does not bracket -32.22
issues.explanation: In the PImax, PImax%, PEmax and PEmax% rows, a positive mean difference sits beside an all-negative CI. The CIs are centred on the negated difference, so the sign convention is simply inconsistent across rows. The heart-rate row is more anomalous: the CI is garbled and its midpoint is about -34.2, not -32.22. Other rows also do not match the means (FVC 4.33-4.14 = 0.19 versus 0.14 printed). The effect is a presentation problem and does not change the direction of any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table note stating the difference is baseline minus after-PR and that the heart-rate CI is mis-typeset.

10.24884/1682-6655-2021-20-4-101-105.headline_claim: In post-COVID-19 cardiovascular patients, high-frequency Doppler shows capillary stasis and shunt flow consistent with microthrombosis, and microcirculation improved after sulodexide therapy.
10.24884/1682-6655-2021-20-4-101-105.overall: The headline claim that sulodexide improved microcirculation and normalised the coagulogram rests on an uncontrolled before/after comparison with no sample sizes per analysis, no quantitative Doppler outcome and visual interpretation of example tracings. The coagulogram text and table are not consistent with each other, so the reported normalisation is only tentatively supported.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly named; microcirculatory Doppler spectral/shape characteristics (nail bed, 25 MHz) before and after sulodexide

issues.title: Sulodexide benefit claimed from uncontrolled before/after change over 4 weeks in 49 post-COVID patients
issues.explanation: All patients appear to have received sulodexide and were re-examined after 4 weeks, with no concurrent untreated comparison group. Improvement in Doppler spectra and coagulogram values one to two months after COVID-19 may reflect natural recovery. Also, the table gives no n, only M±m, and no per-group results, and the conclusion nonetheless states that microcirculation improved after sulodexide. The causal attribution to sulodexide is not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated post-COVID control group followed for the same 4 weeks showing no comparable improvement.

quotes.text: Показатели микроциркуляции у больных, перенесших COVID-19, улучшились после курса профилактической терапии Сулодексидом.

second_reader.what_stands: The claim of sulodexide benefit rests on an uncontrolled before/after comparison of the 49 post-COVID patients over 4 weeks, with no group left without sulodexide. Improvement cannot be attributed to the drug rather than natural recovery, prior or concurrent anticoagulant effects, or regression to the mean, and the Conclusion does not acknowledge this.

issues.title: Microcirculation outcome is visual Doppler curve/spectrum reading, with no scoring, blinding or validation
issues.explanation: Doppler tracings were analysed 'by shape and spectrum', and conclusions about stasis, shunt flow and microthrombosis and later 'normalisation' rest on visual impressions of a few example tracings. No quantitative index, reader blinding, reproducibility or comparison with a reference standard is given, and the healthy comparison is a figure from a 2002 publication. The microthrombosis interpretation is not demonstrated by the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A validated, blinded quantitative scoring method with reproducibility data linking spectrum features to microthrombosis.

quotes.text: Анализ  допплерограмм  выполняли  по  форме  и спектру кривых.
Выявленные изменения в совокупности с изменениями в системе гемокоагуляции, подтверж -денными данными коагулограммы, клинически со -ответствуют микротормбозу.

second_reader.what_stands: The microcirculation outcome is a visual, qualitative reading of Doppler curve shape and spectrum, shown only through example images, with no scoring system, blinding of the reader or validation against another measure described. The microthrombosis interpretation is supported only by the paper's inference from the spectral appearance plus coagulation markers, not by a validated imaging criterion.

issues.title: Fibrinogen called normal before and after treatment, yet table shows 4.74 to 2.73 g/L with p<0.05
issues.explanation: The text says fibrinogen was within reference values both before and after treatment, and the abstract says the remaining coagulogram parameters were normal. The table lists fibrinogen among parameters with a significant pre/post change (4.74 to 2.73 g/L, p<0.05). Either the text description or the table row is inaccurate, and the reference range is not given, so which cannot be settled. Coagulogram 'normalisation' is therefore not described consistently.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated fibrinogen reference range (e.g., 2-4.5 g/L or wider) showing both values are within it, and a statement that the table is a descriptive comparison rather than a claim of abnormality.

issues.title: Antithrombin III described as 1.5x above normal, but table shows 112.55% before treatment
issues.explanation: The text says antithrombin III was 1.5 times above normal before treatment, but the table gives 112.55% before and 99.56% after. Activity of 112.55% is only about 1.1 times a typical normal of about 100%. The size of the described abnormality is not matched by the table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A laboratory reference range for ATIII under which 112.55% equals 1.5 times the normal value.

quotes.text: антитромбин III был в 1,5 раза выше нормы (таблица)
Антитромбин III, %112,55±0,54

issues.title: Citation [12] (version 9) given for statement about version 10 of recommendations, which is ref. [13]
issues.explanation: The Methods sentence attributes the addition of DOACs to the 10th version but cites reference 12, which is listed as version 9. Version 10 is reference 13. Nothing in the results depends on this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Version 9 itself containing the DOAC prophylaxis addition.

quotes.text: только  в  10-ю  версию  реко -мендаций

10.24884/1682-6655-2024-23-2-38-43.headline_claim: COVID-19 accelerates progression of isolated horizontal venous reflux, and early surgical correction of this reflux is clearly superior to conservative treatment for achieving good cosmetic and clinical results.
10.24884/1682-6655-2024-23-2-38-43.overall: The headline claims, that COVID-19 accelerates reflux progression and that surgery 'undoubtedly' beats conservative care, are not supported: there is no unexposed comparison and the surgical comparison is non-randomised, with self-selected controls and small strata. Most apparent sample-size discrepancies are explained by CEAP-class stratification, but the overall sex totals do not match the group splits and the statistical methods (Fisher's exact test for VCSS scores, undefined p-values) are inadequate for the claims made.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: Surgery vs conservative care compared in self-selected, non-randomised groups; 'undoubted' superiority claimed
issues.explanation: Group II consists of patients who declined surgery, so choice of treatment may relate to prognosis, age, comorbidity or severity. The groups differ in CEAP class mix and no adjustment is made. The study is open-label, with no sample size justification, no blinding of VCSS assessment and no adverse events reported. With 4-11 patients per analysed stratum, the conclusion that surgery 'undoubtedly' surpasses conservative therapy is not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline comparability data across arms, an adjusted analysis, or a randomised or matched design.

quotes.text: которые отказались от оперативного лечения и получали традиционное консервативное лечение
имеет несомненное преимущество пред

second_reader.what_stands: The comparison is between self-selected, non-randomised groups (surgery vs patients who declined surgery), with unequal baseline severity and no adjustment, yet the abstract and Conclusions claim an 'undoubted' superiority of surgery. That wording is not supported by this design, because patient choice could be linked to prognosis.

issues.title: Fisher's exact test stated for VCSS scores; comparisons behind p-values undefined, strata of 4-11 patients
issues.explanation: Methods say significance was assessed with Fisher's exact test, which does not apply to mean VCSS scores. The tables give M±m and a single p per arm without saying whether it is a before/after or between-arm comparison. No test of arm difference or interaction is given, even though the conclusions are about group I vs group II. Many comparisons are made across CEAP classes and symptoms with no multiplicity handling.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of the actual tests used for VCSS, with between-group comparisons and their p-values.

quotes.text: Достоверность различий определяли с помощью точного критерия Фишера.
quotes.location: Материал и методы исследования, statistics paragraph

second_reader.what_stands: The statistics paragraph names only Fisher's exact test, which is not an appropriate test for the mean VCSS scores reported, and the paper does not say which comparison (within-group pre/post or between-group) each p-value refers to. With strata of 4-11 patients, and with unreadable p-values, the 'significant' differences for VCSS cannot be verified. I did not check the p-values themselves, since the printed forms are not interpretable.

issues.title: Sex totals 34 women/25 men conflict with group splits summing to 31 women/28 men
issues.explanation: The text and abstract say the 59 patients were 34 women and 25 men. The two groups described in Methods contain 20+11=31 women and 19+9=28 men. Both totals cannot be right, so the sex breakdown is internally inconsistent. This changes no outcome result but shows the cohort description is not carefully reconciled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that some patients were counted in neither group or that the overall totals refer to a different set, or a corrected sex split.

quotes.text: Среди обследованных пациентов было 34 женщины и 25 мужчин
Контрольную группу составили 20 пациентов, из них 11 женщин и 9 мужчин

10.24884/1682-6655-2025-24-1-47-56.headline_claim: The dynamic inversion table may be effective for improving vasomotor (microcirculatory) function and physical quality of life in post-COVID patients with reduced reserves, and may be promising for rehabilitation of microcirculatory dysfunction.
10.24884/1682-6655-2025-24-1-47-56.overall: The direction of the findings (larger gains in the device arm) is supported by internally consistent tables, apart from one misprinted control-change cell. The causal conclusion is weakened by marked baseline imbalance with no adjustment, an undefined and unblinded control, and conclusions about quality of life that were never measured. The results are best treated as preliminary.

primary_outcome.name: Work performed (power, W) during incremental cardiorespiratory exercise testing

issues.title: Marked baseline imbalance (age p=0.001) and unadjusted change comparisons; dice randomization
issues.explanation: The main group was older (median 62 vs 50, p=0.001) and had worse baseline oxygen kinetics, MET and post-occlusive flow. Between-group differences in change are compared without baseline adjustment. Groups starting lower have more room to rise, and the control group's high baseline post-occlusive flow then falls, so the reported differences may partly reflect baseline differences and regression to the mean. Dice-roll allocation with no concealment described adds to the doubt.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ANCOVA or baseline-adjusted analysis giving a similar treatment effect on the primary endpoint.

quotes.text: однако средний возраст пациентов основной группы был выше - 62 против 50 (табл. 1)
выполнялось распределение участников по группам путем рандомизации методом игральной кости

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does show a marked baseline age imbalance (median 62 vs 50 years, p=0.001) and lower baseline MET/oxygen kinetics in the treated group, yet compares change scores between groups with unadjusted Welch/Mann-Whitney tests and no ANCOVA or other adjustment, so the effect estimates are not adjusted for age or baseline values. Allocation is described only as 'randomization by dice', with no allocation concealment, sequence generation or blocking details, which cannot be verified and sits uneasily with the large chance imbalance; the claim that the paper has dice randomization is accurate,

issues.title: Control arm undefined, no blinding or sham; effort-dependent primary endpoint
issues.explanation: The paper does not say what the control rehabilitation involved or whether it matched the device arm in time and attention. No blinding is described, and the primary outcome (maximal work in a ramp test) depends on patient effort. Part of the difference may therefore reflect expectation or attention, not the device.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol describing a matched control programme and blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: Пациенты контрольной группы получали десятидневный курс реабилитации согласно временным методическим рекомендациям

issues.title: Table 4 control-group change -23.79 for post-occlusion flow does not match Table 5 (-43.79)
issues.explanation: Table 4 prints main-group change 80.42 and control change -23.79 but a difference of 124.20. Those two changes imply 104.21. Table 5 means give a control change of -43.79 and a difference of 124.21, so the -23.79 cell appears to be misprinted. The headline difference and its CI are internally consistent and the effect is not changed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing a control change of -23.79 with a difference of 124.20 derived another way.

quotes.text: для показателя микроциркуляции постокклюзионного кровотока - 124,20 (95 % ДИ - [81,29; 167,12])

issues.title: Conclusion cites improved 'physical quality of life' and confirmed endothelial link; neither was tested
issues.explanation: No quality-of-life measure was collected, yet the conclusion says the method may improve physical quality of life. The paper also says the results confirm a link between endothelial dysfunction and reduced reserves, but this was not analysed. Only short-term exercise-test and flow measures support the claims, from an unblinded 10-day comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified quality-of-life outcome with reported data, or text showing patients were selected for microcirculatory dysfunction.

quotes.text: может быть эффективным для пациентов со сниженными резервами для улучшения физического качества жизни
Данный метод может быть перспективным для реабилитации пациентов с дисфункцией микроциркуляции.

issues.title: Abstract assigns standard rehabilitation and the inversion table both to the 'control group'
issues.explanation: The abstract (Russian and English) says the control group received standard rehabilitation, then says the control group received the inversion table. The Methods and Results make clear the table was given to the main group. A reader of the abstract alone cannot tell which arm received the device.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not refutable; the wording is on the page.

quotes.text: Пациенты контрольной группы получали десятидневный курс реабилитации согласно временным методическим рекомендациям
patients of the control group received a ten-day course of using a dynamic inversion table

issues.title: Device manufacturer named; no funding statement and conflicts declared as none
issues.explanation: The study tests a table made by a named company, with no statement of who funded the work or supplied the device. Authors declare no conflicts. Readers cannot judge the manufacturer's role from the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A funding or device-supply statement showing no sponsor role.

quotes.text: производства ООО «Белмединновация», Республика Беларусь
Авторы заявили об отсутствии конфликта интересов.

issues.title: Baseline post-occlusion flow called significantly different, but Table 2 gives p = 0.062
issues.explanation: The Results list post-occlusion flow with oxygen kinetics and MET as measures that differed significantly at baseline. Table 2 gives p = 0.062 for it, which is above the paper's 0.05 threshold. The error is small, but it changes how much baseline imbalance the reader is told about.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alpha above 0.062 for baseline comparisons, or a corrected Table 2 p-value below 0.05.

quotes.text: Показатель микроциркуляции пост окклюзионого кровотока, медиана (Q1, Q3)
В основной группе показатели оказались хуже

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 35 vs 35; primary endpoint declared 'achieved'
issues.explanation: The paper gives no power calculation or basis for 70 patients. The text states the primary endpoint was achieved and that this shows the hypothesis is correct. With statistically clear effects, the main limit is a single-centre, 10-day, small sample, which supports only a tentative conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or registry entry with a prespecified sample-size calculation.

quotes.text: В исследовании приняли участие 70 пациентов в возрасте от 18 до 75 лет (35 в основной и 35 в контрольной группах)

issues.title: No trial registry number reported for a randomized device study
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval but no registration, so the stated primary endpoint and analysis cannot be checked against a prespecified record. The Methods do name the primary and secondary endpoints. Whether registration was required cannot be settled from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry that predates enrolment and matches the stated endpoints.

quotes.text: Исследование одобрено советом по этике Минздрава России и локальным этическим комитетом.

10.25040/ntsh2024.01.17.headline_claim: Inosine pranobex given for 12 weeks produced 60.1% clinical and 79.1% virological efficacy, with good tolerability and safety, in long COVID-19 patients with HHV-6 reactivation.
10.25040/ntsh2024.01.17.overall: The claim of 60.1% clinical and 79.1% virological efficacy, with safety, rests on a 20-patient uncontrolled before-after series with an unvalidated, undefined clinical outcome. The virological figure is printed two ways (79.4% and 79.1%) and is not reproducible from Table 2. The data are at most hypothesis-generating; efficacy and safety are overstated..

primary_outcome.name: Clinical effectiveness of 12-week inosine pranobex treatment (percentage, author-defined)

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from an uncontrolled before-after series of 20 patients
issues.explanation: All 20 patients got the drug and are compared with their own baseline. The healthy controls are untreated but are not patients, so they cannot show what would have happened without treatment. Spontaneous recovery of long COVID symptoms, regression to the mean and expectation effects are not separable, yet the paper concludes 'clinical and virological efficacy'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An untreated or placebo comparison group of patients followed over the same 12 weeks.

quotes.text: The study group consisted of 20 patients with long COVID-19 and HHV6 reactivation
Thus, the clinical effectiveness of the treatment of long COVID-19 patients with the replicative activity of HHV6 with inosine pranobex for 12 weeks amounted to 60.1%.

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is claimed from a single-arm, uncontrolled before-after series of 20 patients. The healthy controls do not serve as a treatment comparator, so regression to the mean, the natural course of symptoms and expectation effects cannot be separated from any drug effect. The limitations section does not name the lack of a treatment control, and the conclusion states the efficacy figures without qualification.

issues.title: 60.1% clinical efficacy rests on an author-modified questionnaire with no stated scoring or calculation
issues.explanation: Symptoms were recorded in the authors' own questionnaire. The paper does not say how the 60.1% was derived (which symptoms, which threshold, which denominator) and Figure 1 content is not given in the text. The headline clinical figure therefore cannot be reproduced or compared with validated long-COVID measures, and it was not preselected as a primary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The attached questionnaire with a defined scoring rule that reproduces 60.1%.

quotes.text: improved by us, which is attached.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, patient data paragraph

quotes.text: Thus, the clinical effectiveness of the treatment of long COVID-19 patients with the replicative activity of HHV6 with inosine pranobex for 12 weeks amounted to 60.1%.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not state how the 60.1% was calculated. It gives no scoring, threshold or formula, and the instrument is an author-modified, non-validated questionnaire. What is not established from the text is that the 60.1% is derived from that questionnaire, since the paper never says so and the attachment was not seen.

issues.title: Safety 'demonstrated' from 4 mild adverse events and non-significant lab changes in 20 uncontrolled patients
issues.explanation: Safety rests on four mild adverse events (20%) in 20 patients with no comparator, plus four biochemistry markers whose before-after differences were non-significant. With n=20 and no sample-size calculation, these cannot rule out meaningful liver or kidney effects or rarer events, and the AST/ALT means rose slightly. The conclusion that safety and tolerability were demonstrated is stronger than this supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified safety analysis with a comparator or a justified non-inferiority margin.

quotes.text: The number of adverse events totaled 4 (20.0%).
a low sample size

second_reader.what_stands: The safety and tolerability conclusion rests on 4 mild adverse events (20%) and non-significant changes in four biochemical markers in 20 uncontrolled patients. That cannot establish safety, because non-significance in a small sample is not evidence of no change and the confidence limits are wide. The paper's own note about sample size is not reflected in its wording that safety was 'demonstrated'.

issues.title: Stated study period (Sept 2020 - Dec 2023) starts before ethics approval of 27 Feb 2022
issues.explanation: The study period begins 17 months before the approval date, and the patient window (COVID Sept 2021 - Apr 2022, then 12 weeks of symptoms) means some patients may have been enrolled before approval. The paper does not say when enrolment and treatment actually took place, so the sequence cannot be settled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Dates of first enrolment and first dose showing they followed 27 Feb 2022, or retrospective approval wording.

quotes.text: from September 2020 to December 2023
protocol No. 1/22 from 27.02.22

issues.title: Table 1 differential counts labelled g/L but are percentages (healthy column sums to 100.0)
issues.explanation: Segmented granulocytes of 63 g/L cannot exceed total leukocytes of 6.12 g/L. The differential rows sum to about 100, so they are percentages of leukocytes mislabelled as g/L. The values are probably usable, but the table as printed is wrong and a reader cannot interpret the absolute counts.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the differential values are absolute counts.

issues.title: No trial registration reported for a 12-week treatment study
issues.explanation: No registry identifier or prespecified primary outcome is reported, so selective reporting cannot be assessed. This is a modest concern for a small pilot, but efficacy is stated as a result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier with a prespecified outcome matching the reported ones.

10.25259/ijmr_827_2024.headline_claim: A combined progressive muscle relaxation and spinal muscle training protocol delivered by telerehabilitation significantly reduced systemic inflammation (serum IL-17) and improved functional independence (Katz ADL) in male manual labourers with post-COVID paraspinal myalgia, compared with standard neurosurgical care.
10.25259/ijmr_827_2024.overall: The direction of the findings (lower IL-17 and higher ADL in the exercise arm) is plausible and the numbers are internally consistent apart from a trivial 127/128 slip. But the non-random, unblinded, unadjusted comparison of two different programmes in 60 men supports only a tentative conclusion, and the claims about cost-effectiveness, scalability and telerehabilitation are not supported by anything measured.

primary_outcome.name: Serum IL-17 change and Katz ADL score (no single primary outcome named; both presented as main outcomes)

issues.title: Non-random timeslot allocation with unadjusted comparisons supports causal efficacy claims
issues.explanation: Participants were assigned by outpatient timeslot, not randomly, and groups were compared with simple unadjusted t-tests. Baseline ADL was lower in the control group (2.50 vs 2.93), and the 'similar' label rests only on a non-significant P value in 30 per group. The paper still concludes that the intervention 'effectively reduced' inflammation. The Limitations note possible selection bias but the conclusion is worded causally and without hedging.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Analysis adjusted for baseline values and for allocation cluster showing the same between-group effects.

quotes.text: since random allocation was considered impractical in this situation
The intervention significantly reduced systemic inflammation and improved functional outcomes compared to conventional standard neurosurgical care (SNC).
Baseline Katz ADL scores were also found to be statistically similar ( P =0.114).

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation followed OPD timeslots in a non-random way. The between-group tests are unadjusted unpaired t-tests on endpoint values, with no covariate or baseline adjustment, no allowance for clustering by timeslot, and no blinding mentioned. Despite this, the abstract says 'significantly efficacious', the Discussion says the intervention 'significantly reduced' inflammation 'compared to' SNC, and the conclusion says it 'effectively reduced' it. The paper does acknowledge selection bias in its limitations and the baseline groups look similar on the variables tested. But 'statistically similar' f

issues.title: 'Greater improvement' claims rest on post-value tests; ADL baseline gap of 0.43 not adjusted
issues.explanation: The between-group P values in Table II compare post-intervention values, yet the text states the experimental group showed a 'greater' reduction or improvement. For IL-17 the baselines match so this is minor. For ADL the control group started lower, so a post-value test mixes baseline difference with change, and an ANCOVA or change-score test would be the matching analysis. The raw ADL gain (2.10 vs 1.03) still points in the same direction, so the direction is likely robust but its size is not.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A direct test of change scores, or ANCOVA adjusted for baseline, giving similar results.

quotes.text: Paired t-tests were used for within-group comparisons, and independent (unpaired) t-tests were used for between-group comparisons.
On comparison between the groups, the experimental group showed a greater IL-17 reduction

issues.title: Conclusions claim cost-effectiveness, scalability and telerehabilitation benefit that were not tested
issues.explanation: The final paragraph says the findings support a 'scalable and cost-effective' solution, but no costs were measured and no scalability data were collected. Both arms used telerehabilitation, so its effect cannot be separated from the exercise content. The authors acknowledge the missing in-person comparator but the conclusion still credits telerehabilitation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Collected cost data and an in-person comparison supporting these statements.

quotes.text: as a scalable and cost-effective solution to extend rehabilitation services to underserved populations
This study also highlighted the role of telerehabilitation in intervention delivery to socio-demographically limited populations.
Lack of a comparison group receiving in-person rehabilitation makes it challenging to isolate the advantages of telerehabilitation.

issues.title: No blinding of participants or outcome assessors reported; Katz ADL is assessor- or self-rated
issues.explanation: The paper does not say whether participants, physiotherapists or outcome assessors were blinded. Participants in an exercise programme cannot be blinded to it, and the control programme was a visibly lighter regimen, so expectation effects on the ADL score are plausible. IL-17 is an objective lab measure and is less affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that ADL assessors and laboratory staff were blinded to group.

quotes.text: Trained physiotherapists supervised the participants to ensure adherence to the correct exercises and relaxation techniques.

issues.title: Prospective interventional study reports no trial registration
issues.explanation: This is a prospective study that allocated and treated participants, but no registry identifier is given. Without one, the outcomes and analysis plan cannot be compared against a pre-specified protocol. The paper's two reported outcomes match its stated aims, so this is a transparency gap rather than evidence of outcome switching.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective registry entry (e.g. CTRI) predating enrolment with the same outcomes.

issues.title: Screened individuals reported as 127 (Methods, figure) but 128 (Results)
issues.explanation: The Methods and the figure caption state 127 individuals were screened, while the first Results sentence says 128. The two counts describe the same stage, so they cannot both be right. The 68 eligible and 60 enrolled figures are unaffected, so no result depends on this.

10.26355/eurrev_202112_27335.headline_claim: A multivitamin food supplement containing hydroxytyrosol, acetyl L-carnitine and vitamins B, C and D may improve self-perceived physical and mental status in people recovering from COVID-19 compared with healthy non-users, and could proceed to clinical trials.
10.26355/eurrev_202112_27335.overall: The paper is a small, open, uncontrolled-in-effect pilot, and its finding that the supplement produced greater improvement than in non-users cannot be relied on: the comparator is healthy people with different baselines, no statistical test is reported, and the outcome is self-rated. The authors appropriately limit their conclusion to proceeding to trials, but the Discussion wording is stronger than the evidence, and several secondary percentages (taste, GI side effects) do not reconcile.

primary_outcome.name: Self-reported fatigue and energy status (AD ACL subscales: energy, tiredness, tension, calmness)

checklist.control: non-equivalent healthy comparison group without placebo

issues.title: Comparator is non-randomised healthy volunteers without COVID; baselines differ markedly, so effect not isolated
issues.explanation: Users were post-COVID patients with fatigue, while the comparison group were healthy people without COVID-19 who were not given a placebo. Baseline scores differ substantially (users' energy 155 vs non-users' 273), so larger changes in the user group could reflect regression to the mean, natural recovery or a different response range. A supplement effect cannot be separated from these.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomised placebo-controlled comparison, or a comparator of untreated post-COVID fatigue patients with matched baselines.

quotes.text: Twenty other subjects (10 females and 10 males), who did not have COVID-19

second_reader.what_stands: The comparator is 20 non-randomised people without COVID-19 who did not take the supplement, with allocation not described as random. Their baseline scores differ markedly from the users' (for example energy 155 vs 273), so any difference in change cannot be attributed to the supplement. The authors acknowledge the baseline gap in the Table I caption and recommend a randomized trial, but they still state the comparative result as an improvement 'with respect to' healthy volunteers.

issues.title: No statistical test of any kind; 'more improvement than non-users' rests on descriptive percentage changes
issues.explanation: The paper reports only percentage changes in summed adjective scores per arm. No test, p-value or confidence interval is given for the within-group or the between-group change, yet the text says the non-users 'did not show any significant change'. The between-group claim is untested, and sums of ordinal item scores are used without variability measures.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test (e.g. ANCOVA on change scores) with confidence intervals supporting the difference.

quotes.text: Self-reported energy levels doubled after 15 days on the food supplement (+123%)

second_reader.what_stands: The comparative claim ('more improvement than non-users', 'did not show any significant change') rests only on descriptive percentage changes in summed scores, with no statistical test, p-value, or interval. The percentages themselves are arithmetically correct. The user group's large relative changes also start from a much lower energy baseline, which a bare percentage does not account for.

issues.title: Open-label supplement with self-rated fatigue outcome and no placebo; expectation effects uncontrolled
issues.explanation: Users knew they were taking a supplement offered for fatigue, and the outcome is self-rating of how they feel. Expectation and demand effects could produce part of the large reported change. Much of this is already captured by the lack of a placebo comparator, so this is a narrower additional concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A blinded, placebo-controlled design or an objective outcome corroborating the self-report.

quotes.text: Participants were instructed to rate each adjective according to how they felt while answering the questionnaire
complained of fatigue and were offered the food supplement

issues.title: Pilot with 20 per arm and no sample-size justification; estimates imprecise but authors call it preliminary
issues.explanation: Each arm has 20 participants, with no sample-size calculation. A pilot of this size can only be hypothesis-generating. The authors do describe the results as preliminary and call for a randomised trial, which moderates the concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size justification or a pilot-feasibility framing without efficacy inference.

quotes.text: Although our population was not large

This attributes the change to the supplement although the groups differ in disease status and baseline, and no test was performed. The hedge 'may' and the pilot framing in the abstract soften but do not remove the problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Wording limited to descriptive association with explicit acknowledgement of the non-equivalent comparator.

Symptoms per volunteer can overlap, so the 75% may be a union of volunteers with any GI symptom, but the paper does not show this. It cannot be confirmed or refuted from the text.

10.26442/00403660.2022.03.201398.headline_claim: Inhaled activated hydrogen increases nasal granulocyte and oral monocyte phagocytosis and nasal sIgA, and the authors state it is effective as adjunct therapy for COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome.
10.26442/00403660.2022.03.201398.overall: The paper shows some within-arm changes in mucosal phagocytosis and sIgA after hydrogen inhalation, but the design (undescribed allocation, no sham, no blinding, uncorrected multiplicity, borderline p-values) supports only a tentative exploratory signal. The conclusion that the data indicate therapeutic efficacy for COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome is not supported by biomarker-only outcomes and no safety data.

primary_outcome.name: Phagocytic index (granulocytes and monocytes) and sIgA; no single primary outcome is designated

issues.title: Biomarker changes in 60 patients presented as therapeutic efficacy; no clinical or safety outcomes
issues.explanation: The study measured only phagocytosis indices and sIgA, with no symptoms, function or clinical endpoints and no adverse-event reporting. Immune-marker changes, some in opposite directions (pharyngeal sIgA fell about 2-fold), do not establish clinical benefit. The abstract nonetheless states that the data indicate efficacy for COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Prespecified clinical efficacy outcomes showing benefit, with safety data, in a controlled design.

quotes.text: Полученные данные указывают на эффективность терапии, которая может применяться как в лечении COVID-19, так и при постковидном синдроме в качестве дополнительной терапии.
активная форма водорода значимо меняет показатели мукозального иммунитета верхних дыхательных путей

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract conclusion states that the data indicate therapeutic effectiveness for COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome, yet the study reports only laboratory markers in 60 patients, with no clinical outcomes and no safety data. The conclusion body is more modest in wording (changes in mucosal immunity indicators, further study needed for some results), but does not address the missing clinical and safety endpoints.

issues.title: sIgA effect (2.9-fold nasal rise) rests on within-arm change only; no between-group sIgA test reported
issues.explanation: For phagocytosis, the paper reports both within-arm and versus-control comparisons, so the screen overstated the problem there. For sIgA, only the within-group day 1 to day 10 change is tested; the control group is said to show no significant change, but no between-group comparison is given. A within-arm change cannot separate a hydrogen effect from time, recovery or the usual-care regimen, yet nasal sIgA is listed in the conclusion as an effect of hydrogen.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group (treatment vs control) test or ANCOVA on day-10 nasal sIgA showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: Уровень sIgA на 10-й день в назальных соскобах достоверно повышался относительно 1-го дня в 2,9 раза
В  контрольной  группе  не  показано  достоверно значимых отличий на 1 и 10-й дни забора в назальных и фарингеальных соскобах.

second_reader.what_stands: In the text, the 2.9-fold nasal sIgA increase is supported only by a within-group day 1 vs day 10 comparison in the hydrogen arm; no between-group test of sIgA in scrapings is reported, although the control arm was measured at both timepoints. This is based on the text and captions; figure contents could not be checked.

issues.title: Control group allocation, baseline comparability and blinding not described (n=30 vs 30)
issues.explanation: The paper does not state whether patients were randomized, how controls were chosen, or whether the groups were similar at baseline. Between-arm differences, such as the 1.1-fold nasal granulocyte difference at p=0.047, could therefore reflect group differences rather than hydrogen. The control also received no sham inhalation, so non-specific effects of the procedure are not excluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of randomized or matched allocation with a baseline comparison of the two groups.

quotes.text: Контрольная группа пациентов находилась на лечении согласно стандартному протоколу ведения пациентов, перенесших COVID-19

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not describe how patients were assigned to the hydrogen or control group, gives no baseline characteristics for either group, and does not state any blinding (including of laboratory assessors). Group sizes of 30 vs 30 are stated, and the control arm is described only as standard rehabilitation care.

issues.title: About 10 outcomes tested at p≤0.05 uncorrected; borderline hits (p=0.047, p=0.041) drive the conclusion
issues.explanation: Phagocytosis was tested in blood, nasal and pharyngeal samples for two cell types, plus sIgA in nasal, pharyngeal and saliva samples, each within-arm and versus control, with no multiplicity correction. The two borderline results (nasal granulocytes vs control p=0.047; pharyngeal monocytes vs day 1 p=0.041) would fail even a modest correction. Several outcomes were null and pharyngeal sIgA fell, yet the conclusion states that hydrogen 'significantly changes' mucosal immunity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis in which these findings remain significant.

quotes.text: Различия считали статистически значимыми при допустимой вероятности ошибки р ≤ 0,05.
ФИ моноцитов в фарингеальном соскобе показал достоверное повышение относительно 1-го дня лечения в 2,8 раза ( p =0,041103), однако не отличался относительно контроля.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states a single uncorrected threshold of p ≤ 0.05 across many comparisons, and two of the reported hits (p=0.047410 and p=0.041103) would not survive a Bonferroni correction for about 12 comparisons. However, not all findings are borderline (nasal granulocyte day 1 vs 10, p=0.000189, would survive), and the pharyngeal monocyte finding is reported as not different from control in the paper itself.

10.26442/00403660.2022.11.201981.headline_claim: Brainmax (a succinate-trimethylhydrazinium complex) is effective and has a high safety profile in patients with post-COVID-19 asthenic syndrome.
10.26442/00403660.2022.11.201981.overall: The primary MFI-20 result (median -19.5 vs -3, p<0.001) points to a benefit, but the paper reports no sample size calculation, analysis population or attrition, and describes the effect inconsistently (four-fold versus six-fold). The safety and cognitive claims, and the benefit of the oral phase, go beyond the data shown; the safety conclusion in particular conflicts with the 63 vs 18 adverse event counts.

primary_outcome.name: Change in MFI-20 score from Visit 0 to Visit 5 (day 41)

issues.title: 'High safety profile' claim despite 63 vs 18 adverse events and no reported safety analysis; 'representative' sample
issues.explanation: Table 3 shows 63 adverse events in the Brainmax arm against 18 on placebo, with 59 of 63 judged definitely, probably or possibly related, while patient-level incidence is similar (18 vs 16 patients). The text asserts a statistical analysis showed a comparable or more favourable profile, but none is shown, and the event-count excess points the other way. A 160-patient, 41-day trial under strict eligibility criteria cannot establish a high safety profile or a representative sample.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group safety analysis showing no excess of events, or an explanation that the 63 vs 18 counts are a misprint.

quotes.text: Проведенный  статистический анализ свидетельствует о сопоставимом либо более благоприятном профиле безопасности исследуемого препарата в сравнении с плацебо.

issues.title: Advantage over placebo described as four-fold and as more than six-fold; Table 2 medians give about 6.5
issues.explanation: The Results call the MFI-20 advantage 'four-fold' in the Fig. 4 paragraph and 'more than 6-fold' in the Fig. 3 paragraph. 10.26442/00403660.2023.05.202224.headline_claim: BRAINMAX (succinate-trimethylhydrazinium complex) is effective across a broad range of post-COVID asthenic symptoms, with convincing demonstration of efficacy.
10.26442/00403660.2023.05.202224.overall: The trial shows between-group differences on several patient-reported scales (PSQI, FAS-10, DHI, BAI), but the headline claim of 'convincing' broad efficacy is stronger than the evidence printed. The primary MFI-20 result is shown without a placebo comparator, cognition is null unless adjusted, VAS is borderline, and no analysed numbers, multiplicity control or registration are reported. 10.26442/00403660.2023.08.202349.headline_claim: L-ornithine-L-aspartate (LOLA) is effective in post-COVID syndrome, reducing blood ammonia and improving cognitive test scores, and measuring NH3 and treating with LOLA is advisable for patients with mild and moderate post-COVID syndrome.
10.26442/00403660.2023.08.202349.overall: The headline claim that LOLA is effective in post-COVID syndrome rests on an uncontrolled pre-post change in 30 students, with the control group measured only at baseline and drawn from people without COVID. Large before/after differences are reported, but they cannot be attributed to the drug, and the practice recommendation goes beyond the design. Reporting slips (sex percentages, swapped test names, date order) add to the uncertainty but are secondary.

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from pre-post change in 30 treated students; controls never followed and had no COVID
issues.explanation: All 30 treated students received LOLA and were tested at baseline and after 1 month. The 30 controls had no prior COVID-19 and were measured only at baseline, so there is no comparison of change between treated and untreated post-COVID patients. Improvements in ammonia, enzymes and cognitive scores may reflect natural recovery, regression to the mean, or practice effects on repeated testing, and the confident efficacy statement is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up data from an untreated post-COVID comparison group showing no similar change.

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from before-after change in 30 treated post-COVID students. The comparison group was healthy, had no COVID, received no LOLA, and has no reported 1-month data, so it cannot separate drug effect from spontaneous recovery, regression to the mean or test practice. The wording 'never followed' goes slightly beyond the text: the methods say all testing was repeated at 1 month, but no control follow-up results are reported.

issues.title: Recommendation of NH3 testing and LOLA for all mild/moderate post-COVID patients rests on 30 uncontrolled cases
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says LOLA is effective and recommends measuring NH3 and prescribing LOLA to patients with mild and moderate post-COVID syndrome. The evidence is a 30-patient open pre-post comparison in students, with no randomised or concurrent control, no sample-size justification, no limitations section and no adverse-event reporting. The conclusion goes beyond what that design can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data showing superiority of LOLA over no treatment or placebo in post-COVID patients.

quotes.text: Терапия LOLA  достаточно  эффективна,  отмечены  значительные улучшения в уровнях NH₃ и показателях ТСЧ.

second_reader.what_stands: The recommendation to test NH3 and give LOLA to patients with mild/moderate post-COVID syndrome generalises from 30 young, selected, uncontrolled, 1-month cases to a much wider population, without stated limitations. issues.title: Methods pair Mann-Whitney with paired data and Wilcoxon with unpaired normal data, reversing the standard tests
issues.explanation: The Methods say paired non-normal data were analysed with the Mann-Whitney U test, and unpaired normally distributed data with the Wilcoxon test. These are the wrong way round, and Wilcoxon is a rank test not used for normal data. The actual tests behind the uniform p < 0.001 cannot be determined, though large effects likely hold under any suitable paired test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of the specific test used for each outcome that matches standard practice.

10.26442/00403660.2023.12.202523.overall: The finding that the Zakofalk arm reports lower symptom scores is plausible, but the headline claim of a 'significant' increase in effectiveness is not backed by a reported between-arm test, variability measures or blinding. issues.title: Efficacy claimed 'significant' from within-arm changes; no between-group test, SDs or CIs reported
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion state that Zakofalk significantly increases treatment effectiveness. The only significance markers are asterisks on the Zakofalk arm's own day-1 and day-30 values and statements about change within group 2. No comparison of change between the arms is reported, no variability measure is given for any score, and the tests used are never named. second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not report how patients were allocated and does not describe the study as randomised, and the printed CT grade 4 figures (47.1% vs 17.6%, 8 vs 3 patients) do differ visibly. However, the omnibus CT test is non-significant (p=0.29), so calling the imbalance a demonstrated baseline difference is not supported; the more accurate statement is that small numbers leave baseline comparability unestablished, and that the abstract's 'groups did not differ' rests on underpowered tests, with time since infection (p=0.08) and corticosteroid use (p=0.07) also showing gaps.

issues.title: 'Clinical efficacy' concluded from 34 non-randomised, open-label patients without sample-size justification

10.26442/00403660.2026.03.203537.overall: The headline claim that iNO/iH2 is effective, and better than iNO alone, rests on a small open-label study with unexplained allocation, baseline imbalances in BMI and symptom duration, many uncorrected comparisons and mostly subjective outcomes. issues.title: Open-label, no-sham comparison with self-reported symptom outcomes; conclusion states efficacy without caveat

Objective outcomes (6-MWT, FORT, capillaroscopy) are less affected, but the control arm received no inhalation at all.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sham-controlled or blinded-assessor design, or objective outcomes alone supporting the conclusion.

issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary endpoint or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis plan.

10.26442/20751753.2025.3.203073.headline_claim: The course of pulmonary rehabilitation after COVID-19 pneumonia was effective in patients with chronic bronchoobstructive disease, improving blood markers, immunoglobulin A, dyspnoea scores, lung CT involvement and spirometry compared with a group without rehabilitation.
10.26442/20751753.2025.3.203073.overall: The claim that rehabilitation was effective rests on a small, non-randomised 18 vs 16 comparison with no between-group tests, no adjustment and visible baseline imbalances, so causal conclusions are only tentative. Several reported magnitudes (lung involvement fold change, CRP, pneumofibrosis) conflict with the paper's own tables, which lowers confidence in the exact effect sizes. The direction of improvement in the rehabilitation group is plausible, but its size and attribution to the intervention are not established.

issues.title: Non-randomised 18 vs 16 comparison, no adjustment or between-group tests, supports 'effective' conclusion
issues.explanation: Patients who received rehabilitation were compared with 16 patients who did not, with no stated allocation method, no baseline adjustment and no sample-size rationale. Baseline values differ visibly between groups, and 'comparable' is asserted only in prose. Improvements are reported as within-group changes (p<0.001) and the abstract labels them 'compared with the control group', but no between-group test is reported. Selection, regression to the mean and natural recovery after COVID-19 pneumonia could explain much of the difference, so the efficacy and causal conclusion goes beyond the design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described allocation procedure that is independent of patient or clinician choice, plus between-group tests adjusted for baseline.

10.26502/acbr.50170337.headline_claim: A pilot open-label trial suggests transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation is a possible therapeutic modality for Long Covid meeting the 1994 CFS case definition, and the authors describe the trial as a successful pilot.
10.26502/acbr.50170337.overall: The pilot's own success criterion is probably met, but the headline 57% rate does not match the 15 patients analysed (8/15 = 53%), and Table 1 and the text disagree on the patient breakdown. More fundamentally, a single-arm open-label study with subjective outcomes can only support feasibility, not the efficacy language used, which rests on a historical placebo rate.

primary_outcome.name: Improvement on at least two of four criteria (SF-36 physical function, VAS most troubling symptom, loss of Chalder fatigue caseness, PGIC +2/+3)

issues.title: Single-arm open-label pilot (n=15) with self-reported outcomes cannot show efficacy; placebo argued from a historical 24%
issues.explanation: All participants received active stimulation, with no sham or concurrent control, and every primary component is subjective. The 8/15 responder rate with a very wide uncertainty range (roughly 27% to 79%) is compared with a placebo rate taken from a different literature to argue that placebo is unlikely. The study cannot distinguish stimulation effect from expectancy, natural fluctuation or regression to the mean. It supports feasibility and a case for a controlled trial, not the 'possible therapeutic modality' and 'successful' framing.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent sham or blinded comparator, or objective outcome measures, showing the responder rate exceeds placebo.

quotes.text: This open label pilot study suggests non-invasive stimulation of the auricular branch of the vagus nerve is a possible therapeutic modality for treating this ailment.

The authors do acknowledge the lack of a sham arm, use hedged language ('suggests', 'possible') and call for a controlled trial, so the paper does not claim proven efficacy. The 'successful pilot' label is defensible only against the stated a priori one-third threshold. The quoted 57% improvement rate does n

issues.title: Improvement rate printed as 57% (= 8/14) but Results analyse 15 patients (8/15 = 53%); Table 1 has 14 rows
issues.explanation: The Results say 15 patients were analysed and 8 improved, which is 53.3%. The Discussion reports a 57% improvement rate, which equals 8/14 and matches the 14 subjects in Table 1. The text counts 6 patients with no improvement, but Table 1 shows only 5 blank rows, so one subject appears to be missing from the table or the 57% uses the wrong denominator. The success criterion of at least one third is met either way, but the headline rate and the placebo comparison use the larger figure.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 7 patients, not 8 of 15 or that the 57% was computed on 14 analysable patients, or a corrected Table 1 listing 15 subjects with 8 positives.

issues.explanation: The Results say two patients improved on all four measures, one on three and five on two. issues.title: No trial registration reported; a priori outcome criteria cannot be checked against a prospective record
issues.explanation: The Methods mention IRB approval but no registry identifier for a prospective interventional study. The a priori responder definition and success threshold are described only in the paper. Their prespecification therefore cannot be verified externally. This matters little for a pilot but weakens the 'a priori' claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment with the same outcome criteria.

10.26574/maedica.2025.20.1.48.headline_claim: Eight weeks of yoga improved pulmonary function tests and reduced arterial stiffness in post-COVID-19 mild-to-moderate patients.
10.26574/maedica.2025.20.1.48.overall: The paper's claim that yoga improves lung function and arterial stiffness rests on a single-arm 27-person pre-post comparison, so changes cannot be attributed to yoga and the practice recommendation outruns the evidence. Reporting is also loose: the Table 1 caption n of 19 conflicts with 27 analysed, and many outcomes were tested uncorrected. The physiological changes are large for pulse wave velocity, but only as observed associations over time.

primary_outcome.name: Pulmonary function tests (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC) and arterial stiffness (baPWV, cfPWV) before vs after 8 weeks of yoga

issues.title: Single-arm pre-post design with no control group used to attribute changes to yoga
issues.explanation: All participants received yoga and were measured before and after, with no comparison group. Changes in spirometry, blood pressure and pulse wave velocity could reflect recovery from COVID-19 over time, measurement familiarity, or regression to the mean (baseline values were selected as abnormal). The analysis mentions one-way ANOVA and Tukey-Kramer tests, which have no group structure to apply to here. The causal attribution to yoga is therefore not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control or waitlist group showing no comparable change.

quotes.text: Data from pre- and post-intervention tests were analyzed using paired t-tests, one-way ANOVA and Tukey-Kramer post hoc tests.
This suggests that regular practise of yoga can effectively reduce both SBP and DBP

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm pre-post design with no control group, so changes in blood pressure (and other outcomes) cannot be separated from regression to the mean, natural post-COVID recovery over time, measurement or familiarity effects, or other concurrent changes. The Results statement that yoga 'can effectively reduce both SBP and DBP' goes beyond what this design supports. The ANOVA/Tukey-Kramer methods are stated but no between-group analysis is evident in the text provided.

issues.title: Conclusion recommends yoga as a valuable strategy and routine testing from an uncontrolled 27-person study
issues.explanation: The conclusion states yoga 'can be a valuable strategy' for respiratory and cardiovascular health and suggests regular PFT and arterial stiffness assessment. The study has no control group, no long-term follow-up, no clinical outcomes and no adverse event reporting. The hedge 'appear to improve' and the call for more research soften it, but the recommendation still outruns the evidence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled evidence of benefit; or conclusion limited to feasibility and hypothesis generation.

quotes.text: A regular yoga practice can be a valuable  strategy  for  improving  respiratory  and cardiovascular health in post-COVID-19 subjects

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion does recommend yoga as a 'valuable strategy' and suggests routine PFT and arterial stiffness assessment on the basis of an uncontrolled study of 27 completers, which is stronger than the evidence supports, and no limitations are discussed. It is partly tempered by 'appear to improve' and the call for more research, and the testing suggestion is phrased as 'can be suggested' rather than as a firm recommendation, and it is not derived from anything tested in this study.

issues.title: Table 1 caption says 19 participants; Results say 27 analysed
issues.explanation: The Table 1 caption describes 19 participants, while the Results state 27 were included and analysed (15 male, 12 female). The paper never explains the 8-person difference. It may be a caption slip, but the reader cannot tell which n the baseline characteristics describe. The same section also gives sex as 55% and 44%, which do not sum to 100%.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 1 body showing n=27 with the caption being a typographical error, or a note explaining a subset of 19.

quotes.text: The present study included  27  participants aged 20 to 50 years
TABLE 1. Baseline demographic characteristics of 19 study participants with mild and moderate post-COVID-19

issues.title: Roughly a dozen outcomes tested at p<0.05 without correction; several reported only as p<0.05
issues.explanation: The methods specify an uncorrected two-sided threshold of 0.05 across many spirometry, blood pressure and arterial stiffness outcomes. Several results are reported only as 'p<0.05' (SBP, MABP, pulse rate, FEV1 etc.), where borderline results could be chance findings. The strongest results (baPWV, cfPWV at p<0.001) are likely robust, so this mainly weakens the secondary findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or a correction showing the key results remain significant.

quotes.text: All statistical tests applied were two-sided and a p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
No significant  differences  were  found  in  other indices  of  arterial  stiffness,  including  ASI,  ABI and  AIx  (p>0.05)

issues.title: 3 of 30 withdrew (10%); completers-only analysis, no sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Three participants withdrew because of respiratory infections and were excluded from analysis, with no imputation or sensitivity analysis. Those who fell ill may be the participants least likely to benefit, so completers-only results could be modestly optimistic. The loss is small, so this is a minor weakness rather than a major one.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis including the 3 withdrawals (e.g., last observation carried forward) with unchanged findings.

quotes.text: Three participants withdrew from the study due to upper respiratory tract infections, which prevented them from attending the yoga sessions.

issues.title: No trial registry identifier reported for a prospective interventional study
issues.explanation: The paper reports ethics approval but no registry number, so outcomes and analyses cannot be compared against a prospective plan. This matters more given the many outcomes tested and no designated primary outcome. It may simply be unreported rather than absent.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry entry (e.g., CTRI) made before enrolment with matching outcomes.

quotes.text: After taking the approval of Institutional Ethical Committee  (IEC)  (IEC  ref  no.  AIIMS/BBN/IEC/ SEPT/2023/317)

issues.title: cfPWV post-intervention SD (113.19) nearly duplicates baseline SD (123.19)
issues.explanation: The cfPWV baseline is 917.37 ± 123.19 and post-yoga 748.05 ± 113.19; the two SDs differ only in one digit. This could be coincidence or a transcription slip. The effect is large either way (a fall of about 169), so conclusions do not depend on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The raw data or the Table 3 entries showing these SDs are correct.

quotes.text: The baseline mean value of cfPWV was 917.37 ± 123.19. After eight weeks of yoga, it significantly decreased to 748.05 ± 113.19

10.26717/bjstr.2022.47.007512.headline_claim: VITAMIC BIOSEN® markedly affected the clinical symptoms of LONG COVID patients and modified their molecular pattern of immunoinflammatory biomarkers.
10.26717/bjstr.2022.47.007512.overall: The headline claim that the supplement markedly improved long-COVID symptoms and that biomarkers predict responders is not supported: the design is uncontrolled and open-label, no effect sizes or exact statistics are given, and the stated primary outcomes are never reported. Baseline percentages are not attainable shares of 60 patients, and ethics approval and funding are not documented. At best the paper is a descriptive pilot with hypothesis-generating biomarker patterns.

primary_outcome.name: Functional status (PCFS) and EuroQol-5D quality of life at 6 weeks

issues.title: Efficacy and causal claims drawn from an uncontrolled, open-label single-arm study with no reported effect sizes
issues.explanation: All 60 patients received the supplement, with no control group, and outcomes are self-reported symptom scores, so natural recovery, regression to the mean, co-treatment and expectation cannot be separated from any product effect. The conclusion nonetheless says the product 'markedly affected the clinical symptoms' and that biomarker effects 'could explain' symptom changes. No means, differences, test statistics or exact p-values are given, only statements that significant differences occurred.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control comparison, or reported effect sizes showing changes beyond expected natural recovery.

quotes.text: A low-intervention, single-arm, open-label study with 60 patients suffering from post-acute COVID syndrome (LONG COVID).
VITAMIC BIOSEN® markedly affected the clinical symptoms of LONG COVID patients
one or more p-values have been less than 0.05

second_reader.what_stands: The paper draws efficacy and causal conclusions ('markedly affected', 'beneficial effects', biomarker changes 'could explain' symptom changes) from an uncontrolled, open-label single-arm study with self-reported outcomes. It reports no effect sizes, confidence intervals or exact p-values in the text, only a statement that 'one or more p-values' were below 0.05. The one caveat is that Figure 7 is an image and may contain numbers I could not see.

issues.title: Primary outcomes (PCFS, EuroQol-5D) never reported; conclusions rest on secondary symptoms and 20-patient biomarker clustering
issues.explanation: The methods declare PCFS and EuroQol-5D as primary outcomes, and the conclusion lists them as objectives 1 and 2, but no results for either are presented. Instead the conclusions emphasise secondary Likert symptom changes and exploratory biomarker heatmaps and PCA from 20 patients. The claim that biomarkers identify patients who 'will successfully respond' is predictive and unsupported by a pre-specified analysis in so small a subgroup.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: PCFS and EuroQol-5D results reported in the paper or a supplement with pre-specified analysis.

quotes.text: Primary outcomes Functional status, according to PostCOVID Functional Scale (PCFS) one, two, three and six weeks after treatment  initiation.
quotes.location: Research Methods, Evaluation of the Response

quotes.text: High AGP, Fetuin A and A2M blood level discriminate patients before treatment who will respond to VITAMIC BIOSEN®.

second_reader.what_stands: In the text, the primary outcomes (PCFS, EuroQol-5D) are never reported, and the conclusions rest on Likert symptom results (secondary outcomes) and on 20-patient clustering and PCA, with no response definition or validation for the claim that biomarkers identify future responders. I cannot confirm that the primary outcomes are absent altogether, because Figure 7 and the other figures are images I could not read.

issues.title: Baseline symptom percentages (69.38, 79.58, 58.9, 22.45) are not attainable shares of 60 patients
issues.explanation: The paper states 60 patients are monitored, but gives symptom percentages such as 69.38% and 79.58% with no counts. With n = 60 only multiples of 1.667% are possible (68.33 or 70.00 near 69.38), so these figures cannot be shares of 60. The denominator is never explained, and two different symptoms share the identical 69.38 value. The descriptive baseline data cannot be verified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the percentages are means of visit-level or severity data, or counts and denominators per symptom.

A total of 60 patients are being monitored at this primary care clinic.

issues.title: Ethics approval never confirmed; only submission to a committee is stated

issues.title: No funding or conflict statement; biomarker assays run by the test manufacturer
issues.explanation: All biomarker samples were processed by the company that makes the ENCHEPAX test, and the paper contains no funding, sponsor or conflict-of-interest statement, including for the supplement itself. Whether that company or the supplement maker influenced design, analysis or reporting cannot be determined. The biomarker-based conclusions depend on this assay.

issues.title: No trial registry identifier reported for a prospective supplement study
issues.explanation: The study prospectively assigned a supplement and followed outcomes at 6 weeks, but gives no registry number or protocol reference. Since primary outcomes are then not reported (see the selective-reporting issue), the absence of a registered protocol means this cannot be checked. Observational-study regulations may not require registration, so this is a transparency gap.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry identifier or a published protocol predating recruitment.

10.26717/bjstr.2024.59.009252.headline_claim: EchA Marine (sea urchin egg supplement containing Echinochrome A) is an effective and natural treatment for improving quality of life in long COVID patients, with supporting effects on IL-2 and IL-10.
10.26717/bjstr.2024.59.009252.overall: The headline conclusion that EchA Marine is an effective and safe treatment for long COVID is only weakly supported. The main support is a borderline multivariate result (p = 0.048) in a small per-protocol sample (46 of 100 planned), in a trial registered late with primary outcomes that differ from those registered. The cytokine claims are not supported by the ANOVA as reported (no interaction test, Time effects non-significant), no safety data are given, and Tables 2-3 contain several transcription errors.
