issues.title: Conclusion calls supplement 'effective' and 'safe'; no safety data and weak, per-protocol evidence
issues.explanation: The Methods say safety was evaluated, but the Results report no adverse events. The efficacy claim relies on a final MANOVA with p = 0.048, a per-protocol set of 46, a retrospectively registered trial with switched outcomes, and cytokine claims not supported by the Time or interaction tests. The statement that the findings are 'critical' goes beyond this evidence. An industry-linked co-author supplied the product.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adverse-event data and a confirmatory analysis with intention-to-treat and multiplicity control.

quotes.text: Our findings indicate that a dietary supplement based on sea ur -chin egg extract rich in Echinochrome A is an effective treatment option for long COVID patients
providing a safe and natural solution

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion calls the supplement 'effective' and 'safe', but the paper presents no safety or adverse-event data. The efficacy evidence is limited to per-protocol analysis, a borderline multivariate result, 3 of 5 non-significant EQ-5D dimensions, a cytokine analysis without an interaction test, and 7 unreported registered primaries.

issues.title: Paper's primary outcomes (EQ-5D, cytokines) differ from 8 registered primaries; 7 not reported
issues.explanation: The registry lists eight primary outcomes, including spirometry, 6-minute walk, depression and cognitive tests, none of which are reported. The paper instead calls quality of life (EQ-5D dimensions, VAS, TTO) and four cytokines its primary outcomes. A trial that does not report most of its registered primaries and highlights different ones cannot be read as confirmatory. The positive results shown may be a selected subset.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The registry history showing the registered primaries were changed before data collection, or a companion paper reporting the remaining registered outcomes.

quotes.text: The primary outcome variable was the improvement in patients' quality of life, analyzed on the basis of its 5 dimensions and 3 levels

second_reader.what_stands: Of the 8 registered primary outcomes, only EQ-VAS appears in the paper, and the other 7 are not reported. The paper's primary outcomes (EQ-5D dimensions, TTO, cytokines) are not registered as primary in the current record. The caveat is that earlier registry versions were not seen and cytokines may be a registered secondary.

issues.title: 46 analysed vs 100 planned (50 per group); borderline results called 'robust'
issues.explanation: Less than half the planned sample was analysed, and the main multivariate result is p = 0.048. Treating significance in a small sample as evidence of robustness is not justified. The sample-size calculation also does not correspond to the outcomes tested. Effect estimates here are therefore imprecise and likely inflated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Confidence intervals on effect sizes that exclude trivial benefits, or a replicated result in a larger sample.

quotes.text: Thus, a total of 50 patients per group will be included.
Considering that, despite the small sample size, the results were statistically significant and can be seen to be robust

second_reader.what_stands: Only 46 patients were analysed against 100 planned, and this shortfall is not stated as a deviation. The sample-size calculation assumed a one-tailed test. Describing the findings as 'robust' is not supported for the borderline ones (MANOVA p = 0.048, cytokines p = 0.038) in a small per-protocol analysis without multiplicity control, although pain and TTO (p = 0.005, 0.003) are not borderline.

issues.title: Cytokine 'significant' changes rest on a Treatment main effect; no Treatment x Time test, Time p = 0.71 and 0.30
issues.explanation: The text says three months of treatment significantly lowered IL-2 and raised IL-10. The two-way ANOVA contains only Treatment and Time main effects, and the Time effects are non-significant (IL-2 p = 0.7056, IL-10 p = 0.2977). The Treatment term averages baseline and final samples, so it cannot show an effect of the intervention. The ANOVA also treats repeated measures as independent. Its 78 observations are not 2 x 46 patients, which is unexplained. The IL-2 final means (90.03 vs 84) differ by only about 6 pg/ml with SDs of 11-15, which would be unlikely to be significant on its own.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported Treatment x Time interaction or within-group and final-visit comparisons showing significant IL-2 and IL-10 differences, with the analysis accounting for repeated measures.

quotes.text: decrease in IL-2 mean values (Placebo mean: 90.03
Two-way analysis of variance was used to compare Interleukin values between the basal and final conditions of each group

second_reader.what_stands: The only significant cytokine results (IL-2 and IL-10, both p = 0.0382) are Treatment main effects pooled over basal and final samples. No Treatment x Time test is reported, and the Time effects are non-significant (IL-2 p = 0.7056, IL-10 p = 0.2977). The model also treats repeated measures from the same patients as independent, so these results do not show a change over time attributable to treatment.

issues.title: Per-protocol analysis only: 4 of 50 dropouts excluded, no ITT or flow by arm
issues.explanation: Only complete data sets were analysed, and the 4 non-completers (8%) are not described by arm or reason. A per-protocol analysis of a randomised trial can favour the treatment if dropouts differ between arms. The loss is small, so this weakens rather than overturns the findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An intention-to-treat or sensitivity analysis giving the same results, plus dropout numbers by arm.

quotes.text: Accounting  for  the  lack  of  adherence,  the  Per  Protocol Analysis  (PP)  was  used.
Four of them did not finish the protocol.

issues.title: Trial registered 2022-08-19, about 11 months after study start (2021-09-22), during recruitment
issues.explanation: The registry shows first submission on 2022-08-19, nearly a year after the trial began, and the paper dates the registration 07/09/2022. The record therefore cannot independently confirm the outcomes that were planned before data were collected. This compounds the mismatch between registered and reported primary outcomes. It limits confidence rather than invalidating the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of an earlier registration or a protocol time-stamped before enrolment.

issues.title: 7 EQ-5D outcomes and 4 cytokines tested at alpha 0.05 with no correction
issues.explanation: No multiplicity correction is described. Some results, such as mobility (p = 0.013), IL-2 and IL-10 (p about 0.03-0.04), would not survive a Bonferroni correction. The omnibus MANOVA partly protects the EQ-5D tests, so this weakens secondary claims.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified hierarchy or correction showing the key results hold.

quotes.text: A p-value <0.05 was red statistically significant in all statistical tests.

issues.title: IL-10 Treatment p = 0.0382 duplicates IL-2's; F = 4.84 on (1,75) df implies p about 0.031; SS 82.12 probably 83.12
issues.explanation: IL-2 (F = 4.45) and IL-10 (F = 4.84) have the same df but are given the same p of 0.0382. For F(1,75) = 4.84 the p is about 0.031. The IL-10 Treatment sum of squares of 82.12 also does not fit the Model SS: 82.12 + 18.89 = 101.01, while Model SS is 102.011. A value of 83.12 would reconcile Model SS, F and the Error mean square. The IL-10 result stays significant, but the table contains several transcription errors.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source statistical output showing p = 0.0382 for both rows.

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.0382, but recomputed from the printed f = 4.84 p is at most 0.03097, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show. This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Baseline MANOVA F printed as 1.552 in text but 1.52 in Table 2 (Pillai 0.222, df 7, 38)
issues.explanation: The text and Table 2 give different F values for the same baseline MANOVA. For a two-group MANOVA, F = V/(1-V) x errordf/hypdf, which gives about 1.55 and matches the text. The table cell therefore looks mistyped. The baseline test remains non-significant either way, so no conclusion changes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A source dataset or output showing F = 1.52 for these Pillai and df values.

issues.title: Table 3 totals do not add: IL-2 Error SS 1075.43 (about 10705 implied); TNF-α Total 60.66 vs 62.66

For TNF-α, Error + Model is 62.66 but Total is 60.66. These are typographical slips that do not change the F tests, but they show the table was not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source output showing Error SS 1075.43 together with Error MS 142.74.

10.26766/pmgp.v10i1.546.headline_claim: The remote medical and psychological rehabilitation program is effective for anxiety and depressive post-COVID disorders in wartime Ukraine, with benefits sustained three months after completion and prevention of PTSD chronification.
10.26766/pmgp.v10i1.546.overall: The direction of the reported group differences is large and consistent across scales, but the design (undescribed comparison arm, no reported randomization method, blinding, registration or primary outcome, self-report scales) supports only a tentative efficacy conclusion. Two headline percentages are printed wrong (PHQ-9 84.3% should be 94.3%; the SSS-8 39.0%/37.3% pair is swapped) and repeated in the Abstract and Conclusions. The claim of preventing PTSD chronification is not supported by the data presented.

primary_outcome.name: AD-7 anxiety score (presumed primary; the paper does not label a primary outcome)

issues.title: Undescribed comparison arm, no blinding or randomization detail, self-report outcomes, very large between-group effects
issues.explanation: The comparison group is mentioned only as having 'self-directed' adaptation, and the paper does not say what care or contact it got. Randomization method, allocation concealment, blinding and a pre-specified primary outcome are not reported. With self-reported scales and no attention-matched control, the huge between-group differences (e.g. AD-7 1.1 vs 13.1) cannot be attributed to the program itself with confidence. Baseline (Day 1) group data are also not presented, so the comparability of arms cannot be judged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial protocol or earlier report (e.g. the cited Burdeinyi 2024 paper) documenting concealed randomization, outcome-assessor blinding and an attention-matched or standardized comparison condition.

quotes.text: що було рандомізовано на групу дослідження (n=122) та групу порівняння (n=118)
звертаючи увагу на адаптаційні процеси та самостійні підходи до вирішення власного психоемоційного стану

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not say what the comparison arm received, and it gives no randomization method, allocation concealment or blinding. Every outcome (GAD-7, PHQ-9, SSS-8, PCL-5, CQLS) is a self-report questionnaire, and the Day 153 between-group effects are very large (d about 2.2 to 3.5). The reported figures are internally consistent, but the design details needed to judge bias are missing from this paper, and part of them may sit in the cited earlier paper.

issues.title: 'High efficacy in preventing chronification' of PTSD rests on 44→47 of 118 and a mean-score t-test, with no baseline for study arm
issues.explanation: The Conclusions link the 44→47 change in the comparison arm to a p<0.001 and to a preventive effect. The p-value belongs to a Day 153 between-group PCL-5 score comparison, and the comparison arm barely changed (44/118 = 37.3% to 47/118 = 39.8%). The study was not designed or powered to show prevention, and it has no concealed or blinded design. The conclusion therefore overreaches what the data show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specified PTSD prevention outcome with baseline PCL-5 caseness for both arms and a between-group test of incidence or change in caseness.

quotes.text: Це вказує на високу ефективність програми у запобіганні хроніфікації посттравматичних станів
кількість учасників із симптомами ПТСР зросла з 44 до 47 осіб

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions' 'high efficacy in preventing chronification' is supported by the between-arm contrast at Day 153 (0 versus 47 of 118) and the mean-score tests, not by the 44→47 change, which is a 3-person shift in the comparison arm. The attached p<0.001 is from a mean-score t-test, and the study arm's baseline and Day 63 symptomatic counts are not printed in the text. 'Preventing' chronification is also a stronger word than the data show, because participants had post-COVID disorders and some were already symptomatic. It would be wrong to say no baseline was analysed, since Table 6 uses Day

issues.title: PHQ-9 minimal depression: 115/122 is 94.3%, but 84.3% is printed in Results, Abstract and Conclusions
issues.explanation: The Results give 115 of the 122 study-group participants with minimal depression, and 7 with mild depression (5.7%). Those two counts exhaust the group, and 115/122 is 94.3%, not the 84.3% printed. The wrong figure is repeated in the Abstract and Conclusions. The headline depression result is therefore understated, and the figure is inconsistent with the paper's own counts.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the true count of minimal-depression participants is about 103 and 115 is the typo, but then the counts would not sum to 122.

quotes.text: у 115 учасників (84.3%) мінімальні прояви депресії
Regarding depression, 84.3% of the study group had minimal symptoms

script.explanation: 115/122 = 94.26%, but the paper prints 84.3, outside the rounding interval [84.25, 84.40]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 136.4 rather than 122.

issues.title: SSS-8 comparison group: 44 (moderate) printed as 39.0% and 46 (high) as 37.3%; n=118 gives 37.3% and 39.0%
issues.explanation: The percentages for moderate and high somatic-symptom intensity are attached to the wrong counts. The error is repeated in the Abstract and Conclusions as '39.0% moderate and 37.3% high'. The direction of the group difference is unaffected, but the figures reported as headline results are inconsistent with the stated counts.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the counts, not the percentages, are the printed errors would change which numbers to correct but not the inconsistency. Nothing short of a corrected table removes it.

quotes.text: у 44 учасників (39.0%) середній ступінь та у 46 учасників (37.3%) високий ступінь

issues.title: No trial registration, protocol identifier, primary outcome or sample-size justification reported for a randomized study
issues.explanation: The paper describes randomized enrolment into two arms and an intervention period, yet gives no registry identifier and no pre-specification of a primary outcome. It reports five outcomes with no multiplicity handling and no sample-size calculation. Readers cannot verify that the reported scales are the pre-planned ones.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment (October 2022) listing these outcomes.

10.26766/pmgp.v9i3.526.headline_claim: A remote medical and psychological rehabilitation program significantly reduced depression and anxiety symptoms in post-COVID patients compared with standard treatment after 63 days.
10.26766/pmgp.v9i3.526.overall: The paper shows very large between-group falls in self-rated PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, and the recomputed day-63 t-statistics agree with the printed ones. However, it is an open-label trial against an unspecified usual-care control with no limitations stated, no registration, and a completers-only analysis. The effect direction is credible, but its size and the unqualified claim of effectiveness are not well supported. Several printing errors (withdrawal total, Table 3 and Table 1 values) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: PHQ-9 depression score at day 63 (AD-7 anxiety score analysed in parallel)

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-rated PHQ-9/GAD-7 outcomes, unspecified usual-care control, and unqualified efficacy claims
issues.explanation: Participants knew their allocation and rated their own symptoms, and the comparator was unspecified 'standard treatment' with no matched contact. The 8-9 point drop in the intervention arm with almost no change in controls may partly reflect expectancy, attention and reporting effects. Allocation concealment is not described, there is no limitations section, and the conclusion states effectiveness and 'evidentiary strength' as settled. The direction of benefit is plausible, but the size and certainty are not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Blinded or objective outcome assessment, or an attention-matched control showing a similar difference.

quotes.text: паралельне рандомізоване несліпе контрольоване дослідження з двома групами
Шкала заповнюється самим пацієнтом за 1-2 хвилини
Такі значні зміни в стані психічного здоров'я учасників досліджуваної групи підкреслюють важливість та доказовість проведення інтервенцій

second_reader.what_stands: The trial is explicitly open-label, both primary outcomes are patient self-rated with no blinded or clinician-rated outcome, and the control arm ('звичайне/стандартне лікування') is never specified or matched for contact. The Conclusion then states effectiveness and 'доказовість' without discussing blinding, self-report or control-condition limitations.

issues.title: Completers-only analysis: 8 of 248 randomised (2 intervention, 6 control) dropped; no ITT, 'no missing data' stated
issues.explanation: Eight randomised participants (3.2%) withdrew, unevenly across arms, yet statistics were run on 240 completers and the paper says no missing data were found. No intention-to-treat or sensitivity analysis is reported, so the effect of removing the withdrawals is unknown. Given the large observed effect the attrition is unlikely to reverse it, but the analysis does not follow the randomised groups.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ITT analysis or sensitivity analysis showing the same effect with withdrawals imputed.

quotes.text: Розрахунок статистичних даних відбувався в умовах 240 учасників

issues.title: Table 1 χ² column holds the p-values, and baseline age t=0.084 does not fit its p=0.744 (recomputed t≈0.33)

issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors' software output showing these statistics under a different test definition.

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

issues.title: PHQ-9 Time SS printed as 4771 (copied from GAD-7); its F=378.9 implies about 3125

issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors' ANOVA output showing a PHQ-9 Time SS of 4771 with a different error df.

issues.title: Control-group day-63 PHQ-9 categories sum to 126, not 118: '28 (17%)' should be 20

issues.title: Employed:unemployed ratio printed 1:0.96 but 175 and 65 give 1:0.37

issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different definition of the ratio that yields 0.96 from these counts; none is apparent.

quotes.text: 175 осіб (72.9%), а 65 осіб (27.1%) є непрацюючими, що відповідає співвідношенню 1:0.96

script.explanation: ratio: 65 / 175 gives 0.371429, not the printed 0.96. For the printed value to hold the denominator would have to be 67.7083, not 175.

10.26766/pmgp.v9i4.545.headline_claim: A remotely delivered medical and psychological rehabilitation program is effective in reducing PTSD symptoms (PCL-5) in patients with post-COVID anxiety and depressive disorders during the war in Ukraine, with effects persisting three months after the program.
10.26766/pmgp.v9i4.545.overall: The direction of the finding, that self-reported PTSD symptoms improve more with the programme than with waitlist/usual care, is probably real. Its size, durability and implementation-ready status are overstated, because the trial is open-label, unregistered, completer-analysed, has only 3-month follow-up and has no discussion of limitations. The reported statistics are internally consistent on recalculation.

primary_outcome.name: PCL-5 total score (PTSD symptoms)

issues.title: Open-label trial with self-reported PCL-5 primary outcome; effects of 15-21 points not protected from expectation bias
issues.explanation: The trial is open-label and every outcome (PCL-5, PHQ-9, GAD-7) is self-reported. The control group knew it was on a waitlist, which can inflate the contrast. The reported effects are very large, with t above 10, and the paper never mentions this bias. The direction of improvement is probably real, but its size is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Assessors blinded to allocation, or a clinician-rated or objective primary outcome confirming the self-report effect.

quotes.text: паралельне рандомізоване відкрите контрольоване дослідження

second_reader.what_stands: The trial is explicitly open-label, the PCL-5 is self-reported, and no blinded assessment is described, so the 15.9 and 20.9 point between-group differences are not protected from expectation or reporting bias; this part stands. The paper never labels PCL-5 formally as a pre-specified primary outcome and does not itself discuss expectation bias, so those wording elements are the reviewer's characterisation.

issues.title: 'High effectiveness' and clinical-practice recommendation from one unregistered open-label trial with no limitations section
issues.explanation: The Conclusions recommend wider clinical use and describe 'high effectiveness'. The evidence is one open-label, self-reported, waitlist-controlled trial with no registration. It analyses only completers, 240 of 248 (3.2% lost), and mixes patients above and below the PTSD cut-off. No limitation is discussed. The results support a promising effect on self-reported symptoms, not a confident implementation recommendation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A limitations discussion and tempered wording, or confirmatory blinded and registered replication.

quotes.text: показало високу ефективність та може бути рекомендоване для подальшого впровадження у клінічну практику

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions call the programme highly effective and recommend clinical implementation, based on one single-site, open-label, self-reported-outcome trial analysed on completers, with no limitations section in the text supplied and no trial registration number given. Whether the trial is registered cannot be verified here as no registry record was supplied, but the paper itself reports no registration and does not caveat its recommendation.

issues.title: All 240 called 'clinically confirmed PTSD' but only 111 (46%) reach the PCL-5 cut-off of 33 at day 1
issues.explanation: The Results say all 240 analysed participants had clinically confirmed PTSD. The same section reports that only 57 of 122 and 54 of 118 met the PCL-5 threshold of 33 or more. The baseline mean PCL-5 is about 30, below that threshold. The sample is therefore a mixed anxiety/depression cohort in which fewer than half had probable PTSD. The PTSD-treatment framing and the mean-score comparisons overstate how many participants had the target condition.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that all participants met DSM-5 PTSD criteria on clinical interview, together with an explanation of why many scored below the PCL-5 cut-off.

quotes.text: усі 240 учасників дослідження у яких був клінічно підтверджений ПТСР
у 57 з 122 учасників з групи дослідження та у 54 з 118 учасників групи контролю наявний симптоматичний комплекс посттравматичного стресу

issues.title: Waitlist/usual-care control lacks an attention-matched comparator
issues.explanation: The control arm received standard treatment and was waitlisted, so contact time, expectation and engagement all differ between arms. The paper presents the gap as due to the programme's methods. This limits conclusions about mechanism and specificity, though not the conclusion about superiority to no added care. The point overlaps with the open-label concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An attention-control arm, or an explicit framing of the claim as superiority over waitlist only.

quotes.text: що отримувала стандартне лікування, а також були внесені у лист очікування

issues.title: No trial registration, pre-specified primary outcome or sample-size calculation reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomised trial but gives no registry identifier and does not name a primary outcome. It also gives no sample-size calculation or randomisation method. Outcome selection and analysis choices cannot be checked against a prior plan. This weakens confidence in the reported effects but does not show any specific discrepancy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment with the same primary outcome.

quotes.text: З жовтня 2022 року по грудень 2023 року було проведено паралельне рандомізоване відкрите контрольоване дослідження

issues.title: 'Long-term' effect claimed from a single assessment 3 months after the programme ends
issues.explanation: The only post-intervention assessment is at day 153, three months after the programme. The Conclusions call this a 'long-term' effect and speak of stability. Three months supports persistence in the short to medium term only. The follow-up also has no reported attrition and no intention-to-treat handling.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up data at 6-12 months, or rewording the claim as 'persisting at 3 months'.

quotes.text: що свідчить про довготривалу дію застосованих методів

issues.title: Day-63 residual PTSD count: 5 'out of 57' (Abstract) versus 5 'of 122' (Results)
issues.explanation: The abstract puts 5 against the 57 baseline cases, and the Results put the same 5 against the 122 group members. The denominators differ in definition but are mutually consistent. The abstract's phrase 'reduced in 5' misdescribes a fall to 5. This is a wording ambiguity with no effect on the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Clarifying that 57 is the baseline case count and that 5 is the day-63 count.

quotes.text: the PTSD symptom complex reduced in 5 out of 57 participants
де у 5 учасників з 122 зберігся симптоматичний комплекс посттравматичного стресу

10.28920/dhm55.2.104-113.headline_claim: Ten sessions of hyperoxia at varied pressures and oxygen fractions produced no significant between-group difference in Long COVID symptoms or cognition; the null hypothesis cannot be rejected, and claims of HBOT benefit need further verification.
10.28920/dhm55.2.104-113.overall: The null finding (no significant difference between the four oxygen and pressure conditions) is reasonably supported as an absence of detected effect, but the power calculation assumed an implausibly small SD, so a modest benefit cannot be excluded. The numeric slips (patient counts, two percentages, a mis-described VAS result) are minor, while the uncorrected within-group tests and the placebo conclusion about another trial are over-reads that should not be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: Power calculation assumes 10% effect with 5% SD (d≈2), unrealistic against spread seen in Table 2
issues.explanation: The target of 18 per group was reached, but it rests on an effect of 10% with an SD of 5% taken from a 10-patient case series. The observed percent-of-baseline values vary far more than that (for example DSB 115 to 134 and VAS 82 to 105). With realistic variability, four groups of 21 to 29 could easily miss a moderate real effect. The conclusion that 'the null hypothesis cannot be rejected' is correct as worded, but this study cannot exclude clinically useful effects. It also cannot support strong statements that the effect is nil.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Observed SDs of the percent-of-baseline outcomes close to 5%, or a post hoc power or equivalence analysis for a smaller effect.

quotes.text: we assumed an a priori effect size of 10% in the measured parameters, with a standard deviation of 5% in both groups

second_reader.what_stands: The stated assumptions (10% effect, 5% SD) do imply d=2, which is very large for subjective and cognitive outcomes and was based on a 10-patient uncontrolled series. Those assumptions would also require only about 7 per group, not the stated 18, so the paper's n=18 and its stated inputs are not consistent with each other. The claim that this is unrealistic against the spread in Table 2 cannot be checked, because Table 2 contains no SDs; the only evidence of spread is the text statement that responses were highly variable.

issues.title: Conclusion attributes another trial's gains to placebo though this trial tested only 10 sessions
issues.explanation: The Conclusions state that the modest improvements in the Zilberman 40-session trial 'may very well have been due to a placebo effect'. This study used 10 sessions and measured no matching outcomes in a comparable design. It also had no true no-treatment arm, so it cannot separate placebo from natural course or regression to the mean. Its non-significant result, from a study with questionable power, cannot show that a longer course was ineffective.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data from this trial on a 40-session arm, or a placebo-controlled analysis of the long course.

quotes.text: our results suggest that the overall very modest clinical improvements reported in that study may very well have been due to a placebo effect

issues.title: Pressure condition confounded with treatment chamber; patients self-selected treatment periods
issues.explanation: Groups A and B were treated in one chamber and groups C and D in another, so pressure and chamber are not separable. The text says 'the only variable ... was the actual treatment chamber', which describes the confounding. Different group sizes (29, 29, 22, 21) are in line with chamber or period capacity. Because the main result is null, this adds uncertainty rather than creating a false effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation that participants were randomised to chambers within the same sessions and staffing.

quotes.text: Thus, the only variable in the treatment schedule was the actual treatment chamber.

issues.title: Text calls all bold changes 'significantly improved' but VAS in group B (81.67, **) is a worsening
issues.explanation: The Results say that the scores marked in bold were significantly improved. Table 2 marks VAS in group B (40% O2 at 253 kPa) as 81.67 with P < 0.01. By the Methods, VAS above 100 means improvement, so this is a significant deterioration of about 18% from baseline. The other starred cells (EQ-5D group D, C19-YRSm group A, MathProc group A) are improvements. The description is therefore wrong for one result. It also shows the within-group tests pick up changes in both directions, consistent with noise.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence the table value was printed inverted, for example a raw VAS score of 122 rather than 81.67.

quotes.text: some of the scores (marked in bold in Table 2) being significantly improved after the study treatment
score higher than 100 means improvement

issues.title: Completers-only analysis (101 of 120 scheduled); unequal arms 29/29/22/21 and no ITT analysis
issues.explanation: The analysis uses the 101 completers. Of the 19 not analysed, 11 were never included, 4 dropped out for unrelated reasons and 4 left because of barotrauma. No ITT or sensitivity analysis is reported. Arms C and D (the 1 atm groups) ended up smaller than A and B, which is odd for 1:1 allocation and not explained. Because the main result is null, completers-only analysis is unlikely to hide an effect, but the bias is hard to assess.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing the 11 non-included patients were never randomised, plus an ITT or sensitivity analysis giving the same null result.

quotes.text: After randomisation, 120 patients were scheduled to start, but 11 could not be included because of time constraints or logistic difficulties
Four patients dropped out because of middle ear barotrauma, two in the 2.5 ATA pressure groups (A and B)

issues.title: About 36 uncorrected within-group one-sample tests; 4 starred results highlighted despite null between-group test
issues.explanation: The authors tested percent-of-baseline change within each group with one-sample t-tests and marked the significant ones in bold. With 9 outcomes in 4 groups and no correction, a few chance significances are expected. They are discussed as partly explained by subgroup or symptom clusters. The between-group conclusion (no difference) is not affected. The bold cells should not be read as evidence of benefit from any oxygen dose, and the Results wording leans toward doing so.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Within-group p values surviving a Bonferroni or Holm correction across the 36 tests.

quotes.text: Statistical significance was then assessed by means of a one-sample t -test.
Even though some groups showed a significant effect on some scores and tests

issues.title: Military (35) plus civilian (68) = 103 patients, but 101 completed; civilian count should be 66
issues.explanation: The Results give 35 military and 68 civilian patients, which sums to 103. The paper says 101 patients completed, and Table 1 group sizes (29+29+22+21) also sum to 101. The civilian denominator is therefore wrong or undefined, and the percentages built on it (41.2%, 30.9%) are slightly off. The male counts also differ: 31+21 = 52 in the text against 10+15+13+13 = 51 in Table 1. This is a minor reporting error with no bearing on the main comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 68 civilians include non-completers, or a corrected analysis set showing 66 civilians.

quotes.text: as opposed to 28 of 68 (41.2%) civilian patients.
In total, 101 patients completed the study

issues.title: Results describe symptom-cluster 'improvement' patterns by pressure level without any supporting test
issues.explanation: Table 3 shows mean improvement points by symptom cluster with all differences non-significant, yet the Results describe pulmonary, systemic and neurocognitive 'patterns' by dose. The Discussion then offers physiological explanations for them. The authors also state clearly that the analysis does not support subgroup conclusions. The cautionary wording limits the harm, and it does not alter the overall null conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal interaction test showing a symptom-cluster by treatment effect.

quotes.text: patients with systemic symptoms had an improvement with either 101.3 kPa (1 atm abs) or 253 kPa (2.5 atm abs) oxygen rather than 21 kPa (0.21 atm) oxygen
statistical significance not reached due to small numbers

issues.title: No trial registration number and no prespecified primary outcome reported for a randomised trial
issues.explanation: The Methods give an ethics committee number and approval date but no registry identifier. The paper also defines no single primary outcome among about ten measures. Registration and prespecification therefore cannot be checked, which limits how far the outcome selection can be trusted. This matters less than usual because the main result is null.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment that names the outcomes.

quotes.text: The research protocol was approved by the Hospital Ethics Committee of the University Hospital Brugmann, Brussels (B0772022000037) on 12 April 2022.

issues.title: Group B 'happy to have participated' 9/29 (31%) sits oddly with 77-86% elsewhere and with the narrative
issues.explanation: Table 4 gives 'happy to have participated' as 86%, 31%, 77% and 86% across the four groups. Group B at 31% is an outlier, even though 76% of that group would pay for more treatment. The text describes participants in each group as glad to have participated without noting this. Either the cell is a misprint or the text glosses over a large difference. The effect on the conclusions is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The raw questionnaire data showing 9/29 is correct and that the text is meant only as 'some patients in each group'.

quotes.location: Table 4, 'Happy to have participated', Group B

quotes.text: were glad to have participated and would be willing to pay for further treatment

issues.title: Group A 'condition similar at 3 months' 18/29 printed as 67%; 18/29 is 62%
issues.explanation: 18/29 equals 62.1%, not 67%. The printed 67% fits 18/27, which would imply a follow-up denominator that the table does not state. The other cells in this row use the allocated group n. This is one reporting error in a secondary patient-reported follow-up item, and it does not change the null between-group finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that only 27 group A patients answered at 3 months.

quotes.location: Table 4, 'Condition at three months similar' row, Group A

script.explanation: 18/29 = 62.07%, but the paper prints 67, outside the rounding interval [66.50, 68.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 26.9 rather than 29.

issues.title: Group C male sex 13/22 printed as 58%; 13/22 is 59.1%
issues.explanation: 13/22 equals 59.1%, which rounds or truncates to 59%, not 58%. This is a one-point slip in a baseline characteristic that is compared as 'ns' across groups. It has no effect on any outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing a different male count (for example 12.8/22 is impossible, so a changed count or denominator).

script.explanation: 13/22 = 59.09%, but the paper prints 58, outside the rounding interval [57.50, 59.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 22.4 rather than 22.

10.29001/2073-8552-2023-655.headline_claim: A consensus feature-subset method (ReliefF, chi-squared and mRMR filters with NSGA-II search, scored by Kendall's W) identifies eight features that the authors describe as most important for predicting a 15% or greater improvement in the six-minute walk test after post-COVID rehabilitation; the authors call the linear SVM models preliminary.
10.29001/2073-8552-2023-655.overall: The paper is a methods demonstration, and its headline claim that the 8-feature set is of greatest prognostic importance is stronger than the evidence supports. Features were selected on all 64 patients before cross-validation, the best set was picked on the same test folds, and there is no external validation. The result should be read as a hypothesis-generating feature ranking, not a validated prognostic finding.

primary_outcome.name: Improvement of at least 15% in six-minute walk test result (binary classification label)

issues.title: Feature subsets chosen on all 64 patients before 5-fold CV, so reported test accuracy (77.9%) is optimistic
issues.explanation: The filters (which use the outcome label) and the genetic search ran on the full dataset, and the classifier was then cross-validated on the resulting fixed subsets. Test folds therefore influenced which features were chosen, so the accuracy is not a clean held-out estimate. The 8-feature set was also picked as best among seven candidate sets on the same test folds, adding selection optimism. The 'most important features' claim rests on this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that filter ranking and NSGA2 search were repeated inside each training fold, or evaluation on an independent held-out cohort.

quotes.text: Все эксперименты проведены по схеме пятикратной кросс-валидации
полученные на предыдущем этапе работы с помощью авторского метода нахождения согласованного

second_reader.what_stands: The paper's own description (fixed subsets found before CV on the whole dataset, using label-dependent filters) indicates selection leakage into the CV test folds, so 77.9% is probably optimistic. The paper does not state outright that selection used all 64 patients, and the size of the bias cannot be computed from the paper. The test accuracy was not an unbiased estimate, and the authors' remark that the small train-test gap shows 'no overfitting' does not address this kind of leakage.

issues.title: Abstract concludes the 8 features are of 'greatest importance' for prognosis from 64 patients and ≤78% accuracy
issues.explanation: The conclusion states the method identified the features most important for predicting rehabilitation effectiveness. The evidence is agreement among three filters (K=1) and a cross-validated accuracy no higher than 78% on one small sample (64 patients, 58 candidate features, no sample-size calculation or external validation). Agreement among filters is not evidence of prognostic importance, and the claim is stronger than a methods demonstration with preliminary models supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Validation of the selected features in an independent cohort, or stability analysis showing the same subset is recovered under resampling.

quotes.text: Хотя точность прогноза не превышает 78%
имеющие наибольшую важность для прогноза эффективности реабилитации
набор данных из 58 признаков, включающих анамнез пациентов

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract conclusion wording is stronger than the evidence: 64 patients, 58 candidate features, one CV scheme with probable selection leakage (see i1) and accuracy of at most 78% with no uncertainty interval. The paper does present the model as preliminary in the body, and its main claim is about a selection method, so the overstatement is mostly limited to the abstract's 'greatest importance' sentence. The paper does not test whether the 8 features are more predictive than other subsets, only that they are the most concordant among the filters.

10.29011/2577-1515.100182.headline_claim: A blend of Lactobacillus probiotics and inulin prebiotic 'strongly suggests' enhanced recovery from Covid-19, particularly for individuals with symptoms or conditions suggestive of poor gut health, and was safe and well tolerated.
10.29011/2577-1515.100182.overall: The data show that symptoms improved over 30 days in an uncontrolled, open-label cohort, but the design cannot show that the supplement caused that improvement. The Conclusion 'strongly suggests' enhanced recovery and the safety statement go beyond what a single-arm study analysing only completers can support. Tables 1, 2 and 5 contain several numerical inconsistencies (group sizes, CIs, p-values, mean differences, effect sizes, a direction mismatch in the subgroup text), and the subgroup conclusions rest on uncorrected tests.

primary_outcome.name: Mean cough, fatigue and subjective well-being symptom scores at day 1 and day 30

issues.title: Uncontrolled single-arm before-after design used to conclude the supplement 'enhances recovery'
issues.explanation: Everyone received the supplement and symptoms were compared only between day 1 and day 30. No control group is present, so the paired t-tests show change over time, not an effect of the supplement. The authors concede the design is weak but the Conclusion says the study 'strongly suggests' the supplement enhances recovery and was safe and well tolerated. The data show improvement in symptoms over 30 days; they do not show it was caused by the probiotic.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparison with a concurrent or matched untreated group showing a larger improvement in treated participants.

quotes.text: it became clear that participants would buy their own probiotics
the trials committee decided to provide the probiotic to all participants
this study strongly suggests that this specific probiotic supplement

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm before-after design with no control group, so the day 1 to day 30 changes cannot be attributed to the supplement. The Discussion acknowledges the lack of randomisation, but the Conclusion still says the study 'strongly suggests' the supplement 'enhances recovery', which goes beyond what an uncontrolled design can show. The authors' argument that chronic-phase improvement was unlikely to occur spontaneously is reasonable but untested, and it does not cover the early-phase group, where improvement was expected anyway.

issues.title: Chronic-phase group is n=86 in Methods but n=96 in Table 2 (40+96=136, not 126)
issues.explanation: Methods split the 126 participants into 40 early and 86 chronic. The Table 2 header labels the chronic cohort n=96, and the chronic t-tests use 95 df, which fits 96 pairs. With 40 early participants this implies 136 people, so either the table or the Methods is wrong, or some participants were counted twice. The analysed population for the chronic subgroup is therefore unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 10 participants were counted in both subgroups, or a corrected Table 2 header and df.

quotes.text: 86 (68%) in a Chronic Phase
Chronic Covid cohort (n=96)

issues.title: Identical means and SDs repeated across different Table 5 subgroups (ethnic/BMI wellbeing; BMI fatigue/GI wellbeing)
issues.explanation: Wellbeing change in the ethnic subgroup (4.2 ± 10.3 vs 3.8 ± 7.5) reappears in the BMI subgroup with minus signs. BMI fatigue (2.7 ± 10.1 vs 4.7 ± 9.3) matches the new-GI wellbeing row exactly. The groups differ in size and composition, so identical means and SDs are implausible. At least some Table 5 rows appear to have been copied or mis-pasted, which undermines confidence in the subgroup table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing these subgroups genuinely share these summary values.

quotes.location: Table 5, Ethnic group, subjective wellbeing row
Table 5, BMI subgroup, subjective wellbeing row
Table 5, BMI fatigue row and New GI symptoms wellbeing row

issues.title: Mean-difference column in Tables 1 and 2 disagrees with the printed means and CIs in four cells
issues.explanation: The early-phase fatigue difference is printed 4.70 but the means give 5.75, and the CI midpoint (5.745) agrees with 5.75. The chronic fatigue difference is also printed 4.70 while means and CI give 4.48. Wellbeing differences are printed 4.11 (all) and 3.23 (chronic) but the means give 4.33 and 3.52. The early and chronic fatigue values being identical suggests a copying error. The changes are small relative to the effects, but the table column is unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Unrounded source data showing the printed differences are the true paired means with a different n per timepoint.

issues.title: Analysis restricted to those who took capsules for at least one month; no flow of recruited vs analysed
issues.explanation: Only participants given the capsule for at least one month were included, but the number recruited, lost or discontinued is not given. Selecting on completion can overstate benefit and understate adverse events, since people who stopped early are the most likely to have had problems or no benefit. The paper reports two discontinuations for bloating, yet the safety conclusion is drawn from an analysed set defined by continued use.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant flow showing everyone who started was analysed, with the reason for any exclusions.

quotes.text: For this analysis, we only included participants who were given a capsule containing a 5 species Lactobacillus probiotic blend
Only two patients discontinued their capsules because of an increase in bloating

issues.title: About 24 subgroup tests at p<0.05 without correction; Discussion explains the 'findings'
issues.explanation: Eight subgroup comparisons across three outcomes are tested at an uncorrected alpha of 0.05. The Results list six subgroups as having 'statistically greater benefit for one or more' outcomes, and the Discussion offers mechanisms for them. With this many tests, some p<0.05 results are expected by chance, and several are marginal (p=0.04). The subgroup conclusions should be treated as hypothesis-generating at most.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified correction or interaction tests showing these subgroup differences survive adjustment.

quotes.text: those previously hospitalised, no prior indigestion, new or worse GI symptoms at trial entry had a statistically greater benefit for one or more measurable outcomes
Males had statistically significantly better benefit to the intervention than females

issues.title: Reported Cohen's d for fatigue and wellbeing (1.36, 1.10) are about twice the printed mean change divided by SD
issues.explanation: The text calls fatigue and wellbeing improvements 'large' with d=1.36 and d=1.10. The printed mean differences and SDs give about 0.69 and 0.45. The same holds in the subgroup text (fatigue d=1.8 early, 1.3 chronic vs about 0.68 and 0.69 from the table). The cough d (0.48) matches its inputs, so the other values are inconsistent. The 'large magnitude' wording overstates the size of change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alternative d formula (for example one using a different SD) that reproduces 1.36 and 1.10 from the data.

issues.title: Table 5 CIs often do not contain their own estimates (e.g. fatigue 3.2 with CI -0.6 to 0.5)
issues.explanation: For male vs female fatigue the difference is 3.2 but the printed CI is -0.6 to 0.5, which excludes the estimate. The wellbeing row prints 2.7 (0.6 to 5.6) with p=0.10. The lower bound should presumably be -0.6, since a CI excluding zero is incompatible with p=0.10. Several other rows have the same problem: age cough 0.3 (0.9 to 0.4), age fatigue 4.8 (7.2 to 2.5) and exercise wellbeing 5.3 (-9.7 to -0.9). The CI column cannot be relied on to interpret the subgroup results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The source table showing correct CI values, with only a conversion error in this copy.

quotes.location: Table 5, Gender subgroup, subjective wellbeing row

issues.title: New-GI-symptom fatigue difference 1.2 (CI -1.5 to 3.8) is printed with p=0.01; recomputed p ≈ 0.36
issues.explanation: The CI spans zero, so p cannot be 0.01. Recomputing from the printed group means, SDs and sizes gives p of about 0.36. This row is one of the grounds on which the text claims greater benefit in people with new GI symptoms, so that claim rests on a mis-printed p-value.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing a real between-group difference of this size with a narrower CI.

quotes.location: Table 5, New GI symptoms at baseline, fatigue row

quotes.text: New GI symptoms at baseline Yes (41) vs No (85)

issues.title: Subgroup Results text names the wrong direction for age, exercise and indigestion vs Table 5
issues.explanation: The subgroup Results say those <60, those exercising >3 h/week and those with no prior indigestion benefited more. Table 5 shows larger improvements in the over-60s (fatigue 6.4 vs 1.6), the <3 h/week group (fatigue 7.6 vs 4.1) and the prior-indigestion group (fatigue 9.4 vs 4.4). The Discussion states the older and less active benefited more, contradicting the Results. A reader cannot tell from the text which subgroups are claimed to benefit more.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction showing the Results sentence refers to something other than the Table 5 change scores.

quotes.text: it appeared that males, those <60 years, those exercising more than 3 hours a week
benefit from this intervention was greater in the older participants and those who exercised less

issues.title: BMI subgroup sizes differ: Methods 47/79 vs Table 5 46/80
issues.explanation: The Methods give 47 normal-weight and 79 overweight/obese participants. The Table 5 BMI header gives 46 and 80. Both sum to 126, so one participant is classified differently, or a header was copied from the hospitalised row. The effect on results is small but the group sizes cannot both be right.

10.29081/gsjesh.2024.25.2.7.headline_claim: An individualized kinesiotherapy/respiratory rehabilitation program of about 8 weeks improves respiratory function, mobility (TUG) and quality of life in patients with long-lasting COVID-19, with the authors concluding that respiratory therapy with long-term exercise can improve quality of life.
10.29081/gsjesh.2024.25.2.7.overall: The TUG and VEMS interaction effects are reported with internally coherent ANOVA statistics, and the Table 1 data support the text, so the exercise group probably improved more on these two measures in this small pilot. The paper's stated conclusion on quality of life is not supported by any measured outcome. Randomisation details, baseline VEMS imbalance, absent blinding and unreported secondary outcomes make the effect sizes tentative, and Table 2 has swapped group labels.

primary_outcome.name: not specified; TUG and spirometry VEMS analysed as primary outcomes

issues.title: Conclusion that therapy improves quality of life rests on no quality-of-life measurement (pilot, n = 24)
issues.explanation: The stated conclusion is that the therapy can improve quality of life, yet only TUG and VEMS results are presented, and no quality-of-life or mood data appear. The sample is 12 per arm with no power calculation, and the paper itself calls the work a pilot. The functional findings may be real, but the headline quality-of-life claim is not supported by the data shown.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported quality-of-life data from a validated instrument showing between-group improvement.

quotes.text: The conclusion of the study is that respiratory therapy, along with long-term exercise therapy, can improve the patient's quality of life.
This  pilot  study  provides  us  with  disease  correlations,  health  implications, and  rehabilitation  methods

second_reader.what_stands: The paper reports no quality-of-life measurement; only TUG time and VEMS results are presented. The conclusion that therapy 'can improve the patient's quality of life' is therefore an inference from functional and spirometric outcomes and from cited literature, not from data collected here. The Methods also list anxiety, depression and symptom measures, but no results for them are shown. The paper does label the study a pilot with n = 24, but it states the quality-of-life conclusion without qualification.

issues.title: Control arm is an undescribed no-treatment group; no attention control and no blinding reported
issues.explanation: A concurrent control group exists and the interaction tests compare groups. However, the paper never says what controls received, and the intervention arm also got supervised contact. No blinding of assessors or patients is described. Effects on TUG and VEMS may therefore partly reflect attention, expectation or assessor knowledge rather than the exercises alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that assessors were blinded and that controls received matched supervised contact.

issues.title: Randomisation method and concealment not described; baseline VEMS differs 3.21 vs 2.61 L between arms
issues.explanation: The paper states only that patients were randomly divided, with no method or concealment. The groups differ at baseline in VEMS by about 0.6 L, and the authors admit the starting contexts differ. With 12 per arm, this imbalance (and possible regression to the mean in the lower-baseline group) weakens the VEMS between-group result, which is only modestly significant.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of concealed, computer-generated allocation, or a baseline-adjusted analysis giving the same VEMS effect.

issues.title: Many listed outcomes (FVC, dyspnoea, anxiety, depression) are claimed improved but no data are shown
issues.explanation: The Methods list a dozen measures, but results are given only for TUG and VEMS. The Results text nonetheless states real improvement in vital capacity, dyspnoea, pain and sleep. Those claims cannot be checked, and with no registered primary outcome the reader cannot tell whether reported outcomes were selected for favourable results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A report or supplement presenting the FVC, dyspnoea and mood data for both groups.

10.29296/25877305-2023-08-11.headline_claim: Virtual reality and biofeedback mechanotherapy added to basic treatment improves exercise tolerance, reduces dyspnea and some cardiovascular indices in patients with post-COVID syndrome, and can be recommended for rehabilitation.
10.29296/25877305-2023-08-11.overall: The reported gains in maximal work and in mild or moderate dyspnea are plausible, but they come from an open-label add-on comparison with no stated primary outcome, sample-size calculation, or blinding of subjective outcomes. The abstract and conclusion overreach by claiming effects on hypoxic syndrome and cardiovascular indices that the tables do not show. The printed errors are small (one impossible quartile in Table 2), and the headline conclusion holds only as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Maximum work performed (MET) on cardiopulmonary testing, plus dyspnea severity (MRS) as the effectiveness measures

issues.title: No blinding or assessor masking described; MRS dyspnea and effort-dependent CPET are headline outcomes
issues.explanation: The methods say nothing about masking of patients or outcome assessors, and the dyspnea outcome is a self-reported grade. An open-label add-on arm with extra sessions is prone to expectation effects on dyspnea and on effort during exercise testing. The size of the reported improvement cannot be separated from that bias.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the dyspnea assessor and the CPET operator were blinded to group, or independent of the treating team.

quotes.text: использовали шкалу Медицинского исследовательского совета
Исходная оценка показателей одышки по шкале MRS

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes no blinding of participants, outcome assessors or analysts, and no allocation concealment, even though the headline outcomes are the MRS dyspnea grade (subjective) and effort-dependent CPET measures (max work, VO2 at the first ventilatory threshold). Because the interventions are visibly different, participants could not have been blinded; whether assessors were masked is simply not reported, so the risk of detection and performance bias is unaddressed and the paper has no limitations discussion of it.

issues.title: Control arm gets basic treatment only: extra sessions and attention are not matched
issues.explanation: The control arm received 40 basic sessions while the main arm received the same basic treatment plus 30 additional device sessions. Differences in dyspnea and exercise capacity therefore combine the specific devices with extra training time, attention and expectation. This is a defensible pragmatic choice, but it limits attribution to the technologies themselves.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the control programme was matched for session time and contact hours, or that the paper claims only an add-on package effect.

quotes.text: В группе контроля (n=60) пациенты получали только базовое лечение.

issues.title: Abstract reports dyspnea gains as within-arm p-values; 'no dyspnea' share does not differ between arms (p=0.550)
issues.explanation: The abstract cites within-main-group changes (e.g. no dyspnea 8.3% to 26.7%, p=0.009). The control group improved similarly (11.7% to 33.3%, p=0.005), and the between-group p for 'no dyspnea' after treatment is 0.550. Between-group differences exist only for mild and moderate dyspnea, and the categories were tested separately. The abstract's within-group framing therefore overstates the specific advantage of the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group test of change in MRS score (e.g. ANCOVA or ordinal model) showing a significant advantage for the main group.

quotes.location: Results and discussion, control group dyspnea paragraph
Results and discussion, main group dyspnea paragraph

issues.title: Causal, general recommendation drawn from a 12-day single-centre open comparison without follow-up or safety data
issues.explanation: The conclusion states that the technologies 'lead to' higher endurance and recommends them for practice. Outcomes were measured only immediately after the course, and the paper reports no adverse events or tolerability data. The between-group evidence is mixed: peak oxygen uptake rose in both groups without a difference (p=0.700).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Longer follow-up data, safety reporting and replication in an independent blinded trial.

issues.title: Abstract conclusion claims reduced 'hypoxic syndrome' and improved cardiovascular indices not shown in the results
issues.explanation: The abstract conclusion states that the intervention reduces hypoxic syndrome and improves cardiovascular performance. No hypoxia measure is reported, and the cardiovascular results are limited to a diastolic pressure change of a few mm Hg in the main group. Heart rate and systolic pressures did not change, and the peak VO2 gain was the same in both arms (p=0.700).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported oxygen-saturation or gas-exchange outcome showing improvement, and a prespecified cardiovascular endpoint reaching significance.

quotes.text: гипоксического синдрома, одышки и улучшению показателей сердечно-сосудистой деятельности

issues.title: Control resting SBP after rehabilitation printed as 130 (20; 130): Q1 of 20 mm Hg is implausible
issues.explanation: Table 2 gives the control group's post-rehabilitation resting systolic pressure as median 130 with a first quartile of 20 mm Hg. A quartile of 20 is not a physiological value and is probably a mistyped 120. This cell underlies the between-group comparison (p=0.02) that the abstract reports for resting SBP, so the reader cannot check that result from the table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors' source data showing the true control Q1 (e.g. 120) and confirming that the p=0.02 was computed from the raw values.

issues.title: No sample-size justification, primary outcome or registration reported for the 60 vs 60 trial
issues.explanation: The paper gives no sample-size rationale, no declared primary outcome and no registration, and does not describe allocation concealment. With about 10 outcomes tested at alpha 0.05, the reader cannot tell which result was the prespecified test of efficacy. This is a reporting limitation that makes the confident conclusion harder to trust.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registered protocol or sample-size calculation naming the primary outcome and effect size.

issues.title: Patent-holding authors declared; one patent holder ran and interpreted the exercise tests
issues.explanation: Four authors disclose co-ownership of a patent developed using these results, so the interest is stated. The contributions section shows that one of them conducted and interpreted the cardiopulmonary testing, and no blinding is described. This does not show bias, but it raises the importance of independent outcome assessment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that CPET analysis was done by a blinded operator not involved in the patent.

10.29296/25877305-2023-09-11.headline_claim: Adding biofeedback mechanotherapy (Con-Trex, Stabilan) and virtual-reality training to standard rehabilitation improves balance, muscle strength and gait in post-COVID syndrome, with statistically better results than standard therapy alone.
10.29296/25877305-2023-09-11.overall: The directional finding that adding mechanotherapy and virtual reality improved balance, strength and gait is plausible, but the paper has several reporting errors (1245.5 vs 1345.5 N, baseline claims contradicted by tables, a right-leg reversal contradicting the text). It also lacks registration, a primary outcome, a described randomisation method and an effort-matched control, so the stated conclusion of statistically better results should be taken as tentative and exploratory.

primary_outcome.name: Not designated; balance (stabilometry), gait speed, muscle strength and endurance are all reported as outcomes

issues.title: Conclusion of 'statistically better results' from technologies, with unmatched therapy volume and 10-day follow-up
issues.explanation: The main group received 30 additional sessions on top of standard therapy, while controls received standard therapy only, so the comparison cannot separate technology effects from extra therapy time. Outcomes were measured only about 10 days after the course, without blinding described, and the results are mixed rather than uniformly favourable. The unqualified conclusion that the programme yields statistically better results is stronger than this single-centre, open-label evidence supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A dose-matched control arm, blinded assessment and longer follow-up showing the same advantage.

quotes.text: позволяет достичь статистически лучших результатов лечения.
Контрольное обследование, аналогичное базовому, проводилось сразу после окончания процедур (10-й день ±3 дня).

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion states that the added technologies 'allow achieving statistically better treatment results', but the intervention arm received about 30 more sessions than control (70 vs 40, as counted from the Methods), so the effect cannot be attributed to the technologies as opposed to the larger therapy volume. Outcomes were measured only immediately after the course (day 10 ±3), so the conclusion supports at most a short-term difference and says nothing about durability.

issues.title: Right-leg extension force: abstract and text 1245.5 N vs Table 5 1345.5 N; left-leg text also mismatched
issues.explanation: The abstract and the between-group sentence in the Results give the post-course main-group right-leg force as 1245.5 N. Table 5 and the preceding Results sentence give 1345.5 N. The left leg has a similar slip: the Results text gives 1257 N for the main group's post-course left-leg force (the control value), whereas Table 5 gives 1471.5 N in magnitude. These are reporting errors that change individual reported values, and the group-comparison p values are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrigendum or raw data showing which main-group value (1245.5 or 1345.5 N) is correct and that the other is a typesetting slip.

issues.title: Right-leg single-leg stance after treatment is longer in controls (15 s, 10 s) than in main group (12 s, 6 s)
issues.explanation: The text states the main group had better functional test results than controls in Table 3. For right-leg stance, controls scored higher than the main group with eyes open (15 vs 12 s) and eyes closed (10 vs 6 s), with p3 of 0 and 0.007. Longer stance time is better, so these two tests favour controls, contradicting the blanket statement. The left leg eyes-open difference (p=0.062) is also not significant. Part of the right-leg eyes-closed gap was present at baseline (4 vs 7 s).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that rows for the right leg have group labels swapped in Table 3, or that lower values are better for these rows.

issues.title: No registration, primary outcome, sample-size rationale, randomisation method or blinding reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes a randomised, controlled, prospective study but reports no trial registry number, no designated primary outcome and no sample size justification. The method of randomisation, allocation concealment and assessor blinding are not described, and no adverse events are reported. Without these, selective emphasis on favourable outcomes among many cannot be excluded, and the study should be read as exploratory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol with prespecified primary outcome and sample size, and a description of the randomisation and blinding procedures.

quotes.text: После базового обследования участники были рандомизированы на 2 группы.

issues.title: Bonferroni mentioned but no adjusted alpha; about 25 between-group tests, several with p 0.012-0.041
issues.explanation: The Methods mention Bonferroni correction for between-group tests but give no number of comparisons or adjusted alpha, and elsewhere set the critical level at 0.05. Roughly 14 functional tests, 6 device measures and 7 stabilometry parameters are compared between groups with no primary outcome. Many p values lie in the 0.012-0.041 range and would not be significant under a Bonferroni threshold for that many tests. Results with p near 0.000 are not affected, so the strongest findings remain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the printed p values are already Bonferroni-adjusted, or a designated small set of primary outcomes with the correction applied to that family.

issues.title: Text says no baseline differences, but Table 2 shows p=0.002 (4 vs 7 s); post-only between-group tests
issues.explanation: The text says no significant baseline group difference was found (p>0.05), but Table 2 shows right-leg eyes-closed stance of 4 s in the main group vs 7 s in controls, p=0.002. Between-group comparisons in Tables 3 and 5 use post-course values only, with no adjustment for baseline or analysis of change. Some of the apparent between-group gaps in single-leg stance and walking may therefore reflect starting differences; for the right-leg eyes-closed item the imbalance favours controls.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A baseline-adjusted (ANCOVA) or change-score analysis showing the same between-group results, or a correction showing the 0.002 is a misprint.

issues.title: Identical p-value sets printed for different tests in Tables 3 and 4; baseline table has post-course p columns

Table 4, titled as baseline, also has p2 and p3 columns, and its p3 values (0.013, 0.023, 0.008) equal the post-course values in Table 5. issues.title: Baseline 'within age norms' contradicted by Table 2: Up-and-Go 16 s vs norm <10 s; walk 0.7 m/s vs 1.31-1.43
issues.explanation: The Results state that baseline functional tests were within age norms (Up-and-Go under 10 s, 10-m walk 1.31-1.43 m/s). Table 2 gives a main-group median of 16 s and a walking speed of 0.7 m/s, both clearly outside those norms. The sentence misdescribes the baseline status, which if anything shows more impairment than stated; it does not affect the between-group comparisons.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the quoted norms were for a different test protocol or that Table 2 units are wrong.

issues.title: Eyes-closed centre-of-pressure speed (15%, p=0.094) described as a significant gain
issues.explanation: The Results say significantly more main-group patients reached reference values on listed stabilometry parameters compared with baseline. One listed item, eyes-closed centre-of-pressure velocity (+15%), has p=0.094, above the stated alpha of 0.05. In addition, chi-square 3.5 with 1 df would give p of about 0.06 rather than 0.094, so the printed statistic and p do not match each other either, though neither reaches significance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that this item was excluded from the 'significant' list or a different stated alpha for this comparison.

10.29296/25877305-2024-05-12.headline_claim: Selank nasal drops added to a neuroprotective complex are reported to show a good effect in post-COVID asthenia with impaired mental performance, with relief of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
10.29296/25877305-2024-05-12.overall: The conclusion that Selank has a good effect in post-COVID asthenia is not well supported by what is presented. The comparison is an open add-on design with subjective outcomes, and the abstract gives no scores or between-group statistics. At most the study is hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: unclear

issues.title: Open add-on comparison without placebo or stated blinding supports 'good effect' of Selank only weakly
issues.explanation: Group 2 received the same neuroprotective complex without Selank, with no placebo or sham drop. Asthenia, anxiety and depression are subjective outcomes that are prone to expectation effects. Without blinding, the abstract's conclusion that Selank itself has a good effect is not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A full text describing blinding or a matched placebo, or objective outcome measures.

issues.title: Abstract claims 'good effect' with no scores, between-group comparison or p-values reported

issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full-text tables with between-group comparisons showing a significant difference favouring Selank.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract states 'good effect' and relief of anxiety and depressive symptoms without giving any scores, between-group comparison or p-values. Whether the full text reports these could not be checked, because only the abstract and reference list were available.

issues.title: Allocation method and baseline comparability not described for two groups of 32
issues.explanation: The abstract says patients were 'divided into 2 groups' without saying whether allocation was random. Baseline comparability is also not described. This weakens confidence in the comparison but cannot be classed as an error from the available text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods section describing random allocation and a baseline characteristics table showing balance.

10.29390/cjrt-2021-074.headline_claim: The SingStrong online singing and breathing retraining programme shows promise as a viable treatment option for long COVID, with significant pre-post improvements in breathlessness, fatigue and other symptoms; further studies are needed to investigate efficacy.
10.29390/cjrt-2021-074.overall: The study is an uncontrolled, completers-only pilot with 21 analysed participants, so the within-group improvements cannot be attributed to the programme. Breathlessness gains are the most robust results; the other highlighted improvements (P 0.01-0.04) are fragile under multiplicity. There are several small numeric slips, but none change a result. The cautious abstract wording is only partly undone by causal phrasing in the Conclusions.

primary_outcome.name: Not stated as a single primary outcome; pre-post change in C19-YRS breathlessness, fatigue and other symptom domains and DSQ-SF ME/CFS criteria

issues.title: Benefit claims rest on a single-arm pre-post design with within-group paired tests only (n=21)
issues.explanation: All efficacy statements come from paired pre-post comparisons in one uncontrolled group. These tests show that scores changed, not that the programme caused the change, especially in a condition where symptoms fluctuate and often improve over time. The authors concede they do not know what other clinical support participants received. The Conclusions nonetheless say participants 'experienced significant improvements'. The pilot supports feasibility and hypothesis generation, not treatment benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group showing no change over the same period, or a conclusion restricted to feasibility.

quotes.text: This pilot study used a one-group pre-test-post-test research design
Paired sample t -tests were used to evaluate pre-post data
The absence of a control group further limits robust interpretation of results

second_reader.what_stands: The design and analysis are as described: a single-arm pre-post study of 21 completers with only within-group paired tests, so the improvements cannot be attributed to the intervention. The authors openly state this limitation and call for RCTs, and the abstract concludes only that the programme 'shows promise', but the wording 'significant improvements' and 'benefits... may result' still goes further than the design supports.

issues.title: About 15 symptom-domain tests at alpha 0.05, no primary outcome or correction; five 'significant' results at P 0.01-0.04
issues.explanation: Ten severity and five impact domains were each tested at P ≤ 0.05 without correction, and no primary outcome was designated. Fatigue (0.03), usual activities (0.04), pain (0.03), voice (0.01) and cognition (0.04) are reported as improvements, and these would not survive even a modest correction. Only the breathlessness results (P < 0.001) are robust to multiplicity. The headline list of improvements is therefore stronger than the evidence supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome, or a stated correction under which these results remain significant.

quotes.text: Statistical significance was set at P ≤ 0.05.
fatigue ( P = 0.03), usual activities ( P =  0.04), pain/disability ( P =  0.03), voice quality ( P =  0.01)

issues.title: Completers-only analysis: 6 of 27 (22%) enrolled participants excluded, no ITT or sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Outcomes are reported only for the 21 participants who attended at least half the classes. The six others (five dropouts plus one low attender) are excluded, so the improvements describe people who persisted with the programme. The paper gives no comparison of excluded and included participants and no sensitivity analysis. This probably overstates the effect that would be seen in everyone who enrolled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An analysis including all 27 participants (for example baseline carried forward) showing similar improvements.

quotes.text: data from 21 who completed at least 10 (50%) classes were analysed

issues.title: Conclusions state 'significant improvements' and feasibility 'established' from an uncontrolled pilot
issues.explanation: The closing Conclusions describe participants as having experienced significant improvements in numerous issues, which reads as an effect of the programme. The Discussion also says feasibility was established, although no feasibility targets, recruitment rate or retention benchmark were set. The abstract's more cautious wording only partly offsets this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specified feasibility criteria that were met, with the conclusions phrased as associations.

issues.title: Pre-COVID health SD of 5.5 is impossible for a 0-10 scale with mean 7.4 (maximum about 4.4)

issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected value (for example 2.5) or the underlying data showing an SD of at most 4.4.

issues.title: Mobility Cohen's d printed as 0.010 although t = 0.44 with n = 21 implies about 0.10

Mobility t = 0.44 should give d of about 0.10, not 0.010. The mobility change is non-significant either way, so no result changes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors' raw data showing d = 0.010 for mobility.
