issues.title: C19-YRS scale described as 0=worst, but severity tables behave as 0=none; t signs also inconsistent
issues.explanation: The Methods say the C19-YRS is rated 0 (worst) to 10 (best). Table 4 shows pre-COVID severity of 0 rising at baseline and falling after the intervention, which is only coherent if higher means worse. The reader cannot tell the scoring direction from the Methods. Table 4 also prints a negative t (-4.5) for breathlessness at rest and positive t for the other items, although all are reported as improvements.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors confirming that the severity items are scored 0 = none to 10 = worst and that the sign difference is a labelling artefact.

quotes.text: rates on a scale from 0 (worst) to 10 (best)
Breathlessness at rest 0 (0-0) 2.5(2.2) 1(0-2)

issues.title: Several printed percentages do not match their counts (19/21 as 91.5%, 17/27 as 63.9%, 11/21 as 52.8%)
issues.explanation: At least three percentages do not equal their own count over the stated denominator. Each is off by about 0.4 to 1.0 percentage points. These are small transcription errors affecting descriptive statistics only. They do suggest the numbers were not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator stated in the paper that makes all of these percentages reconcile.

quotes.text: 17 (63.9%) reported between one and four pre-existing medical conditions
Voice quality/issues 14 (66.6%) 11 (52.8%)

script.explanation: 19/21 = 90.48%, but the paper prints 91.5, outside the rounding interval [91.45, 91.60]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 20.8 rather than 21.

10.29407/js_unpgri.v9i1.19575.headline_claim: Single 45-minute combined aerobic, strength and breathing exercise session improved pulmonary function and oxygen saturation in women with post-COVID-19 syndrome, and the session was feasible and safe.
10.29407/js_unpgri.v9i1.19575.overall: Feasibility and safety findings (full adherence, no injuries) are reasonably supported, but the claim that exercise improved pulmonary function is not. It rests on uncontrolled pre-post comparisons across ten uncorrected tests, and one of the 'improvements' (SVC) actually decreased. The efficacy conclusion should be treated as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Pulmonary function parameters (FEV1, FEV1/FVC%, PEF, SVC, MVV, MVVt, SpO2); no single primary outcome is named

issues.title: SVC listed as increased in text, but Table 3 shows a fall (3.03 to 2.7, ES -0.58, p=0.030)
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion say SVC increased after exercise and count it among the improvements. Table 3 shows SVC fell from 3.03 to 2.7 L with a negative effect size. The one significant SVC change is therefore a worsening, yet it is counted in support of the conclusion that exercise improved pulmonary function.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A source dataset or corrected table showing SVC post-exercise was higher than pre-exercise.

quotes.text: As shown in Table3, there were increases in post-exercise FEV1, FEV1/FEV, PEF, SVC, MVV, MVVt, and spO2

second_reader.what_stands: Table 3 shows SVC falling from 3.03 to 2.7 L with a negative effect size (-0.58) and p=0.030, yet the Results and Discussion list SVC among the parameters that increased. The text misdescribes the direction of this result, and the decrease is not discussed.

issues.title: Efficacy of exercise claimed from an uncontrolled single-group pre-post design (n=36)
issues.explanation: All changes are before versus immediately after one session in one group. Repeated spirometry (practice and effort effects) and measurement variability cannot be separated from any exercise effect. The conclusion nonetheless states that the session improved pulmonary function and SpO2, and that the findings 'indicate' improvement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control or sham-session group, or repeat-baseline testing without exercise, showing no change.

quotes.text: The study was a one-group pre and post-test design study on 36 women
this study did not assign a control group, so we cannot  distinguish  whether  the  increase  was  largely  due  to  the  natural course of the disease or treatment
The positive acute effect was also indicated with improved pulmonary function and oxygen saturation in women with post-COVID-19 syndrome.

second_reader.what_stands: The design is a single-group pre-post with n=36 and cannot support efficacy claims; the authors do acknowledge this in the limitations. What stands is that the Conclusion and Results still describe improvement and a 'positive effect' of the exercise without the control-group caveat, and the 'natural course of the disease' wording is an odd explanation for a change within about an hour.

issues.title: Causal 'improves pulmonary function' wording from an uncontrolled single-session feasibility study
issues.explanation: The Results say the exercises 'improve' inhalation and exhalation, and the Discussion says the findings 'indicate' improvement. Yet the study is a single-group, single-session feasibility design with no control, and the authors concede the changes could be natural course. The SVC result also goes in the opposite direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled evidence of the same acute changes, or conclusions worded purely as feasibility and hypothesis-generating.

quotes.text: The results suggest  that  the  aerobic,  strength,  and  breathing  exercises  improve inhalation and exhalation of pulmonary function and oxygen saturation in post-COVID-19 women.
quotes.location: Results, end of acute effect section

quotes.text: indicate  that  a combination of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, strength training, and breathing improves pulmonary function and oxygen saturation

second_reader.what_stands: The Results and Discussion use causal, general 'improves' wording from a single-session, uncontrolled study in which several parameters did not change and one (SVC) fell. The paper does call the study a feasibility and acute-effect study and notes the missing control group, but the causal phrasing exceeds what the design supports.

issues.title: Ten outcomes tested at nominal p<0.05 without correction or designated primary outcome
issues.explanation: Ten pulmonary and oximetry outcomes were each tested with no multiplicity adjustment and no pre-specified primary outcome, then the significant ones were summarised as improvements. Results with p of 0.018 and 0.030 would not survive a Bonferroni threshold of 0.005, while FVC, MRf and MVt were not significant and are omitted from the conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or multiplicity plan in a protocol or registration.

quotes.text: There were also increases in FEV1, FEV1/FEV, PEF, SVC, MVV, MVVt, and spO2 p value < 0.05
Changes in the outcomes pre and post-exercise were examined using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test

10.30629/2658-7947-2025-30-3-53-60.headline_claim: Adding cytoflavin to a complex outpatient regimen for post-COVID syndrome produced greater positive dynamics in clinical, spirometric and HADS measures, and the authors recommend its use in outpatient complex therapy.
10.30629/2658-7947-2025-30-3-53-60.overall: The conclusion that cytoflavin is superior to the comparator rests on within-group before/after fold-changes with no described between-group test, no registered primary outcome, and no described blinding. Several printed numbers also disagree with their own counts, including a CGI p-value that does not reproduce. The data suggest improvement in both arms, but the claimed added benefit of cytoflavin is only tentatively supported.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; the abstract reports chest pain, headache and tachycardia changes (p<0.01) as the most pronounced differences

issues.title: Superiority of cytoflavin asserted from within-group fold-changes with no between-group test
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion state that cytoflavin gave 'more pronounced' improvement, using ratios of before/after frequencies in each arm and p < 0.01 attached to those changes. The Methods name only Shapiro-Wilk and a threshold of 0.01 and describe no comparison between arms, no adjustment for baseline, and no correction for many outcomes. The between-arm differences are therefore not shown to be statistically supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described between-group test (e.g. chi-squared or ANCOVA on change) with arm-versus-arm p-values supporting the highlighted differences.

quotes.text: Включение цитофлавина способствовало более выраженной положительной динамике клини -ческих показателей
Статистическая обработка данных проведена с использованием программного пакета Statistica 12.0.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract, results and conclusion assert that cytoflavin gave a more pronounced improvement, using within-arm fold-changes (6 vs 2.2, 7 vs 3, 5.2 vs 3) with a p<0.01 that is not tied to a named between-group test. The Methods describe no between-group comparison. A rough comparison of the post-treatment counts for these three symptoms does not reach p<0.01 (my estimates are approximate, not exact). The between-arm attribution of the asterisks in Table 2 is ambiguous, but the superiority claim for the symptom and HADS outcomes is not supported by a reported between-group test.

issues.title: CGI 'no effect' 5/56 vs 12/50 reported p < 0.01; recomputation gives p about 0.035; 9.1% implies n = 55
issues.explanation: The text says the 'no effect' result was seen in 5 of group I and 12 of group II patients with p < 0.01. From those counts a standard 2x2 chi-squared test gives p near 0.04, which does not meet the paper's own 0.01 threshold. The group I percentages (9.1%, and the headline 90.9% improved) also correspond to 55 rather than 56 patients.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated alternative test (such as a trend test across all CGI categories) that yields p < 0.01 from these counts.

quotes.text: лечения « без эффекта » был зафиксирован у 5 (9,1%) пациентов в то время , как в группе II у 12 (24%) больных ( р < 0,01)

second_reader.what_stands: The printed 9.1% for 5 patients is inconsistent with n = 56 (5/56 = 8.9%). The stated p<0.01 for 5/56 vs 12/50 is not reproduced: the uncorrected chi-square gives p of about 0.035 and a continuity-corrected or exact test gives about 0.05-0.07. This is not significant at the paper's own alpha of 0.01. The 90.9% 'effective' figure inherits the same small rounding error and counts 'minor improvement' as effective.

issues.title: Comparator is saline placebo plus B12 tablets, with no description of blinding or matching
issues.explanation: Group II received placebo infusions followed by vitamin B12 tablets, whereas group I received cytoflavin infusions and then cytoflavin tablets. The paper says nothing about masking of patients or assessors, or whether the tablets looked alike. Most outcomes are patient-reported (symptom complaints, HADS, CGI), so unblinded assessment could inflate the apparent benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that patients and outcome assessors were masked and that the tablets were matched in appearance.

quotes.text: получали ежедневно внутривенно капельно 10,0 мл плацебо , разведенного в 200,0 мл 0,9% раствора натрия хлорида

issues.title: No registration, sample-size rationale or randomisation method for a claimed randomised comparison
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were split 'randomly' but gives no method, concealment, protocol, registry entry or sample-size reasoning. Many outcomes were measured (about 25 table rows), and the paper highlights those that favour cytoflavin. Without a prespecified primary outcome, the selection of highlighted results cannot be checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol naming the primary outcome and describing the randomisation procedure.

quotes.text: Пациенты случайным методом были разделены на две группы сопоставимые по полу , возрасту и со -путствующей патологии .

issues.title: Table 3 group I percentages use n = 50 instead of 56; '12.5-fold' depression reduction is 14-fold by counts
issues.explanation: Several group I after-treatment percentages in Table 3 do not match their counts over 56, but do match the counts over 50. The reported 12.5-fold fall in clinical depression is derived from the mis-scaled percentage. The error slightly understates group I's depression reduction, and the main findings are not reversed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that the group I post-treatment percentages were computed on a reduced analysed sample of 50.

script.explanation: 1/56 = 1.79%, but the paper prints 2.0, outside the rounding interval [1.95, 2.10]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 50.0 rather than 56.

issues.title: Text says group I minute volume rose 1.1 L; Table 2 gives 11.7 - 10.3 = 1.4 L
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 2 disagree on the size of the group I increase in minute respiratory volume. One of the two is wrong. The mismatch changes the apparent between-group gap (1.1 vs 0.6 L, or 1.4 vs 0.6 L) but not its direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the text figure refers to a different time point or subgroup than Table 2.

quotes.text: соответственно на 1,1 л в группе I и на 0,6 л -во II
Minute respiratory volume, MV, (l) | 10.3 ± 0.4 | 11.7 ± 0.8 | 10.9 ± 0.05

10.30841/2786-720x.1.2024.300442.headline_claim: Adding a combination of L-arginine, L-carnitine and coenzyme Q10 to standard antihypertensive therapy after COVID-19 more effectively restored psychological and cognitive function and improved blood pressure control.
10.30841/2786-720x.1.2024.300442.overall: The headline claim that the supplement improved psychological, cognitive and BP outcomes beyond standard therapy is not supported: no between-group tests are reported, the control had no placebo, and the dates, eligibility and category totals contain several internal inconsistencies. Treat the results as descriptive and tentative; the study is small and appears unregistered, and the timeline cannot be reconciled with the stated follow-up.

primary_outcome.name: BP control, cognitive (MMSE) and psychological (PHQ-9, SSS-8) outcomes; primary outcome not labelled in the paper

issues.title: Efficacy claims rest on within-arm changes and descriptive percentage differences, no between-group tests
issues.explanation: The BP 'additional effect' is supported by a significance mark versus baseline, and the cognitive, depression and symptom benefits are described only as differences in percentages between arms. No between-group test, estimate or confidence interval is reported for any outcome. A within-arm change does not show that the supplement beat standard therapy, so the abstract and conclusion of superiority are not supported by the analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-group tests (e.g. ANCOVA on change or Mann-Whitney on change scores) showing group 1 differing from group 2 with adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: зниження АТ достовірно порівняно з початком дослідження (р ˂ 0,05)
Зареєстровано додатковий ефект щодо поліпшення контролю АТ лише на тлі медикаментозної терапії в комплексі із комбінацією L-аргініну
contributed to a more effective recovery of psychological and cognitive disorders

second_reader.what_stands: In the text and tables, the efficacy claims in the abstract and conclusions rest on within-arm change from baseline and on descriptive percentage-point differences between arms. They are not supported by reported between-group tests despite the Mann-Whitney method being listed, and the 'only in group 1' BP claim compares significance across arms. This applies to the text and tables; figure images were not available to check.

issues.title: Ethics approval 06.12.2023 and receipt 26.12.2023 (20 days) cannot contain 4-week or 3-month follow-up
issues.explanation: The ethics protocol is dated 06.12.2023 and the manuscript was received 26.12.2023, only 20 days later. The design has a 14-day active phase plus a 4-week phone visit, and Table 2 reports a 'Через 3 міс' (3-month) column, while methods say total observation was over 1 month. Either enrolment started before ethics approval, the dates are wrong, or the 3-month column is mislabelled; in each case the timeline of data collection cannot be trusted as reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation that recruitment started after 06.12.2023 and a corrected follow-up schedule, or an erratum fixing the dates and the Table 2 column label.

quotes.text: (Протокол №14 від 06.12.2023 р.)
Стаття надійшла до редакції
Через 3 міс

second_reader.what_stands: As printed, a 20-day gap between approval and receipt cannot hold 4-week follow-up, and cannot hold 3-month follow-up, if enrolment began after approval. The paper gives no recruitment or follow-up dates and says nothing about whether approval was retrospective, so the timeline conflict is real but its cause cannot be determined. The paper also reports 4 weeks in Methods and 3 months in Table 2 without explanation.

issues.title: No placebo for a supplement; subjective PHQ-9/SSS-8/symptom outcomes with open-label usual care comparator
issues.explanation: Group 2 received standard therapy only, with no placebo or sham product. Most outcomes are questionnaire or symptom reports, and blinding is claimed only as 'blind' allocation without any description. Expectation and extra attention effects could produce the larger improvements in group 1, so the supplement cannot be shown to be the cause.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of a matched placebo or blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: the patients in the second group received standard therapy.
Questionnaires (MMSE, SSS-8, PHQ-9) were chosen to assess anxiety-depressive disorders and cognitive function.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper describes no placebo; the control arm received usual therapy alone, and the main outcomes are self-reported or subjective, which exposes them to expectation bias if patients knew their arm. The paper does not state that patients were unmasked, and its 'blind' wording leaves masking unclear. The open-label description is therefore an inference from the absence of a placebo, not an explicit statement. MMSE is a partial exception because it is performance-based.

issues.title: 53 patients, no sample-size calculation, efficacy stated firmly
issues.explanation: No power calculation is reported and 53 patients are split into 28 and 25. The Limitations section acknowledges the small sample, but the abstract and conclusions state that the combination contributed to more effective recovery. This weakens the strength of the conclusion but is not a numeric error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified power calculation or hedged efficacy language.

quotes.text: У дослідження було залучено 53 пацієнта
обмеженої кількості пацієнтів

issues.title: Entry required BP below 140/90, but baseline mean BP is 141.5/91.6 and 140.8/90.7
issues.explanation: Inclusion required BP below 140/90 mmHg on treatment. The baseline group means are above this in both arms for both systolic and diastolic readings, so many patients cannot have met the criterion at baseline. Selecting or enrolling people with higher values makes later falls partly regression to the mean, which would flatter the reported BP fall in group 1.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that eligibility used a different measurement (e.g. clinic BP at an earlier visit) from the baseline values.

quotes.text: АГ (АТ ˂ 140/90 мм рт.ст. на фоні медикаментозної терапії)
Середній рівень систолічного артеріального тиску (САТ) у першій групі становив 141,5±5,3

issues.title: Eligibility 'mild to moderate' depression, yet 19/28 and 18/25 had 'minimal' depression at baseline
issues.explanation: The methods say only patients scoring from 'mild' to 'moderate' depression on PHQ-9 were included. The baseline results show 67.8% (group 1) and 72% (group 2) in the 'minimal depression' category. Most patients therefore did not meet the stated entry rule, or the categories are mislabelled; either way, the 'recovery' from depression is measured on a mostly non-depressed baseline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 'minimal' label was used for a mild band, or that baseline PHQ-9 was taken before screening.

quotes.text: Пацієнти, результати обстеження яких входили в межі діапазону від «легкої депресії» до «помірної депресії», були включені у дослідження.
«мінімальна депресія» - у 19 (67,8%) пацієнтів першої групи

issues.title: PHQ-9 advantage given as 11.8% in Results and 17.8% in Discussion
issues.explanation: Results state 11.8% more patients without depression in group 1. The Discussion states normalisation was 17.8% better than controls. Using the endpoint counts the first figure matches (67.8 - 56 = 11.8), and no category combination obviously gives 17.8.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of 'normalisation' under which 17.8 follows from the printed counts.

quotes.text: Кількість пацієнтів без ознак депресії у першій групі виявлено на 11,8% вище, ніж у другій
була на 17,8% краще, ніж у контрольній групі

issues.title: SSS-8 endpoint categories add to 11 of 28 (group 1) and 11 of 25 (group 2)
issues.explanation: At baseline the five SSS-8 categories sum to 28 and 25. At the end of active observation the listed categories account for only 11 patients in each group, with the very-high category stated as absent. About 17 and 14 patients are missing, so the endpoint distribution and the claimed SSS-8 advantage cannot be reconstructed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 4 data showing the full endpoint distribution, with the text listing only some categories.

quotes.text: «низький дискомфорт» - у 4 (14,2%), «середній дискомфорт» - у 5 (17,8%)
«високий дискомфорт» - в 1 (3,5%), «дуже високий дискомфорт» не виявлено
«високий дискомфорт» - в 1 (4%), «дуже високий дискомфорт» у пацієнтів не виявлено

issues.title: Antihypertensive class counts sum to 27 (group 1) and 26 (group 2), not 28 and 25
issues.explanation: The text gives drug-class counts per group that add to 27 in group 1 and 26 in group 2. Table 1 gives group sizes of 28 and 25, and the classes are described as covering every patient. The totals agree at 53, so a single patient appears to be misallocated, which is a small reporting error that does not bear on the efficacy results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that one group-2 patient was counted in group 1 for drug classes, or a patient on a regimen not listed.

quotes.text: 14 осіб у першій групі та 12 - у другій групі
по 2 пацієнти у кожній із груп
6 та 4 осіб відповідно

issues.title: Vaccinated share printed as 41.2%; 21/53 = 39.6%
issues.explanation: The paper reports 21 of the 53 enrolled patients vaccinated and prints 41.2%. 21 out of 53 is 39.6%; 41.2% would correspond to a denominator of 51. This is a minor reporting error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that 51 patients had vaccination status recorded.

script.explanation: 21/53 = 39.62%, but the paper prints 41.2, outside the rounding interval [41.15, 41.30]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 51.0 rather than 53.

10.30841/2786-720x.4.2024.320815.headline_claim: Post-COVID-19 convalescents show oxidative stress, endotoxemia and immune-complex activation that persist for months, and haloaerosol rehabilitation improves these markers but does not fully normalise them.
10.30841/2786-720x.4.2024.320815.overall: The finding that biomarkers of lipid peroxidation, endotoxemia and immune complexes are elevated after COVID-19 versus healthy controls is well supported by large differences. The claim that haloaerosol therapy causes the improvement is not supported, because the design has no concurrent control and relies on within-group before-after tests with co-interventions. The reported numerical slips (2.1 vs 2.2, 1.3 vs 1.4) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: Oxidative stress coefficient (OSI/КВОС) and related lipid peroxidation markers before vs after rehabilitation

issues.title: Efficacy of haloaerosol rehabilitation inferred from uncontrolled before-after change within treated groups
issues.explanation: All reported benefit comes from paired before-versus-after tests within the treated patients; no between-arm test of the change is reported, and there is no untreated or alternatively treated comparison group. The treatment also included exercise and medication, so the effect of haloaerosol therapy alone cannot be separated. The conclusion that haloaerosol therapy 'leads to' improvement is therefore stronger than this design can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control arm receiving the same rehabilitation without haloaerosol, or a between-group test of the change.

quotes.text: Відновлювальне лікування на основі використання курсу ГАТ з визначеними параметрами концентрації та дисперсності приводить до покращення клініко-функціональних показників
Тому порівняння цих двох груп

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy of the haloaerosol course is inferred from uncontrolled before-after change within treated groups (paired t-tests, Table 3; self-rated health 76.9% -> 89.8%), with no concurrent untreated or placebo arm, and the course is combined with exercise, a gentle regimen and bronchodilator/anti-inflammatory therapy, so the effect cannot be attributed to haloaerosol alone. The point is only partly right because the authors do offer a cross-sectional comparison of early vs late admission groups (Table 1, no difference) as an indirect natural-history reference, which weakens but does not remove t

issues.title: Biomarker elevations stated to cause tissue damage and post-COVID syndrome without outcome data
issues.explanation: The study measures blood markers at one time point after COVID-19 and compares them with healthy controls. It does not assess post-COVID syndrome or tissue damage, nor relate marker levels to outcomes. Statements that the changes 'cause' these conditions or 'confirm' their pathogenetic role go beyond the data, which show association only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Analyses linking baseline marker levels to measured post-COVID outcomes in these patients.

quotes.text: що зумовлює розвиток тканинних ушкоджень і постковідного синдрому
Цей факт підтверджує патогенетичну значущість досліджуваних процесів у розвитку постковідного синдрому

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract states that raised MSM and CIC cause tissue damage and post-COVID syndrome and that persistent elevation after treatment confirms pathogenic significance, but the paper presents only biomarker levels and no data on post-COVID syndrome or tissue damage and no analysis linking them. The Conclusions use more cautious wording ('may be the basis'), so the overstatement is mainly in the Abstract Results and in the Discussion phrases about tissue damage; a minor additional inconsistency is the CIC ratio given as 2.1 in the Abstract versus 2.2 in Table 1 and the text.

issues.title: No-spontaneous-change claim rests on non-randomised comparison of two different patient groups (55 vs 36)
issues.explanation: Groups were defined by when patients arrived after discharge, not randomised and not followed over time. Similar baseline values in the two groups are used to conclude that markers do not improve without treatment. Different patients at different times cannot show within-person natural history, and the groups were small enough that moderate differences could be missed. This weakens the implicit counterfactual for the treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Serial untreated measurements in the same patients over the 1-3 month interval.

quotes.text: Отже, без проведення відновлювального лікування в період реконвалесценції (протягом 1-3 міс) прояви оксидативного стресу після ковідної пневмонії не зменшуються

issues.title: Abstract gives CIC increase as 2.1-fold; Table 1 and Results give 2.2-fold (38.1/17.1 = 2.23)
issues.explanation: The abstract says CIC rose 2.1-fold in the whole convalescent group. Table 1 and the Results text give 2.2-fold, which matches the printed means. The 2.1 appears to be the mild-course subgroup value from Table 2. This is a small reporting slip and changes no conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the abstract figure refers to the mild-course subgroup only.

quotes.text: рівня ЦІК у 2,1 раза

issues.title: Table 3 moderate-course post-treatment CIC/NCIC printed 1.3; 24.4/17.1 = 1.43
issues.explanation: In Table 3 the post-treatment CIC ratio for moderate COVID-19 is printed as 1.3. Dividing the printed post-treatment CIC of 24.4 by the control CIC of 17.1 gives 1.43, or 1.4. The other columns in the same row reconcile, so this one cell is inconsistent with its own table. It changes one cell and no conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Individual-level data showing the ratio is not mean CIC divided by control mean, or a corrected table.

script.explanation: Table 3 moderate-course post-treatment CIC/NCIC: 24.4 / 17.1 gives 1.4269, not the printed 1.3. For the printed value to hold the denominator would have to be 18.7692, not 17.1.

10.31032/ijbpas/2025/14.1.8588.headline_claim: Physiotherapy treatment is effective and beneficial in improving quality of life in post-COVID-19 young adults compared with a non-intervention group.
10.31032/ijbpas/2025/14.1.8588.overall: The qualitative finding that the exercise group improved more than an untreated group is plausible, but the paper cannot show that the benefit is caused by physiotherapy. Allocation is undescribed, groups differ at baseline, the control received nothing, and outcomes are self-reported with no stated blinding. Several printed numbers are also internally inconsistent (two mean differences, three z statistics), so the quantitative results need correction before they can be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: SF-36 quality of life (physical functioning domain reported as primary in tables; overall QOL score)

issues.title: Allocation to intervention and control not described; baseline SF-36 scores differ between groups
issues.explanation: The paper labels the design 'experimental' but gives no method of assigning the 100 participants to Group A or B. Group A starts higher than Group B on most domains (PF 79.32 vs 68.18, BP 75.43 vs 60.64). Without a stated allocation method, selection or confounding cannot be excluded as an explanation of the group differences. This undermines the comparative conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random sequence generation and concealed allocation, or a protocol/registration documenting it.

quotes.text: Group A (Intervention group) and Group B (Control group).
Study Design: An Experimental study

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not say how participants were allocated to the intervention and control groups (no randomisation, concealment or other assignment rule is given), despite the label 'Experimental study'. Baseline SF-36 means are higher in Group A on all nine domains, with PF (11.1 points, approx. t = 2.6 from printed SDs) and BP (14.8 points) differing most; no baseline comparison is reported and the analysis does not adjust for these differences. Only PF could be formally checked, because SDs for other domains are not printed.

issues.title: Discussion means disagree with stated differences: Group A GMH (8.10 vs 13.00), Group B BP (7.73 vs 1.72)
issues.explanation: In the Discussion, every domain's stated group difference matches post minus pre except two. Group A GMH means (68.72 to 76.82) give 8.10, but the printed difference is 13.00. Group B BP means (60.64 to 68.37) give 7.73, but the printed difference is 1.72. The Group A GMH difference is the largest in the study and feeds the between-group claim. The affected cells need correcting from raw data; the other 16 pairs reconcile.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data or a table showing the printed differences (13.00 and 1.72) are correct and that the quoted pre or post means are the misprints.

quotes.text: GMH(Group A:13.00 ,Group B:1.87)

issues.title: No-treatment control and unblinded self-reported SF-36 limit attribution of the benefit to physiotherapy
issues.explanation: Group B received nothing and the primary outcome is self-reported quality of life. Any group difference can therefore reflect expectation, attention or contact time as well as the exercise itself. No blinding of assessors or analysts is described. The 'effective' conclusion is stated more strongly than this design allows, though it is at least framed relative to non-intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and analysts were blinded, or inclusion of an attention-control arm.

quotes.text: No protocol for Group B.
Both group were assessed 0 day and after 12 weeks of intervention for QOL using SF-36 Scale

issues.title: Between-group significance claimed for all nine SF-36 domains but a test is shown for PF only
issues.explanation: The Results tables give a Mann-Whitney comparison of change scores only for PF. The Discussion then states a statistical difference between groups for the whole scale without showing the other eight tests or any multiplicity adjustment. The pre-post p values quoted for the untreated Group B do not bear on treatment efficacy. Only the PF between-group result is actually supported by a reported test.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported between-group test statistics and p values for the remaining eight domains, with a stated correction for multiple testing.

quotes.text: which shows there significant different in pre and post intervention score within Group B with p<0.005
According to measure of SF-36 scale the mean difference between Group A and Group B were:-

issues.title: Reported Wilcoxon z (8.686, 7.781) and Mann-Whitney z (10.83) exceed the maximum possible for n = 50 per group
issues.explanation: With 50 paired observations the largest possible |z| for a Wilcoxon signed-rank test is about 6.15. With 50 vs 50 the largest possible |z| for a Mann-Whitney test is about 8.62. The tables print 8.686 and 7.781 for the Wilcoxon tests and 10.83 for the Mann-Whitney test. The printed test statistics are therefore not reproducible from the described design and analysis sets. The unreported analysis details (sample sizes used, tie handling) should be clarified before the p values are relied on.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the tests used a larger effective n or a different statistic (e.g. a parametric test mislabelled), or corrected table values.

quotes.text: Mann-Whitneytest

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 50 vs 50 participants
issues.explanation: The paper states group sizes but no target effect size, power or rationale. Given the large reported differences this does little to threaten the main finding, but it limits assessment of the planned analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation in a protocol or registration.

quotes.text: Group B: 50 Subjects)

10.31080/asms.2023.07.1491.headline_claim: Low-frequency transcranial magnetotherapy (DIAMAG) in complex rehabilitation significantly improves psycho-emotional state, well-being, physical tolerance and quality of life in post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients, and confirms the feasibility of this therapy.
10.31080/asms.2023.07.1491.overall: The paper's headline claim that magnetotherapy gives greater psycho-emotional improvement than placebo is not supported by the analysis shown. It rests on paired within-group tests, with no between-group comparison, no sample-size justification and unclear blinding and registration. The control group also improved on every scale, so the data may show benefit of rehabilitation overall; any added effect of the device remains unproven. A small percentage inconsistency in the second-stage EQ-5D result is minor.

issues.title: Superiority over placebo rests on paired within-group tests; no between-group comparison is reported
issues.explanation: The stated test is the Wilcoxon test 'for dependent variables', which assesses change within one group. The p-values are given per group (significant in the main group, p > 0.05 in control), and no group-by-time or between-group test appears. 'Significant in one arm but not the other' does not show that the arms differ. The control group also improved on every scale (11.5%, 19%), and the claim of 'significantly more pronounced' benefit is unsupported by the analysis shown. This is the central weakness behind the efficacy conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test (for example Mann-Whitney on change scores, or ANCOVA) showing a significant difference between arms.

quotes.text: the nonparametric Wilcoxon W test for dependent variables was used.
in the control group by 11.5% (before treatment - 12.2 ± 0.2 points; after treatment 10.8 ± 0.1 points p > 0.05)
significantly more pronounced in patients of the main group

second_reader.what_stands: The only inferential method stated is the paired (dependent-samples) Wilcoxon test, and all reported p-values are within-group before/after comparisons; no direct main-vs-control comparison (test, p-value or CI) is reported. The claim of superiority over placebo rests on contrasting a significant change in the main group with a non-significant change in the control group, which does not by itself show that the groups differ.

issues.title: Randomization method and allocation concealment not described
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were randomized into two equal groups of 30 but gives no sequence generation or concealment. Consecutive enrolment alone is not a flaw, but without these details the reader cannot confirm that allocation was unbiased. Group baselines look similar on the scales reported, which gives some reassurance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or registry entry describing computer-generated sequences with concealed allocation.

quotes.text: All subjects of the present study were randomized into 2 groups with an equal number of participants:
Subjects were included in the study sequentially

issues.title: 'Blind' trial with self-reported scales, but who was blinded is not stated
issues.explanation: The control device is described as outwardly identical and silent, which suggests participant blinding. The outcomes are self-rated questionnaires (EQ-5D, STAI, Beck, WAM), so any unmasking would bias them. The Methods do not state who was blinded, whether blinding was tested, or whether assessors were masked, even though the Conclusion asserts a 'blind' design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that participants and outcome assessors were masked to allocation, with a check of blinding integrity.

quotes.text: The results of our prospective, randomized, blind, placebocontrolled clinical trial
a placebo device that is outwardly identical to the device 'DIAMAG',  but does not generate a magnetic field when switched on

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 30 per arm while conclusions are stated confidently
issues.explanation: The paper reports 60 patients (30 per arm) and gives no power calculation. With no between-group test, no dropout accounting and multiple scales analysed, the confident conclusions that therapy 'significantly contributes' to improvement go beyond a small study of this kind. The size limitation weakens the secondary and exploratory claims, and it adds to the problem described under c3.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation justifying 30 per arm for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: The  present  study  included  60  patients
The results of the study confirm the feasibility of using lowfrequency magnetic therapy

issues.title: Identical p = 0.0019 repeated for different scales and time points; dispersions inconsistent
issues.explanation: The value p = 0.0019 is printed for EQ-5D and anxiety at the first stage, and again for EQ-5D, anxiety and later anxiety at later stages, although effect sizes differ. Reported dispersions (±0.1 to ±0.5) look like standard errors but are not labelled, and one control value has ±6.7. The tests cannot be checked or reproduced from the printed values. Their reliability is uncertain, and nothing here can be recalculated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data or a table showing each test statistic and its own p-value.

quotes.location: Results of the first stage, anxiety

quotes.text: after treatment - 33.6 ± 6.7 points, p > 0.05
quotes.location: Results of the first stage, anxiety

issues.title: Second-stage EQ-5D change printed as 25.7%, but 12.1 to 8.8 gives 27.3%
issues.explanation: The second-stage sentence gives the same 25.7% improvement as the first stage, but the post-treatment score has moved from 9.0 to 8.8. The printed 12.1 and 8.8 imply about 27.3%, so the percentage appears copied from the first stage. The first-stage figure (12.1 to 9.0, 25.6%) is consistent. The error is small and does not alter any conclusion, and it slightly understates the second-stage change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different second-stage baseline or post-treatment value (for example 9.0 rather than 8.8) in the underlying data.

quotes.text: an improvement in the quality of life according to the EQ-5D questionnaire by 25.7% was noted (before treatment - 12.1 ± 0.2 points; after treatment - 8.8 ± 0.1 points.
an increase in the quality of life according to the EQ5D questionnaire by 25.7% (before treatment - 12.1 ± 0.2 points, after treatment - 9.0 ± 0.1 points p = 0.0019)

issues.title: Follow-up schedule is inconsistent: Methods say 4 weeks, Results report a 3-week visit, plus an undescribed second course
issues.explanation: Methods describe one 14-day course and a follow-up at 4 weeks. Results report a visit at 3 weeks and another at 6 weeks 'after the second course', and no second course is described. The timing of the second-stage assessment cannot be pinned down. This is a reporting inconsistency and does not change any result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or text showing the 3-week and 4-week visits are distinct, planned assessments.

quotes.text: After  4  weeks  from  the  end  of  the  course  of  procedures
3 weeks after the complex medical rehabilitation in patients:

issues.title: No trial registration or protocol cited for a trial called prospective
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective randomized trial but gives no registry identifier or protocol reference. Readers therefore cannot confirm that the outcomes (EQ-5D, STAI, Beck, WAM, spirometry, dyspnoea) and their analysis were specified in advance. Many scales were collected and only some are reported. This limits confidence but does not itself show any outcome was switched.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry (with prespecified primary outcome) or protocol approved before enrolment.

quotes.text: The results of our prospective, randomized, blind, placebocontrolled clinical trial

10.31089/1026-9428-2024-64-10-674-680.headline_claim: A non-drug post-COVID rehabilitation technology (balneotherapy, narzan drinking therapy, oxygen aerosol inhalations, magnetotherapy and related procedures) produced a significantly more pronounced normalization of asthenia, fatigue, latent coronary insufficiency, microcirculation, immune status, lipid peroxidation/antioxidant indices and endogenous intoxication than standard drug therapy, indicating a high therapeutic effect.
10.31089/1026-9428-2024-64-10-674-680.overall: The headline claim of a high therapeutic effect of the non-drug package over drug therapy is weakly supported: allocation was not truly random, the groups were treated in different settings with a multi-component package, and key outcomes were unblinded. The tables also have unexplained features (SD-like spreads far too small, no multiplicity control, one asthenia percentage pair summing to 99.70%). The direction of the effect may be real but its size and attribution cannot be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: Not identified as a single prespecified primary outcome; the paper reports asthenia, fatigue, latent coronary insufficiency, microcirculation, immune status, oxidative-stress markers and medium-molecular peptides

issues.title: Labelled randomised, but allocation by 'unintentional selection' across two different care settings
issues.explanation: The study is called an open randomised trial, yet allocation is by 'unintentional selection' with no sequence generation or concealment described. The two groups were treated in different institutions (sanatorium in Kislovodsk, 2020-2024; city polyclinic) so setting, patient motivation and co-care differ systematically. Between-group differences cannot be attributed to the treatment, and the randomised label is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described random sequence and concealment, or evidence that patients were allocated at random between the two settings.

quotes.text: Проведено открытое рандомизированное исследование методом непреднамеренного отбора.
проходившие поликлиническую реабилитацию по ординарным схемам медикаментозной терапии постковидной симптоматики

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the study randomised, but the only allocation method named is 'unintentional selection', and the two groups were treated in different settings (sanatorium versus polyclinic). No randomisation procedure is described, so the randomised label is not supported by the text. The exactly matched group sizes and sex splits are not explained either, although the paper does not say how they arose.

issues.title: Multi-component sanatorium package compared with outpatient drug care; setting and intensity confounded
issues.explanation: The first group received spa treatment plus aeroionotherapy, magnetotherapy, ozone baths and inhalations in a sanatorium, while the second received standard polyclinic drug regimens. The comparison is a package of care in two settings, so differences cannot be attributed to any specific non-drug element, and the sanatorium stay itself (rest, removal from work) is not matched. The paper's claim is framed as a comparison of technology versus drugs, which the design does not isolate.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparator also treated in a sanatorium setting with matched rest and care intensity.

quotes.text: Пациентам второй группы (медикаментозная терапия) назначали стандартные схемы медикаментозного поликлинического лечения
Кроме этого, для пациентов первой группы наблюдения

second_reader.what_stands: The sanatorium arm received a multi-component package in a resort setting, while the comparator was unspecified standard outpatient drug therapy. Setting, treatment intensity, time away from work and the content of care all differ between arms, so the effect of the non-drug technology cannot be separated from these factors. The paper also does not report the duration or specifics of the comparator regimen.

issues.title: 'High therapeutic effect' asserted from open, non-randomly allocated comparison; limitations omit design bias
issues.explanation: The conclusion states a significantly more pronounced normalisation and a high therapeutic effect of the non-drug technology. The design cannot attribute differences to the treatment because allocation was not random, outcomes were unblinded and the groups were treated in different settings. The only limitation listed is that participants were Kislovodsk residents.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A conclusion that explicitly frames the findings as preliminary and non-randomised.

quotes.text: Полученные данные свидетельствуют о высоком терапевтическом эффекте применения немедикаментозной технологии.
Ограничения исследования. В обследованные группы включены только лица, постоянно зарегистрированные

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion asserts a 'high therapeutic effect' from an open comparison in which allocation was not shown to be random and the arms differed in setting and treatment content. The stated limitation covers only local registration and omits these design biases, as well as the lack of blinding and the unvalidated, partly subjective outcomes. One component, the ∂SO2 index (p = 0.059), did not reach the stated threshold, so the microcirculation claim is only partly supported by the paper's own table.

issues.title: Group 1 treated 2020-2024, but ethics approval is dated 14.04.2021
issues.explanation: Group 1 is described as treated in 2020-2024 while the ethics protocol is dated April 2021. Patients treated in 2020 and early 2021 would have preceded approval, or the data were collected retrospectively, which the paper does not say. The paper also reports written informed consent from every participant, so this cannot be resolved from the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that enrolment began after April 2021, or that the 2020 date refers to the COVID infection rather than the rehabilitation.

quotes.text: протокол № 4 от 14.04.2021 г.

issues.title: Open-label design with self-reported asthenia questionnaire and fatigue grading as headline outcomes
issues.explanation: The study is open, with no blinding of patients or assessors. The asthenia scale is patient-completed and the fatigue stage is a rating, both open to expectation effects, especially in a group receiving an elaborate sanatorium programme. The laboratory and ergometry outcomes are less sensitive to this, so the concern is narrower than for all results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that outcome assessors were blinded to group, or that subjective outcomes agree with blinded objective ones.

quotes.text: Проведено открытое рандомизированное исследование методом непреднамеренного отбора.
предлагалось заполнить (до и после лечения) специализированный опросник «шкала астенизации»

issues.title: Tables 2-3 between-group tests unnamed; ±values likely SEs labelled SD; no multiplicity control over ~25 outcomes
issues.explanation: Table 1 does report between-group p-values, but the tests used for the continuous data in Tables 2 and 3 are not named, and the Methods say SEM was computed while the tables are described as M±sd. The very small spreads (for example CD3+ 73.6±0.01 on n=278) are not plausible SDs for biological measures, so the significance markers cannot be checked. No correction is made for the many outcomes tested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of the test used for continuous outcomes and that ± denotes SD with raw data showing such narrow spread.

quotes.text: Анализ таблиц сопряжения проводили, используя критерий χ 2 (хи-квадрат).
* - достоверные различия до и после лечения в одной группе р ≤0,01; # - достоверные различия после лечения

issues.title: No trial registration identifier reported for an interventional comparison
issues.explanation: No registry number is given, so prespecification of outcomes and sample size cannot be verified. Given the large number of outcomes reported and no sample size justification, this limits trust but is common in this literature.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment listing the same outcomes.

quotes.text: одобрены локальным этическим комитетом ФГБНУ «НИИ МТ» г. Москва (протокол № 4 от 14.04.2021 г.)

10.31089/978-5-6042929-2-1-2021-1-54-58.headline_claim: Ozone therapy within post-COVID CNS rehabilitation reduces the intensity or fully relieves cerebrasthenic and cerebral syndromes, and is also said to restore taste and smell, improve some cognitive functions and quality of life.
10.31089/978-5-6042929-2-1-2021-1-54-58.overall: The conclusion that ozone therapy relieves post-COVID CNS symptoms rests on a non-randomized comparison with patients who had a contraindication, scored by an unnamed questionnaire and analysed only by a Pearson correlation. No outcome data, group sizes or adverse events are given, so the efficacy claims cannot be relied on from this text. Only an abstract-level description is available, so the full text could supply some missing detail.

primary_outcome.name: Severity of cerebrasthenic and cerebral syndromes (0-10 questionnaire score, start and end of rehabilitation)

issues.title: Comparison group defined by ozone contraindication, so treated and comparison patients are not comparable
issues.explanation: Efficacy is inferred by comparing patients who received ozone with patients for whom ozone was contraindicated. Contraindications usually reflect different health status (comorbidity, bleeding or other risks), so differences in outcome may reflect those differences rather than ozone. The abstract nevertheless concludes that ozone therapy relieves symptoms, and it reports no baseline comparability, group sizes or adjustment.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline characteristics showing the groups were comparable, or a randomized or adjusted analysis of the same comparison.

quotes.text: Представлен анализ динамики симптомов у группы пациентов, прошедших курс озонотерапии в сравнении с группой, где озонотерапия была противопоказана.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract states that the comparison group consisted of patients in whom ozone therapy was contraindicated. Such patients may differ systematically (comorbidity, severity) from treated patients, and the paper reports no baseline comparison, matching or adjustment. The abstract itself notes that symptom severity depended on age, severity of illness, timing of rehabilitation and comorbidity, which heightens the concern. Only the abstract is available, so a fuller text might address this.

issues.title: Only a Pearson correlation is named for outcome assessment; no between-group or pre-post test is described
issues.explanation: The abstract states that results at discharge were assessed with the Pearson correlation coefficient. A correlation does not test whether symptom scores fell or whether the ozone group fell more than the comparison group. No effect sizes, p-values or group means are given, so the efficacy conclusion has no stated statistical support. This is narrower than the screen's framing, because it reflects an abstract-only description, but the gap remains.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Full text reporting pre-post and between-group tests with effect sizes and confidence intervals.

quotes.text: Оценка результатов при выписке осуществлялась с помощью коэффициента корреляции Пирсона.

second_reader.what_stands: The only statistical method named is the Pearson correlation coefficient. No between-group comparison or pre-post test (e.g. paired test, Wilcoxon, ANCOVA) is described, and a correlation does not measure treatment effect. This is true of the text provided; the full paper might contain more.

issues.title: Conclusion of full taste/smell recovery and cognitive gains has no reported outcome data
issues.explanation: The concluding paragraph says ozone therapy fully restores taste and smell and improves certain cognitive functions. The only figures given are baseline symptom frequencies (anosmia/hyposmia 11%, memory and attention decline 42%); no post-treatment results, no cognitive testing and no comparison are reported. The conclusion is also causal despite a non-randomized comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported post-treatment rates of smell/taste recovery and cognitive test results, with a valid comparison.

quotes.text: полностью восстановить вкус и обоняние, а также улучшить определенные когнитивные функции

second_reader.what_stands: In the supplied text there are no outcome data on taste, smell or cognition, and cognition was not measured with a named instrument (only a symptom questionnaire and EQ-5D are mentioned). The conclusion of full recovery of taste and smell and cognitive improvement is therefore not supported by anything reported here. Full-text results, if they exist, were not available to check.

issues.title: Symptom severity scored 0-10 by an unnamed questionnaire with no validation or blinding described
issues.explanation: Syndrome severity is rated 0-10 by a questionnaire that is not named or referenced, and nothing is said about who administered it or whether assessors were blinded. Self-rated symptom scores in an unblinded comparison are prone to bias. Because only an abstract is available, the full text may supply the missing detail, so this weakens rather than defeats the finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Citation of a validated instrument and description of blinded administration.

quotes.text: оценка степени выраженности основных синдромов в баллах от 0 до 10 осуществлялась посредством опросника

10.31146/1682-8658-ecg-207-11-5-16.headline_claim: L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) at 9 g/day for 4 weeks corrects hyperammonemia and improves cognitive/hepatic symptoms in patients with post-COVID syndrome, and is 'effective and safe' for this use.
10.31146/1682-8658-ecg-207-11-5-16.overall: The paper shows that ammonia, NCT, ShAS and transaminases fell during 4 weeks of LOLA in 83 selected patients, but the single-arm design cannot attribute the changes to the drug. The conclusions of efficacy and safety, and the practice recommendation, go beyond that evidence. Several reported baseline values also contradict the stated entry criteria, and one percentage set sums to 105%, so data handling is not fully reliable.

primary_outcome.name: Ammonia level (blood ammonia, µmol/L) at 28 days; the paper does not name a single primary outcome

issues.title: Single-arm before-after design cannot attribute improvements to LOLA; causal wording used
issues.explanation: All 83 patients received LOLA and were compared only with their own baseline, with no control group and no blinding. Patients were selected for abnormal ammonia, transaminases and symptom scores, so some improvement is expected anyway through regression to the mean and natural recovery. The subjective scale (ShAS) and the timed NCT are also prone to expectation and practice effects. The statement that LOLA 'led to significant improvements' is therefore not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical untreated comparison group, or conclusions limited to describing changes during treatment.

quotes.text: Для коррекции ГА в рамках исследования пациенты получали дополнительно препарат LOLA в дозе 3 г 3 раза в сутки в течение 4 недель.
Назначение LOLA в дозе 3 г 3 раза в сутки в течение 4 недель привело к значимым улучшениям в объективном и субъективном состоянии пациентов.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, uncontrolled before-after series, so improvements cannot be attributed to LOLA; the Russian abstract conclusion ('привело к значимым улучшениям') nonetheless uses causal wording. The English summary says 'was associated with', which is appropriate, so the problem is specifically the stronger Russian wording.

issues.title: 'Effective and safe' and a routine testing/treatment recommendation drawn from an uncontrolled 4-week series of 83
issues.explanation: The Conclusions call LOLA effective and safe and advise ammonia testing and 9 g/day treatment for post-COVID patients. The data are 83 patients with no comparator and 4 weeks of follow-up. Zero reported adverse events in 83 patients cannot rule out an event rate of a few percent, and there is no evidence on durability or on clinical outcomes beyond scale scores.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A controlled comparison with longer follow-up and prespecified safety monitoring, or conclusions limited to a hypothesis-generating statement.

quotes.text: является достаточно эффективным и безопасным средствам для коррекции проявлений гипераммониемии у больных с постковидным синдромом
а при его повышении назначать такой категории лиц препарат

second_reader.what_stands: The 'effective and safe' conclusion and the routine recommendation to test ammonia and prescribe LOLA are drawn from an uncontrolled 4-week series of 83 patients, which cannot establish efficacy, and zero adverse events in 83 gives only limited safety assurance. The Discussion does acknowledge open questions on long-term effects and regimens, but the Conclusions do not carry this caution into the recommendation.

issues.title: Reported baseline data contradict entry criteria: ShAS <51 in 24.1%, NCT <40 s in 6%, ALT 32 U/L in one patient
issues.explanation: The Methods require ShAS ≥51, NCT >40 s and ALT/AST above 2× the upper limit of normal for inclusion. The Results then report 24.1% of patients with baseline ShAS 30-50 and 6% with baseline NCT under 40 s. The Discussion describes a patient with baseline ALT of 32 U/L and AST of 18 U/L. So the analysed cohort is not the one described by the eligibility rules, and the baseline-to-week-4 changes may include patients who had no room to improve.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that eligibility was assessed on different measurements or earlier values, or a protocol showing that these thresholds were not entry requirements.

quotes.text: Также критерием включения в исследование являлся результат 51 балла и более
до лечения лишь у 6% больных не было ПЭ (время прохождения теста менее 40 секунд)
Лишь в одном случае мы наблюдали значимое повышение уровня АЛТ с 32 ЕД/л до 190,4 ЕД/л

issues.title: NCT-based encephalopathy staging and point-of-care ammonia used without validation evidence in this population
issues.explanation: HE stage was defined only by NCT completion time, with cut-offs stated without citation. Ammonia was measured by a rapid point-of-care device, and the paper gives no validation or sample-handling details. The authors admit the staging does not reflect clinically significant neuropsychiatric impairment. This weakens how far the NCT and ammonia improvements can be read as clinical benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Citations validating the NCT cut-offs and the point-of-care ammonia device against venous reference measurements in this population.

issues.title: Baseline asthenia category percentages sum to 105.0%; 39.94% is not a whole-patient share of 83
issues.explanation: The four baseline severity shares printed in the Results add to 105.0%, which cannot describe a single cohort of 83. The moderate-asthenia figure of 39.94% matches no integer count of 83 (33/83 = 39.76%, 34/83 = 40.96%). It is most likely a typo for 34.94%, which would make the shares sum to 100%. This is a minor reporting error that does not change the efficacy conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A printed corrected value (e.g. 34.94%) or a patient-level table showing the baseline category counts.

issues.title: No trial registry number or ethics approval reported for a protocol-driven drug programme
issues.explanation: The study follows a named protocol and gives LOLA to every patient, yet no registration number or ethics committee statement appears. Readers cannot confirm that the primary outcome and the analysis were fixed in advance. This limits verifiability more than it changes the findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or ethics approval number with prespecified outcomes.

quotes.text: мультицентровое наблюдательное клиническое исследование по протоколу «Клиническое значение гипераммониемии у пациентов с постковидным синдромом (ЛИРА - COVID)»

10.31146/1682-8658-ecg-220-12-140-147.headline_claim: NAFLD has a significant effect on AST before L-ornithine-L-aspartate treatment and on ammonia at 14 days, and LOLA treatment is associated with improvement in objective indicators in patients with NAFLD and post-COVID syndrome, supporting routine ammonia testing and a 4-week 9 g/day course when ammonia is elevated.
10.31146/1682-8658-ecg-220-12-140-147.overall: The headline claim that NAFLD affects AST and ammonia and that LOLA improves outcomes is only weakly supported. It rests on a single-arm cohort, a 23-patient post-hoc subgroup, and two unadjusted, uncorrected p-values near 0.05. The table labelling errors and the sex-count mismatch are smaller but add to doubts about the reporting; the treatment-recommendation conclusion should be read as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Not specified; the paper reports pre/post changes in ammonia, ALT, AST, connection-number test and asthenia scale, and between-group NAFLD comparisons at baseline and 14 days

issues.title: Routine ammonia testing and 4-week LOLA recommended from an uncontrolled post-hoc analysis; no limitations stated
issues.explanation: The study has no control arm, a 23-patient NAFLD subgroup, and borderline unadjusted p-values. It nonetheless concludes that NAFLD 'significantly affects' the course of post-COVID syndrome and recommends ammonia testing with LOLA when raised. No limitations are acknowledged, and ammonia thresholds for treatment were not evaluated. The recommendation goes beyond what a hypothesis-generating analysis can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A limitations section and softened wording, or controlled data supporting treatment based on ammonia level.

quotes.text: Выявленные в ходе текущего post - hoc анализа данные позволяют утверждать, что НАЖБП оказывает значимое влияние на течение ПКС у пациентов.
определение уровня аммиака в крови, при повышении которого оправдано назначение таким пациентам препарата L-орнинитин L-аспартат курсом в течение 4 недель

second_reader.what_stands: The paper recommends routine ammonia testing and a 4-week 9 g/day LOLA course for patients with post-COVID syndrome on the basis of an uncontrolled post-hoc analysis in patients already selected for hyperammonaemia, and it contains no limitations section. The causal wording ('позволяют утверждать', 'оказывает значимое влияние на течение ПКС') exceeds the evidence, even though the post-hoc, observational nature of the work is named in the title.

issues.title: Benefit of LOLA inferred from uncontrolled before/after changes in a selected cohort (n=83; NAFLD subgroup n=23)
issues.explanation: All patients received LOLA and there is no untreated or placebo comparison. Entry required raised transaminases, raised ammonia and a slow connection test, so improvement at day 28 is expected from regression to the mean and natural recovery after COVID. The statement that LOLA use is 'reliably associated' with improvement, and the NAFLD-subgroup within-group p-values, cannot separate drug effect from these.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated or placebo comparison group, or an explicit statement that no treatment effect is claimed.

quotes.text: Выборка пациентов состояла из 83 человек, протестированных до и после лечения препаратом LOLA
Применение LOLA достоверно связано с улучшением объективных показателей у пациентов с НАЖБП и ПКС
В результате лечения препаратом LOLA было выявлено статистически значимое различие (ρ <0,01) по всем исследуемым показателям у пациентов из группы с НАЖБП.

second_reader.what_stands: All treatment-effect claims rest on uncontrolled before/after changes in 83 patients selected for abnormal baseline values (NAFLD n=23), with no control group, so regression to the mean, natural recovery from post-COVID illness and expectation effects cannot be separated from the drug effect. Wording such as 'достоверно связано' and 'положительное влияние' goes beyond what this design supports, although the study is labelled observational and post-hoc.

issues.title: Two borderline between-group p-values (0.043, 0.033) from ~11 uncorrected comparisons drive the main conclusions
issues.explanation: The conclusions that NAFLD affects AST and day-14 ammonia rest on two nominal p-values just under 0.05, with no multiplicity correction and no report of how many comparisons were made. With this many tests a Bonferroni or Holm threshold would not be met. Day-28 ammonia did not differ significantly, yet the authors infer a more treatment-resistant form of hyperammonaemia that needs longer therapy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified analysis plan limited to these two comparisons, or adjusted p-values that remain below the threshold.

quotes.text: Аммиак через 14 дней лечения значимо (ρ=0,033) выше, чем в группе без НАЖБП.

second_reader.what_stands: Two p-values (0.043 and 0.033) from roughly a dozen unadjusted comparisons, with no stated alpha, correction or prespecification, underpin Conclusions 1 and 2, and neither would survive a Bonferroni-type threshold. In addition, the printed day-14 ammonia means in Tables 3 and 4 (74.52 in NAFLD vs 90.35 without NAFLD) run opposite to the text claim that ammonia was higher in the NAFLD group, so the finding is internally inconsistent as presented.

issues.title: Between-group tests do not show adjustment for BMI (32.6 vs 26.7) or sex imbalance
issues.explanation: The NAFLD group has higher BMI (32.57 vs 26.69 kg/m2) and a different sex mix. The paper does not say whether the group comparisons were adjusted for these. It also does not say which test produced the between-group p-values. The attribution of the AST and ammonia differences to NAFLD itself is therefore uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Model output showing the NAFLD effect on AST and ammonia with BMI and sex as covariates.

quotes.text: в среднем ИМТ был выше у группы пациентов с НАЖБП (на 22%)
Влияние факторов на изучаемые переменные исследовалось с помощью многофакторного дисперсионного анализа ANOVA.

issues.title: Tables 3 and 4 appear to have group labels swapped: data fit n=60 in Table 3 and n=23 in Table 4
issues.explanation: Table 3 is labelled NAFLD (n=23) and Table 4 non-NAFLD (n=60). The pooled baseline means in Table 1 are reproduced only if Table 3 holds the n=60 patients. Table 4's CIs match n=23, and the higher AST and day-14 ammonia the text attributes to NAFLD are in Table 4. Readers using the tables as labelled would attribute the subgroup results to the wrong groups.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Subgroup data showing that Table 3 truly holds the 23 NAFLD patients and that Table 1 means come from some other weighting.

quotes.text: Результаты статистического исследования разности показателей до и после лечения препаратом LOLA у пациентов с НАЖБП (n=23)

issues.title: Sex counts in Table 2 (35 men, 48 women) disagree with the overall 36 men, 47 women
issues.explanation: The Results give 36 men and 47 women among 83 patients. The Table 2 subgroup counts add up to 35 men and 48 women, so one patient's sex is recorded differently in the two places. The effect on results is small, but sex is one of the imbalances between the NAFLD and non-NAFLD groups.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that one patient was reclassified, or a corrected Table 2 or Results text making the sex counts agree.

quotes.text: Из них 36 человек - мужчины (43,4%), 47 - женщины (56,6%)

10.31532/physmedrehabil.2.1.005.headline_claim: The authors conclude that supervised group telerehabilitation is feasible and safe for post-COVID condition management, and that its efficacy needs testing in future trials.
10.31532/physmedrehabil.2.1.005.overall: The feasibility conclusions (recruitment 39%, high adherence among completers, no recorded adverse events) are reasonably supported for this small pilot. Efficacy-flavoured statements ('potentially effective', encouraging moderate to large effects, the 5STS finding) are not supported given non-significant results, baseline imbalance, no multiplicity control and a completers-only analysis. The printed errors found (cough percentage, abstract age SD) are minor.

primary_outcome.name: Feasibility outcomes: recruitment rate, adherence, completion, adverse events, technological issues (no between-group efficacy test)

issues.title: Discussion calls a 21-person pilot 'potentially effective' and 'safe' despite non-significant efficacy data
issues.explanation: The Discussion states telerehabilitation is feasible, safe and potentially effective. The trial was sized only for feasibility, and no primary efficacy outcome differed between groups apart from one unadjusted 5STS result. Zero events in 11 participants only rules out common harms. The abstract's and final conclusion's hedging is appropriate, but the Discussion sentence and the 'encouraging, moderate to large effects' language go beyond the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the conclusion is a wording matter and the abstract is already more cautious.

quotes.text: telerehabilitation is feasible, safe and potentially effective
while  not  statistically  significant,  were  encouraging

issues.title: Only 5STS change difference (p=0.024) highlighted; baseline imbalance and 10 uncorrected tests
issues.explanation: The paper reports 5STS as the sole between-group improvement, using an unadjusted t-test of change scores. The arms differed at baseline on 5STS (8.6 vs 6.5 s, p=0.020), and about ten outcomes were tested without correction. At follow-up the 5STS difference was no longer significant (p=0.282). The finding is fragile and should not be read as evidence of effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A baseline-adjusted analysis, or a multiplicity-corrected analysis, still showing a significant 5STS difference.

quotes.text: improvements in 5STS test values in favour of the intervention group
At baseline, 6MWT distance for the telerehabilitation exercise group was significantly lower than the control group (516m vs 634m; p=0.016)

issues.title: Table 3 labelled n=11/n=10 but follow-up data exist for only 9 per arm; completers-only, not ITT
issues.explanation: Two intervention participants withdrew within a week and follow-up was available for 9 per arm, yet Table 3 headers give n=11 and n=10 for change scores. The analysis appears to be completers-only while being labelled as the randomised sample. This hides attrition and the analysis is not intention-to-treat. Dropout (18% of the intervention arm) could bias the exploratory results in either direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Methods stating that change scores were computed on completers with Table 3 headers describing randomised numbers, or an imputation method.

issues.title: Table 1 overall cough 2 (20%) of 21; 2/21 is 9.5%, matching the subgroups' 9% and 10%
issues.explanation: The overall column of Table 1 gives cough as 2 participants (20%) with n=21. Two of 21 is about 10%, which also fits the subgroup rows of 1/11 (9%) and 1/10 (10%). The 20% is a printing slip in a baseline descriptor and affects no conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or protocol showing 4 coughing participants overall, which would contradict the subgroup counts.

script.explanation: 2/21 = 9.52%, but the paper prints 20, outside the rounding interval [19.50, 21.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 10.0 rather than 21.

issues.title: Self-reported FACIT-Fatigue/SGRQ outcomes are unblinded yet cited as encouraging
issues.explanation: Only assessors were blinded; participants knew their allocation, so self-reported fatigue and quality of life could be influenced by expectation. The Discussion nevertheless calls the FACIT-Fatigue improvement encouraging. This is inherent to the design, and the outcomes are exploratory, so the weight is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable.

issues.title: Abstract gives age SD 14 years; Table 1 gives 15 for the overall sample
issues.explanation: The abstract reports mean age 53 ± 14 years but Table 1 reports 53 (15). The arm means (59 vs 47) and arm SDs (14, 13) imply an overall SD near 15, so the abstract value is probably the error. This is a cosmetic descriptive discrepancy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing an overall age SD that rounds to 14.
