10.31655/2307-3373-2022-1-2-27-34.headline_claim: A nutritional supplement ('ІмуноАктив') normalises red blood cell indices and has a favourable immunomodulatory effect on humoral and cellular immunity in patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome.
10.31655/2307-3373-2022-1-2-27-34.overall: The claim that the supplement normalises red-blood and immune indices is not supported: it rests on separate within-arm tests in about 18-19 patients per arm, with no between-arm test, no blinding or placebo, no stated primary outcome and no multiplicity handling. The text also contradicts its own tables in several places and some significance flags cannot be reproduced from the printed summary statistics. The study can be read as hypothesis-generating at best.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; haematological and immunological indices (haemoglobin, erythrocytes, immune subsets, immunoglobulins)

issues.title: Supplement benefit concluded from within-arm changes; no between-group test of change vs rehab-only arm
issues.explanation: The conclusion that the supplement 'normalises' red-blood indices and has immunomodulatory effects rests on pre/post tests in each arm and on comparing which arm reached p<0.05. No test of the difference in change (or in post-treatment values) between group 2 and group 1 is reported, even though group 1 is available. There was no placebo or blinding, so expectation and the supplement cannot be separated, and the outcomes are laboratory indices. The headline efficacy claim is therefore not supported by the analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group analysis (e.g. ANCOVA or difference in change with CI) showing a significant effect favouring group 2.

quotes.text: Застосування біодобавки «ІмуноАктив» нормалізує показники «червоної крові»

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion that the supplement 'normalizes red blood' rests on within-arm before/after tests (p2 <0.05 in group 2) and on a descriptive contrast with group 1; no between-arm test of change (or ANCOVA/difference with CI) is reported. The point is a limitation of inference, not a miscalculation: the numerical direction favours group 2 (+5.5 vs -3.5 g/L), but a formal comparison against the rehab-only arm is missing, and the word 'normalizes' is also a stronger claim than the data on haemoglobin support, since group 2's baseline mean was already inside the reference range.

issues.title: About 28 indices tested with no primary outcome or across-outcome correction (SNK only within each index)
issues.explanation: Twelve haematological and sixteen immune indices are each tested at p<0.05, with SNK used only for multiple comparison of group means. No primary outcome is declared and there is no adjustment across indices. The positive conclusions rest on whichever indices crossed 0.05, so some are likely chance findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or a stated correction across indices.

quotes.text: Стьюдента-Н'юмена-Кейлса

issues.title: Several 'p<0.05' flags do not match the printed means and SDs (e.g. platelets 259.71 vs 245.10)
issues.explanation: Several differences are flagged significant that are small relative to the printed SDs, for example group 1 platelets vs controls (difference 14.6 with SDs of 27-38) and group 1 haemoglobin before vs after (difference 3.5 with SDs of 11-15). The tables give only p>0.05 or p<0.05 and the test used for each comparison is unclear, so these flags cannot be verified. If some are wrong, the apparent effects on indices would shrink, and the same unclear testing applies to the group 2 results the conclusions rely on.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of the tests used for each flag and exact p-values, or paired-test details that reproduce the printed flags.

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

issues.title: Allocation described only as 'random sampling'; no sequence, concealment or blinding stated
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were randomised by 'random sampling' without describing how allocation was generated or concealed, and there is no blinding. The demographic imbalance the screen cites is small, so the concern is mainly the undescribed method. This weakens the between-arm comparison, but the paper makes no between-arm test anyway.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol describing computer-generated allocation with concealment.

quotes.text: методом випадкової вибірки

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; 16/19/18 per group called 'sufficient' for confident conclusions
issues.explanation: Group sizes are 16 (control), 19 and 18, with no power calculation, and the authors assert the groups are sufficient for a representative sample. With about 18 per arm and many outcomes, effect estimates are imprecise. The confident conclusions of normalisation go beyond what such a sample can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation supporting the detected effect sizes.

quotes.text: достатні для репрезентативної вибірки

issues.title: Baseline complaint percentages do not fit group sizes: 17/19 printed as 84.5%; group 2 values fit n=17 not 18
issues.explanation: The fatigue count of 17 in group 1 (n=19) is printed as 84.5%, but 17/19 is 89.5%. Group 2 is stated as 18 patients, but 11 (64.7%) and 13 (76.5%) correspond to a denominator of 17, not 18. These are descriptive baseline figures, so they do not change the efficacy results. They show that the denominators or counts were not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that complaint percentages used different denominators (e.g. one group-2 patient lacking data), or a corrected table.

issues.title: Manufacturer named; no funding or conflict-of-interest statement in a study of that product
issues.explanation: The study evaluates a product from the named manufacturer and reports positive results, yet gives no funding or conflict statement. Whether the manufacturer funded or supplied the work is unknown. This leaves a gap in transparency for a positive efficacy claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A funding and conflict-of-interest statement showing independence from the manufacturer.

issues.explanation: The Results say group 2 had a relative increase in several white-cell types 'with a simultaneous decrease' in lymphocytes, which is then read as a stimulating effect on haemopoiesis. Table 2 shows lymphocytes rising slightly. The same paragraph also says lymphocytes increased relative to group 1. The interpretation built on this sentence is unsupported.

10.31655/2307-3373-2024-3-5-15.headline_claim: Erdosteine plus breathing exercises added to standard inhaled corticosteroid/formoterol therapy improves asthma control, lung function and exercise tolerance in asthma patients after COVID-19 ("clinical effectiveness 99.3%").
10.31655/2307-3373-2024-3-5-15.overall: The directional finding that the main group improved on ACT, ACQ-7, several spirometry indices and 6MWT is plausible, but the design (unallocated, open-label, no placebo, n=15/arm) and the analysis (within-group tests only) do not show that the added treatment is better than control. The headline '99.3% clinical effectiveness' is inconsistent with the paper's own 14/15 = 93.3%, and the FEV1/FVC significance claim contradicts Table 2.

primary_outcome.name: Asthma control (ACT and ACQ-7 scores)

issues.title: Only within-group before/after t-tests; no between-group test of change despite implied superiority
issues.explanation: Every significance marker compares a group's own before and after values, and the only test named is Student's t. The paper contrasts a 'significant, clinically important' change in the main group with 'not reached' in the control group. That is a difference in significance, not a tested difference between groups. Unpaired t-tests in Excel on 15 patients per arm are also a weak basis, and nothing is adjusted for the baseline imbalances or for the many outcomes tested. The superiority of erdosteine plus exercises is therefore not demonstrated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group comparison of change scores (or an ANCOVA on post-treatment values with baseline adjustment) showing a significant treatment effect.

quotes.text: статистично достовірна відмінність показника до та після лікування (р<0,05)

second_reader.what_stands: Every reported significance marker refers to a within-group before/after comparison, and no between-group test of change (or adjusted comparison) is reported, although the abstract and conclusions credit the added treatment. My own check shows the post-treatment ACT values differ by only 0,6 points (t≈0,65, assuming ± is SEM), so the claimed advantage for ACT rests on comparing mean changes against a clinical threshold and not on a formal test.

issues.title: No allocation method described for two groups of 15; baseline ACT and MEF75 differ between groups
issues.explanation: The paper never says how the 30 patients were assigned to the erdosteine or control group, and nothing indicates randomization or concealment. The groups start from different places, for example ACT 11.1 vs 13.1 and MEF75 31.0% vs 43.9%. Any between-group difference in change could therefore reflect allocation and regression to the mean rather than treatment. The age difference cited by the screen is not a real concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the full protocol that allocation was randomized with concealment.

quotes.text: до контрольної групи було включено 15 хворих

second_reader.what_stands: The paper gives no allocation or randomisation method for the two groups of 15, and the main group starts with worse values on every outcome shown; by my calculation the MEF75 gap (about 12,9 points, t≈2,1) and the ACT gap (2,0 points, t≈1,8, assuming ± is SEM) are noticeable. Whether these gaps reflect allocation or chance cannot be determined, since the paper reports no baseline comparison and the statement about significance is my own computation assuming ± is SEM.

issues.title: Open-label add-on design with no placebo; primary outcomes are patient-reported ACT/ACQ-7
issues.explanation: The control arm received only background therapy, and the intervention arm received erdosteine plus breathing exercises and extra clinical attention. No placebo, sham or blinding is described. Patient-reported questionnaires are susceptible to expectation and attention effects. Erdosteine and breathing exercises are also bundled, so the effect of either one cannot be separated from the other.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of blinded outcome assessment or a placebo/sham control in the study protocol.

quotes.text: Пацієнти контрольної групи отримували лікування комбінацією ІКС + формотерол в якості підтримуючої терапії та для полегшення симптомів протягом 2 місяців.

second_reader.what_stands: As described, the design has no placebo and no stated masking, and the headline outcomes (ACT, ACQ-7) are patient-reported, so the results are open to expectation effects that the paper does not discuss. The paper does not use the term 'open-label' and does not formally name ACT/ACQ-7 as primary outcomes, but they are the outcomes featured in the abstract and conclusions.

issues.title: Clinical effectiveness printed as 99.3% in abstract and conclusions, but results give 14/15 = 93.3%
issues.explanation: The abstract and Conclusion 3 state a clinical effectiveness of 99.3%. The only effectiveness figure derived in the Results is 14 of 15 patients (93.3%). With 15 patients, 99.3% cannot be obtained as a share of patients, and no other definition of 'effectiveness' is given. The headline number is therefore unsupported and overstates the reported result. The Results also say improvement was seen in all main-group patients, which sits awkwardly with 14 of 15.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated definition of clinical effectiveness (for example a composite or a weighted index) that yields 99.3% from the study data.

досягнута у 14 (93,3 %) із 15 хворих

issues.title: FEV1/FVC called significantly improved in main group, but 64.6 to 67.6 carries no significance marker
issues.explanation: The abstract and Results list FEV1/FVC among the main-group parameters that rose with a statistically significant difference. In Table 2 the FEV1/FVC row has no asterisk, while the other significant rows do. The 3.0-point change is small against SEMs of 3.4 and 2.4, so the unmarked cell looks right and the text overstates the lung-function result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A paired test on the individual FEV1/FVC values showing p<0.05 in the main group.

quotes.location: Table 2, FEV1/FVC row, main group after treatment

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 15 patients per arm
issues.explanation: The paper reports no sample-size calculation, so it cannot be judged whether 15 per arm can detect the differences claimed. For a small pilot-type study this alone is a modest limitation. It matters more because the conclusions are stated confidently, without caveat.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation or a statement that the study was an exploratory pilot.

quotes.text: до контрольної групи було включено 15 хворих

10.3177/jnsv.70.174.headline_claim: Eight weeks of creatine-glucose supplementation alleviates clinical features of long COVID, and glucose may boost creatine's efficacy in brain creatine replenishment.
10.3177/jnsv.70.174.overall: The headline claim that creatine-glucose is effective and may be better than creatine alone is not supported: it rests on within-arm significance in five patients per arm, while every between-group test for symptoms, fatigue and exercise, and creatine versus creatine-glucose, is null. The only formal between-group findings (two brain locations) come from uncorrected testing across many outcomes. The study is suitable as a hypothesis-generating pilot only.

primary_outcome.name: Total creatine by MRS at brain locations (between-group interaction); the paper also names patient-reported outcomes and exercise tolerance as main outcomes

issues.title: Benefit and glucose advantage inferred from within-arm significance while between-group tests are null
issues.explanation: The symptom reductions and the claimed benefit of glucose rest on whether each arm's change from baseline reached p <= 0.05. The interaction tests for symptoms, fatigue and time to exhaustion were all non-significant, and creatine and creatine-glucose did not differ. The 'eight of fourteen versus three of fourteen locations' comparison contrasts significance in two small arms and is not a test of the difference between them. The glucose control arm also improved on several symptoms, so the symptom gains are not shown to exceed placebo.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-arm comparison (e.g. creatine-glucose vs creatine, or vs control) of symptom change showing a significant difference after multiplicity control.

quotes.text: no  significant  differences  for  time  to  exhaustion,  fatigue  subdomains,  and  patient-reported  symptoms  between  three  groups
Although no significant  differences  were  reported  between  creatine  and creatine-glucose
demonstrating  a  possible  benefit  of  adding  glucose  to the creatine intervention in long COVID

second_reader.what_stands: The glucose-advantage inference rests on counting within-arm significant results (8/14 vs 3/14 locations, 5/8 vs 3/8 symptoms), even though the paper reports no significant creatine vs creatine-glucose difference and null three-group interactions for exhaustion time, fatigue and symptoms. Within-arm effects for symptoms also appear in the glucose arm (anosmia, body aches). The wording is hedged ('possible benefit'), but the argument does not rest on a valid between-arm comparison.

issues.title: Five patients per arm and no sample-size calculation, yet treatment described as effective and recommendable
issues.explanation: Fifteen patients were split into three arms of five, and no sample-size calculation is reported. At this size, apparent differences between arms, particularly baseline imbalances and effect sizes, are highly unstable. The summary nonetheless states the treatment could be recommended as effective.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size justification or confirmation in a larger trial.

quotes.text: could be recommended as an effective procedure in replenishing brain creatine pool and alleviating long COVID features
pilot study, we investigated whether

second_reader.what_stands: There are five patients per arm and no sample-size justification is reported, yet the title, Summary and Discussion describe the intervention as effective and recommendable. The 'pilot', 'preliminary' and 'could' qualifiers and the call for larger trials soften the claim but do not make it consistent with n = 5 per arm.

issues.title: Stated Bonferroni correction not visible: p <= 0.05 used across about 27 outcomes and two creatine groups
issues.explanation: The Methods say a Bonferroni correction was used, but significance is set at p <= 0.05 and the reported p values appear unadjusted. Across 14 creatine locations alone, a Bonferroni threshold would be roughly 0.0036, and the two interaction p values (0.008 and 0.019) would not pass. Fewer than the few sporadic results quoted would survive.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported adjusted p-values or an adjusted alpha applied to the interaction and within-group tests.

quotes.text: A Bonferroni correction was utilized to mitigate the risk of
Significance was set at p # 0.05.

second_reader.what_stands: The Methods mention a Bonferroni correction, but the results are declared significant at the nominal p ≤ 0.05 and no corrected threshold or adjusted p-value is reported. The two interaction results (p = 0.008, 0.019) would not pass any plausible Bonferroni threshold (0.0036 or 0.0018). Many within-arm results at p ≈ 0.03–0.05 would not pass either. The correction, if applied, is not visible or described.

issues.title: Time-to-exhaustion gain of 20 s has 95% CI -173 to 213 s yet is called significant (p = 0.03)
issues.explanation: The text reports a 20 s improvement in time to exhaustion with a 95% CI that runs from about -173 to 213 s. That interval comfortably includes zero, so it cannot go with p = 0.03. With n = 5, the CI implies SE of about 70 s and p of about 0.8. The 'significant' time-to-exhaustion result for creatine is not supported as reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected CI that excludes zero, or a statement that p came from a different test (e.g. Wilcoxon) with a CI not tied to the paired t distribution.

quotes.text: significantly improved for 20 s (95% CI, from 2 173 to 213)

script.explanation: the p-value recovered from the CI is 0.8391 (reachable range [0.8347, 0.8434] across the printed precision of the estimate and its bounds), but p = 0.03 is reported -- this recovery inverts a WALD interval, so if the paper used a bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood or Fieller interval the two numbers are not comparable; confirm the method before treating this as a finding; the CI includes the null (0.0), but the reported p = 0.03 says the result is significant

issues.title: Text says both creatine groups beat control on general malaise; creatine-glucose fell 1.0 vs control 1.6
issues.explanation: The text says both experimental groups tended to be better than control for general malaise. In Table 1, the creatine-glucose group fell by 1.0 point while control fell by 1.6. The statement holds only for the creatine-alone group (4.2 to 1.0). This is a small, non-significant point, but it goes in favour of the glucose claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An adjusted between-group analysis for malaise showing creatine-glucose ahead of control.

quotes.text: tended to be superior to the participants from control group

quotes.location: Table 1, General malaise, creatine plus glucose baseline

issues.title: No registry identifier given; study described as extension arm of a primary trial
issues.explanation: No trial registration number appears, and the protocol is deferred to a primary trial. Without it, the pre-specified primary outcome and analysis plan cannot be checked. The paper lists many 'main outcomes' (14 locations, fatigue, symptoms, treadmill).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry record for this extension arm that lists the primary outcome before data collection.

quotes.text: the current study was an extension arm focused to explore alternative creatine intake

10.31893/health.2026001.headline_claim: Traditional and elastic resistance training are safe and effectively enhance muscle strength and reduce Long COVID symptom severity, with potential to improve quality of life.
10.31893/health.2026001.overall: The headline conclusion that traditional and elastic RT are safe, strengthen muscle and reduce Long COVID symptoms is not supported by this design: eight completers, no non-exercise control, and arms pooled post hoc after a null interaction. The pre-post changes are suggestive for a pilot, and the ELAS-only claim and the safety statement go beyond the evidence. Several numeric slips (the DSQ-COVID significance sentence, Table 1/2 baselines, the effect-size column) are individually minor but show weak internal checking.

primary_outcome.name: Not pre-specified; DSQ-COVID total symptom score and strength variables, with Group*Time interaction as the between-group test

issues.title: Efficacy concluded from post-hoc pooled pre-post change in 8 people with no non-exercise control
issues.explanation: The strength and symptom 'improvements' come from a paired comparison of all eight participants, pooled after the arm comparison showed no significant interaction. There is no non-exercise control, no sample-size calculation, and four per arm, and the Discussion itself says no between-group or strength effect was found at the design level. Time, expectation, learning effects and natural recovery cannot be separated from training. The conclusion that RT 'effectively enhances' strength and reduces symptoms is stronger than this design can support. The attributions in the secondary analyses (SBP change, with one participant starting antihypertensives) are weaker still.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A non-exercise comparison group, or an analysis showing the changes exceed those expected from time alone.

quotes.text: a paired T-test was performed to assess the effect of the training intervention in both groups together, regardless of the initial allocation.
Lastly, the lack of a control group not undergoing exercise is another limitation of this study.
In conclusion, RT, whether traditional or using elastic extensors, effectively enhances muscle strength and reduces the severity of Long COVID symptoms

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy conclusions rest on a pooled pre-post paired t-test in 8 completers (of 13 enrolled) with no non-exercise control, and the Conclusions state efficacy in causal terms even though the authors list the missing control group as a limitation and call the study a pilot. The limitation is disclosed, so the problem is that the conclusion language is stronger than the design supports, not that it is concealed.

issues.title: ELAS-only symptom reduction (P = 0.04) headlined though the Group*Time interaction was not significant
issues.explanation: The Abstract says symptoms fell significantly after training only in the ELAS group. The test comparing the two arms over time was not significant, so the data do not show that ELAS differs from TRAD. The Tukey post-hoc results (p = 0.043 and 0.045) are borderline and come from four participants. The 'only in ELAS' framing therefore rests on a difference between significant and non-significant results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant Group*Time interaction, or a direct between-arm contrast showing ELAS superior.

quotes.text: after training only in the ELAS group (P = 0.04)
Repeated measures ANOVA showed no statistically significant differences for the Group*Time interaction.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract headlines a significant symptom reduction 'only in the ELAS group (P = 0.04)' while the Group*Time interaction was not significant, so the data do not support a claim that ELAS differs from TRAD; the ~45% figure quoted next to it is the pooled n = 8 change, not an ELAS-only value. The null interaction is stated in Results but not in the abstract, and the exact ELAS post-hoc values (0.043 and 0.045) are close to the threshold, so the '0.04' is also slightly loosely rounded.

issues.title: Discussion says DSQ-COVID reduction was non-significant; Table 2 gives p = 0.006, d = 1.33
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the DSQ-COVID reduction did not reach statistical significance and had a moderate effect size. Table 2 and the Results give p = 0.006 and d = 1.33, which is significant and large. The sentence appears to mix up the total score with the individual symptoms. The error understates one of the paper's own positive results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sentence refers only to the three individual symptoms, not the total DSQ-COVID score.

quotes.text: Although this reduction did not reach statistical significance, the effect size was moderate
Systolic blood pressure (SBP), DSQ-COVID score, as well as absolute and relative muscle strength presented significant improvement after the intervention (Table 2).

issues.title: 'Safe' concluded from absence of desaturation and PEM in 8 participants, without systematic adverse-event reporting
issues.explanation: Safety is inferred from two monitored events (desaturation and PEM) in eight people. The paper describes no PEM assessment tool and no adverse-event collection, and one participant started a new antihypertensive. The statement that traditional and elastic RT 'are safe' goes beyond the data; 'feasible and no desaturation or PEM observed' would be supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified adverse-event log and PEM questionnaire showing no events.

quotes.text: RT was demonstrated to be both feasible and safe, as no instances of desaturation or PEM were observed during the intervention.

issues.title: Table 2 effect sizes do not match p-values (HGS p = 0.012 with d = -0.10; uric acid p = 0.589 with d = -1.0)
issues.explanation: Several effect sizes in Table 2 do not fit their own paired p-values. Significant changes (SBP, HGS, RHGS at p about 0.01-0.04) have d = -0.10, while non-significant ones carry larger values (uric acid d = -1.0, p = 0.589). Signs also run opposite to the direction of change. The effect-size column cannot be used to judge the size of benefits, and the Discussion's reliance on effect sizes is unsound.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated formula for d that yields the printed values from the data.

quotes.text: The deltas of variation of all variables were also analyzed, and Cohen's d effect sizes were calculated.

issues.title: 5 of 13 volunteers (38%) dropped out; efficacy analysed in 8 completers only, with no ITT or sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Five of thirteen enrolled participants left, and three gave no reason. All results are from the eight completers, so the effects could reflect who stayed (more tolerant or motivated participants). No intention-to-treat or missing-data analysis is given. The paper does not say whether allocation preceded withdrawal.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that allocation took place only after the five withdrew, or an analysis including baseline data on the withdrawers.

quotes.text: five withdrew (two of them missed sessions due to traveling, and the other three stopped going without providing the reason), leaving eight participants who completed the study.

issues.title: Baseline totals differ between Tables 1 and 2: body fat 36.6 vs 36.3; RHGS 1.1 vs 1.16
issues.explanation: The same pre-intervention variable is given two different values in Table 1 and Table 2, and one total sits outside what its group means allow. The body fat total of 36.6 cannot come from groups of 4 and 4 averaging 36.35. The RHGS total of 1.16 lies outside the range implied by two groups both reported as 1.1. The discrepancies are small and do not change any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing that the totals are computed differently from the group means.

issues.title: Table 3 Minimum/Maximum columns reversed for symptom rows (fatigue -25.0 min, -87.5 max)
issues.explanation: For the symptom rows the 'Minimum' is less negative than the 'Maximum', which reverses the numerical order. The DSQ-COVID row in the same table uses the correct order. The Discussion's '87%' reduction matches the value labelled Maximum. Only the labels are affected, not the means.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table note stating that Min/Max refer to magnitude of reduction.

quotes.text: was reduced by more than 87% in a single participant
Fatigue/extreme tiredness (AU)

10.32000/2072-1757-2022-7-140-145.headline_claim: Heated oxygen-helium mixture inhalations are effective and can be recommended for patients in the long-COVID period.
10.32000/2072-1757-2022-7-140-145.overall: The study is a small, unblinded group comparison with an undescribed allocation method. Some objective between-group differences (breath-hold gain, SpO2 change, VC gain) are suggestive, but dyspnoea and FEV1 benefits are claimed from within-group tests and several results are not corrected for multiplicity. The recommendation for clinical use is not supported; the findings are at best hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; compared outcomes include mMRC dyspnea score, SpO2, spirometry (FVC%, FEV1%), Stange breath-hold test, and LCI%

issues.title: Clinical recommendation and 'marked, rapid regression' rest on 40 patients, unblinded, with mixed results
issues.explanation: The Conclusions recommend the method for long-COVID. Yet the study has 20 patients per arm, no sample-size calculation, no stated randomisation or blinding, and a short course of 7 sessions. Dyspnoea and FEV1 differences between groups are not significant, and the LCI claim rests on a within-group trend (p=0.055) with no control comparison. The phrases 'marked and rapid regression' and 'proved' effects are not supported at this level of evidence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-registered, adequately powered, blinded comparison showing consistent between-group benefit on the main outcomes.

quotes.text: Это сопровождается заметным и быстрым регрессом патологической симптоматики у пациентов, перенесших COVID-19
лечебные сеансы дыхания подогретой кислородно-гелиевой смесью могут быть рекомендованы к использованию в периоде lond-COVID.

second_reader.what_stands: The recommendation and the phrase 'заметный и быстрый регресс' rest on 40 patients (20 per arm) in a study with no described blinding or allocation method, and the results are mixed: several between-group comparisons (end-of-study mMRC, VC%, FEV1%, FEV1 gain, LCI) are non-significant, the control group's SpO2 also improved significantly, and no multiplicity correction or limitations section is given. The conclusion is therefore stronger than the data support.

issues.title: Allocation to heliox vs control groups is not described; no randomisation or blinding stated
issues.explanation: The paper says only that patients 'were divided' into two groups. It gives no randomisation, allocation concealment, blinding or registration. Without these, selection and assessor bias cannot be excluded, and the between-group comparisons cannot be read as causal. Equal group sizes and similar baselines are reassuring, but they do not establish unbiased allocation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or methods statement describing concealed random allocation and blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: Пациенты были разделены на 2 группы: I группа - получающие ингаляции КГС, II группа - контрольная.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states only that patients 'were divided' into an inhalation group and a control group; it does not say how allocation was done, whether it was random, whether it was concealed, or whether anyone (patients, clinicians, outcome assessors) was blinded, and it does not describe what the control group received (e.g., sham inhalation). Baseline similarity in Table 1 is reported but does not substitute for a description of the allocation method.

issues.title: No sham inhalation or blinding: subjective outcomes (mMRC, symptom scales) open to expectation effects
issues.explanation: Controls received only general advice and antihypertensive adjustment, with no sham breathing session and no stated masking. The mMRC score and the five-point symptom ratings are patient-reported and prone to placebo response after 7 supervised sessions. Objective measures such as SpO2 and spirometry are less affected, so the concern is narrower than the screen states. Contact time and attention also differed between the arms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that a sham inhalation was given or that patients and assessors were blinded.

quotes.text: Всем пациентам были рекомендованы прогулки на свежем воздухе, полноценное белковое питание, проводилась коррекция ранее назначенной гипотензивной терапии.

issues.title: Dyspnoea and FEV1 benefit claimed from within-group tests; between-group p = 0.1649 and 0.1055
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion say that dyspnoea fell and FEV1 rose in the heliox group, citing within-group Wilcoxon p-values (0.0082, 0.0075). The between-group comparisons for these outcomes are not significant (mMRC after treatment p=0.1649; FEV1 gain p=0.1055). A significant change in one arm and a non-significant change in the other does not show that the arms differ. Other results (SpO2 and breath-hold change, VC gain) do rest on between-group tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group test (e.g. ANCOVA on the change) showing a significant difference in mMRC and FEV1.

quotes.text: В группе КГС отмечен прирост объема форсированного выдоха за 1 сек в % (ОФВ1%)%) (W-критерий Уилкоксона p = 0,0075) и снижение балла одышки по шкале mMRC (W-критерий Уилкоксона p = 0,0082*).
Прирост ОФВ1 (%)

issues.title: About a dozen outcomes tested with no multiplicity correction; several p-values only just below 0.05
issues.explanation: The paper compares at least a dozen outcomes and complaint scales, plus baseline and follow-up, with pairwise Mann-Whitney tests and no adjustment. Results such as post-treatment SpO2 (p=0.0285) and VC gain (p=0.0132) would not survive a Bonferroni-type threshold. Only the breath-hold change (p<0.001) clearly would. No primary outcome is designated, so any significant result is treated as evidence of benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or a stated correction for multiple comparisons.

quotes.text: дополнительно проводилось парное сравнение совокупностей при помощи U-критерия Манна - Уитни

issues.title: Table 1 percentages do not match counts at n=20 (18 shown as 94%, 8 as 30%, 7 as 33%)
issues.explanation: With 20 patients per group, 18 is 90% and 2 is 10%, but Table 1 prints 94% and 6% for diabetes and smoking in group 2. The sex row has the same problem: 8 of 20 men is printed as 30% (it is 40%) and 7 of 20 as 33% (it is 35%). These are baseline descriptive errors, so they do not change the efficacy results. They do show that the table was not carefully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that group 2 percentages were computed on a different denominator (e.g. 17-19 patients with data), or a corrected table.

script.explanation: 18/20 = 90.00%, but the paper prints 94, outside the rounding interval [93.50, 95.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 19.1 rather than 20.

10.32382/fis.v15i1.54.headline_claim: ACBT increases VO2 max in COVID-19 survivors at BBKPM Makassar and reduces post-COVID sequelae such as dyspnoea and sputum retention.
10.32382/fis.v15i1.54.overall: The headline claim that ACBT increases VO2 max and reduces post-COVID sequelae is not supported: it rests on an uncontrolled study of 15 participants with an unvalidated, formula-derived outcome. The statistical reporting is also internally inconsistent (independent versus paired test, no test statistic). At most the data show a small rise in estimated walk-test performance after 4 weeks, with no way to attribute it to ACBT.

primary_outcome.name: VO2 max (estimated from 6-minute walk test distance)

issues.title: Causal efficacy claimed from an uncontrolled single-group pre-post study of 15 people with no control arm
issues.explanation: All 15 participants received ACBT and were measured before and after 4 weeks; there is no control group, randomisation or blinding. Any change in the walk-test-derived VO2 max could reflect natural recovery after COVID-19, practice on the second walk test, or other factors. The paper nonetheless states that ACBT has an effect on VO2 max and 'mampu meningkatkan' it. The design supports at most an observed change, not efficacy. Methods text also wrongly refers to a control group design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control group measured on the same schedule showing a smaller change.

quotes.text: Metode: Penelitian ini merupakan  penelitian  Quasi Experiment dengan  pre-post test design with one  group
Artinya  pemberian  latihan  Active  Cycle  of  Breathing  Technique  mempunyai pengaruh  terhadap  peningkatan  VO2 Max pada  individu  pasca COVID-19.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper tests a single group of 15 people before and after a 4-week programme with no comparison group. It still concludes that ACBT 'has an effect' on VO2 max, which a pre-post change alone cannot establish, since natural recovery, practice with the walk test and regression to the mean are not separated out. The paper itself concedes the design is not a true experiment and that extraneous variables may have influenced the outcome.

issues.title: Conclusions claim reduced dyspnoea, sputum retention and chest expansion loss; none was measured
issues.explanation: The only outcome analysed is 6MWT-estimated VO2 max in 15 participants. The conclusions nonetheless state that ACBT reduces post-COVID sequelae such as breathlessness, sputum retention and reduced thoracic expansion, and improves functional respiratory capacity. No data on these symptoms or on lung function are shown, and the participants were described as having mild or no severe long COVID, so there was little sputum or dyspnoea to reduce. These claims are unsupported by the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported pre-post measurements of dyspnoea, sputum and chest expansion showing improvement.

quotes.text: Active Cycle of Breathing Technique mampu  mengurangi gejala sisa  pasca COVID-19  seperti  sesak  nafas,  retensi sputum, penurunan  ekspansi thorax
Active Cycle of Breathing Technique mampu meningkatkan kemampuan fungsional respirasi

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion that ACBT reduces dyspnoea, sputum retention and loss of chest expansion has no data behind it, since none of these was measured or reported. The claim of improved functional respiratory ability rests only on the 6MWT-derived VO2 max, which is the same outcome already claimed in the first conclusion, so it is not additional evidence.

issues.title: VO2 max is a walk-distance estimate from an unnamed formula, with no units, and not validated for this group
issues.explanation: VO2 max was not measured directly; walk distance from the 6MWT was put into an unspecified formula. Since the formula, units and validation are not reported, readers cannot tell what the values of 9.04 and 9.68 represent or whether a 0.64 change is physiologically meaningful. Because the estimate is a deterministic function of walk distance, the outcome is effectively a 6MWT change and is also vulnerable to learning effects. This weakens the main result and means 'VO2 max' is overstated as a label.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A cited, validated formula for 6MWT-derived VO2 max in post-COVID adults and printed units consistent with it.

quotes.text: setelah  didapatkan  jarak  dari  Six  Minutes Walking  Test,  maka  dimasukkan  ke  dalam rumus  VO2  Max
Alat  ukur  VO2  Max  menggunakan 6  Minutes  Walking Test (6MWT).

second_reader.what_stands: VO2 max is not measured directly; it is calculated from 6MWT distance with an unnamed, uncited equation, and no unit is reported for the 9.04 and 9.68 values. The paper offers no evidence that the estimate is valid for post-COVID adults. The point that the group is unvalidated is true in the sense that no validation is given; whether a suitable published equation exists elsewhere cannot be judged from this paper.

issues.title: Results text names an independent t-test; Table 5.2 names a paired t-test for the same pre-post comparison
issues.explanation: The Results text says an independent-samples t-test was used for the pre-post VO2 max comparison, while the Table 5.2 note says Paired Sample T-Test. The data are within-subject, so a paired test is the appropriate one and is probably what was run, but the paper does not say which, and the methods section also describes unpaired and control-group tests that were never used. The reported p of 0,000 therefore cannot be traced to a clearly stated test. The size of the effect (0.64 on SDs of about 0.3 to 0.5) makes a significant paired result plausible, so this is a reporting inconsistency rather than a change in conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement from the authors or the raw data showing a paired t-test was run, with the 'independent' sentence being a template remnant.

quotes.text: lalu dilakukan uji independent  sample t-test
Ket : Paired Sample T-Test

10.32592/ircmj.2023.25.4.2080.headline_claim: Clarithromycin was more effective than HCQ and placebo for post-acute COVID-19 cough, HCQ was more effective for shortness of breath, and the authors conclude there was no marked difference in efficacy between HCQ and clarithromycin.
10.32592/ircmj.2023.25.4.2080.overall: The paper's headline comparative claims (clarithromycin better for cough and lung function, HCQ better for dyspnoea and in younger/milder patients) are not supported by its own data: nearly all Table 2 comparisons are non-significant, the lung-function statement contradicts the table, and the Conclusion itself says no marked difference was found. Treat it as a small, exploratory 34-patient study with several printed inconsistencies, not evidence of drug-specific efficacy.

primary_outcome.name: VAS cough

issues.title: Within-arm subgroup correlations (n=12 per arm) presented as predictors of HCQ response, age effect non-significant
issues.explanation: Table 5 reports subgroup differences within each arm (e.g. HCQ hospitalised <10 days, P=0.02; referral <2 months, P=0.009) with no test of arm-by-subgroup interaction and no multiplicity adjustment. The Discussion converts these into claims that HCQ works better in under-50s, shorter stays and early visits, though the age comparison was not significant and other arms were not tested against them. Subgroups of 3-8 patients per cell make these findings unstable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified interaction analysis showing differential HCQ effect by these factors.

quotes.text: The changes in cough (VAS) in the HCQ group showed a significant correlation with hospitalization days (P=0.020)
Patients under 50 years responded better to medications

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion turns within-arm subgroup associations in 12 patients, some P=0.02 and P=0.009 with no multiplicity control and no treatment-by-subgroup interaction test, into claims that younger, shorter-stay, earlier-referral patients respond better to HCQ. The age claim in particular is not supported by the paper's own Table 5 (P=0.06, 0.11, 0.17, all CIs include 0, and enrolment was restricted to ages 20-50).

issues.title: HCQ 'more effective' for dyspnoea rests on two bare RRs with no counts, CIs, P-value or defined outcome
issues.explanation: The Results give RR=0.36 for HCQ and RR=0.60 for clarithromycin vs placebo and call HCQ more effective. They give no event counts, CIs, P-values, definition of dyspnoea, or baseline dyspnoea status, and the statistical methods do not mention RR. With about 11-12 per arm, such RRs have very wide uncertainty, and the dyspnoea claim is a headline finding in the Discussion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table of dyspnoea event counts with CIs showing a significant benefit.

quotes.text: (RR=0.36), indicating moderate efficacy

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that HCQ is more effective for shortness of breath rests on two relative risks (0.36 and 0.60) with no counts, denominators, confidence intervals, P-values or stated outcome definition, in arms of 11-12 patients. The Discussion also quotes 65% versus the Results' 64% (1 - 0.36).

issues.title: Discussion says FEV1/FVC rose more with clarithromycin; Table 2 shows FEV1 equal and FVC lowest on clarithromycin
issues.explanation: Table 2 shows post-treatment FEV1% essentially identical in all arms (90.47, 90.57, 90.47) and FVC% lowest on clarithromycin (78.34 vs 80.81 HCQ and 81.32 placebo). The Discussion nonetheless says FEV1, FVC, MEF25-75 and 6MW increased more with clarithromycin and that it had a greater impact on lung function. All lung-function P-values are 0.32 or above. Only MEF and 6MW are numerically higher, and neither is significant.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline-to-follow-up change data showing larger increases in FEV1 and FVC on clarithromycin.

quotes.text: increased more in the group receiving clarithromycin

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion statement that FEV1 and FVC 'increased more' with clarithromycin contradicts Table 2 (FEV1 identical across arms; FVC lowest with clarithromycin) and the paper's own Results text. The FEV1/FVC point is narrower: clarithromycin did have the highest FEV1/FVC (94.08 vs 92.63 and 91.41), but the Discussion does not name that ratio explicitly and the difference is non-significant (P=0.55, 0.15).

issues.title: Clarithromycin called effective for cough though P=0.08 vs placebo and P=0.29 vs HCQ
issues.explanation: The Discussion says clarithromycin 'effectively controlled symptoms' and was more effective for cough. The cough comparisons are not significant: P=0.08 vs placebo and P=0.29 vs HCQ. The Results also call it 'more effective than placebo' while stating the difference was not significant. The Conclusion's 'no marked difference' contradicts the Discussion's comparative efficacy claims, and with 11-12 per arm the data cannot distinguish the drugs. The lung-function version of this claim is covered in c6.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant adjusted comparison for cough, or an equivalence/benefit threshold stated in advance and met.

quotes.text: Clarithromycin was more effective in reducing cough, as measured by the VAS
however, it was not statistically significant (P=0.080)

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion calls clarithromycin 'more effective' in reducing cough, but neither comparison is significant at the paper's own alpha of 0.05 (P=0.08 vs placebo, P=0.29 vs HCQ), and both CIs include zero. The paper does elsewhere caveat non-significance and the small sample, and the Conclusion states no marked difference, so the overstatement is real but partly tempered.

issues.title: Table 2 SMD CIs are narrower than the MD CIs/P-values imply (cough: SMD CI -1.90 to -0.11 vs P=0.08)
issues.explanation: For clarithromycin vs placebo cough, the SMD CI excludes zero while the same row's P is 0.08 and the MD CI (-2.35 to 0.10) includes zero. This recurs across the table: the SMD CIs have a roughly fixed width of about 1.6-1.7 whatever the MD CI width. For example, FVC comparison 1 has an MD CI of -7.85 to 12.79 with SD about 9.5, which implies an SMD CI of about -0.83 to 1.35, but the table prints -0.56 to 1.08. The SMD intervals therefore look too narrow and give the impression of significance that the P-values do not support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description of an SMD CI computed by a method independent of the adjusted MD CI, with a stated rationale for the narrower width.

quotes.location: Table 2, VAS cough row, comparison 3 SMD

quotes.text: however, it was not statistically significant (P=0.080)

script.explanation: the p-value recovered from the CI is 0.0255 (reachable range [0.0240, 0.0271] across the printed precision of the estimate and its bounds), but p = 0.08 is reported -- this recovery inverts a WALD interval, so if the paper used a bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood or Fieller interval the two numbers are not comparable; confirm the method before treating this as a finding; the CI excludes the null (0.0), but the reported p = 0.08 says the result is not significant

issues.title: 34 patients in three arms (11-12 each), no sample-size calculation, no stated primary outcome
issues.explanation: The trial randomised 34 patients to three arms, reports no power calculation and names no primary outcome among about 12 outcomes. With about 11 per arm the CIs are wide (e.g. FVC MD CI -7.85 to 12.79), so the study cannot rule out meaningful differences or show that any exists. The authors acknowledge this, but they still draw differential efficacy conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registered power calculation and pre-specified primary outcome.

quotes.text: A major limitation of our study was the small sample size
were not statistically significant due to the limited number of samples

issues.title: HCQ cough VAS given as 0.74±1.11 in text but 0.76 (1.11) in Table 2; 0.74 is the HCQ-clarithromycin difference
issues.explanation: The Results quote 0.74 as the HCQ cough VAS, but Table 2 gives the HCQ mean as 0.76. The 0.74 is the mean difference between HCQ and clarithromycin, so the text attaches a difference to a group mean. The error is small and does not change the comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 0.74 is the adjusted difference rather than a group mean.

quotes.text: The HCQ group had a higher VAS-based cough score (0.74±1.11)

quotes.location: Table 2, VAS cough row, HCQ column

issues.title: Registration (2020-08-11) timing relative to enrolment not stated; selection from past records
issues.explanation: The trial was registered on 2020-08-11, while the diagnosis window began in February 2020 and patients were selected from hospital records and follow-up calls. The paper never gives the enrolment dates or states whether registration preceded the first participant, and the registered primary outcome is not stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Enrolment dates after 2020-08-11 and a registry entry matching the reported outcomes.

quotes.text: registered on the clinical trial site of Iran on 2020-08-11
during one year starting from February 2020

issues.title: FEV1/FVC SMD printed as 0.46 in text but -0.46 in Table 2, outside its own CI [-1.29, 0.37]
issues.explanation: The Results give SMD=0.46 with CI [-1.29, 0.37], which does not contain the estimate. Table 2 prints -0.46 with the same CI, so the text sign is wrong or dropped. The CI includes zero either way, so this is a presentation slip.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original manuscript showing -0.46 in the text.

script.explanation: the estimate 0.46 lies outside its own CI [-1.29, 0.37]; the estimate 0.46 is not the arithmetic midpoint of [-1.29, 0.37] (expected about -0.4600) -- note that bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood, bias-corrected and Fieller intervals are all legitimately asymmetric, and this paper does not say which method it used, so confirm the method before treating this as a finding

issues.title: Association of CT severity with dyspnoea class called significant at P=0.050 despite a <0.05 threshold
issues.explanation: The Methods define significance as P<0.05, and the Results call P=0.050 a significant correlation. The preceding sentence says Table 3 showed no significant relationships. The test is a chi-squared on a table with many sparse cells. The result is borderline at best and is not reliable evidence of a correlation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An exact P below 0.05, e.g. 0.0496, from the underlying data.

quotes.text: There was a significant correlation (P=0.050)
was considered statistically significant for all tests

issues.title: HCQ dyspnoea effect stated as 64% (RR=0.36) in Results but 65% in Discussion
issues.explanation: The Results give a 64% figure matching RR 0.36, while the Discussion gives 65% for the same comparison. Both phrase a relative risk reduction as a 'chance of reducing' dyspnoea, which is a misinterpretation of an RR. The discrepancy is small but is a printed inconsistency.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An unrounded RR (e.g. 0.35) reported in the paper.

quotes.text: (RR=0.36), indicating moderate efficacy
HCQ  had  a  65%  chance

issues.title: Table 1 placebo HCQ in hospital: 3 (37.3) should be 27.3% of 11
issues.explanation: The percentage printed for 3 of 11 placebo patients is 37.3, but 3/11 is 27.3%. A trivial slip with no effect on the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator for that cell stated in the paper.

script.explanation: 3/11 = 27.27%, but the paper prints 37.3, outside the rounding interval [37.25, 37.40]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 8.0 rather than 11.

10.32598/jrh.12.6.2046.1.headline_claim: MBCT is effective in increasing resilience and reducing psychological distress in people recovered from COVID-19, and the effect persisted to follow-up.
10.32598/jrh.12.6.2046.1.overall: The headline claim that MBCT is effective for resilience and distress rests on a 30-person, non-randomised, unblinded study with a no-treatment control, self-report outcomes, unadjusted baseline imbalance and internally inconsistent statistics (e.g., group F=8.75 with P=0.0001 and implausible eta-squared values). The direction of effect is probably real but its size and generalisability cannot be relied on.

primary_outcome.name: Resilience (CD-RISC) and psychological distress (DASS-21)

issues.title: No-intervention control with self-reported outcomes; effect sizes (resilience 26.5 to 72.7) implausibly large
issues.explanation: Participants knew they received therapy while controls received nothing, and both outcomes are self-reported, so expectancy, attention and social desirability cannot be separated from a specific MBCT effect. The MBCT resilience mean nearly tripled (26.53 to 72.67) in 8 weeks, which is much larger than typical for such interventions. The unqualified claim of effectiveness is not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Use of an active/attention control or objective outcome measures yielding similar effects.

quotes.text: but the control group received no intervention
Since  all  outcomes were  related  to  and  reported  by  individual  patients

second_reader.what_stands: The control group received no intervention and all outcomes were self-reported, with no blinding described. The reported effects are extremely large (post-test between-group d about 5 for resilience, distress reduced by about 85%), far above the planned effect of 0.7, which is a sign that bias such as expectation or social desirability may be involved. The authors do list self-report and social desirability as a limitation, and the paper does not itself say the effects are implausible, so 'implausibly large' is an assessment rather than a demonstrated error.

issues.title: Non-randomised matched allocation; baseline distress differs 39.00 vs 47.27 despite claimed matching
issues.explanation: Allocation is described as random selection followed by matching, with no allocation method given, and the groups differ at baseline on distress by about 8 points despite the statement that they were matched on distress. The analysis does not adjust for baseline, and the control group's higher starting level leaves more room for change, so group differences in change and in the main group effect are confounded with baseline imbalance.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described randomisation procedure and baseline-adjusted analysis showing the same effect.

quotes.text: Subjects were matched in terms of age, sex, marriage, and psychological distress score

second_reader.what_stands: Allocation is described inconsistently (random selection in one place, matching in others) and was not randomised in the sense of a stated random sequence, and the baseline distress means differ by 8.27 points (d about 0.9, t about 2.4, p about 0.02) despite the claim that distress was matched. The paper does not test baseline differences or adjust for them, although the Results mention ANCOVA while the Abstract and Table 4 describe a mixed ANOVA.

issues.title: Conclusion of effectiveness and rehabilitation use generalised from 30 purposively sampled participants
issues.explanation: The abstract states MBCT is effective and useful for rehabilitation of those recovered from COVID-19, based on 15 per arm, purposive sampling and a non-randomised design. The wording is partly hedged, but the unqualified 'is effective' is stronger than this design supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Replication in a randomised, adequately controlled larger sample.

quotes.text: MBCT  is  effective  in  increasing  resilience  and reducing psychological distress after illness
was selected by purposive sampling

issues.title: Group effect P=0.01 in abstract vs P=0.0001 in Table 4; F=8.75 on (1,28) df implies P about 0.006
issues.explanation: The abstract gives P=0.01 for the group difference while Table 4 prints P=0.0001 for the group effect on resilience. Moreover, an F of 8.75 with 1 and 28 degrees of freedom corresponds to P around 0.006, so the printed 0.0001 does not follow from the F. Eta-squared values (e.g., 0.87 with F=8.75) are also implausible for those F and df.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Output showing different df or a corrected F and p for the group effect.

quotes.text: a significant difference is observed between the experimental and control groups (P=0.01)

script.explanation: The printed f = 8.75 supports p no smaller than 0.00620433, but the paper reports p = 0.0001 -- more significance than the statistic earns at its printed precision.

issues.title: Inclusion required DASS≥39 but MBCT pre-test mean is 39.00 with SD 6.01
issues.explanation: If all participants scored at least 39, a mean of 39.00 would require every score to equal 39 and the SD to be zero. The printed SD of 6.01 means some MBCT participants scored below the stated cut-off, so the inclusion rule was not applied as described (or the scale/cut-off is misreported). The control group mean is 47.27, so the two groups also started at different severity levels.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the cut-off applied to a different scoring (e.g., doubled DASS-21 scores) with all participants meeting it.

quotes.text: DASS≥39, and have a smartphone

issues.title: Abstract cites pooled time main effects (F=30.31, 120.70) as treatment effects rather than the time×group interactions
issues.explanation: A time main effect pools both groups and does not show a treatment effect. The paper does report time×group interactions in Table 4 (F=45.21 and 154.54), which would be the relevant test, but the abstract highlights the time effects and gives only a single unexplained between-group P=0.01. The reader is steered to the wrong statistics for efficacy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Abstract citing interaction effects as the primary test.

quotes.text: positively affected the resilience (F=30.31, P=0.001)
The interaction effect of time and group was also sig -nificant  in  the  three  stages  of  measurement  (F=45.21, P=0.0001,  η=0.89).

issues.title: Sample size power stated as 0.91 and then 0.96 in consecutive sentences
issues.explanation: The Methods first say the sample size calculation used a power of 0.91, then say a power of 0.96 was needed. Both cannot describe the same calculation. The inconsistency makes the sample size justification unverifiable, though the conclusion does not depend on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clarification that 0.91 is the achieved power for the stated effect size and 0.96 a separate requirement.

quotes.text: the power test of 0.91
The  hypothesis  with  a  power  of  0.96  was  needed.

issues.title: No trial registration reported for a prospective intervention study
issues.explanation: The paper describes a prospective intervention but reports no trial registry entry, so the planned outcomes and analyses cannot be checked. Many such studies are unregistered, so this limits verifiability rather than demonstrating a flaw.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry with prospective registration and matching outcomes.

quotes.text: from February 2021 to June 2021

issues.title: Abstract prints P=0.001 for time effects; Results and Table 4 print P=0.0001 for the same F values
issues.explanation: The abstract and results give different p-values for identical F statistics (30.31 and 120.70). Both are far below 0.05, so no conclusion changes, but the numbers are not transcribed consistently.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; the discrepancy is visible in the text.

10.32687/1561-5936-2022-26-4-303-307.headline_claim: Adding vitamin-mineral complexes (vitamins D and C, zinc and selenium) to standard post-discharge rehabilitation improves quality of life in patients with post-COVID syndrome.
10.32687/1561-5936-2022-26-4-303-307.overall: The paper's headline, that vitamin-mineral complexes improve quality of life and the combined regimen works best, rests on about 50 patients per arm, open-label self-rated outcomes, uncorrected tests and mostly within-group significance counts. The data are best read as exploratory and preliminary, as the Discussion partly admits, and the Table 5 labelling and text mismatches reduce confidence further. Individual numeric slips are minor, but the strength of the stated conclusion is not supported.

primary_outcome.name: Quality of life (SF-36 domain scores; no single primary domain named)

issues.title: Regimen benefit argued from within-arm significance; Mann-Whitney named for before/after data, no baseline-adjusted contrasts
issues.explanation: The text describes each arm by the domains whose within-group p* fell below 0.05, and ranks regimens by how many domains reached significance. A difference in significance between arms is not a significant difference between arms. The only test named is Mann-Whitney, which is unpaired and does not match the repeated measures. Between-arm p-values appear only for selected pairs, and baseline values per arm are not shown, so a baseline imbalance cannot be excluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-arm analysis of change from baseline (or ANCOVA) for all four arms showing the same ranking.

quotes.text: улучшала КЖ лишь по домену «интенсивность боли»
теста Манна-Уитни в программе

second_reader.what_stands: The benefit of adding supplements to standard rehabilitation is largely argued from which within-arm before/after p-values are below 0,05. The Methods name only the Mann-Whitney test, which is for independent groups, for what are paired comparisons, and no baseline-adjusted or change-score contrasts are reported. It is not true that no between-arm tests exist: Table 5 prints some, but they are unadjusted, uncorrected endpoint comparisons, and the garbled headers make some hard to identify.

issues.title: 'Best' effect of the combined vitamin-mineral regimen stated in abstract and conclusions despite small arms and uncorrected tests
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusions state that vitamin-mineral complexes improve quality of life and that the combined regimen works best. The evidence is about 50 patients per arm with no sample-size calculation, open-label self-rated outcomes, uncorrected tests and mostly within-group comparisons. The 'preliminary' wording appears only in the Discussion and does not carry into the abstract or numbered conclusions. At most the data suggest hypothesis-generating differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified, adequately powered between-arm comparison of change in a primary SF-36 summary showing the combined regimen superior.

quotes.text: Комплексное введение ВМК в схемы реабилитации позволяет наилучшим образом воздействовать на пациентов, перенесших COVID-19.
можно сделать предварительный вывод о том, что как острый период COVID-19, так и постковидный период влияют на КЖ пациентов

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract and Conclusion 3 state that the combined regimen has the 'most pronounced' and 'best' effect, based on arms of about 50 patients and uncorrected p<0,05 tests, with no limitations section. The data are not contradictory, because the combined arm has the highest means, but only two of the eight domain contrasts against the Б-В arms survive a simple Bonferroni correction, and the superlative is not hedged outside one Discussion sentence. The Table 5 header layout is uncertain, so I assumed the third block is the combined arm.

issues.title: Text says standard care improved only pain, but Table 5 gives group A vitality p*=0.019
issues.explanation: The Results state that standard rehabilitation (group A) improved quality of life only in the pain domain. Table 5 shows a within-group p* of 0.019 for vitality in the same group, which meets the paper's own p<0.05 criterion. The control arm therefore improved in two domains, not one. This makes the contrast with the supplement arms look larger than the table supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that vitality in group A did not reach the clinical-significance threshold, or a corrected p* for that cell.

quotes.text: улучшала КЖ лишь по домену «интенсивность боли»
quotes.location: Results, paragraph on Table 5, group A
Table 5, Жизненная активность row, group A column (p* 0,019)

issues.title: No placebo or blinding for a self-rated SF-36 outcome in an open-label supplement comparison
issues.explanation: Group A received standard rehabilitation only, while the other arms received tablets. The outcome is patient-reported quality of life, which is sensitive to expectation effects when patients know their treatment. The paper does not mention blinding, so part of any between-arm difference may reflect expectation rather than the supplements.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that patients and assessors were blinded, or that a placebo was given to group A.

quotes.text: Group A - standard rehabilitation, mainly including anticoagulant therapy ( n = 47)
The quality of life was assessed using the scales of the SF-36 questionnaire.

issues.title: About 64 p-values in Table 5 (8 domains x 8 columns) tested at p<0.05 with no correction or primary outcome
issues.explanation: The Methods set a single threshold of p<0.05 and name no primary domain and no multiplicity adjustment. Conclusions about which regimen helps which domain rest on which cells fall below 0.05. Marginal findings such as p=0.019 or 0.031 are fragile under any correction, while the smallest p-values would likely survive.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary domain or an adjusted-alpha statement in the protocol.

quotes.text: Значимыми считали различия при p < 0,05.

issues.title: Table 5 arm labels do not match its data columns; combined arm printed under 'Группа В', arms lettered Д/Г/D
issues.explanation: The column headed 'Группа В' carries the comparison p-values 'А/Г' and 'Б-В/Г', so it holds the combined vitamin-plus-mineral arm. The column headed 'Группа Г' behaves like the mineral-only arm, and the comparison labels after groups Б and Г also look shifted. The combined arm is also lettered Д in the methods, Г in results and the table, and D in the English abstract. A reader taking the headers at face value would reverse which arm gained which domains.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The published table image showing correct column headers, with the discrepancy arising only in text extraction.

issues.title: Table 3 emotional-functioning SD of 49.564 exceeds the maximum possible for a 0-100 scale with mean 60.2
issues.explanation: For a 0-100 scale with mean m the SD cannot exceed about sqrt(m(100-m)), adjusted slightly for sample size. With mean 60.163 this is about 49.0 (49.1 with the n/(n-1) correction), below the printed 49.564. The SD at discharge is 13.680, so the admission value is also out of line with the rest of the table. issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original table showing a different SD for this cell.

issues.title: Random allocation of supplement regimens with no registry identifier or protocol reference
issues.explanation: The study allocated patients randomly to four regimens, but no trial registration is given. Without a registered plan, the choice of eight domains and the timepoints cannot be compared with a prior plan. The method of randomisation and the concealment are also not described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or protocol with pre-specified outcomes.

quotes.text: случайным образом рекомендовали четыре схемы реабилитации
