Changes from baseline and at the end of procedure (12 weeks)
Changes from baseline and at the end of procedure (12 weeks)
Changes from baseline and at the end of procedure (12 weeks)

issues.title: Conclusion that the program 'improves physical capacity' lacks a pre-post fitness measure or distance effect
issues.explanation: The study has no baseline-versus-end fitness test and no non-exercising comparator, and distance covered showed no group or genotype effects in most analyses. Post-session lactate across weeks within an exercise program does not demonstrate improved physical capacity. The conclusion goes beyond what was measured, and no effect size or between-session change from baseline is quantified in the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre- and post-program functional or VO2max data showing improvement relative to a comparator.

quotes.text: Hence, a moderate-intensity aerobic physical therapy strategy improves physical capacity in individuals with COVID-19 and long COVID syndrome
no patient underwent a CPET to determine their VO2max before and after the Nordic walking program
For distance, there were no main effects of distance covered (F = 1.597, p = 0.369), group (F = 1.726, p = 0.199) or genotype (F = 1.097, p = 0.451)

second_reader.what_stands: There was no pre-post fitness measure (no CPET or VO2max, as the authors say), and no group received a non-exercise comparison, so 'improves physical capacity' rests only on post-exercise lactate falling across sessions. The distance evidence is mixed rather than uniformly null (the CKM model is null, while session effects on distance were significant in three other SNP models with no significant post-hoc improvement), so the point overstates it if it implies distance showed no effect anywhere.

issues.title: Unadjusted nonrandomized comparison of differently recruited groups used to infer long COVID impairs exercise
issues.explanation: Long COVID patients came from a patient association mailing, controls from advertisements, with no randomization and no adjustment for fitness or lifestyle. Lactate differences between groups cannot be attributed to long COVID, and there is no pre-intervention baseline or untreated control, so the effect of Nordic walking cannot be separated from group differences. The conclusion about reduced exercise ability, stated with 'presumably less exercised beforehand', is speculation beyond the design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An analysis adjusted for baseline fitness, sex and age showing the same group differences.

quotes.text: potential confounding variables, such as differences in baseline fitness levels or other lifestyle factors between participants, were not controlled for
The main findings support that individuals who reported long COVID who presumably were less exercised beforehand appeared to be less able to exercise, based on lactate levels

second_reader.what_stands: The group comparison is unadjusted, nonrandomised and uses differently recruited groups, with baseline fitness not measured, and the paper's own limitation (vi) says so. The authors do hedge ('presumably', 'appeared') and list the limitations, so the point is narrower than a claim of concealment: the interpretation about prior exercise and impaired exercise ability rests on an assumption the data cannot test.

issues.title: 29 participants split over genotype strata (cells of 0 to 9) support genotype-specific efficacy claims
issues.explanation: No sample size justification is given, and the genotype cells are tiny: for example 1 COVID-19 CC for ACTN3, 1 long COVID TT for AMPD1, and 0 COVID-19 TT. The abstract nonetheless states exercise enhanced capabilities in particular genotypes. Such strata can only be hypothesis-generating.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified power calculation or a replication in a larger sample.

quotes.text: Small sample size; the study only included 29 patients
this pilot study did not present power of analysis
Physical therapy strategy through Nordic walking enhanced physical capabilities during aerobic exercise in post-COVID19 patients with different genotypes

second_reader.what_stands: Genotype-specific conclusions (ACTN3 CT/TT, AMPD1 CC/CT, CKM AA) rest on cells of roughly 3 to 9 people per group, with some genotype cells empty, and no power analysis. The authors acknowledge the small sample and missing power analysis, but the abstract and conclusion still state efficacy for specific genotypes.

issues.title: Many genotype × session LSD comparisons at p<0.050 across six SNPs without multiplicity correction
issues.explanation: The analysis runs 6 SNPs × 2 outcomes and then LSD tests across up to 12 sessions per genotype, all at uncorrected 0.05. With so many comparisons, some significant session-wise differences are expected by chance. The abstract's genotype-specific findings (CT and TT in ACTN3, CC and CT in AMPD1) rest on these selected results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Results surviving Bonferroni or Holm correction across the post hoc tests.

quotes.text: The significance level was set at p < 0.050.
a least significant difference (LSD) posthoc analysis was performed

second_reader.what_stands: The paper sets alpha at 0.050 and uses unadjusted LSD post-hoc comparisons across six SNPs, genotypes and 12 sessions, with no multiplicity correction described. Several headline significances (e.g. ACTN3 interaction p = 0.028, AMPD1 p = 0.048) are borderline and would not survive a simple correction across SNPs.

issues.title: Three-way ANOVA with sessions as factor not described as repeated measures; 'paired t-test' for independent groups
issues.explanation: Lactate was measured in the same people across 12 sessions, but the methods describe a three-way ANOVA without a repeated-measures structure, so within-person correlation may be ignored. The 'paired t-test' for comparing two independent groups is also wrong as stated. The exact model cannot be confirmed from the text, so the effect on the lactate findings is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Output showing a within-subject (repeated-measures or mixed) model with session as the within factor.

quotes.text: A threeway analysis of variance (ANOVA; 2 × 3 × 12, corresponding to group × genotype × Nordic walking sessions) was used to compare lactate levels and distance covered.
Demographical data are presented using chi-square for qualitative variables and paired t -test for quantitative variables.

issues.title: Three registered primary outcomes (EQ5D, SF-36, MFIS) not reported; distance reported though not registered as primary
issues.explanation: The registry record lists four primary outcomes, but the paper reports only lactate and distance covered. The omitted quality-of-life and fatigue outcomes are the ones most relevant to patients, and the paper does not say whether they were collected or published elsewhere. Lactate, the one retained primary, is the outcome reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A companion publication reporting EQ5D, SF-36 and MFIS from this trial, or an earlier registry version with only lactate as primary.

quotes.text: The distance covered by the participants in all Nordic walking sessions was measured by POLAR Ignite 2 device
Lactate samples were collected after multiple 45-min Nordic walking sessions once per week for 12 weeks.

issues.title: Abstract swaps group sizes: long COVID 13 / COVID-19 16, versus 16 / 13 in Methods and Table 1
issues.explanation: The abstract gives 13 long COVID and 16 COVID-19 participants. Methods, Table 1 and Table 3 all give 16 long COVID and 13 COVID-19. The total of 29 is unchanged, so it is a labelling slip in the abstract only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that group sizes changed between the abstract and the analysed data; Table 1 and Methods agree, so unlikely.

quotes.text: 29 patients who previously suffered from COVID-19 (long COVID = 13, COVID-19 = 16)
a nonrandomized intervention group (long COVID) (n = 16) and a healthy control (COVID-19) group (n = 13)

issues.title: Registry start 2022-03-01 precedes registration 2022-07-11, but paper reports sessions Feb–May 2023
issues.explanation: The registry record implies registration about four months after the stated start. The paper reports the sessions took place from February to May 2023, after registration, so the registry start date may be a placeholder. The paper also states registration on 14 July 2022 whereas the registry shows 11 July 2022, a small mismatch.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing the start date was a planned date later amended.

quotes.text: The study was registered at the Registry of Clinical Trials (NCT05453188 on 14 July 2022)
completed outdoors weekly from February to May 2023 in Casa de Campo, Madrid, Spain

issues.title: MLCK rs28497577 A-allele frequency 18.7% in Table 2 vs 3 CA + 13 CC genotypes in Table 3 (implies 9.4%)
issues.explanation: Table 3 shows 3 heterozygotes and 13 CC among 16 long COVID patients, with no AA. That gives 3 A alleles out of 32, or 9.4%, not 18.7%. The printed figure matches the heterozygote genotype percentage (18.8%) instead, suggesting the allele frequency was not computed from alleles. This also bears on the HWE and FIS values for this SNP.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A genotype table showing 3 AA and 13 CC (or similar) consistent with 6 A alleles.

quotes.location: Table 2, Myosin light chain kinase rs28497577 row

issues.title: Table 3 prints '90 (0.0)' for COVID-19 MLCK c.49T>C TT genotype in a group of 13
issues.explanation: The cell gives a count of 90 with 0.0%, impossible for a group of 13. The remaining counts (9 + 4) already total 13 and the percentage is 0.0, so the count should be 0. It is a typographical slip with no effect on results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing needed; at most the original table showing a clean 0.

10.3390/ijms26104582.headline_claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation was associated with increased GPx activity in both regimens, decreased IL-6 in the bolus group, and reduced anxiety and depression scores in the daily group.
10.3390/ijms26104582.overall: The headline claim is framed as association, and the GPx increase is supported by within-arm change, but with no concurrent control it cannot be attributed to vitamin D. The abstract misstates the IL-6 result for the daily arm, and the daily-versus-bolus anxiety and depression conclusions rest on significant versus non-significant within-arm tests. Unreported missing 25(OH)D data, retrospective registration and several small table errors lower confidence further.

primary_outcome.name: GPx activity; serum IL-6 (co-primary)

checklist.control: none (two active arms, no placebo or untreated control)

issues.title: Abstract says both regimens decreased IL-6; results show only bolus (p=0.01), daily p=0.30, all p=0.07
issues.explanation: The abstract states that bolus and daily supplementation were both significantly associated with decreased IL-6. Results and Table 3 show a significant fall only in the bolus group; the daily group (p = 0.30) and all patients (p = 0.07) were not significant. IL-6 is a co-primary outcome, so the abstract misstates one of the two main results, although the body text and Conclusions are accurate.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that the abstract IL-6 claim refers only to the bolus group, or an analysis showing a significant IL-6 decrease in the daily group.

quotes.text: Both bolus and daily vitamin D supplementation were significantly associated with increased GPx activity and decreased IL-6 levels.
with no significant change in all patients ( p = 0.07) and in daily group analysis ( p = 0.30)

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract states that both regimens were significantly associated with decreased IL-6, but the paper's results show a significant IL-6 decrease only in the bolus group (p = 0.01), with daily p = 0.30 and all patients p = 0.07. The abstract's GPx claim is correct for both regimens, and the body text and Conclusions state the IL-6 result correctly.

issues.title: All outcomes rest on uncontrolled pre-post change in two active arms; no placebo or untreated group
issues.explanation: Both arms received vitamin D, so no result can be separated from time, natural recovery of PCC, regression to the mean or participation effects. The authors disclose this and word the abstract as association, which limits the overstatement. Still, mechanistic and regimen-comparison conclusions are drawn from within-arm changes that this design cannot attribute to the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Not applicable; this is a design property. Concern is reduced only if conclusions are kept strictly descriptive.

quotes.text: The trial did not include a placebo group as this was not approved by the ethics committee.
As such, this study cannot establish causality, only associations [129].

second_reader.what_stands: All reported outcomes rest on pre-post changes within two active vitamin D arms, with no placebo or untreated comparison group, so changes cannot be separated from regression to the mean, time, or other concurrent influences. The authors openly acknowledge this limitation and phrase their conclusions as associations; the problem is the design, not undisclosed in the paper.

issues.title: Discussion claims symptom improvement, cognitive benefit and daily>bolus depression effect not shown by the data
issues.explanation: Table 5 shows no significant change in cough, dyspnea or fatigue, yet the Discussion says clinical symptoms improved. No cognitive outcome was measured, yet the Discussion says cognitive symptoms were reduced. Between-regimen comparison found a significant difference only in post-treatment HADS anxiety (p = 0.01), not depression, yet the Discussion says daily dosing lowered anxiety and depression compared with bolus.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported between-arm depression results or a cognitive outcome measure in the study.

quotes.text: Moreover, we observed improvements in clinical symptoms following supplementation, which may have positively impacted patients' well-being.
Vitamin D supplementation was significantly associated with reductions in anxiety and cognitive symptoms in patients with PCC.
but daily supplementation was significantly associated with decreased anxiety and depression scores compared to the bolus group.

issues.title: Trial registered retrospectively (registry first submitted 2024-05-15) after recruitment in Dec 2022-Mar 2023
issues.explanation: The paper cites NCT06419712 as if it documents the design, but per the registry the record was first submitted about 14 months after recruitment began and after it ended. Outcomes were therefore not publicly fixed beforehand, which matters for the many secondary tests. The primary outcomes match the current record, which limits the concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing an earlier registration with the same primary outcomes.

quotes.text: Patients were recruited between December 2022 and March 2023.
The study design and data are publicly available in the ClinicalTrials.gov registry under identifier NCT06419712.

issues.title: Discussion claims persistence of benefit and no recurrence, but only day-60 on-treatment data exist
issues.explanation: The Discussion says no recurrence of neuropsychiatric symptoms was reported at follow-up, suggesting persistence of benefit. Methods list assessments only at baseline and day 60, during supplementation, and no off-treatment follow-up is reported or analysed. The persistence claim is therefore unsupported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported off-treatment follow-up assessments with data.

quotes.text: At follow-up, no recurrence of neuropsychiatric symptoms was reported, suggesting potential persistence of the observed benefits.
The primary outcomes included glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity and serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels, assessed at baseline and day 60.

issues.title: Sample size calculation is not tied to a testable effect on GPx or IL-6 (SD 0.5, difference 0.11, finite population 88)
issues.explanation: The stated inputs (95% confidence, 5% margin of error, SD 0.5, finite population of 88) resemble a survey precision calculation, and no units or outcome-specific effect size are given. IL-6 SDs in Table 3 (6 to 12 pg/mL) are about as large as the means, so the study may be poorly powered for IL-6 and for between-arm comparisons. The null IL-6 result in the daily arm and the arm contrasts cannot be interpreted as evidence of absence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A power calculation expressed in GPx and IL-6 units with the stated SDs and effect sizes.

quotes.text: A 95% confidence level, 5% margin of error, standard deviation of 0.5, and a minimum detectable difference of 0.11 were used to determine the required sample size.

issues.title: IL-6 summarised as mean ± SD with SD larger than mean; paired t-tests stated for within-group change
issues.explanation: IL-6 values such as 4.92 ± 9.59 and 6.97 ± 12.05 are heavily right-skewed, so paired t-tests on raw values are fragile; a few extreme values can drive or mask the bolus p = 0.01 and daily p = 0.30. The paper does not state whether non-parametric or log-transformed analysis was used for IL-6.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported Wilcoxon or log-scale analyses of IL-6 giving the same conclusions.

quotes.text: Paired t -tests were used for self-controlled analyses to assess within-group changes over time.

issues.title: Post-treatment 25(OH)D percentages imply n=23 bolus and n=22 daily, not 28 and 26; missing data unreported
issues.explanation: Bolus post-treatment percentages (4.3, 52.2, 43.5) are multiples of 1/23 and daily (27.3, 36.4, 36.4) of 1/22, so about 5 bolus and 4 daily participants lack a post-treatment 25(OH)D value. The paper reports no attrition or missing data and describes 54 participants throughout. Printed change means (23.99, 17.28) also differ from final minus baseline (23.44, 17.00), consistent with a smaller analysed set. The analysed numbers for the primary outcomes (GPx, IL-6) are likewise not stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram or text stating that 5 bolus and 4 daily participants lacked a post-treatment 25(OH)D sample.

quotes.text: In the bolus regimen group, 4.3% of patients remained below sufficiency (<30 ng/mL)
In the daily supplementation group, 27.3% remained below sufficiency, while 36.4% achieved 30-39.9 ng/mL, and 36.4% reached 40-60 ng/mL

issues.title: Daily-vs-bolus anxiety/depression contrast rests on significant vs non-significant within-arm tests, uncorrected
issues.explanation: Daily-arm HADS decreases (p = 0.0001) are set against non-significant bolus changes (p = 0.09 and 0.23), and the conclusion says daily dosing improved anxiety and depression. The difference between 'significant' and 'not significant' is not itself a significant difference, and no between-arm comparison of change scores is reported. About a dozen outcome tests were run with no across-outcome correction, and the daily arm started with higher scores and had more room to fall.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A group-by-time interaction test showing a significant difference in change between regimens for both HADS subscales, with a stated multiplicity approach.

quotes.text: Patients receiving bolus supplements did not show significant differences ( p > 0.05) in either parameter
while daily vitamin D supplementation was associated with improvements in anxiety and depression scores.

issues.title: One daily-arm participant (3.8% of 26) had baseline 25(OH)D 30-39.9 ng/mL despite <30 eligibility
issues.explanation: Methods say all participants were confirmed deficient (<30 ng/mL) as an eligibility criterion. Results say 3.8% of the daily group (1 of 26) had adequate baseline levels of 30-39.9 ng/mL. The inconsistency affects one participant and is unexplained (for example a different screening and baseline sample); it does not change the main findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A note that eligibility screening and baseline assay were separate samples, with the eligible value below 30.

quotes.text: confirming vitamin D deficiency (<30 ng/mL) in all participants as an eligibility criterion
Among patients in the daily regimen group, 3.8% had adequate 25(OH)D levels (30-39.9 ng/mL)

issues.title: Table 5 post-treatment cough: all patients 12 but bolus 6 + daily 4 = 10
issues.explanation: The all-patient post-treatment cough count (12) does not equal the sum of the two arms (6 + 4 = 10). The text's 'improvements' of 3/9 and 4/8 imply a total reduction of 7 not the 5/17 reported. Either the all-patient row or the subgroup rows are wrong; the effect on conclusions is small since all cough changes are non-significant.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or a note that some participants were counted in neither arm.

issues.title: Table 1 obesity/overweight counts printed as 26 in both arms (42.9% of 28 = 12; 50% of 26 = 13)
issues.explanation: The bolus cell reads 42.9% (26) but 26 of 28 would be 92.9%. The daily cell reads 50% (26), where 50% of 26 is 13. The counts appear to be wrong, though the percentages and p value (0.49) are plausible. This is a minor table error.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 1 showing counts of 12 and 13.

script.explanation: 26/28 = 92.86%, but the paper prints 42.9, outside the rounding interval [42.85, 43.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 60.6 rather than 28.

10.3390/ijms26178623.headline_claim: An 8-week HIIT program was effective in reducing inflammation, attenuating oxidative stress, and alleviating dyspnea in individuals with long COVID, while Triphala added no measurable effect beyond HIIT.
10.3390/ijms26178623.overall: The claim that HIIT reduces inflammation and oxidative stress is not supported as stated: every group×time test is null, and the effect rests on within-group changes. The reported F-test degrees of freedom do not match the stated n = 104, and registration was retrospective with registered primary outcomes demoted. The Triphala null and safety conclusions are tentative given the small combined arm.

primary_outcome.name: IFNγ and TNFα (co-primary inflammatory biomarkers, group × time interaction)

issues.title: HIIT efficacy claimed from within-group changes although all group×time tests are null (p=0.175 to 0.968)
issues.explanation: The primary outcomes (IFNγ, TNFα) fall significantly within the HIIT and combined arms but not in control. The group×time interaction is not significant for any biomarker (p = 0.837, 0.175, 0.710, 0.968, 0.546). The authors say the reductions did not differ between groups, yet the Discussion opens with 'significantly reduced' and the Conclusions call HIIT effective. Difference in significance between arms is not evidence of an effect, and the study shows no demonstrated HIIT effect against control. No multiplicity correction is applied across the many within-group tests, several with p of about 0.04.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant pre-specified contrast of HIIT versus control change, or conclusions reworded to say no between-group effect was shown.

quotes.text: indicating that the observed reductions were not significantly different between groups
This study demonstrated that an 8-week HIIT program significantly reduced proinflammatory cytokines
This randomized controlled trial demonstrated that an 8-week HIIT program was effective in reducing inflammation, attenuating oxidative stress, and alleviating dyspnea in individuals with long COVID.

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion and Conclusions state that HIIT significantly reduced inflammation, oxidative stress and dyspnea, but the only controlled test (group×time) is null for every biomarker. The claim rests on within-group significance versus non-significance, and the dyspnea claim has no control data at all. The authors' limitations paragraph mentions low power, but the conclusion still reads as demonstrated efficacy rather than inconclusive evidence.

issues.title: Group×time F tests have error df of 8 to 62, but 104 participants are stated for every outcome
issues.explanation: A 3-group × 2-time repeated-measures ANOVA on 104 people should have error df of about 101. The reported error df are 36 (IFNγ), 8 (TNFα), 56 (MDA), 38 (protein carbonyls) and 62 (SOD). Partial η² for TNFα is consistent with its own F and df, so the df look genuine rather than mistyped. The null between-group interaction results, on which the conclusions about group differences depend, therefore come from analysed samples much smaller than 104, and the paper does not say so. The captions still state n = 104, so the reported tests cannot be reconciled with the stated sample.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A supplementary table giving the number analysed per outcome and group, showing that the df follow from subsets of the 104.

quotes.text: Data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation (SD); n = 104.

second_reader.what_stands: The group×time error df (8, 36, 38, 56, 62) imply analysed samples of about 11 to 65, far below the 104 stated for every outcome, and the paper gives no explanation. The cause (missing biomarker data, a different model, or an error) cannot be determined. For TNFα, the primary outcome, the df imply only about 11 participants entered the interaction test.

issues.title: MDA and protein carbonyl are registered primary outcomes but called secondary in the paper
issues.explanation: The registry lists IFNγ, TNFα, MDA and protein carbonyl as primary. The paper names only IFNγ and TNFα as primary and calls the oxidative stress markers secondary, with no stated reason. The headline conclusion, 'attenuating oxidative stress', rests on those markers. Because only the current registry record was available, one cannot tell whether the change predates data collection.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The first registry version showing only IFNγ and TNFα as primary, or a protocol dated before enrolment.

quotes.text: The primary outcomes of this study were inflammatory biomarkers, specifically IFNγ and TNFα
Secondary outcomes included biomarkers of oxidative stress and antioxidant defensenamely, MDA, protein carbonyls, and SOD activity.

issues.title: Trial registered 2023-12-21, after the June to October 2023 trial period
issues.explanation: The paper states the trial was conducted between June and October 2023 and gives a registration number. The registry shows the record was first submitted on 2023-12-21, two months after the trial ended. Registration after data collection cannot constrain the choice of outcomes or analyses, and the paper does not say it was retrospective. This reinforces the concern about the primary outcome change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry audit trail showing the record was created before June 2023.

quotes.text: This randomized controlled trial was conducted between June and October 2023.
was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Registration No. NCT06208761)

issues.title: Triphala 'no additional effect' conclusion rests on 29 analysed in the combined arm, below the 36 target
issues.explanation: The sample size calculation needed 29.04 per group before a 20% dropout allowance and aimed for at least 36. The combined arm ended with 29, and the calculation was based on a different population and drug. With no equivalence margin and all interaction tests null, the data cannot show Triphala adds nothing. The authors acknowledge the risk in the Limitations but still state the null in the Conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A confidence interval for the combined versus HIIT difference that excludes a clinically important effect.

quotes.text: Combined ( n = 29)
increased to at least 36 participants per group
it may not have been sufficiently sensitive to detect clinically relevant changes in long COVID, potentially leading to type II error

issues.title: 'Safe and well tolerated' rests on two non-significant within-group tests (ALT p=0.315, creatinine p=0.249)
issues.explanation: Safety is inferred from non-significant within-group changes in ALT and creatinine in an 8-week trial with 29 supplemented participants. No values, no between-group comparison and no adverse events by arm are given. Absence of a significant change does not establish safety, and the Discussion's 'no evidence of hepatic or renal toxicity' is stronger than that supports. The conclusion is plausible for a low dose but not demonstrated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported ALT and creatinine values and adverse events by arm showing no difference from control.

quotes.text: Triphala supplementation was safe and well tolerated but did not provide additional measurable effects beyond those of HIIT.
No significant within-group changes were observed in either alanine aminotransferase (ALT)

issues.title: HIIT called an 'evidence-based' strategy for long COVID though post-exertional symptoms were not assessed
issues.explanation: Participants were young, of normal BMI and mostly female (mean age 22 years, 73% female), and screened as having post-exertional malaise. The study did not measure symptom exacerbation within 24 h of exercise. Calling HIIT feasible and evidence-based for people with long COVID goes beyond this sample and these outcomes, although the limitation is stated in the Discussion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Tolerability data including PESE, and results in an older or more varied long COVID population.

quotes.text: Taken together, these findings highlight HIIT as a feasible and evidence-based rehabilitation strategy for individuals with long COVID
it did not include patient-reported outcomes related to post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE) within 24 h of exercise

issues.title: Triphala given daily (1000 mg/day) in Methods but five days per week in Discussion
issues.explanation: Methods state 500 mg twice daily, which is 1000 mg/day, and the control placebo is taken once daily for 8 weeks. The Discussion and Limitations say 1000 mg/day for five days per week. The cumulative exposure differs by about 29% between the two versions, which matters for both the null efficacy and the safety conclusions. The paper does not say which schedule was used.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Dispensing records showing the actual schedule, with one of the two statements identified as a drafting error.

quotes.text: the daily Triphala supplement (500 mg twice daily, totaling 1000 mg/day)
administration at 1000 mg/day, five days per week for eight weeks

issues.title: Section titled 'Non-Blinded' but text claims a double-blind design, with unblinded exercise arms
issues.explanation: The heading of Methods 4.1 says 'Randomized and Non-Blinded', and the first paragraph says 'double-blind'. Participants were told only that they were in a bicycle study, yet the control group did not exercise and only the control group received a placebo. The supervising and analysing researchers were not stated to be blinded. The blinding status of the trial is therefore unclear, which matters for the subjective outcomes (perceived exertion, dyspnea).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol stating who was blinded, with evidence that exercise supervisors and outcome assessors were masked.

quotes.text: Study Design: Randomized and Non-Blinded
This study was conducted using a double-blind design.

issues.title: Combined group post-intervention RPE mode 18 lies outside its printed range 13-15
issues.explanation: Table 1 reports RPE as mode (range). For the combined group after the intervention the mode is 18 but the range is 13-15, so the mode falls outside the range. One of the two figures is wrong. This is a small reporting error, but it affects the only perceived-exertion result in the table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The raw RPE data showing that the printed mode and range are both correct.

quotes.location: Table 1, Rating of perceived exertion, After row, Combined column

issues.title: HIIT work bouts described as 3 min in one paragraph and 4 min in another
issues.explanation: The first Methods paragraph describes four 3-min intervals at 85% HRpeak, with 3-min recovery. The next paragraph describes 4-min work bouts at 85% HRpeak and 3-min recovery in a 4:3 ratio, totalling 28 min. Only the second version adds up to 28 min. The exact dose of the main intervention is therefore ambiguous and the protocol cannot be replicated from the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The trial protocol or session logs confirming the actual work-interval length.

quotes.text: consisting of four 3-min intervals at 85% of peak heart rate (HRpeak)
at 85% of HRpeak for 4 min, alternating with light-intensity cycling at 60% of HRpeak for 3 min

issues.title: Sex split printed as 23% male / 77% female, but 28 and 76 of 104 give 26.9% / 73.1%
issues.explanation: The Results give 28 males (23%) and 76 females (77%) among 104 analysed participants. The counts agree with Table 1, but the percentages do not. Correct values are about 27% and 73%. The error affects nothing else in the paper, since the group comparisons use the counts.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator stated for these percentages, for example the 112 enrolled, which still gives 25.0% and 67.9%.

quotes.text: The sample comprised 28 males (23%) and 76 females (77%)

script.explanation: 28/104 = 26.92%, but the paper prints 23, outside the rounding interval [22.50, 24.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 121.7 rather than 104.

issues.title: Breathlessness change -2.61 and -2.13 printed with entirely positive 95% CIs
issues.explanation: Both estimates are negative, but both intervals are positive, so as printed the estimates fall outside their own CIs. The estimates sit at the intervals' midpoints in absolute value (about 2.61 and 2.13), so this is most likely a sign or formatting slip. The direction of the result (a decrease) is unambiguous.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The original manuscript showing the CIs with minus signs, or a statement that magnitudes are reported.

10.3390/jcm10235623.headline_claim: Monitoring muscle mass and strength in post-acute COVID-19 patients appears to be a key predictor of rehabilitation outcomes.
10.3390/jcm10235623.overall: This is a small, uncontrolled, single-cohort descriptive study with no sample size calculation. Its central claim that muscle monitoring is a key predictor of rehabilitation outcomes is not supported by any predictive or between-group analysis, and the claim that sarcopenic patients improved more rests on within-group p-values only. Several table cells and text statements conflict (Var (%) values, NS ferritin and SpO2 significance, BMI), so the detailed results should be treated as provisional.

primary_outcome.name: Body composition, strength, functional and respiratory parameters at discharge (no single primary outcome named)

issues.title: Muscle monitoring called a 'key predictor' of outcomes with no predictive analysis, in 34 patients
issues.explanation: The abstract and discussion state that muscle mass and strength monitoring predicts rehabilitation outcomes, and that early sarcopenia diagnosis is of paramount importance. The study reports only within-group before-after changes in 20 and 14 patients, with no sample size calculation. No analysis links baseline muscle status to outcomes, and the only correlation shown is a baseline ASM versus spirometry association. The prediction claim goes well beyond the data, and the authors' own caveat about the small sample appears only in the Conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified analysis showing that baseline muscle mass or strength predicts change in outcomes in an adequately sized cohort.

quotes.text: Monitoring muscle mass and strength in post-acute COVID-19 patients appears to be a key predictor of rehabilitation outcomes.
This sample is small and further investigation is necessary.
In S, the correlation between ASM and FVC and FEV1 was statistically significant (0.582 and 0.592, respectively)

second_reader.what_stands: The Abstract calls muscle monitoring 'a key predictor of rehabilitation outcomes' in 34 patients, but the paper reports no predictive analysis; the only correlations are cross-sectional baseline ones with spirometry that was never repeated. The Conclusions' small-sample caveat and the softer Discussion wording ('could be useful to predict') partly temper this, but the Abstract claim is not removed or qualified.

issues.title: 'More pronounced' improvement in sarcopenic patients rests on within-group p-values, with no between-group test
issues.explanation: The Discussion says sarcopenic patients improved more than non-sarcopenic ones in all domains. The evidence is that more S rows crossed p < 0.05 within the group, while NS rows often did not. The groups have 20 and 14 patients, no interaction or between-group test of change is reported, and NS also improved significantly on some measures (TUG, ASM, dyspnea). The difference in benefit between groups is therefore not established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A group-by-time interaction test or a comparison of change scores between S and NS that favours S.

quotes.text: Sarcopenic patients showed more pronounced, statistically significant improvements at T1 in all domains
TUG improved significantly in both S ( p = 0.039 *) and NS ( p = 0.045 *) groups.

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that sarcopenic patients improved 'more' rests on comparing within-group p-values and descriptive changes; no between-group or interaction test of change is reported. The statement is also only partly supported by the paper's own data, since TUG and ASM were significant in both groups and some changes (TUG percent, ASM percent) were as large or larger in NS; only PhA, HG and several respiratory measures favour S.

issues.title: Improvements attributed to rehabilitation come from uncontrolled before-after change in one 34-patient cohort
issues.explanation: All patients received the same programme and are compared only with their own admission values. Spontaneous post-COVID recovery, learning effects on TUG and BIA variation cannot be separated from the intervention. This weakens the causal wording in the Discussion more than the paper's descriptive aim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Concurrent or historical matched controls showing smaller changes without the programme.

quotes.text: were measured before and after a 28-day multidisciplinary rehabilitation program
Additionally, it can be speculated that patients in the S group, starting from a more severely de-conditioned status, benefited more from the rehabilitation intervention than NS patients.

issues.title: More than 25 uncorrected within-group tests; sex-specific claims rest on borderline p (0.017-0.046)
issues.explanation: No correction for multiple testing is described, and no primary outcome is named. Several highlighted findings sit just under 0.05, such as NS female ASM (p = 0.046) and NS TUG (p = 0.045). The 'only in females' pattern is therefore weak evidence, especially with subgroups of 5 to 11 patients.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis in which the sex-specific findings survive.

quotes.text: A p -value < 0.05 was considered to be statistically significant.
ASM in S ( p = 0.001) and NS ( p = 0.009) groups showed a statistically significant improvement only in female patients.

issues.title: Results text contradicts Tables 2-3: NS ferritin 'higher' and 'significant'; NS SpO2-after-TUG 'significant'
issues.explanation: The Results say ferritin was higher in NS than in S, but Table 3 shows the reverse (S 448.5 vs NS 151.0), as the Discussion itself notes. The Results also say NS showed a significant improvement in ferritin, but Table 3 gives p = 0.958. They further say that in NS only SpO2 after TUG improved significantly, but Table 2 gives p = 0.821 for that row. The only NS rows with p < 0.05 in Table 2 are dyspnea rows. The text therefore misdescribes which NS outcomes changed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 2 or 3 in which NS ferritin and NS SpO2 after TUG carry p < 0.05, and NS ferritin T0 exceeds the S value.

quotes.text: In NS, albumin, ferritin and vitamin D levels were higher than S
whereas in NS a statistically significant improvement could only be seen in ferritin level.
In NS, only SpO2 after TUG showed a statistically significant improvement at T1.

issues.title: Several Table 1 Var (%) values do not follow from printed means: TUG S -26.83%, ASM NS 10.67%, HG M S 6.04%
issues.explanation: Table 1 defines Var (%) from the T0 and T1 means, and most rows reproduce. For sarcopenic TUG, 31.5 to 17.9 gives -43.17%, not -26.83%. For NS ASM, 17.9 to 21.6 gives 20.67%, not 10.67%. For sarcopenic male handgrip, 19.9 to 23.9 gives 20.1%, not 6.04%. NS overall ASM T1 (21.6) also exceeds what the NS male (25.9) and female (17.8) means allow (about 20.7 when weighted 5:9). So some printed cells are wrong, and the true size of these changes cannot be read from the table. The TUG error understates the sarcopenic improvement, which is larger than the NS one when computed from the means.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The authors stating that Var (%) is the mean of individual percentage changes for these rows, with raw data reproducing them.

quotes.location: Table 1, TUG row, S Var (%) column

issues.title: NS mean BMI is 28.4 in Results text but 27.3 at T0 in Table 1
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the non-sarcopenic group's mean BMI as 28.4, but Table 1 gives 27.3 for the same group at admission. The table value matches its own percentage change, so the text appears to be wrong. This is a small reporting slip, and the BMI contrast between groups survives either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text value was computed from a different set of patients or time point.

quotes.text: Fourteen patients (M/F 5/9, mean age 68.0 (16.5) years, mean BMI 28.4 (8.9) kg/m 2 ) were not sarcopenic.

quotes.location: Table 1, BMI row, NS T0 column

issues.title: Comorbidity percentages (17.1%, 16.4%, 9.7%) cannot arise from n = 34; sarcopenia 58% vs 20/34 = 58.8%
issues.explanation: The paper reports comorbidity prevalence for 'our sample' of 34 patients as 17.1%, 16.4% and 9.7%. No whole number of patients out of 34 gives these values. The denominator is therefore different from the study sample, or the figures were taken from another source. The abstract prevalence of 58% is also slightly below 20/34 (58.8%). These are reporting errors with little effect on the findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement of the larger or different denominator used for the comorbidity percentages.

quotes.text: In our sample, prevalence was 17.1% for hypertension, 16.4% for cardiac-cerebrovascular disease and 9.7% for diabetes.
Upon admission, the prevalence of sarcopenia among our patients was 58%.

issues.title: Methods say median/IQR and Fisher/chi-square tests; tables show mean (SD) with unidentified within-group tests
issues.explanation: The Statistical Analysis section says continuous variables are reported as median and IQR, but every table caption says mean and SD. The Methods also name only Fisher's test for continuous variables, which does not give a T0-to-T1 p-value. The test that produced the within-group p-values is therefore unclear, and for skewed variables such as ferritin the mean-based Var (%) may mislead.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement identifying the test used for the within-group p-values and confirming that the tables show means and SDs.

quotes.text: Continuous variables were expressed as median and interquartile range.
All data are reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD).

issues.title: Abstract says all parameters improved, but NS female handgrip fell (22.4 to 22.2) and some rows show 0% change
issues.explanation: The abstract says all respiratory, body composition, strength and functional parameters trended better in all 34 patients. Table 1 shows a slight decline in NS female handgrip, and Table 2 shows no change in some dyspnea rows. These are small, so the effect on the overall message is minimal. It is still an imprecise absolute statement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Individual patient data showing that every patient improved on every parameter.

quotes.text: In all of the 34 patients, we observed a trend of improvement in all of the respiratory, body composition, muscle strength and functional parameters considered.

quotes.location: Table 1, HG F sub-row, NS T1 column

10.3390/jcm12010308.headline_claim: Fifteen hyperbaric oxygen therapy sessions coincided with significant and sustained improvements in quality of life, endurance, strength, working memory and attention in unvaccinated patients with post-COVID syndrome, and the therapy is recommended for randomized trials.
10.3390/jcm12010308.overall: The large pre-to-post gain in self-reported quality of life (67.8 to 83.6) is plausible as an observation, but a single-arm, unblinded study of 31 patients cannot attribute it to HBO, and the causal wording of the Conclusions goes beyond that. Several secondary claims (gas exchange, spirometry, 'sustained' benefit, '15 sessions minimum') are contradicted or only weakly supported by the paper's own results. The study is at most hypothesis-generating for a randomized trial.

primary_outcome.name: Quality of life (EQ-5D-5L, 0-100 scale)

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from 31 uncontrolled, unblinded before-after patients (no control group)
issues.explanation: All 31 patients were compared only with their own baseline, with no control arm and no blinding. Most outcomes are self-reported questionnaires, and the fitness tests were repeated four times, which allows practice effects. Spontaneous recovery over time (about six months after infection on average) is also not separable from the treatment. The Conclusions' causal wording that the sessions 'can lead to noticeable improvements' goes beyond what this design can show. The result supports at most a hypothesis for a randomized trial.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group showing no comparable change over the same period.

quotes.text: Therefore, we deliberately chose not to include a control group at this stage of the study.
it can be concluded that the application of 15 compression sessions can lead to noticeable improvements in health and performance parameters

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, uncontrolled, unblinded before-after series of 31 patients with no comparator, which the authors state and weigh as a main limitation, and much of the text uses associational language ('coincided with', 'temporally associated with', 'preliminary'). Even so, the second Conclusions paragraph says 15 sessions 'can lead to' improvements, which is causal-efficacy language that the design cannot support, since placebo effect, natural recovery, regression to the mean and repeated-testing effects are not separable from any HBOT effect; its closing recommendation, however, is

issues.title: FEV1 pre/post-exercise difference reported as both significant (p = 0.032) and not significant
issues.explanation: Section 3.4 reports a significant change in the difference between FEV1 before and after exercise (p = 0.032). Two sentences later it states there were no significant changes in the differences between pre- and post-exercise FEV1 and other spirometry values. Both cannot be true. The identical p = 0.032 also appears for post-exercise saturation, so the spirometry result may be mislabelled. This undermines the 'specific spirometric parameters' claimed as improved in the Conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary data showing that the p = 0.032 refers to a different, clearly labelled quantity from the 'no significant change' statement.

quotes.text: A significant change was observed in the difference between FEV1 before exercise and FEV1 after exercise
There were also no significant changes in the differences between FEV1/FVC, FEV1, PEF, and FEF2575 values measured before and after exercise.

issues.title: '15 sessions is the minimum' conflicts with reported significance at 5 and 10 sessions (p < 0.001)
issues.explanation: The paper reports that quality-of-life changes after 5, 10 and 15 sessions were each significant versus baseline (p < 0.001). It then says 15 sessions is the minimum needed for a significant improvement. By the authors' own tests, 5 sessions already sufficed. No comparison between 10 and 15 sessions or against a clinical threshold is shown. The claim may be a loose wording of 'largest effect at 15', but it is not supported as written.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified threshold or a 10-vs-15 session comparison showing that only the 15-session result crosses it.

quotes.text: This indicates that 15 HBO treatments is the minimum number required to significantly improve quality of life.
the reported changes in quality of life after 5, 10, and 15 HBOT sessions were statistically significant

issues.title: Discussion says gas exchange improved, but venous pO2 and pCO2 showed no change
issues.explanation: The Results report no change in pH, pO2, pCO2 or excess base; only the anion gap and lactate changed. The Discussion nonetheless states emphatically that improved gas exchange was observed. The data do not show this, and the measurements are venous, so they are poor indicators of gas exchange. The Conclusions' wording about 'specific blood gas parameters' is narrower and partly supported, but the gas-exchange claim is not.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported arterial gas or oxygenation data, or a significant change in venous pO2 or pCO2.

quotes.text: In contrast, there were no changes in pH (negative logarithm of hydrogen ion activity), pO2 (partial pressure of oxygen), pCO2 (partial pressure of carbon dioxide), or excess base.
as we observed improved gas exchange in our patients

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes tested at 0.05 with no correction; marginal p-values support the secondary claims
issues.explanation: The Statistical Analysis section sets a significance level of 0.05 and applies no multiplicity correction or primary-outcome hierarchy. Many questionnaire items, fitness tests, spirometry and gas parameters were tested, and the Conclusions pick out those that came out significant. Several cited findings have p-values between 0.015 and 0.033 and are fragile under correction. The quality-of-life result is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome and a multiplicity adjustment under which the cited secondary results remain significant.

quotes.text: The significance level was set at 0.05 (5%).
specific gasometric and spirometric parameters, and working memory and attention

issues.title: 'Sustained' improvement rests on self-reported phone follow-up at 2-24 weeks (30 of 31 patients)
issues.explanation: Long-term data come from a single telephone call 2-24 weeks after treatment, with patients rating their own quality of life. Some patients were therefore assessed only two weeks after the end of the program. There was no repeated, standardised assessment of fitness or spirometry. The authors themselves list the lack of long-term follow-up as a limitation, yet the Conclusions describe the improvement as 'sustained'. At most the data show that the self-reported gain persisted in the short term.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Standardised assessments at a fixed later time point (for example 6-12 months) showing maintained improvement.

quotes.text: A telephone survey was conducted with participants 2–24 weeks after program completion to verify the long-term impact of HBO on their quality of life.
Thus, our lack of a long-term follow-up can be considered to be one of the limitations of this work.
significant and sustained improvement in quality of life

issues.title: No trial registration; study described as both prospective protocol and retrospective data
issues.explanation: The Methods describe an ethically approved protocol with scheduled tests, which reads as prospective. The Discussion calls the data retrospective and says it could not be relied on for a proper clinical trial. Ethics approval is not trial registration, and no registry number is given. Readers therefore cannot check that the outcomes reported are those planned. The inconsistency affects the confidence placed in the outcome set rather than any single number.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry or a protocol listing the outcomes before enrolment began.

quotes.text: The scientific protocol presented in this study received a positive opinion from the Bioethics Committee of the Medical University of Silesia in Katowice, Poland
the analysis of such retrospective data may raise some controversy.

issues.title: Text says men scored higher after 5 sessions; Table 1 has women higher (73.6 vs 68.7)
issues.explanation: The Results state that men had higher mean quality of life than women both before treatment and after 5 sessions. Table 1 shows men higher only at baseline. After 5 sessions the women's mean is 73.6 and the men's is 68.7. The error is confined to one sentence about a sex difference and does not affect the main result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 1 in which the men's after-5 mean exceeds the women's.

quotes.text: Males had a higher mean life quality than females before oxygenation and after 5 sessions

quotes.location: Table 1, Woman row, After 5 HBO column

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; 31 analysed against a planned 40
issues.explanation: The paper reports no sample-size justification and enrolled 31 patients where the approved scheme planned 40. The small sample is acknowledged as a limitation, and the conclusions are framed as support for further randomized trials. The size mainly weakens the subgroup findings (sex and BMI effects) and the many secondary outcomes. For a pilot this is an ordinary weakness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation showing that 31 patients gave adequate precision for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: In addition, the study scheme basically considered a group of 40 patients.
Thus, the proposed therapy can be recommended for use in randomized clinical trials

10.3390/jcm12030741.headline_claim: After personalised coordination-team support, including a second phone consultation, some symptoms (dyspnea, anxiety, chest pain) decreased and patients valued the call, so relatively simple actions such as a phone call might be very useful to reduce feelings of abandonment.
10.3390/jcm12030741.overall: This is an uncontrolled, single-centre descriptive series of 45 patients. The descriptive findings (persistent fatigue and neurocognitive symptoms, mixed return to work) are usable, but the abstract's claim of determined efficacy and the benefit of the second call are not supported by the design or the data. Several figures are inconsistent between sections (full recovery 9% vs 4%; one third vs about 60% not back full-time), and the symptom tests are uncorrected.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly defined; pre- vs post-support frequency of self-reported symptoms (chest pain, dyspnea, anxiety, others)

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from an uncontrolled 45-patient before-after phone series with no control group
issues.explanation: Each patient was compared only with themselves at the first call (about 15 months after infection) and the second (about 22.6 months), with no concurrent control. Changes in symptoms may reflect natural recovery, regression to the mean, or the rehabilitation they received rather than the coordination support. Only 45 of 105 contacts were analysed, and the 9 lost to follow-up were not compared with completers. The abstract and Discussion nonetheless state that efficacy was determined or suggested, and the limitations do not mention the missing control.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical comparison group with a matched symptom course, or authors' text restricting the claim to descriptive change over time.

quotes.text: Self-reported symptoms, feelings of improvement and ability to return to work allowed us to determine the efficacy of the therapeutic strategy proposed.
Organ-related symptoms such as chest pain and dyspnea significantly decreased after re-education, suggesting therapeutic efficacy.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper claims efficacy ('allowed us to determine the efficacy' in the Abstract; 'suggesting therapeutic efficacy' in 4.2) from a single-arm series of 45 patients with only before-after McNemar tests on yes/no self-reported symptoms, no control group and no adjustment for spontaneous recovery over the 7.5 months between calls. The Discussion wording is hedged ('suggesting') and the overall conclusions are modest and partly negative, but the Abstract statement is firmer than the design supports and the limitations section does not mention the absent control group.

issues.title: 'All patients greatly appreciated' the second call is not backed by any reported measure
issues.explanation: The abstract states that all patients greatly appreciated the second phone consultation, and the conclusion builds on this to say a phone call may reduce feelings of abandonment. The Methods and Results report no satisfaction or abandonment measure. Only the 45 patients who completed the second call could be asked, and the 9 lost to follow-up are not mentioned in this claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported satisfaction or abandonment measure from the second call, with responses from all 45 patients.

quotes.text: All patients greatly appreciated the second phone consultation.
relatively simple actions such as a phone call might be useful to reduce patients' feelings of abandonment

issues.title: Conclusion says one third did not return full-time; Results imply about 60% (36% not working at all)
issues.explanation: Among the 40 non-retired patients, 40% worked full-time, so about 60% did not return to full-time work. Only 36% did no work at all. The Conclusion attributes non-return to full-time work to 'one third', which fits the 36% not working at all but not the full-time definition it uses. The final conclusion therefore makes work outcomes look better than the Results show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 6 showing that about one third, not 60%, of non-retired patients were below full-time work.

quotes.text: 40% of them worked full-time
many patients (one third) felt the help insufficient and accordingly, did not return to work full-time

issues.title: Ethics approval (12/10/2022) post-dates the Sept 2021-Mar 2022 inclusion window of a 'prospective' study
issues.explanation: All contacts between September 2021 and March 2022 were included, and the first calls were made 15 months after infection. The ethics approval is dated 12/10/2022, after the whole inclusion window on either reading of the date. The paper does not say whether consent and approval covered contacts made before approval, or whether the data were collected retrospectively. A 'prospective' label is hard to reconcile with this timeline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the data came from routine care and were analysed retrospectively with approval, or evidence of earlier consent or an earlier approval reference.

quotes.text: All queries addressed to the coordination team between September 2021 and March 2022
approved by the ethics committee of the University of Strasbourg (CE-2022-108, 12/10/2022)

issues.title: About 8 symptom McNemar tests at p<0.05, uncorrected; dyspnea (p=0.013) fails Holm
issues.explanation: Each symptom was tested separately with no multiplicity adjustment. Chest pain (p=0.007), anxiety (p=0.004) and dyspnea (p=0.013) are reported as significant reductions and carried into the abstract. With roughly eight tests, the dyspnea result would not survive a Holm or Bonferroni correction and chest pain would be borderline. These are secondary descriptive outcomes, so the effect is limited.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified correction or a statement that the symptom tests were exploratory and no inference should rest on them.

quotes.text: Statistical significance was considered at p < 0.05.
the frequency of chest pain demonstrated a significant reduction

issues.title: Full recovery at 22 months given as 9% in Results but 4% in Discussion
issues.explanation: Section 3.5 gives 9% felt healthy, 33% moderate and 20% minimal improvement, and 38% no improvement, which sum to 100%. The Discussion then cites 'total recovery (4%)' alongside the same 33% moderate figure. The two statements cannot both describe the same 22-month outcome, and the Discussion's own categories (4+33+20+38) sum to only 95%. This is a single wrong figure and the main claims are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Figure 5 showing 4% complete recovery with a different category (for example 5% 'healthy' but not recovered) that the text does not explain.

quotes.text: only 9% of the population of complex SARS-CoV-2 patients felt healthy 22 months after virus infection
either total recovery (4%) or moderate improvement (33%)

issues.title: Symptom outcomes from an unvalidated, unblinded phone checklist; 1-10 ratings collected but not reported
issues.explanation: Symptoms were recorded by yes/no questions from a formalised but non-validated list during phone calls by the same team that delivered the support. The 1-10 severity ratings are described in the Methods but never presented. The limitation is acknowledged, but it still weakens the symptom-change results that support the efficacy claim.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the checklist was validated or that outcomes were assessed independently of the care team.

quotes.text: If the answer was yes, we asked patients to rate it from 1 to 10 (10 being the worst).
Self-reported symptoms are by nature subjective and validated questionnaires should add value to the results.

10.3390/jcm12030776.headline_claim: A 14-day telerehabilitation therapeutic exercise program of strength and breathing exercises is effective in improving physical and respiratory function in non-hospitalized people with post-COVID-19 conditions.
10.3390/jcm12030776.overall: The large short-term differences in BS and MD12 are probably real, but the conclusion that the programme was 'demonstrated to be effective' rests on an open-label comparison with a no-treatment control and largely self-reported or home-performed outcomes. The paper contradicts itself on blinding, misstates control-group significance for BS and MD12, and prints between-group tests for only three of five outcomes. The result is best read as tentative evidence of short-term benefit.

primary_outcome.name: not designated; five outcomes reported: BS, MD12, VAFS, 6MWT, 30STST

issues.title: Trial called 'double-blind' though participants and therapists were unblinded; outcomes are self-reported against no-treatment control
issues.explanation: The paper states both that participants and therapists were not blinded and that participants and assessors were blinded, so the design is called double-blind. Participants knew whether they were exercising or resting, and the control arm received no intervention or attention. Fatigue, dyspnea and effort were self-rated by the patient on a video call, and the walk and sit-to-stand tests were self-performed at home. Expectation and response bias could therefore inflate the between-arm differences, and the headline effect sizes cannot be separated from them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the self-reported outcomes were collected and scored in a way independent of participants' knowledge of allocation, or an attention-matched control arm.

quotes.text: Participants and therapists were not blinded to treatment due to the nature of the interventions.
Still, assessors and participants were blinded to group assignment, so the study design was double-blind.
This is a self-report scale measured from 0 to 10, and it is a valid and reliable instrument for the quantitative assessment of fatigue

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the trial double-blind while stating participants and therapists were not blinded, and then asserts participants were blinded, which is contradictory and implausible against a no-intervention rest control. Most outcomes (fatigue, dyspnea, effort, and home-recorded steps) are self-reported or participant-generated, so the large effects are open to expectation and performance bias that the conclusion does not weigh; only assessor blinding and the evaluator-counted 30STST are partly shielded.

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from EG-significant/CG-non-significant contrast; between-group p printed for only 3 of 5 outcomes
issues.explanation: The Results argue that the programme worked because the exercise arm changed significantly while the control arm did not. A difference in significance is not a test of the difference between arms. Table 2 places p-values under each arm's within-group change. A between-group F and p appear only for BS, MD12 and 30STST, and VAFS and 6MWT have only an R² with no test statistic. The control-group 'no change' premise is also contradicted by Table 1 for BS and MD12. The very large between-group effects on BS and MD12 are probably real, but the claim for the other outcomes is under-documented.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Printed between-group test statistics (e.g. an independent t-test or ANCOVA with p and CI) for VAFS and 6MWT showing significant differences.

quotes.text: which has not obtained significant intragroup differences ( p > 0.05) in any study variable (Table 2)
induced statistically significant improvement between groups (Figure 2) and within groups in the experimental group

issues.title: 6MWT replaced by self-recorded phone step counts at home; Borg/VAFS values chosen by patients
issues.explanation: The '6MWT' is the number of steps counted by the participant's own smartphone at home, not a supervised walking distance. The Borg and fatigue values were whatever value the patient considered adequate when asked on a video call. The Discussion lists 'validated outcome measures' as a strength although these adaptations were not validated. The measurements are noisy and open to bias, but a bias that applies to both arms could be partly offset in the comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Validation data for smartphone step counts as a 6MWT substitute in this population, or supervised measurements in a subsample.

quotes.text: It consists of recording the number of steps through the 'StepsApp', using the patient's smartphone, and performing the following procedure:
asked the patients what the VASF value they considered adequate was

issues.title: Conclusion states effectiveness 'demonstrated' from an unblinded 14-day trial with self-reported outcomes
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says the programme has been demonstrated to be effective in improving physical and respiratory function. The trial was open-label against a no-treatment control, used mostly self-rated or self-performed outcomes at home, and followed participants only to the end of the 14-day programme. The Discussion admits the short follow-up, but the Conclusion does not say 'short-term' or mention the lack of blinding. The effects look large, so a short-term benefit is plausible, but 'demonstrated to be effective' is stronger than this design supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A conclusion qualified as short-term and open-label, or blinded and objective corroboration of the effect.

quotes.text: has been demonstrated to be effective in improving physical and respiratory function post-COVID-19.
The study had some limitations in that we only performed a short-term follow-up, when the exercise program finished.

issues.title: Reported F(1,75) is incompatible with 48 analysed participants; R² values imply df2 = 46
issues.explanation: The F statistics are printed with a second degrees of freedom of 75, but only 48 participants were analysed. The reported R² values reproduce the F values only if df2 is 46, which fits n = 48. The df is therefore a misprint, which is minor, but it also shows that the between-group F test is only partly reported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 75 refers to something other than the error df of a two-group, n = 48 analysis.

quotes.text: After conducting 68 evaluations, 52 participants met the inclusion criteria and were enrolled in the study, and 48 completed the trial (92%).

issues.title: Five outcomes each tested at 0.05 with no primary outcome named
issues.explanation: Five outcomes were each tested at the 0.05 level with no correction and no designated primary outcome. The sample size calculation does not say which outcome it was based on. The key results are at p < 0.001, so correction would probably not change them. The weaker outcomes, VAFS and 6MWT, have less certain support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registered primary outcome and analysis plan naming a single primary outcome, or adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: A p -value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant in all analyses.

10.3390/jcm12062233.headline_claim: A 3-month cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program improves recovery of endothelium-dependent vasodilation and arteriosclerosis in convalescent COVID-19 patients.
10.3390/jcm12062233.overall: The direction of the finding is plausible and the main tables are mostly internally consistent, with two small text-versus-table errors. The strong 'conclusively' claim of improved arteriosclerosis, and the IL-6 patient-selection claim, are not supported by an unregistered, open-label study of 30 per arm with no randomization details, so the conclusions are tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Flow-mediated dilation (FMD), brachial artery (paper does not name a primary outcome; FMD is the first-listed outcome)

issues.title: 'Conclusively' improves arteriosclerosis claimed from an open-label two-arm study of 30 per arm, no power calculation
issues.explanation: The abstract states conclusively that rehabilitation improves arteriosclerosis and endothelial recovery. The evidence is 30 patients per arm, no sample-size calculation, a non-blinded control of 'advised to be physically active', and surrogate functional measures (PWV, AIx) rather than structural arterial disease. The Discussion itself says the small sample may limit credibility. The control arm's FMD also improved, so the benefit is relative, not absolute. The direction is plausible, but 'conclusively' is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified power calculation and blinded outcome assessment, with the claim framed as arterial stiffness rather than arteriosclerosis.

quotes.text: Conclusively, a 3-month cardiopulmonary postacute COVID-19 rehabilitation program improves recovery of endothelium-dependent vasodilation and arteriosclerosis.
The results of our study should be interpreted with caution, since the relatively small sample size may limit its credibility.

second_reader.what_stands: The abstract's closing sentence is stated more strongly than a single 60-person randomized study with no reported power calculation, no stated blinding and no multiplicity handling supports; 'Conclusively' and the unqualified 'improves ... arteriosclerosis' are not matched by the abstract's own content, and the small-sample caveat appears only in Section 4.2. The point is overstated in two respects: the paper does not itself call the study open-label (only the design implies it), and the interaction tests for PWV (p < 0.001) and AIx (p = 0.005) are genuinely significant, so the stiffness resul

issues.title: No participant flow, attrition or outcome-assessor blinding reported for an open-label comparison
issues.explanation: All 60 randomized patients appear in the analyses, with no stated dropouts despite monthly re-infection testing and exclusion of positives. The control arm was only advised to be active, so FMD, PWV and AIx are open to unblinded measurement bias. FMD in particular is operator-dependent. The size of the effects therefore carries extra uncertainty.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CONSORT flow diagram and a statement that operators were blinded to allocation.

quotes.text: Patients in the no rehabilitation group were advised to be physically active.
All tests were performed by the same operator throughout the study.

issues.title: Median-split IL-6 subgroup (n≈15 per half) headlined as effect modification without an interaction test
issues.explanation: The claim that rehabilitation helps high-IL-6 patients more rests on a median split inside the 30-patient rehabilitation arm. About 15 patients fall in each half, and no IL-6 by rehabilitation interaction p is reported. The control-arm comparison is non-significant, but a difference in significance is not a test of difference. The Conclusion treats this as guidance for selecting patients, which the data cannot support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported rehabilitation-by-IL-6 interaction test using IL-6 as a continuous variable, or a pre-specified analysis plan.

quotes.text: Convalescent COVID-19 subjects of the study group (rehabilitation) with increased serum levels of circulating IL-6 had a greater reduction in FMD.
especially in patients with high levels of IL-6 before the initiation of cardiac rehabilitation.

issues.title: Randomized trial with no registration reported; the one NCT number cited belongs to a different trial
issues.explanation: The study is described as prospective and randomized, but no registry number or pre-specified outcomes are given. The NCT05668039 record concerns enhanced external counterpulsation and fatigue, not this study. Without registration, outcome selection (FMD, PWV, AIx, IL-6 subgroup) cannot be checked against a plan.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registration number for this study with pre-specified outcomes.

quotes.text: An ongoing randomized trial (NCT05668039) on the effectiveness of this method in improving long-COVID-19 fatigue is expected to provide further evidence.
In this study, we prospectively enrolled 60 adult convalescent patients from COVID19 infection one month post-acute disease.

issues.title: Randomization method and concealment not described; baseline severity 7 vs 2 severe cases called 'evenly distributed'
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were randomized 1:1 but gives no sequence generation, concealment or stratification. Baseline disease severity differed numerically (severe 23.3% vs 6.7%, mild 16.7% vs 33.3%), and age and BMI also differed by several units. The text calls the groups evenly distributed. Without a described method, the reader cannot judge whether allocation was truly random, and no adjusted analysis is given.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of computer-generated sequence and concealed allocation.

quotes.text: Regarding the disease course in the acute phase, the individuals were evenly distributed.
Convalescent COVID-19 subjects were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to participate or not in a rehabilitation program.

issues.title: Baseline PWV for no-rehabilitation group: text 8.8 (1.9) m/s vs Table 1 and Table 2 8.9 (1.8) m/s
issues.explanation: The baseline-characteristics paragraph gives the control group's baseline PWV as 8.8 (1.9) m/s. Table 1 and Table 2 (T0) give 8.9 (1.8), and 8.8 (1.9) is the T1 value. Recomputing from the table values reproduces p = 0.10, whereas the text values would give about 0.15. The error is confined to the text.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text used a different time point or subset for baseline PWV.

quotes.text: PWV (rehabilitation: 8.2 (1.4) m/s vs. no rehabilitation: 8.8 (1.9) m/s, p = 0.10)

quotes.location: Table 1, PWV row, No Rehabilitation column

issues.title: Baseline AIx between-group p: text 0.28 vs Table 1 0.49 for identical means and SDs
issues.explanation: The Results text gives p = 0.28 for the baseline AIx comparison. Table 1 gives 0.49 for the same row. Recomputing from the printed means and SDs supports 0.49. The text p is a reporting error, and the conclusion of no baseline difference does not change.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text p came from a different test, such as adjusted or non-parametric.

quotes.text: AIx (rehabilitation: 25.9 (9.8)% vs. no rehabilitation: 27.6 (9.2), p = 0.28)

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

issues.title: Methods call 60 subjects 'the control group'; the randomized control arm is n = 30; healthy controls not described
issues.explanation: Methods 2.1 says 60 subjects were enrolled and served as the control group, while the randomized no-rehabilitation arm is 30. Results 3.1 refers to 60 healthy controls from Supplementary Table S1. The Methods never describe how these healthy controls were recruited or measured, and the terms 'control group' and 'healthy controls' are used for different groups. The randomized comparison itself is not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Methods description of the healthy-control cohort in the paper.

quotes.text: 60 subjects were enrolled and served as the control group
The entire study population consisted of 60 convalescent COVID-19 individuals and 60 healthy controls (Supplementary Table S1).

issues.title: Abstract supports PWV and AIx benefit by within-arm significance; interaction p only in Results
issues.explanation: The abstract contrasts significant change in the rehabilitation arm with non-significant change in controls for PWV and AIx. That contrast is not itself a between-group test. The Results do report interaction p-values (PWV < 0.001, AIx = 0.005), so the conclusion has support, but the abstract wording is weaker. The interaction tests are repeated-measures ANOVA without baseline adjustment, despite numerically different baselines.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Abstract reporting interaction p for PWV and AIx.

quotes.text: PWV was improved in the study group (8.2 ± 1.3 m/s vs. 6.6 ± 1.0 m/s, p < 0.001) but not in the control group (8.9 ± 1.8 m/s vs. 8.8 ± 1.9 m/s, p = 0.74).

10.3390/jcm12134390.headline_claim: Both low-intensity and high-intensity cardiopulmonary rehabilitation improve cardiopulmonary parameters over 3 months in patients recovering from severe COVID-19, with no clear difference between the two intensities.
10.3390/jcm12134390.overall: The within-arm improvements in lung and exercise measures over 3 months are plausible, but the design (no untreated control, unpaired tests on paired data, unexplained baseline imbalance) cannot attribute them to rehabilitation, and the abstract's 'proving' and 'long-term' language overreaches. Several printed results are also inconsistent (work intensity in the high-intensity arm, swapped group labels in the text), so the conclusions should be read as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Not specified; no single primary outcome is named (multiple pulmonary, cardiac and exercise-test measures)

issues.title: Causal benefit of rehabilitation claimed from pre-post change with no untreated control
issues.explanation: Both arms were rehabilitated and each is compared only with its own baseline measured at discharge. Spontaneous recovery after severe COVID-19 over 3 months could produce the same improvements, and the authors concede this. The conclusions nonetheless say rehabilitation 'plays a pivotal role' in improvement.
