issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified single primary outcome or a correction showing the result survives.

quotes.text: The threshold for statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
However, the significance of this result is low ( p = 0.047, almost on the verge of being insignificant)

issues.title: Registered fatigue primary outcome not reported; paper names no primary and headlines FIM
issues.explanation: The registry lists muscle fatigue assessment and isokinetic force as primary outcomes. The paper reports isokinetic force but no fatigue measure, designates no primary outcome, and its abstract highlights FIM and extensor strength. Because only the current registry version was retrieved, a registry change cannot be ruled out, but the omission of the registered fatigue outcome from a trial about fatigue syndrome is unexplained.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing fatigue was removed before enrolment, or a protocol naming FIM as primary.

quotes.text: The Berg scale, Tinetti scale, six-minute walking test, isokinetic muscle force test, hand grip strength, Barthel Index, and Functional Independence Measure were used to measure the outcomes.
Several measurement tools were used to assess functional physical ability

issues.title: No sample size calculation or non-inferiority margin, yet non-harm of robot substitution is asserted
issues.explanation: No power calculation or equivalence margin is reported, and the study says only that a few more participants than required were enrolled. A non-significant interaction in 81 participants does not show that substituting robot time for therapist time did no harm. The statement is plausible given similar gains but is not established by the design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified non-inferiority margin and power calculation.

quotes.text: The study initially included a few more participants in both groups than required because we expected dropouts.
Substituting a part of traditional rehabilitation with robotic rehabilitation did not negatively alter rehabilitation outcomes.

10.3390/v14122614.headline_claim: Oral and inhaled bacteriophage cocktails were safe in post-COVID rehabilitation and produced a threefold decrease in the anaerobic imbalance ratio and in ESR, with the study concluding that phages are relevant to rehabilitating the microbiota.
10.3390/v14122614.overall: The safety observations and the descriptive before-after changes are reported plausibly, but the efficacy conclusions cannot be relied on. There is no concurrent control for the main microbiota ratio, the one significant ratio result is unadjusted among many tests, and 6 of 30 patients are unaccounted for. The authors' wording ('demonstrate relevance') goes beyond what a 24-patient uncontrolled pilot supports, and the developer relationship is not discussed.

primary_outcome.name: Bacteroides fragilis group/Faecalibacterium prausnitzii ratio (anaerobic imbalance ratio)

issues.title: Efficacy claims rest on uncontrolled before-after changes; the ratio result is 1 p=0.033 among ~20 unadjusted taxa tests
issues.explanation: The anaerobic imbalance ratio, saturation, respiratory rate and CRP/ESR changes are all within-patient before-after comparisons in treated patients, so spontaneous recovery after COVID and regression to the mean are not separated from a phage effect. There is no concurrent control for the ratio, no blinding, no randomisation and no sample-size calculation. The ratio's p = 0.033 is one of about 20 taxa and marker tests with no multiplicity adjustment, and the other taxa are non-significant. Even so, the Conclusions say the results 'demonstrate the relevance' of phages for microbiota rehabilitation, which is stronger than a 24-patient uncontrolled pilot can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent control group measured on the same microbiota markers, or a pre-specified primary outcome with a multiplicity-adjusted result.

quotes.text: After phage therapy, a statistically significant threefold decrease in the anaerobic imbalance ratio was detected.
The results demonstrate the relevance of bacteriophages in the rehabilitation of the microbiota of patients who have undergone COVID-19 and received antibiotic treatment.

second_reader.what_stands: The efficacy claims (ratio decrease, ESR, saturation, 'demonstrate the relevance' in the Conclusions) rest on a single-arm before-after comparison. The comparison group (n = 8) is reported only for some clinical variables, not for the ratio, and the groups differ in sex and age. The ratio's p = 0.033 is one of roughly 20 unadjusted taxon-level tests with no stated alpha or correction, so it would not survive a standard multiplicity adjustment. The conclusion is therefore stronger than the design supports. The exact test count cannot be fixed because of table scrambling, and the median fold cha

issues.title: 30 enrolled but microbiota and CRP results are reported on 24, with no flow or reason for the 6 missing
issues.explanation: Methods and demographics describe 30 participants. The microbiota and CRP results are given for 24 (22/24 with high bacterial mass; CRP in 4 of 24), and the paper never says what happened to the other 6. Table 1 and Table 3 give no n at all. The reader cannot tell who was analysed or whether the loss of 20% of patients was related to outcome. The problem is incomplete reporting, not a proven numeric contradiction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A participant flow stating that 6 patients lacked paired samples for reasons unrelated to outcome, with the n for each table.

quotes.text: Our prospective pilot study included subjects with the post-COVID syndrome ( n = 30)
Almost all subjects had levels of total bacterial mass above the reference values on admission (92%, 22/24)

issues.title: ESR/haemoglobin 'versus control' claim relies on Table 1 before-after p values and an 8-person non-randomised group
issues.explanation: The text says haemoglobin rose and ESR fell significantly in comparison with the control group, but the only p values in the paper (0.007 for each) are before-after within the treated group. The comparison group has 8 patients, 7 of them female (87%) versus 53% in the treated group, and was rehabilitated only in August 2022. No between-group test or adjustment is shown, so the abstract's ESR result is not shown to be caused by the phages.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table S1 with a between-group test of change, adjusted for sex, age and baseline values.

quotes.text: A statistically significant increase in hemoglobin level and decrease in erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (Table 1) were registered in comparison with the control group (Table S1).
7 study participants were female (87%), and 1 was male (13%).

issues.title: Phage products made by the authors' own company yet 'no conflict of interest' is declared
issues.explanation: Both cocktails were developed by RPC 'MicroMir', which is the first-listed affiliation of many authors. The paper nevertheless states no conflict of interest and no external funding, and gives no information on the company's role in analysis or interpretation. A reader cannot judge whether this developer relationship could bear on the favourable framing.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the developing centre has no financial interest in the product and played no role in analysis or reporting.

quotes.text: Both cocktails were developed by research and production center 'MicroMir' (RPC 'MicroMir') and included phages from an in vitro study.
The authors declare no conflict of interest.

issues.title: Prospective interventional pilot has ethics approval but no registry entry or stated primary outcome
issues.explanation: The paper reports an ethics protocol number but no trial registration and no pre-specified primary outcome. The headline ratio result is therefore one of many measured outcomes, which adds to the multiplicity concern. Whether registration was expected for this kind of pilot is a matter of judgement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry record or published protocol listing the outcomes.

quotes.text: approved by the Ethics Committee of Federal Research and Clinical Center of Intensive Care Medicine and Rehabilitology (protocol code PP #4/20 from 22 September 2020).

issues.title: Supplementary Fig S1 legend: lung damage 800/3220 cm3 printed as 26%, arithmetic gives 24.8%
issues.explanation: The legend gives lung capacity 3220 cm3 and damage 800 cm3 and calls this 26%. The division gives about 24.8%. The left and right lung volumes (436 + 364 = 800) are consistent with the 800 cm3 total, so the percentage is the figure that does not match. It affects one illustrative example, not the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 26% is a mean of lung-specific percentages rather than damage divided by total capacity.

quotes.text: Lung capacity 3220 cm 3 , lung damage 800 cm 3 (26%)

10.34883/pi.2024.27.4.012.headline_claim: An integrated programme of acupuncture reflexotherapy, exercise with yoga elements and small-group psychotherapy was the most effective rehabilitation for neuropsychological post-COVID manifestations, with the greatest improvement in symptoms, mood and functional capacity.
10.34883/pi.2024.27.4.012.overall: The finding that all groups improved is plausible, but the claim that the acupuncture-plus-exercise programme was most effective is weakly supported. Allocation is not described as random, baselines differ, the control is not contact-matched, and the headline HADS reductions are not reproduced by the printed table means. Several table and text values are also internally inconsistent.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome designated; conclusion rests on change in symptom frequency, with HADS, EQ-5, 6MWT, Borg and mMRC also reported

issues.title: Labelled randomized but allocation method absent; groups defined by programme received
issues.explanation: The paper calls the study an open randomized trial, but gives no randomization method or concealment, and describes groups as formed according to the programme conducted. Baseline tables show the main group differed (HADS depression 6,5 vs 10,1; 6MWT 363,6 vs about 352-354 m). Without credible randomization, the between-group superiority claim may reflect selection or baseline differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described random allocation procedure (sequence generation and concealment) or a registry record.

quotes.text: открытое рандомизированное проспективное исследование
В зависимости от проводимой программы медицинской реабилитации пациенты были разделены на 4 группы

second_reader.what_stands: The study is labelled 'открытое рандомизированное', but the text gives no allocation method and defines the groups by the programme they received. I could not see Fig. 1, so I cannot exclude that the figure explains allocation.

issues.title: Claim that the programme minimises late COVID-19 complications is not an outcome measured
issues.explanation: The closing statement says the method helps minimise the development of late COVID-19 complications. The study measured symptom frequency, function and mood scores in patients who already had post-COVID symptoms, not the incidence of new complications. The preventive claim goes beyond the data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data on incidence of new late complications over follow-up compared with a control.

quotes.text: способствует минимизации развития поздних осложнений COVID-19
Наиболее эффективной оказалась программа реабилитации, включающая процедуры ИРТ и ЛФК

second_reader.what_stands: Symptom and function improvements were measured, but the development of late COVID-19 complications was not, so the sentence overstates what the data show. The wording is acceptable only if it is read as symptom reduction in patients who already had post-COVID syndrome.

issues.title: HADS reductions of 66,7%/53,5% in main group vs about 21%/16% implied by Table 5 means
issues.explanation: The text says main-group HADS depression and anxiety fell by 66,7% and 53,5%. Table 5 means imply only about a 21% fall (6,5 to 5,1) and a 16% fall (6,08 to 5,1). The main group also started with a much lower baseline depression score (6,5) than the other groups (10,1), contradicting the claimed homogeneity of groups. The headline psycho-emotional advantage is therefore not supported by the table as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of the percentages (for example, share of patients reaching normal HADS) that reproduces 66,7% and 53,5% from the data.

quotes.text: по шкале HADS степень выраженности депрессии и тревожности снизилась на 66,7% и на 53,5%

quotes.location: Table 5, HADS depression, После, main group

second_reader.what_stands: The 66.7% and 53.5% reductions in the main group cannot be reproduced from Table 5, where the means imply about 21.5% (depression) and 16.1% (anxiety). The comparison-group percentages also do not match the table, and the main group started from a much lower baseline depression score than the others (6.5 vs 10.1). The paper does not say what metric the percentages refer to.

issues.title: Main group's multi-component programme compared with unsupervised home exercise; contact not matched
issues.explanation: The main group received supervised exercise, acupuncture and group psychotherapy. The control did home exercise with no supervision or matched contact. Differences therefore reflect the whole package and extra attention, not acupuncture itself, yet the conclusion names acupuncture and exercise as the effective ingredients. The acupuncture-only arm is the only partial test of acupuncture, and the paper does not test main versus that arm directly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A factorial or dismantling design, or a contact-matched control showing the same difference.

quotes.text: самостоятельно в домашних условиях ежедневно занимались лечебной физкультурой
В основную группу входили 46 пациентов, которые получали комплексное реабилитационное лечение

second_reader.what_stands: The main group received a supervised multi-component programme (acupuncture, yoga/qigong exercise, group psychotherapy) while the control did unsupervised home exercise, so contact time and attention were not matched. The main-versus-control difference therefore cannot be attributed to any specific component. Comparison group 2 (acupuncture only) offers only a partial component contrast.

issues.title: Superiority inferred largely from within-group percent changes; between-group tests partial
issues.explanation: For 6MWT, symptom prevalence and HADS the comparison between programmes rests on percentage change from each group's own baseline, with no between-group test or baseline adjustment. Some Borg and EQ-5 comparisons are tested between groups. The claim that the main group was best is therefore tested directly only for some outcomes.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Between-group comparisons (e.g. ANCOVA on follow-up values) for each outcome showing the main group superior.

quotes.text: Увеличилась дистанция ходьбы при проведении теста ТШХ на 18%, при этом выраженность одышки по шкале Борга снизилась на 53%, а мышечной усталости - на 50% (p<0,05).

issues.title: Many outcomes and timepoints tested at p<0,05 with no primary outcome or correction
issues.explanation: The methods set a single threshold of P<0,05 with Student's t-tests across a dozen outcomes, four groups and three timepoints. No primary outcome is named and no correction is applied. Isolated nominal significances could arise by chance, although the consistency of direction across outcomes lessens this concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: За статистически значимые изменения принимали уровень достоверности Р<0,05.

issues.title: Identical baseline HADS depression 10,1±1,2 in control and both comparison groups
issues.explanation: Table 5 prints the same baseline mean and SD for three groups, while the main group has 6,5±2,6. Exact agreement in three groups is improbable for independent samples, and suggests a copy-forward or reporting slip. It cannot be resolved without source data and it affects the depression comparison against the main group.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level baseline HADS data showing identical summaries in these groups.

quotes.location: Table 5, depression, До, control and comparison groups

issues.title: Open-label design with mainly self-reported outcomes; no blinded assessment
issues.explanation: The study states it is open, and most headline outcomes (symptom frequencies, Borg, HADS, EQ-5) are subjective. No blinded outcome assessment is described. This weakens the size of the reported advantage, though blinding would be difficult in this setting.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors and analysts were blinded to group.

quotes.text: открытое рандомизированное проспективное исследование

issues.title: Main group baseline weakness prevalence: text 71,4% vs Table 1 71,7% (33/46)
issues.explanation: The Results text gives the main group's baseline general weakness/irritability as 71,4%. Table 1 gives 33 of 46, printed as 71,7%, which is the arithmetically correct value. This is a small reporting slip and does not alter any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Nothing; the figure is checkable from the printed counts.

quotes.text: общей слабости и повышенной раздражительности с 71,4% до 13,04%

quotes.location: Table 1, general weakness row, main group

issues.title: Baseline values differ between Tables 2-3 and Table 4 (6MWT 352,7 vs 353,5 m; SpO2 96,7 vs 95,7%)
issues.explanation: The same pre-treatment measurements are printed differently in the baseline tables and in the dynamics tables. Comparison group 1 6MWT is 352,7 m in Table 3 and 353,5 m in Table 4. Comparison group 1 SpO2 is 96,7% in Table 2 and 95,7% in the Table 4 baseline row. Similar small differences appear for comparison group 2 (351,7 vs 351,3 m; Borg 6,26 vs 6,27) and the control 6MWT SD (30,46 vs 30,4). These do not change conclusions but show the baselines were not consistently carried between tables.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that Tables 3 and 4 use different analysis sets, or the original table showing matching values.

issues.title: Control sleep-disturbance count printed as 2 of 38 beside 63,1% (24/38 = 63.2%)

10.35339/ic.11.3.kov.headline_claim: Increasing the number of physical rehabilitation sessions per day (2 vs 1) in ICU-treated severe COVID-19 patients demonstrates significant potential for reducing post-COVID syndrome manifestations and improving psycho-emotional state.
10.35339/ic.11.3.kov.overall: The headline claim that two daily sessions reduce post-COVID syndrome manifestations is weakly supported. Allocation was by an unstated process without randomization or adjustment, only two subjective, unblinded, unadjusted outcomes reached p=0.02, and the objective functional and cognitive outcomes were null. Post-COVID status was assessed only days after discharge, so the finding is at best hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: PCFS scale (post-COVID functional status) score; no primary outcome is explicitly designated

issues.title: Dose groups (51 vs 51) formed by an unstated rule; no randomization, no adjustment, no baseline outcomes
issues.explanation: Patients were placed in 1-session or 2-session groups, but the paper does not say how, or whether the choice depended on clinician judgement, period or patient condition. Several comorbidities are imbalanced (diabetes 43% vs 29%, CKD 25% vs 16%) and the between-group outcome tests are unadjusted. Baseline HADS and PCFS are not reported, so differences at discharge may reflect who got more sessions rather than the extra session itself. This undermines the causal reading of the HADS and PCFS differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A described allocation procedure unrelated to patient characteristics (for example alternating allocation or a fixed staffing period), plus adjusted analyses or baseline HADS and PCFS showing balance.

quotes.text: Group 1 consisted of 51 patients who underwent 1 session per day, while Group 2 included 51 patients who had 2 sessions per day.
It is important to note that a group of patients without rehabilitation was not formed for ethical reasons.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does not state how patients were allocated to 1 versus 2 sessions per day, does not describe randomization, reports no baseline values for any outcome, and compares groups with unadjusted tests only, so confounding by allocation cannot be excluded. It is not true that baseline comparability is unexamined: Table 1 compares demographics, comorbidities and admission severity, with no significant differences reported for the tested variables, although the comorbidity rows have no p values and show some imbalance (e.g. diabetes 43% vs 29%). The lack of a no-rehabilitation arm is explained

issues.title: Conclusion claims reduced post-COVID syndrome from PCFS taken 5-7 days after discharge; other outcomes null
issues.explanation: The conclusion says two daily sessions show significant potential for reducing post-COVID syndrome manifestations and improving psycho-emotional state. PCFS was measured on average 5-7 days after discharge, which captures early functional status rather than the persisting symptoms that define post-COVID syndrome. AM-PAC, JH-HLM and MMSE showed no significant differences. The positive findings rest on two unadjusted p=0.02 results in a non-randomized comparison, so the headline overstates what the data support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Follow-up of at least 3 months showing a PCFS or symptom difference in a randomized or adjusted comparison.

quotes.text: The survey was performed, on average, 5-7 days after discharge from the hospital.
However, the difference between these groups was not statistically significant (p=0.24).
Intensive rehabilitation programs may assist in alleviating symptoms such as fatigue and weakness

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion's wording about reducing post-COVID syndrome and alleviating fatigue and weakness rests on a PCFS taken only about 5-7 days after discharge, which is too early to establish post-COVID syndrome and does not measure fatigue or weakness separately; the conclusion also omits the short follow-up caveat given in the limitations. It is not accurate that all other outcomes were null, since HADS also differed (p = 0.02), though AM-PAC, JH-HLM and MMSE did not.

issues.title: Only outcomes showing a difference (HADS, PCFS) are subjective; blinding of assessors not reported
issues.explanation: The two outcomes with p=0.02 are the self-rated HADS and the PCFS, collected at a first visit or by phone. The paper does not report blinding of patients, therapists or assessors. Objective or observer-rated functional measures (AM-PAC, JH-HLM) showed no difference. Expectation or assessment bias could therefore account for the subjective differences, and this is not addressed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that PCFS and HADS were administered by assessors blinded to group.

quotes.text: This subjective method is designed for the screening of anxiety and depression in hospitalized patients.
The PCFS evaluation was conducted during the first visit to the physician or during a phone contact with the physician.

second_reader.what_stands: The two outcomes with p = 0.02 (HADS and PCFS) are the self-reported or interview-based ones, and the paper does not report assessor blinding or who administered the scales. The statement that only these are subjective is too strong, since MMSE, AM-PAC and JH-HLM also depend on a rater, and the paper itself does not say they were blinded either.

issues.title: No sample-size calculation or multiplicity control: two of six outcomes at p=0.02 drive the conclusion
issues.explanation: No power calculation is reported. Six outcomes (AM-PAC, JH-HLM, MMSE, HADS, PCFS and the baseline tests) were compared with unadjusted U-tests. The only 'significant' findings are p=0.02 for HADS and PCFS. With six outcome comparisons and no correction, two nominal p=0.02 results are weak support for a confident conclusion, and PCFS is described as 'one of the most significant findings'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome (PCFS or HADS) with a power calculation, or adjusted p-values that stay below the threshold.

10.36017/jahc202461273.headline_claim: Personalized exercise reconditioning is effective in improving functional capacity, overall condition and quality of life in individuals with post-COVID pathology syndrome.
10.36017/jahc202461273.overall: The data show clear improvement in walking distance, independence and symptoms between admission and discharge in 24 patients. The paper's causal claim that the exercise programme is effective cannot be supported without a comparator, since recovery over about 41 days would be expected anyway. The pneumonia, fibrosis and quality-of-life claims are not backed by any outcome measured, and the subgroup findings are uncorrected exploratory results.

primary_outcome.name: Change in 6MWT compared to the baseline evaluation

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from an uncontrolled before-after comparison in 24 patients with no comparator
issues.explanation: All 24 patients received the programme, and every outcome is a change from admission to discharge. Patients recovering from severe COVID-19 pneumonia and ICU stays are expected to improve over weeks regardless of treatment. The data therefore show improvement during rehabilitation, not that exercise reconditioning caused it. The paper acknowledges the missing control group but still states effectiveness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A contemporaneous or historical matched comparison group without the programme showing smaller gains.

quotes.text: the lack of a control group limits our ability to compare the outcomes of
The findings of this study indicate that personalized reconditioning plan is effective in improving the functional capacity

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, retrospective admission-versus-discharge comparison in 24 patients with no comparator, yet the abstract and Conclusions state that the programme 'is effective' and describe 'efficacy'. The limitation about the missing control group is acknowledged but does not temper the efficacy wording. Natural recovery over a stay of about 53 days, regression to the mean and co-interventions (oxygen, robotic therapy, medical care) cannot be excluded. The limitation is narrowly phrased, as limiting comparison 'of the outcomes of COVID-19 pneumonia patients', rather than as limiting

issues.title: Conclusions claim improved pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis, and quality of life, none measured as outcomes
issues.explanation: The Conclusions say exercise reconditioning showed positive outcomes in improving pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis. The study did not measure these as outcomes, and it has no control group. The abstract's quality-of-life claim has no matching measure. Patients with fibrosis actually had a different 6MWT change in Table 4, which does not show fibrosis improving.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-post imaging or fibrosis-severity outcomes analysed in the study.

The findings of this study indicate that personalized reconditioning plan is effective in improving the functional capacity

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions claim improvement in pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis, and the abstract claims improved quality of life, but none of these was a defined or reported outcome. Pneumonia and fibrosis appear only as baseline descriptors and subgroup labels, and quality of life is inferred from dyspnoea and fatigue scales rather than measured. The measured improvements (6MWT, FIM, FiO2, Borg, mMRC) support at most a functional and symptom claim.

issues.title: 40 uncorrected subgroup tests; 5 nominal hits (p 0.011-0.047) interpreted as smoking and fibrosis effects
issues.explanation: The subgroup analysis has 40 tests at alpha 0.05 with no adjustment. Five are nominally significant, which is close to the number expected by chance (2). Two are borderline at p=0.047. The text interprets the smoking and fibrosis results as possible effects on recovery. These associations should be read as hypothesis-generating. Main Table 3 comparisons are far below any plausible correction threshold.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified, corrected analysis plan for subgroup comparisons.

10.36028/2308-8826-2025-13-2-8-13.overall: The paper's direction (larger improvement with IHHT added to exercise) may be real, but allocation, blinding, baseline handling and multiplicity are undescribed, so the 'high efficacy' conclusion is only tentatively supported. issues.title: Causal efficacy claim rests on a two-group comparison with unreported allocation, blinding and adjustment
issues.explanation: The paper does not state how the 40 participants were assigned to the two groups, whether assessors or patients were blinded, or whether the control group had any sham session. The between-group comparison uses post-treatment values only, with no baseline adjustment and no correction across five outcomes. Despite this, the discussion states the results 'demonstrate high efficacy' and describe physiological mechanisms the study did not measure. The direction of the improvements may be real, but the size and causal attribution are not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of randomised, concealed allocation and blinded outcome assessment, or a baseline-adjusted between-group analysis showing the same differences.

issues.title: Efficacy claimed from pooled pre-post change; no experimental vs control comparison reported
issues.explanation: Participants were allocated to experimental or control exercise, yet all outcomes are analysed as pre-post change across the whole sample of 30. Improvement over one week of any exercise, practice effects or natural recovery cannot be attributed to the physiotherapy protocol. The 'between groups' comparison in Table 2 compares left and right hands, not treatment arms.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-arm analysis showing the experimental group improved more than the control group.

quotes.text: mean score of 1 min sit to stand test is significantly less in pre-test compared to posttest by one-tailed paired t-test.
Hence showing improvement in fatigue levels experienced by the patient.

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from pooled pre-post changes in all 30 participants (one-tailed paired tests), and no experimental vs control comparison is reported even though the Methods describe two arms and a two-sample test. The 'between groups' comparison in Table 2 is right vs left hand, so the conclusion on fatigue improvement cannot be attributed to the intervention over the control exercise.

issues.title: Conclusion claims fewer complications and better quality of life; neither was measured
issues.explanation: Outcomes were 1-min STS, grip strength, fatigue and L-test after one week. No complication, daily-living or quality-of-life measure is reported, so these conclusions have no supporting data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported complication or quality-of-life outcomes in the paper.

quotes.text: helped in reducing the complications and helped the patients to carry out their activity of daily living much more efficiently and hence improved their health-related quality of life.

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion claims reduced complications, more efficient ADL performance and improved health-related quality of life, but no complication, ADL or quality-of-life outcome was measured or reported; only fatigue, sit-to-stand, L-test and grip strength were. These claims go beyond the data, and the study's short one-week follow-up and lack of a reported control comparison are not weighed against them.

issues.title: n=30 with no sample size justification, and one-tailed tests, behind confident efficacy conclusions
issues.explanation: The study enrols 30 patients, with no power calculation and no arm sizes reported. Paired tests were one-tailed, which halves p-values, and no multiplicity adjustment is made across the outcomes. The conclusion nevertheless states confident improvement.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample size calculation and arm-wise results.

quotes.text: 30  samples  will  be  selected  randomly  depending  on  the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study

issues.title: Left-hand grip change printed +0.06 but post minus pre means give -0.05
issues.explanation: Table 2 shows left-hand grip strength of 14.05 pre and 14 post, a fall of 0.05, yet the change row prints +0.06. Rounding cannot account for a 0.11 discrepancy, while the right-hand column reconciles (0.08). The error is small and the grip result is null either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing the mean paired change is +0.06, e.g. different n per time point.

issues.title: Conclusion misstates 1-min STS result ('less time' pre-test; 'did make much of a difference')
issues.explanation: The 1-minute STS counts repetitions, with 26.75 pre and 28.75 post, so subjects did not take 'less time' pre-test. The conclusion also says the intervention 'did make much of a difference', which reads as the opposite of a significant improvement (p=0.002). The wording is garbled, but the numbers in Table 1 are not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the test was scored as time and that the conclusion's wording was intended as printed.

quotes.text: subjects took  less  time  in  pretest  compared  to  post  test
mean score of 1 min sit to stand test is significantly less in pre-test compared to posttest

issues.title: Conclusion reports a grip-strength result in males; no sex-stratified analysis is shown
issues.explanation: The conclusion states no change in grip strength in males, but no analysis by sex appears in the results. The claim is unsupported, though it concerns a null secondary outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sex-stratified grip analysis in the paper.

quotes.text: there was no change in grip strength observed in males.

10.36141/svdld.v40i4.15055.headline_claim: Long-term immunosuppressive therapy (methylprednisolone with or without mycophenolate mofetil for 6 months) may be preferred as an effective and safe treatment for symptomatic post-COVID-19 ILD, improving quality of life, respiratory parameters, and radiologic findings.
10.36141/svdld.v40i4.15055.overall: The paper shows that 33 treated post-COVID ILD patients improved on several measures over six months, but with no comparator and substantial internal inconsistencies (Table 1 versus Table 3 baseline SpO2; Table 2 totalling 46 patients) the efficacy and safety conclusions are tentative at best. The claim of improved quality of life has no measurement behind it. Descriptive improvement is credible, causal attribution is not.

primary_outcome.name: No single primary outcome specified; within-group change from baseline to 6 months in mMRC, SpO2, FVC, FVC%, FEV1%, and DLCO%

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from uncontrolled before-after change in 33 treated patients, with no comparator
issues.explanation: Improvement from admission to month 6 is attributed to immunosuppression, but spontaneous post-COVID recovery, regression to the mean after selection for poor baseline values, and learning on repeat testing are not separable from treatment effect. The untreated patients were not analysed over time, so even a descriptive comparison is missing. The data support a descriptive observation of improvement, not the stated conclusion of effectiveness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparison with the untreated group or a historical control showing the improvement exceeds natural recovery.

quotes.text: We did not perform a statistical comparison between the two groups because of the small number of patients in this group.
According to the results of our data, prolonged immunosuppressive therapy should be considered in post-COVID-ILD treatment.

second_reader.what_stands: All efficacy conclusions rest on before-after changes in 33 treated patients with no analysed comparator, so natural recovery, regression to the mean and co-interventions cannot be separated from a drug effect. The authors list the lack of a comparison as a limitation, but the Discussion and abstract still use the language of demonstrated efficacy and a recommendation to consider treatment.

issues.title: Conclusion claims improved quality of life and safety; no QoL measure exists and 2 of 35 patients were excluded
issues.explanation: The abstract and conclusion state the therapy improves quality of life, but no quality-of-life instrument is described or reported. Safety is described as good tolerability, while the only non-completers (one discontinuation, one death) are removed from the analysis with no cause given and side effects are reported as unqualified percentages. Long-term steroid-related events are therefore likely underreported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A QoL questionnaire analysis, or documentation that the death and discontinuation were unrelated to treatment.

quotes.text: an effective and safe treatment option that improves the quality of life, respiratory parameters, and radiologic findings
one discontinued treatment in the fourth month and the other passed away in the fifth month
The treatment was well-tolerated by all patients, with no significant adverse effects that required discontinuation.

second_reader.what_stands: No quality-of-life measure was collected, so the claim that treatment improves quality of life is unsupported (mMRC measures dyspnea only). The statement that treatment was well tolerated with no adverse effects requiring discontinuation is made after excluding one patient who discontinued and one who died, with no reasons given, so the safety conclusion is not fully supported by the analysed data.

issues.title: Table 2 mMRC rows total 46 patients, not the 33 treated; text says 3 with full dyspnea regression, table shows 11 at mMRC 0
issues.explanation: The mMRC transition table sums to 46 patients while the treated cohort is 33. The 46 equals 33 + 13 untreated, and the mMRC 0 admission row is impossible for treated patients (Table 1 minimum is 1). The text also reports complete dyspnea regression in 3 (9%) patients, yet the table's month-6 mMRC 0 column holds 11 patients. The McNemar-type p<0.001 for mMRC therefore rests on a population that is not the one described.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected Table 2 with 33 treated patients, or an explanation that it deliberately pools treated and untreated patients.

quotes.text: whereas the mMRC level was 4 in 16 patients at baseline, it was 4 in 1 patient at month 6
dyspnea had completely regressed in three (9%) patients compared to the initial evaluation

second_reader.what_stands: Table 2 totals 46 patients, not the 33 analysed treated patients, and its 6-month mMRC 0 column shows 11 patients (10 even if the single baseline-0 patient is excluded), not the 3 stated in the text. The 46 equals treated plus untreated, which suggests the table pools both groups, but the paper does not say so.

issues.title: Admission SpO2 in treated group is 93.64±3.91 in Table 1 but 90.09±5.22 in Table 3
issues.explanation: The same 33 treated patients at admission have two different SpO2 means and SDs in two tables, while every other admission value matches. The baseline SpO2 is a headline outcome, and the size of the change to 95.88 at month 6 depends on which baseline is correct (about 5.8 versus 2.2 points). The reader cannot tell which value was analysed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the two tables use different measurement conditions or subsets for admission SpO2, or a corrected table.

issues.title: Abstract states p<0.005 but Table 3 shows p=0.006 (FVC) and 0.011 (DLCO%); no multiplicity control over ~20 tests
issues.explanation: The abstract's blanket threshold misdescribes several reported p-values. About a dozen outcomes at multiple time points plus six HRCT items were each tested at 0.05 without correction. The stronger findings (SpO2, FVC%, ground glass, reticulation) are robust, but DLCO% and FEV1-related results are fragile under any correction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or correction method, or a corrected abstract with exact p-values.

quotes.text: significant improvement in mMRC score, saturation (SpO2), FVC, FVC%, FEV%, and DLCO% values (p<0.005)
Type I error rate was taken as 0.05 in the study.

issues.title: McNemar test named for five-level ordinal mMRC and HRCT scores; actual test unclear
issues.explanation: The paper names McNemar's test for ordinal five-category scores, which it is not designed for. Whether a generalised version was used is not stated, and the ordinal information is ignored by such tests. The large observed shifts make a substantive change in conclusion unlikely.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that McNemar-Bowker or Wilcoxon signed-rank was actually used.

quotes.text: mMRC scores at the first and last measurements were compared using the McNemar test

issues.title: Some percentages (side effects 2.8%, asthma 8.6%) fit a denominator of 35, not the 33 analysed
issues.explanation: With 33 patients, 3 would be 9.1% and no count gives 2.8%. Both fit 35, the number started on therapy, suggesting some tables or sentences use a different denominator than the stated analysis set. This is an unexplained inconsistency in safety reporting, with no effect on the efficacy findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that adverse events were counted over all 35 initiated patients.

quotes.text: increased appetite (2.8%), and anemia (2.8%)

issues.title: Treatment-arm percentages wrong: 21/33 printed 66.6% (63.6%), 1/33 printed 0.4% (3.0%)
issues.explanation: The abstract and Results give the proportions on methylprednisolone alone and MMF alone that do not match the counts. The MMF-alone figure is off by a factor of about seven. Nothing in the efficacy analysis depends on these figures.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Counts different from 21/11/1 of 33 that reproduce the printed percentages.

quotes.text: Of 33 cases, 21 (66.6%) were treated with methylprednisolone, 11 (33%) with methylprednisolone + MMF, and 1 (0.4%) with MMF alone.

script.explanation: 21/33 = 63.64%, but the paper prints 66.6, outside the rounding interval [66.55, 66.70]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 31.5 rather than 33.

10.36422/23076348-2021-9-3-82-88.headline_claim: Medical rehabilitation after COVID-19 is effective, as shown by improved lung function, reduced dyspnoea and better quality of life.
10.36422/23076348-2021-9-3-82-88.overall: The data show that lung-function, dyspnoea and quality-of-life scores improved over about 8 days in 30 patients, but the design cannot attribute this to rehabilitation, so the 'effectiveness' conclusion is not supported as worded. There is also a minor numeric inconsistency (FVC gain 6.4 in text versus 4 in Table 2) and no multiplicity control, but these do not change the direction of the findings.

primary_outcome.name: Pre- vs post-rehabilitation change in spirometry and DLCO (primary endpoint not explicitly named)

issues.title: Effectiveness concluded from uncontrolled pre-post change in 30 patients retested after about 8 days
issues.explanation: All 30 patients had the same multi-component programme and were compared only with their own earlier results, about 8 days apart, early after discharge when natural recovery is expected. The Conclusion nonetheless says the improvements 'indicate the effectiveness' of rehabilitation. The authors acknowledge the small, descriptive study, but the headline claim is worded causally and without hedging. The data show improvement over time, not that rehabilitation caused it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent comparison group, or reworded conclusions stating only that function improved during rehabilitation.

quotes.text: Выполнено обсервационное описательное исследование.
свидетельствуют об эффективности медицинской реабилитации пациентов после COVID-19
Мы осознаем, что наше исследование ограничено небольшим объемом выборки и является описательным.

second_reader.what_stands: The effectiveness conclusion rests only on an uncontrolled before/after comparison in 30 patients retested a median of 8 days later (QR 6-12), so natural recovery, regression to the mean and learning effects on the tests cannot be separated from any rehabilitation effect. The authors do admit the small sample, the descriptive design and the lack of a comparison group in the Discussion, but the Conclusion and abstract still state that the improvement 'свидетельствует об эффективности' of rehabilitation without carrying that caveat. Statistically significant paired changes show improvement over

issues.title: Text gives FVC gain of 6.4 %pred but Table 2 means differ by 4 points (88 to 92)
issues.explanation: The abstract and Results state a mean FVC increase of 6.4 %pred (270 ml). Table 2 gives FVC means of 88 before and 92 after rehabilitation, a 4-point difference. The other parameters match the table within about 1 point, so this one figure is inconsistent. One reported result is unreliable, but the direction of change and its significance are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 6.4 figure is a median of individual changes, or a corrected Table 2 with FVC means about 6.4 points apart.

quotes.text: The average increase in SVC, FVC, FEV 1 , DLCO and VA was 4.5% (150 ml), 6,4% (270 ml)
ФЖЕЛ , % долж .88±2392±22

issues.title: No multiplicity control across about 15 outcomes; FEV1/VC (p=0.02) would not survive Bonferroni
issues.explanation: Many outcomes were each tested at p<0.05 with no correction or prespecified primary outcome. The headline results, mainly FVC, FEV1, DLCO, dyspnoea and EQ-VAS, have p<0.001 and are robust to this. The marginal ones the abstract also lists as significant, such as FEV1/VC at p=0.02, are not. The effect on the conclusion is small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A declared primary outcome or a multiplicity correction under which the highlighted results remain significant.

quotes.text: Различия считались статистически значимыми при р<0,05.

issues.title: Conclusion generalises to all post-COVID patients from 30 referred, more severe, mostly male patients
issues.explanation: The authors state that patients sent to rehabilitation were mainly those with more severe disease and comorbidity. The conclusion nonetheless covers 'patients after COVID-19' in general. The sample was a single military hospital, 90% male, and selected by referral, which limits generalisation. This is secondary to the design problem in c2.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Wording limited to the studied referred hospital population, or evidence from a broader sample.

quotes.text: на МР были направлены в первую очередь пациенты с более тяжелым течением COVID-19
свидетельствуют об эффективности медицинской реабилитации пациентов после COVID-19

10.36425/rehab608182.headline_claim: The authors conclude that ReOxy controlled hypoxia-hyperoxia therapy is a justified component of rehabilitation for patients with multimorbidity, citing a clear subjective benefit on the VAS and a significant reduction in CRP, while the HIF-1a change was not significant.
10.36425/rehab608182.overall: The paper shows a CRP and VAS difference between 27 treated and 15 placebo patients, but the primary HIF-1 result was null and the report does not match the registered primary outcome (back-pain VAS). Registration came after the study started, and the conclusion of an 'obvious' effect and general justification is stronger than this small trial supports. The CRP finding is the most credible result and should be read as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Serum HIF-1a and C-reactive protein, baseline vs end of 2-week course

primary_outcomes.measure: Back pain intensity will be measured by the Visual Analog Scale

issues.title: Conclusion claims an 'obvious' effect and general justification from 42 patients, null primary and secondary VAS
issues.explanation: The primary HIF-1 result was not significant. The conclusion rests on a patient-reported secondary VAS and on CRP, calling the effect obvious. It then states the method is justified for multimorbid patients with varied baseline characteristics. The evidence is one small single-centre trial (27 vs 15, no sample-size calculation, 2 weeks of follow-up). It supports a tentative signal on CRP and VAS, not a general justification.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified power calculation and a significant, change-based between-group primary result in a larger sample.

quotes.text: очевидный положительный эффект курсового применения интервальной гипокси-гиперокситерапии
объективно выявленное снижение уровня классического острофазового показателя
Ограничения работы связаны с небольшим размером выборки пациентов.

second_reader.what_stands: The primary HIF-1 result is null, and the conclusion calls the effect 'obvious' and the method 'justified' for multimorbid patients in general. That rests on n=27 versus n=15 patients who all had osteoarthritis and post-COVID syndrome, with no confidence intervals, exact p-values or named between-group test. The limitations section mentions the small sample, but the conclusion does not carry that caution through. It is not true that the VAS was null: Table 2 marks it significant within the group and against the control group. The control-group VAS ratio is also reported inconsistently (1.3 ver

issues.title: Registered primary outcome (back-pain VAS) is not reported; paper's primary is serum HIF-1 and CRP
issues.explanation: The registry lists back-pain intensity on a VAS as the only primary outcome. The paper names HIF-1 and CRP as its primary outcome and reports only a general-health VAS as additional. The back-pain VAS never appears. The registry also lists 90 actual participants against the 42 analysed, which adds to the doubt about how closely the report follows the registered plan. Readers cannot tell which outcomes were prespecified.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A dated registry history showing the primary outcome was changed to HIF-1/CRP before enrolment, or a report of the back-pain VAS elsewhere.

quotes.text: Основной исход исследования.
динамика общего состояния здоровья также оценивалась

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does define its primary outcome as serum HIF-1 and CRP, and its only VAS is a general-health VAS, not back pain. Whether the registered primary outcome was back-pain VAS cannot be established from the paper, so a registry mismatch is not confirmed. The paper also does not say which of HIF-1 and CRP is the single primary outcome.

issues.title: HIF-1 result called 'stabilisation' (Abstract) though it rose 17% non-significantly, with no between-group test
issues.explanation: The Abstract describes the CRP fall as occurring with 'stabilisation' of HIF-1. The Results give a 17% rise in the treatment group (52.62 to 61.38 pg/ml), which is not significant, and the text says the rise was 'evidently more pronounced' than in controls. No test of the between-group difference in change is given. The wording presents a null primary result favourably.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified definition of 'stabilisation' and a between-group test of HIF-1 change showing no difference.

quotes.text: стабилизации динамики HIF-1
выявленные различия не являются статистически значимыми
умеренному увеличению уровня HIF-1a в сыворотке крови

issues.title: Registry lists 90 actual participants; paper reports only 42 randomised, with no explanation
issues.explanation: The registry record gives actual enrolment of 90. The paper includes and analyses 42 patients and says recruitment was difficult. The paper does not say whether a larger target was set or why enrolment stopped at 42.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Registry history showing 90 was a planned figure later corrected, or a statement of the planned and achieved sample.

quotes.text: включено 42 пациента
Недостаточное количество участников исследования обусловлено сложностью набора пациентов

issues.title: Labelled 'prospective' but registered 2021-08-26, after the stated April/June 2021 start
issues.explanation: The title and abstract call the trial prospective and cite NCT05053672. The paper says the study ran from April 2021. The registry gives a start of 1 June 2021 and first submission on 26 August 2021, marked retrospective. The outcomes were therefore not fixed before recruitment, which fits the outcome mismatch with the registry.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry record or protocol dated before the first enrolment.

quotes.text: одноцентровое рандомизированное плацебоконтролируемое проспективное исследование
Длительность исследования составила 1 год (с апреля 2021 по май 2022 года).

issues.title: Corresponding author uses the device maker's e-mail domain while no competing interests are declared
issues.explanation: The corresponding author is affiliated with AsFor Group and writes from an aimediq.com address. The ReOxy device is made by Ai Mediq SA. The paper declares no competing interests and does not explain the relationship. A possible link between an author and the maker of the tested device should be stated explicitly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the author has no employment, financial or other interest in Ai Mediq or the ReOxy device.

quotes.text: g.spirina@aimediq.com
AsFor Group, Moscow, Russia
The authors declare that they have no competing interests.

issues.title: Control-group VAS improvement given as 1.3-fold in Results but 1.4-fold in Discussion; Table 2 gives 1.33
issues.explanation: The Results say the control-group general-health VAS fell 1.3-fold. The Discussion says 1.4-fold for the same quantity. Table 2 means (59.08 to 44.3) give 1.33, so the Discussion value is wrong and slightly narrows the apparent gap to the 2-fold treatment change. The error is minor and does not alter any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Unrounded control-group VAS data giving a ratio of at least 1.35.

quotes.text: В группе сравнения значения показателей общего состояния здоровья по шкале ВАШ снизились в 1,3 раза
тогда как в группе сравнения - только в 1,4 раза

script.explanation: Control-group VAS baseline/end ratio printed as 1.4 in Discussion: 59.08 / 44.3 gives 1.33363, not the printed 1.4. For the printed value to hold the denominator would have to be 42.2, not 44.3.

issues.title: Study period starts April 2021 but ethics approval is dated 11.05.2021
issues.explanation: The Methods date the study from April 2021, while the approval protocol is dated 11 May 2021. If April refers to enrolment, procedures preceded approval. The registry start of June 2021 suggests April may be preparatory, so this cannot be settled from the paper alone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that first enrolment occurred after 11 May 2021.

quotes.text: протокол № 4 от 11.05.2021
Длительность исследования составила 1 год (с апреля 2021 по май 2022 года).

issues.title: Three outcomes and several correlations tested at nominal p<0.05 with no multiplicity statement
issues.explanation: HIF-1, CRP and VAS are each compared within and between groups, plus several Spearman correlations, all at nominal p<0.05 with no correction mentioned. The CRP difference is large enough to survive. The VAS difference is closer to the margin. Between-group tests are on end values, not on change from baseline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified hierarchy of outcomes, or adjusted p-values that stay below 0.05.

quotes.text: Результаты считались статистически достоверными при р <0,05.

10.36425/rehab688680.headline_claim: Adding personalised normobaric interval hypoxic-hyperoxic therapy (NBIGGT) to a base day-hospital rehabilitation programme improves hypoxia tolerance, pulmonary function and six-minute walk performance after moderate COVID-19 pneumonia, and is safe.
10.36425/rehab688680.overall: The headline conclusion that the add-on significantly improves hypoxia tolerance, lung function and exercise tolerance is only partly supported. Between-group tests after treatment are significant only for breath-hold tests; spirometry p-values are 0.85-0.98 and 6MWT is 0.051. The study is unblinded, has no sham control, no registration or sample-size calculation, and the text and Table 2 disagree on every within-group spirometry p-value.

primary_outcome.name: not specified as primary; the paper reports several co-equal outcomes (Stange and Genchi tests, spirometry indices, 6-minute walk test)

issues.title: Superiority claimed from within-group significance; end-of-treatment between-group p are 0.85-0.98 (spirometry), 0.051 (6MWT)
issues.explanation: The Conclusion and Abstract say the add-on 'statistically significantly' improves hypoxia tolerance, pulmonary function and exercise tolerance. The between-arm comparisons after treatment are not significant for any spirometry index (p 0.850-0.978) or for the 6-minute walk (p 0.051). The claim rests on within-group p-values and on the main arm having smaller p-values than the comparison arm, which is not a test of difference. Only breath-hold tests (Stange 0.044, Genchi <0.001) show a between-arm difference. The recommendation for rehabilitation programmes also goes beyond a 10-day, unblinded, 2-week study with no follow-up.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group analysis (for example ANCOVA on change scores) showing significant differences for spirometry and 6MWT.

quotes.text: статистически значимо улучшает переносимость гипоксии, функцию внешнего дыхания и толерантность к физической нагрузке

second_reader.what_stands: For spirometry and 6MWT, the abstract and conclusion claim a statistically significant improvement and the Discussion calls the main group's improvement 'statistically more significant'. The between-group end-of-treatment p-values are 0.85-0.98 for spirometry and 0.051 for the 6MWT, so superiority is supported only by within-group changes or by comparing significance levels across groups. The claim of better hypoxia tolerance is supported by between-group p of 0.044 (Stange) and <0.001 (Genchi).

issues.title: Within-group spirometry p-values in text disagree with Table 2 in all 8 comparisons (e.g. FEV1 0.241 vs 0.042)
issues.explanation: The text and Table 2 give different within-group p-values for every spirometry index in both groups. Some differences change significance: the comparison group's FVC is significant in the text (0.049) but not in the table (0.070), VC is p<0.001 in the text but 0.073 in the table, and FEV1 is 0.241 in the text but 0.042 in the table. The text says only VC and FVC improved in the comparison group, while the table suggests FEV1 and not VC or FVC. The p1/p2 footnote labels also do not match the table layout. The spirometry significance pattern cannot be relied on and needs re-analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the text p-values are adjusted and the table p-values are raw (or the reverse), with the adjustment method.

second_reader.what_stands: All 8 within-group spirometry p-values in the Results text differ from the within-group values in Table 2. Some differences change the significance call: comparison-group FEV1 is 0.241 (not significant) in the text but 0.042 (significant) in the table, and comparison-group VC is <0.001 in the text but 0.073 in the table. The p1/p2 labels in the table are also inconsistent with its footnote.

issues.title: No sham control and no blinding reported; effort-dependent outcomes (breath-hold, 6MWT) assessed in open design
issues.explanation: The comparison group received basic rehabilitation only, with no sham gas procedure. The Limitations section admits there is no placebo group. Blinding of patients and assessors is not mentioned, and the endpoints (breath-holding times, 6-minute walk distance) depend on effort and encouragement. Differences between arms cannot be separated from non-specific effects of the extra daily session and attention, so a causal claim for the therapy itself is weakly supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that outcome assessors were blinded and that a sham procedure was delivered.

quotes.text: в исследовании не выделена группа плацебо
Толерантность к физической нагрузке измеряли с помощью теста шестиминутной ходьбы (ТШХ).

second_reader.what_stands: The paper has no sham or placebo control and reports no blinding of participants or outcome assessors. Effort-dependent outcomes (breath-hold times, spirometry, 6MWT) were therefore probably measured unblinded. The authors acknowledge the missing placebo group as a limitation but do not weigh this in the efficacy conclusion, and the open design is inferred from the lack of any blinding statement.

issues.title: Study period starts January 2023 but ethics approval is dated 24 April 2023 (amendment 26 May 2023)
issues.explanation: The Methods say the study ran from January to December 2023, but the ethics extract approving the protocol is dated 24 April 2023, and an amendment is dated 26 May 2023. If patients were enrolled from January, some may have been studied before approval. The paper does not give actual enrolment dates, so the point is unresolved rather than shown to be a breach. The '1 1' in the protocol number is a text-extraction artefact.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Enrolment dates showing the first patient was recruited after 24 April 2023.

quotes.text: Исследование проводилось в период с января по декабрь 2023 года.
extract from Protocol No. 1 1 dated 04/24/2023

issues.title: No trial registration, primary outcome, or sample-size calculation reported for a 'prospective randomised' study
issues.explanation: The paper calls itself a prospective randomised trial but gives no registry identifier, no designated primary outcome and no sample-size calculation. With about ten outcomes tested and no primary endpoint, selective emphasis on favourable results cannot be excluded. This limits confidence in the conclusion but does not itself show a bias.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment naming the primary outcome.

quotes.text: Проведено  сравнительное  проспективное  рандомизированное клиническое исследование

issues.title: Baseline spirometry implausibly high (VC 129%, FVC 142% predicted) and Tiffeneau SD 28 contradicts 'all >80%'
issues.explanation: Mean baseline VC is 129% and FVC 142% of predicted, rising to about 146-151% after rehabilitation, in patients said to have post-COVID pulmonary impairment. The Tiffeneau index has mean 99.1 with SD 28.2 in the comparison group, which is incompatible with the statement that all patients exceeded 80%. These figures suggest a data or reference-value problem, and the reported 'improvement' in lung function may reflect values already above normal at baseline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level spirometry showing all Tiffeneau values above 80% and a stated reference equation explaining the high percent-predicted values.

quotes.text: Значение индекса Тиффно выше 80% у всех пациентов

issues.title: Sequence generation not described and no group-wise baseline demographics, only 'homogeneous' groups
issues.explanation: The paper says patients were allocated by opaque sealed envelopes but does not state how the sequence was generated. It gives only overall age and sex rather than by arm. The measured baselines in Tables 1-3 are similar, so there is no visible imbalance, but allocation integrity cannot be fully checked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Description of the sequence generation and a per-arm baseline table.

quotes.text: Методом непрозрачных запечатанных конвертов исследуемые были распределены на две однородные группы.

issues.title: Hyperoxic oxygen fraction stated as 30-40% in one place and 20-30% in another
issues.explanation: The device is described as producing hyperoxic mixtures of 30-40% oxygen. The procedure description then says the apparatus raises oxygen to a 'hyperoxic concentration (20-30%)'. Air is about 21% oxygen, so the lower range is not hyperoxic. The delivered dose of the intervention is therefore unclear, though no result depends on the discrepancy.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A clarification that 20-30% is a rise above the preceding hypoxic level and not an absolute fraction.

quotes.text: от 30 до 40% (гипероксические)
до гипероксической концентрации (20-30%)

issues.title: Limitations say baseline hypoxia and exercise tolerance were not determined; Tables 1 and 3 report baselines
issues.explanation: The Limitations section says baseline hypoxia and exercise tolerance indices were not determined, but Table 1 and Table 3 give baseline values for both groups. This is probably a loosely worded sentence and does not alter the data. It does make the Limitations section unreliable as a guide to what was measured.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Author clarification of what was not determined, for example baseline testing in the comparison group with the ReOxy test.

quotes.text: первоначальные показатели, характеризующие переносимость гипоксии и физических нагрузок
Изначально показатели устойчивости к гипоксии

10.36425/rehab90576.headline_claim: Adding hyperbaric oxygenation (HBO) to a three-week outpatient rehabilitation programme after COVID-19 pneumonia further reduces dyspnoea, improves exercise tolerance and speeds resolution of lung changes, and may be recommended for routine practice.
10.36425/rehab90576.overall: The headline claim that sequential HBO after rehabilitation is effective and suitable for routine use rests on a non-randomised comparison in which the HBO group was selected for persistent symptoms and had much greater baseline lung involvement, with no adjustment. Several reported figures (mMRS values, CT changes, CT coverage) are internally inconsistent, and the DLCO support comes from 14 versus 14 patients without any test. The conclusion can be treated only as hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: No primary outcome designated; dyspnoea (mMRS), diffusing capacity (DLCO) and CT lung involvement are reported

issues.title: HBO group chosen for persistent symptoms and larger CT involvement (54.4% vs 35.9%); no adjustment
issues.explanation: Patients with persistent symptoms after rehabilitation were referred for HBO; the comparison group was those not referred. Baseline CT involvement differed markedly (54.4% vs 35.9%) and no adjustment, matching or randomisation was used. Regression to the mean, differences in natural recovery and the extra time and attention all can explain changes, yet the conclusion states HBO is effective.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomised allocation or an adjusted analysis showing the same effect.

quotes.text: Проведение баротерапии на этапе реабилитации у этих пациентов эффективно

second_reader.what_stands: HBO patients were selected for persistent symptoms and had markedly larger baseline CT involvement (54.4% vs 35.9%), and the paper reports only unadjusted comparisons (t-tests, chi-square) while concluding that HBO is effective. The imbalance is disclosed in the text but not addressed analytically or in the conclusion's wording; the possibility of regression to the mean or selection effects is not discussed.

issues.title: Dyspnoea benefit of HBO supported by within-group change; no between-group mMRS test reported
issues.explanation: The mMRS result for HBO ('fell by half again, p<0.001') is a pre-post test within the HBO group, while the comparison group is described only as improving 'to a lesser degree' with no numbers or test. A between-group test of mMRS change is not shown in the text. Since the HBO group started sicker and the comparison group also improved, the dyspnoea claim is not established.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 3 reporting a significant between-group test for mMRS change.

quotes.text: У больных группы сравнения одышка также стала менее выраженной, но в меньшей степени.

second_reader.what_stands: In the text, the dyspnoea benefit of HBO rests on within-group change (p<0.001 for the HBO group's further decline) and a qualitative statement that the comparison group improved 'to a lesser degree'; no between-group mMRS test or comparison-group numbers appear in the prose. Whether Table 3 reports such a test cannot be verified because its content is not available in the extracted text.

issues.title: Post-rehabilitation mean mMRS given as 1.92 (from 2.67) and as 2.35 (from 2.7); baseline also differs
issues.explanation: The text says the mean dyspnoea index fell 1.4-fold from 2.67 to 1.92 after the rehabilitation course, and later says it fell 13% to 2.35 after the same course. Baseline is printed as 2.67 in one place and 2.7 in another. These cannot both describe the same timepoint in the same population, so the size of the dyspnoea benefit of rehabilitation alone is unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Table 3 showing 1.92 as an all-patient value at a later timepoint (after HBO/1 month) and 2.35 as post-rehabilitation.

quotes.text: уменьшился в 1,4 раза (с 2,67 до 1,92 балла)
он снизился на 13% - 2,35 балла

issues.title: Text says all patients had one-month CT; Table 4 shows none for the 58 comparison patients
issues.explanation: The text says half of patients had a control CT after rehabilitation, then that all patients had a control CT one month after the course. Table 4 lists the 58-patient comparison group's CT at that time as not performed, and gives no 1-month value for the total. Only the 2-month CT exists for everyone, so the sentence is inaccurate and the analysed sets are unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 'all patients' refers to the 2-month scan.

quotes.text: всем пациентам была выполнена контрольная КТ легких
Не выполнялась

issues.title: CT reductions in text (15.2%, 11.9%) disagree with Table 4 means (13.4, 16.6 points)
issues.explanation: Within the HBO group, Table 4 gives 54.4, 41.0 and 24.4 at baseline, 1 month and 2 months. These imply reductions of 13.4 and 16.6 points, but the text gives 15.2% and 11.9%. For the same patients, paired differences should equal differences of means, so the reported CT change attributed to rehabilitation versus HBO is inconsistent. The two reductions even swap in order of magnitude.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Different patient subsets or relative (percentage) reductions explained in the paper.

issues.title: DLCO effect (+16.2% vs -0.76%) from 14 vs 14 selected patients, no variance or between-group test
issues.explanation: DLCO was measured in only 28 of 98 patients, 14 per arm, with no SDs, no p-value and no between-group test. It is used as the mechanistic support for the HBO conclusion. The percentages also do not match Table 5 simply: 84 to 97.6 is +13.6 points (16.2% relative) and 78.8 to 78.2 is -0.6 points (-0.76% relative).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test with adequate precision.

quotes.text: (14 получили лечение в барокамере и 14 из группы сравнения)
наблюдалось небольшое снижение ДСЛ (на 0,76%)

10.36740/abal202201102.headline_claim: Adding high-frequency laser therapy to a comprehensive exercise-based rehabilitation program gives better pain reduction and knee function than exercise alone in athletes with chronic patellar tendinopathy.
10.36740/abal202201102.overall: These are several small, mostly uncontrolled or non-randomised studies. Most of the printed numbers are self-consistent, but several tables and text passages disagree (Post-COVID Table 4, Smiianov Tables 1-2 and Results, knee pain scores), and the stated chi-square p labels in the H2S study are partly wrong. The headline efficacy conclusions are therefore tentative at best: they rest on uncontrolled before/after comparisons or on non-random, confounded groups, and in the AMP study the conclusions go beyond a finding of no difference from controls.

primary_outcome.name: Pain intensity on Visual Analog Scale (VAS); VISA-P functional score reported alongside

issues.title: Post-COVID study: non-randomised groups, controls who refused treatment, no statistical methods, strong superiority claim
issues.explanation: Test group 1 received four neuroprotective drugs, Test group 2 a rehabilitation programme, and the Control group is made of patients who 'refused' both. No allocation rule, no randomisation, no statistical test and no blinding are described, yet the paper reports p<0.01 'verified' effects and compares groups. The Conclusions state that neuroprotection reduces severity and sick-leave duration, and that rehabilitation alone is less effective. Self-selected controls and unspecified tests cannot support that comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomised or concealed allocation procedure, a stated analysis plan with the tests used, and adjusted between-group comparisons.

quotes.text: who refused to perform rehabilitation program and receive neuroprotection
The patients receiving neuroprotection formed Test group 1.
It was also shown that administration the comprehensive rehabilitation program alone tends to have an overall lesser effect than neuroprotection.

second_reader.what_stands: The groups are not randomised and the allocation method is not described. The Control group consists of patients who declined both interventions, so group differences may reflect patient characteristics rather than treatment. No statistical methods are stated, and the ± values are not defined. The Conclusion claims neuroprotection significantly reduces severity and has a greater effect than rehabilitation alone. The word 'tends' softens only one sentence; the Results and Summary state 'verified (p<0,01)' superiority.

issues.title: AMP analyzer study: no difference from controls (p>0.05), yet changes attributed to COVID and analyzer deemed useful
issues.explanation: The Results say the indicators were abnormal in post-COVID patients but not significantly different from controls (p>0.05); control medians are almost identical in Table 1. The authors still say the values 'are a consequence of the disease'. The paper never compares the analyzer with laboratory or clinical reference measures, yet the Conclusions say it can determine the direction of rehabilitation. Neither a disease effect nor the analyzer's validity is shown by these data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A validation study of the analyzer against reference measurements, and data showing patients differ from matched controls.

quotes.text: compared with the control group, was not found a statistically significant difference between the above indicators (p>0.05)
In our opinion, such values are a consequence of the disease and are the basis for describing the main long-term consequences that correspond to the post-covid syndrome.
allows determining the direction of rehabilitation treatment taking into account concomitant chronic diseases

second_reader.what_stands: By the authors' own comparison the COVID group does not differ from controls on the listed indicators, yet the paper attributes the out-of-norm values to the disease and to post-COVID syndrome. The analyzer is also said to guide rehabilitation, although no validation against reference measures or treatment outcome is reported. The conclusions go beyond what the data show.

issues.title: Confident laser superiority claim from 11 per arm, unblinded, no sham, no sample-size calculation
issues.explanation: Twenty-two men were split into two groups of 11 with no power calculation, and the control group received no sham laser. The outcomes are self-reported pain and function, which are open to expectation effects when participants know they received laser. The Conclusions say the laser programme 'shows better results', without presenting it as preliminary.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sham-controlled or blinded-assessor design with an a priori sample-size calculation, or conclusions labelled as pilot.

quotes.text: The study involved 22 people, all men aged 20 to 35 years.
shows better results for reducing pain and improving the functioning of the knee joint than without it

second_reader.what_stands: The study has 11 per arm and no stated blinding, no sham or placebo laser, and no sample-size calculation. The conclusion states superiority without noting these limitations. The claim of no randomisation does not hold, since randomisation is stated. The effect sizes in the printed means and SDs are large, so the direction of the finding is plausible. Its size and certainty are unverified, because a between-group post-treatment test is not clearly reported and the groups differ in more than laser alone only if the exercise programmes differed.

issues.title: Knee study concludes the procedure 'eliminated pain', but every patient still reports pain (scores 1-8)
issues.explanation: The Summary and Conclusions state that arthroplasty or the procedure eliminated pain. Table 2's After row shows all 20 patients with a pain score of at least 1, 15 of them at 3 or higher, and one at 8. The study is also a single-arm before/after survey with pre-surgery status recalled by patients operated 1 to more than 5 years earlier. It cannot separate the effect of surgery from rehabilitation, which the title and aim are actually about.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing most patients at zero pain after the 3-week programme, or a rewording to 'reduced pain'.

quotes.text: The procedure helped increase mobility, improved the quality of life and eliminated pain in the patients.
The answers were as follows: 40% described their pain as 4, 30% as 2, 15% as 5 (Figure 8).

second_reader.what_stands: Conclusion 3 (and the Summary) say the procedure 'eliminated pain', but every patient reports some pain after surgery. About 30% score 1, and one patient scores 8. The mean falls from about 7.9 to about 3.0, so pain was reduced, not eliminated. The text and Table 2 also disagree by one point on the score labels.

issues.title: H2S baths: outpatient vs sanatorium comparison, non-random; Table 1 age and DM-duration gaps recompute to p<0.01
issues.explanation: The control group got standard outpatient treatment and the bath group went to a sanatorium and also had baths, so rest, diet, daily care and the bath effect are mixed. No allocation method is given. The paper calls the groups comparable, but the Table 1 means and SDs imply clear baseline gaps in age and diabetes duration, printed as p>0.05. The overall DPN duration in the Methods (5.55) lies outside both group means in Table 1 (4.91 and 5.19), so the table or the text is wrong.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A randomised or documented allocation, a sanatorium-only control group, or a corrected Table 1 showing no baseline imbalance.

quotes.text: in addition to standard treatment received hydrogen sulfide baths in a sanatorium
The groups were comparable in age, duration of diabetes and the severity of clinical manifestations of DPN (Table 1).
(average duration 5.55 ± 2.94 years)

second_reader.what_stands: The comparison is non-random: outpatients on standard care against a sanatorium group that received baths plus a sanatorium stay, with other sanatorium elements as confounders. The claim of comparability is not supported. Recomputed from Table 1, the age gap (t≈3.0, p≈0.003) and DM-duration gap (t≈2.6, p≈0.009) are both below 0.01, not above 0.05.
