The overall DPN duration of 5.55 years cannot be correct given the group means.

issues.title: Mineral water study: no control group, unpaired tests on 8 outcomes, causal claim of improved liver function
issues.explanation: One hundred patients' records were compared before and after a 14-day spa stay with no comparison group, and diet, rest and the sanatorium programme were applied alongside the water. Eight outcomes were tested with no multiplicity control, and the three 'significant' results are borderline (ALT and cholesterol p≈0.05) when recomputed. Only the thymol test comfortably survives correction. The Conclusions nevertheless say the hydrotherapy leads to improved liver function.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A matched control group without mineral water, paired analysis, and multiplicity-adjusted p-values.

quotes.text: leads to improved liver function of patients after laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Mathematical statistics revealed a significant (p <0,05) improvement in such indicators as: thymol test, alanine transpeptidase activity, total cholesterol.
we cannot be sure that the patients did not consume prohibited foods in commercial food outlets in the city of Morshyn during their rehabilitation

second_reader.what_stands: The study has no control group, so natural recovery, diet, rest and time since surgery (1 month to 1 year) cannot be separated from the water. Eight outcomes were tested without correction. Two of three 'significant' results (ALT, cholesterol) are at p≈0.045-0.047, and only thymol survives a Bonferroni threshold. The Conclusion states a causal improvement in liver function, which the design does not support. The authors themselves note they cannot be sure of dietary compliance.

issues.title: ASS results paragraph disagrees with Table 4 in values, direction and counts for all three groups
issues.explanation: The paragraph on asthenia severity gives percentages and directions that do not match Table 4. It describes weak asthenia as falling in Test groups 1 and 2, while the table shows mild cases rising (25%→65% and 20%→54.6%). It says Test group 2 had no reduction in moderate cases, while the table shows 33.2%→22.7%. It calls a rise in the Control group's moderate cases a 'decrease' and says one control patient still had extreme asthenia, but 16.6% of 12 is two patients. The main severity result is therefore stated inconsistently.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected text or erratum showing the paragraph numbers were taken from a different table, with Table 4 verified against the raw data.

quotes.text: a decrease in weak asthenic syndrome cases (from 40% to 34.6%)
decrease in moderate asthenic syndrome cases (from 33.3% to 41.7%)

second_reader.what_stands: For Test groups 1 and 2 the ASS paragraph's figures and directions do not match Table 4. Weak/mild cases rise in the table but are described as falling, and the moderate and weak percentages quoted in the text are not in the table. For the Control group the quoted values match Table 4, but the moderate change is called a decrease when it is an increase. The claim about 'counts' is not accurate, since both the text and Table 4 give percentages.

issues.title: Post-surgery pain scores in the text (4, 2, 5) do not match Table 2 (3, 1, 4, 5)
issues.explanation: The Results say 40% rated pain 4, 30% rated it 2 and 15% rated it 5. Table 2's After row puts 40% at score 3, 30% at score 1, 15% at score 4 and 10% at score 5, and has no score-2 column. The two sources cannot both be right, so the reader cannot tell which pain distribution is correct. The overall fall in pain is visible either way.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Figure 8 or the raw data showing that the text scores are correct and the Table 2 column headers are mislabelled.

quotes.text: The answers were as follows: 40% described their pain as 4, 30% as 2, 15% as 5 (Figure 8).

issues.title: Remote-service study: two different value sets for target BP and DM compensation within Results and abstract
issues.explanation: One Results paragraph gives target blood pressure rising 21.88%→46.35% and satisfactory DM compensation 45.83%→67.71%. The abstract, Table 3 and the Conclusions give 38.54%→63.54% and 11.45%→40.63% for the same indicators. The earlier DM change (+21.88) differs from the abstract's (+29.18) by 7.3 points, and 46.35% is not attainable from 96 respondents. Readers cannot tell which figures are correct, although the abstract and Table 3 agree with each other.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors showing the first paragraph's figures refer to different, defined variables, with the raw survey counts.

quotes.text: Also, the part of respondents with the target level of AP has increased by 24.47%.
quotes.location: Results, para on blood pressure targets

quotes.text: There was an increase by 21.88% in the share of respondents, who have a satisfactory level of DM compensation.
quotes.location: Results, para on glycaemia and blood pressure

issues.title: Laser study period June-September 2021 but manuscript received 22 June 2021 with 2-month results
issues.explanation: The Methods say the study ran from June to September 2021 with a two-month programme. The article is stamped received on 22 June 2021 and reports end-of-programme results. If received is the original submission date, the reported outcomes did not yet exist. A revision explains the sequence, but the paper gives no way to confirm the real study dates.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Journal records showing the manuscript was substantially revised, with results added, after 22 June 2021.

quotes.text: The study was conducted from June to September 2021.

issues.title: Difference columns in Tables 1-2 do not equal 2019 minus 2018 (4 rows, e.g. -15.10 vs -7.81)
issues.explanation: Four rows of the difference columns disagree with the percentages beside them. Table 1 'Every day' prints +8.33 where 20.83 minus 8.33 is +12.50. Table 2 prints -10.94, -15.10 and -9.37 for rows whose printed values give -9.90, -7.81 and -12.50. The Table 2 2018 column also sums to 94.8%, so some input values are wrong as well. This affects secondary descriptive results, not the headline BP/glycaemia targets.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw survey counts showing the printed differences are right and the 2018 column values are the ones that are mis-transcribed, with all columns reconciled.

issues.title: Laser benefit rests on within-group tests; the between-group test is unstated and its table marker unexplained
issues.explanation: The Results report that pain fell significantly in both groups and then compare the post-treatment means (2.0 vs 3.5). They never name a between-group test or its p-value for pain or VISA-P, and the symbol beside the main-group values in Tables 3 and 4 is not defined. The printed means and SDs suggest the end-of-treatment difference is large, so the conclusion is probably directionally right but not shown as claimed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A defined between-group test of change (e.g. t-test or ANCOVA on change scores) with its p-values for VAS and VISA-P.

quotes.text: At the end of the intervention, a significant reduction in pain was observed in both groups (p≤0.05).
The average scores on the VAS scale were reduced to 2.0 points in the main group and to 3.5 in the control one.

issues.title: Hydrogen sulfide study: chi-square 19.508 labelled p>0.05; 3.98 and 3.85 (p≈0.05) also labelled p>0.05
issues.explanation: Within group 2, chi-square 20.01 is p<0.05 but the vibration value 19.508 is labelled p>0.05. For a 2x2 comparison a value this size has p well below 0.001, and the Discussion itself claims reliable recovery of all sensitivity types in group 2. In group 1, 3.98 and 3.85 exceed the df=1 critical value of 3.84 yet are labelled p>0.05, which feeds the claim that only pain was reliably restored in group 1. The labelling errors run in both directions and bear on the between-group conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors stating a different test and df for 19.508 that yields p>0.05 from the printed counts.

quotes.text: xi-square = 19.508 p>0.05
quotes.location: Results, group 2 vibration sensitivity after treatment
Results, group 2 temperature sensitivity after treatment

quotes.text: The best clinical effect of treatment (reliable recovery of all types of sensitivity) was achieved in patients of group 2

script.explanation: Reported χ² = 19.508 matches the uncorrected Pearson value (19.5079); the Yates-corrected value would be 17.8485. The paper prints p > 0.05, but recomputed from every convention tried on this table (Pearson, Yates, Fisher, McNemar, likelihood ratio, Fisher-Freeman-Halton where they apply) p is at most 0.0001781, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show, and on the other side of alpha = 0.05 (a decision error). This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Ethics commission confirmation dated 11 Nov 2021, five months after the 21 June 2021 receipt date
issues.explanation: The Methods say compliance with the Helsinki principles was confirmed by the Bioethics Commission on 11 November 2021. The manuscript is marked received on 21 June 2021 and accepted on 20 December 2021. The confirmation therefore came after submission and probably after patient assessment, which suggests retrospective review. A revision-stage addition would explain the order, so it is a point to query rather than an established defect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Documentation of an earlier ethics approval before data collection, with the November date being a later confirmation or re-registration.

quotes.text: as was confirmed on the meeting of Bioethics Commission of I.Horbachevsky Ternopil National Medical University of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine of November 11, 2021

issues.title: Group 2 baseline percentages: 39/64 printed as 68.5% (should be 60.9%); 33/64 printed as 54.09%
issues.explanation: The baseline sensitivity sentence prints percentages for group 2 that do not match its n=64. The correct figures are 60.9% for 39 patients and 51.56% for 33 patients, and the 54.09% matches group 1's denominator of 61. These are small slips in a baseline description, but they sit in the sentence used to argue the groups were comparable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A group-2 denominator other than 64 that reproduces both percentages.

quotes.text: in 39 (68.5%) and 56 (87.5%) patients of the 2 nd group
whereas a decrease in pain sensitivity occurred in 32 (52.45%) patients and 33 (54.09%) patients

script.explanation: 39/64 = 60.94%, but the paper prints 68.5, outside the rounding interval [68.45, 68.60]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 56.9 rather than 64.

issues.title: Total rows of Tables 3 and 5 use n=20 as the base: 'no' printed as 125%, 4 of 40 as 20%
issues.explanation: Table 5's Total row prints 75% and 125% for 15 and 25 of 40 responses, so the row sums to 200%. The percentages were computed against 20 patients, not the 40 pooled responses in the row. Table 3's Total row repeats the pattern (4 of 40 shown as 20%). Nothing in the conclusions rests on these cells, so the damage is cosmetic.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that Total-row percentages are deliberately expressed per 20 patients; even then a value of 125% would still be wrong.

issues.title: Conclusions extend from 22 male athletes (2-month follow-up) to patients with patellar tendinopathy
issues.explanation: All participants were men aged 20-35 who trained intensively in sport, with two months of follow-up. The abstract and Conclusions recommend laser as an important adjunct for patients with patellar tendinopathy generally. Women, older or non-athletic patients and longer follow-up are not covered.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Conclusions restricted to young male athletes, or data in a broader population.

quotes.text: We believe that highfrequency laser therapy can be used as an important adjunct to various types of therapeutic exercises in the comprehensive rehabilitation of patients with patellar tendinopathy.

issues.title: Randomised comparison without any trial registration or protocol reference
issues.explanation: The study describes random allocation to two arms but gives no registry identifier or protocol. The primary outcome is therefore not stated in advance, and VAS and VISA-P are both reported as outcomes. Without registration, selective outcome reporting cannot be ruled out.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry dated before enrolment listing the same outcomes.

quotes.text: The study was conducted from June to September 2021.

issues.title: Plasma density called 'overestimated' in both groups, but Table 1 medians are below or within the normal range
issues.explanation: The Results list plasma density among indicators overestimated in both groups. Table 1 shows a patient median of 1046.705 g/l, below the range 1048-1055, and a control median of 1048.775, inside it. Other listed indicators are above their ranges, so this item looks like a labelling slip. It does not alter the paper's central statements.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Individual-level data showing most patients and controls above 1055 g/l.

quotes.text: Both in the experimental group and in the control group were overestimated: pulmonary ventilation, heart rate, and CO2 content in venous blood, plasma density

issues.title: Baseline 'no significant differences' reported with p<0.05 (threshold reversed)
issues.explanation: The Results state there were no significant baseline differences between the groups and attach p<0.05, which literally says the opposite. The Figure 1 note defines an asterisk as a significant baseline difference at p<0.05. This is a printed slip that most readers would interpret as p>0.05.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: None needed beyond a corrected sign; this is a typographical issue.

quotes.text: There were no significant differences between groups before treatment (p<0.05)
the difference between the groups before treatment is significant (p<0.05)

10.36740/wlek202105110.headline_claim: A four-week comprehensive rehabilitation program (physical exercise plus brain activity stimulators) significantly reduces asthenic syndrome severity and disability duration in post-COVID-19 patients and effectively prevents long-term asthenia.
10.36740/wlek202105110.overall: The headline claim that early rehabilitation prevents long-term asthenia and shortens convalescence is not supported: allocation was by patient choice, follow-up was about four weeks, outcomes were self-reported, and no between-group test of change is reported, while the control arm also improved. Several table-text inconsistencies (baseline percentages not matching n=22, a control 'decrease' that is an increase) further reduce reliability. The data can at most suggest a possible benefit in a small, self-selected sample.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly defined; WAM well-being/activity/mood and ASS/MFI-20 asthenia scores reported

checklist.control: non-randomised concurrent control (patients who refused the programme)

issues.title: Causal 'prevents long-term asthenia' claim from a 4-week, non-randomised, open-label study
issues.explanation: The conclusions state that early rehabilitation effectively prevents long-term asthenia, but follow-up was only about four weeks, while the paper defines chronic asthenia as lasting over 6 months. Allocation was by patient choice and there is no valid between-group test. The causal and preventive claims are not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Randomised or adjusted comparative data with follow-up beyond 6 months.

quotes.text: An early rehabilitation intervention after  the  termination of the acute phase in COVID-19 effectively  prevents  the  development of long-term side effects in the form of asthenic syndrome

second_reader.what_stands: The causal claim that rehabilitation 'prevents' long-term asthenia is not supported by a 4-week, non-randomised, open-label study with self-selected arms and no long-term follow-up. All patients were already symptomatic at baseline, so prevention of onset could not be assessed, and the control arm also improved. At most the data suggest short-term symptom-score improvement, with the between-group comparison untested.

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from within-group changes; control also improved and no between-group test of change
issues.explanation: Significance is reported separately for each arm against its own baseline. The control arm also showed starred improvements on WAM and ASS, and no test compares changes between arms. Concluding that the programme works therefore rests on a difference in significance rather than a direct comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group analysis of change (e.g., ANCOVA) showing a significant advantage of the programme.

quotes.text: none significantly different among the groups
No verifiable difference

second_reader.what_stands: The paper infers efficacy from within-group significance (asterisks versus none) and the control arm also improved, notably on WAM well-being and mood. No between-group test of change is reported, apart from an unexplained statement about the ASS shifts. The two quoted passages themselves concern baseline comparability, so they do not by themselves show the problem; the problem lies in the rest of the Results.

issues.title: Non-random allocation by patient choice; control arm is self-selected refusers
issues.explanation: Test group 2 declined exercise and the control group refused the programme, so arm membership reflects patient choice. Baseline differences such as age (test group 2 mean age 69) and motivation can confound outcomes. Group comparisons cannot be attributed to the intervention.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of a randomised or matched allocation, or adjusted comparisons with baseline balance.

quotes.text: The test group 2 consisted of 6 patients who declined physical exercises and thus were engaged only brain activity stimulators.
who refused perform rehabilitation program

second_reader.what_stands: The paper states that test group 2 declined physical exercise and that the control group refused the rehabilitation program, so allocation was by patient choice and the comparator arms are self-selected refusers. No randomisation or adjustment for baseline differences (e.g. age, which the Discussion gives as 69±5.74 for group 2) is described.

issues.title: Open-label design with self-reported outcomes (WAM, MFI-20, ASS)
issues.explanation: Every outcome is a self-assessment questionnaire completed by patients who knew whether they were exercising. Expectation effects could inflate improvement in the treated arms. This weakens, but does not by itself invalidate, the findings given the other design flaws.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence of blinded outcome assessment or objective outcome measures.

quotes.text: The  patients  were  offered  to  mark  the  degree  of severity of a particular characteristic of their condition.

issues.title: Control moderate asthenia 'decrease' from 33.3% to 41.7% is an increase; also called verified (p<0.01)
issues.explanation: The text describes a decrease in moderate asthenia in the control group, but the printed figures rise from 33.3% to 41.7%. The same sentence labels the change as verified at p<0.01, while the discussion says the control group's changes were unverifiable. The control-group narrative is therefore unreliable, which matters because the control comparison is used to argue the program works.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table showing the control moderate share falling.

quotes.text: decrease in moderate asthenic syndrome cases (from 33.3% to 41.7%)

issues.title: Stated sample of 28 patients excludes the 12 controls; 22+6+12 = 40 analysed
issues.explanation: The methods report 28 patients examined, but Table headers show three groups totalling 40. Demographics and COVID severity are given only for the 28, so the control group's age (32 to 74) and severity are not comparable with the test groups. This leaves baseline comparability of the control arm undocumented.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the 28 excluded the controls with controls' characteristics reported.

quotes.text: We examined 28 post-COVID-19 patients (18 female and 10 male)
The control group embraced 12 post-COVID-19 patients

issues.title: Test group 1 baseline severity shares 46.8%, 33.2%, 20% are not whole-patient shares of n=22
issues.explanation: No integer count out of 22 gives 46.8%, 33.2% or 20.0%, though the week-4 shares in the same group (22.7%, 54.6%) fit n=22 exactly. The baseline distribution on which the 'improvement' is measured therefore cannot be reconstructed from whole patients. This casts doubt on the baseline-to-week-4 comparison for the main group.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Per-patient data showing counts consistent with these percentages (e.g., a different denominator).

quotes.text: Test group 1 (n=22)

issues.title: Very small, unequal arms (22, 6, 12) with no sample-size justification, yet efficacy 'proved'
issues.explanation: Arms of 6 and 12 patients with no power calculation give very imprecise estimates, and no confidence intervals or effect sizes are reported. The paper nonetheless says the research 'proved' the programme's efficacy. The size issue is mainly a limit on how firm the conclusion can be.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation supporting these arm sizes.

quotes.text: The original representative results obtained in the present study indicate the efficacy of the low cost comprehensive rehabilitation program

issues.title: Same mean and SD (57.32 ±1.21) for WAM Mood and ASS Weak level, test group 1 week 4
issues.explanation: Table II (WAM mood) and Table IV (ASS weak-level score) give an identical mean and SD for test group 1 after treatment. These are different instruments on different scales, so exact agreement of both values is improbable. It cannot be determined from the paper which cell is correct, and no main conclusion depends on this single value.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data showing the two instruments genuinely produced the same summary values.

quotes.location: Table IV, Weak row, Test group 1, time 2

issues.title: No trial registration or ethics approval/consent reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes an intervention study but reports no registry entry, protocol, ethics approval or informed consent, only a statement of Helsinki compliance. Outcome selection therefore cannot be checked against a prespecified plan. This has limited bearing on the numerical results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry number or ethics committee approval for the study.

quotes.text: All methods applied during the study complied with requirements of the Helsinki Declaration of the World Medical Association.

issues.title: Text calls MFI-20 activity change insignificant, but Low activity carries significance asterisks in both test groups
issues.explanation: Table III marks the Low activity change as verified in both test groups, while the text says the activity increase was insignificant. This may stem from confusion over scale direction, but the text and table disagree on significance. The effect is on a secondary MFI-20 subscale.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors clarifying that the text refers to a different measure than the starred row.

quotes.text: an insignificant activity increase in test groups 1 and 2

10.37506/brrffb35.headline_claim: Deep breathing techniques have a high impact in improving respiratory rate and Post COVID-19 Functional Status Scale scores among post COVID-19 patients, and are more effective than stacking breathing techniques.
10.37506/brrffb35.overall: The headline claim that deep breathing is better for respiratory rate and PCFS is poorly supported. The respiratory rate rose in both arms, and more with deep breathing, which contradicts the paper's own definition of improvement. The PCFS results favour deep breathing in direction, but they come from small, non-randomized, unblinded groups analysed with an unspecified test and with internal inconsistencies in the text and dose.

primary_outcome.name: Respiratory rate (breaths per minute); PCFS also named as primary

issues.title: RR rose in both arms (13.00→15.47; 13.10→17.17) yet deep breathing is said to improve RR
issues.explanation: The paper defines a fall in respiratory rate as improvement. Respiratory rate went up in both groups, and by more with deep breathing (+4.07) than with stacking (+2.47). The text calls the higher post-test value 'better results' and concludes that deep breathing improves respiratory rate, which the printed data contradict.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement in the paper that a higher RR was the intended or favourable direction, or evidence that the post-test means were mislabelled and actually fell from baseline.

quotes.text: indicate improved respiratory efficiency and reduced energy expenditure associated with breathing
Post intervention, Respiratory rate of the participants those who received deep breathing for 4 weeks Mean (17.1700)
deep breathing techniques have a high impact in improving Respiratory rate

second_reader.what_stands: Respiratory rate rose in both arms (by 2.47 and 4.07 breaths/min), and the Introduction defines improvement as a reduction, so the Results and Conclusion that call deep breathing's higher RR an improvement contradict the paper's own stated direction. The paper offers no rationale for treating an increase as beneficial.

issues.title: 'More effective' / 'high impact' conclusion rests on an unnamed test, non-randomized arms and no inert comparator
issues.explanation: Both arms receive an active breathing programme with no untreated arm, so within-arm pre/post changes (each p < 0.0001) cannot show an effect of either technique. The between-group claim relies on post-test means and an unspecified test, with no effect size, CI, sample size justification or adjustment for baseline. The conclusion of a 'high impact' on RR is also contradicted by the RR data (see c1), and no limitations are discussed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A named between-group analysis (e.g. ANCOVA) with effect sizes and CIs from randomized, blinded arms, plus a no-treatment or usual-care comparator.

quotes.text: This study also shows that deep breathing exercises are more effective than stacking breathing techniques among post covid 19 patients.
This study finally concluded that deep breathing techniques have a high impact in improving Respiratory rate
Group B is the control group (n=30) and they will be given deep breathing exercises

second_reader.what_stands: The 'more effective' and 'high impact' conclusions rest on an unnamed test, non-randomized convenience allocation and a comparator (deep breathing) that is itself an active intervention, with no inert or usual-care arm and no stated limitations. The reported p<0.0001 is arithmetically plausible for the post-test RR difference, but it does not establish causal superiority, and on RR the higher value in deep breathing runs against the paper's own definition of improvement.

issues.title: Group B post-test PCFS given as Group A's 1.40 (SD 0.77) in one sentence, 0.83 (SD 0.75) in another
issues.explanation: The sentence reporting Group B's pre/post PCFS gives a post-test mean of 1.40 (SD 0.77) and labels it Group A stacking. These are Group A's figures. The later between-group sentence gives Group B's post-test as 0.83 (SD 0.75). The within-group result for Group B is therefore misreported, and the reader cannot tell from the text which value the graphs and test used.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data or the graph for Group B showing a post-test PCFS of 1.40, which would make the 0.83 the erroneous value.

quotes.text: (PCFS) for Group A Stacking breathing technique
quotes.location: Results, Group B pre/post PCFS sentence

quotes.text: the standard deviation (0.75) showed better result

issues.title: Intervention dose stated as 3 sessions/week and also as twice daily (about 6 vs 14 sessions/week)
issues.explanation: The procedure first says each group received 3 sessions per week for 4 weeks, then says both groups did their exercises two times per day. These describe very different exposures, so the actual dose delivered, and whether the two arms were comparable in dose, cannot be established. Adherence is not reported either.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol statement distinguishing supervised from home sessions and reporting the dose each arm actually received.

quotes.text: during 3 sessions per week
stacking breathing exercise for weeks two times per days

issues.title: Convenience sampling, allocation method not described; no baseline table beyond pre-test outcome means
issues.explanation: Participants were enrolled by convenience sampling and 'divided' into two groups of 30, with no description of how allocation was done or concealed, and no blinding. Groups may therefore differ in ways other than the intervention. The similar pre-test outcome means are reassuring for those two measures only, since age, sex, BMI and time since COVID-19 are not tabulated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement of a concealed random sequence, or a baseline table showing balanced demographics and clinical features.

quotes.text: The enrolled subjects were divided into Groups A (n = 30) and B (n = 30)
This is an Experimental study done using convenient sampling technique

issues.title: No trial registry identifier reported; only an institutional ethics number is given
issues.explanation: The only identifier is an institutional ethics number. A prospective interventional trial would normally be registered so that its prespecified outcomes can be verified. Whether registration was required or done cannot be settled from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry (e.g. CTRI) with a date before enrolment and matching outcomes.

quotes.text: ISRB number-03/060/2022/ISRB/SR/SCPT

10.37506/ijpot.v16i2.18051.headline_claim: Telerehabilitation (breathing and therapeutic exercise at home) is a viable and safe option for post-COVID-19 patients, with the experimental group recovering more rapidly than the conventional-care control group.
10.37506/ijpot.v16i2.18051.overall: The headline claim that telerehabilitation produced faster recovery than conventional care is not supported by the data printed: only within-group p-values for the experimental arm appear, with no control-arm results, no between-group comparison, no group sizes and no baseline data. Safety, daily-living and sex-difference statements go beyond anything measured. The study is at best a very small pilot, and its conclusions are tentative at most.

primary_outcome.name: Modified Borg Dyspnoea Scale (MBDS) and VAS for fatigue (VAS-F); no single primary outcome named

issues.title: Superiority claim rests on within-arm pre/post p-values; no between-group test result reported
issues.explanation: The methods say the change in the two groups was compared by t-test, but the Results/Discussion report only pre vs post p-values within the experimental group (p=0.0056/0.0112 for Borg, p=0.018/0.036 for VAS-F). No between-group estimate, p-value or control-arm result is printed. Significant within-arm change does not show that the programme beat conventional care, yet the paper concludes the experimental group recovered more rapidly.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A table or text giving the between-group comparison of change scores (means, SDs, n, p) showing a significant difference favouring the experimental arm.

quotes.text: statistically significant  difference  in  between  PR (MBDS)  and  PO  (MBDS)  i.e.,  (p=0.005605  &  p= 0.01121)
experimental  group  showed  prompt  recovery  in comparison  of  controlled  group
The change (pre to post) in outcome measures of two groups were compared by t-test.

second_reader.what_stands: The superiority claim ('experimental group showed prompt recovery in comparison of controlled group') is supported only by p-values that the paper labels as pre vs post within the experimental group, while the control group is also said to have improved significantly. No between-group test result, effect estimate or confidence interval is reported, even though the Methods say a between-group comparison of change was done.

issues.title: Randomization method, concealment, baseline data and flow not reported for the 30-person trial
issues.explanation: The study is called randomized, but there is no sequence generation, concealment, baseline table, group sizes or participant flow. Without group sizes or baseline comparability, the claim of randomization cannot be assessed and the arm comparison is hard to trust.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description of computer-generated sequence with concealed allocation, plus a baseline table showing comparable arms.

quotes.text: Study Design : Randomized controlled trials (RCTs)

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls itself an RCT but reports no randomization method, allocation concealment, arm sizes, baseline characteristics or participant flow for its 30 participants. A reader cannot judge whether the groups were comparable or whether any participants were lost.

issues.title: Safety and daily-living independence claims have no supporting data (n=30, 6 weeks, no ADL outcome)
issues.explanation: Only dyspnoea and fatigue were measured, yet the Discussion asserts independence in daily living activities and no complications, and the Conclusion mentions improved pulmonary function and physical function, which were never measured. Safety rests on one sentence with no description of how adverse events were monitored, in 30 people. The conclusion therefore goes beyond the outcomes collected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported measures of pulmonary and daily-living function and a described adverse-event monitoring process.

quotes.text: demonstrated independence in their daily living activities without any further complications
significant improvement  in  pulmonary  function  and  physical functions
No  adverse  events  occurred  to patients receiving telerehabilitation.

second_reader.what_stands: The claims of independence in daily living, improved pulmonary and physical function, and no adverse events have no supporting data in the paper, since only dyspnoea (Borg) and fatigue (VAS-F) were measured and no adverse-event methods or counts are given. The safety statement is an unsupported assertion from a small, short trial, though the Conclusion hedges it somewhat with 'may be a safe way'.

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 30 participants alongside confident conclusions
issues.explanation: Thirty participants total, with no stated power calculation, are used to claim the null hypothesis is rejected and that telerehabilitation is safe. Small samples limit precision and cannot exclude uncommon harms. The consequences are mainly captured in the overstated-conclusions issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation showing adequate power for the primary outcome.

quotes.text: Sample size : 30 subjects
The  results  of  this  study  proved  the  alternate hypothesisand rejectsthe null hypothesis.

issues.title: Usual-care control with subjective outcomes; claimed patient blinding is implausible and unexplained
issues.explanation: The control arm received undefined conventional care while the experimental arm received a 4-day-per-week exercise protocol. Outcomes are self-reported (Borg, VAS-F). The paper claims patients did not know their group, but does not explain how this was achieved, so subjective outcomes may reflect attention and expectation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of the conventional care and a credible blinding procedure, or results for an objective outcome.

quotes.text: The Controlled Group had been put on Conventional Care and Experimental Group  was  provided  with  a  Therapeutic  Treatment Protocol, 4 days a week for next 6 weeks.
also they didn't  know  if  they  belong  to  the  experimental  or controlled group.

issues.title: Sex-difference conclusion stated with no sex-stratified data or interaction test
issues.explanation: The Discussion says females were more fatigued and benefited more, but no sex-specific results, group counts by sex or interaction test are presented. In a 30-person trial any subgroup comparison would be very imprecise. The claim is unsupported by the paper's reported results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sex-by-treatment interaction analysis with data supporting the statement.

quotes.text: The study also concluded that females were more fatigued than males and got benefitted more with the therapeutic program.

10.37506/pkxqyr14.headline_claim: Diaphragmatic strength training was more effective than thoracic mobility plus diaphragmatic breathing in improving functional status (PCFS) and dyspnoea in post-COVID subjects.
10.37506/pkxqyr14.overall: The headline claim that strength training is more effective than conventional exercise is weakly supported: the analysis is described as within-group, no between-arm test of change is clearly reported, and the intervention dose is described inconsistently (4, 5 or 8 weeks; 2 or 3 sets). Allocation, blinding and sample size are poorly reported, so only the modest conclusion that both groups improved is reasonably reliable.

primary_outcome.name: PCFS (Post-COVID Functional Status scale) and dyspnoea scale (MRC)

issues.title: Superiority over conventional care claimed without a clearly reported between-group test of change
issues.explanation: The analysis is described as paired t-tests within the experimental group, and the Results give one t value per outcome for 'group A' vs 'group B' means without saying what they are (arms, or pre vs post). The Conclusion admits only 'somewhat more improvement' yet states the strength-training arm was more effective. A within-group improvement, or an unlabelled comparison, cannot establish superiority over an active comparator that also improved.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported independent-samples comparison of change scores between arms, with adjustment for baseline, showing a significant difference.

quotes.text: were  analysed  using  paired  t-tests  within the study population for  MRC  dyspnoea  scale, PCFS scale
Hereby we conclude that  Diaphragmatic  strength  training exercise  was more effective than the conventional group.
Somewhat more  improvement  in  strength  training  group

second_reader.what_stands: The paper does report a between-group comparison (group means with t and p values for PCFS and dyspnoea), so it is not true that no between-group test appears. But the test is not clearly specified: it is not stated whether it compares post-test values or change from baseline, whether it is paired or unpaired, or whether baseline differences were accounted for, and the Discussion describes only within-group paired t-tests. The claim of superiority over conventional care therefore rests on a between-group test whose basis for change is not clearly reported, and the Conclusion's wording ('somewh

issues.title: Intervention duration given as 4, 5 and 8 weeks in different sections; sets (2 vs 3) and days (4 vs 5) also conflict
issues.explanation: The strength-training protocol is described as 4 weeks (Exercise 1, Treatment Protocol), 5 weeks (Discussion) and 8 weeks (Exercise 2). The same section also gives 3 sets in Exercise 2 but 2 sets in the Treatment Protocol, and 4 days per week versus 5 days per week. The dose actually delivered cannot be determined, so the study cannot be replicated and the comparison with the conventional arm (4 weeks, 2 sets, 5 days) is unclear.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol stating that Exercise 1 and Exercise 2 were separate phases with the stated durations, sets and frequencies, or a corrected single description.

quotes.text: Frequency-5days per week for a period of 4 weeks
The trial lasted 5 weeks, and workouts were given 5 days each week.
the training was given four days a week, for eight weeks.

issues.title: Randomisation by closed envelopes with no sequence generation or concealment detail; convenience sampling
issues.explanation: The paper says participants were randomly assigned using the closed-envelope method but does not describe how the sequence was generated, whether envelopes were opaque and sequentially numbered, or who allocated. Without this, selection bias cannot be excluded. Baseline characteristics are also not reported, so balance cannot be judged.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods description of sequence generation and concealed allocation, plus a baseline table showing balance.

quotes.text: Convenient sampling Technique using closedenvelope method.
Using the closed-envelope method, participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups.

issues.title: No blinding reported for subjective ordinal outcomes (PCFS 0-4, MRC dyspnoea 0-4)
issues.explanation: Both outcomes are coarse ordinal scales dependent on self-report or rater judgement, and the paper never states whether participants or outcome assessors were blinded. With a modest between-arm difference claimed, expectancy and assessment bias could contribute. Participant blinding is hard in exercise trials, so the main concern is assessor blinding, which is unreported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that outcome assessors were blinded to allocation.

quotes.text: A  respondent  chooses  a  whole  number  (0-4 integers) on the PCFS that best describes the functional activity
is measured using the MRC Dyspnea scale.

issues.title: No sample-size justification for 15 per arm while stating superiority
issues.explanation: The study enrolled 30 participants (15 per arm) with no power calculation, and no trial registration is reported. Small samples give imprecise estimates and no confidence intervals are provided, yet the Conclusion states superiority outright. The overreach is mostly captured by the between-group testing issue.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified sample-size calculation supporting 15 per arm for the stated effect.

quotes.text: The  study  was  conducted  on  30  subjects. Both the group has 15 subjects each.

issues.title: Ethics approval stated without committee name, approval number or date
issues.explanation: The paper says only that a generic 'institutional scientific review board' approved the study and gives no reference or date. Written informed consent is reported. This limits verifiability but does not affect the results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An approval number and date preceding July 2022.

quotes.text: The  study  was  approved  by the committee of institutional scientific review board.

10.38025/2078-1962-2022-21-3-45-57.headline_claim: The paper investigates the effectiveness and safety of a rehabilitation program with aquatic training for patients with Long Covid, but the excerpt provided contains only the title page, so the authors' stated conclusion is not available.
10.38025/2078-1962-2022-21-3-45-57.overall: The supplied text contains only the title page, author list and affiliations. It has no abstract, methods, results or tables, so no claim can be checked and no issue can be defended. The screen raised no candidates and none are added.

10.38025/2078-1962-2023-22-2-136-145.headline_claim: A combined rehabilitation programme using virtual reality, robotic mechanotherapy with biofeedback and interactive balance therapy can be recommended for post-COVID syndrome, improving cardiorespiratory endurance, diastolic blood pressure at peak load and dyspnoea.
10.38025/2078-1962-2023-22-2-136-145.overall: The improvement in cardiorespiratory indices and the shift toward milder dyspnoea in the main group is supported only as an exploratory finding. The trial is unregistered, has no stated primary outcome or sample size, is unblinded, and the main group appears to receive additional therapy on top of the basic programme. The claim about hypoxic syndrome has no data behind it, and the 'no dyspnoea' result favours control. There are also minor inconsistencies (pneumonia rate, patent and ethics dates).

primary_outcome.name: Maximum work performed (MET) and VT1 oxygen consumption on CPET; dyspnoea (MRS) reported alongside (no single primary designated)

issues.title: No trial registration, primary outcome, sample-size calculation or blinding for a recommendation-level claim
issues.explanation: The study is called a prospective randomised trial, but no registry entry is given, only a state research-topic number. No primary outcome or sample-size calculation is stated, and neither allocation concealment nor blinding is described. Eight CPET indices and five MRS categories were tested at an uncorrected 0.05 critical level, which makes isolated p-values such as 0.016, 0.017 and 0.037 hard to interpret. The results are best seen as exploratory.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry record or protocol dated before enrolment that names the primary outcome, sample size and blinding of outcome assessors.

quotes.text: в рамках приоритетной темы НИР № НИОКРТР 121121600137-9
были распределены методом простой рандомизации на 2 группы

second_reader.what_stands: Confirmed from the paper's text: no clinical trial registry identifier is given (only a state R&D topic number), no single primary outcome is designated, no sample-size calculation is reported, and blinding is not mentioned, yet the conclusion says the programme 'can be recommended'. What I could not verify is whether the trial was registered elsewhere, since no registry record was supplied, so the registration element is limited to what the paper itself reports; blinding of participants would in any case have been impractical, though blinded outcome assessment is not described.

issues.title: Patent application (11.08.2022) said to use study results predates ethics approval (28.11.2022)
issues.explanation: The conflict-of-interest statement says the patent, applied for on 11.08.2022 and granted on 28.10.2022, used the study results. Enrolment and follow-up dates are not given, so the reader cannot tell.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Stated enrolment dates after 28.11.2022, or a statement that the patent used earlier separate data.

quotes.text: заявка № 2022121831 от 11.08.2022), при разработке которого использованы результаты исследования

issues.title: Dyspnoea superiority rests on per-category tests and within-arm contrasts; 'no dyspnoea' favours control (33.3% vs 26.7%)
issues.explanation: The text contrasts a significant change in the main arm with a non-significant change in the control arm, which does not show a difference between arms. Between-group testing was done only on the post-treatment distributions, category by category, five tests at uncorrected alpha 0.05. The no-dyspnoea proportion is higher in the control group after treatment, and the control group also improved significantly on that category. This is not a benefit of the new complex, but it is listed in the abstract and conclusion as one. The shift towards milder dyspnoea is supported, but a superiority claim on dyspnoea is weaker than stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An ordinal between-group test (for example Mann-Whitney or proportional odds) on MRS change or final scores showing a significant advantage for the main group.

issues.title: Unpaired Pearson chi-square used for pre/post MRS dyspnoea in the same patients
issues.explanation: Table 3 compares baseline and repeat dyspnoea distributions in the same 60 patients per arm with Pearson chi-square, which assumes independent samples. A paired or ordinal test (McNemar, Wilcoxon signed-rank) is needed. The error most likely understates significance, but the reported within-group p-values cannot be taken at face value. The between-group test on the post-treatment distribution is not affected by pairing.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the pre/post MRS comparison used a paired test.

issues.title: Conclusion recommends the programme to reduce 'hypoxic syndrome', which was not measured
issues.explanation: The aim and the conclusion name hypoxic syndrome as a target and as an outcome. The Methods list clinical examination, history, cardiopulmonary exercise testing and the MRS dyspnoea scale, with no oxygen saturation, blood gas or other hypoxia measure. This part of the recommendation has no data behind it. Findings on dyspnoea and exercise capacity are not affected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Reported oxygenation data (SpO2 at rest or on exertion) before and after rehabilitation.

issues.title: Main arm appears to receive the basic programme plus the new complex; the control arm only the basic one
issues.explanation: The Methods say the new complex was prescribed 'на фоне базового лечения', and that control received basic treatment 'идентичное таковому в основной группе'. If correct, the main group had about 7 modalities against 4 for the control group, with more sessions and staff contact, and the trial was not blinded. The better CPET and dyspnoea results then cannot be attributed to the VR and robotic technologies specifically. The abstract's description of the arms is inconsistent with this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the new complex replaced the basic programme with matched session numbers.

issues.title: Main-group pneumonia: text 21.7% (p = 0.657) vs Table 1 11/60 = 18.3% (p = 1.0)

issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction or source data showing the main group count is 11 (or 13) and which p-value applies.

issues.title: Inclusion requires post-COVID manifestations, yet 6/60 main and 4/60 control are listed 'asymptomatic'
issues.explanation: The Methods say the sample consisted of patients with post-COVID manifestations. Table 1 lists 10 of 120 patients as asymptomatic. The category is undefined, so it is unclear whether these patients met the stated inclusion condition. The effect on the efficacy conclusions is probably small.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition of 'asymptomatic' in Table 1 (for example, no listed symptom beyond dyspnoea or reduced exercise tolerance) that is compatible with the inclusion criterion.

10.38025/2078-1962-2023-22-4-96-104.headline_claim: A combined programme of audiovisual stimulation (ECG/EEG-based resonance-acoustic device) and cognitive-behavioural psychotherapy, added to standard rehabilitation, reduces emotional disturbance (anxiety, depression, situational and personal anxiety, subjective comfort) in patients with post-COVID disorders and helps 'effectively relieve emotional tension and change inadequate behaviour'.
10.38025/2078-1962-2023-22-4-96-104.overall: The central claim that the combined programme beats standard rehabilitation on emotional outcomes is only tentatively supported. It rests on unblinded self-report, an unspecified randomisation, an attention-unmatched control, and within-group significance reasoning. Several printed statistics are also inconsistent: Table 4 p-values, non-integer 'medians', and the conclusion's percentages. The behavioural-change wording goes beyond anything measured.

primary_outcome.name: Not explicitly designated; HADS anxiety and depression, Spielberger-Khanin situational/personal anxiety and subjective-comfort index are all reported as outcomes

issues.title: Superiority inferred from which arm was significant versus baseline; prose contradicts Table 1 for Group II
issues.explanation: Many claims rest on Group I being significant against its own baseline while Group II was not, or was less so. A difference in significance between arms is not a test of difference between arms. The text also says anxiety fell significantly in both groups (p<0.05), then that significant decreases occurred only in Group I; Table 1 marks Group II anxiety with an asterisk. Before/after chi-square tests on the same patients also break the independence assumption. Between-group post-treatment tests exist, but with no adjustment for baseline or for the many outcomes tested, the advantage of the combined programme is only tentatively supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-group comparison of change scores, adjusted for baseline and multiplicity, showing a clear advantage for Group I.

quotes.text: значимое снижение значений медиан по шкалам тревоги и депрессии наблюдалось только в I группе

quotes.location: Table 1, Group II HADS anxiety, after

second_reader.what_stands: The prose statement that significant decreases in anxiety and depression occurred 'only in Group I' contradicts Table 1 for anxiety, where Group II is flagged * (p<0.05) and the preceding sentence says both groups fell; it holds for depression, and for anxiety only at the p<0.001 level. Inference of Group I's superiority also partly rests on significant-versus-nonsignificant within-arm changes, though direct between-arm Mann-Whitney tests are reported and are significant for anxiety, Spielberger scales and comfort, but not for depression.

issues.title: Table 4 Group II statistics (chi2 = 5.6 and 6.0) printed with p = 1.0
issues.explanation: For Group II in Table 4 the paper prints p = 1.0 beside chi2 = 5.6 (before/after) and chi2 = 6.0 (between groups before). For a 3-category table these statistics correspond to p of about 0.06 and 0.05, so p = 1.0 cannot be right. The printed counts (0/7/23 before vs 0/10/20 after) imply a much smaller chi2, so the statistics themselves look unreliable. The 'no significant change in Group II' reading is still plausible, but the table's inferential figures cannot be trusted as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Corrected table showing the printed p-values correspond to the statistics.

quotes.location: Table 4, middle level row, Group II p
Table 4, middle level row, between-group p before

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 1.0, but recomputed from the printed chi2 = 5.6 p is at most 0.06235, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show. This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Table 1 'medians' of integer HADS scores printed as 8,9, 4,3, 7,8, 7,2, 5,2, 4,8
issues.explanation: Table 1 is labelled as medians [Q1; Q3], but several HADS cells carry values like 8,9 and 4,3. HADS subscale scores are integers, so a true median would be a whole number or a half. These values look like means, which makes the statistic label or the Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney basis unclear. The size of the real effect is hard to read from this table.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Statement that the HADS subscales were scored non-integrally or that the values are means.

quotes.location: Table 1, HADS anxiety, Group I before
Table 1, HADS anxiety, Group I after

issues.title: Conclusion's 79.4 % and 48.3 % are rises in middle-level counts, not the Table 3 high-level reductions (72.4 %, 58.6 %)
issues.explanation: Conclusion 2 says situational and personal anxiety fell in 79.4 % and 48.3 % of patients. In Table 3, Group I's high-level counts fall by 21 and 17 of 29 (72.4 % and 58.6 %). The quoted figures instead match the increase in middle-level counts (23/29 and 14/29), and 79.4 does not match 23/29 = 79.3. The headline percentages are therefore not the proportion of patients whose anxiety was reduced.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A definition in the paper of the conclusion's percentages as the proportion moving into the middle level, with 79.4 reconciled to 23/29.

quotes.text: ситуативную и личностную тревожность у 79,4 и 48,3 % пациентов соответственно

issues.title: Patent application (10.08.2022) citing study results predates ethics approval (28.11.2022)
issues.explanation: The disclosure says a patent application filed 10.08.2022 used the study results. The ethics committee approval is dated 28.11.2022, later than both the application and the patent grant on 11.11.2022. Either some data were collected and analysed before approval, or the dates have another explanation the paper does not give. This casts doubt on the 'prospective' label and on the approval sequence.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Statement that the patent used earlier pilot data, or that recruitment and treatment began after 28.11.2022.

issues.title: Randomisation method and allocation concealment not described; no registration or sample-size calculation
issues.explanation: The paper states patients were randomised but gives no sequence generation, concealment, registration or sample-size justification. Baseline balance looks good, so there is no direct sign of imbalance. Allocation quality still cannot be verified, which weakens confidence in the between-group comparisons.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Protocol or registry entry describing sequence generation and concealment.

quotes.text: Все пациенты рандомизированы на две группы.

issues.title: Self-rated outcomes, no blinding or attention/sham control against a different standard programme
issues.explanation: All outcomes are patient-rated questionnaires, and the intervention arm receives extra audiovisual sessions and psychotherapy that the control arm does not. Expectation and attention effects could therefore contribute to the larger improvements. The paper does not report blinding or any mitigation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Statement that outcome assessment was blinded, or an active attention-matched control.

issues.title: Conclusion claims effective change of 'inadequate behaviour', which no outcome measured
issues.explanation: The outcomes were HADS, Spielberger-Khanin anxiety and a subjective comfort index, all self-reported emotional states. No behavioural or coping outcome was measured. The word 'effectively' also rests on an unblinded, within-group-driven analysis with no sample-size justification.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A behavioural or coping measure with a reported between-group effect.

quotes.text: помогает эффективно снять эмоциональное напряжение и изменить неадекватное поведение пациентов с постковидными нарушениями.

10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-1-38-48.headline_claim: Adding the placental hydrolysate Laennec to complex rehabilitation improves quality of life, lowers inflammatory markers and liver enzymes, and is clinically effective and safe in post-COVID patients with steatosis.
10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-1-38-48.overall: The headline claim of established efficacy and safety is not supported by a 40-patient, unblinded, unregistered study with no primary outcome and no multiplicity control; only some between-group differences (ferritin, ALT, AST, PCS-12, memory and concentration complaints) are directly shown. The anti-inflammatory conclusion is the weakest part: IL-6 values conflict between text and table, and CRP and ESR significance is claimed without supporting data or described follow-up.

primary_outcome.name: Change in liver enzymes (ALT, AST) and pro-inflammatory markers (ferritin, IL-6) between arms; primary outcome not explicitly designated

issues.title: 20 per arm, no sample-size rationale, no primary outcome; firm efficacy/safety and recommendation drawn
issues.explanation: With 40 patients, no stated power calculation or primary endpoint, and many outcomes, the study can at most be exploratory. The Conclusion nonetheless says it established significant clinical efficacy and safety, and the abstract recommends use. Arms also differed in setting (day-hospital versus round-the-clock inpatient) and sex mix (9/20 versus 14/20 men), which confounds the comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation and primary outcome, plus setting-matched arms.

quotes.text: В исследование были включены 40 пациентов
установило значимую клиническую эффективность и безопасность применения данного препарата
Медицинская реабилитация проводилась в рамках круглосуточного стационара.

second_reader.what_stands: The study has 20 patients per arm, no stated sample-size justification, no designated primary outcome, no multiplicity correction, and treatment setting differs between arms (day vs 24-hour hospital), yet the Conclusion asserts significant clinical efficacy and safety and recommends use. The strength of the conclusion exceeds what this design supports.

issues.title: Conclusion asserts efficacy, safety and anabolic/neurotrophic mechanism; none measured, safety from 20 patients
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says the study established significant efficacy and safety and attributes symptom changes to anabolic, neurotrophic and bioenergetic effects. No mechanistic markers were measured, the trial was 12 days, and adverse events are covered by one sentence on 20 treated patients. The comparison group's adverse events are not reported, and the mechanistic language is borrowed from other studies.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Mechanistic biomarker data and a pre-specified safety analysis in both arms.

quotes.text: установило значимую клиническую эффективность и безопасность применения данного препарата
нежелательных реакций на внутривенные вливания не выявлено
что обусловлено, по-видимому, анаболическим, нейротрофическим

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion states efficacy and safety without qualification, although safety rests on 0 events in 20 treated patients (upper bound about 15-17%) with no comparison-group safety data, and the anabolic, neurotrophic and bioenergetic mechanism is not measured anywhere in the study; it is only softened by 'по-видимому'. The mechanism is thus speculation presented in a conclusion.

issues.title: Discussion claims significant CRP and ESR fall (p<0.05) that Table 5 does not show; no follow-up described
issues.explanation: The Discussion asserts a significant reduction in ESR and CRP a month after treatment in the main group. Table 5 shows no significance marker for either, with medians essentially unchanged (CRP 0.1 to 0.1; ESR 8 to 7), and the Methods and Results describe no one-month follow-up. The Conclusion repeats the CRP claim, so the anti-inflammatory narrative is stated more strongly than the reported data allow.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data from a one-month post-treatment assessment showing significant CRP and ESR reductions, with a described follow-up protocol.

quotes.text: в крови через месяц после окончания лечения ( p < 0,05) у пациентов основной группы
С-реактивный белок высокочувствительный, мг/мл / High-sensitivity c-reactive protein, mg/mL

second_reader.what_stands: The Discussion (and Conclusion) state a significant (p<0.05) fall in ESR and CRP one month after treatment, but Table 5 marks neither as significantly changed (CRP median 0,1 to 0,1; ESR 8 to 7) and no post-treatment follow-up is described in the Methods or Results. The claim is unsupported by the data presented.

issues.title: IL-6, CRP and ESR benefit inferred from within-group significance; no between-group test (only ferritin has **)
issues.explanation: For ferritin, ALT and AST the paper marks a between-group Mann-Whitney difference. For IL-6 the table has only a within-group asterisk, and for CRP and ESR nothing, yet the text says the effect is confirmed by its absence in the comparison group. Inferring a drug effect from one arm reaching p<0.05 and the other not is not a valid comparison, so the anti-inflammatory conclusion is only partly supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test (or ANCOVA on change) for IL-6, CRP and ESR showing significance.

quotes.text: только у пациентов основной группы выявлено снижение уровня
что подтверждается отсутствием такового эффекта в группе сравнения

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that the benefit is confined to the main group rests on within-group Wilcoxon results, with no between-group test marked for IL-6, CRP or ESR; only ferritin (and ALT/AST) carry **. For ESR the changes in both groups are identical (-1 mm/h) and for CRP neither group changed, so a group difference is not shown; the statement 'absence of the effect in the comparison group' is not a valid comparison.

issues.title: Main-group IL-6 in text (8 to 3.4) differs from Table 5 (10.4 to 6.5)
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 5 give different medians and quartiles for the same group, variable and time points. Since IL-6 is one of only two markers named as significantly reduced and underpins the anti-inflammatory conclusion, readers cannot tell which values are right. The size of the fall also differs (4.6 versus 3.9 pg/mL in the medians).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Authors' clarification that the text and table use different statistics or subsets, or a corrected version showing identical values.

issues.title: Study funded by drug company contract; funder role unstated and conflicts declaration silent on it
issues.explanation: The funding statement names LLC Pharmaceutical Corporation 'RANA' as contracting party, but the paper never says whether the company had a role in design, analysis or writing. The conflicts statement lists editorial roles and says the others declare no conflicts, and it does not address the funder, in an unblinded trial of the funder's drug with a positive conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in design, analysis, interpretation or reporting.

Остальные авторы заявляют об отсутствии конфликта интересов.

issues.title: Dozens of outcomes tested at uncorrected p<0.05; few between-group ** results among ~40 comparisons
issues.explanation: The paper tests 16 complaint items, five MFI-20 subscales, PHQ-9, GAD-7, SF-12 and 15 laboratory variables, each at p<0.05 with no correction. The between-group significant results are few (memory, concentration, PCS-12, ferritin, ALT, AST), and with this many tests a few would be expected by chance. This weakens the secondary findings and the mechanistic claims built on them.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A declared primary outcome or a multiplicity adjustment under which the key results remain significant.

quotes.text: Различия считали достоверными при p < 0,05.

issues.title: No trial registration; randomization only 'simple', arms treated in different settings; no primary outcome
issues.explanation: No registry entry or protocol is cited, so outcome selection cannot be checked. The 'simple randomization' is not described further, no concealment or blinding is stated, and the arms differ in setting (day hospital versus 24-hour inpatient) and sex mix, which makes the allocation hard to credit as unbiased.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A trial registry entry with pre-specified outcomes and a described, concealed allocation sequence.

10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-2-7-16.headline_claim: A 12-week cardiopulmonary physical rehabilitation (CPR) programme improved dyspnoea (mMRC), VO2max and 6MWT distance in cardiological patients with post-COVID syndrome compared with physical-activity and control groups, and warrants larger randomised trials.
10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-2-7-16.overall: The direction of benefit for the CPR programme is plausible, since the objective measures (6MWT, VO2max, spirometry) all favour it. However, the participant flow cannot be reconciled (128 completers equals 128 allocated, yet 41.6 % CPR dropout is reported), the abstract misstates the PA group's mMRC median, and several percentage changes are computed inconsistently. The 'high efficacy' conclusion should be read as tentative pilot-level evidence only.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; 6MWT distance and mMRC dyspnoea score are presented as main outcomes

issues.title: 'High efficacy' conclusion for an unregistered pilot with unclear flow, open assessment and no primary outcome
issues.explanation: The Conclusion states high efficacy and superiority over both comparators. That rests on a pilot with an irreconcilable attrition account (128 completed, yet 41.6 % CPR dropout), unreported blinding and concealment, unadjusted multiple testing, and several mismatched numbers between abstract, text and table. The abstract itself calls for larger randomised trials. The effects look real in direction, but their size and the claim of efficacy are stronger than this report supports.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome with an intention-to-treat analysis showing the same effects, plus a full participant flow.

quotes.text: Программа реабилитации CPR для пациентов кардиологического профиля с постковидными осложнениями показала высокую эффективность
в рамках более масштабных рандомизированных клинических испытаний

second_reader.what_stands: The main-text conclusion states 'high efficacy' for a small pilot with no named primary outcome, no stated blinding, no registration statement in the paper, no multiplicity handling and unclear participant flow, and the Limitations section does not discuss these. This is partly offset by the abstract, which properly calls for larger randomised trials, and by the stated use of randomisation and covariate-adjusted analysis; absence of registration and blinding is based only on the paper not mentioning them.

issues.title: Participant flow irreconcilable: 128 allocated = 128 completed, yet 41.6 % CPR dropout reported
issues.explanation: The Methods allocate 42, 42 and 44 patients (total 128). The Results say all 128 completed the study, and the sex counts match the allocation exactly. The Conclusion then reports that 41.6 % dropped out of the CPR subgroup, which is impossible with 42 patients and contradicts completion by everyone. There is no CONSORT flow diagram, so the reader cannot tell who was enrolled, who dropped out, or whose data enter Table 1. This also means any attrition-related bias cannot be assessed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow diagram showing the enrolled number per arm, the dropouts and the analysed numbers, with a denominator that yields 41.6 %.

quotes.text: 47 (36,7 %) мужчин и 81 (63,3 %) женщина
42 (32,8 %) пациента, в составе 13 (31,0 %) мужчин и 29 (69,0 %) женщин
число выбывших во время реабилитации составило 41,6 %

second_reader.what_stands: The paper reports 128 participants allocated and 128 'fully completed' with group sex counts that sum exactly, while the conclusion states 41.6% dropout in the CPR group; both cannot be true, and 41.6% does not correspond to an integer count of 42 or 128. No flow diagram, dropout numbers or per-group analysed n are given, so the flow cannot be reconstructed.

issues.title: mMRC median for PA group at 12 weeks: abstract/Discussion 2.0, Table 1 and Results 1.0
issues.explanation: The abstract and Discussion say CPR (median 1.0) beat both the PA and control groups (median 2.0). Table 1 and the Results text give the PA group a median of 1.0 at 12 weeks, the same as CPR. The headline dyspnoea advantage of CPR over PA is therefore overstated in the abstract.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the abstract figure comes from a different time point or a different analysis, or a corrected Table 1 showing PA at 2.0.

issues.title: Self-rated mMRC dyspnoea is a headline result with no blinding or assessor masking described
issues.explanation: The dyspnoea difference is a featured abstract result, but the paper does not say whether outcome assessors were masked. Patients knew they were in the supervised programme, so expectation effects could inflate self-reported dyspnoea. Objective measures point the same way, so the conclusion is weakened rather than overturned.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that mMRC and the other tests were scored by assessors masked to group.

issues.title: VO2max gain in CPR: abstract 8.3 %, Results 10.4 %, printed endpoints 32.1 to 35.8 imply 11.5 %
issues.explanation: Three different numbers describe the CPR VO2max improvement. The abstract gives 8.3 ± 3.8 %, the Results give 10.4 %, and the endpoints printed beside the 10.4 % imply 11.5 %. The size of the benefit cannot be pinned down, and the abstract figure is not defined as a within-group or between-group quantity. The improvement direction is not in doubt.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that 8.3 % is the mean of individual percent changes and 10.4 % a rounded different summary, with the individual data reproducing both.

отмечали в пределах 10,4 % - с 32,1 мл/кг/ мин до 35,8 мл/кг/мин

issues.title: CPR 6MWT gain printed as 29.2 %, but 487 to 688 m is a 41.3 % rise from baseline
issues.explanation: The Results say the CPR walk distance rose by 29.2 % from 487.0 m to 688.0 m. A 201 m gain over a 487 m baseline is 41.3 %; 29.2 % only results from dividing by the final value. The distances themselves are consistent with Table 1, so only the percentage is wrong, and it understates the improvement. The mixed denominators make the percentage changes across outcomes hard to compare.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated definition of percentage change as change relative to the final value, applied consistently to every outcome.

quotes.text: увеличилась на 29,2 % - с 487,0 м до 688,0 м

issues.title: Dozens of outcome and time-point tests at p < 0.05 with no primary outcome and no correction
issues.explanation: Table 1 tests roughly 15 outcomes at three time points at an unadjusted 0.05 level, and no primary outcome is named. Many of the p-values are far below 0.05, so the main findings are probably robust to correction. Marginal results (e.g. HR at 6 weeks p = 0.022, SBP) would not be.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or an analysis plan that handles multiplicity.

quotes.text: статистически значимыми различиями показателей считали при p < 0,05

issues.title: No trial registration identifier reported
issues.explanation: The study reports allocation and 12-week follow-up but gives no registry number. Outcome selection, in particular which outcomes are headline, cannot be checked against a prior plan. The paper also calls itself a partial report of a larger evaluation, so outcome selection is a live concern.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry with the planned outcomes dated before enrolment.

10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-5-41-51.headline_claim: Response to post-COVID rehabilitation is associated with TLR4 Asp299Gly genotype, with the AG heterozygote group showing the greatest benefit and the most pronounced clinical symptoms, and the GG group needing a longer rehabilitation course.
10.38025/2078-1962-2024-23-5-41-51.overall: The headline claim that TLR4 genotype determines rehabilitation efficacy (AG best, GG needing longer courses) is not supported: between-genotype symptom comparisons are null and the conclusion rests on within-group significance and a handful of uncorrected between-group tests in small, unadjusted, non-randomised groups with baseline imbalance. There are also several printing errors (SD 0.00 with non-integer means, 77% vs 66.7%, mismatched text/table values), none of which alone changes the picture but which lower confidence in the tables.

primary_outcome.name: not explicitly designated; clinical symptom scores, functional tests and quality-of-life measures compared before and after rehabilitation by genotype

issues.title: Genotype-dependent rehabilitation claims rest on within-group significance; between-group symptom tests are null
issues.explanation: The paper concludes that AG patients have higher rehabilitation potential, that GG patients need longer rehabilitation, and that efficacy is linked to TLR4 genotype. But all between-genotype symptom comparisons were non-significant, and the few significant between-group results (FVC, PEF, 6MWT, ESR) are among dozens of uncorrected tests in 92 patients (groups of 22-37). Claims that one group changed 'significantly' and another did not are not evidence that the groups differ, and no recommendation about longer courses for GG patients was tested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A formal genotype-by-time interaction test, or multiplicity-adjusted between-group comparisons of change showing consistent differences.

second_reader.what_stands: For the clinical symptom scores, all 15 between-genotype tests are null, and the claims that rehabilitation is more effective in AG and less so in GG rest on within-group significance and on the differing patterns of which within-group tests were significant. The functional measures do have a few nominally significant between-group differences in change (FVC and PEF for AA vs AG, 6MWT for AG vs GG), but these are uncorrected across many comparisons, so it is not true that all between-group tests are null. The conclusion that GG patients need a longer course is not tested directly, since course

issues.title: AA-group symptom scores show SD 0.00 with non-integer means (e.g. 1.41 ± 0.00) for integer 0-4 scores, n=22
issues.explanation: The symptom scale is integer-valued (0-4) and the AA group has 22 patients. An SD of exactly 0.00 means all 22 scores are identical, so the mean would be an integer, not 1.41, 0.74 or 0.11. These cells, and others like them with a suspicious SD of 1.41 for a mean of 0.63, cannot be right. The AA-group results, and the within-group significance stars attached to them, are therefore unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw AA-group patient scores showing the dispersion was computed differently, or a corrected table.

issues.title: Baseline imbalance (AG more severe; GG all female) not adjusted; larger AG change may reflect higher baseline
issues.explanation: The AG group started with the most severe symptoms and lowest PEF, so larger improvements there are expected regardless of genotype (more room to improve, regression to the mean). Sex composition also differs (GG 33/33 female vs AA 17/22) and no covariate adjustment was made. The genotype attribution of the greater AG response is therefore not separable from baseline severity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Baseline-adjusted analysis of change (ANCOVA) showing the AG advantage persists.

quotes.text: состояние пациентов с более выраженными клиническими симптомами было в группе больных с генотипом AG

issues.title: Uncontrolled before-after design: improvements cannot be attributed to rehabilitation itself
issues.explanation: All patients received the same programme and change is measured within genotype groups only, so natural recovery (patients were 2-15 months post-infection) and regression to the mean are not separated from treatment effect. This matters less for comparing genotypes but undermines wording such as rehabilitation being 'effective' in a group. It weakens, rather than defeats, the paper's conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A comparator group, or a framing restricted to between-genotype differences in change.

issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the 77% was computed by a stated alternative method (e.g. mean of individual percentage changes).

issues.title: Laboratory section says no significant changes yet reports AG vs GG ESR difference (p3 = 0.03)

The statement is internally inconsistent. The ESR result is also one of many unadjusted comparisons, and WBC is borderline at p3 = 0.05.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Clarification that the opening sentence refers only to within-group changes.
