10.38025/2078-1962-2025-24-5-34-46.headline_claim: Comprehensive rehabilitation with personalised normobaric interval hypoxia-hyperoxia therapy (NBIGGT) statistically significantly improves rehabilitation effectiveness after coronavirus pneumonia.
10.38025/2078-1962-2025-24-5-34-46.overall: The qualitative direction, that the add-on therapy group improved more on most measures, is plausible, since many differences are large with p<0.001. However, the design is open-label with self-drawn envelopes, has no registration, primary outcome or multiplicity control, reports no safety data, and draws superiority on spirometry and 6MWT from within-group significance. Reporting errors in the abstract and ethics dates, and the unclear flow, reduce confidence, so the conclusion should be treated as tentative.

issues.title: Abstract gives main-group Genchi gain 24.14% (p=0.006); Table 2 gives 38.13% (p<0.001)
issues.explanation: The abstract reports the Genchi (breath-hold on exhalation) gain in the main group as 24.14% with p=0.006. In Table 2 those figures belong to the comparison group's Stange row. The main group's Genchi row shows 38.13% with p<0.001. The abstract therefore misstates one headline result; the table values still favour the main group, so the error is in the abstract only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A Genchi analysis in which the main group's gain was 24.14% with p=0.006, in conflict with Table 2's 38.13%.

issues.title: Envelope allocation self-drawn by patients and self-reported; concealment and blinding not established
issues.explanation: Patients chose a sealed envelope and told the investigator which group they would join, with verification afterwards. This is a random-like process, but there is no stated opacity, no independent allocator and no sequence generation. The comparison is open-label with no sham, while most outcomes (dyspnoea scales, HADS, SF-36, breath-holds) are subjective or effort dependent. Some bias is therefore possible in the between-group differences.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol stating opaque, shuffled envelopes opened by an independent person, and blinded outcome assessors.

issues.title: No primary outcome and no multiplicity control across dozens of outcomes and time points
issues.explanation: The paper tests many outcomes at several time points (dyspnoea, breath-holds, heart rate, 6MWT, spirometry, perfusion, HADS, eight SF-36 domains) at alpha 0.05. The only correction mentioned is Bonferroni for comparing several groups, which does not apply to two arms. Highly significant results are likely robust, but the marginal ones are less secure, and the blanket conclusion of significant improvement across all domains is not protected against false positives.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome and hierarchical or corrected testing in which the claimed secondary results remain significant.

10.38079/igusabder.1654185.headline_claim: Calisthenic exercise, delivered either therapist-supervised or as a home programme, led to a significant improvement in quality of life (EQ-5D-3L) in patients with post-COVID syndrome, and home delivery can be as effective as supervised delivery.
10.38079/igusabder.1654185.overall: The finding that EQ-5D scores improved over 8 weeks in both arms is plausible given the large mean changes, but the design (no non-exercise control) cannot attribute the change to calisthenics. The 'home exercise is as effective' conclusion is not supported: no equivalence analysis was done, and the printed t, p and chi-square values across Tables 2-4 are mutually inconsistent, with at least one outcome (general health score) whose means imply a significant between-group difference. Registration was also filed after the study started.

primary_outcome.name: EQ-5D-3L quality of life

primary_outcomes.measure: EQ-5D-3L (European Quality of Life 5 Dimensions 3 Level Version)

issues.title: After-treatment general health score: means 75.78 vs 68.57 imply p≈0.026, but p=0.982 is printed
issues.explanation: The post-treatment general health scores differ by 7.2 points between arms, with SDs of 18 and 24 and 88 per arm. A two-sample t-test on these numbers gives a clearly significant difference, yet the table prints p = 0.982 and t = -1.959 (which would itself give p of about 0.05, not 0.98). The 'no difference between groups' conclusion therefore does not follow from the printed data for this outcome.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data showing different means or SDs for this score, or a corrected table in which the t and p match.

quotes.text: P-values are derived from the Independent Samples T-test.

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.982, but recomputed from the printed group means and SDs p is at most 0.02736, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show, and on the other side of alpha = 0.05 (a decision error). This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

second_reader.what_stands: The printed p=0.982 does not match the printed means, SDs and n, which imply t of about 2.25 and p of about 0.026. Recomputed, the after-treatment general health score would favour the home group at the 0.05 level, which contradicts the paper's statement of no significant between-group difference. This assumes n=88 per group at follow-up as in Table 2; I could not check the Figure 1 flow numbers.

issues.title: Test statistics and p-values in Tables 2-4 do not correspond (e.g. t=8.554 with p=0.120; p=5.749)
issues.explanation: Across Tables 2, 3 and 4 the printed t (or chi-square) values cannot produce the printed p-values with about 88 per arm. Table 3 even prints a p of 5.749, which is impossible, and Table 2 prints a chi-square of 17.556 with p = 732 for groups described as similar. The reported statistics are therefore unreliable, and it is unclear which column, if either, is correct. The direction of the within-group improvements is likely robust to this, but the exact test results and the between-group nulls cannot be taken as printed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source data or a corrected table showing t and p pairs that agree at the stated sample sizes.

quotes.location: Table 3, After Treatment, Usual activities row

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.12, but recomputed from the printed t = 8.554 p is at most 5.998e-15, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show, and on the other side of alpha = 0.05 (a decision error). This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

second_reader.what_stands: Many t and p pairs in Tables 3 and 4 are mutually inconsistent. Examples are t=8.554 with p=0.120, and p=5.749, which is not a valid probability. Recomputing from the printed means and SDs does not reproduce the printed t values, so the test statistics and p-values cannot be relied on. I checked only the three cited rows (plus the Table 3 score row under i15) and did not check every row of Tables 2-4.

issues.title: Benefit of calisthenics inferred from pre-post change in two exercise arms, with no non-exercise control
issues.explanation: Both arms received the same calisthenics programme, and the evidence for benefit is the significant baseline-to-8-week change within each arm. Without a no-exercise or usual-care group, these changes cannot be separated from natural recovery of post-Covid symptoms, regression to the mean or expectation. The abstract and conclusions nevertheless say exercise 'led to' (and, in the abstract, causes) an improvement in quality of life. The supported finding is that scores improved over time in both arms, not that calisthenics caused it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent non-exercise comparison arm, or an argument supported by external data that spontaneous change over 8 weeks is negligible in this population.

quotes.text: significant improvements were observed in therapist-supervised and home exercise groups
led to an improvement in patients'  QoL
calisthenics exercises were actively practiced in the control group.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper's improvement claim rests on pre-post changes within two exercising arms with no non-exercise comparison. Natural recovery from post-Covid symptoms over 8 weeks, regression to the mean, expectation effects and the video-call contact cannot be separated from any effect of calisthenics. The causal wording ('led to an improvement') is therefore not supported by the design.

issues.title: Non-significant between-group difference presented as home exercise being 'as effective' as supervised exercise
issues.explanation: The conclusion that home exercise 'can be as effective' as therapist-supervised exercise rests on p > 0.05 for each comparison. The study had no pre-specified equivalence margin and reported no confidence intervals for the between-group differences. The trial was powered only to detect d = 0.5, so non-significance is compatible with a clinically relevant difference. Equivalence is therefore not demonstrated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified equivalence margin with confidence intervals lying inside it.

quotes.text: the correct delivery of home exercise training can be as effective
there was no difference between the therapist-supervised and home exercise program

second_reader.what_stands: The paper moves from 'no significant difference' to 'home exercise can be as effective' without any equivalence or non-inferiority analysis or confidence intervals. A non-significant superiority test does not show equivalence. The printed p-values are also unreliable, and the one score difference I recomputed (about 7 points) is not trivially small.

issues.title: Self-reported EQ-5D outcome with participants unblinded; only assessment was blinded
issues.explanation: Participants knew whether they exercised at home or under supervision, and the outcome is a self-completed questionnaire. Expectation effects could inflate the within-group improvements. The effect on the between-group comparison is probably small because both arms did the same programme, and the authors disclose this limitation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the questionnaire was administered by the blinded assessor with no knowledge of allocation, or an objective co-primary outcome showing the same pattern.

quotes.text: The  second  limitation  is  that  blinding  was  done  only  during  the assessment.
Each dimension has three levels and is completed by checking one of the boxes

issues.title: Trial described as prospective but registered 2024-08-21, after the registry start date (2023-11-01)
issues.explanation: The paper calls the trial prospective and cites NCT06568393 without noting that registration was filed after the study period had begun. The registry record shows a first submission on 2024-08-21 with a study start of 2023-11-01, and the paper dates the work January to December 2024. Registration therefore cannot show that outcomes and analyses were set before data collection. The registered primary outcome matches the reported EQ-5D-3L, which limits the practical impact.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version dated before enrolment, or a documented protocol with the outcome specified in advance.

quotes.text: This prospective and randomized controlled trial was completed at the Physical Therapy Laboratory of Avrasya University between January and December 2024

issues.title: Table 2 sex percentages are swapped relative to counts out of n=88 (42 printed as 52%, 46 as 48%)
issues.explanation: Table 2 prints 42 men (52%) and 46 women (48%) in the home arm, and 40 men (55%) and 48 women (45%) in the other arm. Out of 88 per arm the correct values are 48%/52% and 45%/55%, so the percentages are attached to the wrong rows. This is a labelling slip with no effect on the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that percentages were computed over a base other than the arm size.

quotes.text: Baseline n=88 n=88

script.explanation: 42/88 = 47.73%, but the paper prints 52, outside the rounding interval [51.50, 53.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 80.8 rather than 88.

issues.title: Twelve within-arm EQ-5D tests at p<0.05 without multiplicity adjustment; no single primary outcome named
issues.explanation: Six dimensions in each of two arms were tested separately with paired t-tests and no correction, and the abstract says all parameters improved. Some of the borderline p-values would not survive a correction. Given the size of the mean changes, the main finding of improvement over time probably would.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A declared primary dimension or composite, or adjusted p-values that remain below 0.05.

quotes.text: The  level  of statistical significance was accepted as p<0.05.
P-values are derived from the Paired Samples T-test.

issues.title: Three-level ordinal EQ-5D items summarised as means and compared with t-tests
issues.explanation: Each EQ-5D-3L dimension has only three response levels, so means and parametric tests are a loose fit and a non-parametric or proportional-odds analysis would suit the data better. The paper reports a normality test but gives no results. This is a modest weakness; the large mean shifts make a different conclusion unlikely.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis using ordinal or non-parametric methods that gives the same results.

quotes.text: When  comparing  two  groups,  the  independent  samples  t-test  was  used  if  the  parametric  assumption  was  met.
