10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1177_23.headline_claim: Telemedicine-based pulmonary rehabilitation in recovered COVID-19 pneumonitis patients is effective in reducing dyspnoea, reducing morbidity, increasing endurance and improving quality of life.
10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1177_23.overall: The finding that patients improved over six weeks is supported descriptively, but the conclusion that telemedicine rehabilitation is 'effective' rests on an uncontrolled, unblinded single group with partly patient-reported outcomes, and the Discussion wrongly refers to a between-group comparison. The SF-36 results are internally ambiguous because three domains fall without any stated scoring direction, so the QoL claim cannot be verified. Other problems are minor reporting inconsistencies.

primary_outcome.name: 6-minute walk test (laps) pre vs post 6 weeks; not explicitly designated primary

issues.title: Efficacy concluded from a single uncontrolled, unblinded pre-post series of 50 patients
issues.explanation: All 50 patients received the programme with no comparator, and no one assessed outcomes blind. Improvements in walking, sit-to-stand, dyspnoea and QoL from baseline to six weeks cannot be separated from spontaneous post-COVID recovery, expectation and practice effects. The conclusion says the programme 'is effective', and the control-group limitation is mentioned only as a future need. The data show change over time, not a treatment effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or historical control group showing less improvement over the same six weeks, or blinded outcome assessment.

quotes.text: Telemedicine-based pulmonary rehabilitation in patients with recovered
Larger sample size and control group is warranted

second_reader.what_stands: The paper draws an unqualified efficacy conclusion ('is effective') from a single-arm, uncontrolled pre-post series of 50 patients, with no blinding described, so improvement cannot be attributed to the intervention rather than spontaneous recovery. The authors do note that a larger sample and control group are warranted, but this brief limitation is not reflected in the strength of the conclusion.

issues.title: SF-36 scoring direction unstated: 3 of 8 domains fall (pain 84.05 to 28.4, role limits 98 to 2.3) yet all called improved
issues.explanation: Five SF-36 domains rise from low to high values, while pain and both role-limitation domains fall from near the maximum to near zero. The paper says all eight domains improved and the QoL conclusion rests on this, but it never states a scoring direction. Under the standard scale, three domains would show marked deterioration. The QoL conclusion therefore cannot be verified from the printed numbers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A methods statement that these domains were scored on a reversed scale (or as a burden score), with the other domains scored conventionally.

quotes.text: role limitations due to physical health (98 ± 9.9 to 2.3 ± 5.07)

second_reader.what_stands: True: the paper never states the SF-36 scoring direction, and three domains (role-physical 98 to 2.3, role-emotional 100 to 2.67, pain 84.05 to 28.4) fall while all eight are called improved, with no explanation of reversed coding. Not established: that the results are actually wrong, since reversed coding for those domains would explain the pattern, but the paper does not say so, and the very high baseline role scores (98 to 100) are hard to reconcile with standard SF-36 direction in recently discharged patients.

issues.title: Discussion claims significance 'between the two groups' though the study had one group
issues.explanation: The Discussion says the SF-36 scores were significant within the intervention group and between the two groups. The study enrolled a single group of 50 and reports only paired pre-post tests, so there is no between-group comparison. This wording suggests a controlled comparison that does not exist and reinforces the overstated efficacy conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data from a second group and a between-group test in the paper.

quotes.text: were statistically significant within the intervention group and between the two groups

issues.title: Session length given as 40 minutes (video consultation) and as 45 to 60 minutes (PR session)
issues.explanation: The Methods describe a 40-minute video session three times a week, but the programme description says each PR session lasted 45 to 60 minutes. The two may refer to different parts of the session, but the paper does not say so. The exact dose delivered is therefore unclear, though no result depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that 40 minutes was the supervised video component and the remainder was unsupervised home exercise within the 45 to 60 minute session.

quotes.text: Video consultation/40-minute session
45  to  60  minutes
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, PR programme description

issues.title: Same change (38.5 to 52.9) given P < 0.001 in one sentence and P = 0.036 in another
issues.explanation: The Discussion reports a mental component score change from 38.5 to 52.9 with P < 0.001. Two sentences later the identical change is reported with P = 0.036. Both are attributed to the external Gloeckl study, so the literature comparison is internally inconsistent. It does not affect this study's own results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: The source paper (Gloeckl et al.) reporting both p-values for different tests of the same change.

quotes.text: (from 38.5 to 52.9 points; P < 0.001)

issues.title: CTRI approval mentioned but no registration number or prespecified outcomes given
issues.explanation: The paper refers to 'CTRI approvals' without a registration identifier or date. Readers cannot check whether the reported outcomes match a prospective protocol. This is a transparency gap and does not by itself show any outcome switching.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A CTRI registration number with a prospective registration date and matching outcomes.

quotes.text: after CTRI approvals

issues.title: Calculated minimum sample size not stated and no flow or completer count for the 50 patients
issues.explanation: The Methods say the sample size was calculated with a 10% attrition allowance but never give the resulting number. They also say the first 50 consenting patients were used. No completer or dropout count is given, though the tables imply a complete analysis. Readers cannot judge whether the study met its target or lost anyone.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated calculated sample size and a flow statement showing all 50 completed and were analysed.

quotes.text: First 50 eligible patients from the study population, consenting to participate comprised the study sample.

10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1221_24.headline_claim: A selective yoga regime for about 8 weeks improves pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1) in COVID-19 survivors with altered lung function and may be given as additive treatment.
10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1221_24.overall: The paper shows that spirometry percent-predicted values were higher after 8 weeks of yoga than before, but with no control group, natural post-COVID recovery cannot be separated from any yoga effect. Paired data were analysed with unpaired tests, and the conclusions on faster recovery, cost-effectiveness and a 3-month minimum are not supported by what was measured. The headline claim of effectiveness is therefore tentative at best.

primary_outcome.name: Pulmonary function test parameters (FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, FEF25-75, PEF, % predicted)

issues.title: Efficacy of yoga inferred from uncontrolled pre-post change; natural post-COVID recovery not separable
issues.explanation: All participants had spirometry before and after yoga, with no concurrent control group. Lung function after COVID-19 commonly recovers spontaneously over the weeks to months studied, so the improvement cannot be attributed to yoga. The paper nevertheless concludes that yoga may be given as treatment and shows effectiveness. Participants were also all continuing other therapies.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated or active control group showing no comparable improvement.

quotes.text: This was a follow-up, comparative study based on a tertiary care centre in Central India.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Study design and settings

quotes.text: To improve altered pulmonary functions in COVID-19 survivors

second_reader.what_stands: Efficacy is inferred from an uncontrolled before/after change in one cohort over about 8 weeks, so any yoga effect cannot be separated from natural recovery, regression to the mean or practice effects on spirometry. The paper states effectiveness in the Discussion and recommends yoga in the Conclusions without acknowledging this limitation.

issues.title: Paired pre/post data analysed with independent-sample rank-sum and chi-square tests (82 vs 73)
issues.explanation: The same survivors were measured before and after yoga, but the paper compares the two time points as independent groups, using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and Pearson chi-square, and includes 9 people with baseline data only. Paired data should be analysed with a paired test on the 73 with both measurements. The reported P values therefore do not follow the design, although the large effects probably survive and borderline ones could change in either direction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that a paired signed-rank test was actually run on matched participants.

quotes.text: The PFT variables were compared before and after the selected yoga regime intervention using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
2 Wilcoxon rank sum test

second_reader.what_stands: The same participants were measured twice, but the paper reports independent-sample tests (Wilcoxon rank-sum, Pearson chi-square) on 82 vs 73 observations, which ignores the pairing and the 9 dropouts. This is the wrong test for paired data, so the reported p-values do not reflect the paired design. I could not check which direction that biases the p-values.

issues.title: Conclusions claim faster recovery and cost-effectiveness, neither measured in an uncontrolled spirometry study
issues.explanation: The study measured spirometry only, over 8 weeks, with no control group and no cost data. It cannot show recovery that is faster than natural recovery, nor cost-effectiveness. The conclusions and the Discussion's statement that the study shows effectiveness go beyond what the data support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A controlled comparison and cost data supporting these statements.

quotes.text: may recover faster and more efficiently with selective yoga regime
Hence, the present study shows the effectiveness of

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusions claim faster and more efficient recovery and cost-effectiveness, yet the study has no comparison arm, no repeated time points to estimate recovery speed, and no cost data. The 3-month duration recommendation is also not tested, since follow-up was 8 weeks.

issues.title: FEF25-75 reported P = 0.014 (alpha 0.05) but described as non-significant in Results and Discussion
issues.explanation: The Methods define significance as P < 0.05, and Table 5 gives P = 0.014 for FEF25-75. Yet the Results and Discussion list FEF25-75 among the parameters that did not improve significantly. The text misclassifies one result by the authors' own criterion, and it understates the benefit.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated stricter alpha or multiplicity correction under which 0.014 is non-significant.

quotes.text: except for the ratio of FEV1/FVC ( P = 0.6), FEF 25-75 % ( P = 0.014), and PEF % ( P = 0.12)
except the FEF (25-75%), ratio of FEV1/FVC, and PEF
the P value < 0.05 is considered significant

issues.title: Claim that yoga 'must last at least 3 months' rests on literature, not on an 8-week study
issues.explanation: All participants practised for about 8 weeks, and there was no comparison of durations. The conclusion that the regime must last at least 3 months is not tested by any data here, and long-term durability was not measured. This is largely subsumed in the broader overreach in the conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data comparing 8-week and 3-month regimes in this cohort.

quotes.text: underwent a selective yoga regime for 8
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Selective yoga regime as rehabilitative therapy

quotes.text: it must last over a longer period of

issues.title: Completers-only analysis: 9 of 82 (11%) lost to follow-up, no sensitivity analysis
issues.explanation: Results are reported only for the 73 who returned, and the 9 without follow-up are not accounted for in the main analyses (the baseline column still includes all 82). Those not returning may have had poorer or better outcomes. The loss is small, so the effect on conclusions is limited.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sensitivity analysis imputing the missing 9 that leaves results unchanged.

quotes.text: In this study, 9 participants are lost to follow-up.
9  participants  had  not  attended  the  follow-up OPD for evaluation
quotes.location: Selective yoga regime as rehabilitative therapy

issues.title: Table 4 sex rows: preyoga counts 24+56=80 vs N=82; sex totals 47+106=153 vs 155 elsewhere
issues.explanation: In Table 4 the preyoga sex counts sum to 80, not 82, and the combined sex denominators sum to 153, whereas other rows (diabetes 75+80, hypertension 93+61, COPD 144+11) sum to 155. Two participants appear to be missing from the sex row, or the cells are mistyped. This is a baseline description error that does not alter the outcome results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Two participants with missing sex data, stated by the authors.

quotes.location: Table 4, Sex row, Female, Preyoga column
Table 4, Sex row, Male, Preyoga column

issues.title: 'One in four' benefit statement is not matched by 30% (FVC) and 41% (FEV1) crossing the 80% cutoff
issues.explanation: The Discussion says one in four survivors benefitted, but the same paragraph reports 22/73 (30%) for FVC and 30/73 (41%) for FEV1 reaching the 80% cutoff. One in four (25%) does not match either figure. Also, the denominator of 73 omits the 9 lost to follow-up, so the proportion among all 82 enrolled would be lower (22/82 = 27%, 30/82 = 37%).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A defined composite benefit outcome yielding 25%.

quotes.text: one out of  a total of  4 COVID-19 survivors benefitted
This classification represents that FVC and FEV1 parameters are improved by 30% and 41%

issues.title: Prospective 8-week intervention with ethics approval number but no trial registration reported
issues.explanation: Participants were enrolled prospectively in July to November 2021 and received an intervention, but no registry number is given. A pre-specified primary outcome therefore cannot be checked, and the many spirometry measures were all tested without a declared primary. Whether registration was required is uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry (e.g., CTRI) with a pre-specified primary outcome.

quotes.text: COVID-19 survivors were enrolled in the study from July 2021 to November 2021.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Study design and settings

quotes.text: IHECLOP/2020/EF0219

10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_903_22.headline_claim: Supervised hospital-based pulmonary rehabilitation of at least three weeks produced perceptible benefits in long COVID patients and should be offered to all such cases unless contraindicated.
10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_903_22.overall: The reported improvements are real within this cohort, but an uncontrolled retrospective before-after series cannot show that rehabilitation caused them, so the recommendation to offer it to all long COVID patients is not supported. There are also several count and p-value inconsistencies between the text and Tables 1c, 2b and 3, and the unpaired tests on paired data are the wrong choice. These are minor individually.

primary_outcome.name: Impact of pulmonary rehabilitation on outcome of long COVID patients (primary not operationalised as a single measure)

issues.title: Benefit attributed to rehabilitation from an uncontrolled retrospective before-after series of 71 patients
issues.explanation: All 71 patients received rehabilitation plus pharmacotherapy and were compared only with their own admission values over about three weeks. Spontaneous recovery, concurrent drugs (steroids, antifibrotics, antibiotics) and regression to the mean cannot be separated from any effect of rehabilitation. The conclusion that rehabilitation 'resulted in perceptible benefits' and has a 'positive impact' is therefore not supported by this design. At most it shows that patients improved during an admission that included rehabilitation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or matched control group receiving the same pharmacotherapy without rehabilitation, showing a between-group difference.

quotes.text: who was admitted and managed in the post COVID pulmonary ward during the period from April 1, 2021 to December 1, 2021.
Pulmonary rehabilitation therapy offered to long COVID patients resulted in perceptible benefits as evidenced by

second_reader.what_stands: The paper is an uncontrolled retrospective before-after series of 71 inpatients, and the Conclusion attributes 'perceptible benefits' and 'positive impact' to PR without a comparator and without separating PR from concurrent drug treatment and natural recovery. The limitations (small, single-centre, retrospective) are acknowledged in the Discussion but not weighed against the causal wording of the Conclusion.

issues.title: Recommendation for all long COVID patients and 'immune-modulatory role' claimed from an uncontrolled 71-patient series
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says rehabilitation 'should be offered to all such cases' and gives clinicians a 'road map', and the Discussion says the fall in biomarkers 'shows immune-modulatory role of PR'. The data are a single-centre retrospective series without a comparator, in which pharmacotherapy, spontaneous recovery and admission care were all operating. The data do not support either a general treatment recommendation or a mechanistic claim about biomarkers.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Controlled data showing rehabilitation-specific effects on biomarkers and outcomes.

quotes.text: hence it should be offered to all such cases unless otherwise contraindicated
Fall in biomarkers level following PR in our study shows immune-modulatory role of PR

second_reader.what_stands: The universal recommendation ('all such cases') and the statement that falling CRP and D-dimer 'shows immune-modulatory role of PR' are not supported by an uncontrolled, single-centre, retrospective series of 71 selected inpatients, in which biomarker normalisation cannot be separated from natural resolution and concurrent drug therapy. The Conclusion and Discussion do partly hedge the immune-modulation point as an area for further research, so the overstatement is clearest in the final Discussion sentence and in the 'all such cases' recommendation.

issues.title: OAD group n=30 conflicts with 27 cured + 4 on O2 = 31; pattern counts sum to 70, not 71; Table 1c cell 26 vs 27
issues.explanation: Table 3 lists 27 cured and 4 on oxygen for obstructive airway disease, which is 31 patients, but labels the column n=30. The four pattern groups then add to 70, not the 71 patients analysed. The cured counts across the four patterns (27+14+12+8) do reach 61, so the OAD denominator looks like the error. Table 1c, which gives 26 fully recovered OAD patients, is the one that disagrees with the text and Table 3. It sums to 60 fully recovered patients, not 61. This is a one-patient reporting error that shifts percentages slightly and does not change the findings.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that one patient had no assigned pattern, with the OAD cured and O2 counts and percentages recomputed on a base that reconciles.

quotes.text: Obstructive airway disease (n=30)
Out of 71 cases 61 (85.9%) were cured and discharged in whom majority belongs to following entities: OAD-27, pneumonia-14, non IPF ILD-12 and IPF ILD-8
Broadly long COVID cases were managed under the category of obstructive airway diseases pattern in thirty patients

issues.title: Outcome-defined groups (cure vs home oxygen) used to show improvement; no pooled result for all 71 patients
issues.explanation: Fully recovered is defined as discharge with cure and partly recovered as discharge on home oxygen. Improvement in the 'cured' group is therefore partly true by construction. The 10 non-improving patients are reported but the conclusion speaks of long COVID patients generally, with no overall effect estimate for all 71. This is a presentation weakness rather than hidden data.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pooled analysis of all 71 patients' change from baseline, with the conclusion tied to that result.

quotes.text: Fully recovered category was discharge with cure and the part recovery category was discharge with home oxygen support
Sixty-one patients in fully recovered group show remarkable improvement in parameters like

issues.title: Text says partly recovered group had no significant improvement, yet Table 2b shows SpO2 87→91, p=0.01
issues.explanation: The Observations state that the 10 partly recovered patients showed no significant improvement in the same parameters (SpO2, mMRC, cough). Table 2b reports a 4-point SpO2 rise with p=0.01, below the paper's own 0.05 threshold. So the narrative understates the SpO2 change in this group. The conclusion that this group did not improve on the other measures is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the SpO2 change was judged clinically trivial or that the p-value in Table 2b is a typo.

quotes.text: While 10 people in partly recovered group show no significant improvement in same parameters

issues.title: Before/after values in the same patients tested with an unpaired t-test; footnotes cite Fisher exact test
issues.explanation: The Methods state that an unpaired t-test was used to compare the two sets of values, which are repeated measures in the same patients. Recomputing from the printed means and SDs reproduces the Table 2b p-values as unpaired tests, so pairing was apparently ignored. The Table 2 footnote instead says Fisher exact test, which does not fit means or ordinal grades. The test choice is wrong but with these effect sizes in Table 2a the within-group conclusions probably survive; the small partly recovered group would need re-analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Methods or output showing paired t, Wilcoxon or McNemar tests were run on the individual before/after data.

quotes.text: The unpaired ttest was used to compare two discrete variables.
Table 2a: Change in Variable after Pulmonary Rehabilitation therapy-full recovered group (n=61)

issues.title: Text swaps partly recovered counts: non-IPF ILD 3 and IPF-ILD 2, but Tables 1c and 3 give 2 and 3
issues.explanation: The Results text assigns 3 partly recovered patients to non-IPF ILD and 2 to IPF-ILD. Table 1c and Table 3 give the reverse: 2 non-IPF and 3 IPF-ILD. The tables are internally consistent with group sizes of 14 and 11, so the text is wrong. This is a minor slip that does not change any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source records showing 3 partly recovered non-IPF ILD patients, with the tables then wrong.

quotes.text: OAD-4, non IPF ILD-3, IPF ILD-2, and pneumonia-1

issues.title: Baseline SpO2 (mean 87±4 and 90.03±3.89) and 5 ventilated patients conflict with stated exclusion criteria
issues.explanation: Patients with SpO2 below 90% and those needing ventilatory support are listed as excluded. Yet the partly recovered group has a mean baseline SpO2 of 87, the full-recovery group has a mean of 90.03 with SD 3.89, and 5 patients had NIV or invasive ventilation. Different timing of measurement could explain it, but the paper does not say, so it cannot be settled.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Methods stating that exclusion criteria applied at referral or on oxygen, and that Table 2 baselines are at a different time point.

quotes.text: patients with oxygen saturation less than 90% or de-saturating more than 4% from baseline on exertion

issues.title: Table 1c: identical 30/26/4 counts in three rows carry different p-values (0.84 vs 0.37); leucocytosis % missing
issues.explanation: The leucocytosis, bronchopneumonia and OAD rows all show 30 patients, 26 fully recovered and 4 partly recovered. The first two give p=0.84, but the OAD row gives 0.37 (the same value as the IPF-ILD row), and Table 3 gives 0.84 for OAD. Identical counts cannot give two different p-values. The four radiological rows also reproduce the four pattern counts (14/11/30/15), which suggests label reuse. These are table-reporting errors affecting secondary baseline comparisons only.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Source records showing that the same 26/4 split genuinely applies to all three variables, with the OAD p-value corrected to 0.84.

quotes.text: Leukocytosis was seen in 30 (42.2%) patients.

10.4103/jpgm.jpgm_650_23.headline_claim: Adding creatine monohydrate to breathing exercises reduces respiratory discomfort and improves creatine status and post-exertional malaise in long-COVID patients, supporting creatine as a well-tolerated adjuvant.
10.4103/jpgm.jpgm_650_23.overall: The headline claim that creatine added to breathing exercises has demonstrated benefits and can be recommended is not supported: eight patients, no multiplicity control, and no placebo despite a double-blind label. Several 'significant' results (time to exhaustion, six within-arm brain creatine increases) are contradicted by their own confidence intervals. At most the study is hypothesis-generating.

primary_outcome.name: Tissue total creatine by MRS (muscle and brain regions), with symptom and exercise measures listed as main outcomes

issues.title: Eight-patient pilot (4 per arm, no sample size calculation) 'demonstrated' benefit and recommends creatine
issues.explanation: The Discussion states that the pilot demonstrated beneficial effects and that creatine could be recommended as an adjuvant. The study has eight participants, no sample size calculation, many uncorrected outcomes and several results that do not reconcile with their CIs. It can generate hypotheses but cannot establish benefit or justify a recommendation.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified, adequately powered analysis confirming the benefits.

quotes.text: The present pilot  study  has  demonstrated  the  beneficial effects  of  adding  creatine  to  breathing  exercises  protocol
Creatine monohydrate could be thus recommended as a well-tolerated adjuvant to breathing exercises

second_reader.what_stands: Eight patients (4 per arm) with no sample size justification cannot 'demonstrate' benefit, and a recommendation for creatine as an adjuvant goes beyond the evidence, especially as most clinical outcomes showed no between-arm difference. The paper does call it a pilot and asks for larger studies, which partly tempers the language but not the stated conclusion.

issues.title: Time to exhaustion +54 s called significant: P = 0.05, but 95% CI -201 to 309 and between-arm P = 0.11
issues.explanation: The Results and Discussion call the 54 s gain in time to exhaustion significant. The printed CI spans zero by a wide margin and implies a p-value far above 0.05, and P = 0.05 is not below 0.05 in any case. The only significance rests on a within-arm change; the between-arm comparison is described as only a tendency (P = 0.11). The claim of a significant improvement is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected CI or p-value showing that the within-arm change is significant, or a significant between-arm contrast for time to exhaustion.

quotes.text: was significantly improved by 54 s (95% CI from - 201 to 309) in the study group post-administration ( P = 0.05)
A statistically significant improvement in time to exhaustion after creatine intake (54 s)

script.explanation: the p-value recovered from the CI is 0.6781 (reachable range [0.6747, 0.6815] across the printed precision of the estimate and its bounds), but p = 0.05 is reported -- this recovery inverts a WALD interval, so if the paper used a bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood or Fieller interval the two numbers are not comparable; confirm the method before treating this as a finding

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the 54 s improvement 'significant' (Results and Discussion) although its own 95% CI (-201 to 309) includes zero and is inconsistent with the printed P = 0.05, and the between-arm comparison is P = 0.11. The authors do note the between-arm result is only a tendency and the gain is of minor clinical importance, but still describe it as a 'statistically significant improvement'.

issues.title: 'Double-blind' trial whose control arm received no placebo, with subjective symptom outcomes
issues.explanation: The design is called double-blind, but the control group is described as breathing exercises only, with no placebo capsule. Patients taking a daily supplement know they are receiving it. Subjective outcomes, such as post-exertional malaise and fatigue, favour the open-label supplement arm through expectation effects. The post-exertional malaise advantage cannot be attributed to creatine itself.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that a matching placebo was given to the control arm.

quotes.text: double-blind parallel-group design (1:1)
breathing exercises only (control group)

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the trial double-blind but describes a control arm receiving breathing exercises only, with no placebo or masking procedure reported, so participants appear to have known their allocation. This matters most for the subjective outcomes (VAS symptoms, post-exertional malaise P = 0.03, MFI-20), which are open to expectation effects; the MRS and treadmill outcomes are less affected. Whether assessors were blinded cannot be determined from the paper.

issues.title: Within-arm creatine rises reported at P = 0.01-0.04 have 95% CIs spanning zero (e.g. 3.9 mM, CI -4.9 to 12.7)
issues.explanation: Three of the six significant within-arm creatine increases (vastus medialis, thalamus, left parietal gray matter) have 95% CIs that include zero. Two others, right precentral white matter and right paracentral gray matter, also include zero. Their printed P-values do not match those intervals. The six "significant" locations that headline the brain-creatine claim are therefore unreliable as reported. The same problem affects the time-to-exhaustion CI. This covers the CI/p mismatches in c7.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw individual data or a stated test showing the printed P-values are correct, and corrected CIs.

quotes.text: vastus medialis muscle (mean change 3.9 mM, 95% CI from - 4.9 to  12.7; P = 0.04)
thalamus (0.9 mM, 95% CI from - 0.8 to 2.6; P = 0.03)
left parietal messial gray matter (1.8 mM, 95% CI from - 2.0 to  5.6; P = 0.01)

script.explanation: the p-value recovered from the CI is 0.3851 (reachable range [0.3763, 0.3939] across the printed precision of the estimate and its bounds), but p = 0.04 is reported -- this recovery inverts a WALD interval, so if the paper used a bootstrap, exact, profile-likelihood or Fieller interval the two numbers are not comparable; confirm the method before treating this as a finding; the CI includes the null (0.0), but the reported p = 0.04 says the result is significant

second_reader.what_stands: All six reported creatine rises in the creatine arm have 95% CIs that include zero, yet are reported at P = 0.01-0.04 and described as significant. With n = 4 the printed CIs imply P values far above 0.05, so the P values and CIs cannot both be correct as printed; the paper gives no explanation.

issues.title: About 14 brain sites plus symptom and fatigue outcomes tested without correction; nominal P = 0.01-0.04 headlined
issues.explanation: Table 1 reports interaction P-values for 14 creatine locations, 5 MFI-20 scales, 3 symptoms and time to exhaustion, with no multiplicity adjustment and no single prespecified primary outcome. The between-group creatine claims depend on four brain sites with nominal P of 0.01 to 0.03, which would not survive correction. With n = 8, one or two sites at P < 0.05 is what chance alone would be expected to produce.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome with an adjustment strategy, or adjusted p-values that remain below 0.05.

quotes.text: outcompetes breathing exercises in alleviating post-exertional malaise and improving brain creatine levels at 3-month follow-up
The participants from the study group experienced an increase in tissue total creatine levels for all 14 locations evaluated in the present study

second_reader.what_stands: The paper tests about 23 outcomes (14 creatine sites plus symptom, exercise and fatigue measures) at nominal P < 0.05 with no stated correction, and headlines P = 0.01-0.04 results; none of the between-arm P values would survive a Bonferroni threshold. The Discussion does call for larger studies but does not flag multiplicity.

issues.title: Title says creatine plus breathing reduces respiratory discomfort, but discomfort fell to 0 in both arms (P = 0.57)
issues.explanation: The title implies creatine contributes to reduced respiratory discomfort. The Results report that breathing difficulty and respiratory discomfort were reduced to zero in both groups, so any improvement is equally attributable to breathing exercises alone. The between-arm test for breathing difficulties was nonsignificant. The title's claim about the creatine contribution is unsupported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A between-arm analysis showing a creatine-specific reduction in respiratory discomfort.

quotes.text: Creatine supplementation combined with breathing exercises reduces respiratory discomfort and improves creatine status in patients with long-COVID
Breathing difficulty and respiratory discomfort were reduced to zero in both groups at 3-month follow-up.

second_reader.what_stands: Respiratory discomfort fell to 0 in both arms (interaction P = 0.57 for breathing difficulties, 0.11 for chest pain), so the data give no evidence that creatine added to the reduction. The title's claim that creatine plus breathing exercises 'reduces respiratory discomfort' is only true in the trivial sense that the control arm's breathing exercises did the same, and the paper has no no-exercise arm to show the exercise effect either.

issues.title: Table 1 marks control-arm 'Reduced motivation' (16.0 to 13.0) significant, text says no MFI-20 change
issues.explanation: The Results state that no MFI-20 sub-domain changed significantly. Table 1 marks the control arm's reduced-motivation score at 3 months with a dagger, defined as P < 0.05 versus baseline. One of the two statements is wrong. This affects a secondary outcome and, if anything, a control-arm result, so it does not inflate the creatine effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Evidence that the dagger is a typographical error, or that the text refers only to between-arm tests.

quotes.text: No significant changes in MFI-20 test sub-domains were found throughout the study

quotes.location: Table 1, Reduced motivation, Breathing exercises, 3 months

issues.title: Baseline creatine differs between arms at several sites (e.g. right parietal 6.0 vs 8.2 mM); method not described
issues.explanation: Randomisation and allocation concealment are not described, and baseline brain creatine differs between arms at several sites. The control arm's larger baseline at some sites (e.g. right frontal gray 7.9 vs 6.6) also raises regression to the mean as an alternative explanation for the control-arm drops. Change scores in four patients per arm are sensitive to this, though the paper's interaction test partly addresses it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of a valid random sequence and an analysis adjusted for baseline showing the same group differences.

quotes.text: Right parietal messial gray matter
randomized controlled pilot trial

issues.title: No trial registration or registered outcomes reported for the extension arm
issues.explanation: The paper gives no registration number and defers methods to the original trial. Without a registered primary outcome, the choice of which of the 14 sites or other outcomes to emphasise cannot be checked. The parent trial may be registered, so this is a disclosure gap rather than a demonstrated problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registration record for the extension that lists the same outcomes.

quotes.text: Detailed information about the study methods and testing protocols is available in  the  original trial.
Here, we conducted an extension arm of the original trial

issues.title: Supplier-funded trial of its product; funder's role in design and analysis not stated
issues.explanation: The creatine product comes from a company that co-funded the work, and the senior author reports an advisory role with that company's creatine division and a creatine patent. These are declared, but there is no statement about the funder's role in design, analysis or reporting. Combined with the positive framing of weak results, readers should weigh this.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the funders had no role in design, analysis or reporting.

quotes.text: creatine monohydrate (Creavitalis; AlzChem Group AG, Trostberg, Germany)
SMO serves as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board on creatine in health and medicine (AlzChem LLC).

10.4149/bll_2023_013.headline_claim: Mountain spa rehabilitation was beneficial for clinical symptoms, and ubiquinol supplementation during rehabilitation (MRQ) increased CoQ10 and reduced symptoms and mitochondrial dysfunction more than rehabilitation alone.
10.4149/bll_2023_013.overall: The biochemical finding that ubiquinol raises blood, plasma and platelet CoQ10 is supported by large, clear differences, although several table and text figures are inconsistent. The clinical claims (rehabilitation benefit 'proven', ubiquinol reducing symptoms more, improved organ bioenergetics) are not supported by an uncontrolled, untested 36-patient before/after comparison with undescribed allocation and retrospective registration.

primary_outcome.name: Not designated in the paper; clinical symptoms (questionnaire) and CoQ10 concentration are both emphasised

issues.title: Rehabilitation benefit declared 'proven' from uncontrolled, untested before/after symptom counts
issues.explanation: Both arms received the same rehabilitation, so improvement in symptoms cannot be separated from natural recovery over time. No test is reported for the symptom changes, and only 30 of 36 patients (20/22 and 10/14) completed the questionnaire. The healthy controls provide no information about symptoms. 'Proven' is not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated or usual-care control group in which symptoms did not improve over the same period.

quotes.text: clinical symptoms of the patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome was proven
Paired Student´s ttests were used for the evaluation of

second_reader.what_stands: The conclusion says the beneficial effect of rehabilitation on clinical symptoms was 'proven', but the evidence is an uncontrolled before/after comparison of symptom counts in 10 and 20 respondents. No symptom test is shown, and no comparison group without rehabilitation exists. Spontaneous recovery after COVID-19, regression to the mean and reporting bias cannot be separated from a rehabilitation effect, and some MR-arm symptoms did not change at all.

issues.title: Conclusion claims improved organ bioenergetics and reduced oxidative stress; no such data shown, TBARS p = 0.10
issues.explanation: The Conclusion says ubiquinol decreased oxidative stress and improved bioenergetics of organs. The only oxidative-stress marker, TBARS, fell non-significantly (p = 0.10), and platelet respiration data are not presented, only cited from a conference abstract. 'Organs' also goes beyond platelet measurements. Registered primary outcomes of lung function and platelet bioenergetics are absent from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Presentation of the platelet respiration and lung-function results with between-group tests supporting the claim, and a significant TBARS reduction.

quotes.text: the bioenergetics of organs was improved
slightly decreased after MRQ (to 92.8 %, p = 0.10)
quotes.location: Results, whole blood and plasma paragraph

quotes.text: Our preliminary results showed that platelet mitochondrial Complex I-linked

second_reader.what_stands: The Conclusion says ubiquinol decreased oxidative stress, but the only supporting number is a non-significant TBARS change (p = 0.10, a 7.2% fall from a baseline already at control level). It also says bioenergetics 'of organs' improved, although this paper presents no bioenergetic data and measured only platelets, relying on cited abstracts for the OXPHOS result. The CoQ10 increases in blood, plasma and platelets are, however, supported by Table 2.

issues.title: Ubiquinol symptom advantage asserted from per-arm before/after percentages; no between-group test, n=20 vs 10
issues.explanation: The Discussion says symptoms improved more markedly with ubiquinol than with rehabilitation alone. The only comparison is of before/after percentages within each arm in Table 1. No MRQ-versus-MR test and no significance test for the symptom data are reported, and the baseline symptom burden differs between arms. The unpaired tests described in the Methods compare patients with healthy controls. The superiority claim is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified between-group analysis (e.g. ANCOVA adjusted for baseline) showing a significant MRQ vs MR difference.

quotes.text: have been improved more markedly after the mountain rehabilitation with ubiquinol supplementation (MRQ) as compared to MR alone (Tab. 1).
The effect of MR without ubiquinol supplementation was not noted in clinical symptoms

second_reader.what_stands: The claim that symptoms improved more with ubiquinol rests only on separate before/after percentages in arms of 20 and 10 patients, with no between-arm test or adjustment for baseline. For several symptoms (fatigue, muscle and joint pain, difficulty breathing, headache) the MR arm changed as much as or more than the MRQ arm, so the blanket statement is not even descriptively uniform. The MRQ muscle and joint pain baseline is also reported inconsistently between text (50%) and table (55%).

issues.title: Plasma beta-carotene: MR and MRQ cells share identical means and p-values; MR2 SEM 0.171 exceeds its mean 0.140
issues.explanation: In Table 2 the plasma beta-carotene means for MR1 and MRQ1 (0.208) and for MR2 and MRQ2 (0.140) are identical, with identical p-values, although the groups differ in size and SEM. The MR2 SEM of 0.171 is larger than its own mean and is incompatible with p=0.002 versus control. At least one set of cells appears to be a transcription error. The effect on conclusions is limited, as the paper states ubiquinol did not affect beta-carotene.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data confirming the identical means and p-values in both groups, and an SEM of 0.171 for MR2.

quotes.location: Table 2, plasma beta-carotene row, MR2 column
Table 2, plasma beta-carotene row, MRQ1 column

issues.title: Allocation to MRQ or MR not described (22 vs 14); baseline muscle/joint pain differs 55 % vs 100 %
issues.explanation: The paper never states how patients were assigned to ubiquinol or no ubiquinol. Group sizes are unequal and baseline symptom prevalence differs. Without a described allocation method, the ubiquinol-versus-rehabilitation-alone comparison could be confounded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol or CONSORT description of the randomization sequence and concealment.

quotes.text: They were divided into two groups

issues.title: Muscle and joint pain at MRQ1: text says 50 %, Table 1 gives 11/20 = 55 %
issues.explanation: The Results text reports baseline muscle and joint pain in the ubiquinol group as 50 %. Table 1 gives 11 of 20 patients, which is 55 %. The text figure is wrong or the table count is. The error is small and does not change the direction of the finding.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Patient-level data showing 10 of 20 patients with muscle and joint pain at baseline.

quotes.text: Muscle and joint pain decreased from 50 % to 20 %

issues.title: Trial registered retrospectively (registry first submitted 2022-01-03; enrolment May-June 2021)
issues.explanation: The paper cites a registry ID without a date, and enrolment is stated as May-June 2021. The registry shows first submission in January 2022, after the study had begun. This limits confidence that outcomes and analyses were set in advance, and the paper does not disclose the retrospective timing.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registration record, or a protocol with a dated outcome list, from before enrolment.

quotes.text: Study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05178225.
In May and June 2021, 36

issues.title: Control platelet alpha-tocopherol: 2546.5 in text vs 2456.5 in Table 2
issues.explanation: The Results text and Table 2 give different control values for platelet alpha-tocopherol. The digits appear transposed. Either way the baseline MRQ1 value of 6020.0 is far above control, so the conclusion is unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected version showing the same value in both places.

quotes.location: Results, platelet CoQ10 and tocopherols paragraph
Table 2, platelet alpha-tocopherol row, Control column

issues.title: Platelet CoQ10 '+68 %' is labelled versus control but matches the MRQ1 baseline; vs control is ~+95 %
issues.explanation: The text attributes the +68 % rise to a comparison with control values. Table 2 gives a control of 84.1 and an MRQ1 baseline of 97.5. The +68 % corresponds to the within-group change from MRQ1 to MRQ2. Relative to control the rise would be about 95 %, so the stated comparator is mislabelled and the effect against control is understated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the percentage is relative to MRQ1, with control comparison reported separately.

quotes.text: as compared to control values (+68 %, p < 0.0001)

issues.title: Blood CoQ10 rise given as +194 % in Results and 192 % in Discussion (printed means imply +193 %)
issues.explanation: The same increase in whole-blood CoQ10 is reported as 194 % in the Results and 192 % in the Discussion. The printed means (0.399 to 1.17) imply about 193 %. This is a rounding-level inconsistency and nothing depends on it.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Unrounded group means giving the same percentage that both passages could be rounded from.

quotes.location: Results, whole blood and plasma CoQ10

quotes.text: (by 192 and 232 %, respectively)
quotes.location: Discussion, CoQ10 in whole blood and plasma paragraph

10.4235/agmr.24.0175.headline_claim: Slow deep breathing exercise significantly improves cardiopulmonary function, physical performance, and various health markers in older adult patients with long COVID.
10.4235/agmr.24.0175.overall: The physiological findings for blood pressure, HRV and 6MWT are supported by interaction tests and blinded assessors, but this is a small, single-site, unregistered, unblinded-participant trial with about 40 uncorrected outcomes and no sham control. The symptom and several biochemical or stress claims are weaker than the abstract conclusion states, and the stress-index directions are contradictory between sections. The headline of broad, definite benefit should be treated as tentative.

primary_outcome.name: Long COVID symptom burden (GEE: fatigue, cough, joint pain, memory, smell, sleep, anxiety)

issues.title: Unblinded participants and no attention/sham control; self-reported symptoms and effort-dependent tests vulnerable
issues.explanation: Participants knew their arm, and the control group simply continued usual routines with no sham or attention comparator. Long COVID symptoms were collected by asking participants whether they had experienced each symptom, which is open to expectation and reporting bias. The between-group symptom effects are marginal (p 0.031 to 0.046), so a modest bias could change them. Effort-dependent tests carry a similar risk. The symptom-reduction claim is therefore weaker than stated.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A sham or attention-control arm, or symptom data collected by a blinded rater with a validated instrument, showing the same effect.

quotes.text: while participants knew their assigned intervention
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Patients and Design

quotes.text: all participants were interviewed about long COVID symptoms with questions asking whether they had experienced any symptoms
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Clinical characteristics and anthropometry

quotes.text: The control group (n=30) maintained their usual daily routines for 8 weeks.

second_reader.what_stands: Participants were unblinded and the control group received no attention or sham intervention, so symptom reports (a yes/no interview) and effort-dependent tests (6MWT, strength, spirometry, respiratory pressures) are open to expectation and attention effects. The authors disclose the single-blind design, and several outcomes (blood pressure, assays, automated HRV) are objective, but the limitations section does not discuss the unblinding or the missing attention control. I did not verify whether the interviewer for symptoms was an assessor blinded to allocation; the paper does not say.

issues.title: ~40 outcomes tested with no primary outcome; between-group tests uncorrected, several p just under 0.05
issues.explanation: The study analysed cardiovascular, HRV, respiratory, pulmonary, performance, biochemical, oxidative and stress outcomes plus seven symptoms. Bonferroni correction is stated only for within-group repeated-measures comparisons. Between-group t-tests at each timepoint and the symptom GEE group effects have no stated correction. With this many tests, some of the marginal results are expected by chance, and the paper itself admits 'marginal statistical significance'.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified primary outcome and hierarchical testing plan, or adjusted p-values that still fall below 0.05 for the claimed effects.

quotes.text: Within-group differences were analyzed using one-way repeated measures ANOVA, with Bonferroni corrections for multiple comparisons.
Unpaired t-tests compared control and exercise groups at each time point.

second_reader.what_stands: About 40 outcomes were analysed with no designated primary outcome, the between-group time-point t-tests have no stated multiplicity correction, and several interaction and group p-values lie between 0.040 and 0.046. The Bonferroni correction applies only within groups, and the authors note marginal significance without addressing multiplicity. The interaction ANOVA is a single omnibus test per outcome, so the uncorrected exposure is smaller than a count of tests at every time point suggests, and the outcomes are correlated.

issues.title: Lipid, CAT, SOD and fatigue-index 'improvements' rest on within-group change; no group-time interaction reported
issues.explanation: For biochemical markers the only significant group-time interactions reported are FBS and MDA. Lipids, CAT and SOD are claimed as improved in the abstract and Discussion because they changed significantly in the exercise group but not in controls. A difference between 'significant' and 'not significant' is not itself a significant difference. The conclusion that the exercise improves 'various health markers' goes beyond what the between-group tests show. The same applies to fatigue index.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary Table S5 showing significant between-group differences or interactions for TC, TG, LDL, HDL, CAT and SOD.

quotes.text: In contrast, no significant changes were found in the control group.
A significant group-time interaction was observed by FBS (F=8.46, p=0.000) (Fig. 4A).
quotes.location: Results, Biochemical and Oxidative Stress Markers

second_reader.what_stands: For TC, TG, LDL, HDL, CAT, SOD and the fatigue index, the main text reports only within-exercise-group changes and no group-by-time interaction, while the abstract and conclusion present them as improvements attributable to the intervention. Interactions are reported only for FBS and MDA (biochemical) and stress resistance and stress index (stress). The supplementary tables, which I could not see, may contain the missing interaction tests.

issues.title: Stress outcomes: direction contradicts across sections; fatigue-index fall (lower = more fatigue) read as benefit
issues.explanation: The Results say stress resistance and the fatigue index both significantly 'reduced'. The Methods define higher stress resistance as better and a lower fatigue index as more fatigue. The Discussion then says stress resistance rose and treats the fall in the fatigue index as a reduction in stress. At least one of these statements has the wrong direction, so the claimed stress benefit is not established as printed. The fatigue index also has no reported significant group-time interaction.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Supplementary Table S6 showing the stress resistance mean rising and the fatigue index mean rising (or the index being scaled opposite to the Methods definition).

quotes.text: Significant reductions were observed in the exercise group for stress resistance (F=4.31, p=0.018), stress index (F=5.86, p=0.005), and fatigue index (F=4.61, p=0.014)
where lower values indicate higher fatigue levels
quotes.location: Methods, Heart rate variability and stress parameters

quotes.text: a decrease in both the stress index and fatigue index, indicating a reduction in stress levels

issues.title: Randomized trial with no registry identifier or pre-specified primary outcome reported
issues.explanation: The paper describes a randomized controlled trial and gives an ethics approval number, but no trial registration. There is no declared primary outcome, and the sample size is based on a different study's SD. Selective reporting among about 40 outcomes cannot be excluded.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prospective registry entry listing the same primary outcome and analysis plan.

quotes.text: This study utilized a randomized control trial design.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Patients and Design

issues.title: Respiratory interaction p-values (F=2.54-2.87, p=0.040-0.041) look too small for the F values
issues.explanation: Several group-time interaction tests are reported as significant at p about 0.04 with F between 2.5 and 2.9. For a 3-timepoint, 60-participant design the 5% critical F is about 3.07, so these F values would give p of roughly 0.06 to 0.08. The p-values are also not ordered consistently with F across rows. If the F values are right, the PEF, FEF25-75% and PImaxFRC interactions are not significant. The degrees of freedom are not printed, so this cannot be settled from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Printed degrees of freedom or a stated df correction under which F=2.54 and 2.87 correspond to p of about 0.04.

quotes.location: Results, Respiratory Muscle Strength and Pulmonary Function

quotes.text: PImaxFRC (F=2.87, p=0.041) (Fig. 2A)
quotes.location: Results, Respiratory Muscle Strength and Pulmonary Function

script.explanation: The printed f = 2.54 supports p no smaller than 0.0824524, but the paper reports p = 0.04 -- more significance than the statistic earns at its printed precision.

10.4236/ojtr.2025.133013.headline_claim: A post-COVID rehabilitation service has a significant positive impact on long COVID symptoms and real-world functioning, with significant improvements in symptom severity, functional disability and usual activities.
10.4236/ojtr.2025.133013.overall: The headline claim that the service has a significant positive impact is not supported by this design: it is an uncontrolled, open-label, self-reported before-after study of 21-30 completers with an unknown denominator and no multiplicity handling. The reported symptom-severity and functional-disability improvements are modest and borderline after correction, and a few numeric typos (t = 6.838, 47.52%, p = 0.61) are minor. The data are best read as descriptive change in service users, not evidence of effectiveness.

primary_outcome.name: Not specified as a single primary outcome; C-19 YRS symptom severity and functional disability and EQ-5D-5L usual activities are the significant results

issues.title: Uncontrolled, open-label before-after data used to claim the service causes improvement
issues.explanation: All tests compare the same patients at baseline and 12 weeks, with no comparison group, blinding or between-group analysis. Natural recovery, regression to the mean, concurrent treatments and expectation effects in self-reported scores could each produce the observed change. The abstract and conclusions nonetheless state that the service has a positive impact and is effective, and the discussion says it 'enabled' improvements. This is a main-conclusion problem. The data can describe change over time, not service effect.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent or waiting-list control group showing a between-group difference, or wording limiting the conclusion to descriptive change in service users.

quotes.text: There was no control group, the sample size was small, and the treatment was open-label and adjunct to any existing treatments or therapies.
The results show that a post-COVID rehabilitation service can have a significant positive impact on symptoms of long COVID and real-world functioning.
had enabled improvements in patients' ability to get about

second_reader.what_stands: The data are uncontrolled, open-label before-after measurements, and the Abstract, Discussion and Section 5.2 use causal wording ('can have a significant positive impact', 'had enabled improvements', 'are effective') that a single-arm design with no comparison group cannot support, since regression to the mean, natural recovery and concurrent treatments are not separable. This is partly mitigated because the authors list the lack of a control group, small sample and open-label design as limitations and call for more evidence on long-term effectiveness. The mobility claim in the Discussion is a

issues.title: Only 21-30 completers analysed from an unknown referral base; no sample-size rationale
issues.explanation: The analysis uses 21 EQ-5D-5L and 30 C-19 YRS paired datasets from a convenience sample, with no predetermined sample size and no record of how many were excluded or lost. Patients with both baseline and follow-up data may differ from those who dropped out, which could inflate the apparent benefit. The confident conclusion is not supported by estimates this unstable and potentially selected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data showing that the analysed completers were a representative or complete cohort of service users in the study period.

quotes.text: There was no predetermined sample size.
Numbers excluded and reasons were not recorded.

second_reader.what_stands: Only 21 (EQ-5D-5L) and 30 (C-19 YRS) complete-case participants were analysed, with no stated sample-size rationale, and the paper records neither the number referred or enrolled nor the numbers and reasons for exclusion, so the completer proportion and risk of selection or attrition bias cannot be assessed. Absence of a predetermined sample size is ordinary for a retrospective service evaluation and the small sample is acknowledged as a limitation, but the unknown referral base and attrition are not addressed.

issues.title: Mobility called an improvement (abstract, discussion) despite p = 0.407 and a thin level shift
issues.explanation: The abstract and discussion state that mobility improved and that the service enabled better ability to get about. The only mobility test in Table 2 is non-significant (p = 0.407, d = 0.185), and the text itself describes all non-usual-activities EQ-5D-5L changes as non-significant. The claim rests on a descriptive shift in level counts in a sample of 21, with no test. The claim is not supported.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A significant test of mobility change, or discussion wording limited to a descriptive, non-significant shift.

quotes.text: The improvements in mobility (walking about) indicate that the post-COVID rehabilitation service had enabled improvements

issues.title: Nine within-group tests with no correction; 'significant' findings at p = 0.049, 0.013 and 0.006
issues.explanation: Six EQ-5D-5L and three C-19 YRS outcomes were each tested at 0.05 with no adjustment or declared primary outcome. After a Bonferroni correction for nine tests, none of the three significant results is clearly significant, and the usual-activities finding at p = 0.049 is the most fragile. This weakens the secondary findings, and the symptom severity result is only borderline.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome or a stated correction showing the findings survive adjustment.

quotes.text: The only EQ-5D-5L dimension which saw a significant improvement was for 'usual activities', with a significant (p = 0.049)

issues.title: Health today t = 6.838 printed beside p = 0.874 and d = -0.035
issues.explanation: Table 2 gives t = 6.838 for the change in EQ-5D-5L health today, but the same row gives p = 0.874 and d = -0.035, and the text calls the change non-significant. A t of 6.838 with about 20 degrees of freedom would be highly significant. The p and d agree with a near-zero change, so the t is the likely misprint. Only this one cell is affected, and the conclusion is not changed.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A corrected table or dataset showing t = 6.838 is correct and p = 0.874 is the typo (very unlikely given the means).

quotes.text: non-significant (p = 0.874) increase in health today score

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.874, but recomputed from the printed t = 6.838 p is at most 1.205e-06, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show, and on the other side of alpha = 0.05 (a decision error). This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: r = 0.415 with n = 21 printed with p = 0.61; it implies p of about 0.06
issues.explanation: The correlation between baseline and follow-up EQ-5D-5L health today scores is given as r = 0.415 with p = 0.61. With 21 pairs this r corresponds to p of about 0.06, so the printed p appears to have lost a zero. The 'non-significant' label stands in both cases, but the p-value is misprinted.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different n for this correlation (about 5 pairs would give p of 0.61) which the paper does not suggest.

quotes.text: non-significant (p = 0.61) moderate positive correlation (r = 0.415)

script.explanation: The paper prints p = 0.61, but recomputed from the printed r = 0.415 p is at most 0.06173, allowing for the rounding of every printed input: the paper reports LESS significance than its own numbers show. This is a reporting inconsistency, not the over-claiming direction, and not evidence of fabrication.

issues.title: Table 1: 10 of 21 shown as 47.52% (White) and 47.62% (Not stated)
issues.explanation: Two rows each report 10 participants out of 21, but with different percentages. 10/21 is 47.62%, so the White row is a typographical error. Nothing depends on it, and the paper's conclusions are unaffected.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A different denominator for the White row, which is not supported by the 90.9% figure (10/11).

quotes.text: 10 (47.52%) (90.9% of those who stated their ethnicity)

script.explanation: 10/21 = 47.62%, but the paper prints 47.52, outside the rounding interval [47.52, 47.53]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 21.0 rather than 21.

10.46235/1028-7221-13492-atc.headline_claim: Topical application of a synthetic GM-CSF active-centre peptide (Acegram-spray) to the nasopharyngeal mucosa in post-COVID patients significantly influenced neutrophil NBT activity, increased the T-helper percentage and raised C3a, so the peptide appears to act mainly on innate immunity.
10.46235/1028-7221-13492-atc.overall: The conclusion that the peptide stimulates neutrophil NBT activity and mainly affects innate immunity rests on an uncontrolled before/after comparison in about 20 patients. Many parameters were tested without correction, and the test type is unclear (several p-values are not reproducible from the printed M±m). The data can at most generate hypotheses, not show efficacy or causation.

primary_outcome.name: NBT neutrophil spontaneous activity (no single primary outcome designated; several immune parameters tested)

issues.title: Single-arm before/after comparison supports causal 'stimulates' conclusion with no control group
issues.explanation: The same patients were measured before and after a 10-day peptide course, with no placebo or untreated comparator. Changes in NBT activity, T-helper share and C3a could reflect time since infection, assay variability or regression to the mean, and cannot be attributed to the peptide. Conclusion 1 nevertheless says the peptide 'stimulates' these measures and that it acts mainly on innate immunity.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent untreated or placebo group with the same measurements, or repeat pre-treatment baselines showing stable values.

quotes.text: Пептид активного центра ГМ-КСФ применялся по стандартной схеме 3 раза в день в течение 10 дней
стимулирует спонтанную и индуцированную НСТ-активность нейтрофилов

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm before/after comparison with no control or placebo group, yet Conclusion 1 states causally that the peptide 'stimulates' these parameters. The word 'randomized' is also used for what are in fact repeated measures in one cohort. The data show only that values were higher after the course, not that the peptide caused the rise.

issues.title: Test type for before/after data unstated; several p-values not reproducible from printed M±m
issues.explanation: The same patients are analysed as two comparison groups, and the Methods do not say the tests were paired. If unpaired tests were used, they ignore within-patient correlation. Using the printed means and errors, several p-values (spontaneous NBT intensity, spontaneous NBT activity, T-helpers) are smaller than an unpaired test would give. Whether they are valid depends on an unstated paired analysis.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that paired t or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used, with the per-patient data or paired SDs reproducing the printed p-values.

quotes.text: Использовали критерии Стьюдента при параметрических данных
Пациенты были разделены на 2 группы сравнения по гейтированию панлейкоцитарными маркерами

second_reader.what_stands: The Methods do not state whether the Student or Wilcoxon tests were paired, or which test was applied to which variable. Treated as unpaired comparisons of the printed M±m, three of the six p-values (spontaneous NBT activity, spontaneous NBT intensity, T helpers) come out larger than printed, and the intensity one is not significant (p about 0.12). Only a paired analysis with moderate-to-high within-patient correlation, which is not reported, could explain them, so they cannot be confirmed from the paper. The other three (induced activity, induced intensity, C3a) are consistent with the printe

issues.title: Many immune parameters tested with no primary outcome or multiplicity correction; only significant ones shown
issues.explanation: Well over a dozen outcomes were tested in about 20 patients at p<0.05. Only six significant results are tabulated, and the non-significant ones are not shown. With this many tests, a few p-values below 0.05 are expected by chance, and several of the printed ones are borderline (p<0.05, p<0.03). The 'innate immunity' conclusion rests on these selected results.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified primary outcome list or a multiplicity-adjusted analysis in which the NBT and C3a findings remain significant.

quotes.text: Остальные показатели иммунной системы не имели достоверных отличий.
These findings indicate that the synthetic peptide primarily affects innate immunity factors.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper tests dozens of immune parameters with no stated primary outcome or multiplicity adjustment, tabulates only the significant ones, and draws the mechanistic conclusion that the peptide acts mainly on innate immunity from them. The text does mention that other parameters did not differ, but their values are not shown. The claim of no effect on T, B and NK cells rests on non-significance in about 21 patients with no control group.

issues.title: Patient number is 21 in Abstract and Table 1 but 20 in Methods (n = 20 per group)
issues.explanation: The Abstract and both Table 1 headers give 21 patients. The Methods say 20 patients were examined and give n = 20 for both the before and after groups. The paper does not say which number was analysed, so the denominators behind the p-values are uncertain.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A flow statement showing 21 enrolled and 20 analysed, or a correction of the Methods or Table 1 count.

quotes.text: A total of 21 patients who previously suffered with SARS-CoV-2 infection were included in the study.
Было обследовано 20 пациентов

issues.title: Prospective peptide treatment study reports ethics approval but no trial registration
issues.explanation: Patients received an intervention under a protocol, but no registry entry or prespecified outcomes are reported. This leaves the primary outcome and analysis plan unverifiable. Whether registration was required cannot be settled from the paper.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A registry entry with prespecified outcomes, or a statement that registration was not required.

quotes.text: были одобрены Независимым локальным этическим комитетом

issues.title: Groups called 'randomised' although the same patients are compared before and after treatment
issues.explanation: The Methods say the groups were randomised by sex, age and comorbidity using chi-square. The two groups are the same patients before and after treatment, so there was no random allocation. The wording could make readers think the study had a randomised comparison.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of random allocation to treatment arms.

quotes.text: Группы были рандомизированы по полу, возрасту, сопутствующим заболеваниям по критерию

10.46607/iamj09p5022021.headline_claim: iWALL Tablet is safe and effective in Mild Post COVID Syndrome, with statistically significant symptom reduction.
10.46607/iamj09p5022021.overall: The paper's conclusion that the tablet is safe and highly effective cannot be relied on. It rests on a single-arm, open-label, 25-patient before/after comparison of self-rated symptoms, with no control and no adverse-event data. Table 2's test statistics are also internally inconsistent, so only the observed improvement itself can be taken at face value.

primary_outcome.name: Symptom scores (fatigue, myalgia, cough, sore throat, shortness of breath) before vs after 12 weeks of treatment

issues.title: Efficacy inferred from single-group before/after change in subjective scores, with no control
issues.explanation: All 25 patients received the tablet and were compared with their own baseline scores. The only inference is the within-group before/after t-values, so any improvement cannot be separated from spontaneous recovery, which the introduction itself says is common. Nor can it be separated from placebo or expectancy effects, since the study was open-label with self-rated symptoms. The efficacy conclusion is therefore not supported by this design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent placebo or active control arm, or a between-group comparison in the paper.

quotes.text: Number of Groups: Single.
shows that i WALL Tablet is effective in reducing all subjective parameters

second_reader.what_stands: The paper infers efficacy from before/after change in a single uncontrolled group of 25 on subjective symptom scores. Spontaneous recovery, regression to the mean and placebo effects cannot be separated from any drug effect. The Table 2 t-scores do not reproduce from the printed means and SEs and do not appear to test the before/after change, so the 'statistically significant' claim is not supported by the printed analysis either.

issues.title: 'Safe and effective' / 'highly effective' conclusion from 25 uncontrolled patients with no adverse-event data
issues.explanation: The conclusion and discussion state the tablet is safe and highly effective. The safety claim rests on a single sentence with no adverse-event definition, monitoring plan or results. The efficacy claim rests on within-group score changes in 25 patients. The wording is much stronger than a small open-label case series can support.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A prespecified safety assessment with reported adverse-event data, plus controlled efficacy evidence.

quotes.text: effective in Mild Post COVID Syndrome
does not show any adverse effect in patients

second_reader.what_stands: The 'safe and effective' and 'highly effective' conclusions rest on 25 uncontrolled patients, and no adverse-event data are presented, only an assertion of none. The sample could not exclude adverse events occurring in roughly 1 in 8 patients or fewer. The efficacy conclusion also depends on the uncontrolled before/after comparison described in i3.

issues.title: Symptom outcomes use an unvalidated, locally defined 0-4 grading with no rater or blinding details
issues.explanation: Outcomes are a researcher-defined severity grading for each symptom, with no reference to validation or reliability. The paper does not say who scored the patients or whether scoring was blinded. Combined with the open-label single-arm design, the size of the score changes cannot be benchmarked.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A citation showing the scales are validated, or a statement that scoring was by a blinded assessor.

quotes.text: analyzed and rated as per scoring pattern of mild, moderate and severe symptoms as follows

issues.title: Table 2: t-scores do not match means/SEs, and Sore Throat AT mean 0.02 is impossible for 25 integer scores
issues.explanation: The printed 't' values (about 61-104) cannot be reproduced from the printed mean and SE (e.g. 3.28/0.18 is about 18). The test used is never defined, so these values cannot be interpreted. The post-treatment sore-throat mean of 0.02 would need a total score of 0.5 across 25 patients, which is impossible. It is also inconsistent with an SD of 0.41. The significance conclusion probably survives, but the reported statistics are unreliable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A stated test definition that reproduces the printed t-values, and a corrected Sore Throat AT mean (e.g. 0.32).

quotes.text: Sore Throat AT

issues.title: Poor response: 4 patients (20%) in text vs 05 patients (20%) in Table 3
issues.explanation: The results paragraph says 4 patients had a poor response, while Table 3 says 5. Only 5 of 25 gives 20%, and 12+8+5 = 25, whereas 12+8+4 = 24. The text figure is a wrong count that does not change any conclusion.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: One patient being excluded from the text count for a stated reason, with 20% computed on a different base.

quotes.text: 4 patients (20%) shows poor response
Poor Response

script.explanation: 4/25 = 16.00%, but the paper prints 20, outside the rounding interval [19.50, 21.00]. The printed percentage implies a denominator of about 20.0 rather than 25.

issues.title: Publication date 'January 2020' precedes receipt (08/02/2021) and acceptance (11/02/2021)
issues.explanation: The header says the article was published online in January 2020, but it was received in February 2021 and cites sources accessed in January 2021. The date is almost certainly a typographical error. It affects no result.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A journal record showing a January 2020 online publication date.

quotes.text: ( Published online: January 2020)

10.47026/2413-4864-2022-2-1-8.headline_claim: Neurobiofeedback training with the Neuro V system (alpha-band stimulation, 8-14 Hz) is effective for rehabilitating people with emotional disorders after COVID-19 and is recommended for use.
10.47026/2413-4864-2022-2-1-8.overall: The favourable direction of change in the trained group is plausible, but the efficacy and 'recommended for use' conclusion is not supported by this design: allocation is undescribed, the control got no training, outcomes are unblinded self-reports, and the baselines differed. The statistics also contain inconsistencies (mean age, ± labelling, p-values that do not fit the printed means), and the authors' possible commercial interest is not declared.

primary_outcome.name: No single primary outcome named; stress (PSM-25), state and trait anxiety (Spielberger-Khanin) and depression questionnaire were all reported

issues.title: Efficacy and recommendation for clinical use drawn from 40 non-randomised, unblinded participants
issues.explanation: The conclusion calls the technology 'effective' and 'recommended for use' in rehabilitation. This rests on 40 people (24 vs 16), an undescribed allocation, a no-training control and self-report questionnaires, with no sample-size justification and no limitations discussed. The design supports at most a preliminary signal.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Randomised, adequately powered evidence or conclusions explicitly framed as preliminary.

quotes.text: является эффективным и рекомендуется к использованию
The study involved 40 people (27 women and 13 men)

second_reader.what_stands: The paper bases an unqualified recommendation for clinical use on 40 participants, with no stated randomisation, no blinding, self-reported outcomes, and a group imbalance in age. No limitations are weighed in the conclusion, so the recommendation goes beyond what this design can support.

issues.title: Table 4 p-values and ± labels do not fit the printed means: depression endpoint not significant, baselines differ
issues.explanation: Methods define the ± term as the standard error of the mean, but the Table 4 values only make sense as SDs, because for 24 people an SE of 26.6 would imply an SD of about 130 on a bounded scale. Taking them as SDs, the endpoint depression difference (58.4 vs 65.1) gives t of about 1.4 and p of about 0.18, not <0.05. Several baseline differences that the paper calls non-significant come out around p of 0.002 to 0.04, which weakens the claim that the groups were comparable.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Raw data or the exact test used showing p<0.05 at the depression endpoint and p>0.05 at the baselines.

quotes.text: разность по сравнению с показателями в контрольной группе достоверны
среднюю ошибку средней арифметической ( m )

script.explanation: The reported statistics fit NEITHER Welch's nor Student's t-test on these group statistics, under either tail convention, allowing for rounding of the printed inputs.

second_reader.what_stands: The printed means and ± values do not reproduce Table 4's p-values. The depression endpoint difference (65.1 vs 58.4) is not significant on any reading (t about 1.4, p about 0.18) although it is starred as p<0.05.
