10.7759/cureus.76148.headline_claim: This pilot study successfully demonstrated the feasibility, safety, and tolerability of using omega-3 supplements for the treatment of long COVID syndrome.
10.7759/cureus.76148.overall: The feasibility description is largely descriptive and honest about the absence of significant symptom effects, but the Conclusions overreach: safety for 'treatment' is asserted from a tiny, high-attrition trial, and the AA:EPA 'pronounced decline' is untested and internally contradictory in direction. Reliable takeaways are limited to recruitment and retention figures and the lack of a detectable symptom difference.

primary_outcome.name: Long COVID symptoms at 12 weeks (shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, lack of taste, lack of smell); the stated primary objective is feasibility, which is not tested between arms

primary_outcomes.measure: Feasibility Study for Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation v. Placebo in Adult Patients to Limit Long Covid Syndrome - Compliance as Captured by the Number of Participants Who Remain Compliant for the Whole Duration of the Study by Taking All Pills Daily

Feasibility Study for Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation v. Placebo in Adult Patients to Limit Long Covid Syndrome - Recruitment as Illustrated by the Number of Screen Failures (Potential Participants Approached But Not Interested in Participating).
primary_outcomes.time_frame: 6 months recruitment efforts (starting on actual study start date)

primary_outcomes.measure: Feasibility Study for Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplementation v. Placebo in Adult Patients to Limit Long Covid Syndrome - Retention as Illustrated by the Number of Participants That Initiate But do Not Complete the Study.

issues.title: Safety/tolerability 'demonstrated' for treating long COVID from 18 completers, 1 vs 5 adverse events, no power basis
issues.explanation: The Conclusions say the pilot successfully demonstrated safety and tolerability of omega-3 for the treatment of long COVID. The trial had no sample-size basis, no symptom benefit, and only 1 versus 5 adverse events among 16 per arm, with no intervals. The dosing and 12-week exposure support at most a preliminary signal of tolerability. The headline wording overstates what 32 randomized participants can show.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Pre-specified feasibility and safety thresholds that were met, with precision estimates, and wording limited to pilot feasibility.

quotes.text: This pilot study successfully demonstrated the feasibility, safety, and tolerability of using omega-3 supplements for the treatment of long COVID syndrome.
Our sample size was significantly small and insufficient to demonstrate the efficacy of the omega-3 supplement.

second_reader.what_stands: The descriptive finding is real: no serious adverse events, and 1/16 versus 5/16 adverse events (p ≈ 0.17 by my calculation, not tested in the paper). A 32-person trial with no stated sample-size basis, 14 non-completers, and no efficacy signal cannot 'demonstrate' safety or treatment benefit. The Conclusions wording 'successfully demonstrated ... for the treatment of long COVID syndrome' goes beyond the data and sits uneasily with the authors' own Discussion statement that the sample was too small to show efficacy.

issues.title: Feasibility called successful despite 14/32 (43.8%) non-completion and no feasibility thresholds
issues.explanation: Only 18 of 32 randomized participants completed, and Table 2 excludes those lost to follow-up. Four placebo participants left because of side effects, which also bears on the tolerability comparison. No progression criteria were stated, so 'successfully demonstrated feasibility' cannot be judged against anything, and the retention figure arguably points to a feasibility problem.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A protocol pre-specifying retention and recruitment targets that this study met.

quotes.text: For this feasibility study, 32 participants were recruited, 14 dropped out, and 18 completed the study.
quotes.location: Materials and Methods, Participants and sample size

quotes.text: TABLE 2: Outcomes (excluding those lost to follow-up) at 12 weeks by treatment arm

second_reader.what_stands: The paper calls the study feasible and 'successful' although 43.8% of randomised participants did not complete it, and it states no prespecified thresholds for retention, recruitment or compliance. Compliance, a registry primary outcome, was not assessed. The reasons for 10 of the 14 dropouts are not given; only 4 placebo dropouts are attributed to side effects.

issues.title: AA:EPA 'pronounced decline' (11.4 vs 3.06) claimed with no between-group test, n = 6 vs 7, SDs 19.7 and 9.77
issues.explanation: The claim rests on comparing each arm's mean change in AA:EPA. No between-group test or confidence interval is given, and only 13 participants have blood data. A rough Welch comparison from the printed SDs gives a difference of 8.3 with SE about 8.9, so the difference is nowhere near distinguishable from zero. Medians even run differently (placebo -1.80, supplement 18.2) with wide ranges.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A reported between-group test or interval for the AA:EPA change excluding no difference.

quotes.text: The mean difference in the AA:EPA ratio in the placebo arm was 3.06, whereas the supplement group had 11.4, indicating a more pronounced decline in inflammatory markers in the supplement group.
The mean difference in the AA:EPA ratio in the placebo vs. supplement group showed a pronounced decline in inflammatory markers in the supplement group.

second_reader.what_stands: The words 'pronounced decline' rest on a difference in means (11.4 vs 3.06) that was not tested between groups, from 13 of 32 randomised participants. The interval from the printed summaries comfortably includes zero (about −12.5 to 29.2, p ≈ 0.38), the SDs are as large as or larger than the means, and the placebo arm also declined. The direction of the numbers is internally consistent, but the Discussion's 'lower ratio = higher inflammation' sentence is stated backwards.

issues.title: Discussion's supplement-arm SOB/cough/fatigue percentages (50/37.5/25%) differ from Table 2 (37.5/25/62.5%)
issues.explanation: The Discussion gives the share of supplement-arm participants still symptomatic as about 50%, 37.5% and 25% for SOB, cough and fatigue. Table 2 shows 37.5%, 25% and 62.5% for those rows. The fatigue discrepancy is the largest: the text says 25% still have fatigue, the table says 62.5%, which makes the supplement arm look better than its data. Taste and smell (50%) agree.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the Discussion refers to a different time point or population than Table 2.

quotes.text: In the supplement group, the percentage of participants still experiencing SOB, cough, fatigue, lack of taste, and lack of smell were about 50%, 37.5%, 25%, 50%, and 50%, respectively.

quotes.location: Table 2, Fatigue, 'I still experience this symptom' row, omega-3 column

issues.title: AA:EPA fall (23.1 to 11.8) called less inflammation after defining a lower ratio as more inflammation
issues.explanation: The Discussion states that a lower AA:EPA ratio represents higher inflammation. It then reads the supplement arm's fall in ratio as a decline in inflammatory markers. Both statements cannot be true, so a reader cannot tell which direction the authors consider favourable. The mechanistic rationale in the Introduction (more EPA displacing AA) implies the definition sentence is the one that is wrong.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A correction showing the definition sentence was meant as 'a higher ratio'.

quotes.text: A lower AA:EPA ratio represents higher inflammatory levels and is used as a marker of chronic inflammation [6].
indicating a more pronounced decline in inflammatory markers in the supplement group.

issues.title: Registered primary 'compliance' outcome not assessed or reported; recruitment and retention only descriptive
issues.explanation: The registry lists pill-taking compliance over 12 weeks, recruitment and retention as primary outcomes. The paper states adherence was not assessed, so the compliance measure is absent, and feasibility is judged without it. Symptom and blood outcomes are presented as secondary objectives, which fits the registry, but the safety, tolerability and AA:EPA claims in the Conclusions go beyond the registered primaries.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version in which compliance was not a primary outcome, or a reported pill-count compliance result.

quotes.text: Intervention adherence was not assessed
The primary objective of this study is to explore the feasibility of using omega-3 supplements vs. placebo among healthcare workers with long-term symptoms.

issues.title: Supplier and part-sponsor KD Pharma; role in design, analysis and reporting not stated
issues.explanation: KD Pharma supplied the supplement and placebo and partly sponsored the study. The paper does not say whether the company had any role in design, analysis or the decision to publish. The disclosure itself is present, so this is a minor transparency gap.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that the sponsor had no role in design, analysis or reporting.

quotes.text: This study was sponsored, in part, by KD Pharma, which also supplied the supplement and placebo free of charge.

issues.title: Enrollment dates differ: Oct 2021 to Mar 2023 versus opened Jan 2022 for 12 months
issues.explanation: The Methods give an enrollment period starting October 2021, while Recruitment says enrollment opened in January 2022 and stayed open 12 months. The two statements are not reconcilable as written, although the difference could reflect study period versus enrollment window. It is a minor reporting inconsistency.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Text defining the October 2021 to March 2023 span as the overall study period rather than enrollment.

quotes.text: The enrollment period was from October 2021 to March 2023.
After Institutional Review Board approval, the study opened for enrollment in January 2022 and remained open for 12 months.

10.7759/cureus.81530.headline_claim: Dual sympathetic blocks may be an effective intervention for alleviating sympathetically mediated symptoms in patients with PASC.
10.7759/cureus.81530.overall: The reported pre-post improvements may be real as descriptive observations, but this single-arm, open-label pilot with self-reported outcomes cannot show that the blocks caused them. The lead COMPASS-31 outcome is not among the registered primaries, and the mechanistic and 'demonstrates effectiveness' language goes beyond the data. The findings are hypothesis-generating only.

primary_outcome.name: Improvement in overall autonomic symptoms (COMPASS-31 total), orthostatic intolerance, pain interference, and pain scale

primary_outcomes.measure: Ability to participate in social roles and activities status

issues.title: Single-arm, open-label pilot with patient-reported outcomes only; no control, so effect cannot be attributed to blocks
issues.explanation: All participants received the blocks and were compared only with their own baseline. The outcomes (COMPASS-31, PROMIS-29, subjective improvement) are all self-reported by unblinded patients. Placebo and expectation effects, regression to the mean, and natural recovery are therefore not separable from any treatment effect. The paper concedes this in the limitations but still concludes that the study demonstrates effectiveness.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A concurrent sham or usual-care control arm, or blinded objective outcome measures showing the same change.

quotes.text: This is a prospective, open-label, non-randomized pilot study
as placebo effects and spontaneous recovery cannot be excluded
This study demonstrates that DSBs may be an effective intervention for alleviating sympathetically mediated symptoms in patients with PASC.

second_reader.what_stands: The study is a single-arm, open-label pilot using only self-reported outcomes, so any change cannot be attributed to the blocks themselves. The authors disclose this in the limitations, but the Conclusions still use the wording 'demonstrates' and 'effective', which is stronger than the design permits.

issues.title: Headline COMPASS-31 outcome not registered as primary; registered fatigue and sleep demoted to secondary
issues.explanation: The registry lists only PROMIS-29 items as primary outcomes (depression, anxiety, physical function, pain interference, fatigue, sleep, social roles). The paper makes autonomic symptoms and orthostatic intolerance, measured by COMPASS-31, its first primary outcome. It relabels registered primary fatigue and sleep as 'secondary', and calls pain intensity primary. The headline autonomic-benefit claim therefore rests on an outcome that was not pre-specified as primary in the available record.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: An earlier registry version, or the protocol, listing COMPASS-31 or orthostatic intolerance as a primary outcome before data collection.

quotes.text: The primary outcome was improvement in overall autonomic symptoms, orthostatic intolerance, pain interference, and pain scale. Secondary outcomes included less fatigue and better quality of sleep.
Paired t-test analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in total COMPASS-31 scores from baseline to week four (p = 0.0016).

second_reader.what_stands: Against the current registry record, the paper's headline COMPASS-31 outcome (p = 0.0016) and orthostatic intolerance are not listed as registered primary outcomes, and registered primaries fatigue and sleep disturbance are labelled secondary in the paper. Whether COMPASS-31 was registered as the single secondary outcome, or was changed over time, cannot be settled because earlier record versions were not seen.

issues.title: Conclusions claim restored sympathetic signalling and increased cerebral blood flow, which were not measured
issues.explanation: The only data are self-reported questionnaire scores before and after treatment. The paper nevertheless says its findings indicate improved cerebral blood flow and that the blocks restore dysregulated sympathetic signalling. No physiological measure supports either statement. The Conclusions also say the study 'demonstrates' effectiveness, which goes beyond an uncontrolled before-after design.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Physiological measurements (cerebral perfusion, autonomic testing) reported in the study showing the claimed change.

quotes.text: Our findings indicate that SGB may counteract these effects by enhancing CBF and reducing sympathetic-driven vasoconstriction
These findings suggest that DSBs have the potential to restore dysregulated sympathetic signaling and provide meaningful symptom relief for individuals suffering from Long COVID.

second_reader.what_stands: The paper measured no cerebral blood flow and no physiological index of sympathetic signalling, yet the Discussion says its findings indicate SGB enhances CBF, and the Conclusions suggest DSBs restore dysregulated sympathetic signalling. The Conclusions wording is hedged ('potential') and the CBF mechanism is attributed to earlier studies, so the problem is unsupported mechanistic framing and not an explicit claim of measured CBF increase.

issues.title: Uncorrected paired t-tests across many outcomes; fatigue (p=0.049) and sleep (p=0.016) called significant
issues.explanation: Paired t-tests were run on COMPASS-31 total and domains and on several PROMIS-29 subscales, at two timepoints, each at p<0.05 with no correction. The Methods also say tests were done 'upon finding significance', which is an unclear selection rule. The headline COMPASS-31 and pain interference results likely hold. The fatigue (p = 0.049) and sleep (p = 0.016) improvements, which the Conclusions cite as significant, would not survive correction across this many tests.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified analysis plan designating a single primary test with hierarchical or adjusted handling of the other outcomes.

quotes.text: Upon finding significance, two-tailed paired t-tests
The PROMIS-29 fatigue scores showed marginal improvement at week one (p = 0.052) and significant improvement by week four (p = 0.049).

10.7759/cureus.87026.headline_claim: Olfactory training with or without budesonide irrigations did not produce a statistically significant olfactory improvement at eight weeks in children with post-COVID olfactory dysfunction, and the authors frame the study as a pilot foundation for larger pediatric trials.
10.7759/cureus.87026.overall: The trial cannot answer its question: only 1 of 9 OT + BI participants completed follow-up, so no arm comparison exists, and the OT-only null (n = 7) is too small to be informative. The authors label the work exploratory and mostly disclose these limits, so the conclusions are usable only as a feasibility signal for future trials.

primary_outcome.name: Change in UPSIT score from initial visit to eight-week follow-up (OT arm only; no between-arm comparison)

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) Score From Baseline to First Follow-up
primary_outcomes.time_frame: Before and after 8-12 weeks of smell retraining

issues.title: Differential attrition (OT 4/11 lost; OT + BI 8/9 lost) leaves 8/20 analysable; completer-only analysis
issues.explanation: Only 7 of 11 OT and 1 of 9 OT + BI participants completed follow-up, so the study's randomised comparison cannot be made and the OT-only result rests on completers. The loss was heavily differential and mostly unexplained, so dropout may relate to treatment burden or lack of effect. No imputation or sensitivity analysis was done. The authors acknowledge this, but the primary question is unanswerable and the OT-only null is only tentative.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Outcome data for the dropouts or a sensitivity analysis showing conclusions unchanged.

quotes.text: In the OT + BI group, one of nine participants completed follow-up
No imputation methods were applied, and per-protocol analysis was used

second_reader.what_stands: The paper reports 4/11 lost in the OT arm and 8/9 lost in the OT + BI arm, leaving 8 of 20 randomised participants (7 + 1) with follow-up data. Its Methods and Limitations state that non-respondents were excluded from paired analyses, no imputation or sensitivity analysis was done, and the analysis was per-protocol. The authors acknowledge the high attrition-bias risk, label the findings exploratory, and do not compare arms at follow-up, so the problem is real but openly disclosed and weighed in their conclusions.

issues.title: Only within-arm paired tests (OT arm, n = 7); no between-arm comparison of the randomised arms
issues.explanation: The paper compares eight-week with baseline scores inside the OT arm only (P = 0.6, n = 7) and states that arms were not compared. A non-significant within-arm change in seven people cannot show that OT is ineffective nor answer the OT versus OT + BI question. The authors state this limitation clearly and call findings exploratory, so the issue is largely disclosed and consistent with their conclusions.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: N/A; this is a design limitation the authors already disclose.

quotes.text: SNOT-22 and UPSIT scores at eight-week follow-up were not compared between OT + BI and OT only groups due to significant loss to follow-up.
There was no statistically significant difference in the average UPSIT scores between the initial clinic visit and eight-week follow-up for the OT-only arm (P = 0.6).

issues.title: No sample-size calculation; 20 of 60 targeted enrolled, so the null OT result is uninformative
issues.explanation: The trial enrolled 20 of a 60-participant target, reports no sample-size justification, and analysed only 7 OT participants at follow-up. A null result in such a sample cannot distinguish no effect from low power. The authors call the findings exploratory and a pilot, which limits the consequence, but the Discussion still states there was no objective or subjective improvement after eight weeks of OT.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A pre-specified sample-size calculation showing adequate power for the analysed sample.

quotes.text: The study was terminated before the target enrollment of 60 participants due to progressively slowing enrollment.
These findings should be considered exploratory due to the small sample size and substantial attrition.

issues.title: OT + BI baseline n is 9 for SNOT-22 but 8 for UPSIT, and 15/18 UPSIT denominator, without explanation
issues.explanation: The OT + BI arm has 9 participants at baseline for SNOT-22 but only 8 for UPSIT, and the misidentified-odorant figure uses a denominator of 18, whereas arm-level baseline UPSIT counts sum to 19 (11 + 8). The paper never states which participant lacked a baseline UPSIT. This is a small unexplained reporting gap; it does not change any reported result, and the 18 vs 19 mismatch is likely the same missing-data issue (or one further missing item-level record).
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A statement that one OT + BI participant did not complete a baseline UPSIT and one further participant had missing item-level data.

quotes.text: the mean UPSIT score at the initial clinic visit and eightweek follow-up was 21.0 ± 10.1 (n = 8)
lime and soap (15/18, 83% misidentified for each)

issues.title: One participant moved from randomised OT to OT + BI by clinician discretion; concealment not described
issues.explanation: One of 20 participants received OT + BI despite being randomised to OT because of allergic symptoms, and the enrolling physician also deployed treatment. The paper does not describe allocation concealment. Since the arms were never compared, the practical effect is small, but the reassigned participant adds to the unexplained baseline imbalance in allergy history.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: A description of concealed allocation and an as-randomised analysis.

quotes.text: One participant was placed in a treatment arm (OT + BI) different than what was randomly assigned (OT) at the initial clinic visit.
The attending pediatric otolaryngologist enrolled participants.

issues.title: Conclusion on earlier intervention and longer training rests on adult data, not on this trial
issues.explanation: The Conclusions say earlier identification and intervention may improve outcomes and that longer treatment may be efficacious. This study did not vary timing or duration, and found no change in OT-only. The language is hedged and flagged as hypothetical, so the overreach is mild, but the Discussion also says presentation delay explains the null, which is untested.
issues.would_be_refuted_by: Data in this trial linking shorter duration of dysfunction to greater improvement.

quotes.text: earlier identification and intervention in pediatric patients may be associated with improved outcomes
Several studies in adults have also shown that a shorter duration of OD is correlated with greater improvement in olfactory outcomes
